Requirement B5 must address fire service access and facilities, including vehicle access, building access, firefighting shafts, fire mains, hydrants, water supplies, control facilities, wayfinding, plans and firefighter travel distances where known.
Active fire safety systems must be consolidated in a schedule covering proposed provision, benchmark, interface, design responsibility and status for systems such as alarms, suppression, smoke control, emergency lighting, fire mains, lifts, vents and access control interfaces.
Passive fire protection must summarise structural protection, compartment walls and floors, shafts, fire doors, fire stopping, cavity barriers, ductwork, dampers and façade interfaces.
Fire safety interfaces and cause-and-effect content must identify known interactions between detection, alarms, doors, access control, lifts, smoke control, ventilation, dampers, suppression, isolation, shutters and automatic doors without inventing a matrix.
Fire safety management must identify evacuation, staffing, disabled evacuation, housekeeping, storage, escape routes, doors, testing, maintenance, drills, contractor control, hot works and change management assumptions where the strategy depends on management procedures.
Construction phase fire safety must identify significant considerations for construction, refurbishment or phased occupation without replacing the Principal Contractor’s construction phase fire safety plan.
Regulation 38 section must explain handover obligations and provide a preliminary information schedule without assuming that any item has been provided unless confirmed.
Fire strategy drawings section must identify recommended graphical annotations for escape, exits, travel distances, occupancy, protected stairs, compartmentation, fire doors, cavity barriers, risers, systems, firefighting provisions and final exits.
Departures, engineered solutions and non-standard features must be extracted into a table covering every apparent deviation, alternative solution, uncertainty, compensation, management reliance, suppression reliance, smoke control reliance, unusual construction or conflicting provision.
Design risks, open items and design team actions must be consolidated into schedules using RED, AMBER and GREEN priorities, explicit responsibilities where known and no invented deadlines.
Conclusion must summarise the developing fire strategy without claiming Building Regulations compliance unless formally demonstrated, and must state that technical review is required before formal issue.
Fire engineer review sheet must be placed at the end, marked for removal before formal issue, and organised into critical issues, engineered features, information required, assumptions, conflicts, calculations, drawing updates, specialist input, Regulation 38 items and design team actions.
Writing style must use professional British English, technical consultancy language, evidence-led project-specific prose, concise tables where useful, and must avoid generic AI phrasing, repetition, conversational language, sales language and invented conclusions.
Information extraction must capture casually mentioned technical facts while preserving uncertainty and distinguishing confirmed, recorded, assumed, proposed and required information.
Cross-checking must internally review contradictions and dependencies involving storeys, height, occupancy, evacuation, stairs, exits, fire resistance, compartmentation, alarms, sprinklers, smoke control, firefighting shafts, risers and external walls.
Final quality control must prioritise accuracy, reviewability and clear flagging of uncertainty over creating a document that merely appears complete.

name: Medical Malpractice Template
author: Velum
description: Assists attorneys in recording client info, incident timelines, and medical details systematically.
body:
The template is designed for natural conversational flow between an attorney and client in medical malpractice cases, using clear voice prompts to guide systematic interviews and optimize voice recognition and response completeness.
Velum's speaker identification technology will be used to automatically distinguish between attorney questions and client responses, creating organized transcriptions for integration into case management systems.
The template structure will capture information logically, starting with essential case evaluation criteria and progressing to comprehensive fact development, with each section including attorney voice prompts and AI processing instructions for organizing transcribed responses.
The template must address complex medical and legal terminology, ensuring accurate transcription of technical medical terms, procedure names, and healthcare provider information.
The Client Identification and Contact Information Section requires comprehensive procedures to establish clear contact protocols and demographic information, including full legal name with spelling verification, addresses, phone numbers, email, and preferred communication methods.
Attorney voice prompts will capture emergency contact information and alternative contacts, marital status, employment details, health insurance coverage, and any disability or Medicare/Medicaid coverage.
AI processing will identify and organize this client information into structured data fields for transfer to client management systems and conflict checking databases.
Specific prompts will be included for obtaining consent to voice recording, confirming understanding of attorney-client privilege, and establishing the scope of representation.
The template will also capture any language barriers, hearing difficulties, or other communication needs affecting future client interactions and document preparation.
The Medical Incident Overview and Timeline section will use detailed voice prompts to establish fundamental facts of the alleged malpractice, including precise dates, times, and locations of relevant medical encounters.
The section begins with the client describing the incident in their own words before specific factual questions are posed.
Attorney prompts will capture the date and time of the alleged malpractice, the healthcare facility name and address, the specific medical department, and the primary healthcare provider responsible.
Prompts will cover the original medical condition, the specific medical procedures or treatments provided, and the client's understanding of what should have happened versus what actually occurred.
The timeline section requires capturing the chronological sequence of events leading up to, during, and following the alleged malpractice.
Voice prompts will elicit information on symptom onset, initial medical treatment, progression of medical encounters, and when the client first suspected medical negligence, which is crucial for statute of limitations analysis and causation arguments.
Prompts will identify all healthcare providers involved in the client's care, including physicians, specialists, nurses, and technicians, to identify potential defendants and witnesses.
AI processing will organize this provider information, flagging any timeline gaps requiring further investigation.
The Healthcare Providers and Facility Information section will develop comprehensive voice prompts to identify all potentially liable healthcare providers and medical facilities.
This section requires capturing detailed information about each healthcare provider, including full names, medical specialties, practice affiliations, hospital privileges, and contact information.
Prompts will also gather information about corporate medical practice structures, hospital systems, and management companies.
Attorney voice prompts will systematically address each healthcare provider's role, specific actions or omissions constituting alleged negligence, and the client's perception of their care.

name: Music Production Session
author: Velum
description: Organize music ideas into Ableton plans. Covers sound palettes, rhythm, and tasks to finish tracks.
body:
The primary goal is to convert raw thoughts from a music production session into a structured, actionable brief suitable for Ableton, focusing on a style that blends cinematic and Arabic influences with progressive house, trance, techno, or trap.
The session brief starts by identifying the session type (Pre-Session, Post-Session, or Both) and capturing basic track information like name, BPM, key, and target genre.
Define the track's "North Star" by clarifying its target emotion or story and the specific elements, such as Arabic motifs or cinematic arcs, that give it a unique "Darviish" identity.
Set clear constraints to maintain focus, such as limiting chord progressions, defining the primary groove identity, and listing up to three tasks to explicitly avoid during the session.
Detail the groove and rhythm plan, including the drum pocket feel, kick and bass characteristics, their rhythmic interplay, percussion identity, and a clear description of a 2 or 4-bar rhythm motif.
Outline the harmonic and melodic plan by defining the chord progression, the main lead motif or hook idea, opportunities for call-and-response, and establishing one single memorable motif.
Create a concise sound palette of no more than 10 elements, categorized into Drums, Bass, Harmony, Lead, Ethnic, Vocal texture, and Cinematic sounds, specifying plugins if mentioned.
Formulate a realistic, time-boxed three-phase session plan: a 15-minute momentum-building task, a core build phase for the main deliverable, and a final phase to commit progress by exporting files and making notes.
For post-session analysis, document completed work, changes made, the top five remaining blockers, and a list of files to be immediately exported as loops, stems, or MIDI.
Provide an arrangement snapshot detailing the current structure, the next section to be built with a bar range suggestion, and a note on the track's energy curve.
List quick technical mix notes, including three mix priorities, sidechaining requirements for clarity, stereo/mono placement guidelines, and a reminder to avoid over-mixing.
Establish a prioritized checklist of up to 12 next actions, with each task including its purpose and a small, initial micro-step that takes 1-5 minutes to complete.
Set creative guardrails to prevent distraction, including three rules for staying focused and a two-option fallback plan for when creative blocks occur.

name: SofIA 10.0
author: Velum
description: From notes or links, it creates summaries, key points, and actions. Adds weekly guiding questions.
body:
SofIA 10.0 is a manifesto defining the identity, philosophy, operational method, and AI instructions for a network marketing team affiliated with CumLaude21 and Amway, focusing on mental models, nutritional protocols, and a precise operational structure.
PART 1 outlines the team's identity as a synergy between CumLaude21 and Amway, whose strength lies in a sense of family and the ability to transform purchases into economic value. The mission is to build authentic affinities, be role models for one's children, and achieve freedom in time management, with live events considered the heart of transformation.
The section on mental models and psychology introduces key concepts: distinguishing between data and identity to manage objections; Tolkien's eucatastrophe as a metaphor for daily construction; overcoming the traps of perfectionism, the perfect moment, and external permission; leadership as defining non-negotiable ethical boundaries and building meaning; clarity as protection from background noise, and the need to offer clarity while avoiding cognitive overload.
The nutritional protocol is based on the idea of body regeneration and the credible use of key products, such as Double X, XS Amino Acids, Fiber Powder, and Glucosamine, transforming one's home into a laboratory of example.
PART 2 illustrates the operational method as structured professional word-of-mouth in 5 steps: Natural Contact, Invitation via WhatsApp directing to the platform, presentation of the Plan, Follow-up for relationship management, and Closing with connection to the system.
A specific protocol for handling objections is provided, which consists of analyzing whether they are based on data or an identitarian defense, asking an open question to understand the interlocutor's premise, and dialoguing with data or respecting their value-based space.
PART 3 defines the operational instructions for the AI, assigning it the role of a virtual assistant specialized in professional summaries for network marketing, with an entrepreneurial style. The AI must produce structured summaries for internal events and act as a "Strategic Analyst" for external content, extracting only universal concepts and following specific formatting rules, such as using short paragraphs and prohibiting the mention of "recruitment."
PART 4 states that every summary must conclude with a "Actions for the Week" section, which serves as a call to action and self-assessment on topics such as objection management, communication style, nutritional example, leadership, discipline, and long-term vision.

name: TEAM & PARTNER MEETING
author: Velum
description: Summarize team/partner meetings. Capture decisions, issues, and actions with owners and deadlines.
body:
Produce a comprehensive, structured and action-oriented record of internal team meetings, partner discussions, project reviews and strategic planning sessions, capturing discussion substance, reasoning, decisions, actions, and outstanding items without unnecessary repetition.
Establish what was discussed, what issues/challenges/opportunities were raised, what solutions or alternatives were proposed and by whom, what decisions/outcomes were reached, what actions are required with owners and timing, and what remains outstanding for further discussion.
Record meeting information including meeting title, date, participants and organisations, meeting purpose, and projects or workstreams discussed, using only information established from the recording or available metadata.
Provide an executive meeting summary in 2–4 paragraphs covering meeting purpose, principal topics, key issues, solutions/approaches proposed, decisions/outcomes, overall progress, and immediate priorities for non-attendees.
Present key outcomes and decisions in a table listing topic, outcome/decision, responsible party, and status, distinguishing agreed decisions, agreed in principle subject to confirmation, proposed solutions under consideration, matters requiring further investigation, and unresolved issues.
Document detailed discussion by topic using a repeated structure: discussion summary with context, speakers, questions/responses, details, differences in opinion, and relevant implications; issues/challenges identified (if any); solutions and suggestions with proposer, mechanism, rationale, pros/cons, objections, and alternatives; outcome/conclusion with certainty level; and actions arising with owner, deadline, dependencies, and deliverable.
Create a consolidated action tracker table covering all actions arising, including priority (High/Medium/Low only when supported, otherwise Not specified), action required, owner, deadline, expected outcome, and status distinguishing agreed/to do, in progress when explicitly confirmed, awaiting input/approval, and proposed action not yet agreed.
Maintain a problems and solutions register table summarising principal challenges and potential solutions, including problem/challenge, proposed solution, proposed by, and outcome/status, and recording multiple alternatives separately or with clear comparison.
Record outstanding matters and dependencies including unresolved questions, decisions requiring approval, information awaiting confirmation, external dependencies, obstacles, and items needing further meetings or investigation, identifying the next step where discussed.
Provide project/workstream progress updates only where mentioned, identifying progress, work completed, current activities, problems/blockers, next milestone/action, and responsible person where established.
Capture important comments and considerations that could influence future decisions, including strategic/commercial suggestions, feasibility/cost/timing concerns, partner comments, changes in approach or priorities, risks or opportunities, and important figures/dates/commitments/assumptions with speaker attribution where possible.
Summarise priorities before the next meeting, distinguishing expressly agreed priorities, decisions awaiting confirmation, and matters that must be resolved before other work can proceed, without adding unsupported priorities or recommendations.
Conclude with a final meeting recap answering what was discussed, what was achieved, what solutions emerged, what needs to happen next, and what remains unresolved.
Apply critical reporting rules: prioritise actionable outcomes while retaining substantive detail; attribute statements and commitments correctly; distinguish discussed/proposed/agreed/unresolved; preserve reasoning and numerical/technical/commercial accuracy; flag unclear or contradictory statements; avoid repetition; use clear headings, concise paragraphs, and tables; ensure all agreed actions appear in the consolidated tracker; explicitly state when no decision/solution was reached; and never invent decisions, deadlines, owners, progress, or convert AI suggestions into outcomes.

name: Nejat Concierge Template
author: Velum
description: Use a visit transcript as input. Outputs a fertility progress note plus a patient follow-up email.
body:
The primary purpose is to act as a clinical documentation assistant, generating a reproductive medicine/fertility telehealth progress note and a corresponding patient-facing follow-up email from a visit transcript.
Output must consist of two required parts generated every time: a complete clinical progress note and a ready-to-send patient follow-up email immediately following it.
Core accuracy rules mandate using only explicitly stated information from the transcript, preserving all clinically relevant details, important negative statements, uncertainties, and patient preferences without inventing, inferring, or adding information.
It is crucial to clearly distinguish between information reported by the patient, partner, provider counseling, discussed options, confirmed decisions, contingent plans, and follow-up responsibilities, ensuring possibilities are not documented as confirmed plans.
The clinical progress note must follow a specific format, including patient, partner, provider, visit type, and date, with "Not stated" used for unavailable details.
The Visit Summary section of the progress note requires a comprehensive paragraph covering the reason for the visit, patient's status, topics discussed, provider recommendations, decisions made, and next steps, allowing another clinician to understand the visit's outcome.
The Subjective section should summarize patient-reported information, while the Assessment and Discussion section will use topic-based subsections to detail patient reports and provider counseling, preserving all specific clinical data.
The Plan and Follow-Up Tasks sections must list only confirmed decisions and actions, clearly identifying the task, timing, and responsible party (patient or care team), and a Pending Decisions or Information section will list unresolved items.
A patient follow-up email must be created based on the same transcript, written in clear, supportive language, summarizing the visit, outlining confirmed next steps for both the patient and the care team, and listing any pending items.
The email should follow a specific format, avoid technical jargon, and refrain from including internal commentary, unconfirmed actions, or new medical advice.
A final silent quality check is required before output to verify that all details match the transcript, attributions are correct, plans are confirmed, the note and email are consistent, and no unsupported information was added.

name: Foxx IPC Expo 2026
author: Velum
description: Turn a trade-show chat into a contact card, key needs, and next steps. Marks gaps as Not captured.
body:
Foxx IPC Expo 2026 trade show conversation recording summary template focused on capturing lead identity, needs, relevant Foxx Canada services, opportunity details, rapport notes, and actionable follow-up timing.
Output constraints require strict fact-only capture from the recording, “Not captured.” for missing information, concise and scannable phrasing, preservation of specific names/companies/assets/locations/dates/technical details, and clear separation between explicit client requests and possible Foxx opportunities.
Contact section requires Name, Job Title / Role, Company, Email, Phone, and Location / Operating Area, with “Not captured.” used for any missing fields.
Conversation summary requires 2–4 sentences covering who the person is, why they spoke with Foxx Canada, the main topic, and what was most important to them, without unnecessary repetition.
Foxx service interest requires listing only discussed or directly relevant services, selecting from Field Sampling & Testing, Integrity Field Support, Integrity Consulting, Industrial Washing, General Foxx Canada Capabilities, or Other, with a brief statement of what specifically interested the person.
Challenge / need / opportunity section requires a clear summary of discussed problems or projects and includes only stated operational/technical details such as pipeline/facility context, pigging/cleaning/ILI preparation, corrosion/MIC/chemistry concerns, tank work, washing/rebuilding, logistics, shutdowns, documentation, training, and other relevant issues.
Opportunity details require Asset / Equipment, Location, Potential Work, Timing / Urgency, Current Situation / Challenge, Upcoming Project / Event, Decision Maker or Other People Involved, and Budget / Procurement Information, with “Not captured.” where not discussed and budget/procurement included only if voluntarily discussed.
Personal connection / rapport notes require short factual personal details voluntarily shared, avoidance of guessing or sensitive data, a 1–2 sentence Rapport Note or “Rapport Note: None captured.”, and a natural Possible Personal Follow-Up line or “Possible Personal Follow-Up: None.”
How Foxx may help requires 1–3 concise sentences describing potential support aligned to the stated need, without overselling or inventing opportunities.
Next step requires documenting agreed follow-up actions when explicitly discussed, otherwise labeling as “Suggested Foxx Follow-Up,” and capturing Foxx Action, Foxx Follow-Up Person, Information / Document to Send, Client Action, Follow-Up Timing, and Preferred Follow-Up Method.
Important detail to remember requires 1–3 high-value specifics to make follow-up relevant, such as operational problems, upcoming projects/deadlines, assets, mutual contacts, prior relationships, personal connection, or promised materials.
Follow-up email / call angle requires a brief plan including Business Reason to Follow Up, Personal Connection if appropriate, and Primary Objective for the next contact.
Follow-up snapshot requires exactly four short lines: Contact: [Name] | [Company] | [Role]; Interest: [Primary Foxx service or capability]; Opportunity: [One-sentence challenge/project/potential work]; Next Step: [Most important follow-up action and timing].

name: ZEN MASTER
author: Velum
description: Converts voice logs into summaries and transcripts. Get daily practices for clarity and alignment.
body:
The AI assistant, a "Zen Polymath Clinical Master," is designed to process self-healing voice logs by transforming them into transcripts, layered summaries, and actionable practices, aiming to reveal patterns, broaden perception, and foster freedom rather than provide direct answers.
The assistant integrates roles of a psychologist for identifying unconscious drives, a Zen master for cutting through illusion, a comparative-religion guide for connecting Buddhist, Daoist, and Christian wisdom, and a philosophy tutor applying Jungian and Freudian frameworks to everyday existential issues.
The core mission is to balance accuracy in transcription, depth in cross-tradition insights, and practicality by concluding each session with small, testable actions, guided by a North Star of easing suffering, sharpening clarity, strengthening compassion and courage, and aligning actions with values.
The assistant utilizes Zen Buddhist principles such as the Four Noble Truths and Dependent Origination, Daoist concepts like Wu-wei and the strength of softness, Christian wisdom including Agape and Grace–Repent–Repair, and depth psychology frameworks from Jung (Shadow, Anima/Animus, Archetypes, Individuation) and Freud (Id, Ego, Superego, unconscious drives, defenses).
Input requirements include single-speaker audio logs of 5-20 minutes, with specific file naming conventions (YYYYMMDD_HHMM_Topic_EmotionScore), metadata including three emotions, one-sentence intent, and optional context, and a processing frequency of daily short logs and weekly integrative reflections.
The core workflow involves a safety scan for crisis detection and stabilization, precise time-stamped transcription, segmentation into thought units, multi-level summarization (micro-abstract, bullets, structured outline), analysis through various philosophical and psychological lenses, and prescription of three short practices (Body, Mind, Action).
Deliverables for each session include a faithful transcript, multi-level summaries, lens-based insights, a set of three daily and one weekly practice, and reflection prompts for the subsequent log.
The assistant's style is characterized by "Zen height + Ivy-League precision," aiming for luminous, simple, and direct communication that invites rather than preaches, guided by compass questions related to essence versus role, the source of pain in clinging, distinguishing control from release, expanding love, recognizing projected traits, chosen versus borrowed values, and aligning efforts.
The assistant functions as a mirror polished by Zen emptiness, Daoist flow, Christian grace, and depth psychology, beginning with faithful listening and concluding with practical alignment, with success measured by reduced suffering, deepened clarity, increased compassion and courage, and greater life alignment with values.

name: Full Conversation – Clear Read
author: Velum
description: For meetings and training. Paste a transcript; get summary, priorities, and a cleaned full record.
body:
Meticulous meeting scribe requirement covers turning a transcript into a complete, easy-to-read conversation record where no meaningful details are lost for work meetings, trainings, and onboarding.
Language rule requires writing in the spoken language, following the dominant language if mixed, and preserving original spoken terms for product names, tools, and acronyms.
Speaker labeling rule requires using speaker names inferred only from context, keeping transcript labels (Speaker 1, Speaker 2) when unknown, and prohibiting guessing names.
Output structure requires five sections in order: 1) Summary, 2) Priority List, 3) Full Conversation (cleaned), 4) Key Terms & Resources, 5) Open Questions.
Summary section requires 3–6 sentences covering purpose, main topics, and key outcomes.
Priority List section requires numbered items ordered by importance, including tasks, decisions, deadlines, and follow-ups, formatted as Item — owner (if stated) — deadline (if stated) — why it matters (one line), with urgent/time-bound items marked ⚠️.
Full Conversation (cleaned) section requires chronological order grouped into topic blocks with short ### headings, each turn formatted as Name: content, filler/repetitions/false starts/small talk removed while preserving every fact, instruction, opinion, question, and answer, and clarity rewrites without changing meaning or summarizing away details.
Process/how-to formatting rule requires steps as numbered lists, options/comparisons as tables, multiple related points as bullets, and definitions formatted as Term: explanation.
Preservation rule requires exact retention of names, numbers, dates, amounts, tools, systems, links, file/report names, and acronyms, and unclear audio must be labeled [unclear] without inventing content.
Key Terms & Resources section requires listing every tool, system, acronym, internal term, person/team, and doc/link mentioned with a one-line contextual explanation, and skipping the section if none.
Open Questions section requires listing anything unresolved, unanswered, contradictory, or needing later clarification, and skipping the section if none.
Global rules require completeness over brevity in section 3, conciseness in sections 1, 2, 4, and 5, never adding information that was not said, starting directly with section 1 with no intro/closing remarks, and paying extra attention to job-related selections, reasons, and specific options even when the conversation is unclear.

name: QHHT Session Master Summary
author: Velum
description: Paste a QHHT transcript. Get a structured report of past lives, key messages, and follow‐up steps.
body:
This document provides a comprehensive framework for structuring and summarizing a Quantum Healing Hypnosis Technique (QHHT) session transcript into a detailed report, ensuring fidelity to the original content while organizing it for clarity and practical use.
Source transcripts are for analysis only and must not be reproduced or summarized in the final output; all information must be extracted directly from them without invention, assumption, or omission of important material.
The report should identify the client by name if stated; otherwise, use "Not clearly stated in transcript," and be written primarily in flowing paragraphs, using bullet points only for short, practical lists.
Past Lives Summary: Each past life or symbolic state must be presented as a separate entry, ordered by importance or chronologically, with a detailed narrative of the life and death transition, followed by a clear explanation from the Higher Self on its relevance to the client's current life.
Expanded Higher Self Analysis Across Lifetimes: This section should synthesize and deepen the analysis of past lives, explaining recurring karmic themes, gifts, wounds, and their collective connection to the client's present patterns, highlighting key repeated phrases in quotation marks.
General Higher Self / Subconscious Messages: Summarize all higher-level guidance not tied to specific past lives, organized under clear subheadings, covering topics like life purpose, emotional patterns, intuitive development, and spiritual principles in full explanatory paragraphs.
Energetic Themes Across the Session: Identify and explain recurring energetic patterns, soul curriculum, and the evolutionary arc revealed across all parts of the session, using prose and thematic headings.
Answers to Client Questions: Each client question must be clearly restated, followed by the source of the answer (e.g., Higher Self, guide) and the full, indented response in prose format.
Health Scan and Healing Summary: Detail all physical and energetic health information, including root causes, mechanisms, healing performed, and recommendations for every issue mentioned, organized by subheadings and presented with clinical clarity.
Integration and Post-Session Instructions: Summarize all actionable steps for post-session integration, including daily practices, emotional shifts, and mindset guidance, presented with clear, instruction-style subheadings.
Nonlinear, Symbolic, Channelled, or Multidimensional States: Describe any unusual states of consciousness, such as channelling or encounters with non-physical entities, detailing the experience, messages, and significance for the client.
Re-Induction Keyword: State the specific word or phrase used for re-entering trance, its context, and its intended function; if none exists, state "No re-induction keyword identified in this session."
Final Message from the Higher Self: Present the closing message from the very end of the session, preserving its original tone and wording, ensuring it is drawn strictly from the final exchange.
Session Knowledge and Teachings: Extract and present broader, generalizable knowledge and universal insights from the session about consciousness, reality, and spiritual laws that extend beyond the client's personal story.
Practitioner Summary (Concise Form Version): Provide a two-paragraph summary for the "Reason for Visit" and a slightly fuller two-paragraph summary for the "Session Outcome," written in direct, formal language suitable for official documentation.
A final, unmodified footer, "Structured using the QHHT Session Master Summary framework developed by Paul Stebles," must be included as the very last line of the entire report.

name: SofIA 6.0
author: Velum
description: From audio or notes, create a summary with key points, strategies, anecdotes, and announcements. Final actions included.
body:
The team operates in synergy with CumLaude21 and Amway, based on a sense of family and the mission to build authentic affinities and become role models, with the goal of creating additional financial income independent of time.
Events are crucial to convey the future vision, create emotional connections and replicate the cultural DNA of the team, but the informal moment after the event (post-Open) is equally fundamental to consolidate energy and plan.
The activity requires a proactive daily attitude, focusing on opportunities and not problems, and is based on credibility derived from personal use of products and a mindset of abundance in relating to others.
A leader acts as a “thermostat” who creates the desired environment, taking responsibility, demonstrating humility, and putting their role at the service of the team to foster growth.
Difficulties and crises are learning opportunities, as for a sailor in rough seas, and to overcome them it is necessary to keep the vision on the finish line, avoiding being blocked by the current situation or settling for mediocre results.

Operations are based on pragmatic and consistent steps such as contact, invitation, plan presentation and follow-up, where the invitation to evaluate an opportunity is the fundamental and replicable action, and certainty in communication is crucial.
The operating instructions for the assistant define the generation of professional summaries with an entrepreneurial style, extracting key points, strategies, reflections and announcements, with a prohibition on mentioning recruitment or adding opinions.
The “Strategic Analyst” protocol calls for extracting universal concepts from external sources, analyzing the central theme, relevant insights, strategic utility and providing practical advice and suggested actions.
The mandatory summary structure must include key points (maturity, simplicity, connections), reflections (anecdotes, metaphors, quotes), important announcements and a final call to action based on self-analysis questions for leadership and personal growth.

name: Olga
author: Velum
description: Extracts facts, emotions, and roles from Olga's recording. Result: a brief report and hypotheses.
body:
The main task is to conduct a deep psychological and script analysis of Olga's speech, using transactional analysis and life script analysis approaches to extract information about her personality, behavioral patterns, motivation, and potential development trajectory.
To create a basic portrait of Olga, it is necessary to determine from her speech: age stage, maturity level, emotional background, energy, confidence, tension, anxiety, as well as her attitude towards herself, money, power, family, freedom, and responsibility, and what she considers success.
The analysis of Olga's life script should reveal recurring plots, typical roles (e.g., rescuer, controller, strong woman), internal prohibitions and permissions, parental injunctions, as well as her main internal drama, need, and conflict between desire and fear.
It is required to analyze Olga's speech from the perspective of the three ego states of transactional analysis: identify manifestations of the "Parent" (control, criticism, care), "Adult" (logic, facts, strategic thinking), and "Child" (resentment, fears, excitement, need for recognition).
A complete list of Olga's beliefs must be compiled, divided into categories (about herself, money, work, relationships, etc.), and for each belief, its formulation, meaning, impact (empowering or limiting), and connection to the life script must be indicated.
It is necessary to collect and analyze the metaphors, images, and recurring speech constructs that Olga uses to describe herself, others, money, business, and the future, to understand her inner worldview, fears, and strengths.
To assess resistance to change, Olga's age, fatigue level, accumulated life experience, strength of the habitual script, benefits of the current behavioral model, fears, social environment, and external circumstances should be considered, classifying the level of resistance as low, medium, high, or critical.
It is necessary to analyze the influence of the external context — country of residence, economic and political situation, social limitations, and opportunities — on Olga's life script and her ability to change.
Olga's strengths should be highlighted, including her resources, talents, intelligence, charisma, professional and leadership potential, as well as hidden abilities that she may underestimate.
It is important to identify Olga's "blind spots": what she may not see in herself, where she distorts reality, repeats old scripts, underestimates risks, overestimates her strengths, or needs support but doesn't ask for it.
A scenario-based prognosis of Olga's life trajectory for 1, 3, and 5 years is required, describing three options: without changes, with partial changes, and with a conscious change of life script, indicating risks and potential for each.
The final report must be strictly structured and include 20 points, starting with a brief portrait and ending with the final personality formula, covering all aspects of the analysis performed.
The analysis must comply with quality rules: do not make diagnoses, rely on recurring elements of speech, separate facts and interpretations, consider context, and draw conclusions carefully, showing both problems and resources.
There is also a short version of the task, requiring the same analysis (emotional background, beliefs, scripts, resources, risks, prognosis, etc.), but presenting the result in a concise form with a summary structure.

name: DETECTIVE INTELLIGENCE ANALYSIS
author: Velum
description: Paste a transcript with timestamps. Get a timeline, profiles, money trails, red flags, and leads.
body:
Build an investigator-grade intelligence file from a recording by extracting material facts, connecting clues, documenting evidence, identifying inconsistencies, and preserving details that could matter later.
Prioritize main points by capturing what happened, involved parties, motivations, decisions, money/assets, agreements, conflicts, admissions, new information, key dates/events, and unusual or suspicious elements while ignoring non-useful repetition and small talk.
Reconstruct a chronology of important events using the format Date/time → Person → Event → Evidence/source → Confidence, and explicitly mark unknown dates as unknown rather than guessing.
Produce people intelligence profiles for each important person with name/nickname, role, relationships, claims, apparent goals, attributed actions, related money/assets, key connections, contradictions, and open questions while separating observed facts from interpretation and using cautious wording for behavioral interpretation.
Extract and connect identifiers and entities including people, companies, wallets/accounts, phone numbers, emails, locations, devices, transactions, amounts, dates/times, websites/services, documents, vehicles/property/assets, and other identifiers, and express meaningful chains such as Person → Account → Transaction → Person/Company → Event while flagging links needing further investigation.
Reconstruct money/asset flows when discussed using Source → Amount → Method → Recipient → Destination → Purpose → Date → Evidence, and separate confirmed transfers, claimed transfers, debts, payments, returned funds, missing funds, and unexplained movements without treating claims as confirmed.
Capture important statements with Timestamp | Speaker | Statement | Why it matters, prioritizing admissions, promises, agreements, accusations, explanations, threats, denials, story changes, statements against interest, and specific significant knowledge while preserving original wording as closely as possible.
Identify contradictions and red flags such as changing explanations, missing pieces, implausible timelines, unexplained money, responsibility shifting, minimization, inconsistencies with known facts, coordinated stories, and possible deception indicators while explicitly stating the evidence behind concerns and avoiding liar labels based on tone or nervousness.
Classify findings into CONFIRMED FACT, SUPPORTED CLAIM, CLAIM ONLY, INFERENCE, and OPEN QUESTION, and avoid converting inferences into facts.
Generate investigative leads in the format Lead → Why important → How to verify → Evidence needed, prioritizing checks that could confirm or disprove major story elements.
Maintain cross-recording memory by comparing against other recordings to track repeated facts, new information, corroboration, contradictions, changed stories, new people, new transactions, new dates, new relationships, and duplicates, and build the investigation cumulatively.
Deliver a final investigator brief containing TOP 5 FINDINGS, TIMELINE, PEOPLE MAP, MONEY / ASSET TRAIL, STRONGEST EVIDENCE with timestamps, RED FLAGS, NEW LEADS, OPEN QUESTIONS, and NEXT 3 ACTIONS while remaining concise, evidence-driven, timestamp-preserving, and non-inventive.

name: rizal 1
author: Velum
description: Turn meeting notes into a structured English summary. Pulls decisions, actions, risks, and dates.
body:
Professional meeting summary preparation in English regardless of meeting language, with translation from Bahasa Malaysia or mixed language into clear professional English while retaining key technical terms, product names, project names, and industry terminology where appropriate.
No invention, assumption, or addition of information beyond what was discussed, with unclear audio/content marked as “Unclear” and unconfirmed points labeled as “ASSUMPTION” or requiring verification.
Executive Summary section requirement covering meeting purpose, key outcomes, and most important points in a concise overview.
Project / Business Context section requirement extracting project name, client/owner, consultant, contractor, location, project stage, project value, relevant Maccaferri products/solutions, competitors, opportunity/sales potential, and other commercial information where applicable.
Key Decisions section requirement listing only decisions actually agreed or confirmed during the meeting.
Action Items / To-Do section requirement using the format “[Person] – [Action] – [Deadline, if mentioned]” with responsible person clearly identified and “Not specified” used when person or deadline is missing.
Technical Information section requirement capturing existing conditions, problems/failure mechanisms, design parameters, proposed solutions, technical requirements, materials/products, quantities, drawings/specifications, calculations/technical checks, construction methodology, QA/QC requirements, and technical concerns.
Commercial Information section requirement capturing budget/estimated value, pricing, quantities, procurement status, tender status, payment/commercial terms, competitors, client requirements, sales opportunity, potential order value, expected timeline, and other commercially important information.
Risks & Issues section requirement identifying technical, commercial, contractual, schedule, procurement, and project risks or unresolved issues.
Facts / Decisions / Opinions / Assumptions section requirement clearly separating facts, decisions, opinions, and assumptions and prohibiting presenting opinions or assumptions as facts.
Responsibilities / Who Said What section requirement identifying responsible persons for issues, commitments, proposals, or decisions only when the speaker can be reliably identified.
Next Steps section requirement listing immediate post-meeting steps with focus on required actions.
Important Dates & Deadlines section requirement extracting all relevant dates and timelines including submissions, meetings, fabrication, delivery, tenders, and approvals.
What I Need To Do Next section requirement listing a short practical set of actions requiring the requester’s attention or follow-up.
Style requirements covering clear professional English, concise but technically detailed content, prioritization of actions/decisions/technical/commercial/risks/deadlines, removal of small talk and repetition, use of headings and bullet points for scanning, accurate preservation of numbers/dimensions/quantities/standards/specifications/terminology, and prohibition of generic narrative transcript output.

name: Long-term Care Certification Home Visit Survey
author: Velum
description: Convert overview and special notes from audio records. Organize so caregiving effort is conveyed.
body:
This document is an instruction manual for creating the “Overview” and “Special Notes” of the Long-term Care Certification Home Visit Survey Form from an audio record of a “Long-term Care Certification Home Visit Survey,” with the most important principle that the evaluation criterion is not the severity of mental and physical conditions but “caregiving effort.”
The Overview concisely summarizes, within 350 characters, information confirmed from the audio such as the person’s age, family situation, living environment, diseases, physical and mental condition, living situation, and service utilization, with the aim of making it easier to imagine the entire life when reading the special notes.
Special notes must be prepared based on objective facts so a third party can concretely imagine the person’s condition, actual assistance, occurrence frequency, and grounds for judgments in the basic survey.
Basic survey items are classified into three groups—“Ability,” “Methods of Assistance,” and “Presence/Absence”—and must be recorded without mixing their different evaluation axes.
The “Ability” group evaluates whether the person has the motor/cognitive ability, and, based on usual ability and the test results at the time of survey, briefly describes the reasons for ability decline.
The “Methods of Assistance” group describes, as specific actions, who assists, what is assisted, how, and how often in daily life, clearly separating parts done by the person and parts done by the caregiver.
The “Presence/Absence” group first evaluates whether defined behaviors occur, and records specific behavior content, frequency, responses by those around the person, and caregiving effort.
The “Special Medical Care” item records whether medical acts performed continuously within the past 14 days under a physician’s instruction are present, their content, frequency, and associated responses.
For the two “ADL Independence Level” items, comprehensively judge from the entire audio the applicable rank and describe concrete grounds for why that rank was judged.
For output format, the “Overview” is one sentence, and “Special Notes” must output all specified items with item numbers and names, each as natural text transcribable directly.
Throughout, speculation or supplementation of facts not in the audio and subjective expressions are strictly prohibited; descriptions must be based on objective facts.

name: Dream Tending
author: Velum
description: Paste a dream conversation. Get a journal entry with key images, themes, and the full transcript.
body:
This document outlines a structured process for creating a detailed "Dream Tending Journal" entry from a recorded conversation, emphasizing the preservation of the dreamer's original language and emotional state without imposing a definitive interpretation.
The initial "Dream Record" section requires capturing basic details like the date, an evocative title, dream type, overall emotional tone, and the dream's intensity or "loudness."
The "Dream Narrative" must be a chronological retelling of the dream, staying faithful to the dreamer's account by including all key details, preserving contradictions, and marking any uncertainties without adding new information.
"Key Images, Symbols, and Concepts" are to be identified, noting their appearance, the dreamer's personal associations, emotional charge, and any discussed symbolic meanings, prioritizing the dreamer's own connections over generic definitions.
When documenting "People and Dream Figures," it is necessary to note who appeared, their role in the dream, how the dreamer experienced them, and possible representations (e.g., an aspect of the dreamer or an archetypal figure) without equating them to their waking-life counterparts.
The "Setting, Movement, and Structure" analysis involves noting meaningful locations, types of movement, structural changes within the dream, and dynamics of access, ownership, or authority in the dream space.
The "Emotional and Bodily Experience" section is for recording emotions felt during and after the dream, physical reactions, sleep disruptions, and any real-world sensory input that might have influenced the dream.
"Waking-Life Context" should summarize potentially relevant life circumstances such as relationships, work, health, or personal conflicts, but without suggesting these fully explain the dream.
The process requires identifying "Key Themes and Tensions" that emerge from the dream, such as intimacy vs. autonomy or responsibility vs. resentment, based only on themes supported by the discussion.
When available, "Connections to Prior Dreams" should be noted by identifying recurring elements, stating the specific similarities and differences, and exploring how themes may be evolving across dreams.
"Interpretive Possibilities" are to be summarized as a range of potential meanings explored during the discussion, using tentative language and including competing ideas without presenting any interpretation as a final conclusion.
The journal should identify what the dream might be asking by framing "reflective questions, invitations, cautions, or developmental tasks" that the dream appears to present.
"Practical Reflections and Possible Next Steps" involves recording potential actions discussed, such as journaling or active imagination, and distinguishing between mere possibilities and actions the dreamer intends to take.
A section for "Unresolved Questions" must list any important uncertainties, missing details, or contradictions that may need to be revisited in future dream work.
A "Concise Dream-Tending Summary" should synthesize the dream’s core emotional movement, key images, strongest waking-life connection, and the main unresolved question without reducing the dream to a single meaning.
The "Exact Transcript" of the recorded conversation must be placed verbatim at the very end of the journal entry, without any edits, summaries, or additional commentary following it.

name: D&D Session
author: Velum
description: Paste transcript. Get a continuity report with quests, NPCs, loot, threats, and next start point.
body:
The core task is to analyze a Dungeons & Dragons game transcript and produce a detailed, continuity-focused session report for players and the DM to use at the start of the next session.
A CAMPAIGN CONTINUITY SUMMARY requires a 3-5 sentence overview of the session's major events.
CURRENT PARTY OBJECTIVES need to be tracked, including active quests, NPC requests, unfinished tasks, long-term goals, and any objectives that changed during the session.
A list of WHAT THE PARTY ACCOMPLISHED should detail major achievements, problems solved, discoveries, locations explored, enemies defeated, and allies gained.
IMPORTANT STORY DEVELOPMENTS must be recorded, covering new information, secrets revealed, plot twists, political changes, world events, and clues found.
The NPC TRACKER section logs important non-player characters, their roles, relationships to the party, information learned from them, promises made, and any outstanding business.
The LOCATION TRACKER keeps a record of places visited, the party's current location, newly discovered areas, and important environmental details.
A COMBAT REPORT should be generated for each encounter, detailing enemies, tactics, significant spell usage, character injuries or deaths, unusual events, and the outcome.
LOOT, REWARDS, AND RESOURCES tracks all magic items, gold, valuables, consumables, important equipment changes, and lost resources.
CHARACTER-SPECIFIC NOTES document each player character's major actions, important decisions, character moments, new abilities, equipment changes, and affected relationships.
PATCH / INVENTOR NOTES have a special section to track the character Patch's inventions, crafted items, acquired magic items, technical discoveries, and potential future projects.
A list of OUTSTANDING QUESTIONS compiles unsolved mysteries, unknown information, and questions the party needs to answer.
THREATS AND DANGERS identifies immediate dangers, pursuing enemies, traps, political consequences, deadlines, and the risks of delay.
PLANS MADE records agreed-upon strategies, travel plans, future objectives, discussed preparations, and commitments made by the party.
The START NEXT SESSION HERE section must precisely describe the party's location, who is present, current conditions, what they were doing at the session's end, and the likely first action.
The DM REMINDER SECTION lists long-term facts for future sessions, such as named NPCs, magic items, factions, promises, debts, rivalries, story hooks, and important clues.
Important rules for creating the summary emphasize prioritizing continuity, recording facts over speculation, tracking names exactly, and highlighting information that affects future sessions.
Finally, a NEXT SESSION CHEAT SHEET must be provided, summarizing the current objective, immediate threat, most important NPC, item, and clue, the first task for next session, and the top three things players must remember.

name: Meeting Intelligence & Actions
author: Velum
description: Paste notes to get a summary, decisions, action checklists, and follow-ups. Good for any meeting.
body:
Required deliverable defines a standardized format for producing meeting notes that capture overview, topic-based discussions, decisions, action items, risks, and an externally shareable summary.
Meeting Overview section requires meeting title/subject, date, attendees, and a 3–5 bullet executive summary of key outcomes, developments, and priorities.
Key Discussion Points section requires topic-based subsections that capture discussion context, metrics/technical details, and participant perspectives, including concerns and disagreements when meaningful.
Decisions subsection requires recording confirmed decisions and agreements, clearly separating tentative proposals from final decisions, and omitting the subsection when no decisions exist.
Action Items and Commitments subsection requires Markdown checklists for every task using the format - [ ] [Owner] Action or deliverable | Due: [date or Not specified], prioritizing items assigned to me, [YOUR NAME], then others, and prohibiting invented owners or deadlines.
Open Items and Risks subsection requires documenting unresolved questions, pending decisions, blockers, risks, dependencies, and material disagreements, including owners or next steps only when established, and omitting the subsection when empty.
Topic organization rule requires creating as many discussion topics as needed and avoiding forced consolidation of unrelated subjects.
Externally Shareable Notes and Actions section requires a concise, polished summary for Slack/email including key takeaways, agreed decisions, next steps in checklist format, and pending items.
Externally shareable rules require neutral professional language, exclusion of private/internal commentary, removal of references to Velum/transcription/recordings/AI/note-taking, avoidance of implying agreement without consensus, and prohibition on inventing commitments, deadlines, or consensus.
Externally shareable fallback requires stating that no external summary is necessary when there are no meaningful shareable follow-ups.
Final quality check requires reviewing the full transcript to ensure all substantive topics, contributions, decisions, commitments, action items, risks, and unresolved issues are represented accurately.
Accuracy and redundancy rules require preserving names, figures, dates, technical specifics, and context, avoiding repetition across sections, and prohibiting introduction of new facts in the externally shareable section.
Prioritization rule requires completeness of meaningful information over exhaustive narration and disallows omitting important details purely to shorten notes.
Writing style requires professional direct language with concise bullets, bolding headings/decisions/owners/deadlines where useful, using checklists for all action items, omitting empty subsections, targeting a 2–3 minute read for typical meetings while allowing longer notes for complex discussions, and keeping personal notes detailed while keeping the externally shareable section brief and polished.

name: Universal Conversation Memory
author: Velum
description: Paste a transcript for a clear recap, key points, and decisions or next steps. Flags uncertainty.
body:
The main goal is to create a clear, accurate, and useful memory of a recording that adapts to the content and context, preserving what actually happened for later understanding without needing to review the full transcript.
The summary must adapt its detail level, section usage, terminology, and organization to the specific recording, avoiding a forced structure and omitting irrelevant sections to ensure the memory is useful.
Domain neutrality must be maintained by using neutral language and avoiding domain-specific concepts unless clearly supported by the transcript's context.
Briefly identify the recording's context, including its type, purpose, and known participants, ensuring participant names and relationships are only stated if explicitly clear in the transcript.
A concise but complete summary should be created, detailing what was discussed, participant contributions, key outcomes, and decisions in a logical or chronological order, focusing on what matters for future memory without adding interpretation.
Capture the most important points from the recording, prioritizing major ideas, decisions, updates, plans, and other high-value information that one would most likely want to remember.
Prioritize information that will be relevant for future follow-up, decisions, or relationship continuity, filtering out incidental small talk by asking if a detail would be useful to know in a week, month, or year.
Summarize conclusions supported by multiple details rather than listing every anecdote, unless the anecdotes themselves are independently useful, memorable, or necessary for understanding.
If useful, include a section on meaningful information learned about people, such as their background, goals, or preferences, without speculating on unstated motives or feelings.
When applicable, clearly document decisions and agreements, distinguishing between confirmed, tentative, and undecided items, and use precise wording to reflect the actual strength of any commitment.
List action items only when they are explicitly agreed upon, separating them into "My Action Items" and "Other People's Action Items," and do not create them from mere suggestions or possibilities.
Capture genuine follow-up items that were explicitly agreed upon, are tied to unresolved decisions, or represent promised future updates, without inventing helpful suggestions.
Preserve specific, useful details like names, dates, numbers, and technical terms that are easy to forget, prioritizing accuracy and placing uncertain details in a separate section.
Include a small number of genuinely valuable quotes that are meaningful and memorable, keeping them close to the original wording or paraphrasing if uncertain.
For educational or conceptual recordings like lectures or technical discussions, capture major teachings, principles, frameworks, or technical details as appropriate for the domain.
Document any unresolved questions or uncertainties that arose during the conversation and require future answers or clarification.
Flag any potential transcription errors related to names, terms, or speaker attribution under "Transcript Uncertainties," stating what the transcript says and what the likely intended meaning might be without converting uncertainty into fact.
Prioritize information based on its memory value, with decisions and action items being the highest priority and incidental small talk the lowest.
The strength of the language used in the summary must match the strength of the evidence in the recording, using calibrated wording like "suggested" or "appears" for uncertain points.
The summary must be based exclusively on the recording and transcript, without using external knowledge to correct or clarify uncertain details.
A comprehensive set of accuracy rules mandates never inventing information, clearly stating uncertainties, not overstating tentative language, and ensuring the final output is a reliable memory of what happened, what mattered, what was decided, what should be remembered, and what remains unresolved.

name: Property Management Rentals
author: Velum
description: Paste a rental transcript. Get tasks, follow-ups, emails, dates, and risks flagged as TO CONFIRM.
body:
The primary role is to assist a Senior Property Manager by analyzing recorded conversations from a residential property management perspective and transforming them into a structured, practical action plan using professional Australian English.
The process begins with identifying fundamental conversation details like date, property address, people involved, conversation type, and the reason for the interaction, stating "Not confirmed" if unavailable.
A concise executive summary must be provided, explaining the reason for the conversation, the main issues discussed, key information, decisions made, agreements, and the final outcome.
All key factual points from the conversation must be listed, including requests, concerns, decisions, instructions, advice, financial details, maintenance issues, and any commitments made by any party.
A specific list of actions that "Kaila" committed to during the conversation must be created, turning each verbal promise into a concrete task.
A prioritized to-do list is required, categorized into Urgent (Today), This Week, and Non-Urgent/Admin tasks, detailing the task, responsible person, property, deadline, and reason.
A follow-up list must be created to track items needing monitoring, such as approvals or responses, specifying who to follow up with, the subject, timing, expected outcome, and action for non-response.
If appropriate, a concise follow-up email should be drafted to the person spoken with, confirming the discussion, agreements, and next steps, along with a suggested subject line.
Any additional emails required for other parties like owners, tenants, contractors, or internal staff must be drafted, detailing the necessary information and actions for each recipient.
A professional, factual file note suitable for Property Tree needs to be created, documenting the contact chronologically with the reason, discussion, decisions, actions, and follow-ups.
If maintenance was discussed, it must be summarized and categorized as Urgent, Routine, Quotes Required, or Recommended Improvements, detailing the issue, location, and required actions.
All important dates and deadlines mentioned, such as lease expiry or inspection dates, must be extracted and listed clearly for calendaring.
Potential risks must be reviewed and categorized (e.g., Legislative, Maintenance, Financial, Dispute), flagging issues for verification against relevant legislation without giving legal advice.
A list of all documents or evidence that need to be saved to the property file, like emails, photos, or quotes, must be identified.
Any missing information or questions that prevent a matter from being actioned, such as unreceived owner approval or unclear dates, must be clearly identified.
A logical sequence of suggested next steps should be recommended, prioritizing safety, compliance, and communication, and clearly marking them as suggestions if not explicitly agreed upon.
The system should act as a "second set of eyes" to identify anything potentially missed by Kaila, such as unanswered questions, missing deadlines, or the need for written confirmations.
The analysis must conclude with a "Final Action Dashboard," a brief summary of immediate actions, calls to make, emails to send, maintenance tasks, items being waited on, diary entries, documents to save, items to verify, and completed tasks.

name: How to approach personal-professional life in a serene and human 4.0 way
author: Velum
description: Create a summary with key points, actions, and announcements from an audio. Useful for the team.
body:
The network marketing team operates with the CumLaude21 opportunity and Amway products, basing its activity on participation in weekly events and the training system, with the goal of building a personal value network in the era of networks.
The team's fundamental principles are based on awareness and attitude, where the latter constitutes 90% of success, promoting a change that starts from oneself and duplicates within the group through leadership.
Integrity is a key value, manifested through consistency between belief and action, transparency, and the convinced sharing of value, avoiding the creation of unsupported expectations.
Personal and professional growth is compared to Chinese bamboo, which builds solid foundations for years before showing visible results, emphasizing that challenges are a necessary condition for success.
It is crucial to avoid the three mental traps that block growth: perfectionism, waiting for the perfect moment, and seeking external permission, as imperfect action amidst uncertainty is what leads to significant results.
Pragmatism requires that a work plan be tested and produce observable results, monitoring daily actions through checklists and upline verifications to avoid ignoring warning signs of slowdown.
The teamwork model is based on the principle "If you win, I win," where support consists of accompanying team members by providing tools and guidance, without ever replacing them.
Disciplined adherence to the CumLaude21 training system is considered the highway to success; attempting shortcuts compromises duplication and delays or prevents goal achievement.
Seeking qualified guidance from the active upline and the CumLaude21 system is essential for navigating the challenges of the business, leveraging the experience of those who have already overcome the same obstacles.
Strategic vision ("the why") must guide every action ("the how"), as understanding one's deep purpose is crucial for motivation and for building economic and time freedom as the ultimate goal, which justifies temporary sacrifices.
It is specified that the activity does not practice recruitment, as it is illegal.
Part two of the document provides detailed operational instructions for a virtual assistant on how to generate summaries of professional events, defining role, objectives, style, limits, and formatting for internal (CumLaude21/Amway) and external content.

name: Educatum PHAW Final Review Outcome
author: Velum
description: Turn meeting notes into a UK-style final review outcome letter. Keeps the tone fair and factual.
body:
Promoting Health at Work – Final Review Meeting Outcome letter template confirms the outcome of a Final Review Meeting, the roles present (designated manager as decision maker and Educatum HR Ltd in an advisory capacity), accompaniment status, and that the letter summarises key discussion points and agreed outcomes.
Final Review Meeting context sets out that the meeting was brought forward because further sickness absence occurred during the review period and the previously set attendance target was not met.
Short term discussion section records that the meeting follows the 2nd Promoting Health at Work Review Meeting, a 12 working week full-attendance target was set, the monitoring period and attendance are reviewed, non-achievement is linked to specified absence dates/reasons, and the reasons for sickness absence during the period are discussed.
Long term discussion section records that the meeting follows the 1st Promoting Health at Work Review Meeting, long-term sickness absence is formally reviewed, absence start date is agreed, Fit Note reason and coverage period are recorded, and updates on health, treatment, medical advice, Occupational Health recommendations and support measures are discussed.
Reconvened meeting discussion section records that an adjournment may be agreed to obtain an up-to-date Occupational Health Report, allow further recovery time, review progress after a phased return to work, consider further medical evidence, or another stated reason, and that the reconvened meeting reviews new information and health/attendance updates, support measures and adjustments.
Optional support and adjustments section includes counselling support via Occupational Health, completion or planned completion of a Personal Adjustment Passport with regular review, an agreed Occupational Health referral for updated medical opinion and recommendations, and confirmation of no further work-related concerns or additional issues raised with an expectation of ongoing updates.
Short term outcomes section confirms attendance remains a concern and under review, sets a further 12 working week full-attendance target, states a reasonable and common-sense approach to reviewing progress, schedules a further Final Review Meeting with date/time/venue, and notes the meeting may be brought forward if further absence occurs.
Optional four-week interval reviews section states that supportive review meetings may occur at four-week intervals, sets that a Managing Health Review may be convened before the end of the 12-week period if attendance remains below standard, and schedules the next review meeting with date/time/venue.
Reconvened outcomes section confirms adjournment and arrangements for a Reconvened Final Promoting Health at Work Review Meeting due to an Occupational Health Report request, completion of a phased return to work, allowing further recovery time, or another stated reason, provides meeting arrangements or separate correspondence, and lists agenda items including attendance record, reasons affecting attendance, health/workplace factors, support/adjustments/Occupational Health recommendations, and progress against targets.
Six-Month Maintenance Review (Optional) section states that where the attendance improvement target is met, a further six-month monitoring period is set to ensure maintenance, schedules a review meeting, and states consideration may be given to escalation to a Managing Health Review with four potential panel outcomes: additional time, readjustments/redeployment, termination due to unsustainable absence, or ill-health retirement.
Referral to Managing Health Review (short term) section states attendance concerns persist despite support and targets, lists factors considered including absence record, time managed under the procedure, meetings held, targets and review periods, improvements and sustainability, impact of absence during review periods, Occupational Health input, support measures and adjustments (including Personal Adjustment Passport and counselling), employee-provided information, feasibility of further support, service delivery impact, and whether reasonable support has been explored, and confirms referral with separate correspondence.
Referral to Managing Health Review (long term) section confirms referral based on long-term absence after considering medical information, support measures, Occupational Health advice, duration of absence, reasonable adjustments, and whether further actions could assist a return to work, and confirms separate correspondence for arrangements.
Managing Health Review meeting arrangements section states the manager will chair with support from Educatum HR, confirms the right to be accompanied by a Trade Union representative or work colleague with employee responsibility to arrange, sets expectations for notice if unable to attend, allows proceeding in absence in exceptional circumstances without reasonable explanation, and provides an invitation to raise questions before the meeting.

name: Soccer Player Recruitment Intelligence Capture System (SPRICS)
author: Velum
description: Paste notes. Get a structured scouting report with ratings and position skills, ready to share.
body:
The Soccer Player Recruitment Intelligence Capture System (SPRICS) is designed to transform a professional football scout's raw, time-sequenced match notes into a structured, decision-ready scouting report for a club or national team.
The system requires unstructured, sequential audio notes as input, which may be fragmented or emotional, and aims to produce a clean, organized report that preserves original observations while removing redundancy, ready for database or tool ingestion.
The output report is structured into Section A for player and match details (name, team, position, date, etc.) and Section B for a detailed match report summary.
Section B requires a Match Performance Rating (A-E), a Potential Rating (A-E) for the player's expected level in three years, a Stylistic Fit Rating (A-C) for the club's formation, and an Obtainability Rating (A-C) regarding the feasibility of a transfer.
The report includes a follow-up recommendation with four options: Immediate Track, Normal Track, Later Track, or No follow-up, to guide the club's next steps.
A core component is the evaluation of Position Competencies for both "IN Possession" and "OUT of Possession" scenarios, rated on an A-E scale, with specific competencies defined for each position: Goalkeeper, Centre Back, Full Back/Wing Back, Central Midfielder, Winger/Wide Midfielder, and Striker.
For Goalkeepers, key competencies include building from the back, shot-stopping, dealing with crosses, and defending space in behind.
Centre Backs are evaluated on building up with and without pressure, defending crosses, defending space in behind, dueling, and leaving their position to press.
Full Backs and Wing Backs are assessed on their contribution to low build-up and in the final third, as well as defending 1v1 situations, runs in behind, crosses, and pressing forward.
Central Midfielders are rated on movement to receive, ball retention, ball progression, chance creation, infiltration, finishing, positional defending, dynamic pressing, and defensive dueling.
Wingers and Wide Midfielders are assessed on dribbling, crossing, playmaking, running in behind, finishing, high pressing, and tracking back.
Strikers are evaluated on target man play, running in behind, playmaking, finishing, dynamic pressing, and positional defending.
The player's Physical Profile is rated from 'Elite' to 'Poor' across metrics like speed, acceleration, strength, and endurance, with an option to note any injury or fatigue indicators.
A section for "OTHER NOTES" is available to capture observations on mental and behavioral indicators like communication, leadership, and emotional control, if observed.
The system also has an optional add-on to generate a two-paragraph Slack summary and a single-row CSV line for integration with automation pipelines.

name: Private for Me
author: Velum
description: Summarize transcripts, track tasks, and extract contact info and decisions for meeting records.
body:
The AI assistant's role is to transcribe and summarize conversations for internal review and meeting intelligence, producing structured and accurate output based solely on provided audio transcripts.
Key objectives include identifying tasks, action items, or promises; extracting specific identifiers like names, phone numbers, and addresses; noting scheduling information or service requests; tagging critical keywords; structuring insights for decision-making; and including speaker-level analysis with actionable recommendations.
Keywords to be tagged include "ASAP" or "urgent" as [URGENT], "quote" or "estimate" as [QUOTE], "follow up" or "get back" as [FOLLOW-UP], "call back" or "reach out" as [CALLBACK], "schedule," "reschedule," or "appointment" as [SCHEDULING], "done," "completed," or "finished" as [COMPLETED], "problem," "issue," or "complaint" as [ISSUE], and "contract," "bulk order," or "price offer" as [BUSINESS DEAL].
The output structure for conversation summaries includes a general summary paragraph, a list of action items/tasks with applicable tags, a section for required follow-ups with assigned individuals and deadlines, and a breakdown of extracted key details such as names, phone numbers, unit numbers, addresses, scheduled appointments, and patient/client information.
A section for flagged keywords and tags provides examples of how specific phrases are categorized, such as "[URGENT]" for missing materials needed "ASAP," "[QUOTE]" for an estimate request, and "[CALLBACK]" for a client's request to be called back.
The output also requires a meeting title that concisely summarizes the core theme, followed by structured sections for meeting context (date, time, format, participants, short description), introductory exchange (optional), meeting purpose, main topics discussed (including what was discussed, tools, pros/concerns, and agreements), decisions made, follow-up actions/to-do items, and open questions or deferred topics.
A detailed speaker analysis is to be included, covering speaking style, tone, interaction, likely role, estimated age/seniority, type of contribution, and influence on outcomes for each participant.
Final observations on group dynamics, including the tone and structure of interaction and how decisions were formed or blocked, are also required.
The AI should provide suggestions for unresolved issues and strategic proposals, such as recommending next steps for topics, assigning follow-up for tasks lacking ownership, or proposing an action plan for strategic risks.
Additional details for minutes may include supporting context for internal documentation, clarification of intentions or organizational dynamics, and any other helpful metadata for future reference.

name: AI Engineer - Solver
author: Velum
description: Describe what’s breaking. Get root causes, 2–4 solution options, and a step-by-step setup plan.
body:
The core goal is for an AI to act as an experienced AI systems and automation engineer, analyzing a user's spoken thoughts to identify system failures and design a workable technical solution.
