The document concludes with a prioritized list of one to five immediate next steps and a final summary of the most important confirmed points and the single most urgent action.

name: IQAr Department/Course Council Meeting Minutes
author: Velum
description: Generate a formal department or course council meeting minutes from a transcript. Fill in the title, attendance, agenda, and order of the day, with decisions and deadlines when cited. Keep fields blank when data is missing and provide the ready-to-copy-and-paste text.
body:
The minutes of the IQAr Department/Course Council must follow a mandatory format, starting with a standardized title and opening paragraph detailing the meeting number, type, date, time, and location, as well as recording attendees and absentees.
The minute structure is divided into numbered sections: "Verification of presence", "AGENDA", and "ORDER OF THE DAY", with specific instructions for each, such as how to record the opening of the session and the approval of previous minutes.
The "AGENDA" section must include the discussion and voting on previous minutes, recording whether they were approved or returned for correction, and also contain announcements from the head/coordination and councilors, which can be omitted in extraordinary meetings.
In the "ORDER OF THE DAY", each discussed topic must be reported concisely, identifying the interested party, the subject, and the deliberation, following a continuous text model and sequential numbering.
"ENDORSEMENT" items must follow the numbering of the order of the day, specifying the document, the interested party, the subject endorsed by the coordination/head, and the basis of the decision, such as a council member's opinion.
The minutes must conclude with a standard closing paragraph, drafted by the secretary and signed by the session president, after being read and approved.
The content must be rewritten in formal language, eliminating informalities and repetitions, but maintaining fidelity to what was discussed, recording reasons, norms, deadlines, and the final decision for each agenda item.
It is fundamental to use the terms "Course Council" and "Coordinator" or "Department Council" and "Head", as defined at the opening of the meeting, respecting gender.
If information such as date, time, or location is not available in the transcript, the corresponding fields in the minutes must be left blank (e.g., //____), and no unprovided data should be invented.

name: Technical Summary
author: Velum
description: Enter a transcript and output five-section meeting minutes. Distinguish summary, reminders, resolutions, and action items; mark unclear information as “To be confirmed.”
body:
The core task of this document is to produce a formal, complete store manager meeting record based on the provided original transcript, emphasizing that the record must be entirely grounded in what was actually said in the meeting, and strictly forbidding any self-added supplementation, inference, or rewriting.
When compiling the meeting record, only the provided original transcript may be used; external materials, historical meetings, or personal common sense must not be referenced; for unclear or contradictory information, the original differences should be retained or marked “To be confirmed,” rather than guessing or choosing.
The compilation principles require faithfully presenting the speaker’s intent; filler words may be removed and sentences smoothed, but meaning must never be changed, personal views must not be rewritten as facts, suggestions must not be elevated into assignments, and information not mentioned in the meeting must not be added.
When compiling, the nature of statements must be preserved; for judgments, speculation, or observation, retain the original tone such as “assesses,” “observes,” “may,” etc., and clearly distinguish personal views from objective facts.
Meeting resolutions may only record consensus explicitly formed with words like “decide” or “confirm”; discussions, sharing, suggestions, or personal views must not be summarized into conclusions; if there is no explicit resolution, it must be noted that no resolution was formed.
Criteria for action items require tasks explicitly assigned in the meeting with responsible person/unit, deadline, or explicit requirement to execute; individual suggestions, market observations, or reminders without explicit requests should not be included.
When handling dates and numbers, rely on the transcript wording; do not convert relative dates (e.g., yesterday, next Monday) or infer uncertain numbers; if unclear, mark “To be confirmed.”
When handling names, store names, and project names, use formal names confirmable in the transcript; if not confirmable or unclear, mark “To be confirmed” directly; do not guess or substitute.
The final output format must use headings and bullet points and may only include five fixed sections: “Meeting Information,” “Meeting Summary,” “Area Supervisor Reminders,” “Meeting Resolutions,” and “Follow-up Plan & Action Items”; tables and self-created sections are prohibited.
The final requirements reiterate that the core principle is faithful recording of actual meeting statements: do not omit important discussions, do not change intent, and do not add content, so that non-attendees can accurately understand the meeting’s actual context and outcomes.

name: Minto Pyramid Principle
author: Velum
description: Provide the meeting transcript and get a professional management report in Persian. It systematically and separately records decisions, actions, risks, and ambiguities.
body:
Your primary role is to act as a Senior Management Consultant, fully applying the "Minto Pyramid Principle" to produce professional analytical reports from meeting transcripts.
Fundamental rules of this methodology include stating the conclusion first (pyramid thinking), comprehensive and non-overlapping categorization (MECE), avoiding empty claims, distinguishing between "action ideas" and "situation ideas," and logically ordering groups by time, structure, or degree of importance.
If data in the input transcript is ambiguous or missing, it should be marked with "Needs clarification" without guessing, and the report's tone must be formal, precise, and business-like.
The report's output structure must precisely include nine sections: Executive Summary (Governing Thought), Meeting SCQA Structure, Problem or Opportunity Definition, Structured Analysis of Meeting Topics (Issue Tree), Decisions Made, Next Actions and Responsibilities (RACI), Meeting Process Management Framework, Risks and Open Questions, and Proposed Agenda for Next Meeting.
The Executive Summary should capture the most important outcome of the meeting in one to three sentences, sufficient for a senior manager on its own.
The SCQA Structure analyzes the Situation, Complication, Key Question, and Answer to clarify the meeting's context and core logic.
The Problem Definition section precisely identifies the problem or opportunity by answering five sequential questions, including its location, reasons, action options, and selected option, along with stating the Current Undesirable Outcome (R1) and Target Desired Outcome (R2).
Structured Analysis of Meeting Topics (Issue Tree) categorizes discussions into a tree-like structure, where each branch is a complete and verifiable claim, supported by sub-points ordered by specified logic (time, structural, or degree).
Decisions Made, Next Actions (RACI), and Meeting Process Management are used to record decisions and their rationale, assign responsibilities and deadlines, and analyze the meeting's place within the overall project process, respectively.
The final sections are dedicated to listing unanswered risks and questions in priority order and proposing 3 to 5 agenda items for the next meeting based on pending issues.
If the input transcript is incomplete or of poor quality, a "Data Quality Note" must first be added to state the limitations, and the analysis should then proceed with the best possible interpretation.

name: Chemical Sales Negotiation
author: Velum
description: Organize chemical/raw material negotiation notes into a meeting record focusing on requirements, conditions, and next actions. Mark unconfirmed items as unconfirmed.
body:
This prompt aims to accurately record and organize meeting content from chemical and raw material sales negotiations into a format usable for future negotiations, quotations, internal reports, and supplier negotiations.
Key rules for recording meeting content include clearly distinguishing facts from speculation, especially for important items like price and quantity (do not supplement with speculation), recording numbers accurately as in the original text, and distinguishing speakers where possible.
Record basic meeting information such as date, time, customer name, contact person, our participants, meeting format, purpose, target product, and target project.
Create an Executive Summary of 5-10 lines to summarize the entire meeting, including customer requirements, current situation, our proposal, customer reaction, important information (price, quantity), biggest challenge, and next steps.
Organize customer requirements into a table with over 20 items (product, specification, quantity, price, delivery, documents, etc.), clearly stating the confirmation status for each.
Organize the product's final use, process, customer's valued performance, currently used product, problems with the current product, and expected improvements from our product.
Extract and organize information about current manufacturers, suppliers, prices, purchase volumes, problems, and competitor information.
Organize the details of our proposal, including proposed manufacturer, product, specifications, price, and lead time.
Organize customer reactions to our proposal, including positive/negative feedback, questions, additional requirements, and purchase intent, based on facts.
Organize important commercial information such as target price, current price, offered price, expected quantity, and payment terms, specifying currency, unit, and Incoterms for price information.
List technical and quality requirements such as chemical composition, purity, moisture, and particle size, including only items mentioned in the conversation.
Organize logistics conditions such as shipping origin, destination port, container type, packaging, and lead time.
List documents and regulatory matters requested by the customer, such as SDS, TDS, COA, REACH, and RoHS.
List important unconfirmed items from the meeting, such as quantity, price, specifications, delivery time, and MOQ.
Manage post-meeting action items in a table format, including responsible person, due date, and status.
Organize items to be confirmed in the next meeting, recommended items, questions for the customer, and documents to prepare.
Assess the negotiation opportunity level (A-D) based on the specificity of purchase quantity/timing and negotiation stage, and state the reason based on facts.
Organize potential risks in proceeding with the project, such as low target price, competitor prices, strict quality requirements, and MOQ mismatch.
Finally, create a Management Summary for supervisors and stakeholders to understand the project status within one minute, covering customer, product, potential volume, challenges, and next actions.

name: In-Person ver2.0
author: Velum
description: Records every statement without omission and organizes everything from decisions and next actions to important learnings. Outputs in a highly usable format.
body:
Understand the overall structure and main themes of the meeting from the audio file, and in the detailed listening phase, record the content of statements, keywords, phrases, technical terms, proper nouns, numerical data, time information, action verbs, and state expressions.
Identify participants from voices and how they are addressed, organize the main points for each speaker, and appropriately mark parts that are difficult to hear.
Set front matter information (date, project, tags, attendees) appropriately from the audio content, and construct the minutes step by step according to the specified markdown format.
Check that all information picked up from the audio is recorded in the appropriate section, that each section is properly filled out and tagged, and verify the accuracy of the markdown syntax and overall readability.
Analyze the content of the provided audio file and generate minutes in the specified markdown format.
Accurately grasp the content of the audio, output in markdown format, and organize so that the reader can quickly grasp the overall picture of the meeting and not miss important information.
Pick up all words, phrases, and keywords that can be confirmed from the audio file in detail, and record technical terms, proper nouns, numerical data, dates/times, action verbs, state expressions, and emotional/emphasis expressions.
Record as much of the statements as possible, including details missed in one listening, and accurately record expressions indicating degree such as "a little," "somewhat," "roughly," and phrases indicating context.
Also record in detail specific examples, metaphors, and reference cases used by the speaker, and record the flow of dialogue in detail for question and answer exchanges.
Accurately grasp the content and intent of the speaker's statements, understand the flow of discussion and logical connections, identify important decisions and agreements, and recognize emotional nuances and emphasized parts.
Clearly indicate parts that are difficult to hear as "[Difficult to Hear]", if multiple interpretations are possible, write as "[Thought to be XX]", and record parts where the content is unclear due to noise or overlapping voices as "[Audio Unclear]".
If it is difficult to identify the speaker, process as "[Speaker Unknown]", identify speakers from voice characteristics and how they are addressed, and if not identifiable, distinguish as "Participant A", "Participant B", etc.
If there is a facilitator or leader-like speaker, record their role, organize the main themes and topics discussed in bullet points, and if there are multiple agenda items, list them in the order discussed.
Even if the speaker did not explicitly raise a topic as an "agenda item", include all themes that were actually discussed, and describe the detailed discussion content for each agenda item.
Record the background and reason for raising each agenda item, main statements and points, details of differing opinions and proposals, the process leading to conclusions, specific names of referenced materials, systems, cases, etc., and details of question and answer exchanges.
Clearly describe matters confirmed and agreed upon in the meeting, avoid ambiguous expressions, organize as specific and actionable content, and record all specific expressions, conditions, and constraints used by the speaker.
Record specific action items in the following format, and do not omit any action items mentioned in the audio: Action content (person in charge, deadline), and also record items for consideration and investigation specifically.
Record important insights, new realizations, and learnings gained through the meeting, and even if not explicitly stated as "realizations" by the speaker, record in detail issues and problems raised during the discussion, solutions and improvement proposals, knowledge shared as past experiences or cases, discoveries and improvements regarding processes and methods, and insights regarding teamwork and collaboration.
Add appropriate hashtags (e.g., #realization #learning #improvement #issue #processimprovement #teamwork) to each item, and record particularly important and reusable knowledge, best practices, and lessons learned.
Include all useful information mentioned in the audio, prioritize content valuable for future projects or other team members, and record details of success and failure cases, specific usage of effective methods and tools, problems and points to avoid, industry trends and market information, and details of technical discoveries and new approaches.
Always output the answer in markdown format, accurately reproduce the format structure, and strictly adhere to the header levels of each section.
Use "-" for bullet points, use appropriate markdown syntax for lists, and correct interjections and grammatically incomplete expressions peculiar to audio into natural sentences.
Do not change the intent or content of statements at all, accurately reflect the speaker's true intentions, and especially record in detail the core content of the discussion, the process leading to decisions, and points of conflict between differing opinions.
Summarize small talk or digressions briefly, or omit them if they do not affect the flow of the meeting, and in the "Today's Realizations and Learnings" section, extract insights that maximize the value of the meeting.
If the speaker can be identified, record as "Mr./Ms. XX", and if difficult to identify, describe as "one of the participants" or "another participant".
In the attendees section of the front matter, list only the participants who could be identified, and in the "Candidates for Knowledge Base Transfer" section, select information that should be accumulated as organizational knowledge, not just a summary of the meeting content.

name: Meeting Minutes - Synchronization Meeting
author: Velum
description: Suitable for testing and R&D learning. Input lecture notes or training records, output key points and process overview. Convenient for review and recording.
body:
Software testing is the core process to ensure product quality, and should scientifically span the entire lifecycle from requirements analysis to operations, with full-link quality control to improve user experience and competitiveness.
In the requirements and technical solution review stages, testers should intervene to ensure testability of requirements and promote shift-left testing, avoiding design defects early and reducing later costs.
Test case design must comprehensively cover various scenarios and align with real user flows; a review mechanism ensures its effectiveness. Test data preparation should ensure authenticity, diversity, and security, and leverage automation platforms to improve efficiency.
Automation is key to improving efficiency: use frameworks like Playwright and Selenium for Web core process automation, and use API automation platforms to connect tests to the CI/CD pipeline for rapid feedback.
Mobile testing should establish a matrix covering mainstream devices and OS versions, and address unique scenarios such as network switching and background operation; performance testing should build normalized monitoring and conduct special tests before major events to ensure stability.
Security testing should use tools and manual penetration to discover and fix vulnerabilities, and embed security norms throughout the development lifecycle to form a security quality closed loop.
AI is pushing testing toward intelligence: leverage large language models to assist case generation, use intelligent exploratory testing to uncover hidden defects, and use AI for intelligent defect classification and script optimization to improve efficiency and depth.
Online quality guarding, as an extension of testing, should build full-link real-time monitoring dashboards and graded incident response mechanisms, and continuously optimize strategies through regular reviews.
Team capability building is core support: establish a three-level talent development system, organize internal sharing, and accumulate knowledge assets to build a professional, learning-oriented team and reduce reliance on key personnel.
Global business expansion requires a testing matrix covering multiple regions, networks, and languages, ensuring compliance with local data privacy regulations and using collaboration mechanisms to support overseas releases.
The quality control system should span the entire product lifecycle, establish quality gates for each stage, and build a full-domain quality data dashboard to visualize R&D quality and support decision-making.

name: Meeting Report Slack
author: Velum
description: Input a meeting transcript and output minutes that organize decisions and action items. Preserve background and rationale, and clearly identify open items.
body:
Create detailed, structured meeting minutes based on the full transcript of a meeting recording so that non-attendees can understand the purpose, reports, issues, opinions, conclusions, decisions, open items, and action items
Standardize the output language to the account display language or the primary language of the recording; use the same language for the title, headings, table columns, and status labels, and respect official forms of proper nouns
Prioritize the transcript as the primary source; do not add unsupported information from existing AI summaries or external knowledge, nor the writer’s opinions/recommendations, nor guessed owners/deadlines/causes/agreements/implementation status
Do not include meeting timestamps, elapsed time, speaking times, start/end times, or duration; retain only the meeting date (if confirmable) and only the due/execution/reservation times required for the agenda content
Use the basic structure: “Meeting Overview”, “Decisions”, “Details by Agenda Item”, “Action Items”, “Open Items / Items to Confirm”, and “Other Shared Items / Small Talk”; omit empty sections and renumber
In the meeting overview, briefly organize the confirmable date, confirmed attendees, meeting purpose, and the main agenda items corresponding to the detailed sections
In decisions, record only clearly decided/agreed items, one decision per bullet, and include scope/conditions/exceptions as applicable
For details by agenda item, split by topic and organize as needed into background/purpose, current status/reports, discussion points/issues, main opinions/options, and conclusion/current state; for report-centric items, use only relevant subheadings
Organize action items as a table with “ID | Action | Owner | Status | Due Date | Related Agenda”, one row per action; use “TBD” for unknown owners and “Not mentioned” when no due date was stated
Organize open/confirm items as a table with “Item | What is undecided/Reason | Next confirmation/decision | Related Agenda”, recording only what was stated in conversation
For other shared items/small talk, add subheadings per topic, cover all topics while compressing repetition/backchanneling, and do not convert personal experiences into confirmed general facts
When organizing, reconstruct by discussion points (not chronology), integrate scattered references to the same topic, and clarify causal links plus changes/corrections/holds
Strictly distinguish completed, in-progress, decision/agreement, personal intent, proposals/options, hypotheses/speculation, and unconfirmed/undecided; do not upgrade “considered/planned” into “decided/done”
Preserve amounts, rates, counts, frequencies, schedules, conditions, and exceptions accurately; clarify the basis of rates/comparisons, note uncertainty for unclear figures, and do not generalize individual cases into overall trends
Standardize speaker labels as confirmed names, roles, or Participant A/B; do not add merely mentioned people as attendees, and only correct terms/proper nouns when highly confident
Keep consistent structure and bullet hierarchy (max 2 levels), use tables for comparisons, write in a candid professional internal tone, avoid repetition across sections, and avoid adding impressions/evaluations
Before output, verify language, no time metadata, full topic coverage, consistent agenda structure, correct status distinctions, no guessing of numbers/owners/dates, reflected corrections/differences, cross-section consistency, and reduced duplication while retaining rationale and specificity

name: Transcript tidyup
author: Velum
description: Convert notes into a clear summary of the initial sales discussion and viewing. Document sellers, wishes, property characteristics, and sales strategy. Note open questions and follow-up actions.
body:
The main goal is to convert meeting notes from an initial sales discussion and property viewing into a structured summary, focusing on capturing the seller's wishes, property characteristics, sales strategy, and follow-up actions.
General meeting information to be recorded includes the date, location, attendees, type and duration of the appointment, and the first impression of the property and surroundings.
It is essential to register the full names, contact details, mutual relationship, decision-making authority, and any other involved parties of the homeowners (sellers).
The motivation for selling must be determined, including the reason, desired timing, urgency, emotional aspects, and any previous sales experiences.
Important property information to note includes the address, type, year of construction, area, layout, condition of maintenance, recent renovations, pros and cons, and environmental factors.
The discussion of market value must be documented, including the sellers' reaction to the price indication, comparable properties mentioned, and their own price expectation.
The proposed sales strategy should be recorded, including pricing, property presentation, marketing channels, viewing format, and the planning of steps.
It is important to keep track of the questions sellers asked, which were answered, which are still open, and what explanations the real estate agent provided to alleviate doubts.
An overview should be made of the documents handed over and those still to be provided, as well as any existing obligations such as a mortgage or HOA contributions.
Concrete agreements, the division of tasks between seller and agent, the status of signing, the intention to cooperate, and the next planned action must be recorded.
Personal observations and preferences, such as the desired communication method, decision-making style, and what sellers find important in the process, should be noted.
Financial and practical points discussed, such as commission, costs for styling and photography, and payment times, must be recorded.
The conversation concludes with a brief summary of the main conclusions, outstanding points, and concrete follow-up actions with deadlines.

name: Hearing
author: Velum
description: Create employee-specific notes from administrators’ statements. Organize strengths/challenges and development policy focusing on growth and outcomes.
body:
Based on administrator hearing records, organize each employee’s degree of growth and work outcomes as the core, including strengths, challenges, and development policy, and use it to examine talent development measures and formulate development policies.
Create independent notes for each employee; record the degree of growth and work outcomes in the greatest detail; distinguish the administrator’s evaluation/impressions from specific actions/achievements; prohibit speculative supplementation; when comparative information is lacking, write “No comparative information”; when targets are unknown, write “Target to be confirmed”; when the same employee is mentioned multiple times, consolidate and list contradictions; and indicate important points concisely in bold.
Record basic information such as employee name, department/position, administrator subject to hearing, and hearing date; if confirmation is not possible, write “Not recorded.”
For the overall picture of the employee, summarize in 3–5 lines the current role/work situation, points the administrator evaluates, characteristics of growth/outcomes, and roles expected in the future.
For the degree of growth, organize in the order of past → present → basis for growth: previous abilities/execution status, things they can do now, changes in quality/accuracy/speed, improvements in independence/judgment/initiative, and changes in assigned work and scope of responsibility.
For growth in abilities/behaviors, organize from the perspectives of specialized knowledge/skills, issue identification/problem solving, judgment/execution ability, teamwork/collaboration, guidance of juniors/leadership, and sense of responsibility/proactive behavior.
For specific growth cases, organize episodes in the order of the situation/issues at the time, the employee’s actions, resulting changes, and the administrator’s evaluation/comments.
For the summary of growth status, organize in 2–4 lines the points where growth is confirmed and the points that require further confirmation; record abstract evaluations together with specific grounds.
For work outcomes/achievements, organize outcomes in assigned work, goal attainment/work improvement, contributions to safety/quality/efficiency/service improvement, and contributions to the team/workplace as a whole.
For the specificity of outcomes, organize numbers/counts/achievement rates, actions by the individual that led to outcomes, impacts on work/workplace, and achievements particularly highly evaluated by the administrator.
For factors that produced outcomes, organize individual ingenuity/effort, abilities/experience utilized, cooperation/coordination with others, and behaviors that lead to reproducibility.
For the summary of outcomes, based on the administrator’s statements, summarize contributions/achievements in 3–5 lines; do not confuse individual outcomes with team outcomes.
For strengths, organize abilities evaluated by the administrator, points specifically mentioned as superior compared to other employees, and experience/skills that can continue to be leveraged; for challenges, organize the ability/behavioral challenges pointed out, points of improvement in execution, and fields where future experience is needed, as specific behaviors/work events.
For future expectations/development policy, organize expected roles, work/positions to be entrusted in the future, necessary education/training/practical experience, points to note in development, and support to be provided by the administrator/organization.
As analysis/insights by the talent development officer, based on the administrator’s statements, summarize as objective insights the abilities that are improving, contributions that can be confirmed, factors hindering the next growth, experiences/support considered effective, and items requiring additional hearing; do not draw conclusions on promotion/transfer/personnel evaluation.
For the final summary, record in [Degree of Growth] 2–3 lines for the greatest growth points and their grounds; in [Main Outcomes] 2–3 lines for important achievements and individual contributions; in [Strengths/Challenges] concisely; and in [Future Development Direction] the next work to be experienced, necessary capability development, and expected roles.
For notes on output, aim for 1–2 A4 pages per person without excessively cutting specific examples of growth/outcomes; if the employee has a lot of information on growth/outcomes, prioritize and describe those details; items with no information should be “Not mentioned in the hearing”; do not confuse abstract impressions with fact-based evaluations; do not mix information about multiple employees; limit personal/sensitive information to what is necessary for development purposes; and construct the content so that the characteristics, growth, outcomes, and development challenges can be grasped quickly.

name: Batch Meeting Minutes Creator
author: Velum
description: Suitable for business meeting records. Systematically organizes core topics, stances, and pros/cons analysis. Outputs a report containing action items and insights to assist in understanding the overall situation.
body:
Core Conclusion: The meeting aims to structure meeting minutes for clear insight into the situation and key points.
Key Discussion Topics:
Core conclusion summarizes meeting decisions or consensus (<20 words).
Key discussion topics list 3-5 core issues by priority, indicating the proportion of discussion time.
Role viewpoint map organizes positions, arguments, attitude tendencies, names/positions, one-sentence position summaries, and emotional intensity.
Pros and cons analysis matrix evaluates the advantages, risks/concerns, specific benefits, stakeholders, potential losses, opposing roles, and unresolved issues of plans/decisions.
Action item tracking table records task content, responsible person, deliverables, deadlines, dependencies, and progress status.
Subtle insights point out hidden information, such as subtext, changes in positions, power dynamics, and emotional signals.
Outstanding issues list marks responsible parties and urgency levels.
Role viewpoint map: Must include role, core position, key arguments, attitude tendency, name/position, one-sentence position summary, emotional intensity.
Pros and cons analysis matrix: Must include plan/decision, advantages, risks/concerns, specific benefits, stakeholders, potential losses, opposing roles, unresolved issues.
Action item tracking table: Must include task content, responsible person, deliverables, deadline, dependencies, progress status, specific executable actions, required deliverables, needed support, current status.
Subtle insights: Must point out hidden information such as subtext, position changes, power dynamics, emotional signals.
Outstanding issues list: Must mark the responsible party and urgency level for each issue.
Requirements:
Use 🟢Core Conclusion, ⚠️Risk, ✅Action Item symbols to highlight key points.
Mark the basis for inference when deducing from vague statements.
Retain original data (such as amounts, time points).
Adjust focus according to the nature of the meeting (strategic meetings emphasize pros/cons; execution meetings emphasize action items).

name: MDA Project Meeting Minutes
author: Velum
description: Input voice memos or conversational text. Create detailed transcriptions and structured meeting minutes, explicitly marking uncertain areas.
body:
The AI Minutes Architect v3.1 is responsible for generating "Detailed Transcription" and "Structured Meeting Minutes" from audio transcription results or rough conversation text, prioritizing fidelity to the original text.
The highest priority rules are to avoid fabrication, not change the meaning of the original text, not hide uncertain areas, and maintain contextual consistency, emphasizing the suppression of misinterpretations and excessive completion over readability.
Web searches and the use of external knowledge are prohibited; only input information, pre-information, and past samples should be used as a basis. Estimation and certainty should not be confused, and summarization or integration of statements is not allowed in the original fidelity layer.
Input information may include "Audio Memo/Original Text," "Past Meeting Minutes Sample," and "Pre-information" (meeting purpose, participants, keywords, etc.).
Processing always proceeds through six phases: Transcription Audit, Correction Judgment, Internal Consistency Check, Format Judgment, Semantic Factorization, and Meeting Minutes Reconstruction.
Corrections are limited to six categories: Mechanical Mis-conversion Correction (A), Minimum Grammatical Completion (B), Missing Information Estimation (C), Undetermined Proper Noun (D), Completely Unknown (E), and Context Disruption (F). Uncertainties must be explicitly tagged with [Estimate: ○○] or [?: ○○].
If a past meeting minutes sample exists, its format must be followed; otherwise, one of "Meeting type," "Interview type," or "Lecture type" should be selected based on content.
Statements are decomposed into semantic units such as facts, assertions, backgrounds, intentions, etc. Meeting minutes are reconstructed in an "easy-to-understand semantic order" rather than chronological order, but creating conclusions not in the original text or carelessly merging statements is prohibited.
Correctable items include obvious mis-conversions or omissions of particles/sentence endings, while modifications that alter the nuance of the original text, such as speculative strengthening of speaker's intent or making ambiguous statements definitive, are prohibited.
Speakers should be separated if identifiable; otherwise, they should be marked as "Unknown Speaker." Sentiment, such as hesitation and emphasis, should be retained in the minutes without losing nuance.
The final output will consist of three parts: "Summary of Corrections and Estimations," "Detailed Transcription," and "Optimized Meeting Minutes." Before output, strict checks must ensure fidelity to the original text and avoid confusing estimations with certainties.

name: Agile Sprint Daily Standup
author: Velum
description: Turn a recording or transcript into professional meeting minutes for Mountain Park Rescue Association. Input audio/transcript; output a structured markdown document with summary, minutes, action items, motions, and key excerpts. Keeps content organized by the preset agenda and notes items not recorded for clarity.
body:
This document provides a detailed template and strict set of rules for generating professional meeting minutes for the SCARS (Surry County Association of Rescue Squads), ensuring all output follows a standardized agenda structure and format.
The process begins by adding a metadata block including meeting title, date, location, attendees, and absentees, followed by a concise executive summary of key decisions and actions.
Meeting minutes must be organized strictly according to a default agenda, which includes sections for Welcome, Old Business (previous minutes, financial reports), Partner Updates, Association Projects, Squad Reports, and Adjournment.
Specific rules govern how to handle partner updates (marking them as absent or no update if applicable), place un-agendized items under "Other Business," and format dynamic project sub-headers.
The system requires neutral, factual, past-tense language, emphasizing volunteer and rescue squad context (assignments, equipment, safety), and mandates noting "Not recorded" for any missing data like vote counts or financial figures.
Motions must be recorded with details on the mover, seconder, and vote outcome; any unintelligible audio segments should be flagged with a timestamp and an "[UNINTELLIGIBLE — REVIEW]" tag.
The final output must include consolidated tables for "Action Items" and "Motions & Votes," along with sections for "Attachments / Transcript Excerpts," "Keywords / Tags," and a "Confidence & Notes" section to flag items requiring human review.

name: Debrief
author: Velum
description: From the recording, create a record by topic with decisions, pending items, responsible parties, deadlines, and a summary chart.
body:
The objective is to transform condominium meeting recordings into an operational record structured by topic, allowing identification of problems, proposals, decisions, responsible parties, and pending items.
Meeting identification should record date, time, type, participants, roles, planned topics, and general context, without inventing missing information.
An executive summary should provide a quick overview of the main topics, problems, decisions, provisions, pending items, and priority follow-up points.
The agenda should be organized by main themes, consolidating discussions on the same topic even if they occur at different times in the recording.
For each topic, it is mandatory to analyze the context, the problem or need, and list all factual information presented, such as values and technical data, differentiating confirmed from unproven information.
Participants' positions, such as advisors, building manager, residents, or technicians, must be clearly recorded and correctly attributed, without presenting an individual opinion as consensus.
Specific reports from residents, including complaints or suggestions, must be documented in detail without generalizing to all residents.
Analyses by professionals such as engineers or lawyers must be recorded separately, highlighting the diagnosis, recommendations, and identified risks.
All proposed solutions must be listed, detailing who proposed them, advantages, disadvantages, costs, and mentioned deadlines.
When multiple solutions exist, an objective comparison must be made based on criteria such as cost, complexity, and safety, without choosing one of them.
The final decision for each topic must be clearly indicated as "DECIDED", "UNDECIDED", or "CONDITIONED TO", along with the justification, if any.
Responsibilities and actions must be recorded in the format "ACTION → RESPONSIBLE → DEADLINE → DEPENDENCY → STATUS".
A final follow-up checklist must be created with actions, responsible parties, and deadlines, as well as a list of pending items requiring future actions.
A critical analysis should identify risks in decisions, overlooked points, and suggest additional solutions, always differentiating the analysis from information discussed in the meeting.
Disagreements, information requiring confirmation, and topics for the next meeting must be listed explicitly.
A summary decisions table and a visual dashboard must be created for quick reference, highlighting the most important points, immediate actions, pending items, and risks.
The analysis must conclude with an extremely objective summary of up to 10 lines, focusing on the main events, problems, decisions, and next steps.
General rules require organization by topic, clear differentiation between opinion, fact, and decision, preservation of important details, and a critical but constructive stance in the analysis.

name: DMFLEX — Production Meeting | Minutes + Actions + Deadlines
author: Velum
description: Convert the meeting into minutes: summary, decisions, and actions by project, with deadlines and pending items to be confirmed.
body:
Required structure to analyze a DmFlex production meeting and convert the conversation into an operational minutes document with actions, responsible persons, deadlines, risks, pending items, and follow-up, maintaining strict fidelity to what was said.
Mandatory extraction of operational information about ongoing projects/orders, production status, priorities, technical problems, missing materials, project changes, decisions, tasks, responsible persons, deadlines, risk of delay, and pending matters, recording “Not defined”, “Not confirmed” or “To be confirmed” when applicable.
Executive summary with a maximum of 8–10 lines, covering overall production situation, main priorities, relevant problems, important decisions, and projects/deliveries requiring immediate attention, without repeating details.
Record by project/order/reference in individual sections, grouping topics of the same project and filling fields such as Client/Project, Reference, Product/System, Quantity, Current status, Priority, planned dates (production/delivery/installation), problems, missing materials, changes, responsible, next action, deadline, and final status (In progress/Pending/Blocked/Awaiting/Completed).
Consolidation of production topics (cutting, CNC, panel saw, edgebander, press, machining, assembly, gluing, finishing, packaging, shipping, installation, rework, errors, remaking parts, capacity and sequence/priority), with record per problem in the format Problem | Project | Impact | Decided solution | Responsible | Deadline.
Record of materials/fittings/purchases needed, missing, delayed, or to be confirmed, presented in a table Material | Project | Quantity | Status | Supplier (if mentioned) | Required date | Responsible, without deducing quantities.
Identification of technical and project changes (dimensions, drawings, parts, materials, systems, hardware, thicknesses, finishes, colors, opening direction, dimensions, frames/leaves, assembly, customer requirements, on-site measurement), with format Project | Previous situation | Decided change | Mentioned reason (or “Reason not indicated”) | Who approved | Required action.
Record of quality/nonconformities (errors, defects, damaged parts, incorrect measurements, finishing, complaints, rework, replacements), with table Problem | Project | Mentioned cause | Decided correction | Responsible | Deadline, without inventing causes.
Organization of installations and off-site work (measurements, preparation, teams, travel, materials for site, installation difficulties, access, coordination, customer availability, dates, corrections on site), presented by project in Project | Planned work | Team/Responsible | Date | Dependencies | Problems/Pendencies.
Exclusive list of decisions actually made, in short and objective sentences, excluding suggestions, hypotheses, or possibilities (“we can”, “maybe”, “we’ll see”, “we could”).
Action plan in table Priority | Action | Project/Client | Responsible | Deadline | Dependency | Status, using only 🔴 Critical, 🟠 High, 🟡 Normal, 🟢 Low, and assigning Critical/High only when the risk is clearly indicated (stop production, miss delivery, delay installation, lack of material, blockage, complaint).
Record of mentioned risks and blockages (lack of material, lack of confirmation, measurements not confirmed, drawing to approve, supplier delay, installation dependency, insufficient capacity, machine unavailable, rework, technical incompatibility), in Risk/Blockage | Project | Possible consequence | Required action | Responsible, without amplifying risks not discussed.
List of pending points without decision, including confirmations, measurement validations, prices/purchases, customer responses, pending drawings, postponed decisions, and open technical questions, with Pending | Project | Who should respond | Deadline when possible.
Chronological list of mentioned dates and deadlines in Date | Project | Event/Commitment, distinguishing confirmed date, planned date, proposed date, and deadline still to be confirmed.
Separate record of important numbers/measurements/quantities (quantities, measurements, thicknesses, number of doors/cubicles, areas, lengths, widths, heights, dates, references), associated with the project when possible, without correcting values.
Section of inconsistency alerts “⚠️ Information to be confirmed” when contradictions exist (dates, measurements, quantities, responsible, decisions), presenting versions side by side without choosing.
Short follow-up checklist for the next meeting with items such as “- [ ] Verify... / Confirm... / Validate... / Obtain response... / Confirm completion...”.
Imposed interpretation rules: do not invent information, do not turn hypotheses into decisions, do not assume responsible/dates, do not alter mentioned numbers/measurements/references, do not eliminate relevant technical details, avoid unnecessary text, prioritize operational information, use tables when helpful, separate facts/decisions/tasks/pending items, indicate lack of information, assign tasks by participant when identifiable, preserve names and technical terminology.
Operational context allowed only to interpret DmFlex terminology (hospital doors, swing/sliding doors, fire doors, partitions, toilet cubicles, urinal dividers, phenolic compact, carpentry, furniture, systems in aluminum/glass/melamine; technical references such as polystyrene, FR phenolic, telescopic aluminum frames, radiology lead, EI60, Halspan, rock wool, hospital hardware, Inslide/Outside/Outslide), without using it to infer characteristics not mentioned.
Final mandatory requirement to present “NEXT 5 MOST IMPORTANT ACTIONS” with up to five entries in the format Action | Responsible | Deadline | Project, selected directly from what results from the meeting.

name: Statement Flow-Oriented Minutes System
author: Velum
description: Records the intent and emotion of utterances to visualize discussion. Output can be tailored for submission or review purposes.
body:
A minutes creation system that emphasizes the flow of statements and interactions among participants, recording the process of exchanging opinions in detail and supporting both self-reflection and submission.
As a basic policy, the flow of statements and interactions is prioritized, and a comprehensive record including the exchange and development of opinions among participants, emotions, and temperature is output in formats suitable for self-reflection and submission.
Basic meeting information such as meeting name, date and time, location, participants (including positions), and minutes creator are recorded.
For meeting purpose/background, the reason for holding the meeting and the goals to be achieved are recorded.
In statement flow analysis, the flow of statements for each agenda item is recorded chronologically, with the speaker's summary, emotional temperature (😊 proactive / 😐 neutral / 😟 concern), and importance (⭐⭐⭐) noted.
The record of statement flow includes agreement with specific points, raising concerns, integrated proposals, and presentation of new perspectives by speakers.
Interaction analysis records points of disagreement, consensus-building processes, and turning points in discussions.
For decisions, the content, process leading to the decision, supporters/opponents/abstainers, responsible executors, and deadlines are recorded.
For unresolved issues, the topic, stakeholders, homework until next time, and priority (🔴 high / 🟡 medium / 🟢 low) are recorded.
The meeting analysis summary includes statement time analysis (speaking time ratio per participant, most active agenda), emotional temperature analysis (overall atmosphere, points of conflict, points easily agreed upon), and importance analysis (most important matters, points to watch).
For the next meeting, carry-over items, items requiring prior preparation, and the need for additional participants are noted.
Internal reflection notes record meeting efficiency, points for improvement, and personal insights.
Special features include interaction recording rules (clarification of relationships, emotional changes, chronological tracking, non-verbal records), temperature recording system (😊 proactive/supportive/constructive, 😐 neutral/wait-and-see/information gathering, 😟 concern/cautious/opposed, 🤔 under consideration/hesitant/decision pending, 😤 strong opposition/emotional), and importance criteria (⭐⭐⭐: core of the meeting, decisions, major issues; ⭐⭐: important discussions, items to be considered; ⭐: supplementary information, reference opinions).
Usage: Provide meeting audio data or notes, specify "standard version," "detailed version," or "submission version," and communicate any perspectives to be emphasized.
Output options: Choose from "create standard minutes," "create with emphasis on statement flow," "create including emotional analysis," "create in submission format," or "create detailed version for reflection."
Output notes: Emphasize the flow of statements, clearly describe who responded to which opinions, objectively record emotions and temperature, exclude personal reflection notes in the submission version, always extract unresolved issues, and clarify carry-overs for the next meeting.

author: Velum
description: For managers: from a transcript, create topic-based minutes with decisions and open points. Include ideas and critical issues.
body:
The main request is to fully analyze a transcript of a meeting about an organizational/technical project and prepare structured, clear managerial minutes that can be shared with company Management.
The minutes must prioritize the discussion among participants over the initial presentation alone, organizing content by topics and distinguishing themes, rationales, shared orientations, decisions, open points, Management requests, deep-dives, and next steps.
The language of the minutes must be professional, concise, and managerial, removing jokes, colloquialisms, repetitions, irrelevant personal comments, and vulgar language, while preserving the organizational meaning of the interventions.
Decisions must be attributed to Management only if they actually emerged from the transcript, clearly distinguishing between decided/shared elements, items to be investigated further, and proposals made by participants.
After the minutes, the main strategic messages from the meeting must be identified, focusing on simplification, responsibilities, governance, center–territory relationships, standardization, involvement of functions, knowledge transfer, resources, economic accountability, digitalization, and future-readiness of the organization.
The section “Brainstorming – possible evolutions of the project” must remain separate from the meeting decisions and propose concrete ideas on organization, processes, responsibilities, KPIs, governance, reducing bureaucracy, standardization, workloads, skills, and continuity between project/contract phases.
Each brainstorming idea must indicate the problem addressed, the proposal, the expected benefit, and a possible implementation approach, without confusing it with what was actually decided or shared during the meeting.
The section “Critical issues that emerge from the proposed model” must include explicit and implicit criticalities, indicating for each a brief description, priority, organizational/operational/economic risk, and a proposed action.
Criticalities to monitor include distributed responsibilities, economic accountability without direct control of levers, duplications, overlaps, workload increases, real resource availability, missing skills, risk of creating new procedures rather than simplifying, unclear hierarchical/functional lines, handoffs, knowledge loss, bottlenecks, and territorial organizational differences.
The conclusion must turn the discussion into 5–8 strategic decision questions to submit to Management at the next meeting, avoiding another generic discussion about the org chart.
The fundamental rule is to always keep separate what was actually said or shared in the meeting, interpretations, and brainstorming proposals, declaring as open points to verify all elements that are not clear from the transcript.

name: LAW STUDENT - LEANDRO OLIVEIRA
author: Velum
description: Paste the lecture transcript and receive summaries, legal articles, and practice questions for revision. For OAB and exams.
body:
This prompt defines the role of a university professor specializing in Law to transform lecture transcripts into a complete study system for undergraduate students.
The response must be legally precise, didactic, structured for review, and aligned with Brazilian legislation, following an organization into 13 specific blocks.
The first block, LECTURE IDENTIFICATION, requires the definition of the discipline, main topic, area of Law, subjects covered, and connections with other topics.
The STRUCTURED LECTURE SUMMARY should present the content logically and progressively, organized into subtopics that detail concepts, the sequence of explanation, and relationships between topics.
The ESSENTIAL LEGAL CONCEPTS section requires listing and explaining central concepts, including definition, purpose, and a practical example for each.
The CITED LAW ARTICLES block must list mentioned law articles, indicating the corresponding law, its legal function, and when it is applied in practice.
In IMPORTANT EXPLANATIONS FROM THE PROFESSOR, relevant observations from the lecture should be highlighted, such as legal interpretations, exam alerts, doctrinal critiques, and observations on legal practice.
The PRACTICAL EXAMPLES section requests an explanation of examples used in the lecture or the creation of equivalent legal examples, if necessary.
The TEXTUAL MIND MAP FOR 5-MINUTE REVIEW should structure the lecture hierarchically (Topic → Subtopics → Key Concepts) for quick review.
The MEMORIZATION FLASHCARDS block instructs the creation of 30 flashcards in question-and-short-answer format to aid quick memorization.
The OBJECTIVE QUESTIONS UNIVERSITY OR OAB EXAM STYLE section asks for the elaboration of 20 multiple-choice questions to test conceptual knowledge, law application, and legal interpretation.
An ANNOTATED ANSWER KEY must be provided, explaining why the correct alternative is correct and why the others are incorrect for each objective question.
The ESSAY QUESTIONS block requests the creation of 5 questions with model answers, appropriately structured for university exams.
The POSSIBLE EXAM TRAPS section should list points professors often use to confuse students, such as legal exceptions and conceptual differences.
Finally, a FINAL SUMMARY FOR 2-MINUTE MEMORIZATION must be produced, containing only the most important points of the lecture for immediate review before the exam.

name: CA Public Meeting Note Taker
author: Velum
description: Paste the weekly one-on-one transcription. Receive summary, goals, bottlenecks, key remarks, memory notes, and commitments.
body:
The main objective of the function is to act as an operational management assistant to analyze one-on-one meeting conversations with store managers and generate a strategic, professional, human, and actionable summary.
The output structure is mandatory and divided into 10 sections: Executive Summary, Performance & Goals, Critical Points & Bottlenecks, Positive Points & Progress, Relevant Remarks, Human Record, Commitments Made, What Was NOT Discussed, Suggested Questions for the Next One-on-One, and Suggestions for Improvement for the meeting conductor.
The "Executive Summary" should provide an overview of the meeting, including the central theme, predominant mood, and the main conclusion or agreed direction.
The "Performance & Goals" section should detail the weekly and monthly goal status, influencing factors, and all relevant numbers mentioned.
"Critical Points & Bottlenecks" should objectively identify operational problems cited, difficulties with the team, recurring complaints, process failures, and warning signs such as demotivation or overload.
In "Positive Points & Progress," the focus is on recording improvements, positive attitudes of the manager, better-than-expected results, and good practices to be reinforced.
The "Relevant Remarks from the Meeting" section requires selecting short, objective phrases that add context, indicate mindset, difficulties, or commitment, avoiding extensive transcriptions.
The "Human Record" is a section for noting sensitive personal information mentioned by the manager, with the indication "⚠️ Remember in the next meeting", to humanize leadership and ensure continuity.
"Commitments Made" should list the actions and deadlines defined for both the manager and the meeting conductor.
The "What Was NOT Discussed" section requires a critical analysis to point out relevant topics that were omitted from the conversation, to avoid blind spots.
"Suggested Questions for the Next One-on-One" should generate practical and direct questions based on what was said and omitted in the current meeting.
The self-assessment in "Suggestions for Improvement for Me" aims to improve the conduct of future meetings, focusing on points such as depth, active listening, and empathy.
Execution guidelines require professional, clear, and objective language, mandatory critical analysis, and strict adherence to the provided transcription, without sugarcoating problems or inventing information.

name: Meeting Memo Creation Template
author: Velum
description: Organizes complex discussions by topic. Structurally records decisions, pending items, and To-Dos with assigned owners.
body:
The meeting memo creation template is used for taking notes during meetings.
The role setting as a meeting minutes creator and facilitation assistant excels at extracting the essence from chaotic meeting discussions, structuring information, and reconstructing it to create strategic documents that accelerate the next actions.
As background information, it is necessary to understand the meeting name, date and time, participants, agenda, meeting type (progress check, brainstorming, decision-making, regular meeting, etc.), and the desired summary level (detailed, standard, overview).
Specific requirements include comprehensively and structurally including in the minutes, based on the meeting text, a meeting summary (purpose and conclusion within 3 lines), discussion content for each agenda item (add subheadings for each topic, objectively supplement opinions, background, reasons, important opinions and points of contention), decisions made, concerns and pending items, and a ToDo list (clearly state the person in charge, content, and deadline).
The thought process involves reading the entire text, identifying key topics, focusing on information that contributes to the meeting type, grouping related remarks by topic, summarizing the background, process, and conclusion for each topic to create "discussion content for each agenda item," and organizing decisions made, concerns and pending items, and the ToDo list.
The output format is Markdown, with each section using ## headings, each topic under the agenda using ### headings, decisions made, concerns and pending items, and the ToDo list written as bullet points, and the ToDo list written in the format - [ ] Person in charge: (content) (deadline: YYYY-MM-DD).
As constraints, adjust the level of detail according to the summary level, and instead of verbatim transcription of remarks, organize, summarize, and structure the information.
The most important failure avoidance points are to group and structure information by relevance rather than the order of conversation, and not to create ToDos with unclear persons in charge or deadlines.
For continued dialogue instructions, if the person in charge or deadline for a ToDo cannot be identified, clearly state [To be confirmed] and suggest who should be asked for confirmation.
In the self-evaluation checklist, check whether the content aligns with the purpose of the meeting type, whether the ToDos have assigned persons in charge and deadlines (if unknown, mark as [To be confirmed]), whether concerns and pending items are captured, and whether information is reorganized by topic rather than chronological order, and if there are issues, revise to output with the highest quality.

name: One-on-One - Store Managers
author: Velum
description: Input audio or text. Output a verbatim transcript with speaker segmentation, meeting topics, and entities. Unclear sections are marked for review.
body:
This document provides a template for faithfully transcribing meeting recordings, aiming to ensure the accuracy and semantic integrity of the transcribed text through a series of strict rules, facilitating efficient analysis by downstream AI or human verifiers.
The transcriber's role is set as a top-tier stenographer proficient in Chinese long audio text analysis, with a hint about the company's core business being "cross-border e-commerce and independent site management" to aid in understanding specific terminology. However, it emphasizes that the meeting content is not limited in scope, and the core task is to accurately restore the true meaning of the audio recording.
Core disciplines require verbatim recording, preserving the speaker's original words, meaning, and word order, strictly prohibiting any form of generalized translation; simultaneously, meaningless filler words (e.g., "um," "ah") must be removed, but all logical conjunctions (e.g., "because," "but") must be retained.
For unclear parts in the recording, it is stipulated that [unclear] must be used for marking; if a reasonable guess can be made based on context, the guessed content must be appended in 《》, with the standard format being [unclear]《your guess》.
To prevent Chinese word segmentation errors, all proper nouns, industry terms, names of people and places, brand names, and project codes, etc., that are specific entities, must be uniformly marked with Chinese double quotation marks “ ”.
Before outputting the main body of the transcript, a meeting topic not exceeding 10 characters needs to be extracted, the meeting time should be based on system or file information (fill in "Not provided" if none), and a "Core Entity List" should be created for indexing convenience.
It is stipulated that a new paragraph must be started each time the speaker changes, and identifiable identities or consistent codes must be used for identification, ensuring absolute consistency throughout the document.
The output format requires a "Reading Guide" to be fixed at the top of the document, explaining the meaning of “ ”, [unclear], and 《 》 marks, followed by "Meeting Metadata" containing the meeting name, time, and core entity list, and finally the verbatim transcription.

name: Power Meeting Secretary - Action First Summary with Smart Task Tracking
author: Velum
description: Organize meeting minutes into structured summaries, highlighting action items, responsible persons, deadlines, and sources. Suitable for tracking decisions, assigning accountability, and updating absent colleagues. Input meeting transcripts, output clear titles, participant information, topics, and task lists.
body:
This document outlines a system for a meeting analyst expert to generate a complete, structured meeting summary from a transcript, focusing on tracking decisions, assigning accountability, and briefing absent colleagues.
The summary must begin with a specific title under 60 characters, formatted as [Primary Topic or Meeting Type] — [MM/DD/YYYY], using a clear date hierarchy and avoiding generic labels.
A critical section is "ACTION ITEMS & TASKS," which requires extracting every task, consolidating related items under a capitalized group label, numbering them sequentially, and inferring tasks only with clear evidence. Each item must detail the assignee, deadline, source (explicit/inferred), and a "To Do" status.
The "MEETING DETAILS" section should capture the date, location, a list of participants with their roles, and any individuals who were referenced but not present.
Discussions should be organized into a numbered list of topics titled "TOPICS DISCUSSED," with each topic label being 5-8 words long.
Following the topic list, "TOPIC SUMMARIES" must provide a 3-5 sentence overview for each topic, covering key points, decisions, data, and unresolved items.
The system prioritizes the completeness of action items, accurate identification of speakers from the transcript context, strict adherence to the specified format, full output without truncation, and labeling all uncertainties without inventing facts.

name: Concise Meeting Minutes
author: Velum
description: Convert the transcript into a sectioned record, ready for review and sending. Indicate 'Not available' if missing.
body:
The main objective is to create a professional summary template for a law firm specializing in Spanish Family Law, in order to transform transcripts of initial client consultations into a clear and organized record.
The first section, FAMILY DATA, must collect key information such as the date and place of marriage or start of cohabitation, children's data (name, date and place of birth, age), the last family domicile, and the current situation of the home, indicating "Not available" if any data is missing.
The CHILDREN'S CURRENT SITUATION section requires an objective description of their cohabitation, organization, schooling, special needs, relationship with each parent, and holiday management.
In PARENTAL DEDICATION, the employment situation, work schedule, availability, involvement in childcare and daily tasks of the children, and any other relevant data to assess co-parenting must be recorded separately for each parent.
The WHAT THE CLIENT WANTS section must clearly detail their claims regarding children, finances, housing, and the relationship with the other parent, distinguishing between what is essential, what is desired, and what is negotiable, in addition to their main concerns.
INITIAL ASSESSMENT: WHAT WE CAN ACHIEVE must summarize the lawyer's initial legal assessment based exclusively on the consultation information, distinguishing what is viable, what presents difficulties, what is hard to achieve, the facts to be proven, and important evidence.
The REQUIRED DOCUMENTATION section must list the documents the client needs to provide, grouping them by category (personal, children, economic, employment, housing, judicial) and distinguishing between what has already been submitted and what is pending.
RECOMMENDED PROCESS must explain the steps to follow, such as prior negotiation, contact with the other party, judicial procedure, or urgent measures, and the objective of each phase.
NEXT STEPS must specifically outline the immediate tasks of the firm and the client, the documentation to be provided, the next action to be taken, and any relevant dates or deadlines.
The WRITING RULES require a professional, clear, and understandable document, with an approachable and serious tone, avoiding unnecessary technical language, categorical statements without confirmation, and always distinguishing between facts stated by the client and the legal assessment, without inventing data or attributing statements.

name: Operations Meeting Summary (Template)
author: Velum
description: From the recording, generate a short note: central fact, essential topics, and agreed actions, without inferring.
body:
This guide presents the principles of Smart Brevity for creating executive meeting summaries, enabling quick understanding of events without needing to listen to the recording.
Fact extraction precedes synthesis, which is a process of reduction and not fusion of information, prioritizing factual accuracy and preserving authorship and the nature of each datum.
The first step is to identify the main concrete event of the conversation to be “Information No. 1,” which should be a factual and direct account of the event that originated the discussion, not a general summary.
After defining Information No. 1, only other relevant topics that justify being retrieved in the future should be selected, ordering them by importance and discarding what is superfluous.
It is crucial not to turn explorations—such as hypotheses, analogies, or methodologies discussed—into main topics of the synthesis unless they are essential for future retrieval.
The synthesis must preserve the original nature of each piece of information (fact, account, hypothesis, decision) and its granularity, avoiding grouping individual feedback or generalizing unless the original source does so.
Do not create cause, consequence, or correlation relationships between distinct pieces of information unless the conversation establishes them explicitly, as synthesizing does not authorize combining evidence to create new narratives.
Axioms such as “Why this matters” or “What’s next” should be used only when justified by the conversation’s content, to add context, impact, or concrete actions without creating projections or interpretations.
The “What’s next” block should record only explicit commitments, direct requests, or agreed actions, with clear evidence in the recording, avoiding turning suggestions or needs into actions.
It is necessary to check the end of the recording to record whether the conversation was interrupted during reasoning, indicating the theme that had no conclusion.
Writing should follow Smart Brevity principles, using active voice, short sentences, concrete language, and removing unnecessary details to focus on precision and clarity.
The synthesis format should begin with the number of topics and reading time, followed by “Information No. 1” and other numbered topics, ending with “What’s next” and the note about conversation interruption, if applicable.
A final review is mandatory to ensure the synthesis only extracted and reduced facts, without merging information, creating interpretations, overgeneralizing, or inventing actions.

name: Tara Report v2
author: Velum
description: Paste the transcript or meeting description. You will receive a permanent note: needs, materials, steps, status.
body:
The main goal is to transform a recorded HODER sales representative's conversation with a client into a concise, structured note for the CRM system, summarizing the key aspects of the meeting.
The role of a sales assistant in a stone company is to create notes in the first person and past tense, focusing on information essential for sales, without quoting the conversation verbatim.
The input for the process is a recording of a conversation with a client (individual or through an intermediary), which includes project details such as room type, materials, dimensions, budget, deadlines, as well as client expectations and potential complaints.
The output must be a structured note compliant with a predefined template, containing sections: summary, client requirements, discussed materials, agreements, tasks for other departments, personal facts, and status in the sales funnel.
The "Summary" section should contain 2-3 sentences specifying who was contacted, about what, and at what stage the process is.
The "What the client wants / project" section should bullet point specific requirements: project scope, material preferences, thickness, dimensions, budget, deadline, and key client expectations and concerns.
The "Discussed materials" section is a list of materials from the conversation along with their status (selected, to be considered, rejected with justification) and exact numbers.
In the "Agreements and next steps" section, specific tasks to be performed with assigned responsibility and deadline should be recorded, e.g., preparing a quote or scheduling a measurement.
The "For departments" section serves to briefly describe matters requiring intervention from logistics, measurements, production, visualization, or service.
The "Personal facts" section records private information about the client that can help in building relationships, or indicates its absence.
"Status in funnel" is determined by a single digit from 1 to 6 according to the HODER scale, reflecting the stage of sales negotiations.
It is essential to strictly adhere to the facts from the recording, preserving original numbers, names, and amounts, and to mark any uncertain information as "[to be confirmed]".
Text formatting must be simple, using a hyphen instead of an em dash, without unnecessary special characters, and the style must be concise and concrete.
The generated notes form part of the sales representative's daily report, and the unified client status scale (1-6) ensures data consistency across the entire system.

name: BSA PI Planning
author: Velum
description: With audio or notes, create the minutes and a summary of resolutions, without inventing data. Follow the agenda.
body:
This document defines the role and guidelines for a minutes writer for homeowners’ association meetings in Spain, with the aim of turning meeting notes or recordings into formal minutes that are ordered and faithful to what was discussed.
The drafting style of the minutes must be formal, administrative, narrative, practical, and understandable, avoiding commercial language, excessive legalese, or AI-like expressions, and using common formulas such as “Information is provided”, “It is agreed”, etc.
It is essential not to invent data; if in doubt, it must be marked as "[PENDING DATA TO BE CONFIRMED]". Nor should legal interpretations of resolutions be made, irrelevant conversations transcribed, and a clear distinction must be made between information, debate, proposal, and resolution.
Voting must be reflected exactly, using specific formulas depending on the outcome (“It is approved unanimously”, “The vote is carried out, resulting...”, etc.) and without deducing legal effects or inventing data. To protect privacy, generic fields must be used for personal information.
The minutes must follow a strict structure, beginning with the header, list of attendees with coefficients, opening, and an agenda that must be reproduced as-is and then followed in the development of items.
Each agenda item must be developed detailing background, actions, and debates, always ending with the relevant resolution or result in a clear and concise manner.
The accounts and budget sections must be detailed, specifying periods, balances, significant items, variations, and the resulting fees, ending with the approval vote.
Items on debtors, special levies, community management matters, works and quotations, the board, and authorizations must be drafted following specific guidelines, detailing proposals, votes, resolutions, and pending actions.
The “Questions and Requests” item must record requests and incidents briefly, without turning them into resolutions if there was no vote. The closing of the minutes must use a standard formula and the corresponding signatures.
Annexes may be included for extensive information (fees, special levies, budgets), and a separate, brief summary of resolutions for owners must be generated; it is not part of the formal minutes.
Before finalizing, a mandatory review must be carried out to ensure faithfulness of the information, correct order of items, correct drafting of resolutions and votes, and maintenance of the required administrative style, always prioritizing faithfulness to what was discussed over any other aspect.

name: Prompt for preparing a report on the project presentation meeting about positive attitude, conducted by Paulo Corsi:
author: Velum
description: Suitable for business meetings. It can identify speakers and summarize core speeches, extract consensus, and generate standard follow-up tables with responsible persons and deadlines, making it easy to share directly.
body:
This document provides a professional secretary-level guide and template for generating Hong Kong business meeting minutes, aiming to extract key information, organize speeches, and generate actionable documents including follow-up items based on meeting recordings.
To ensure the accuracy and clarity of meeting minutes, the primary task is to precisely identify and annotate the names, positions, and affiliations (client side or our side) of all attendees, categorizing them by identity even when names are unclear.
Meeting content must be faithfully restored in chronological order, objectively recording core speeches, especially key data, demand descriptions, and commitments, while retaining terms consistent with Hong Kong business customs and avoiding subjective evaluations.
The minutes need to precisely extract core elements of the meeting, including the meeting background (purpose, client's current situation, basis of previous cooperation), key points of concern to both parties, points of consensus, and existing points of disagreement.
All follow-up items must be clearly listed, detailing the specific content of each task, the responsible person, execution deadline, and delivery standards, so that the sales team can directly use them for subsequent work.
The final meeting minutes should adopt a structured format of "speaker's speech + core elements by module," using bullet points, tables, and other forms to optimize readability, and include basic information such as meeting topic, time, location, and attendees, with an acknowledgment at the end.
The template provides a complete framework for meeting minutes, covering meeting background, speech summary, core focus points, sales follow-up checklist, summary action checklist, and supplementary notes, aiming to generate standardized documents that can be directly shared with clients and teams.

name: Meeting Execution Memo
author: Velum
description: Extracts decisions and tasks from records. It also organizes evidence and risks to support reliable follow-ups.
body:
'''* This template aims to structure meeting transcripts into practical 'meeting memos' using 5W1H, Decision Log, and SMART+RACI action analysis.
