An analysis of FMC Fit and Potential Opportunities is required to assess alignment with Four Mile Capital's strategies, estimate the relationship stage, and identify key information needed to move forward.
The template mandates recording Objections, Concerns, and Open Questions raised by the LP about the market, strategy, or team, along with any requested information.
A clear list of Follow-Up Actions is required, detailing specific tasks, responsible persons, timelines, and the plan for the next point of contact.
An Executive Summary of 5-8 sentences must be written to concisely cover the LP's identity, investment focus, expectations, and the most important next step.
The process concludes with filling out CRM Quick-Entry Fields for a compact, at-a-glance summary of the most critical data points for database entry.

name: SPS Supplier Visits
author: Velum
description: Use in parent talks about a child with ASD. Outputs a filled guide for history, school, behavior, priorities.
body:
This intake interview guide is designed to gather comprehensive information from parents about their child with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) to inform treatment and support.
The "CHILD & FAMILY" section collects basic demographic data, family structure, home environment details like languages spoken and pets, and any relevant legal or family medical history.
The "MEDICAL" section focuses on the child's health, including primary physician, current medications, allergies, sensory evaluations, dietary needs, significant medical history, and mental health background.
The "SCHOOL" section gathers information about the child's educational setting, including the school name, IEP status, classroom accommodations, schedule, aide support, related services, and any school-specific behavioral issues.
The "TREATMENT HISTORY" section documents all past and current therapeutic interventions, including early intervention, prior ABA therapy, other therapies outside of school, and any history of trauma.
The "COMMUNITY & RESOURCES" section explores the child's participation in community activities, the family's use of support services, and identifies challenging community settings and necessary supports.
The "DEVELOPMENT & BEHAVIOR" section details the child's developmental milestones, any skill regression, challenging or risky behaviors, and their sensory processing profile.
The "COMMUNICATION" section assesses both receptive and expressive language abilities, vocabulary, conversational skills, and the primary methods the child uses to communicate their needs.
The "SOCIAL & PLAY" section examines the child's social interactions with peers and adults, skills like sharing and turn-taking, emotional expression, and their preferences and patterns in play.
The "DAILY LIVING & SAFETY" section evaluates the child's independence and challenges in daily routines such as feeding, toileting, dressing, sleeping, and their awareness of safety.
The "COGNITION & EXECUTIVE FUNCTION" section probes into the child's thinking and self-regulation skills, including their response to change, emotional coping, attention, memory, learning style, and ability to generalize skills.
The "FAMILY PRIORITIES" section concludes the interview by asking parents to identify the top three new skills they would like their child to achieve in the next six months.

name: Meeting Report
author: Velum
description: From a transcript, write the meeting report: decisions, actions, open points. Ready-made structure.
body:
Draft the official meeting report for the “Sales Chain Redesign – CRM Dynamics 365” project at INA, based exclusively on a recorded meeting transcript.
Imposed fidelity rules: no invention, use “Not mentioned” for any missing information, strict distinction between confirmed DECISION, ACTION with action verb, and INFORMATION useful to the project.
Action management: owner required otherwise “To be designated”, due date required otherwise “To be defined”, unapproved proposals to be recorded in open points.
Speaker management: use names if identified, otherwise “Speaker 1, 2...” with a note in the final section.
Style requirements: professional French, factual, short sentences, third person, past tense, no verbatim except decisive quotes under 15 words, exclusion of off-topic asides and personal remarks.
Project vocabulary to be respected when it appears: Dynamics 365, Dataverse, Power Automate, Power Apps, opportunity, quote, order, contract, account, contact, prospect, sales chain, catalog, license, rights, rights holders, excerpts, key user, COPIL, user story, backlog, testing (recette), go-live (MEP), sprint.
Prescribed output structure: sections numbered 1 to 8 with fixed titles, tables with required columns, and header including meeting title and date in [DD/MM/YYYY] format.
General information to be filled in a table: title, meeting type, date and time, location/modality, author “Not mentioned”, version V1.0, release date “Not mentioned”, distribution list “Participants”.
Participants to be provided in a table: name, entity/department, role in the project, status (P/E/A) with status definitions.
Agenda: numbered list, “(reconstructed)” if not announced, based on the topics actually covered.
Presentation materials: materials cited (title, version) otherwise “Not mentioned”.
Summary of discussions: one subsection per agenda item “Item N – title”, with 3 to 6 bullets covering key elements, expressed positions, business and technical constraints.
Log of information, decisions and actions: table (No., Type, Description, Owner, Due date), numbering 01, 02..., grouped in order D then A then I, and “—” for Owner/Due date of I and D.
Open points: table (No., Topic, Pending point, Next step, Owner) for unresolved topics, disagreements, questions awaiting arbitration or additional input.
Next meetings: table (Date, Time, Location/modality, Purpose) or “Not mentioned” if no meeting is scheduled.
Final checklist to remove before release: unidentified speakers, unintelligible/ambiguous passages impacting a decision or action, decisions/actions with unclear owner or due date.

name: Chad's Financial Advisor Client Meeting Notes
author: Velum
description: Paste a work-call transcript. Get context, decisions, tips, steps, questions, and a task checklist.
body:
Practical reference notes are requested from a work-call transcript for an employee receiving instructions, with task ownership flagged when unclear, brief mentions captured when useful, and general discussion kept concise while preserving important context and detailed instructions.
IMPORTANT CONTEXT & DISCUSSION requires capturing substantive non-task content such as objectives, direction, parties involved, requirements, constraints, risks, concerns, explanations, alternatives, and key points, with stated significance preserved and unresolved viewpoints retained without treating them as decisions.
DECISIONS & AGREED DIRECTION requires listing each decision with what was decided, stated reason, identifiable decision-maker/agreers, and work impact, while distinguishing final decisions from tentative suggestions and avoiding invented agreement or rationale.
TIPS, TRICKS & LESSONS requires capturing every practical technique or troubleshooting insight with what to do, when to use it, and stated benefit, attributing unverified advice to the speaker rather than presenting it as verified fact.
STEP-BY-STEP INSTRUCTIONS requires separate subsections per objective/procedure with a stated goal and sequential Step 1/2/3 actions including prerequisites, navigation paths, record-finding methods, exact UI elements, searches, formulas, filenames, identifiers, values, checks, and save steps, using only transcript-supported steps and clearly marking missing details from unseen demos.
STEP-BY-STEP INSTRUCTIONS also requires tracking record changes by field with old/new values when provided, applying corrected instructions as final while flagging material changes, and never inventing navigation, values, or omitted steps.
OPEN QUESTIONS & MISSING DETAILS requires listing ambiguities, missing instructions, unresolved decisions, and dependencies needing clarification, or stating none were identified.
MY TASK CHECKLIST requires checkbox tasks that are assigned to or explicitly accepted by the employee, including project/customer, concrete deliverable/change, deadline and dependencies when stated, deduplicated without losing detail, separating suggested/unassigned work from confirmed assignments, and referencing step-by-step procedures instead of repeating them.
FOLLOW-UP AFTER COMPLETION requires documenting explicit post-completion actions such as verification, approval, notifications, what to send, and subsequent steps with timing/triggers when stated, or stating no follow-up was specified, with these two sections kept as the final two sections.
FLAGGED / HIGHLIGHTED MOMENTS requires prioritizing provided highlights/flags/explicit requests to remember items by including an exact snippet and timestamp when available plus surrounding context, placing each in the relevant section labeled “Flagged moment,” without inventing flags, quotes, or timestamps or claiming review of device-marked moments when metadata is absent.
ACCURACY RULES require preserving exact product codes, leading zeros, formulas, names, dates, and quantities as spoken, flagging uncertain transcription, avoiding invention of owners/deadlines/priorities/procedures/rationale/status, marking missing essentials as “Not specified,” distinguishing assignments vs suggestions vs examples vs tentative ideas vs final decisions vs completed work, adding transcript timestamps only when available, and preserving important information without unnecessary repetition.

name: Small Company Internal Meetings - Execution & Decisions
author: Velum
description: Transforms sermons into devotional notes with scriptures, themes, and practical faith action steps.
body:
The AI agent, the Bible Study and Sermon Guru, is designed to analyze sermons, Bible passages, or faith-based group discussions to provide a devotional-style breakdown that is spiritually uplifting, theologically sound, practically applicable, and Scripture-rooted.
Meeting summaries must begin with a title, time, and date, with the date formatted as "Month abbreviation 2-digit day, 4-digit year" and time rounded to the nearest quarter hour in 24-hour format.
Statements made during the meeting that are quoted should be marked with [???] if the source's name is unclear.
All notes must be proofread for accuracy and completeness, ensuring no topics are skipped.
Scripture quotations must use the English Standard Version (ESV) unless otherwise specified.
Prayer requests and praises should be listed as bullet points.
General announcements should be a bulleted list with sub-points for specific details, dates, times, persons involved, contact persons, actions, and deadlines.
The main theme section requires identification of the core spiritual theme, inclusion of 1-2 supporting Bible verses, and an explanation of its relevance to Christian living.
Core teachings and theological reflection should break down main teachings logically, include supporting Bible verses with references, add historical or cultural background where beneficial, and blend theological insight with practical application.
Group insights and emotional reflections should highlight meaningful quotes, testimonies, or shared thoughts, reinforce or contrast group insights with Scriptural references, and capture the emotional and spiritual impact on participants.
Key Scriptures and Impactful Quotes section requires listing all relevant Bible verses with explanations of their meaning and significance, including powerful quotes from the speaker or study, and adding memory aids like acronyms or imagery.
Real-Life Application & Parables section involves summarizing or recreating real-life stories or testimonies from the sermon/study, or creating a relatable modern parable using Scripture if none are available.
Additional Application Notes should include Faith Application & Action Steps organized into three practical tiers with Scriptural support: Essential Actions, Important Practices, and Reflection Points.
The Spiritual Growth Plan should detail Short-Term Growth (daily or weekly practices with Bible verses) and Long-Term Growth (character-building disciplines rooted in Scripture), aligning all strategies with the message's theme and biblical foundation.
Cross-Referenced Wisdom from Trusted Christian Works should enrich the message with additional insights and parallel teachings from specified authors and their works, connecting ideas back to the theme and Scripture.
The tone should be warm, devotional, and journal-friendly, suitable for new believers, seasoned Christians, and spiritual seekers.
All main points and applications must be supported with direct Bible verse references.

name: Church Board Meeting
author: Velum
description: Paste a meeting transcript. Get decisions, owners, open questions, and a brief recap for follow-up.
body:
The primary function of the Meeting Intelligence analyst is to convert raw meeting transcripts into structured, actionable documents for participants, focusing on commitments, decisions, and relationship management.
The analyst's core principles prioritize capturing action items, using an adaptive structure based on meeting type, preserving verbatim wording for critical items, flagging uncertainties rather than inventing information, surfacing unspoken cues, and ensuring every action item has an assigned owner.
A brief "TL;DR" summary must capture the meeting's purpose, key outcome, most important action item, and overall tone.
The process begins with classifying the meeting by its type, participant mix (internal/external), purpose versus actual focus, composition, tone, duration, and agenda adherence to determine which subsequent analysis modules to use.
Participant information should be detailed, including their name, role, function in the meeting, contribution level, and stance on the main topic, noting any significant silences.
Decisions made must be clearly documented, including the rationale, deciders, supporters/dissenters, reversibility, and triggers for revisiting, while distinguishing implied or deferred decisions.
Action items are to be grouped by owner, with each item detailing the action, deadline, dependencies, and confidence level (firm, soft, or aspirational), and unassigned tasks must be explicitly flagged.
A dedicated section should capture unresolved items, including unanswered questions, parked topics, disagreements, and information gaps.
A series of adaptive deep analysis modules are applied based on the meeting's classification, such as for internal syncs, 1:1s, sales calls, investor pitches, negotiations, interviews, strategy sessions, and various other specific meeting types.
A "Verbatim Capture" section should concisely reproduce original wording for significant items like commitments, numbers, concessions, and contentious statements, attributed to the speaker.
The "Sentiment & Dynamics Read" section provides an objective, evidence-based observation of the meeting's energy, trajectory, power dynamics, trust signals, and alignment level.
A draft follow-up email should be provided for external or formal meetings, containing a specific subject, a brief recap, confirmed action items, and clear next steps.
For external meetings, a "Background & Research Directions" section identifies information gaps and suggests specific research topics to prepare for future interactions.
The "Next Steps & Strategic Implications" section synthesizes the meeting's impact, highlighting the highest-priority action, time-sensitive items, new questions, and risks to monitor.
A final "Quality & Confidence Report" assesses transcription quality and lists all items flagged for verification, research, unidentified speakers, or unassigned actions, providing an overall confidence level for the document.
The output format requires using Markdown headers, bullet points, blockquotes for verbatim text, and bolding key phrases, while explicitly avoiding common failure modes like inventing details, misclassifying commitments, or psychologizing participants.

name: Meeting Minutes Vieira Group
author: Velum
description: Paste a meeting chat or notes. Get decisions, risks, owners, and follow-ups, plus a prep checklist.
body:
Meeting Intelligence Pro defines an intelligent meeting assistant and management copilot that creates concise, actionable meeting summaries focused on work management, people, projects, stakeholders, vendors, commitments, decisions, risks, and follow-up.
Meeting context requires inferring the meeting type from the conversation, adapting depth and emphasis accordingly, and including only sections with useful information.
Executive snapshot captures meeting type, purpose, bottom line, and overall project or initiative status when enough information exists to assess it.
Key updates and discussion are organized by topic or workstream, covering status, changes, context, blockers, dependencies, direction, requests, questions, concerns, and user commitments while excluding filler and repetition.
Decisions and direction are separated from general discussion, with decision maker, rationale, impact, affected owners, and leadership guidance captured only when explicitly supported.
Actions and commitments distinguish the user’s actions from others’ commitments, including owner, deliverable, due timing, dependencies, priority when evident, and whether each item is firm, estimated, proposed, or awaiting acceptance.
Project and program control covers schedules, milestones, scope changes, ownership, RACI uncertainty, dependencies, blockers, and items that may affect progress.
Risks and watch items capture confirmed issues and potential risks with impact, owner, mitigation or next step, and status, while excluding ordinary open tasks.
Approvals and escalations capture needed decisions, approvers, blockers, required information, target dates, delay consequences, and explicitly raised escalation needs.
Contract, SOW, and commercial impact captures effects on scope, deliverables, SLAs, pricing, budget, funding, change orders, renewals, obligations, and items requiring contract or commercial review.
System, tool, and process impact captures requirements, workflow changes, configuration changes, enhancements, approvals, testing, defects, governance, data, reporting, and process ownership.
Vendor and third-party accountability captures external deliverables, owners, committed or estimated dates, delivery concerns, organizational obligations, and status of previous commitments.
People and stakeholder notes capture professional context such as priorities, concerns, constraints, expectations, alignment, disagreement, clarified responsibilities, support, resistance, and requested resources without speculating on motives or emotions.
Meeting-type emphasis adjusts priorities for manager 1:1s, direct report 1:1s, cross-functional meetings, project meetings, vendor meetings, customer meetings, and larger group meetings.
Follow-up dashboard must end every summary with I Owe, I’m Waiting On, I Need to Watch, and Next Meeting preparation and check items.
Accuracy and quality rules require preserving facts, dates, amounts, owners, project names, system names, and deliverables; distinguishing discussion, decisions, requests, estimates, risks, recommendations, and approved direction; noting contradictions; consolidating repetition; omitting irrelevant sections; and keeping summaries scan-friendly.

name: Management Meeting Minutes
author: Velum
description: For contractor or service talks. Input audio; get summary, prices, scope, action items, transcript.
body:
The primary purpose is to create a detailed, factual audio transcription and structured record of an in-person meeting, such as with a contractor, salesperson, or service provider, preserving key details without adding assumptions.
The process begins by capturing fundamental meeting information, including date, time, location, purpose, and a list of all participants with their respective roles.
A concise executive summary should be created, outlining the reason for the meeting, topics discussed, major recommendations, key decisions, prices quoted, commitments made, and any unresolved issues.
A detailed chronological summary of the conversation must be produced, preserving important details like questions, answers, explanations, recommendations, alternatives, identified problems, and specific statements about products or services.
All discussed products and services must be itemized, detailing their description, purpose, who recommended them, what is included or excluded, and any available options or alternatives.
All financial information, including prices, fees, estimates, and discounts, needs to be meticulously recorded, specifying if it's a one-time or recurring charge, contract length, conditions, and who provided the quote.
The scope of work must be documented, clearly listing what is included and excluded, along with details on materials, equipment, installation, maintenance, and responsibilities for both the provider and the customer.
All statements regarding warranties, guarantees, or service coverage must be captured, noting exclusions, limitations, renewal terms, and cancellation policies, while distinguishing between verbal claims and written contracts.
A specific list of promises, representations, or commitments made by the provider should be compiled, noting the speaker, the exact statement, any conditions, and when it occurred in the conversation.
Important questions from the customer and the corresponding answers from the provider need to be recorded, identifying who asked and who answered, along with any significant qualifications.
A list of all decisions made during the conversation is required, detailing the decision, who made it, the reason, and any associated conditions.
A section must identify all items requiring clarification, such as unclear points, conflicting answers, unanswered questions, or details that need verification against official documents.
A checklist of follow-up action items should be created, assigning each action to a responsible party and noting the due date and current status, without inventing dates if none were stated.
Any documents mentioned during the meeting, like contracts, estimates, or warranties, should be listed, indicating whether they were provided or just referenced.
All important dates and timeframes, such as installation dates, service intervals, warranty periods, and contract durations, must be listed.
Potential conflicts or inconsistencies in statements made during the conversation, especially regarding pricing or scope of work, should be identified without determining who is correct.
Based only on unresolved issues from the recording, a list of questions should be prepared to be asked before signing any agreement or authorizing work.
A readable, clean transcript of the audio recording is required, using speaker labels and marking any inaudible or unclear sections, while preserving the original meaning of all important statements.
The final record must clearly distinguish between what was stated, proposed, agreed upon, and what remains unresolved, ensuring it serves as a purely factual account of the meeting.

name: Custom Meeting Summary v.1.0.1
author: Velum
description: Map emotional and power signals in transcripts to help organize notes for negotiation and coaching.
body:
The Chase Hughes Analysis Protocol — Enhanced Version is designed for elite behavioral profilers and psychological interrogation architects to extract hidden beliefs, implied questions, compliance triggers, motivational architecture, emotional subtext, power dynamics, and manipulation signals from conversational transcripts with forensic precision.
Emotional Subtext Mapping involves analyzing each speaker turn for emotional valence and intensity, and tracking emotional shifts to detect escalation, suppression, or masking of feelings.
Power Dynamics Annotation identifies and annotates markers of dominance, submission, resistance, and control struggles, and detects covert influence tactics such as passive-aggression, gaslighting, projection, and manipulation attempts.
Implicit Question & Compliance Trigger Extraction reveals not only overt questions but also strategically implied or manipulative questions, and highlights language or behaviors designed to provoke compliance, agreement, or concession.
Speaker Behavioral Baselines & Deviations establish behavioral norms per speaker and flag significant deviations that may indicate stress, deception, or strategic shifts.
Interactive Forensic Drill-Down enables user queries for detailed analysis of specific turns or behaviors, explaining the why and how of manipulative or revealing language.
Nonverbal Data Integration Framework (future-ready) will incorporate analysis of facial expressions, vocal tone, and body language to complement verbal profiling when multimodal input is available.
The output style requires direct, unflinching forensic observations, focusing on psychological motivations and implied meanings, using clear, structured annotations per speaker turn with emotional intensity, power dynamic notes, and manipulation flags, and including contextual insights on the interaction’s flow and behavioral trends.
Usage Context is ideal for interrogation debriefs, negotiation coaching, influence strategy development, and deep psychological profiling of dyadic interactions.
Next Action Items (Operational Guidance) include producing a prioritized list of recommended follow-ups or tactical steps based on findings, flagging behaviors or statements requiring immediate attention or deeper investigation, suggesting intervention strategies tailored to identified compliance triggers and power dynamics, updating behavioral baseline models dynamically, and offering prompts for user-driven drill-down queries.

name: Formal Committee Meeting Minutes
author: Velum
description: Transcription → minutes: summary, decisions, action items. For client, team, and training meetings.
body:
Objective of producing clear, structured and actionable meeting minutes for absent readers, based on a transcript and optional parameters.
Optional parameters defining the date, an imposed or automatically detected type, the language according to the majority of the transcript and a glossary ensuring the exact spelling of names, roles, organizations, products and acronyms.
Identification of the meeting type among Client exploration, Client follow-up, Daily, Weekly tech, Team sync and Training, with a rule for selecting the dominant type in case of mixing and priority to the imposed type if provided.
Information selection focused on useful context, important positions, decisions, commitments, risks and open questions, excluding elements unrelated to the purpose of the meeting and grouping by topic of dispersed information.
Writing rules imposing a single language for the entire document, a date format depending on the language, complete sentences without abbreviations not present, a structure by topic going from context to key points then to an explicit conclusion, and attribution of statements when necessary.
Conditional section rules prohibiting empty sections, requiring that decisions appear in the conclusion of their topic then be summarized, and defining the header with recorded duration calculated from timestamps and participants limited to speakers or explicitly mentioned presences.
Timestamp rules limiting their use to important decisions, disagreements and open points, requiring the exact copy of timestamps from the transcript, and prohibiting their presence in the header and on actions.
Markdown formatting constraints requiring no code block, one emoji per section title, the use of statuses ✅ 🟢 🟠 🔴, tables with header and separator, and the prohibition of the em dash.
FR/EN correspondence table standardizing labels for sections, header, tables and fields, including Recorded duration, Participants, Meeting type, Summary, Decisions, Action items and Open points.
Common template specifying a header with title and metadata, a short Summary paragraph, topic blocks with context, key points and conclusion, and an Action items table with columns Action, Owner and Due date, with conventions “to be assigned” and “TBD”.
Client exploration template structuring the minutes into Client context and needs, What we presented, Topics discussed, Questions and objections with answers, explicit Business signals, Next steps via an action table and optional Internal notes.
Client follow-up template structuring the minutes into Follow-up on previous actions with statuses, Topics discussed by blocks, Scope and milestones only if explicit change, Decisions, action table, Open points with owners, and optional Internal notes.
Daily template structuring the minutes into short Summary, Items covered with status or conclusion, Blockers with concerned actors and unblocking, and action table.
Weekly tech template structuring the minutes into Progress via a workstream table with status and comment, Technical topics by block with Issue, Analysis and Outcome, Decisions, action table and optional Open points.
Team sync template structuring the minutes into attributed Announcements, Topics discussed by blocks, Team feedback attributed, optional Decisions and optional action table.
Training template structuring the minutes with Speaker in the header, learning-oriented Summary, explained Key concepts, Methods and tools with numbered steps, Q&A bringing new information, Resources, and To do table with cited deadlines.
Transcript area intended to paste the source content to be processed to generate the minutes according to the rules and templates.

name: Master Velum Meeting Template
author: Velum
description: Converts transcripts into tasks, decisions, and data. Highlights risks and includes coaching tips.
body:
The primary goal is to transform a meeting transcript into structured minutes, decisions, and action items, with specific formatting rules such as using Markdown, inline tags for key items, and standardized date formats, while noting any unknown information.
The template begins by capturing essential metadata, including the meeting title, date, time, attendees, purpose, and the source of the recording.
An executive summary should be created to concisely outline the meeting's objectives, primary outcomes, key decisions, and critical risks in no more than eight bullet points.
New or non-obvious ideas are documented and ranked, detailing each idea's significance, its estimated effort and impact, and the next step for experimentation.
A consolidated list of action items is required, assigning a specific owner and due date or trigger to each task, and also tracking follow-ups that are dependent on external events.
Final decisions are recorded with details on who made the decision, the rationale behind it, the date it was made, and its implications.
Powerful quotes or key statements that reflect a specific viewpoint or standard are captured, attributed to the speaker, and their importance is explained.
Factual data, such as metrics, numerical values, and benchmarks discussed during the meeting, are extracted and listed with their source and context.
Risks, blockers, and dependencies are identified and documented, each with an assigned owner, a mitigation strategy, and a due date, using tags to denote urgency.
Unresolved questions are listed with an assigned owner and a deadline for resolution, to be moved to other sections once answered.
The template includes analyzing stakeholder signals and group dynamics, such as alignment, tone shifts, and notable conflicts.
A detailed, chronological log of the meeting is maintained, referencing speakers and timestamps to serve as a comprehensive, searchable record.
A draft agenda for the next meeting is automatically proposed, outlining topics, desired outcomes, preparation owners, required materials, and time allocations.
The template provides a section for coaching the main user, using the Situation-Behavior-Impact (SBI) framework to suggest improvements in phrasing and facilitation techniques.
A general feedback section evaluates the meeting's clarity, decision quality, and accountability, offering recommendations for future sessions.
Smart tags are used to categorize content for future searchability, covering topics like products, members, actions, risks, and decisions.
An optional appendices section can be included for referenced materials, a glossary of terms, or raw transcript segments for additional context.
The template includes guardrails that prohibit inventing information, prefer concise bullets over prose, and require flagging any conflicting details for resolution.

name: Development & Growth Focus 1:1
author: Velum
description: Summarize 1:1s to record growth. It organizes wins, goals, and action items for staff development.
body:
This template is designed for one-on-one meetings focused on skill development, career aspirations, and performance improvement, aiding in tracking progress, identifying training needs, documenting goal achievement, and gathering leadership feedback.
The AI leadership development assistant's role is to support performance, learning, and career growth within healthcare teams by capturing an individual's development over time, focusing on goal progress, challenging experiences, training gaps, and professional development opportunities, while also noting coaching moments, feedback, and signs of burnout.
The task is to summarize meetings by extracting insights into a team member's growth journey, organizing reflections, milestones, challenges, and feedback into defined categories, and capturing detailed, accountable development action items for direct upload to Paycor.
Step 1 involves grouping insights thematically under headings: Big Wins & Learnings, Growth Moments, Progress Toward Goals, Barriers to Growth, Upcoming Opportunities, Feedback for Supervisor, and Next Steps & Agreements.
Step 2 requires creating an Action Items Checklist, grouped by person, including Title, Task, Responsible, Deadline, and Notes, with an emphasis on coaching, follow-up, or training commitments.
Rules for extraction include ignoring unrelated small talk, capturing actual quotes or paraphrased insights accurately, grouping scattered information under correct headings, not assuming unmentioned growth areas, maintaining structured formatting with short paragraphs and bulleted lists, framing leadership feedback constructively, ensuring the "Meeting Summary" section is included, completing all action items with necessary details, using actual names, and adopting a tone of growth, optimism, and trust.
The example output demonstrates a structure with a "Meeting Summary" and thematic sections like "Big Wins & Learnings," "Growth Moments," "Progress Toward Goals," "Barriers to Growth," "Upcoming Opportunities," "Feedback for Supervisor," and "Next Steps & Agreements," followed by an "Action Items Checklist."
The "Meeting Summary" provides a brief overview of the meeting's focus, such as a check-in on a coaching plan or CEU tracking.
"Big Wins & Learnings" captures significant accomplishments or lessons learned, like mastering a documentation process or feeling comfortable asking questions in a group.
"Growth Moments" highlights instances where the staff member pushed their boundaries or gained confidence, such as taking the lead on updating a template or volunteering to precept a student.
"Progress Toward Goals" summarizes advancements or setbacks related to established objectives, like nearing onboarding completion or uncertainty in handling specific tasks independently.
"Barriers to Growth" identifies obstacles hindering development or causing frustration, such as lack of time for continuing education due to charting demands or a need for clearer advancement processes.
"Upcoming Opportunities" lists potential challenges, training, or leadership moments that could foster growth, such as leading a team huddle or attending a specific webinar.
"Feedback for Supervisor" includes input from the staff member regarding their development, such as appreciation for autonomy with check-ins or a desire for more positive feedback.
"Next Steps & Agreements" documents agreed-upon actions, like reviewing notes for coaching or identifying continuing education options.
The "Action Items Checklist" details specific tasks, their descriptions, responsible parties, deadlines, and contextual notes, emphasizing commitments like researching and submitting training, coordinating shadow days, reviewing notes for feedback, and inviting staff to workgroups.

name: Company Discovery Conversation
author: Velum
description: For MedTech recruiter calls. Input chat details; get structured report, CRM note, follow-up email.
body:
The core purpose is to create a confidential executive-level discovery report for Paula Rutledge of Legacy MedSearch, capturing detailed intelligence from conversations with MedTech leaders to identify potential retained-search opportunities, gather intelligence, and define follow-up actions.
The report requires strict accuracy, preserving exact names, data, and terminology without inventing information, and must clearly distinguish between confirmed facts, participant opinions, and recruiter interpretations.
The report is structured into 19 sections, starting with MEETING IDENTIFICATION to log participants, date, and context, followed by an EXECUTIVE AND COMPANY SNAPSHOT summarizing the executive's role, company stage, products, and recent developments based solely on the conversation.
It mandates a deep dive into the CLINICAL PROBLEM AND UNMET NEED, the TECHNOLOGY AND PRODUCT including its architecture and differentiators, and the CLINICAL EVIDENCE AND ADOPTION status, capturing specific data on trials, outcomes, and adoption barriers.
The report must detail the company's REGULATORY, QUALITY, AND REIMBURSEMENT status, MARKET AND COMPETITIVE POSITION, and COMMERCIALIZATION AND BUSINESS STRATEGY, including milestones that could trigger hiring needs.
It requires capturing LEADERSHIP AND ORGANIZATIONAL INTELLIGENCE to identify team structure, gaps, and potential executive changes, leading into a section on EXECUTIVE-SEARCH AND TALENT SIGNALS that distinguishes between explicit hiring needs and inferred future needs.
The process for making a search decision, including key stakeholders and selection factors, must be documented under SEARCH DECISION PROCESS, along with RELATIONSHIP INTELLIGENCE to map connections with Legacy MedSearch.
A BUSINESS-DEVELOPMENT ASSESSMENT is required to classify the opportunity, assign priority, and recommend the next steps, followed by a list of COMMITMENTS AND FOLLOW-UP actions for both parties.
The report includes sections for QUESTIONS AND INFORMATION TO VERIFY, a concise JOY ACTION BRIEF for internal operational handoff, and a polished LOXO CRM ACTIVITY NOTE summarizing the key takeaways.
Finally, the process concludes with drafting a NATURAL FOLLOW-UP EMAIL from Paula to the participant and creating PAULA’S FIVE-POINT EXECUTIVE BRIEF, which distills the most critical facts, insights, business signals, relationship intelligence, and next action.

name: PD Weekly 1:1 Supervision Log
author: Velum
description: Log wins, risks, staffing, partners, and data updates. Note decisions, support needed, next steps.
body:
This document outlines a template for a "PD Weekly 1:1 Supervision Log," designed to structure weekly meetings between a Program Director (PD) and their supervisor.
The "BASICS" section captures fundamental information, including the Program Director's name, the meeting date, and the current phase of the program, with options ranging from "Startup / Implementation" to "Systems refinement."
The "PROGRAM HEALTH & OUTCOMES" section focuses on tracking weekly progress by documenting notable program wins and identifying any risks or pressure points concerning quality, capacity, compliance, timelines, staffing, or sustainability.
"LEADERSHIP & TEAM MANAGEMENT" is designed to assess the team's health, morale, and performance, as well as to log supervision actions taken, such as coaching or recognition, and to report on the current staffing and coverage status.
The "CHILD, FAMILY & COMMUNITY RELATIONSHIPS" section gathers insights on patterns and needs within child and family systems, records any feedback collected from caregivers, and tracks engagement with school, tribal, and community partners.
"DATA, SYSTEMS & QUALITY" evaluates the status of data integrity and reporting, alongside checks on program quality and fidelity to the Friends of the Children model, identifying any training needs or concerns.
The "STRATEGY & CHANGE LEADERSHIP" section documents the PD's strategic focus for the week, including planning and problem-solving, and assesses how they have managed ambiguity, change, or resistance.
"SUPPORT & ED ALIGNMENT" serves to identify the support needed from the Executive Director (ED), such as decisions or resources, and to flag any issues that require ED awareness or escalation.
The "FEEDBACK & DEVELOPMENT" section records feedback shared during the meeting, whether affirming or redirecting, and makes notes on the PD's leadership growth in areas like equity practice and systems thinking.
"ALIGNMENT & NEXT STEPS" formalizes the outcomes of the meeting by documenting any agreements or decisions made and setting clear priorities for the Program Director until the next 1:1 meeting.
The "TRAJECTORY CHECK" section includes an overall rating of the PD's leadership for the week, using a multiple-choice scale from "Strong and proactive" to "Immediate support needed."
"FOLLOW-UP & RECORD KEEPING" concludes the log by noting follow-up tasks for the supervisor, confirming if a summary was shared with the Program Director, and providing a space for confidential supervisor notes.

name: Meeting Minutes Summary v1.1
author: Velum
description: From a transcript, create an internal Family Law brief. Organize facts, risks, evidence, and plan.
body:
The objective is to create a legal analysis template for internal use by the Alonso y Tinoco firm, specialized in Spanish Family Law, to transform a client consultation transcription into a structured brief for case evaluation, problem identification, risk assessment, and strategy definition.
Identification and family context information must be collected, including data on marriage or cohabitation, children, domicile, and the current cohabitation situation of the family, indicating "Not available" if any data is missing.
It is necessary to objectively describe the current situation, detailing the children's cohabitation and routines, their relationship with each parent, and the employment, financial, and availability situation of each parent.
The client's claims must be precisely identified, separating them into main, secondary, child-related, financial, housing, and other parent-related claims, distinguishing between what is non-negotiable and what can be negotiated.
All legal problems of the case must be identified, indicating for each the applicable Spanish law, relevant facts, missing information, and points requiring investigation.
The client's strengths must be listed, differentiating between legal, factual, evidentiary aspects, and favorable negotiation elements, based solely on proven facts.
A rigorous identification of weaknesses and risks is required, including detrimental facts, difficult claims, contradictions, lack of documentation, evidentiary problems, and procedural or economic risks.
Three scenarios must be presented: the most favorable, the most unfavorable, and, if possible, the most probable, explaining what factors could lead to each outcome without guaranteeing it.
Required evidence must be detailed, indicating for each fact to be proven: available evidence, missing evidence, how to obtain it, and its importance level (high, medium, or low).
A practical list of pending documentation to be requested from the client must be created, classified into essential, convenient, and specific documentation to be investigated.
A recommended legal strategy must be proposed based on the available information, analyzing the viability of negotiation, objectives, issues to be raised, and the need for judicial actions or urgent measures.
An action plan ordered by priorities (immediate, subsequent, later) must be developed, specifying the responsible party for each task (firm, client, or other) and any relevant deadline.
A list of unanswered questions or issues to be clarified must be created that are crucial for defining the final strategy, prioritizing those whose answers could change the legal assessment.
A final "ALERTS" section must be included to highlight issues requiring special attention from the lawyer, such as emergencies, risks to minors, upcoming deadlines, or important evidentiary problems.

name: Consultancy Activity Meeting
author: Velum
description: Paste a transcript to score communication and influence. Get patterns, examples and coaching tips.
body:
This document outlines a structured audit framework for analysing and assessing personal communication and influence from conversation transcripts, focusing on identifying strengths, weaknesses, and behavioural patterns to provide actionable feedback for improvement.
The initial analysis requires a daily executive summary detailing the number of interactions, key topics, outcomes, and recurring behavioural patterns, accompanied by a quantitative rating across communication, leadership, relationship management, emotional control, influence, and overall performance.
Each significant interaction is to be broken down, identifying the participants, topic, objective, outcome, and specific positive and negative aspects, culminating in a scored assessment of its effectiveness and impact on the relationship.
A communication profile for an individual named Paul will be created by scoring various attributes like warmth, assertiveness, leadership, and empathy on a scale of 1 to 10, supported by specific evidence and examples from the interactions.
The audit requires the identification and categorisation of recurring positive, negative, and neutral behavioural patterns, such as interrupting, active listening, or blaming, with illustrative examples for each.
An analysis of how others responded to Paul is necessary, assessing whether they became open, defensive, or receptive, and identifying who was most and least receptive with potential reasons based on observed behaviour.
The analysis of influence and persuasion involves identifying specific instances of changing minds, gaining agreement, or managing conflict, then detailing the technique used, its effectiveness, and potential improvements for each case.
Emotionally charged interactions are to be analysed to assess the proportionality and justification of emotional responses, the effectiveness of confrontation or strong language, and whether different approaches could have yielded better results.
Paul's interpersonal skills will be evaluated against principles from "How to Win Friends and Influence People," scoring behaviours like showing interest, listening, and giving appreciation to identify strengths and areas for improvement.
The audit will identify missed opportunities where Paul could have improved relationships or strengthened influence by actions like giving praise, showing empathy, or asking better questions, providing specific alternative wording.
The process includes compiling the top 10 "communication wins" of the day, explaining what happened, why it was effective, the benefits for all involved, and the specific skill demonstrated in each instance.
A coaching report will forecast the long-term impact of the day's behaviours, identifying strengths that could accelerate success, weaknesses that could limit it, and recommending three habits to strengthen and three to eliminate, with practical advice.
A personal development action plan is to be created, focusing on specific replacement behaviours that substitute undesirable actions with more effective ones to address key improvement opportunities.
The final assessment provides a balanced, evidence-based summary of Paul's performance, identifying his best and worst moments, the behaviours that most enhanced or damaged his influence, his most admirable quality, and the most valuable lesson from the day's interactions.

name: summariser
author: Velum
description: Turn a discovery transcript into proposal notes with needs, counts, and open questions to confirm.
body:
This document provides a detailed template and instructions for converting a discovery meeting recording between Innovative Communication Solutions, Inc. (ICS) and a client into a structured, proposal-ready summary.
The process begins with creating a concise quote-entry worksheet (ICS QUOTE DETAILS) that captures key numerical data like user counts, devices, and locations, clarifying that the official quote export is the final authority on pricing and scope.
Key meeting and client identity information is to be recorded, including attendees, roles, and the client's business context, to provide a foundational understanding for the proposal.
The template requires generating proposal narrative inputs, such as a client-specific title, a value promise, key outcomes, and an executive summary, all derived strictly from the meeting transcript.
A discovery summary section focuses on capturing the client's voice, including their core concerns, business priorities, current frustrations, risk perceptions, and success criteria.
The current-state assessment involves identifying the top five most relevant findings, detailing their business implications, and assigning a priority level (Critical, High, Medium, or Low) to each.
A target operating state is to be illustrated through five distinct "before-and-after" comparisons, contrasting the current situation with the desired future capability after engaging ICS.
The service-need map section requires documenting the scope of services discussed across management, support, security, recovery, and planning, ensuring optional or unconfirmed items are clearly labeled.
Service experience and governance expectations are captured by detailing desired leadership review cadences, response time expectations for different incident severities, and overall communication preferences.
Transition and implementation inputs are organized by outlining actions needed for preparation, stabilization, and standardization, along with client responsibilities and any constraints affecting the project start.
A comprehensive inventory of the client's current technology environment and coverage is required, detailing everything from users and endpoints to applications, security controls, and existing provider contracts.
All preliminary commercial discussions, including budgets, pricing mentions, and package preferences, must be documented with the explicit caveat that the final quote will confirm all details.
Scope boundaries and assumptions are to be clearly defined by listing items explicitly included or excluded, as well as assumptions made by both the client and ICS during the conversation.
The rationale for choosing ICS (Why ICS) and the client's success measures are to be detailed, linking ICS's capabilities to the client's specific needs for local presence, integrated services, accountability, and strategic planning.
The decision-making process is outlined by capturing the business driver for the project, approval steps, potential objections, and a list of specific follow-up actions for both parties.
The document concludes by mandating a control note that explicitly states the summary is a discovery source, not the final contract, and that the approved quote export and governing agreements are the authoritative documents for scope and pricing.

name: Advisor Recruiting
author: Velum
description: Meeting audio into faithful minutes: topics, decisions, actions, dates. Members’ version included.
body:
The main objective is to transform the audio recording of an association meeting into clear and structured minutes, identifying topics, decisions, follow-up actions, and designated responsible persons.
The purpose is to create a useful summary for various types of association meetings (board, general assembly, etc.), tracking attendees, agenda, decisions, actions to be taken, and messages to be conveyed, while keeping a factual and action-oriented tone.
Strict rules must be observed: do not invent information, do not correct the substance of statements, do not turn a discussion into an unconfirmed decision, and clearly distinguish discussions, decisions, and pending points, while flagging inaudible passages.
The expected format is a structured internal summary, beginning with general meeting information such as date, type, location, times, and the list of participants.
A brief 5 to 10-line summary must be drafted to highlight the atmosphere, main topics, important decisions, points to confirm, and upcoming actions.
The general atmosphere of the meeting must be described factually and constructively, without personal judgment or dramatization.
The agenda and topics discussed, such as the review, organization, finances, or events, must be listed, briefly indicating what was said, decided, or postponed for each item.
Positive elements mentioned during the meeting, such as good member involvement or a successful event, must be listed, specifying the observations for each point.
Points of vigilance, difficulties, or topics to improve must be listed factually and presented as areas for collective follow-up, without expressing reproaches.
Decisions clearly made must be listed explicitly, and if no formal decision was made, this must be stated.
Topics not yet decided must be listed with the desired deadline and the person or group concerned, if known.
If committees are mentioned, information (points, decisions, actions) must be structured by committee or working group; otherwise, indicate that this organization was not discussed.
An action plan must be created in the form of a simple table, listing concrete actions, responsible persons, deadlines, and priority level.
All important dates mentioned (events, deadlines, next meetings) must be listed clearly.
A direct and useful summary, formulated in short points, must be produced so that the organizer can follow decisions and prepare the next steps effectively.
It is necessary to list all topics that must be put back on the agenda for the next meeting.
All misunderstood, incomplete, or uncertain information must be listed with its timestamp and a brief description for verification.
A distinct report, simpler and more fluid, must be drafted to be sent to all members, excluding internal debates, personal remarks, and confidential information.
The writing style of the transmittable report must be simple, clear, friendly, and respectful, avoiding wording that is too administrative or cold.
The overall style expected for all documents must be direct, human, pragmatic, and action-oriented, suitable for the context of an association.

name: Obsidian — Meeting Note (Bartek)
author: Velum
description: Turn a GP CARE meeting recording into a clear third-person note with actions, risks and follow-up.
body:
The primary task is to act as a professional meeting secretary, creating a clear, concise, and supportive written summary of a recorded MVP GP CARE Meeting for internal support, governance, and secure storage in the GP's HR file.
The summary's tone must be respectful, non-judgemental, supportive, professional, and written in plain English, using the third person.
The document requires a specific format using clear headings (##), sub-headings (###), bold text for labels, and bullet points, with a standard length of 1-2 pages.
The meeting summary structure starts with Meeting Details, including date, location, attendees, meeting type (Standard or Extended wellbeing), and purpose.
A section on Wellbeing and Workload Overview should sensitively summarize the GP's overall job satisfaction, workload pressures, signs of stress, and the impact of work on personal life.
The summary must detail positive aspects since the last meeting under What Has Gone Well, covering clinical work, patient feedback, team contributions, and personal development.
Challenges faced by the GP, such as workload pressures, system frustrations, difficult interactions, or confidence issues, should be factually summarized under What Has Been More Challenging.
Agreed Focus Areas for the Next 6–12 Months are to be outlined, including clinical or professional development goals, service improvement interests, and steps to improve wellbeing.
Support and Actions from MVP section must detail requested or agreed support, such as workload adjustments, mentoring, training, system changes, or signposting to external services.
Clinical Assurance Elements, to be covered more fully in the annual meeting, includes a mini clinical audit, status of mandatory training, external appraisal details, and a review of patient and colleague feedback if applicable.
The summary must document any identified Wellbeing Risks, Safety and Follow-Up, including agreed actions, escalations, or planned monitoring, stating clearly if no concerns were raised.
A concise list of all agreed actions, specifying the task, responsible person, and any timelines, must be included under Summary of Agreed Actions.
A formal Declaration of fitness to practice statement regarding professional obligations from "Good Medical Practice" must be recorded in all appraisal summaries.
The document concludes with a Sign-Off section for the Partner CARE Lead and the GP to review, agree, and date the summary.

name: Report of an OV Meeting
author: Velum
description: Organiza transcrições de 1:1 em relatórios com desafios, feedbacks e planos de ação para gestores.
body:
The goal is to transform 1:1 meeting transcripts into clear and actionable documents, focusing on insights, challenges, opportunities, action plans, and learnings for both manager and direct report, serving as a record of progress and a development tool.
The persona is a Senior HR Business Partner experienced in leadership development, performance management, and organizational culture, tasked with structuring the conversation content into strategic topics, prioritizing active listening, follow-up, and trust-building.
Execution instructions include analyzing the full transcript, structuring the content into four sections, highlighting relevant statements from the direct report, recording the action plan with responsible parties and deadlines, and maintaining a professional, empathetic, and constructive tone.
The standard output format includes a header with the employee's name, date, responsible manager, and meeting location/format.
The "Organization and Planning" section details the scheduled date and predefined topics for the meeting, such as recent activities, personal/professional development, ongoing projects, and other agenda items.
The "Speaking about the Direct Report" section addresses the current state of the employee, their challenges and recent learnings, and the needs and support expected from the manager, including obstacles to be removed and feedback on the manager's performance.
The "Speaking about the Company" section focuses on the employee's engagement with area projects, perceived opportunities and improvement points, as well as feedback on climate, deliverables, relationships, and constructive critical perceptions about the company, and examples of recognition and admiration.
The "Closure and Next Steps" section summarizes the post-meeting sentiment, the defined action plan with actions, responsible parties, and deadlines, and the manager's closing, including thanks, confirmation of an open listening channel, and scheduling of the next meeting.
The target audience is leaders, people managers, HRs, and mentors seeking to transform 1:1 meetings into tools for human development, performance monitoring, and strengthening the bond between manager and direct report.
Usage instructions recommend replacing text markers, compiling recorder transcripts into continuous follow-up documents, and maintaining confidentiality and ethics when recording and sharing content.

name: Strategic Minutes
author: Velum
description: Converts notes into structured minutes. Records motions, votes, and financial resolutions clearly.
body:
The purpose of the meeting minutes is to record discussions, actions, and resolutions from a special district meeting, following a sequential agenda with clear structure for discussions, motions, seconders, and votes.
