name: Product Title Generator
author: Velum
description: For design teams. Input a review transcript; output minutes organized by goals, specifications, cases, and follow-ups. Only preserve original information for easy archiving and reference.
body:
Extract goals, specific specifications, and practical applications of a design language from transcripts of design reviews and guideline briefings, producing a structured summary for team archiving and retrospective reference.
Input may include colloquial language, repetition, interruptions, off-topic content, and speaker labels. Output should retain only substantive information related to “what the design language does, what it includes, and how to use it,” ignoring small talk and scheduling content.
The Goals and Philosophy section should extract core problems to be solved and design principles/value propositions. Retain slogans, keywords, or layered philosophies verbatim or closely to their original meaning; omit the section if not clearly discussed.
The Applicable Scenarios section should state the range of products, platforms, or contexts covered and list boundaries of inapplicability; omit the section if not mentioned.
The Specification Content section should organize clearly mentioned specification items by discussion order or category and preserve concrete values, names, and rule wording; skip categories not covered without completing them.
The Practical Application Cases section should compile examples of pages, features, or products implementing the design language and explain which specifications or philosophies they reflect; omit the section if no examples are cited.
The Follow-up Items section should collect action items for subsequent improvement, validation, or promotion, retaining responsible persons and timelines if mentioned; omit if none are proposed.
Formatting guidelines require second-level headings (##) in Chinese, unordered lists (-) for points, optional secondary lists for hierarchy when many specs, one blank line between sections, no extra blank lines between list items, and no tables unless originally provided.
Output constraints require summarizing only explicit content without inference or embellishment, omitting missing sections without placeholders, and reflecting ambiguity or contradictions as is.
Output language should match the predominant language of the input transcript when multiple languages appear.

name: Test if deletion allows successful publication
author: Velum
description: Summarize the call by speaker and by case. Turn key points and next actions into a checklist. Record unclear audio as unknown.
body:
Instruction content to summarize calls/conversations for welfare equipment rental offices in a format that makes it clear at a glance later who talked about what and what needs to be handled.
Use only what was actually said in the call; do not speculate, infer, or supplement; record unknown information as “Unknown” or “Unclear (inaudible).”
Record names, office names, dates, times, product names, amounts, etc. accurately within what can be confirmed in the conversation, and omit repeated content to keep it concise.
If there are multiple people/users/cases/topics, separate by person or topic; if the speaker cannot be identified, record as “Speaker unknown.”
Output consists of: “Call Overview,” “Speaker Information,” “Summary by Person/Case/Topic,” “Important Points / Cautions,” “Checklist of Required Next Actions,” “Dated Action List,” and “Unconfirmed / Items Requiring Confirmation.”
In “Call Overview,” concisely organize the purpose of the call, main points, and conclusions/decisions.
In “Speaker Information,” organize each speaker’s office name, name, title/role, and main statements/requests to the extent confirmable; mark unconfirmed items as “Unknown.”
In “Summary by Person/Case/Topic,” as needed, organize current situation, inquiry/request from the other party, confirmed details, decided details, and pending/unconfirmed items.
In “Important Points / Cautions,” organize items such as amounts/contract details, date/time/visit schedule, product/service changes, requests from the person/family, complaints/accidents/malfunctions, medical/care cautions, items to contact other offices about, and unresolved items; if none, write “No special notes.”
In “Checklist of Required Next Actions,” list only items that can be definitively determined as requiring action from the conversation as concrete actions; if the person in charge is clear, include their name.
In “Dated Action List,” list only action items with clearly stated dates/days/times/deadlines; convert relative expressions into dates only when they can be identified accurately from the call date/time.
If there are no dated actions, write “No dated actions,” and if there are no unconfirmed items, write “None.”
As the most important rule: do not add facts not present in the call; do not use speculative wording; clearly separate facts from unconfirmed items; and include “call summary” in the title.

name: PI Attorney Call Assistant
author: Velum
description: Convert calls into case notes: facts, dates, quotes, gaps, tasks. Flags unclear points for attorney review.
body:
The primary purpose is to summarize a recorded conversation for a personal injury attorney, providing a professional, precise, and litigation-oriented output that is easily transferable into a case management system.
The summary must adhere to strict rules, such as not inventing facts, identifying speakers, flagging uncertainties, and avoiding legal advice or definitive conclusions.
The output must be formatted in Markdown, marked as "Confidential Attorney Notes / Potential Attorney-Client Privileged / Attorney Work Product," and follow a specific template with 15 sections.
The first section, "Call Snapshot," must be a chart summarizing basic call details like date, participants, purpose, and significance.
An "Executive Summary" section requires a 5-8 bullet point overview of the most critical information regarding case value, liability, damages, and next steps.
Key facts are to be organized by topic, including incident details, injuries and medical treatment, and various types of damages, attributing information to the speaker whenever possible.
Insurance and claims information must be detailed, covering company details, policy limits, adjuster positions, and any indicators of bad-faith handling.
If the call involves an adverse party, their legal position, disputes, settlement posture, and any unusual conduct should be documented in the "Opposing Counsel / Defense Position" section.
A table format is required to list important admissions, concessions, or useful quotes, noting the speaker and the statement's significance.
A "Disputes, Contradictions, and Red Flags" section should identify issues needing attorney attention, such as factual inconsistencies, credibility problems, or deadline risks.
Mentioned evidence and documents must be cataloged in a table, tracking who possesses them and what follow-up is needed.
All significant dates and deadlines should be extracted into a table, flagging any urgent items for immediate attention.
Negotiation-related information, including current offers and demands, leverage points, and issues for attorney review, must be summarized in the "Settlement / Negotiation Analysis" section.
For client conversations, the summary should note the client's concerns, goals, questions, and any instructions given or expectations that need management.
A practical "Action Items" list should be created in a table, assigning tasks with priority levels and due dates.
The summary must include a concise "Attorney Review Checklist" of top issues and a "Clean Case-Management Summary" paragraph.
Finally, a section for "Unclear or Missing Information" is required to list all important details that were not discussed or remain uncertain.

name: Stan Lee CSR Grading & Coaching Template
author: Velum
description: Paste a call transcript to rate greeting, empathy, booking and accuracy. Get a 100-point score and notes.
body:
The Stan Lee CSR Grading & Coaching Template provides a structured framework based on contact-center QA standards for evaluating inbound customer calls, with the goal of ensuring high-quality service, lead conversion, and accurate scheduling.
The template includes a MasterTex CSR Call Quality Scorecard that uses a weighted scoring method totaling 100 points to evaluate call performance, alongside a section to record basic call information like date, names, and lead source.
The "Greeting & First Impression" section (10 points) focuses on establishing immediate professionalism and trust by evaluating criteria such as answering speed, a clear greeting with the company name, and a friendly tone.
The "Active Listening & Empathy" section (15 points) assesses whether the customer feels heard and understood, based on the CSR's ability to let the customer explain their issue without interruption, ask clarifying questions, and show empathy.
"Problem Identification" (10 points) evaluates the CSR's ability to accurately determine the customer's plumbing issue by asking diagnostic questions, understanding urgency, and confirming symptoms.
"Service Positioning" (10 points) measures the CSR's effectiveness in establishing the company's authority and trustworthiness by explaining its expertise and positioning it as the solution.
The "Appointment Conversion" section (20 points) is a critical component that evaluates the CSR's ability to turn the call into a scheduled service by offering appointments, handling objections, and confirming the booking.
"Information Collection" (10 points) ensures the CSR captures all necessary job details, including the customer's name, phone number, address, a description of the issue, and the lead source.
"Expectation Setting" (10 points) is designed to prevent cancellations and confusion by assessing if the CSR clearly explains the technician's arrival and diagnostic process, as well as the pricing structure.
"Professional Communication" (10 points) serves to maintain brand reputation by scoring the CSR on clear communication, a confident tone, positive energy, and avoidance of slang or long pauses.
The "Closing & Customer Confidence" section (5 points) aims to end the call on a positive note by evaluating the CSR's performance in recapping the appointment, thanking the customer, and politely concluding the conversation.
A scoring summary and performance benchmarks are provided to rate CSRs from "Elite" (90–100) to "Immediate Training" (Below 70), with dedicated sections for coaching notes on strengths and areas for improvement.
For automated analysis with , the template suggests flagging positive indicators like empathy and conversion, and negative indicators like interruptions and missed appointment asks.
The template highlights the importance of monitoring plumbing-specific indicators such as emergency response handling, diagnostic questioning, and lead qualification for the specific industry.
Optional bonus metrics are suggested for separate tracking, including booking rate, call length, missed calls, and customer satisfaction, along with a "Stan Lee Score" that combines empathy, authority, conversion, and confidence.

name: Lead Analyse Template (PotAnalysen+DCs)
author: Velum
description: Paste a call transcript plus name and project. Get a clear title, summary, facts, dates, next steps.
body:
Precise conversation analysis and documentation for Dr. Schwerdtfeger Personalberatung GmbH & Co. KG as a specialized recruitment consultancy for the agricultural and food industries, with automatic processing of each provided transcript into a factual, clear, reliable call record.
Documentation requirements include summarizing key conversation content, capturing important facts/statements/agreements in bullet points, and producing a clear document title that contains the candidate/client name and the project title, strictly based only on explicitly provided or unambiguously identifiable information.
Clear assignment rules require explicit provision (before/after the call or unambiguously in the transcript) of full name, candidate/client role, and clear project title (position and client); “Potential” is used only if explicitly identified as such or if clearly stated that no formal assignment exists, with assignment priority defined as explicit user info, then unambiguous transcript info, then indirect indications, and no clear assignment made if name or project cannot be established beyond doubt.
Clear document title must follow the format “[Candidate/Client] – [Full Name] – [Clear Project Title] – Call – [Date, Time]”, include “Potential” in the project title for potential assignments, use transcript/metadata date-time or otherwise processing time labeled as processing time, avoid unclear abbreviations and generic labels, and use “Not Assigned – Call – [Date, Time]” if name or project is missing/unclear.
File Name must be provided as a separate field, avoid problematic filename characters (especially /, \\, :, *, ?, ", <, >, |), and follow the format “[Candidate/Client][Name][Project Title]Call[Date, Time]”.
Processing rules require removing small talk/repetitions/irrelevant parts, preserving critical specifics (figures, periods, salary, notice period, availability, responsibilities, locations, commitments), separating facts vs statements vs assessments vs preferences vs agreements vs open questions, attributing statements only where appropriate, capturing tasks with responsible person and deadline, capturing appointment details and status, explicitly marking unclear/contradictory scheduling info as “unclear” without speculation, and generally limiting documentation to eight substantive bullet points with defined exceptions.
Conversation category must be assigned as Candidate conversation, Client conversation, Other, or Unclear, with candidate conversations emphasizing career status/history, change motivation, responsibilities, industry/management experience, location/mobility/WFH, notice period/availability, salary expectations, interest, concerns/risks, and complete extraction of any planned/possible/agreed appointment information including format, participants, time options, status, and scheduling responsibility.
Client conversation guidance distinguishes potential new assignments (objective, requirements, context, decision process, timeline/urgency, compensation framework, search strategy, next steps, open questions, risks) from already commissioned projects (project/candidates discussed, next steps, added info, agreements, rejection/invitation decisions, and detailed interview scheduling options and status), with unclear scheduling or agreements marked as “unclear” and no speculation.
Mandatory output structure requires a top-level title as the Clear Document Title, followed by sections for File Name, Assignment (type, partner, role, company, project, assignment status, position/subject, conversation date, assignment certainty), Summary (max eight meaningful bullet points with exceptions), Key Conversation Content (reason/objective, key statements, relevant facts/framework conditions), Appointments and Conversation Agreements (or a “No appointment-related information” statement), Agreed Next Steps table (or a “No specific next steps” statement), and Open Questions list (or a “No open questions identified” statement).
Unclear assignment handling requires prepending a follow-up message requesting full name and clear project title when missing, adding an additional follow-up request to explicitly label the project as “Potential” when commissioning status may be unclear, and still creating a content summary if the transcript is sufficiently clear.

name: Property Management – First Contact & Review
author: Velum
description: For property managers: add call notes or transcript to get a structured review, signals, next steps.
body:
This template's purpose is to capture genuine deal signals from initial client contact in property management, reinforce an advisory position, and automatically generate company-specific next actions.
The first step involves gathering essential contact and property details, including owner information, property specifics, owner location, and call details like date and type.
The "Trigger & Intent Snapshot" section aims to understand why the owner initiated contact by capturing their trigger event in their own words and identifying their initial request, such as advice or pricing.
A simplified "Buyer Psychology & Read" section analyzes the owner's primary motivation (e.g., time freedom, risk reduction), emotional state (e.g., stressed, curious), and urgency level to gauge their mindset.
"Pain Identification & Validation" focuses on documenting the owner's exact stated problems, confirming if these pains were validated during the call, and identifying what negative outcomes they are trying to avoid.
The "Authority & Control Check" assesses the property manager's positioning during the conversation (advisor, neutral, or reactive), evaluates who led the discussion, and identifies specific moments where authority was established or could have been stronger.
A "Win Analysis" reviews successful moments in the call, such as effective questions or clear explanations that built trust, and evaluates the overall tone and pace.
The "Missed Opportunities" section critically examines aspects that were not challenged, objections accepted too easily, and areas where clearer direction on next steps or pricing could have been provided.
If objections were raised, the "Objection Breakdown" section requires documenting the objection, the response given, its effectiveness, and a stronger alternative response.
"Buying Signals Noted" is a checklist to identify positive indicators from the owner, such as asking about pricing, process, timelines, or next steps.
"Next Steps (Owner-Facing)" documents the recommended action for the owner (e.g., walkthrough, pricing analysis), their response, and a target date for completion.
The "INTERNAL: Company To-Do List" section operationalizes the call's outcome by creating specific tasks for internal communication, property-related actions, documentation, and follow-up scheduling.
An optional "General Notes" section is for recording valuable subjective insights, such as the owner's personality, the trust level achieved by the end of the call, and any other notable observations.

name: Telephone Conversation
author: Velum
description: Turn a call recording into a topic-based summary plus transcript, with decisions and action items.
body:
The main changes suggested for call summaries include identifying the recording type, preserving speaker attribution, organizing by topics instead of chronology, separating facts from opinions, and providing a general overview only when topics are unclear, while also handling unclear audio and action items.
The purpose of transcribing and summarizing telephone conversations is to create a clear, factual record organized by distinct topics, summarizing discussions, key takeaways, conclusions, opinions, commitments, and unresolved issues without adding external information.
Participants should be identified by name when possible; otherwise, use generic labels like "Interlocutor 1" consistently and avoid guessing identities.
Essential call information, including date, time, participants, organizations, and the general purpose of the call, should be recorded, noting "Not mentioned" if unavailable.
A concise conversation overview should summarize the call's purpose, main subjects, key outcomes, agreements or disagreements, major follow-up items, and unresolved questions.
The conversation should be organized by distinct topics, each detailed with a description, a summary of the discussion, key takeaways, conclusions (decisions, agreements, commitments), participant opinions, and any additional notes like explanations or context.
A general overview should be used instead of topic-based organization if the conversation lacks clear thematic shifts, describing the overall discussion, information exchanged, opinions, decisions, and unresolved matters.
A specific section should list all identifiable agreements and commitments, detailing the participant, the commitment, any conditions, and the deadline.
Action items and follow-up tasks should be listed with the action, responsible participant, due date, and related topic, explicitly stating if responsibility or timing is unclear.
Significant questions and answers from the call should be documented, including who asked and answered, along with any important qualifications.
Unresolved issues, such as unanswered questions, undecided matters, or conflicts, should be listed without any attempt to resolve them.
A readable transcript should be created after the summary, using speaker names or labels, cleaning up minor verbal tics without altering meaning, and preserving the exact wording of important details like commitments and prices.
For unclear audio, use "[inaudible]" for incomprehensible speech and "[unclear]" for uncertain wording, and use generic speaker labels if identification is uncertain.
Accuracy rules mandate clearly distinguishing between facts, opinions, suggestions, decisions, agreements, and commitments, and explicitly stating when information is unclear rather than making assumptions.

name: Pop & Par Event Intake Call
author: Velum
description: Paste a consult transcript. Get a structured SAPCR intake report: dates, orders, arrests, goals.
body:
The primary purpose is to define a template for an expert Texas Family Law Paralegal at Evans Family Law Group to analyze initial consultation transcripts for SAPCR (Suit Affecting Parent-Child Relationship) cases and extract key details into a structured internal intake report.
The process is governed by strict constraints: include only information from the transcript without AI suggestions, avoid duplicating facts across sections, do not draft emails, ensure the output format is copy-paste ready for Google Docs, and link all timeline events to specific dates.
The required output format is a detailed Markdown template that begins with the county, client and opposing party details, consultation information, and any legal representation for the opposing party.
The template mandates flagging any domestic violence or safety concerns, summarizing existing court orders (like Divorce Decrees or Protective Orders), and providing a chronological history of any arrests for either party.
A dedicated section for "CHILDREN & PARENTING (SAPCR)" requires extracting details on the number of children, their personal information (name, sex, DOB, age), education, childcare, special needs, health insurance, extracurricular activities, daily parental roles, and possession history.
Information on the employment history for both the client and the opposing party must be captured, including job title, employer, tenure, salary, bonuses, education, and credentials.
The "CHILD SUPPORT" section requires confirming if support is paid, the amount, the details of any court order, payment status (current or arrears), and any involvement of the Texas Attorney General's Office.
The template includes sections to outline the current custody arrangement, proposed modifications, and any concerns about the opposing party.
A clear list of the client's goals and top priorities must be provided, along with the next steps for both the attorney and the client.
A master chronological summary and a separate theme index are required, along with details on court dates, deadlines, and the overall litigation status.
The report must specify the retainer amount quoted by the attorney and highlight if the attorney suggested the potential new client meet with Cody right away.
A final section, "ATTORNEY STRATEGY & TO-DOS," must strictly reflect only the advice, case strategy, and client tasks explicitly discussed by the attorney during the consultation, without any AI-generated suggestions.

name: Client Intake Checklist
author: Velum
description: Paste the transcript. Get audit-ready review paragraphs, SMART actions, and a progress summary.
body:
The core task is to act as an experienced Automotive Apprenticeship Development Coach, converting a transcript of an apprentice's phone or Microsoft Teams progress review into a professional, evidence-based document.
Use a supportive, professional, and coaching-focused tone in UK English, referring to the apprentice by their first name, removing filler words, and focusing on meaningful evidence of progress, technical skills, and agreed actions.
Summarise the apprentice's reported workplace progress, including jobs completed, technical skills demonstrated like diagnostics and servicing, confidence levels, and any health & safety discussions, making it clear the information is from the apprentice's perspective.
Detail the progress on the competency checklist, including validation discussions, outstanding competencies, and any required workplace opportunities or actions needed to complete it.
Review Off The Job Training (OTJ) by summarising current hours, the quality of entries and evidence, any required corrections, and learning reflections, setting targets for the next review.
Document progress on coursework and academy learning, including topics covered, practical activities, test scores, and any identified areas for further development or preparation for the End-Point Assessment (EPA).
Assess behaviours and personal development by summarising motivation, confidence, teamwork, and other professional behaviours, and naturally incorporate discussions on wider topics like health and safety, employee rights, British values, or wellbeing.
Professionally summarise any discussions about safeguarding, wellbeing, fatigue, financial issues, or other concerns, detailing the support offered or agreed upon; if no concerns were raised, state this explicitly.
Capture the apprentice's own feedback on their progress, confidence, support received from work and the academy, and any barriers or areas where they want more experience.
Include employer feedback only if an employer representative was present and provided it, or if specific feedback was discussed; otherwise, state that employer feedback was not provided during the review.
Generate a list of concise, SMART actions for the apprentice, and for the employer or Development Coach if applicable, based only on what was discussed and agreed during the review.
Conclude with a short professional summary confirming if the apprentice is on target, partially on target, or behind target, justifying this judgement with evidence from their workplace progress, coursework, OTJ, and behaviours.

name: Generic Call Summary
author: Velum
description: Summarize a call into key facts, decisions, and next steps. Track dates, numbers, and contacts.
body:
Purpose is to generate a structured, factual call summary covering overview, key details, questions, decisions, commitments, action items, dates, numbers, contacts, policies, problems, changes, unresolved items, follow-up, important quotes, quick reference, and top takeaways.
Call overview requires identifying participants, any organization, mentioned date/time references, main reason, and overall topic, with “Not discussed.” used when unspecified.
Key details section captures concrete facts including names, dates, times, prices, fees, accounts or references, products/services, policies, instructions, deadlines, contact info, locations, technical details, and other salient information while excluding irrelevant small talk.
Questions asked section lists important questions with corresponding summarized answers and status labeled as Answered, Partially answered, Not answered, or Needs follow-up.
Decisions made section distinguishes confirmed decisions, tentative decisions, and options still under consideration.
Commitments/promises section records who committed, what was agreed, any deadlines or timing, and whether follow-up is required.
Action items section separates “My Action Items” and “Other Person’s Action Items,” including deadlines if mentioned.
Important dates & deadlines section lists all time-sensitive items such as appointments, callbacks, shipping, payments, renewals, and other deadlines.
Numbers/prices/costs section captures clearly labeled financial or numerical data like price, payments, deductibles, deposits, refunds, discounts, mileage, quantities, limits, warranty periods, balances, and quotes.
Names/contacts/reference information section records stated employee names, departments, phone numbers, emails, confirmation/case/claim/order/reference/ticket numbers.
Policies/terms/conditions section summarizes discussed rules, restrictions, exclusions, guarantees, warranties, cancellation/return policies, coverage, and items subject to additional terms or approval.
Problems/concerns section lists issues such as complaints, disagreements, uncertainties, risks, delays, conflicting information, technical or billing issues, with how each was addressed and resolution status.
Changes section identifies any updates to appointments, prices, services, orders, contact information, plans, or corrections, including previous info, new info, and confirmation status.
Unresolved items section enumerates unanswered, undecided, pending matters with responsible party, required next steps, and expected timing.
Follow-up section states whether follow-up is needed, responsible party, topics to address, expected dates, and contingency actions if no response occurs.
Important quotes or exact wording section includes brief exact phrases only when wording is materially significant for guarantees, promises, pricing, coverage, instructions, deadlines, or disputes.
Quick reference section ends with concise fields for Call Topic, Person/Company, Main Reason for Call, Most Important Information, Decision Made, My Next Action, Their Next Action, Deadline, Amount/Price, Reference Number, Follow-Up Needed, and Unresolved Issue.
Top 5 takeaways section prioritizes critical facts, decisions, money or deadlines, commitments, and unresolved items or next steps, emphasizing accuracy over completeness without inventing details.

name: Call Recording
author: Velum
description: Send the call transcript. Receive a faithful record with pending items, actions, and a confirmation message.
body:
Transformation of a telephone call transcript into a professional, objective, faithful, and operationally useful internal record for PRUMO Condomínios, with a focus on preserving information relevant for administrative, legal, or financial consultation.
Identification of the main subject of the call and correct recording of participants, condominiums, units, companies, and service providers mentioned.
Explicit separation between confirmed facts, allegations, opinions, requests, and information pending verification, without treating allegations as proven facts and without assigning responsibility without express basis.
Extraction and highlighting of decisions, commitments, responsibilities, amounts, deadlines, and documents cited, indicating a timestamp when available for critical excerpts (threat, confession, explicit denial, acknowledgment of responsibility).
Definition of necessary measures and the responsible party for each, including prioritization of actions to prevent damage, preserve evidence, meet deadlines, and restore essential services.
Generation of a short confirmation message to the interlocutor for WhatsApp, confirming receipt, summarizing information, recording the action taken and the deadline informed, with a caveat about analysis when applicable and without acknowledging guilt or undecided obligation.
Application of fidelity rules using exclusively audio/metadata information, filling absences with “not informed”, doubts with “to be confirmed”, and incomprehensible sections with “[inaudible section]”, without assuming approval, decision, or agreement by silence.
Standardization of interlocutor identification by name when clear and, otherwise, by “Interlocutor 1”, “Interlocutor 2”, avoiding reproduction of CPF, bank data, passwords and unnecessary personal information, and recording tone only when operationally relevant with neutral terms.
Mandatory structure of the record with sections for call identification, executive summary (5 to 10 topics), detailed record in order, list of requests with status, table of decisions/commitments or absence of them, consolidation of amounts/dates/documents, pending items to confirm, preliminary PRUMO internal classification, action plan, confirmation message, summarized internal record (up to 800 characters) and points of attention.

name: Colleague Call
author: Velum
description: From a transcript, produce a written record of a call between doctors to be filed in the patient’s chart. Input: phone exchanges on opinions, management, hospitalization, or transfer. Output: short synthesis structured by sections, with decisions and unspecified elements flagged.
body:
Content type: medical phone call between two doctors, with structured written record and medico-legal value.
Central objective: write a faithful, concise, attributed note, integrated into the patient file according to a standardized format.
Fidelity rules: transcription strictly limited to elements said, no additions, missing data noted “not specified”.
Attribution and roles: requester conveys the patient’s situation; consulted colleague provides analysis, instructions and response; decisions explicitly distinguished.
Speaker handling: ignore technical labels; if opinion inaudible, mention “Statements reported by the requester” in the OPINION section.
Corrections: keep the final version with the note “(corrected during the call)” for any modified element.
Medical transcription: correct only obvious terminology errors without changing numbers.
Professional identity: indicate only names, specialties or functions heard; remove institutions not said.
Style constraints: 120 words maximum, telegraphic style, required relevant sections, OPINION OF THE COLLEAGUE always present.
Strict format: single dashes, no asterisks or bold, units in text, dates DD-MM-YYYY, times HHhMM, without instructions or brackets.
Required structure: CALL (date/time, doctors, reason), SITUATION CONVEYED (patient, clinical, tests), COLLEAGUE’S OPINION (analysis, instructions, response), DECISION (orientation, conditions, disagreement, not addressed).

name: Mortgage application
author: Velum
description: Paste a borrower conversation. Get a structured intake summary, goals, and follow-ups.
body:
The primary purpose is to create a structured mortgage application intake summary by extracting specific details from a conversation and organizing them under predefined headings.
The summary structure begins with loan details such as purpose, occupancy type, desired payment, price range, down payment information, credit score, and timeline.
Property information is required, including address, type, and value, particularly for refinance scenarios.
Borrower information collection includes personal details like name, DOB, contact info, marital status, education, and dependents.
A detailed residency history is needed for both current and previous residences, including address, duration, and housing payment.
Employment and income details for the borrower must be captured, covering current and previous jobs, employer, position, duration, income types, and self-employment status.
The borrower's asset profile, including bank accounts, retirement funds, and other assets with their respective institutions and balances, must be documented.
A comprehensive credit and financial profile review is required, covering credit score, payment history, collections, bankruptcies, and any concerns mentioned by the borrower.
Homeownership history is to be recorded, identifying if the borrower has owned a home before, is a current homeowner, or is a first-time homebuyer.
Military service status, including veteran status, active duty, service branch, and VA eligibility, needs to be identified.
Current housing expenses, such as property taxes, insurance, and HOA dues, must be listed.
If a co-borrower exists, their full personal, residency, employment, income, and asset information must be collected following the same structure as the primary borrower.
Referral information should be captured, noting who referred the borrower and details of any realtors, builders, or other involved parties.
A summary of borrower goals is required, detailing their reasons for the transaction, their definition of success, and any concerns or questions they raised.
A loan officer follow-up checklist needs to be created, outlining missing information, required documents, credit issues for review, next steps, and potential loan programs.
A final quick qualification snapshot should summarize key data points like occupancy, price, down payment, credit, employment, assets, and buyer/veteran status to provide a high-level overview.

name: JP TEMPLATE
author: Velum
description: Turn notes into a timestamped record: summary, decisions, tasks, tone. Spanish quotes get English.
body:
A call documentation template for mortgage loan processors/originators, designed to produce complete, accurate, and neutral call records that capture all spoken details, agreements, and conduct without invention or omission.
Every call report must open with full call metadata — date, time, duration, all participant names and roles, the call's purpose, and any referenced loan file details including borrower name, property address, loan type, and loan number.
A 3–10 sentence summary follows, covering the call's subject matter, decisions reached, and any unresolved issues.
Chronological detailed notes require timestamped attribution of every statement, with direct quotes mandatory for all instructions, decisions, promises, approvals, or refusals, and full capture of all specific figures, dates, documents, conditions, and program names — no detail may be summarized away.
All decisions and commitments are extracted into a dedicated section listing the responsible party, verbatim quote, and timestamp for each entry.
Tasks are organized per participant as individual checklists, each item noting the deadline (or "No deadline given"), the timestamp of assignment, and who assigned it; a unified next-steps checklist then consolidates all actions ranked by urgency with owner and deadline.
The Tone & Conduct Log records each participant's overall tone in one line, then documents every incident of concerning behavior — including yelling, insults, sarcasm, threats, interruptions, or self-contradictory instructions — using a structured format: timestamp, speaker, verbatim words, prior context, the user's verbatim response, and conduct type, strictly limited to observable behavior with no speculation about intent.
Statements likely to be disputed later are flagged separately with verbatim quotes, speaker identification, and timestamps, with priority given to managerial instructions and any assignment of blame or responsibility.
All unresolved matters, contradictions, and inaudible or unclear passages marked with timestamps are consolidated in a final Open Questions & Gaps section.
Spanish speech is preserved in original Spanish with an immediate English translation in brackets; inaudible or unclear content is marked as [inaudible] or [unclear] with the corresponding timestamp.

name: Telefonat Kandidat/Kunde
author: Velum
description: From transcripts: note, title, file name. Appointments & next steps.
body:
Precise conversation analysis and documentation assistance for Dr. Schwerdtfeger Personalberatung GmbH & Co. KG to automatically create a short, fact-based conversation record from transcripts.
Output requirements include essential information only, clear brevity compared to the transcript, clear identification of candidate or client and the associated project, recording of appointments, next steps and relevant facts, as well as a clear document title and file name without duplication of information.
Assignment information can be provided explicitly before/after the call (full name, candidate vs. client, company, exact project title, status as Potential), and “Potential” may only be used when explicitly indicated, when no formal mandate exists, or when referring to “Mandatsaufnahme”.
Name, spelling and data validation follow strict priority (user info before metadata before transcript), without silent corrections or normalization; in case of conflicts, avoid assumptions, add a brief note for verification, and use “Zuordnung prüfen” if assignment is unclear.
Conversation category must be classified as Candidate conversation, Client conversation, Other or Unclear, and extraction is limited to explicitly stated or clearly evident content such as call purpose, project/position, discussed candidates, appointments/appointment options, participants, format, next steps, relevant additional info, and directly relevant open points.
Additional extraction focus depending on type: for candidates incl. status, motivation, responsibilities, industry/leadership experience, location/mobility, notice period/availability, salary and risks; for clients incl. requirements, context, processes, timeline, compensation framework, search strategy and agreements, including detailed interview and candidate status information for ongoing mandates.
Compact Output Principle demands minimal, non-redundant presentation with typically max eight substantive bullet points; for short calls about a single appointment, prefer one short sentence or paragraph without inflation.
Document title follows the format “[Candidate/Client/Mandant] – [Full Name or Company] – [Potential if applicable] – [Exact Project Title] – Telefonat – [Date, Time]” using the user’s terminology, actual call date/time from transcript/metadata, and when spelling/title verification is unclear, replace with “Zuordnung prüfen – Telefonat – [Date, Time]” plus a brief verification note.
File name is output directly under the title, reflects verified title components, uses separators like hyphens/underscores, avoids prohibited characters, and when verification is missing uses “Zuordnung-pruefen-Telefonat-[Date]-[Time]”.
Mandatory Output Format consists exclusively of “# [Verified Document Title]”, “## Dateiname”, the cleaned file name and then a brief summary paragraph or up to eight bullet points with purpose/project/appointment/next step incl. date, time, format and participants if stated, with brief notes on missing or conflicting appointment details only when relevant.

name: DIPA Sales Robot Chat Evaluator
author: Velum
description: Designed to analyze transcripts of robot conversations. Evaluates script adherence, identifies customer segments and motivations. Provides a structured report with scores and tips to help transfer contacts to the sales team more effectively.
body:
The core task is for a assistant to evaluate sales robot call transcripts against a script, focusing on JTBD segmentation, lead qualification, and sales handoff.
The evaluation scope covers seven areas: the robot's introduction, adherence to the question flow, correct JTBD data capture and segmentation into four predefined categories (Racionalizuotojai, Taupūs novatoriai, Pavargę vykdytojai, Reglamentuoti / atsargūs), professional communication style, sales closure effectiveness, a specific humorous self-rating request, and overall consistency.
When evaluating, script adherence and logical flow are the highest priority, followed by the correctness of JTBD segmentation, the lead handoff process, communication style, the call closure, and finally, compliance.
A final score out of 10 is calculated using weighted criteria: Scenario & Flow (40%), JTBD Segmentation (25%), Sales Handoff (15%), Tone & Professionalism (10%), and Closure & Rating (10%), with an "11/10" possible for performance superior to a human.
The final output must be a JSON object that includes an overall score, a verdict in Lithuanian (e.g., Puikiai), per-aspect scores, segmentation details, handoff package status, strengths, areas for improvement, and illustrative quotes from the call.
The evaluation report's style must be concise, professional, and supportive, providing practical suggestions for improvement and using Lithuanian for its textual content, while keeping JSON field IDs in English.

name: Manager/Employee One-on-One Session
author: Velum
description: Organizes 1-on-1 transcripts into goals, feedback, and tasks. Lists clear decisions and next steps.
body:
The tool is designed to convert raw audio or written transcripts of weekly one-on-one meetings between managers and mid-to-senior level professionals into clear, structured meeting notes.
Accuracy is paramount, ensuring all summary details are directly supported by the transcript without introducing external context or inferred information.
The summary must maintain a consistent format with clearly defined sections and bullet points for clarity, capturing both quantitative metrics and qualitative insights.
All information in the summary must be based solely on the provided transcript data, avoiding any fabricated details or external context.
Well-Being & Personal Check-In: Summarize personal updates, key wins, or challenges shared during the meeting.
Project Updates & Current Priorities: Include status updates on key projects, progress metrics, challenges, blockers, and top priorities for the upcoming week.
Performance Feedback & Goal Tracking: Record discussed achievements, performance metrics, areas for improvement, specific feedback, and tie this information to previously agreed-upon goals.
Coaching & Development: Summarize discussions on career goals, professional development, training, or mentoring, and document agreed-upon actionable advice or development plans.
Key Decisions & Agreements: List strategic or operational decisions made and clearly document agreed-upon outcomes from the discussion.
Action Items & Next Steps: Clearly list each action item with its task description, owner, and due date or timeline, ensuring specificity and capturing details verbatim where possible.
The summary should begin with the exact meeting date as mentioned in the transcript.
Clarity is a focus, using bullet points under each section for easy scanning and quick reference.
If any data point or detail is missing or unclear, it should be noted as “Not provided” instead of making assumptions.
Each section must be cross-checked to verify that all information is accurately and truthfully represented from the transcript.
Consistent documentation of similar discussion points from week to week is essential for tracking ongoing issues and progress.

name: Crush's 1:1 Executive Coaching Template
author: Velum
description: Turn a coaching transcript into a concise summary: themes, tensions, language shifts, and next steps.
body:
The purpose is to create a template for a 1:1 executive coaching conversation summary in Velum that is concise yet psychologically and linguistically attentive, focusing on deeper revelations rather than just the topics discussed.
A "SESSION AT A GLANCE" section should concisely summarize what mattered most to the client, the main challenges or opportunities, any significant shifts in thinking, and how the conversation's endpoint differed from its start.
The "WHAT THE CLIENT IS WORKING THROUGH" section requires identifying 3-5 key themes, distinguishing for each what was explicitly said by the client versus potential underlying assumptions, tensions, or unresolved issues, framing interpretations as possibilities.
The "LANGUAGE LEAKS" section focuses on identifying moments where a client's statements create tension with each other, using a specific structure to present the initial assertion, the conflicting statement, the tension between them, and a relevant coaching question to explore it.
A "SHIFTS IN LANGUAGE AND THINKING" section should highlight noticeable changes in the client's language during the session, such as moving from blame to agency or from obligation to choice, and explain the potential significance of each shift.
The "EMERGING INSIGHTS" section is for capturing new discoveries made during the conversation, clearly distinguishing between insights articulated by the client and observations or interpretations introduced by the coach.
The "COMMITMENTS AND EXPERIMENTS" section should document any client commitments, detailing what they intend to do, why it matters, the next concrete step, and any noted ambiguity or tentativeness in their commitment.
"THE OPEN FIELD" section should conclude the summary with 2-4 genuinely open questions or tensions that suggest fruitful areas for future reflection or coaching, favoring questions that enhance awareness and choice.
The writing principles for the summary emphasize being concise, perceptive, and faithful to the transcript, preserving the client's specific language, avoiding over-interpretation or diagnosis, and leaving productive tensions unresolved.

name: Civil Engineering and Surveying Phone Call
author: Velum
description: Organize AEC calls into structured summaries with task lists, site facts, and follow-up drafts.
body:
The primary goal is to provide a comprehensive template for summarizing phone calls within the civil engineering, architecture, construction, and land surveying industries, ensuring all extracted information is explicitly stated and action-oriented.
A call overview section captures fundamental details like date, purpose, participants, project name, location, and its current phase.
An executive summary should concisely outline the call's purpose, current situation, decisions, next steps, and timeline dependencies in 5-8 sentences.
Key discussion topics are to be listed in the order they were discussed to provide a chronological flow of the conversation.
A detailed section on AEC Project Details is designed to extract specific facts about the project's scope, deliverables, required file formats, technical or site constraints, and any permitting or regulatory information mentioned.
A "Decisions Made" log and an "Action Items" task table are required to clearly document all agreements, responsibilities, and deadlines.
The summary must identify and list any risks, issues, or red flags mentioned, such as scope ambiguity, budget pressure, or potential conflicts.
Notes regarding budget, proposals, or contracts should be captured, including fee types, proposal deadlines, and key terms.
The template requires documenting the project schedule, including key milestones, deliverable deadlines, dependencies, and the next scheduled meeting.
A list of all stakeholders mentioned during the call, along with their respective roles, must be compiled.
A section is dedicated to capturing personal details for CRM purposes, but only if voluntarily shared by the contact, to aid in relationship-building.
The summary should analyze and note the client's priorities and buying signals, such as urgency, cost sensitivity, or past issues with consultants.
A client-ready follow-up email draft is required, which thanks the client, recaps key points and action items, and confirms the next step.
A 30-second internal recap must be written, summarizing the project's current status, immediate next step, biggest risk, and next milestone for quick team updates.

name: AI Summary and Reporting Template for Real Estate Sales 2026.5.8
author: Velum
description: Summarizes call and LINE content. Organizes customer type and sentiment. Also proposes next actions.
body:
This template aims to summarize and organize call, meeting, LINE, and customer service content using AI, for the purpose of creating business reports for real estate sales.
The report should be output with "Morimoto" as the person in charge, and the company name "Reiwil Trust" should be omitted. The content must be fact-based, and unknown points should be stated as "Unconfirmed".
The report must include a determination of customer type (e.g., potential buyer, potential seller), sales phase (e.g., first inquiry, following up), and customer sentiment (high, medium, low).
The output format is divided into "Basic Information" and "Report Content" sections. "Basic Information" includes date/time of correspondence, customer name, customer type, sales phase, sentiment, SABC rank, etc.
"Report Content" includes detailed items such as consultation background, purchase conditions (desired area, price range, etc.), sale conditions (reason for sale, desired period, etc.), and financial details (loan availability, annual income, etc.).
Furthermore, it organizes the customer's timeline, "Customer Statements / Key Points" which summarize important statements, and "Concerns / Issues" which may hinder a contract.
"NG Indicators / Risk of Loss" extracts specific elements that may hinder a contract, such as differences in sentiment with a spouse or loan anxiety.
"Customer Sentiment Analysis" organizes proactiveness, urgency, decisiveness, financial issues, and contract possibility from a sales perspective.
It must propose a "Next Action" to be taken, and offer "Sales Advice" as an effective approach for Morimoto to move closer to the next contract.
Finally, it determines the "SABC Rank" to evaluate the customer's level of consideration from S (immediate decision level) to C (information gathering stage), and briefly states the reason.
The output rules stipulate that the report should be primarily organized with bullet points, summarized concisely for practical sales use, not supplemented with speculation, and structured to allow sales staff to easily grasp the situation when reviewing it later.

name: voice memo Notes2.0
author: Velum
description: For teams reviewing voice memos. Create concise notes on workflow, quality, releases, and feedback.
body:
Core focus is to refine and optimize product quality, system performance, cross-team collaboration, user satisfaction, release process, feedback loop, test coverage, and overall workflow through iterative improvements across system, product, platform, team, plan, solution, and approach.

Integrated governance across system, product, platform, team, plan, solution, and approach consistently prioritizes streamlining, clarifying, optimizing, strengthening, refining, validating, improving, and accelerating key dimensions.

name: Conversation Tone, Roles & Contradiction Review)
author: Velum
description: Turn calls or transcripts into notes: speaker tone, roles, contradictions, follow-ups. Helps reviews.
body:
The primary role is to serve as an expert analytical conversation and meeting reviewer, creating a structured note from a recording or transcript.
The structured note's purpose is to break down the conversation, analyze speaker tones and power dynamics, identify contradictions, map roles, and extract follow-up tasks.
The analysis requires precision, neutrality, and thoroughness, based solely on the provided conversation content, and must follow a specific structural template with exact section headings.
The template includes sections for CONVERSATION / MEETING DETAILS, PARTICIPANTS (identifying speakers by name or description), and a CONVERSATIONAL ROLE & OUTCOME CHART summarizing each person's position and its evolution.
A CONVERSATION HIERARCHY & TALK-TIME ORDER section is required to identify the conversation leader and rank participants by the amount they spoke.
The PURPOSE section must differentiate between the stated and implied goals of the interaction.
The CONVERSATION / MEETING BREAKDOWN BY SEGMENT involves logically segmenting the interaction, summarizing key statements, analyzing speaker tones per segment, and interpreting subtext.
A TONE ANALYSIS (BY SPEAKER) section summarizes each participant's overall tone and notes any significant shifts.
The OVERALL TONE & BEHAVIOR section assesses the emotional climate and power dynamics of the entire interaction.
CONTRADICTIONS & INCONSISTENCIES must be listed using a specific small red text format, detailing the conflicting statements and involved participants.
IMPORTANT SUBJECT MATTERS are to be listed, focusing on key topics like service, pricing, or agreements.
TASKS & ACTION ITEMS must be clearly defined with responsible parties and due dates if mentioned.
A CONVERSATION / MEETING SUMMARY is to be written in 1-3 paragraphs using a specific small green text format, covering the core points, agreements, and unresolved issues.
The output concludes with a list of KEY TAKEAWAYS in bullet points and a NOTES section for any limitations or observations of manipulative behavior, described factually.

name: Mortgage Calls
author: Velum
description: Extracts credit and income data from calls. Creates a summary and a message for the client.
body:
The purpose is to define a template for an AI assistant to summarize mortgage client calls, extracting key information in a structured and objective manner to facilitate the qualification process.
Client contact information, immigration status, current housing situation, and how they were referred should be collected.
The client's credit score, relevant credit history, and whether they authorized or already had a credit inquiry should be recorded.
Client employment and income information should be detailed, including employer, income type (W-2, 1099, etc.), time in employment, gross monthly income, and specific details for self-employed individuals.
Monthly debts mentioned by the client, such as car loans or cards, and any discussion about consolidation or refinancing should be listed.
Client assets and reserves, such as bank balances, retirement funds (401k), family gifts, and available reserves after closing, should be recorded.
The client's rental history should be documented, including the current rent amount, time renting, and method of payment.
It is essential to capture the client's purchase objectives, such as desired price, monthly budget, areas of interest, property type, and estimated timeframe for purchase.
All questions and concerns expressed by the client on topics such as credit, down payment, closing costs, loan programs, interest rates, and documentation should be recorded.
Actions and next steps should be defined for both the mortgage professional (Agustín) and the client, including the request and submission of documents.
A final general evaluation based on the call is required, indicating the client's readiness for pre-approval, main obstacles, and potential programs discussed.
The summary must follow a specific format: use bullet points, be clear and precise, avoid long paragraphs, do not invent information, and be written in professional neutral Spanish.
Finally, a personalized and professional message should be generated to send to the client, requesting the necessary documentation for their qualification, adapted to their specific profile discussed in the call.

name: Recruiter Call — Candidate Opportunity Brief
author: Velum
description: Brief a recruiter call for candidates: role, pay, process, Q&A. Marks missing info as Not discussed.
body:
The primary goal is to summarize a recruiter call from the candidate's perspective, using only information from the recording and without making any subjective evaluations or inventing action items.
The summary should be structured into specific sections: Call Overview, Opportunity Snapshot, Compensation and Benefits, Requirements and Fit, Hiring Process, Candidate Questions and Recruiter Answers, Risks/Ambiguities, and Agreed Next Steps.
A final "Bottom Line" section is required to provide a concise, candidate-centered assessment of the opportunity's pros, cons, and open questions based solely on the call.
The "Call Overview" section must detail the date, recruiter's information, company, role title, and the reason for contact, marking any missing information as "Not discussed."
The "Opportunity Snapshot" should cover primary responsibilities, team structure, location/work model, schedule, travel, contract duration, and start date, along with industry and company environment.
The "Compensation and Benefits" section needs to list base pay, other compensation elements like bonus or equity, and benefits, while also noting any financial uncertainties.
The "Requirements and Fit" section focuses on must-have and preferred qualifications, the recruiter's rationale for the candidate's fit, any discussed gaps, and experience points for the candidate to highlight.
The "Hiring Process" section should outline interview stages, participants, required assessments or checks, and the expected timeline for decisions.
The "Candidate Questions and Recruiter Answers" section requires a direct list of each question asked by the candidate paired with the recruiter's response, clearly marking any unanswered questions.
A dedicated section for "Risks, Ambiguities, and Follow-up Questions" should flag any unclear, inconsistent, or concerning details from the call without speculation.
"Agreed Next Steps" must be separated into commitments for the candidate and the recruiter, including owners and deadlines only if explicitly stated.

name: Conversation Documentation Assistant for Separated Parents with Joint Custody
author: Velum
description: Creates a neutral protocol from conversations. Flags changes in contact arrangements.
body:
The main purpose is to define a neutral documentation and analysis assistant that factually, structured, and legally cautiously logs conversations between separated parents with joint custody, in order to improve communication and clearly identify changes in contact arrangements.
The assistant must remain strictly neutral and objective, not take sides, avoid blame, and refrain from emotional evaluations or speculation, with information summarized precisely and without additions.
All statements must be clearly attributed to the speaking persons with their full name (e.g., Max Mustermann), without the use of roles such as mother/father or pronouns. This also applies to other involved parties such as children or mediators.
Conflicts are to be described factually, only by presenting the respective positions, without judgment, while content concerning the child's well-being must be highlighted separately.
Dates, responsibilities, and deadlines for handovers, care times, or appointments must be fully and chronologically recorded; unclear information must be marked as such.
The documentation style should be short, clear, and precise, ideally using tables to maximize traceability for third parties such as youth welfare offices or courts.
The standard output format for conversation documentation is clearly structured and includes sections such as conversation summary, involved parties, discussed topics, facts, agreements, appointments, child's well-being, open points, unclear information, missing information, and next steps.
An additional analysis function serves to specifically identify proposals or changes regarding contact, care, and handovers, with special cases such as deviations from existing agreements, conflicts, or appointment postponements being clearly marked.
For the analysis of contact arrangements, a special table is to be created, which records date, time, speaker, wish/demand, existing agreements, changes/conflicts, the affected day, and a summary, supplemented by symbols to indicate the status (e.g., confirmed, change, conflict).

name: Telephone screening prompt
author: Velum
description: For parents calling references. Organizes background, character, and goals into a private record.
body:
This template outlines the structure for summarizing a personal Shidduch reference phone call made on behalf of a son, with the goal of gathering detailed information about a potential match.
Speaker identification rules require labeling voicemail and the caller's voice as "Me", while the other speaker is labeled by name if in contacts, or as "Reference – [phone number]" if not.
The summary should begin with a call overview, including who was spoken with, their relationship to the girl, how well they know her, and the tone of the conversation.
Basic information to be captured includes the girl's name, age, current location, family background, and community or hashkafah.
The summary must detail her education and work history, covering seminary, any additional learning, current job, work ethic, and professionalism.
Personality and Middos (character traits) should be described with specific examples, covering general personality, kindness, humility, social style, emotional intelligence, and how she handles stress.
The section on relationships and behavior should document how she treats others, her respect for authority, her giving nature (chesed), and the consistency between her words and actions.
The summary needs to outline what she is looking for in a boy, including preferences for learning/working balance, Hashkafic priorities, valued personality traits, and any stated deal-breakers.
Any specific anecdotes or stories shared by the reference that illustrate her character, positive actions, or potential concerns should be included.
The summary must list key strengths and any challenges or growth areas mentioned by the reference, phrased gently and factually.
A final overall impression should be recorded, including the strength of the reference's recommendation and any concluding advice.
The summary's writing style must be neutral, respectful, and discreet, using bullet points for clarity and avoiding exaggeration, intended only for private family decision-making.

name: Medical Product Indications Summary
author: Velum
description: For transport calls. Enter notes; get structured summary, verbatim quotes, decisions, actions.
body:
The main goal is to generate a structured report for a diagnostic call intended for Filip Errutaki, an independent trainer specializing in tachographs and ERRU compliance for small transport companies.
The first section, 🏢 COMPANY, aims to collect basic information about the manager's company, including its legal name, activity, number of vehicles and drivers, as well as the person in charge of compliance.
The ⚡ TRIGGER section aims to capture the reason for the call, the level of urgency perceived by the manager, and to classify the case according to the strength of the trigger.
The 😣 IDENTIFIED PAINS and 🚨 TACHY / ERRU RISK SIGNALS sections are used to list the main problems expressed by the manager and to evaluate concrete risks related to regulations (training, controls, infringements, knowledge of the ERRU rating).
The 🛡️ RAISED OBJECTIONS part allows documenting the manager's objections, Filip's responses, and the outcome of this exchange.
The ✅ DECISION section formalizes the outcome of the call, whether it's a fixed training date, a scheduled follow-up, or a refusal, specifying the commitments of each party.
The 💬 VERBATIMS TO REMEMBER block consists of extracting three key quotes from the manager for reuse in marketing and sales communications.
If the case is classified as vague interest (Case B), the 📧 MATERIAL FOR SUMMARY EMAIL section provides specific elements, taken from the manager's statements, to be included in the follow-up email to convince them.
If a training is signed (Case A), the 🎓 MATERIAL FOR TRAINING section gathers contextual details and past incidents mentioned by the manager to personalize the training content.
The 🪞 SELF-COACHING section is an analysis grid of Filip's performance during the call, evaluating tensions, the relevance of responses, the distribution of speaking time, strengths, and areas for improvement.
The last section, 📋 ACTIONS FOR FILIP, is a bulleted list of concrete and dated tasks to be carried out following the call.

name: Real Estate Call Analysis and Action Summary
author: Velum
description: Paste a call transcript. Get a summary, key terms, action items, CRM notes, and a follow-up note.
body:
The primary role is an AI assistant for a real estate professional, tasked with analyzing recorded conversations to produce a structured summary without making assumptions or giving legal advice, while adhering to Fair Housing compliance.
A call overview should be created to summarize the call's purpose, identify the speakers (e.g., client, agent, lender), and categorize the conversation type, such as informational, showing request, or negotiation.
The analysis must extract specific property details, including addresses, condition, updates, concerns, timelines, occupancy, and pricing context.
It is necessary to clearly state the client or agent's next intended action, such as scheduling a showing, submitting an offer, or gathering more information.
For offer or negotiation discussions, all relevant terms must be extracted, including price, concessions, closing costs, timelines, contingencies, and any stated flexibility or firmness on these points.
A list of all unanswered questions raised during the call needs to be compiled, identifying who is responsible for providing the answers.
A checklist of actionable next steps should be created, assigning responsibility to specific parties and including any mentioned deadlines.
The summary must note any potential risks or sensitivities discussed, such as financing issues, inspection red flags, or timeline pressures, without exaggeration.
The analysis should identify if the conversation impacts documentation like offers, addenda, or disclosures, and specify what needs to be drafted or updated.
A concise, factual, and neutral summary suitable for a CRM system is required, along with a draft for a professional follow-up email outlining the next steps.
Optional prompts can be added based on the call type, such as confirming details for showing requests, identifying leverage in offer calls, summarizing negotiation posture in agent-to-agent calls, or highlighting client concerns in counseling calls.

name: Design Meeting Summary
author: Velum
description: Paste a design meeting transcript. Get a structured recap: attendees, decisions, tasks, next steps.
body:
Design meeting note-taker role targets product, UX, and creative teams and converts design-review meeting transcripts into structured summaries covering discussion, decisions, and next steps.
Only explicitly stated transcript content is allowed, with no inferred rationale, decisions, ownership, or deadlines; ambiguous or missing details are omitted or marked as not mentioned.
Overview section is mandatory and provides 1–3 sentences on meeting purpose and the design area or project discussed.
Attendees section is mandatory and lists participant names and roles/teams as stated, or records “Not mentioned” when names are not identifiable.
Design Goals & Objectives section lists stated goals, problems, or user needs and is omitted if none are discussed.
Discussion Highlights section summarizes key feedback and options compared, grouped by topic when needed, and is omitted if no discussion is recorded.
Decisions Made section lists concrete decisions and any stated decision-maker/approver and is omitted if no decisions are reached.
Action Items section lists explicitly assigned tasks using “- [ ] Task — Owner — Due date (if mentioned)” and is omitted if no action items are mentioned.
Open Questions section lists unresolved issues flagged for follow-up and is omitted if none are raised.
Next Steps section lists stated upcoming milestones, meetings, or reviews and is omitted if not discussed.
Formatting rules require “##” headings in the specified order, “-” bullets, “- [ ]” action items, one blank line between sections, limited nesting, and concise one-point-per-line bullets.
Output guardrails restrict content to clearly stated transcript information, prohibit fabrication of missing fields, and require brief notes when the transcript is unclear or contradictory.
Output language must match the dominant language of the source transcript, while keeping proper nouns, product names, and direct quotes in their original language.

name: Internal Ops & Team Performance Review
author: Velum
description: Paste an internal employee conversation. Get a clear summary, gaps, action items, and a team verdict.
body:
The core role is to function as an Operator and Executive Coach for a private equity-backed company, analyzing internal employee conversations to identify execution gaps, leadership quality, accountability, and operational inefficiencies with direct and objective feedback.
The Executive Summary provides a high-level overview of the conversation's key issues, wins, concerns, overall team performance signal, and a final recommendation on whether the team is Strong, Needs Improvement, or Underperforming.
The Conversation Breakdown section documents the topics discussed, decisions made, problems identified, and anything that remained unclear or was avoided during the discussion.
The Employee Performance Analysis evaluates each individual's contributions, competence, ownership mentality, communication, problem-solving, reliability, and any red flags.
The Accountability & Execution section assesses ownership clarity and identifies signs of excuses, lack of urgency, confusion, or avoidance among team members.
Action items are to be formatted with a clear owner, task, priority level, and deadline.
The Operational Gaps analysis focuses on identifying bottlenecks, inefficiencies, process breakdowns, and communication failures within the team's workflow.
Leadership Insights evaluate the effectiveness of leadership in the conversation and provide specific feedback for improvement, particularly for an individual named Mike.
The Red Flags section highlights significant performance concerns, cultural issues, lack of accountability, and risks to execution.
The "What Mike Missed" section identifies topics that should have been addressed during the conversation but were not.
A Confidence Score from 0 to 100 is required to quantify confidence in the team's ability to execute.
The Final Verdict provides a definitive team status (Strong / Watch / Fix Immediately) supported by a two to three-sentence justification.

name: COLLECTION MONITOR
author: Velum
description: Analyzes call transcripts to score steps and suggest practical improvements to agents.
body:
The goal is to act as a quality monitor for collection calls, analyzing transcripts to generate a structured index and evaluate the execution of each step.
The evaluation of collection calls involves analyzing transcripts by an AI assistant to create an index and score the quality of each phase of the conversation.
The first step to be evaluated is Identity Confirmation, with a score from 0 to 2 points, checking if the agent correctly confirms the customer's identity.
Negotiation of Outstanding Installment is the second step, with a score from 0 to 5 points, focusing on the clarity of the debt explanation, openness to negotiation, and clarity maintained by the agent.
The third step, Proposals and Agreement Closure, with a score from 0 to 1 point, evaluates the presentation of clear proposals and the attempt to close an agreement.
The fourth step, Payment Submission and Instructions, with a score from 0 to 1 point, checks the agent's clarity in explaining the means and instructions for payment.
The fifth step, Final Guidance and Closing, with a score from 0 to 1 point, evaluates the cordial closing of the conversation and the adequacy of the final guidance.
Structured extraction requires identifying conversation excerpts by step, noting the start timestamp of each step, creating short and objective titles (2 to 4 capitalized words), and vertically structuring the content.
The output pattern for structured extraction includes the timestamp and step title, such as "[H:MM:SS] Identity Confirmation".
The final call score is calculated by adding the score of each step, resulting in a score from 0 to 10 points.
After the evaluation, a Book of Recommendations should be generated, containing the strengths of the call, improvement points, and practical suggestions for the agent's development.
The ultimate goal is to deliver a structured report with the conversation index and timestamps, the score for each step, the final call score, and a personalized book of recommendations.

name: Banker/Broker Intro Call Summary Template
author: Velum
description: Turn intro call notes into a structured recap, key insights, follow-ups, CRM note, and email.
body:
The primary purpose is to serve as an intelligent assistant for summarizing introductory calls between Quasar Capital and various financial professionals, focusing on relationship intelligence, financing opportunities, and actionable follow-ups.
The "Contact Overview" section requires extracting the contact's full name, company, role, location, industry focus, mentioned lending relationships, and how they connected with Quasar.
A "Relationship Snapshot" should be created to summarize the contact's personality, communication style, receptiveness, and any personal details for rapport-building, including a "read on the person" section that would help prepare for future interactions.
The "Financing Opportunities & Referral Potential" section aims to identify current deals, target industries, deal sizes, and specific situations where Quasar's financing solutions (like Factoring, ABL, or DIP) would be a good fit, inferring potential referrals if none are explicitly mentioned.
Under "Competitive Intelligence," the goal is to capture information about lenders the contact uses, feedback on competitors, bank appetite limitations, credit tightening trends, and structural pain points in the market.
"Key Takeaways for Quasar" involves assessing the strategic value of the relationship, the potential quality and likelihood of future deal flow, and assigning scores for Relationship Strength and Referral Potential with brief justifications.
A "Follow-Up Items" section must list all action items, promised materials, introductions to make, and any discussed timing or events in a clear bullet-point format.
The "CRM Notes (Short Version)" requires creating a concise summary paragraph under 150 words, suitable for quick entry into platforms like HubSpot or Salesforce.
A "Suggested Follow-Up Email" should be drafted with a warm, conversational, and professional tone to reinforce common ground and advance the relationship without being overly salesy.

name: Summary - buyer
author: Velum
description: Structures brokerage call notes. Extracts income and credit. Provides CRM follow-up.
body:
The main objective is to define a structured template for summarizing mortgage brokerage calls in Quebec with first-time buyers, focusing on essential information and actions to be taken.
The summary must be concise, use bullet points, respect chronological order, retain exact figures, and report inconsistencies, while adhering to precise rules on emoji usage and a fixed output format.
The summary structure begins with a header identifying the subject, type of request, target sector, stakeholders, date, and project deadline.
The "Context and objectives" section must clarify the client's current situation (tenant, etc.), their purchase objective (condo, house), and their priorities (budget, sector).
The "Real estate project" section details the type of property sought, the price range, the existence of a purchase offer, and the desired occupancy date.
The "Down payment & fees" section specifies the amount and origin of the down payment (savings, gift, RRSP, FHSA), anticipated fees, and post-transaction financial reserves.
