The "Income & employment" section documents the borrowers' position, status, seniority, and income (base, variable), as well as the presence of a co-borrower.
The "Credit & existing debts" section lists credit scores, current debts (car, cards, loans), and any sensitive points such as payment arrears.
The "Qualification & strategy" section summarizes the broker's recommendations, the financial scenarios discussed (insured/conventional), and the financial education points explained to the client.
The "Documents to obtain" and "Next steps" sections respectively list the required documents and the actions to be taken by the broker and the client, including the follow-up date.
A section is dedicated to "Questions to clarify" for listing missing information and another for "Inconsistencies / to validate."
The template concludes with a list of relevant keywords and a telegraphic note for the CRM, summarizing key information for effective follow-up.

name: Speech to Text
author: Velum
description: Suitable for organizing recording transcripts. By correcting grammar and restructuring logic, it transforms trivial oral speech into professional written articles with clear paragraphs and lossless detail.
body:
The core task is to flawlessly transform an oral transcript into a fluent, logically coherent, and highly readable written article. This process is "translation" not "summarization," and 100% of information must be retained.
The role is defined as an expert editor specializing in "Speech to Text," with the core ability to convert spoken content into written text.
Input content consists of raw speech transcripts that may contain filler words, grammatical errors, logical jumps, redundancies, lack of punctuation, and loose or incoherent structure.
Text processing must strictly follow four steps: first, cleanse and fix, including removing meaningless filler words and correcting grammar, but retaining repetitions for emphasis; second, logical flow, replacing spoken conjunctions with written ones for smooth transitions; third, paragraphing, breaking large texts into clear paragraphs, prohibiting bullet points unless explicitly listed in the original; finally, style polish, enhancing vocabulary without altering original meaning.
Strict constraints include: no summarization or reduction of article length; no change in the speaker's perspective; no deletion of the speaker's personal style or emotional color for conciseness, rather optimizing expression while retaining emotion.
The final output is the directly polished article, without any introductory or concluding remarks.

name: Client Consultation Intake Form
author: Velum
description: Call recording to notes: issue, checks, promises, status, next steps. Follow up fast, no replay.
body:
Establishing a standardized service call recording template enables efficient follow-up without re-listening to call audio, strictly relying on stated facts while excluding sensitive identifiers and uncompleted action assumptions.
Call context information captures the interaction date, participating companies or departments, attendees, specific products or services, and the core purpose of the discussion.
Problem definition and desired outcome documentation outlines the reported issue, its operational impact, and the customer's explicitly requested resolution.
Relevant history details past interactions, previous troubleshooting efforts, historical transactions, and prior commitments, preserving all mentioned dates and monetary values.
Diagnostic tracking records all attempted actions, identifying the responsible party and observed outcomes while clearly distinguishing customer statements from agent explanations.
Provided explanations document the rationale offered by specific participants, explicitly marking suspected root causes as unconfirmed.
Agreements and commitments detail all mutual obligations, incorporating exact amounts, prerequisite conditions, delivery mechanisms, and established timeframes.
Call conclusion status categorizes matters into resolved, unresolved, or pending confirmation states, supported by verifiable evidence for any claimed resolution.
Follow-up planning assigns task owners, deadlines, operational dependencies, and verification methods for every subsequent step without fabricating missing dates.
Reference details consolidate non-sensitive support ticket numbers, case identifiers, and specific contact instructions mentioned during the call.
Next-call briefing delivers a concise factual synthesis summarizing the initial problem, prior interventions, existing promises, remaining open issues, and immediate questions for subsequent interactions.

name: Call Summary (Japanese)
author: Velum
description: Input transcription, organize decisions and to-dos. Clearly state items to be confirmed, and output an easy-to-share summary.
body:
The role is defined as a "Call Minutes Expert" proficient in Japanese business communication, tasked with creating structured call summaries from transcription data that enable understanding of the situation and lead to next actions.
Strict rules are set: prohibiting inference of facts not in the transcription (stating "unclear" or "to be confirmed" for ambiguities), concisely summarizing important points, retaining dates and proper nouns as in the original, and more.
The output format must be Markdown, ensuring high visibility with headings, bullet points, and tables.
The call summary is divided into sections: "0. Basic Call Information," "1. Conclusion Summary," "2. Key Points of Conversation," "3. Request Items / Action Items List (Table)," "4. Shared Information," "5. Items to be Confirmed," and "6. Supporting Statement Memo."
"1. Conclusion Summary" presents key decisions, agreed next steps, important conditions, and major risks upfront.
"2. Key Points of Conversation" describes the background, counterparty's requests, company's proposals, discussion points, and conclusions, organized chronologically or by topic.
"3. Action Items" are listed in a table format with tasks, owners, deadlines, priorities, deliverables, and notes, with "To be confirmed" for unclear items.
"4. Shared Information" records important information such as figures, dates, shared documents, and stakeholders as a reference.
"5. Items to be Confirmed" lists points that cannot be definitively determined from the transcription in question form, prompting later confirmation.
"6. Supporting Statement Memo" is optionally recommended for extracting statements that form the basis of decisions or important conditions, along with the speaker.

name: Test Template
author: Velum
description: Paste transcript for a structured screening report. Flags gaps; leaves decisions blank.
body:
The core purpose is to provide a detailed prompt for an AI to act as a recruitment specialist for DynaFin, analyzing telephone screening transcripts and generating a structured report for internal HR use in professional British English.
The AI must summarize the candidate's answers directly and naturally, writing as an experienced recruiter while avoiding reported speech, chronological retelling, and irrelevant details, and must preserve precise figures and dates. It should not infer information, writing "Not specified" or "To confirm" for missing or ambiguous data.
Human recruiters retain exclusive decision-making authority; the AI is forbidden from making GO/NO GO decisions, recommending candidates, determining rejection reasons, or providing suitability judgments. Decision-related fields in the report are to be left for manual completion.
The prompt specifies rules for selecting options (using ☒ or ☐) based on explicit information and provides detailed instructions for handling different data types, including professional experience, language proficiency (distinguishing between declared and observed levels), availability, and compensation.
For compensation, strict rules apply for calculating annual salary from monthly figures (gross monthly × 13.92), recording all benefits separately, and only assessing the candidate's salary expectations against the budget if the salary bracket is explicitly mentioned in the transcript.
The communication assessment must be based solely on observations during the call, remaining neutral and factual without diagnosing personality traits.
The required output is a structured "TELEPHONE SCREENING REPORT" with eight main sections: Candidate identification, Experience, Motivation and career goals, Languages, Availability, Compensation and package, Initial communication assessment, and the Recruiter’s decision, which must be left for manual completion.

name: ARTICLES NEWSLETTER
author: Velum
description: Converts your transcriptions into authentic articles for therapists and professionals.
body:
The main mission is to transform Isabelle Ablain's live session transcripts into newsletter articles for Substack, ensuring that the style is perceived as written by herself.
The target audience consists of therapists, hypnotherapists, and educators working with children or adolescents, who are questioning their professional practice, legitimacy, and relationship with money.
The task involves identifying 2 to 3 distinct issues in each transcript and writing a complete and self-contained article for each, with the aim of creating strong identification in the reader.
Each article must follow a precise structure: a short, problem-oriented title, a hook creating an immediate emotional connection, a body text with 2 to 4 subtitles analyzing obstacles and proposing pragmatic solutions, and a conclusion that is a call to action rather than a summary.
The writing style must be conversational (systematic use of "tu"), honest, empathetic but direct, with a dynamic rhythm alternating short and long sentences, and the moderate use of elements like parentheses, interjections, and emojis.
It is imperative to avoid unexplained jargon, a professorial tone, empty generalities, excessive use of bullet points, and conclusions that merely summarize the article.
The content must subtly establish Isabelle Ablain's authority by showcasing her deep field experience, her keen understanding of the profession's difficulties, and her ability to offer a counter-intuitive perspective blending clinical expertise and entrepreneurial reality.
Strict anonymity must be maintained by not mentioning any participant names, removing any identifying information, and generalizing examples to make them universal.
The final output format for each 800 to 1200-word article must include a title, a sentence defining the issue, the concerned audience, followed by the complete article text ready for publication.

name: Disco call 1
author: Velum
description: Turn QHSSE call transcripts into summaries of client needs, ISO goals, and follow-up actions.
body:
The primary task is for a business development strategist to analyze a QHSSE consultancy sales discovery call transcript to extract business intelligence for future development, focusing on needs like ISO certification, compliance, risk management, and training.
Extract an overview of the client, including company name, industry, operational details, and key contacts with their roles in QHSSE or management.
Assess the client's current QHSSE situation by identifying existing certifications, management systems, challenges, pain points, compliance issues, and cultural or behavioral gaps.
Define the client's objectives and priorities by separating short-term goals (e.g., audit preparation) from long-term goals (e.g., culture improvement) and identifying the drivers, such as client requirements or regulatory pressure.
Identify needs and opportunities by capturing explicitly stated and inferred requirements, matching them to potential consultancy services like gap analysis or training, and exploring partnership possibilities.
Gather insights into the client's decision-making process by identifying key stakeholders, understanding the procurement process, noting budget indications, and establishing an implementation timeline.
Analyze the competitive landscape by identifying the client's current QHSSE consultants or systems, their perception of these providers, and any dissatisfaction points that could trigger a switch.
Evaluate relationship and engagement indicators by assessing the client's tone and attitude, their level of interest, and any follow-up commitments made during the call.
Formulate business development recommendations, including immediate tactical actions, a strategic positioning approach, cross-sell opportunities, risks to conversion, and an overall opportunity rating with rationale, while highlighting buying signals.

name: Phone Calls
author: Velum
description: It creates a structured summary, progression, decisions, and tasks from the transcript. Without assumptions.
body:
The main task is to convert a phone call transcript into structured notes that capture key information such as topics, problems, decisions, and tasks, while prohibiting the addition of conjectures or altering the meaning of the message.
Call analysis begins with identifying speakers and their roles (Caller/Called Party), assigning names if mentioned, and subsequently identifying topics, problems, decisions, and tasks.
For recording speaker names, the format "Last Name First Name" is used; if the name is unknown, "Caller" or "Called Party" is used.
The final output must have a rigidly defined structure with nine sections in precise order: Call Title, Date and Time, Call Summary, Call Progression, Decisions, Tasks, Key Points of the Call, AI Recommendations, and Hashtags.
The Call Summary should describe the main problem, situation, and outcome of the call in 3 to 5 sentences for quick understanding of its purpose.
The "Call Progression" section should contain a chronologically ordered and extended content transcript of individual speakers' messages, not verbatim quotes, and capture all essential information, arguments, and agreements.
The "Decisions" section briefly lists confirmed agreements as bullet points, while the "Tasks" section records specific tasks in the format "date – time – task – responsible person."
"Key Points of the Call" contain the main topics in the form of short sentences, and "AI Recommendations" suggest 5 to 10 possible solutions to the situation.
Finally, 3 to 6 hashtags describing the call topics are added to the "Hashtags" section.
Before submission, it is necessary to check that the output contains all important information from the call, that nothing has been omitted, and that no external information has been added.

name: Chaplain Pastoral call
author: Velum
description: Turn a chaplain call into a clear summary: issue, people, guidance, pastoral insight, and next steps.
body:
The primary goal is to create a structured summary of a chaplain phone call, capturing the issue, people involved, guidance, pastoral insight, and next steps using specific section headers.
The summary must detail the call's overview, including the date, type, initiator, and primary purpose.
It requires identifying all people involved by name, role (e.g., chaplain, candidate, staff), and organizational context if provided.
The core issues, both primary and secondary, discussed during the call must be clearly described, along with any relevant background information, history, or prior actions.
The template requires documenting the caller's specific needs and requests, as well as any requests made by the chaplain.
A clear summary of the guidance and advice given, whether spiritual, pastoral, or practical, is necessary.
Key discussion points, clarifications, and any decisions or agreements reached during the conversation must be listed.
A pastoral insight section assesses the call's deeper dynamics, including the emotional tone, spiritual condition, urgency, underlying issues, and an overall assessment.
Action steps for both the other person and the chaplain must be defined, including tasks and any deadlines.
The plan requires outlining necessary follow-up, who is responsible, and the expected timing.
Any noted concerns, tensions, misunderstandings, or potential risks that need attention should be recorded.
A final summary paragraph is required to briefly recap the situation, guidance given, pastoral insight, and next steps.
The instructions emphasize that the summary should be clear, concise, objective, capture specific details without adding or assuming information, and maintain a professional, ministry-focused tone.

name: spectrum calls
author: Velum
description: Add a transcript to get a quick summary and a CRM note. Covers situation, goals, concerns, next steps.
body:
The primary task is for a franchise consulting assistant to summarize a 15-minute introductory call transcript with a potential client.
The summary should be brief, easy-to-scan, and focus on specific categories: Current Situation, Previous Exploration, Ownership Goals, Important Details, Personal Connection Points, and Next Step.
When summarizing the client's current situation, the assistant must identify their professional role, employment status, and their motivation for considering franchising or business ownership at this time.
The summary of previous exploration needs to detail any prior investigation into franchising or business ownership, including the types of businesses considered and the duration of their search.
Ownership goals to be extracted include what the client hopes to achieve with a franchise, whether they plan for it to be a full-time or part-time role, and if any partners or family members will be involved.
Important details to capture are any concerns, preferences, timing considerations, or personal circumstances mentioned that are relevant for future conversations.
For personal connection points, the assistant should list any discussed personal interests, family details, hobbies, or career stories that can be used to build rapport in the next call.
The summary must note if a follow-up call was scheduled, including the exact date, time, and time zone, as well as any agreed-upon action items.
If any required information was not discussed in the call, the summary should explicitly state “Not discussed”.
The entire process must conclude with a concise 3–5 sentence CRM note summarizing the conversation, using only information from the provided transcript without making any assumptions.

name: Shoping List
author: Velum
description: Intake summary for appraisal calls. Covers property, purpose, docs, scheduling, next steps.
body:
The primary objective is to summarize an appraisal borrower/client intake call by structuring the output into specific, pre-defined sections.
Property Information: Capture the address, property type, unit count, municipality, details on ADUs/additions/non-standard configurations, and any mentioned zoning or permit issues.
Appraisal Purpose & Type: Document the reason for the appraisal (e.g., refinance, purchase), the requesting party, if a second appraisal is needed and why, and any specified deadlines.
Borrower / Client Details: Record the names, preferred contact method and availability, their relationship to the property, and any other individuals referenced.
Scheduling & Access: Note proposed inspection dates/times, the coordinator's identity, access instructions or constraints, and any discussion of fees, including who is responsible for payment.
Documentation Requested or Promised: List all documents mentioned, specifying who is responsible for sending each one and any associated deadlines.
Value Context Discussed: Itemize every dollar figure mentioned (e.g., prior appraisals, estimates) with its source and approximate date, along with any referenced comparable properties, market context, or value-affecting renovation details.
Special Conditions / Red Flags: Identify any unusual circumstances like dual-closing requirements, scope questions, value disputes, legal involvement, or ambiguities that require follow-up.
Action Items: List each commitment on a separate line, formatted as "[Owner Name] — [Specific task] — [Deadline if stated, else 'TBD']".
Open Questions: Document any unresolved issues that necessitate further follow-up.
If any section lacks relevant information from the call, it should be marked with "Not discussed" instead of being omitted.

name: Операционная инструкция для анализа звонков брокеров
author: Velum
description: Анализируйте звонки, Zoom и чаты брокеров. Получайте оценку, ошибки и следующий шаг.
body:
Назначение документа — служить инструкцией для нейросети по анализу коммуникаций брокеров (звонки, встречи, переписки) в соответствии с логикой системы обучения Романа, сфокусированной на продажах недвижимости.
Нейросеть выступает в роли помощника Романа по обучению брокеров, предоставляя управленческий разбор звонков с конструктивной критикой, а не просто пересказ; тон ответа должен быть прямым и практичным.
Главная философия системы продаж заключается в том, что брокер продает не квадратные метры, а доверие, безопасность, спокойствие и мечту клиента, следуя формуле: Доверие → страхи → истинное возражение → техника → инструмент продаж + соус → тип клиента → следующий шаг.
Основной принцип работы брокера — сначала установить доверие и понять клиента (его мотивацию, страхи, опыт), и только потом переходить к презентации объекта недвижимости; преждевременная презентация является ошибкой.
Голова клиента сравнивается со "стаканом", наполненным страхами и сомнениями, и задача брокера — сперва "вычерпать" это содержимое с помощью вопросов, прежде чем наполнять его своей логикой и презентацией.
Для построения доверия брокер должен следовать шести правилам: демонстрировать позитивную энергию, больше слушать клиента, цепляться за детали в его речи, проявлять искренний интерес, находить общие личные темы и позиционировать себя как знающего проводника.
Брокер должен действовать как "проводник", который разъясняет клиенту все этапы сделки, от оплаты до регистрации и сценариев выхода, чтобы развеять страхи и создать ощущение безопасности, что особенно важно для клиентов типа "Безопасность".
Возражение клиента следует рассматривать не как отказ, а как признак заинтересованности, сопряженный с неразрешенным страхом или сомнением, что означает, что клиент все еще находится в процессе сделки.
Брокер должен отличать ложные возражения ("дорого", "подумаю") от истинных, задавая уточняющие вопросы для выявления настоящих причин сомнений, таких как недоверие, страх или недостаток информации.
При отработке возражений следует использовать специальные техники: сначала раскрывать суть возражения вопросами, соглашаться с эмоцией клиента, калибровать его истинные барьеры, применять "продажу от обратного", снимать давление, использовать технику "зеркало + пауза", просто делать паузу и управлять диалогом через формулу "короткий ответ → свой вопрос".
Переписка с клиентом должна быть структурирована: одно сообщение — один главный вопрос, который ставится в конце, и следует избегать перегрузки клиента множеством документов.
Анализ звонка должен включать оценку использованных брокером инструментов продаж: от личной упаковки в WhatsApp и внешнего вида до применения соцсетей, наград, отзывов, инфоповодов, сравнительных таблиц и рассказов о прибыли.
"Соус" — это правильная подача инструмента продаж, упаковывающая смысл так, чтобы вызвать у клиента интерес и мотивировать к действию; при анализе необходимо оценивать наличие и качество этой подачи.
Продажи должны осуществляться через эмоции и визуализацию, создавая у клиента ощущение мечты и будущего опыта, а не просто перечисляя сухие характеристики объекта.
Необходимо определять один из четырех типов клиентов (Эго, Забота, Комфорт, Безопасность) и адаптировать под него аргументацию, продавая статус, заботу о семье, удобство или прозрачность сделки соответственно.
Один и тот же объект недвижимости можно успешно продать любому типу клиента, используя разную аргументацию, адаптированную под его ключевые ценности.
Анализ звонка должен включать 15 обязательных блоков: от общей оценки и портрета клиента до разбора техник, инструментов, "соуса", эмоциональной составляющей, управления разговором и рекомендаций по следующему шагу.
Если требуется PDF-отчет, он должен быть структурирован по определенному шаблону из 17 пунктов, включая обложку, выводы для руководителя, разбор всех аспектов звонка и готовое follow-up сообщение, но без скриптов и чек-листов по умолчанию.
Обратная связь брокеру должна быть конкретной и основанной на примерах из звонка, указывая на упущенные возможности и конкретные ошибки, а не на общие фразы.
Предоставлены примеры конкретных формулировок для анализа, описывающих типичные ошибки брокеров, такие как преждевременная презентация, слабая дожимка, отсутствие "соуса" или неправильная работа с типом клиента.
Приведен пример готовой оценки звонка, включающий балл, краткий вывод, указание на главную ошибку, определение типа клиента и рекомендации по дальнейшей работе с ним.
Предложен полный стартовый промпт для другой нейросети, который задает ее роль, логику анализа, структуру отчета и ключевые принципы работы, включая формат PDF и правила переписки.
Также предоставлена короткая версия стартового промпта для быстрого запуска анализа звонка, фокусирующаяся на ключевых элементах системы оценки.

name: aiops poc and demo
author: Velum
description: Transform sales calls into structured demo guides, POC playbooks, and categorized customer Q&A.
body:
This document outlines the requirements for analyzing an AIOps Proof of Concept (POC) and demo call, with the goal of creating a structured enablement guide.
The first requirement is to produce a clean and structured transcript of the call, identifying speakers, correcting grammar, removing filler words, and marking any unclear audio.
The analysis must break down the demo and pitch for the Dell AIOps Application Observability product (IBM Instana), extracting the pitch structure, demo sequence, features highlighted, pain points addressed, value propositions, effective phrases, and how Instana was positioned with Dell technologies.
A summary of the Proof of Concept (POC) selling strategy is required, including how the POC's value was framed, any "low friction" phrases used, calls to action, and how objections and buying signals were handled.
All customer questions and the representative's answers must be listed and categorized by topic, such as licensing, deployment, integrations, Kubernetes, OTel, dashboards, and metrics/logs/traces.
Key value messages for Dell AIOps / IBM Instana need to be extracted, covering aspects like automated discovery, 1-second granularity, end-to-end tracing, root-cause analysis, container visibility, and integration with Dell solutions.
Any explicit or implied competitive comparisons to products like Dynatrace, New Relic, AppDynamics, and Datadog must be identified, summarizing how Instana was differentiated.
The final output is a comprehensive Demo & Pitch Guide based on the call analysis, which includes a recommended pitch structure, a suggested demo flow, discovery questions for sellers, a POC selling playbook, common customer questions with answers, and observed best practices.

name: Job Call - Event Information
author: Velum
description: Paste the transcription. Receive results, summary, and a table with evidence, points, improvements, and contact.
body:
The objective is to define guidelines for a Vivo sales quality supervisor to analyze and evaluate a call transcription, focusing on the clarity of product presentation, understanding customer needs, and managing the closing correctly.
During the call opening, the salesperson should greet, identify themselves and Vivo, explain the reason for the contact, ask questions to understand customer needs, and present a compatible offer.
The evaluation of the product presentation requires verifying if the salesperson clearly explained the product name, price, internet allowance, promotion duration, loyalty terms, and installation or portability conditions, pointing out vague or contradictory information.
The analysis of argumentation and conduct checks if the salesperson connected benefits to customer needs, answered objections clearly, and maintained a professional demeanor without pressuring the interlocutor.
The call result should be classified as confirmed sale, in progress, no sale, or inconclusive. In case of a sale, it is necessary to verify the offer recapitulation, explicit customer confirmation, and explanation of next steps.
For confirmed sales, a mandatory final conference is required to explicitly validate the customer's contact phone and email, with specific classifications for the status of this verification.
The final response must follow a structured format, including the call result, a summary, an evaluation table with criteria and evidence, and a final highlight of positive points, priority improvements, and the appropriateness of the approach, as well as an alert if contact data confirmation is pending at closing.

name: Family Law: Initial Inquiry Client to Financial Professional
author: Velum
description: Summarizes initial consultations during separation/divorce. Case note plus internal strategy.
body:
The goal is to create a structured summary of an initial telephone conversation between a financial specialist for business valuation and a private individual in separation or divorce proceedings, serving both as an objective case note and an internal analysis of the consulting strategy.
The call log should document the context of the conversation, including date, participants, reason, status of proceedings, and how contact was established.
The case should be briefly described from the perspective of the calling party, including their own situation, that of the spouse, existing documents, the central point of dispute, and possible suspicions.
The client's goals and expectations must be recorded, including the specific request, core questions, financial and temporal constraints, and the legal context involving lawyers or courts.
A list of available and missing documents, such as annual accounts or salary statements, must be created, and the method for secure data transmission determined.
The discussed fee and engagement modalities, such as hourly rates, flat fees, the point at which costs begin, and concerns regarding costs, must be recorded.
The technical procedure proposed by the financial specialist should describe the suggested solution, the rough scope, the role delineation from the lawyer, an assessment of the mandate's meaningfulness, and the initial steps.
An internal analysis, not intended for disclosure, should include an understanding of the case, the suitability of the offer, an assessment of the mandate's chances, and a reflection on one's own conversation management.
The concrete next steps and tasks should be defined in bullet points, along with responsibilities and, if applicable, deadlines.

name: Meeting Report
author: Velum
description: Paste a transcript or notes. Get a snapshot, actions, agreements, and a scannable summary.
body:
The main goal is to create a compact, visual, and complete meeting report that quickly provides insight into the essence, actions, and agreements.
The first step is to create a 'Snapshot', a visual block with the main context of the conversation, such as participants, purpose, core message, tone, and the number of actions, follow-ups, and agreements.
Next, a short summary in 3-5 bullet points is provided, containing only the essence of the conversation such as the most important topics, messages, and decisions.
A clear list of 'My Actions' must be compiled, containing only concrete tasks that the user themselves must perform, with a strict definition that this only applies to explicitly promised or assigned tasks.
A 'Follow-up' section is used to record topics that need to be followed up on during a next contact, distinguishing between explicitly agreed and relevant points.
Concrete 'Agreements & Decisions' are briefly noted, explicitly stating who does what and when, without including others' tasks as one's own action points.
The complete substantive summary of the conversation is structured by logical topic, combining repetition, but retaining relevant details, names, and data.
An 'Between the Lines' analysis can be added to describe the underlying communicative layer, such as dynamics and non-verbal signals, with a strict distinction between fact and interpretation.
Information useful for future conversations and not yet sufficiently covered in other sections, such as goals, preferences, or context, is recorded in the 'Remember for later' section.
The core principles for analysis are accuracy, avoiding speculation or repetition, making responsibilities explicit, and prioritizing scannability and clear language.

name: Call Analysis in the MFC Call Center of Primorsky Krai.
author: Velum
description: The call center fills out a report based on the dialogue. It notes politeness, results, errors, and advice.
body:
New requirements are introduced for daily call monitoring in the MFC Call Center of Primorsky Krai, including mandatory analysis of dialogues with low ratings, politeness checks, and recording of client issue resolution.
Key information for call analysis is recorded: date, time, subject, and conversation duration.
The applicant's speech is analyzed by episodes such as the reason for the inquiry, questions asked, additional clarifications, and their emotional state.
The operator's speech is analyzed by episodes such as greeting, clarifying questions, consultation, proposed solution, and conversation wrap-up.
The use of mandatory speech modules by the operator is checked, including greeting, introduction, polite phrases, needs clarification, understanding check, summarizing, and farewell.
The result of the inquiry is assessed based on whether the issue was resolved (yes/partially/no), and if not, the reasons, operator's actions, and possible alternative options are analyzed.
Identified operator errors are recorded, such as violation of standards, insufficient needs identification, lack of alternatives, lack of final informing, or incorrect consultation.
Positive aspects of the operator's work are noted, including competent consultation, handling objections, showing initiative, and adherence to communication standards.
A final quality assessment of the operator's work is made on a five-point scale based on criteria of politeness, competence, needs identification, issue resolution, and standard adherence.
The quality controller provides a brief conclusion of the conversation and gives recommendations to the operator.

name: Weekly WHS Meeting
author: Velum
description: Convert safety calls into records of incidents and training. Track upcoming work and action items.
body:
The primary purpose is to convert a phone call recording into a structured "WEEKLY WHS CATCH-UP RECORD" for a WHS consultant in NSW.
The record must begin by documenting the date, site, and attendees of the phone meeting.
The first section requires listing any incidents, hazards, or near misses since the last meeting, or stating "None reported" if there are none.
The second section involves confirming that all incidents, hazards, and near misses are logged in Lucidity and listing any outstanding entries.
The third section details training and competency, covering completed training, required or outstanding training, and any due inductions, licenses, or refreshers.
The fourth section outlines upcoming work activities for the next week, specifically identifying any high-risk work or changes in site conditions.
The fifth section addresses change management, describing any modifications to work methods, equipment, personnel, or site conditions, and confirming if SWMS or risk assessments need review.
The sixth section lists any documents, procedures, or registers that require review or updating.
The seventh section identifies the need for creating any new documents, SWMS, procedures, or risk assessments.
The eighth section is for capturing any concerns, suggestions, or safety matters raised by the team.
The ninth section plans the next week's Toolbox Talk, specifying the topic, key points, and the responsible person.
The final sections include space for any other items, a list of action items with responsible persons and due dates, general notes, the name of the person who prepared the record, and the date for the next catch-up.

name: Sales Pitch for Calls
author: Velum
description: For sales calls. Extracts client info and needs. Provides structured summaries and next steps.
body:
Client Introduction: Identify and summarize client details including name, title, company, and relevant background information discussed during the call.
Detailed Call Summary: Provide a narrative summary of the call, covering discussed topics, decisions made, identified pain points, and any significant statements or shifts in direction, maintaining a logical flow and conversational tone.
Client Requirement Breakdown - Requirements: Extract the client's essential needs, encompassing technical, business, or operational objectives.
Client Requirement Breakdown - Demands: Identify explicit conditions or non-negotiable requirements stated by the client, such as pricing, delivery format, legal constraints, or solution architecture.
Client Requirement Breakdown - Preferences: Capture any stated desires that are not strict demands, including preferred interface, workflow, communication methods, or pricing models.
Client Requirement Breakdown - Timeline: Outline any expected timelines, deadlines, or project phases mentioned, including stated launch or pilot dates.
Client Requirement Breakdown - Expected Delivery: Summarize delivery expectations, specifying format (e.g., PDF, API), frequency, or handoff methods, and including any discussed SLAs or cadences.
Client Requirement Breakdown - Special Requests: Identify any unique requests or custom needs, such as localization, branding, security compliance, or integration with third-party systems.
To-Dos and Next Steps: Generate an actionable to-do list based on the conversation, detailing tasks, assigned responsibilities if mentioned, and any associated due dates, presented in clear, concise bullet points.

name: Call Analysis and Communication Coach Template
author: Velum
description: Suitable for workplace call reviews. By restoring the original dialogue, analyzing the other party's emotions and core viewpoints, it helps you formulate more effective communication and response strategies.
body:
Set the role as a professional communication analysis and meeting coach, whose core goal is to complete four steps based on the call transcript content: original transcript, extraction of the other party's views, emotional fluctuation analysis, and communication strategy suggestions.
The first step requires an original call transcript, which needs to retain speaker identifiers, all interjections and colloquial expressions, and mark unintelligible segments.
The second step is to extract the main views and ideas of the other party (not our side), including sorting out their core arguments, attitudes, and demands, and marking key turning points or subtext.
The third step requires analyzing the other party's emotional and affective fluctuations during the call, clarifying the overall emotional tone, and quoting the original text to point out key emotional change segments.
The fourth step is to combine the aforementioned analysis to generate specific communication strategy suggestions for the user, covering dialogue strategies, psychological strategies, and information strategies.

name: Phone Technical Support
author: Velum
description: For support teams. Converts transcripts into structured summaries, issue details, and sentiment.
body:
The AI assistant specializes in analyzing customer service and technical support phone call transcripts to document calls, issues, and relevant details in a structured format.
The primary goal is to process a phone call transcript between a technical support agent and a client, generating a summary and detailed breakdown.
The output requires organization into specific sections: Call Summary, Key Information, Issue Description, Troubleshooting Steps, Resolution, Customer Sentiment Analysis, and Actionable Insights & Recommendations.
Key Information to extract includes Date of Call, Time of Call, Case/Ticket Number, Agent Name, Client Name, Client Contact Information, and Product/Service in Question.
The Issue Description must clearly and concisely detail the technical problem or question, including specific error messages, symptoms, or behaviors.
Troubleshooting Steps should be listed with actions performed, client responses, results, and any agreed-upon suggestions for the client to try.
The Resolution section must state the final outcome, indicating if the issue was resolved, requires follow-up, or was escalated, and detailing the solution or next steps.
Customer Sentiment Analysis involves assessing the client's tone and language, categorizing overall sentiment as Positive, Neutral, or Negative, with justification from transcript examples.
Actionable Insights & Recommendations, if provided, should identify opportunities for product, service, or support process improvements and suggest feedback for other departments.
The output must be presented in a clear, well-organized manner using Markdown for headings and lists.

name: RAH Inquiry Call
author: Velum
description: Summarize inquiry calls into organized reports on client needs, schedules, and care goals.
body:
The primary purpose is to use a template for home care inquiry calls to collect detailed information on prospective clients' needs, living situations, and scheduling preferences for internal assessment and care planning.
The objective is to generate a structured summary of the inquiry call, capturing key details like caller and client information, living situation, care needs, required assistance (ADLs, IADLs), scheduling, and care goals for internal use.
The summary should be a professional, clear, and concise intake document with a compassionate tone, intended for internal review by care coordinators, scheduling staff, and management.
The initial information to collect includes the caller's details (name, relationship, contact) and how they heard about Right at Home, along with the prospective client's personal and contact information.
It is necessary to understand the client's living situation, who they live with, current support systems, and the specific reasons for seeking care, including any recent health changes or diagnoses.
Scheduling preferences must be documented, including the desired care model (e.g., hourly, live-in), days and hours per week, preferred time of day, and the ideal start date.
A detailed checklist is used to identify the specific types of assistance needed, covering Activities of Daily Living (ADLs), Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs), household help, transportation, and companionship.
The summary concludes by capturing the primary goals of care, any special preferences or concerns, the desired service start timeline, and defining the next steps, such as scheduling an in-home assessment or a follow-up call.

name: Phone Note
author: Velum
description: Creates a professional phone note from your input. You enter the date, time, name, and conversation content. A short, coherent text in a fixed structure is generated, without assumptions. Phone numbers are only included if mentioned.
body:
This document defines mandatory formatting and content rules for creating phone notes.
The heading must follow the fixed format "Phone Note: [Weekday], [DD.MM.YYYY] | [Time]".
The second line specifies the type of contact (e.g., Caller, Email, WhatsApp) followed by the person's name, with "Caller" always used for calls and the name taken exactly as provided.
The content is recorded as a coherent, professionally and factually formulated text directly below the contact line, without further subdivisions or interpretations.
A phone note does not automatically represent a cancellation and can include various concerns such as appointment changes, additional services, or callback requests; no assumptions should be made or information added.
A provided callback number must always be noted; if none is provided, no number will be added.
The language style must be professional, concise, and clear, without colloquialisms, bullet points, or evaluations.

name: Chat Assistant for Good Friends
author: Velum
description: Input chat transcripts, output structured discussion outcomes. Extract viewpoints and interactions by person, identify implicit themes. Add objective encouragement and suggestions.
body:
The core task is to act as a professional thought planner, editor, and cognitive organizer, compiling transcribed audio content from multi-person growth discussions into a discussion outcome document that is deep, structured, and allows room for reflection.
A "Discussion Overview" needs to be generated at the beginning of the document, extracting core topics and their significance at the current stage.
Key viewpoints should be organized by individual participants, highlighting new ideas, information, or perspectives with cognitive value, avoiding a mere chronological account.
The interactive relationships between viewpoints must be presented, indicating recognition, supplementation, or questioning by others, and clearly showing the formation of consensus or evolution of viewpoints.
Implicit themes emerging from the discussion, such as recurring values, concerns, or potential consensus, need to be extracted.
After organizing the discussion, act as a bystander AI to objectively provide encouragement and suggestions to each participant.
The document's style should be restrained, sincere, clear in logic, and thought-provoking, like recording an important growth dialogue rather than meeting minutes.

name: Case Management Note
author: Velum
description: For UK case managers. Input call details; outputs neutral OneNote note with actions, agreements, flags.
body:
Case note drafting instructions for Ali Ward, a UK case manager at Chrysalis Case Management, based on a recorded phone call for a OneNote case diary, requiring an accurate, factual, neutral professional record.
Required output structure comprises “Phone call with [full name of the other person]”, “Re: [short topic, 5–12 words]”, “([call length, rounded up to the nearest minute] mins)”, a chronological narrative in paragraphs, “Agreed:” decisions/agreements, “Actions:” named actions with stated dates/timeframes, and “Highlight flags:” covering specified risk-related topics or “None”.
Narrative requirements include stating who initiated the call, writing in first person as Ali (“I called”, “I explained”, “I advised”), reporting others’ statements in past tense reported speech, and omitting small talk and pleasantries.
Accuracy and evidence rules include recording all money amounts, dates, times and names exactly as stated, using quotation marks for word-for-word significant statements (threats, risk, strong emotion, refusals, key commitments) with swearing verbatim, and using “[unclear]” for unclear details.
Style and formatting rules include UK spelling, UK date format (“12th February 2026”), plain text only with no tables and no extra headings, no opinions, interpretations or diagnoses, no added content beyond what was said, and using “None” where a section has nothing in it.
Highlight flags inclusion criteria are risk, safeguarding, health, medication, legal matters, money over £50, complaints, or significant changes in mood or behaviour; otherwise “None”.

name: Universal Phone Call Summary Prompt
author: Velum
description: Organize call notes. Extracts tasks, dates, and outcomes to help track commitments and next steps.
body:
This prompt provides a universal template for summarizing phone calls clearly and accurately by structuring the summary into specific sections.
The initial instruction is to classify the call into one of six types: CASUAL / CATCH-UP, ORGANISING / COORDINATION, WORK – INFORMAL, WORK – DECISION-DRIVEN, SALES / COMMERCIAL, or SUPPORT / ISSUE.
A concise paragraph summarizing the main topics, conversation flow, and any shifts in direction is required.
The call's outcome must be categorized as one of the following: NO ACTION, IN PROGRESS, PENDING, BLOCKED, or WON.
The summary must list all explicit or implied commitments and agreements made during the conversation.
A section for action items or tasks should detail the action, owner, timing, and relevant tags like [FOLLOW-UP] or [SCHEDULING].
Any mentioned or implied follow-ups must be detailed in a dedicated section.
The prompt requires extracting key concrete details such as names, dates, locations, and contact information.
Open-ended ideas, possibilities, or items discussed without a final decision should be captured separately.
Optional but encouraged notes on personal context, conversation tone, and relationship insights can be added.
Any confusion, unknowns, blockers, or risks identified during the call should be flagged, using [ISSUE] where applicable.
A clear statement on the single next best action is required, or "No immediate action required" if none exists.
The summary should conclude by applying relevant tags based on the conversation, such as [URGENT], [FOLLOW-UP], [CALLBACK], [SCHEDULING], [QUOTE], [ISSUE], or [COMPLETED].

name: Person-Centered/Active Listening (OARS) Note
author: Velum
description: Paste one call transcript. Get a snapshot, key turning point, objections, metrics, and fixes.
body:
The primary purpose is to provide a structured template for an expert coach to analyze and provide feedback on a cold call made by an outbound Sales Development Representative (SDR) selling IT services.
The "Call Snapshot" section requires the extraction of basic call details, including prospect information, company, call metadata, who was reached, the outcome, and the next step.
"Outcome & Where the Call Turned" involves a brief summary of the call's conclusion and identifying the single pivotal moment or quote that determined its direction.
The "Call Flow Breakdown" mandates a stage-by-stage evaluation of the call—from opener to close—using specific symbols (✅, ⚠️, ❌) to rate the performance at each step with a concise justification.
"What Was Done Well" is a section for listing 3-5 effective actions taken by the rep, supported by direct quotes to reinforce positive behaviors.
"What to Improve" focuses on 3-5 specific, actionable coaching points, detailing what happened, why it was detrimental, and what should be done differently.
The "Objection Log & Better Handles" section requires cataloging each objection, the rep's response, a rating of that response, and a suggested stronger, conversational rebuttal for future use.
"Talk Metrics" involves analyzing quantitative and qualitative aspects of the conversation, such as the talk ratio, use of filler words, monologue instances, and the rep's energy level.
The "Coaching Summary" concludes the analysis with an overall score and justification, identifying the top strength to maintain, the most critical issue to fix immediately, and a skill to practice.

name: INTAKE CALL Sheet Generator
author: Velum
description: For dementia home-care inquiries. Paste a transcript; get a structured call sheet with next steps.
body:
The primary task is to define a role for an administrative AI to process intake information for Pansy Homecare, a dementia-focused agency, and generate a structured "Client Initial Call Sheet" from transcribed inquiry calls.
Specific information to be extracted from call transcripts includes call metadata, general client and caller information, client demographics, and detailed care concerns.
Care concerns are detailed across several sub-categories: Dementia & Cognitive Status, Activities of Daily Living (ADLs), Medical & Physical Concerns, and Behavioral & Emotional Patterns.
The AI must also capture "Moments That Matter" (client's interests and comforts), a list of needed support areas, a proposed care schedule, the family and caregiver context, and the next steps for follow-up.
The output "Client Initial Call Sheet" must follow a strict format with specific bolded section headers, sub-headers, and formatting rules for different types of information, such as using bullet points for qualitative data and specific label formats for schedules.
The tone must be formal, factual, and use person-centered, respectful language, avoiding terms like "suffers from" and focusing on the client as a whole person, not just their diagnosis.
Key changes from previous versions include elevating "Dementia & Cognitive Status" to its own sub-section, adding a new section for "Moments That Matter (Initial)" to capture personal details early, and replacing a generic notes section with a more specific "Family & Caregiver Context" to understand family dynamics and caregiver stress.

name: Universal Trucking Call
author: Velum
description: Paste a full meeting transcript. Get notes grouped by project with topics and action items.
body:
The primary purpose is to create professional, structured Home Depot project coordination meeting notes from a complete transcript, serving as a detailed project record for development and consultant teams.
The notes must be organized hierarchically, starting with the meeting title, followed by each project identified by name and location, with subject headings for topics discussed and a consolidated list of action items for each project.
A provided list of example subject headings, such as Project Status, Entitlements, and Schedule, should be used only when relevant to the specific project discussion.
The writing style must be professional, concise, and factual, using complete sentences and consolidating repeated discussions while preserving important technical details, dates, and decisions.
The summary should be organized by project, not chronologically, and must clearly distinguish between confirmed decisions and issues still under review.
Do not include casual conversation, verbal filler, or speaker labels; only name individuals when they are assigned a specific action item.
Obvious transcription errors should be corrected, but no assumptions should be made about identities, locations, or technical facts; conflicting information should be flagged as needing confirmation.
The final output must follow a specific Markdown format: the meeting title as an H1 heading, each project as an H2 heading, relevant subject topics as H3 headings, and a final "Action Items" section under each project with a bulleted list of tasks, responsible parties, and deadlines only when explicitly stated.

name: Real Estate Sales Call Summary
author: Velum
description: Paste a call transcript. Get clear headings, actions, and a ready follow-up message.
body:
This document provides a structured template for a real estate agent to summarize a sales call, focusing on extracting key information for practical sales and follow-up notes.
The summary should start with a 3-5 sentence overview of the call, followed by sections detailing contact information, the caller's reason for contact, and their underlying motivation or situation.
A specific section requires identifying the caller's reason for moving from a predefined list of 11 options, assessing confidence, providing evidence, and suggesting a relevant follow-up question.
The template requires capturing the client's timeline, including any key dates or deadlines, and summarizing all mentioned property details such as address, condition, and renovations.
Key questions asked by the client and any concerns or objections they raised regarding price, timing, or market conditions must be listed.
The agent's advice given during the call should be factually summarized, and any potential sales, listing, or referral opportunities must be identified and categorized by lead temperature (Hot, Warm, Long-term, Not active).
A clear action list for the agent, client, or third parties should be created, alongside a suggested warm, professional follow-up message (email or SMS) using New Zealand terminology.
The instructions include creating a concise CRM-ready note detailing motivation, timeline, and next steps, and suggesting relevant CRM tags from a provided list to categorize the lead.
The summary must use New Zealand real estate terminology, remain factual without making assumptions, and focus on information relevant for sales follow-up.

name: MANAGER LED CONFLICT RESOLUTION CALL
author: Velum
description: Create an outline from a manager mediation call. Covers triggers, roadblocks, resolutions, commitments.
body:
The primary objective is to generate a detailed, professional meeting summary for a manager-led conflict resolution call, serving as a record for the participating managers.
The context is a facilitated discussion led by a senior manager between two subordinate managers to resolve structural disconnects, communication shortfalls, or interpersonal conflicts.
The summary should be structured into four chronological sections: default communication styles under stress, communication triggers that escalate conflict, communication styles that promote receptiveness, and a detailed breakdown of specific "roadblocks" discussed.
The "roadblocks" section requires a granular structure for each issue raised, detailing the issue summary, specific examples, the described impact, potential resolutions, and any commitments made by the managers.
The desired style is a blend of therapy session notes, professional mediation, and executive minutes, emphasizing objectivity, detail, and factual accuracy, including emotions and impacts as presented by the speakers.
The tone must be professional and detailed, prioritizing accuracy and comprehensiveness over conciseness, with all speakers referred to in the third person by their first name.
The final output should be a Microsoft Word document with specific formatting: a bold, size 16 title "Meeting Summary – [TOPIC]", the date in bold, size 9 font, and a list of participants also in bold, size 9 font, followed by the structured summary in an outline format with specified headings.

name: slavkigen
author: Velum
description: From call notes, generate a structured report with verbatims, risks, and actions. For small transport businesses.
body:
The role is to act as Filip Errutaki's assistant to generate a structured diagnostic call report, using the words of the transport company manager.
The COMPANY section must capture basic information about the company, including the company name, city, main activity, number of vehicles (HGV/LCV), number of drivers, and the person in charge of compliance.
The TRIGGER section aims to identify the reason for the call via an exact verbatim from the manager, by evaluating the urgency level (low, medium, high) and classifying the case (A: strong trigger, B: vague interest, C: curiosity).
The IDENTIFIED PAIN POINTS section consists of listing a maximum of three main problems expressed in the manager's own words.
The TACHY / ERRU RISK SIGNALS section is used to assess the company's risk level through specific questions about DTCO training, DREAL inspections, recent infringements, knowledge of the ERRU rating, and the archiving procedure.
The OBJECTIONS section aims to document the objections raised by the manager, Filip's responses, and the outcome of the exchange (objection resolved, partially resolved, or not resolved).
The DECISION section formalizes the outcome of the call: appointment booked, follow-up scheduled, refusal, commitments made, and associated dates.
The KEY VERBATIMS and ACTIONS FOR FILIP sections allow for keeping three significant quotes from the manager and listing Filip's next actions with their deadlines.

name: Client Phone Call Summary/Analysis
author: Velum
description: Organize legal call records into summaries. Lists topics and tasks to assist case documentation.
body:
The primary function is to analyze and summarize legal phone call audio recordings and transcripts between attorneys and clients, focusing on operational clarity and client satisfaction.
The output format requires a structured response with clearly labeled sections: Call Overview, Topics Discussed, Tasks to Be Completed, Follow-Up Requirements, and Tone & Empathy Analysis.
The Call Overview should include the date and time, a 3-5 sentence summary of the call's purpose, participant roles, key topics, and any relevant contextual information.
Topics Discussed should be broken down into subsections with bold headers, summarizing the discussion, attorney/client insights, and any supporting data, facts, or timelines.
Tasks to Be Completed must list action items for both attorney and client, specifying the responsible party, due date, and a clear description, using a format like "[Attorney] – Draft demand letter – Due by July 10, 2025".
Follow-Up Requirements involve identifying subjects or documents needing further clarification, noting scheduled meetings, and flagging pending reviews or third-party input.
Tone & Empathy Analysis requires evaluating the attorney's tone, assessing active listening and acknowledgment of client concerns, providing specific transcript examples, and evaluating the overall tone's appropriateness.
Additional instructions emphasize accurate yet accessible legal terminology, grounding insights in the transcript, maintaining a clear professional tone, and highlighting any risk areas.

name: Structured Summary of Drug Information
author: Velum
description: Input drug inserts or medication records to extract key information such as generic name, dosage form, and indications. Output a uniformly formatted structured summary for easy recording and retrieval.
body:
The task is to generate structured drug information summaries based on original text (such as drug inserts, doctor's orders, or medical records).
Content extraction guidelines require prioritizing the extraction and summarization of drug generic name, brand information, dosage form, main indications, specific symptoms, drug classification, specification, approval number, and optional core selling points.
Formatting and structure requirements stipulate that the summary should be vertically arranged, with the brand name (if any) at the top, followed by the drug generic name and dosage form; indications and symptoms are to be presented as a bulleted list; drug classification and core selling points are to be placed in the upper right corner; and specifications and approval number in the lower left and lower right corners, respectively.
The summary style should be objective, professional, concise, with intuitive and clear information presentation, avoiding complex sentence structures.

name: Morning Call
author: Velum
description: Paste a call recording. Get a structured summary with contacts, specs, budget, risks, and actions.
body:
The primary goal is to convert audio from a sales call into a structured summary for a Butler Metal Building project, capturing all necessary details for quoting and follow-up.
Key contact information to be identified includes the lead owner and the full contact details for the client, including their company.
The project overview requires documenting the timeline, site location, and specific building dimensions like length, width, eave height, and roof slope.
Technical requirements to be recorded cover all roof and wall system preferences (such as MR-24, VSR-II, Butlerib II, Moduleze), insulation needs, doors, windows, accessories, and any other special features discussed.
Additional technical specifications needed include requirements for foundation engineering, stamped calculations, installation services, the applicable building code, jurisdiction, and exposure category.
Client priorities and project constraints should be captured, including budget signals, required durability, long-term performance expectations, and any permitting issues.
Qualification factors for the lead must be determined, such as land ownership, budget availability, motivation level, and whether an architect or engineer is already involved or if design assistance is needed.
The final structured output should be organized into seven specific categories: Lead Owner/Contact Information, Project Overview, Client Priorities, Technical Requirements, Budget & Timeline Signals, Risks & Constraints, and Action Items.

name: Orsa call
author: Velum
description: Call analysis by checklist, assessment of client readiness and recommendations for the designer.
body:
Role: Sales analyst and call center auditor specializing in custom kitchen sales.
Task: Analyze the manager's conversation transcript according to 13 checklist points and assess the probability of sale considering critical factors.
Critical factors: Presence of the decision-maker at measurement/signing, kitchen installation within 120 days, client's intention to order a kitchen (not just a sketch).
Checklist: Includes items from greeting and presentation to cost clarification, meeting organization, availability of promotions, and meeting confirmation, as well as critical factors (decision-maker, deadlines, need).
Analysis of key indicators: Assessment of client reaction to points 8 (cost/interest), 11 (address/meeting time/contract), K1 (decision-maker at measurement), K2 (deadlines <120 days), and K3 (need: order).
Sales forecast: Checking the critical trio (K1-K3) to determine a 0% probability or further assessment on a scale.
Key drivers: Positive reaction to cost and meeting organization, confident answers on critical factors, absence of objections on price and deadlines.
Recommendations for designer: Targeted accents and risks based on conversation analysis.
Instructions: Requirement for direct quotes for critical factors, calculation of days until installation, analysis of client's emotional markers for point 8.
Response format: Brief checklist (points 8, 11, K1-K3), analysis of indicators with quotes and conclusions, sales probability forecast with reason (if 0%) and recommendations.

name: Phone Call
author: Velum
description: Capture preferences and tasks from intake calls. Helps agents organize client data and follow-ups.
body:
The provided template structures the summarization of an initial client intake call for a Nashville apartment locator, Sydney Healy of Apartment Insiders, to ensure all critical information is captured.
The initial section requires capturing the client's fundamental contact details: name, phone number, email address, and how they discovered the service.
Client apartment preferences must be documented, including the target move date, desired neighborhoods, budget range, bedroom and bathroom count, essential amenities, and lifestyle factors such as pets, work location, and parking needs.
A summary of the conversation should cover what the client is currently seeking, their original location, any urgency related to their move, and the underlying motivation for relocating.
The agent's process, as explained to the client, involves creating a list of 15-20 apartment options, meeting to narrow choices to a top 3 for touring, and clarifying that the service is free to the client, paid for by property referrals.
A follow-up plan needs to be established, noting the scheduled appointment time, the next steps like sending the options list, and any reminders for future contact.
Key quotes or specific details from the client, such as emotional cues, dealbreakers, or special comments, should be recorded.
The agent's internal action items after the call include adding the client to the CRM, sending a confirmation email with the list of options, and scheduling the appointment in the calendar.

name: Patient Communication Script Compliance Analysis
author: Velum
description: Позволяет оценивать звонки на основе скрипта и проверять качество сервиса.
body:
The main task is to analyze the transcribed conversation between a call center employee and a patient and create a structured report on the employee's adherence to the established script.
The employee must answer the call within 10 seconds, using a standard greeting that includes the time of day, clinic name, position, and name, and offer assistance.
The employee must ask for the patient's name and address them by name at least twice, and also clarify whether the patient is new or returning.
For new patients, the employee must offer an initial appointment and briefly describe the clinic.
The employee must ascertain the patient's request using various types of questions and provide full information about the services, offering at least two alternative options.
The employee must answer all questions and objections, book the patient for a service, clarify contact details, offer additional procedures, and inform about promotions.
When confirming the appointment, the employee must repeat the full name, service, day, date, time, and cost, and also explain how to get to the clinic, parking conditions, and remind them to bring a passport.
The employee must clarify the method of appointment reminder, ask if further assistance is needed, thank the patient, and politely end the conversation, waiting for the patient to hang up first.
The employee is obliged to remind about the service 24 hours before the appointment and confirm the booking.
If the call is put on hold, the wait should not exceed 30 seconds, or the employee should offer to call back; it is also necessary to call back within 15 minutes if the call was missed or interrupted.
The conversation should be free of extraneous noises, jargon, complex medical terms, and the particle "not", and the speech should be clear and understandable.
The employee's communication style should be natural, friendly, engaged, with a smile in their voice, demonstrating a high level of knowledge and competence.
The service should be proactive and intuitive, communication personalized, and the employee should act as an active listener.
In difficult situations, the employee should show self-control and empathy and offer acceptable solutions.

name: Service Call and Resolution Tracker
author: Velum
description: It extracts points, conclusions, and steps for the parties from the transcript. It marks what was not mentioned and recommends the tone for the next contact.
body:
The task is to analyze the transcript of communication between a financial intermediary and a client to create a factual and concise output usable as a summary for the client and as an internal record.
The output should be structured into eight points: summary, key information from the client, discussed topics, conclusions, open questions, next steps for the client, next steps for the intermediary, and a draft email.
When extracting information, focus on specific financial areas such as the 2nd and 3rd pillars, various types of insurance, investment, as well as the client's financial situation, goals, concerns, and decision-making criteria.
The analysis should also include an assessment of the client's communication type (analytical vs. relational) and recommendations for future communication, including appropriate tone, emphasis, and topics to avoid.
All information must be based exclusively on the provided transcript; unverified data should be marked as 'not mentioned' or 'needs completion'.
The resulting document should be professional, in Slovak, and without unnecessary phrases, prepared for use as both an internal summary and a basis for an email to the client.

name: PreQualification Questions
author: Velum
description: Extracts credit, employment, and assets from call transcripts into a structured borrower profile.
body:
The document provides a structured template for extracting and summarizing a borrower's responses during a mortgage pre-qualification call, instructing to ignore irrelevant conversation and leave unmentioned fields blank.
The Borrower Profile section captures the applicant's name, first-time home buyer status, application type (solo or with a co-borrower), and the purpose of the loan.
The Employment Information section requires a two-year history, including employer name, job title, and employment type, with specific details for W2 income (hourly/salary, overtime) and self-employment (business tenure, tax filing method).
The Credit Overview section aims to gather the borrower's estimated credit score and identify the reasons for any negative impacts if the score is 680 or below.
The Assets & Savings section documents the total amount of funds available for a down payment, the source of these funds, and any additional financial reserves.
The Loan Preferences section records the borrower's target monthly payment, preferred loan program, and any special circumstances such as new construction or the need for down payment assistance (DPA).
An Additional Notes section is included to capture any other relevant comments or personal details that could affect loan qualification.
A formatting note directs an AI tool named Velum to return the extracted information in a structured bullet format and to repeat the sections for each individual if there are multiple borrowers.

name: Lucas Leal Advogados (Health Law)
author: Velum
description: Send the transcript and generate a structured summary, documents, amounts and next steps. Cut after the end.
body:
The main objective is to define a template for creating structured summaries of legal meetings on health law, serving the Lucas Leal Advogados firm.
The defined persona is a legal assistant specialized in health law in Brazil, focusing on denials from health plans and SUS, abusive premium adjustments, and income tax exemption for people with serious illnesses.
It is crucial to identify the real end of the meeting and discard any subsequent content, such as farewells, conversations about other subjects or noises, recording this action at the end of the summary.
The summary must follow principles such as objective language, fidelity to facts, exact preservation of names, dates and amounts, and marking uncertainties or approximations.
The output structure is mandatory and hierarchical, starting with a standardized title ([Client's name] - [dd/mm] - [Main subject]) and followed by sections such as Header, Executive Summary, Case Identification, Chronology, Amounts, Legal Aspects, Documents, Next Steps and Points of Attention.
The Next Steps section should be a checklist with actions, responsible parties and deadlines, including standard tasks for each type of case.
The Points of Attention section should highlight medical urgencies, the client's emotional state and critical deadlines.
The template adjusts to the type of meeting, focusing on data collection in screenings and case evolution in follow-up meetings.

name: Call Grading ABA
author: Velum
description: Score sales calls using quotes and ratings to identify coaching needs for better performance.
body:
The Call Grading Template is designed for sales evaluation to ensure quality assurance, identify coaching opportunities, and maintain consistent sales performance.
For each evaluation section, assign a score from 1 to 5 and provide supporting notes with justifications and direct quotes from the call.
Introduction & Agenda: Assess if the representative introduced themselves clearly and confirmed the appropriate time for the call while setting expectations.
Accuracy: Evaluate if the representative provided correct information regarding entity structure, compliance, or tax points, and answered questions clearly and confidently.
Discovery: Determine if the representative asked probing, open-ended questions, followed the sales discovery script, and uncovered future planning opportunities or additional needs.
Pitch & Price: Review if the proposed solution directly connected to the client’s goals and if pricing was presented clearly and confidently.
Objection Handling: Assess if the representative confidently and professionally addressed concerns, effectively using re-framing or redirecting techniques.
Ask for the Sale: Evaluate if the representative confidently asked for the sale or moved to a clear next step with a direct and actionable close.
Additional Call Notes: Record any special circumstances, coaching opportunities, compliance issues, or client follow-up needs, and note if the representative demonstrated professionalism, empathy, or strong rapport-building.

name: Lead Call - Mortgage
author: Velum
description: Paste your call notes. Receive an internal summary with objectives, program, actions, and critical points.
body:
The objective is to define a structured summary format for mortgage lead calls, intended for internal use by a loan partner assistant.
The output format, named "LEAD CALL SUMMARY – INTERNAL", must include the lead's name and the call date.
The first section, "CALL SUMMARY", requires a 3 to 5-line summary about the client's objective, their general situation, and the most relevant points discussed.
The "QUALIFICATION STRATEGY" section should specify the financing program to be used (such as Foreign National, Conventional, FHA, etc.) or indicate "To be defined", listing multiple options if discussed.
The "POST-CALL ACTIONS" section should list objective tasks like sending documents, estimates, analyzing income, or following up, or indicate "No action defined" if applicable.
The "CRITICAL POINTS FOR QUALIFICATION" section should highlight factors impacting approval, such as income type, credit score, source of funds, or transaction structure, or state "No critical points identified".
General guidelines emphasize that the summary is for internal use, should be clear and scannable, without emojis, strictly based on call information, and focused on what impacts qualification and business closing.
The summary generation process involves inserting the lead's name, the call date, and raw conversation notes into an input field ("INPUT") for the assistant to generate the structured report.

name: Clear, clean, and highly detailed.
author: Velum
description: Converts call recordings into task lists. Extracts contact info and follow-ups with priority tags.
body:
The conversation is being recorded for task review, requiring accurate transcription and summarization of actionable insights and follow-up needs.
The summary goals include identifying tasks, action items, or promises; highlighting names, contact details, and addresses; extracting scheduling information or service requests; and tagging critical keywords.
Keywords are to be tagged using specific bracketed notations: [URGENT] for "ASAP" or "urgent", [QUOTE] for "quote" or "estimate", [FOLLOW-UP] for "follow up" or "get back", [CALLBACK] for "call back" or "reach out", [SCHEDULING] for "schedule" or "reschedule", [COMPLETED] for "done", "completed", or "finished", and [ISSUE] for "problem" or "issue".
The conversation summary section is intended for a one-paragraph overview of the call's purpose.
The Action Items/Tasks section requires listing tasks with descriptions and any present tagged keywords.
The Follow-Ups Required section is for detailing follow-up actions with the relevant person/subject and date, including the [FOLLOW-UP] tag.
The Key Details Extracted section is for listing extracted names, phone numbers, unit numbers, and addresses.
The Flagged Keywords & Tags section provides examples of how keywords are flagged, such as "[URGENT]: “Customer said they need this fixed ASAP.”", "[QUOTE]: “Wants an estimate on the plumbing replacement.”", and "[CALLBACK]: “Asked us to call him back tomorrow morning.”".

name: Call/Meeting Notes
author: Velum
