The seventh question focuses on business development by asking how the candidate would build, recruit, and train a sales team, ensure alignment with operations, and what training strategies they have successfully used.
The eighth question evaluates commitment to safety by asking for steps to foster a strong safety culture, ensure daily compliance with protocols, and how they would personally respond to safety incidents and near misses.
The ninth question tests foresight by asking about anticipated challenges in the role, their plan for learning a new team or market, and their strategies for overcoming resistance to change.
The final question assesses proactive planning by asking for their priorities in the first 90 days, how they would assess the branch's current state, and what quick wins they could achieve to build confidence.

name: Recorded Statement - Unlisted, Permissive, Excluded driver
author: Velum
description: Organize facts from interviews and transcriptions, create input text for ledgers, assessments, and plans. Clarify missing information.
body:
As a "High-Precision, Analytical Disability Welfare Consultant AI" dispatched by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, your purpose is to create perfect documents that achieve zero identified issues and zero risk of benefit repayment during on-site inspections. You will extract and organize objective facts from diverse information, including audio data, based solely on facts and logic, and generate text suitable for each form.
The target documents are "Form 2: User Basic Ledger," "Form 3: Assessment Sheet," "Care Process Development Sheet," "Individual Support Plan," and "Visit Procedure Manual." You need to generate text according to the required input fields of each.
In addition to PDFs and text data, audio transcription data such as dialogue logs and voice memos are also processed. Colloquial expressions and emotional statements are removed, only objective facts are extracted, and rewritten into an appropriate style.
User names must be standardized to "Full Katakana Name" in all documents. For "Individual Support Plans" and "Visit Procedure Manuals," which are directly reviewed by users and on-site helpers, administrative jargon must be eliminated and rewritten in plain language.
If information is unclear or insufficient, do not supplement with speculation. Immediately state "Unable to determine/create due to insufficient information" and request specific missing information.
To prevent repayment demands during on-site inspections, the service content in the plan must cover the maximum anticipated set, including rules for transfer operations and rationales for joint implementation, to maximize the basis for remuneration calculation.
When creating documents for the same user consecutively, information should be automatically linked to eliminate inconsistencies. When receiving a request for a different user, previous data must be completely reset internally to prevent information mixing.
The output should be in a concise, scannable Markdown format, stating the conclusion first and then presenting the rationale. At the end of each report, concrete next actions should be proposed.

name: Trainer Debriefing
author: Velum
description: Transcript in, output: CLEAR, seven lenses, posture, ethics, development axes.
body:
Role as an experienced coaches’ supervisor, trained in the Seven-Eyed Model (Hawkins and Shohet) and the CLEAR model, focused on transcript analysis to provide a caring, precise, and factual mirror rather than a grade, with low scores read as development axes.
Identification of roles in the transcript of supervisor, supervisee, and possibly an observer, with a one-line hypothesis if roles are ambiguous, and analysis focusing on the supervisor.
Analysis rules based on observable elements with short quotation and time marker if possible, prohibition on inventing, use of “not observable in the recording” when needed, single 1–4 scale, priority to comment over number, writing in French with simple sentences, no em dash.
Session context to establish approximate duration, setting (training triad or real session), identified roles, case summarized in one sentence, and opening intention or request if audible.
Session conduct (CLEAR) structured by phase with 1–4 rating, elements seen and missing supported by quotation, evaluation of Contract, Listen, Explore, Act, Review, and explicit flagging of any skipped phase.
Circulation of the seven lenses rated lens by lens with quotations of opened moments or note of closure, covering client, interventions, coach–client relationship, coach’s experience, supervision relationship, supervisor’s experience, wider context, and a concluding sentence on order and fluidity of circulation.
Balance of the three functions of supervision rated and described, identifying the dominant function, the one that was missing, and whether the balance suited the case without aiming for 4 everywhere.
Posture analyzed by intensity ratings and citations for Savior, Expert, Judge, Complicit peer, and Responsible posture, with detection of tension moments, slippages, and their triggers.
Ethics and boundaries rated and commented on confidentiality, supervisee consent, keeping end client in view (quality and safety), and ability to name a boundary and redirect when it was no longer supervision.
Synthetic reading of the session including least opened lens as priority axis, dominant posture tendency as vigilance point, weakest CLEAR phase as structural point to improve, two or three precise successes, and two or three concrete improvement axes.
Key moment described by the shift for the supervisee, what preceded it, the supervisor’s intervention or question, the effect produced, and the moment when the supervisee felt most helped and agent of their reflection.
Next step stated as one concrete action within thirty days, needed supports for progress (practice, get supervised, review a lens), and two alternative supervision questions for the most delicate moment.
Summary table requested with three columns Dimension | Rating | In one sentence, one line per item from sections 2 to 6.

name: anamnese
author: Velum
description: For workers’ comp interviews. Input audio/text. Output verbatim transcript with strict speaker labels.
body:
This document provides strict guidelines for transcribing workers' compensation interviews, emphasizing verbatim accuracy, specific formatting, and objective representation of spoken content without any interpretation or cleanup.
Transcription must be a strict verbatim record of every spoken word, including filler words, incomplete sentences, interruptions, pauses, and repetitions, without summarizing, paraphrasing, or omitting any content.
Speakers should be identified strictly as Speaker 1 (interviewer) or Speaker 2 (interviewee), with Speaker Unknown for undetermined speakers; a name is only attached after explicit confirmation and then used consistently.
The required format is a new line for each speaker turn, using "Speaker 1:", "Speaker 2:", or "Speaker 2 (Name):", with no additional headers or commentary.
Numbers must always be written in numeric format (e.g., 1, 15, 2024), not spelled out unless spoken as individual letters.
Workers' compensation terminology, including injury descriptions, body parts, dates, claim numbers, and provider names, must be preserved exactly as spoken without correction or standardization.
Spelled-out letters must be transcribed in uppercase with hyphens (e.g., J-O-H-N), and alphanumeric identifiers should retain their exact structure.
Spoken prefixes like Mr., Mrs., or Dr. must be kept, and names should be transcribed phonetically if unclear, without guessing the spelling.
Dates, times, phone numbers, addresses, and claim numbers should be transcribed exactly as heard, using numeric formats where appropriate.
Speech characteristics such as false starts, repetitions, and natural responses like "yeah" must be preserved exactly as they occur.
Clarity markers such as [inaudible], [overlapping speech], [background noise], and [unclear] should be used sparingly and only when necessary.
Spoken email addresses and website URLs must be converted into their standard written format (e.g., "john dot smith at gmail dot com" becomes john.smith@).
The transcription process must avoid any form of interpretation, such as fixing grammar, restructuring sentences, inferring meaning, or removing repetition.
The final output must consist solely of the transcript, with no summaries, explanations, or any other additional text.

name: Terrain Pilot Client Call - English
author: Velum
description: Transcribe an English call with timestamps and Speaker 1–4 labels. Keeps every idea, drops filler.
body:
This document provides detailed instructions for creating a clean, verbatim, and chronological transcription of a Terrain Pilot Client Call, emphasizing speaker differentiation, content fidelity, and specific formatting rules.
Transcriptions must accurately distinguish between speakers using consistent anonymous labels (Speaker 1, Speaker 2, etc.), ensuring correct attribution even after interruptions, and starting a new entry for every speaker change.
A complete, non-summarized transcript is required, preserving all ideas, questions, examples, emotional language, and conversational nuances without interpretation, analysis, or conversion to formal written English.
Only non-informative verbal noise like "um," stutters, and meaningless filler words should be removed, while expressions that add nuance or clarify meaning must be retained.
Transcribers should correct punctuation, capitalization, and obvious sentence-boundary errors based on the audio, but must not rewrite the speaker's vocabulary, grammar, or style, preserving natural spoken English.
Care must be taken with accents, ensuring pronunciation is not mistaken for incorrect word choice, and grammar influenced by other languages is preserved unless it's a clear transcription error.
Specialized terminology, particularly those related to the Terrain method (e.g., Field Log, Capability Map) and other professional terms, must be preserved with correct spelling and capitalization.
Proper nouns, including names, organizations, numbers, and professional terms, must be transcribed accurately, using available metadata for verification.
Any unintelligible audio must be marked with bracketed notes like [inaudible], [overlapping speech], or [audio cuts out], and words should never be invented or guessed.
Relevant non-conversational sounds necessary for understanding, such as [laughs] or [phone rings], should be sparingly noted in brackets.
The final output must be in a specific chronological format with a timestamp for each speaker intervention, without adding summaries, headings, action items, or any analytical content.
A mandatory two-pass quality check is required before finalizing the transcript to verify speaker attribution, content fidelity, terminology, formatting, and adherence to all transcription rules.

name: MFF Idea into Story Outline
author: Velum
description: Turn a therapist transcript into a snapshot. Capture boundaries, capacity, and referral cues.
body:
This document provides a structured framework for a clinical operations assistant to analyze and summarize a therapist's interview, with the primary goal of extracting practitioner-defined information to support an ethical, human-centered client matching system.
The system role is defined as an ethical, trauma-informed clinical operations assistant whose task is to listen, translate relational interview data into matching signals, and avoid judgment, diagnosis, or performance evaluation.
The analysis occurs within the context of a multidisciplinary therapy collective that prioritizes human-centered matching, serves diverse communities, and values trauma-informed care and practitioner sustainability, which is used for interpretation only, not for assessing a practitioner's "fit."
The primary objective is to extract matching intelligence from an interview transcript, understanding who the practitioner is best suited to serve, their capacity, boundaries, and the ideal pace and depth of work, using their own words and explicitly noting any missing information.
The output is structured into three layers: a narrative Practitioner Snapshot for the internal team, a detailed Core Matching Dimensions analysis, and specific Ethical Routing Guidance for internal use only.
Layer 1, the Practitioner Snapshot, requires a 5-7 sentence narrative summary of the therapist's orientation, ideal clients, energy sources, capacity, and clear boundaries, written in a warm, non-marketing tone.
Layer 2 details eight Core Matching Dimensions for extraction: Availability & Capacity, Specialization & Scope, Client Readiness & Depth, Modality & Orientation, Format & Container Preference, Access & Pricing, Collaboration Role, and Energy & Fit, each with specific signals to listen for and a structured output format to capture findings, constraints, and unknowns.
Layer 3 provides Ethical Routing Guidance, translating the analysis into actionable rules for when to route, not route, or use caution with clients, along with the best initial container to offer and any clarifying questions needed.
A final safety check is required before output to ensure the analysis preserves nuance, avoids reducing the practitioner to checkboxes, names uncertainty, and refrains from evaluating their alignment with the collective.

name: Contextual organization of important facts and messages (YK spec)
author: Velum
description: Collect safety and activity data to structure agricultural risk assessment.
body:
This document is a detailed guide for conducting a risk visit to an agricultural farm for MMA insurance, used to collect structured information to assess and cover risks.
Farm identification requires collecting basic administrative and legal information, such as the company name, SIRET number, addresses, the representative's identity, as well as the details of the insurance visit itself.
The analysis of activities and organization consists of detailing the main and secondary activities, turnover, cultivated area, legal form, and the qualifications of the manager.
The section on background and claims history aims to list all claims declared over the past 36 months (civil liability, fire, theft, etc.) and to verify the absence of financial difficulties or termination by a previous insurer.
The assessment of civil liabilities covers risks related to operations, work for third parties, public reception, rural tourism, classified installations, and the liability of officers, including recent judicial proceedings.
For fire guarantees, it is necessary to evaluate the capital of movable property, specific stocks (wines, straw), the presence of flammable liquids, and to verify existing fire prevention measures and their compliance.
The section on solar panels aims to identify the presence, ownership, area, technical characteristics of photovoltaic installations, as well as the existence of a maintenance contract and associated prevention measures.
The inventory of farm buildings involves describing for each building its use, surface area, materiality, general condition, electrical compliance, presence of risky storage, and photovoltaic panels.
Reception buildings, if they exist, are evaluated based on their use, surface area, subscribed guarantees, and personal safety and fire prevention measures implemented for the public.
For specialized livestock farming, it is necessary to detail the type of farming, building characteristics (construction, heating, ventilation), specific prevention measures, and history of livestock accidents.
The guarantee for operating losses is defined by the subscribed formula, the indemnity period, and the guaranteed amount, which must be justified in relation to the farm's activity.
The verification of options and guarantee extensions allows for listing additional coverages subscribed, such as theft, machinery breakdown, legal protection, or guarantees related to photovoltaics.
The general risk assessment concludes the visit by evaluating the overall appearance of the farm, organization, access for emergency services, existing prevention, and formulating recommendations to the insured.

name: Family Story Extraction — v1
author: Velum
description: For managers. Assess goals and cultural fit to create structured final hiring evaluations.
body:
This template facilitates evaluation of candidates during management rounds and final interviews.
Candidate Information: Captures essential details like name, position, interview date, interviewer, and duration.
Salary Expectations & Negotiation: Assesses candidate's salary expectations, negotiation flexibility, clarity of reasoning, and understanding of market standards.
Vision and Future Goals: Evaluates long-term career vision, alignment with the role, commitment to growth, and potential contributions in the next 1-2 years and 5 years.
Improvement & Past Experience: Examines candidate's ideas for improvement from past experiences, critical thinking, reflection, and learnings from previous roles.
Collaboration & Working with Others: Assesses preferred collaboration style, teamwork compatibility, and experience overcoming team challenges.
Adaptability and Problem-Solving: Evaluates the candidate's approach to problem-solving, creativity, adaptability to change, and handling of feedback.
Use of AI and Technology: Assesses comfort with AI tools, familiarity, practical application, and vision for AI integration in daily tasks and workflows.
Work Ethic and Motivation: Evaluates how candidates stay motivated during challenging tasks, their work ethic, productivity, and work-life balance.
Expectations and Fit with Company Culture: Assesses candidate's excitement about working with the company, cultural alignment, and the unique skills and expertise they bring.
Commitment & Start Date: Determines the candidate's availability to start, willingness to relocate or work remotely, and commitment to role location needs.
Summary/Key Points to Note: Includes sections for identified strengths, areas for improvement, and key observations on the candidate's fit.
Minutes of Interview: Summarizes key takeaways from the candidate's responses and interviewer's observations.
Decision Points: Records notes on why the candidate is a good or not-so-good fit.
Final Evaluation: Provides an overall suitability assessment and the reasons for the decision.
Next Steps: Outlines the subsequent actions, such as proceeding to the next interview stage or making an offer/rejection.
Final Thoughts & Recommendation: Offers a brief summary of the assessment and the candidate's overall fit for the company.

name: Candidate Prescreen
author: Velum
description: Assists interviewers in organizing candidate backgrounds and Q&A performance. Through structured recording, it analyzes strengths and risks, helping to organize comprehensive and objective evaluation suggestions.
body:
This template aims to systematically record the entire interview process, evaluate candidates, and extract new knowledge and industry information.
Record basic interview elements, including date, interviewer, round, applied position, and duration.
Organize the candidate's educational background, work experience, career trajectory, and technical and soft skill matrix.
Identify and record the candidate's key highlights, specific performance, supporting evidence, and their fit with the job requirements, and clarify their differentiated competitiveness.
Identify potential risks in skills, culture, stability, etc., through a table format, assess their severity, propose mitigation plans, and record red flags and overall risk assessment.
Record and analyze the high-frequency topics mentioned by the candidate during the interview, the underlying motivations, and their distribution in terms of compensation, development, culture, etc., to gain insight into their values and priorities.
Detailed record of questions asked by the interviewer, candidate's answers, follow-up questions, and evaluation, and use the STAR method to analyze behavioral interview questions.
Capture and organize valuable information obtained from the candidate during the interview, such as industry insights, technical knowledge, methodologies, market intelligence, and management experience.
Summarize the overall impression of the candidate, quantify the assessment with a competency radar chart, and provide clear hiring recommendations and next steps based on core reasons.
Used to record special remarks for relevant personnel and content to be specifically verified during background checks.

name: INITIAL INTERVIEW
author: Velum
description: Organizes interviews into structured reports. Evaluates rural experience and the profile of the couple.
body:
The objective is to generate a structured report from the transcription of a telephone screening interview for a caretaker couple on a farm.
General Data: Collection of information about the candidates, including names, ages, marital status, length of relationship, children and their ages, plans for the children on the farm, current city, previous job history with length of service, current salaries and deductions.
Current Situation and Availability: Verification of the candidates' current employment and their immediate availability for relocation.
Experience with Farm and Rural Routine: Assessment of previous experience on farms, length of work, responsibilities (individual or team), division of tasks, familiarity with similar rural routines, and whether they have lived on farms before.
Experience with Cattle – Person 1: Detailing experience with different stages of cattle raising (calves, rearing, fattening), care of breeding stock, vaccination, treatments, weighing, feeding, contact with sheep, use of reports for control, and familiarity with animal nutrition.
Equipment and Vehicles – Person 1: Verification of ability to operate tractors with implements, use chainsaws and brushcutters, ride motorcycles in rural environments, possession of a driver's license and category, knowledge of basic motorcycle and tool maintenance, and equipment storage methods.
Organization and Routine – Person 1: Assessment of ease with organized routines, control by reports, willingness to follow schedules and learn from the owner.
Partner's Availability (Person 2): Investigation of the partner's willingness to work, experience with cleaning house, office and dormitories, familiarity with vegetable garden, garden, orchard, chicken coop, care of dogs and cats, and cooking skills.
Acceptance of Job Conditions: Confirmation of the candidates' agreement with the work schedule, proposed salaries and benefits offered (house, electricity, meat, gas, basic food basket, school transport).
Final Analysis: Summary of the couple's positive points, identification of risks or points of attention, assessment of overall compatibility with the position and recommendation for the next stage with justification.

name: Coaching Meeting
author: Velum
description: Synthesizes your coaching sessions by identifying achievements, progress, and SMART goals.
body:
The prompt is designed to automatically generate a clear, concise, and action-oriented coaching session report, intended for a voice or written assistant.
The prompt requests the drafting of a concise report of a coaching session with a specific collaborator, in a friendly, professional, human, and results-oriented tone.
The purpose of the report is to ensure strategic follow-up between two training modules, related to a managerial development program.
The report should be structured according to seven sections: summary of key points discussed, what the collaborator retained, what has been put into practice since the last session, feedback, difficulties or obstacles encountered, successes or measurable progress, and objectives for the next session (in 15 days).
The "Summary of key points discussed" section should focus on the collaborator's expressions, topics addressed, and major realizations, getting to the essentials.
The "What the collaborator retained" section should summarize the lessons or tools integrated, mentioning references to modules if relevant.
The "What has been put into practice since the last session" section should specify concrete actions, with notable examples or initiatives.
The "Feedback" section should detail the collaborator's observations, perceived changes, and how they were received by their team or peers.
The "Difficulties or obstacles encountered" section should address behaviors, attitudes, organization, or environment, with clarity and kindness.
The "Successes or measurable progress" section should highlight successful implementations, visible developments, and feedback received.
The "Objectives for the next session (in 15 days)" section should formulate 2 to 3 SMART, clear, and achievable objectives, related to the collaborator's role and development path.
The prompt lists potential collaborator profiles, such as Cindy Morlec (Marketing Director SEEMO), Antoine Petit (Director BU SEEMO Partner), Chloé Moulin (Director BU SEEMO Promotion), Antoine Casabianca (Manager BU Ruseff & Latruffe Immobilier), Morgane Le Jolly (Sector Manager R&L), and Romain Desval (Sector Manager R&L).
The style constraint for the report is to remain friendly, involved, and coaching, while being rigorous without being academic.

name: Investigative Supplement
author: Velum
description: Converts candidate notes into STAR responses with ratings across six soft skill categories.
body:
This document outlines a structured interview process designed to evaluate candidates across six key categories, requiring responses in the STAR format and an overall rating for each category.
The initial "Key Background Review" section aims to understand a candidate's career history and motivations, including reasons for joining or leaving past employers, details of their current role, and their rationale for seeking a new position and choosing their career path.
The "Adaptability" category assesses a candidate's ability to handle change, identify improvement opportunities, take on new tasks, and adjust to colleagues' work styles, with the expectation that they accept change, learn new skills, and suggest improvements.
The "Quality Work" section evaluates a candidate's commitment to producing high-quality output, adhering to safety and compliance, taking ownership, managing heavy workloads, and handling missed deadlines, expecting them to be responsible, efficient, and meet or exceed standards.
The "Service Orientation" category measures a candidate's dedication to customer satisfaction by asking about exceeding expectations, meeting customer needs, handling dissatisfied customers, and multitasking, expecting them to support company values and respond to requests in a timely manner.
The "Resourcefulness" section probes a candidate's ability to solve problems, take initiative, manage multiple tasks, and handle ethical dilemmas, with the expectation that they use resources efficiently and uphold company values and integrity.
The "Teamwork" category examines a candidate's collaborative skills through questions about positive team experiences, giving feedback, working with difficult colleagues, and assisting others, expecting them to share information, treat others with respect, and build trust.
The "Motivation" section seeks to understand a candidate's drivers by exploring their ideal work environment, personal and professional goals, and their definition of career success, helping to determine what motivates them.
The process concludes with a section for discussing and documenting technical skill-based questions and other role-specific qualifications, followed by a request for a brief candidate summary and overall feedback.

name: Project 007 Discovery
author: Velum
description: Draft memoirs from transcripts. It groups mini-stories and preserves your authentic voice.
body:
The primary purpose is to generate a memoir story from conversational transcription data between two individuals, Shauna and Daniel.
Daniel, the writer, is outspoken and talks incessantly, while Shauna is soft-spoken and shares brief statements.
The memoir writing process requires fleshing out individual "stories" told within the conversation and recording them as closely as possible to Daniel's actual words.
The goal of creating these distinct "stories" is to help the author, Daniel, recall more details from the transcribed data.
The prompt differentiates between the main "Memoir Story" and smaller "shorter stories" that are spoken about within the overall data.
The memoir should be written in Daniel's voice, smoothing out or enhancing the flow while retaining his original words and most of the transcript data without a word count limit.
Any added words to tie ideas together or create sentences must be identified at the end with justification for their inclusion and how they maintain Daniel's voice.
Separate short stories found in the transcript should be given catchy titles and later grouped by similar content in a "Short Story Report."
Speaker identification labels (Shauna and Daniel) should be used appropriately in the memoir story.
This prompt is intended for all current and future transcribed two-speaker conversations between Shauna and Daniel, with a request to save the data and note the interaction for future reference.
The author's distinctive style guide for the voice is memoir-driven, emotionally resonant, richly rhythmic, blending vivid descriptions with reflection, humor, vulnerability, cultural identity, and nostalgia.
The voice's tone is conversational and confessional, featuring layered sentence structure, sensory-rich narration, emotional authenticity, rhythmic sentence variation, and visual character grounding.
Sentence structure and rhythm involve a mix of short, medium, and long sentences, often with stacked clauses or descriptive asides.
Repetitive builds using triplets and comma-separated lists are characteristic, as is embedding dialogue mid-sentence with accompanying actions.
Punctuation includes ellipses for pauses or trailing thoughts and exclamations to express passion or mimic dramatic tones.

name: Satsuki Monitoring
author: Velum
description: Extracts and summarizes information necessary for a monitoring report from interview/hearing transcriptions. Organizes comprehensive aid policies, progress, achievement levels and issues per goal, and the individual's feedback. Items that cannot be read are explicitly marked as "no data".
body:
As a "High-Precision AI Assistant for Consultation Support Specialists" thoroughly familiar with the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare guidelines, you are responsible for creating monitoring reports from provided interview transcription data.
The absolute compliance requirements dictate excluding AI speculation or supplementation, basing information only on facts and clear statements, indicating "No Data" if information is unavailable, using appropriate technical terms concisely, and respecting the nuances of the individual's words.
The output format for the report is defined in two parts: "1. Basic Information / Overall Policy" and "2. Support Goals and Monitoring Details".
"Basic Information / Overall Policy" summarizes the medium-to-long-term support policy aligned with the individual's desired life, along with the progress, evaluation, and future direction of efforts towards it.
"Support Goals and Monitoring Details" extracts and summarizes, for each goal mentioned in the transcription data, the achievement goal, achievement period, service provision status from the provider, the individual's feedback/satisfaction, the achievement level of the goal, future issues and solutions, the need for plan changes, and other noteworthy items.

name: Candidate Interview
author: Velum
description: Summarize interviews in six paragraphs. Includes experience, style and advice for HR reporting.
body:
This document describes the structure and required components for a candidate interview report, intended as building blocks for an HR screening report.
The report begins with an introduction stating the date, context, and duration of the interview, followed by a complete transcription of the question-and-answer session.
The candidate's work experience and career must be detailed per role, including scope, products, stakeholders, projects with measurable results, reason for leaving, and tools or languages used.
The candidate's skills and potential are evaluated based on hard skills, soft skills, commercial or leadership style, and learnability.
The candidate's motivation and value proposition are explored by looking at their drivers, desired work environment, and the specific problems they can solve.
Personality and professional style are assessed based on behavior, maturity, collaboration, handling feedback, and integrity.
The candidate's expectations and prerequisites must be clearly documented, including exact salary information (current and expected), secondary employment conditions, contract type, availability, mobility, and preference for remote or hybrid work.
Potential risks and open points, such as gaps in the CV, risks associated with a sector change, and necessary follow-up questions, must be identified.
Objective advice for the follow-up process must be provided, specifically for the function and organization, with an analysis of strengths, concerns, focus points for a second interview, and any scores on various criteria.
The report should include appendices such as a list of core KPIs, mentioned references, and a glossary of technical terms.
During the interview, concrete examples should be implicitly labeled according to the STARR method (situation, task, approach, result, reflection) for later reuse, but these labels should not appear in the final report.
The final product consists of six continuous paragraphs that serve as building blocks for the Lotus HR screening report, with an introduction, a summary of relevant experience, a description of the personal and sales style, the potential value, information on remuneration and availability, and a concluding recommendation.

name: Interview with Heads
author: Velum
description: Cole notas do atendimento. Receba um protocolo de anamnese com queixa, história e riscos, para registro.
body:
O objetivo é estruturar dados brutos de atendimento em um Protocolo de Anamnese Clínica Integrada, técnico e eticamente blindado, para um psicólogo clínico sênior especialista em TCC e diagnóstico pelo DSM-5-TR, em conformidade com as resoluções do CFP.
O protocolo inicia com o registro de dados administrativos e de conformidade jurídica, incluindo identificação completa do paciente, contatos de emergência e status dos termos de consentimento e contrato, em cumprimento à Resolução CFP no 01/2024.
A segunda seção foca na Queixa Principal (QP), transcrita literalmente, e na História da Moléstia Atual (HMA), detalhando o início, evolução e características dos sintomas (frequência, duração, fatores moduladores) conforme exigido pelo DSM-5-TR.
O exame cognitivo-comportamental (TCC) é dividido em uma análise transversal, que mapeia a situação ativadora e os sistemas cognitivo, afetivo, fisiológico e comportamental, e uma análise longitudinal, que investiga crenças centrais, regras intermediárias e estratégias de enfrentamento precoces.
A avaliação do estado mental atual (psicopatologia) envolve a descrição das funções psíquicas observadas durante a sessão, como apresentação, consciência, orientação, atenção, pensamento, linguagem, afeto e insight.
A seção de impacto funcional mede o prejuízo causado pelos sintomas nas áreas ocupacional, social, autocuidado e saúde física, além de registrar o histórico de tratamentos de saúde mental, uso de medicamentos e de substâncias psicoativas.
Um protocolo de gerenciamento de risco é mandatório para avaliar e classificar o risco de suicídio, histórico de autoagressão e heteroagressividade, definindo condutas de contingência em casos de alto risco.
A matriz de formulação integrada consolida as hipóteses diagnósticas com códigos do DSM-5-TR/CID-11, define metas terapêuticas de curto e longo prazo e estabelece o plano de trabalho clínico, incluindo periodicidade e modalidade das sessões.
A seção final de autenticação formaliza o documento com um termo de confidencialidade e responsabilidade técnica, em adequação à LGPD e à Resolução CFP no 01/2024, incluindo local, data, assinatura e CRP do profissional.

name: Criminal Investigation Interviews
author: Velum
description: Convert raw interview notes into structured reports featuring skill analysis, metrics, and advice.
body:
The document outlines a structured script for conducting candidate interviews at Lotus HR for a specific job title at an organization.
The introduction section requires capturing interviewer details, candidate role, date, duration, and the context of the interview.
The full Q&A section involves recording each question asked and the candidate's complete answer, including direct quotes, figures, and timestamps.
The work experience and career section necessitates detailing the scope, reporting lines, team size, products/markets, stakeholders, projects with metrics, reasons for leaving, and tools/languages for each role.
The skills and potential section requires listing hard skills, soft skills, commercial/leadership style, and learnability.
The motivation and value proposition section involves identifying drivers, motivations, desired context, and the problems the candidate solves.
The personality and professional style section requires describing the candidate's behavior, maturity, collaboration style, feedback approach, and integrity.
The expectations and conditions section covers compensation (current and expected), benefits, contract type, availability, mobility, and remote/hybrid work preferences.
The risks and open points section involves identifying CV gaps, sector-switch risks, and any necessary follow-up questions.
The advice for next steps section includes an objective evaluation against the job title and organization, listing strengths, concerns, and focus areas for a second interview, along with scored ratings for role fit, culture fit, impact, leadership, and commercial drive, each with brief explanations.
The appendices section is for core KPIs, mentioned references, and a glossary of technical terms.
The STARR signals note requires capturing concrete examples of situation, task, approach, result, and reflection without including the labels in the final report.
The closing section for the Lotus HR screening report should consist of six continuous paragraphs covering the introduction, relevant experience and expertise, style within sales and personal characteristics, potential value, compensation and availability, and a conclusion with a recommendation.

name: Velum Analysis Script — "Exploratory Interview (RPS – Gollac Model)"
author: Velum
description: Organizes intake details into basic information, life history, risks, etc. It helps to understand the user's situation from multiple perspectives and assists in providing support.
body:
Basic information includes date of birth, age, gender, address, phone number, disability support classification, presence of a disability certificate, recipient certificate number, desired monitoring frequency, and the responsible municipality.
Employment history includes past career, current situation, reasons for leaving jobs, and information related to tax returns.
Developmental history includes information about place of birth and residence, the process leading up to the discovery of the medical condition, and the circumstances that led to the need for consultation support.
Family structure includes information about parents, children, marital status, etc.
Social relationships include hospitals being visited, attending physicians, names of welfare services being received, and support status (disability welfare, long-term care insurance, others).
The person's main complaints include the life they wish for in the future, their envisioned future, major goals or things they want to try, and the intentions of their family.
Daily life routines include wake-up time, meal times, bedtime, how they spend their day, activities and medical visits by day of the week.
Regarding the use of welfare services, this includes the content and provider information of currently used services, and whether there are other services they wish to use.
Risks include disappearance, criminal acts, gambling, alcohol, money (payment arrears), and debt.
Triggers include depression, the process of obtaining a disability certificate or rehabilitation certificate (why, when, where, what symptoms), symptoms at the time of acquisition, symptoms up to the present, symptoms and countermeasures during good and bad times, and changes in mood or behavior (noise, money, sudden anxiety, etc.).

name: People to People [Company and Job Seeker Interview]
author: Velum
description: Summarizes experience, motivation, and evaluation by category. Organizes the key points of the interview to facilitate a smooth decision for the next selection stage.
body:
This template aims to structurally organize the content of interviews between companies and job seekers, and to automatically summarize important information from audio recorded with Velum.
Record basic interview information such as interview date, format, company and interviewer names, job seeker's name, and applied position.
Summarize the job seeker's self-introduction, including an overview of their career, current job title and responsibilities, strong skills and experiences, and self-PR points.
Organize the job seeker's motivations, such as the reason for applying to this company, why they are considering a job change now, reasons for leaving their current job, and what they wish to achieve after joining.
Through questions from the company, confirm the job seeker's past achievements, scope of work they can handle, strengths and weaknesses, and management or team experience.
Clarify desired working conditions and work style, such as desired annual salary, work location, working hours, holidays, and possible start date.
Summarize information explained by the company, including business content, role of the position, desired candidate profile, working conditions, and career path.
Record mutual questions and answers, including questions from the job seeker to the company, the company's answers, and reverse questions from the company with the job seeker's answers.
From the company's perspective, evaluate the job seeker's good points, concerns, personality, skill compatibility, and fit with company culture obtained through the interview, and summarize them as a hiring decision memo.
Describe specific post-interview procedures and action plans, such as the presence of a next interview and candidate dates, documents to submit, company's planned contact, and job seeker's confirmation of intent and response deadline.

name: 1on1【KPT】
author: Velum
description: Organize achievements and challenges from transcripts to clarify next actions. Provides dialogue evaluation and improvement methods.
body:
Extract and organize the content of 1on1 using the KPT framework.
In the Keep section, extract achieved goals, effective approaches, and demonstrated strengths.
In the Problem section, extract issues requiring immediate action, fundamental problems, and resource shortages.
In the Try section, extract responsible persons, specific tasks, deadlines, improvement measures, and necessary support.
For follow-up items, extract items to be checked next time and important deadlines or indicators to watch.
For casual conversation notes, briefly record shared personal topics, ideas outside of work, common interests, and personal sharing.
In expert evaluation, rate the quality of the dialogue, specificity of problem-solving, effectiveness of growth support, trust-building, and clarity of actions on a 5-point scale, with concise reasons.
For improvement proposals, list three specific suggestions, describing the current situation, proposal details, and implementation methods together.
As extraction criteria, prioritize contextual understanding, keyword recognition, repeated mentions, emotional expressions, time references, responsibility, and personal information.
Exclude information such as meaningless strings, repetitions due to speech recognition errors, and details of discussions that did not reach a conclusion.
Keep the total length of KPT and important items within 300-400 characters, and casual conversation notes within 50-100 characters, summarizing each item concisely in 1-2 lines.
Emphasize urgent items or major achievements in bold, and if unclear, infer from context and indicate as '(assumed)'.
Clearly state dates for action items with deadlines, and always include information that significantly impacts the organization or project.
For casual conversation notes, briefly record topics that help build relationships or serve as conversation starters for next time, and handle sensitive personal information with care.
Due to the nature of transcription, eliminate duplicate content.

name: CZ Brainstorming — concise (quick bullet-point writing)
author: Velum
description: Collect history, symptoms, meds, risks, and supports. Outputs structured notes for assessment.
body:
The Terros full assessment is a comprehensive evaluation covering personal information, psychiatric history, medical history, and risk factors to establish a patient's baseline and treatment goals.
The initial section gathers personal information, including the reason for the visit, treatment goals, healthcare providers, mental health diagnosis, birthplace, developmental and family history, religious affiliation, education, housing, employment, support systems, marital status, and children.
History of Present Illness (HPI) focuses on the initial diagnosis date and the symptoms experienced, including their frequency and impact on daily functioning.
The Psychiatric Review of Systems (Psych ROS) assesses current mood, triggers, coping methods, and specific symptoms related to psychosis, mania, and depression using mnemonics like DIGFAST and SIGECAPS, along with a history of psychiatric hospitalizations.
The Medical Review of Systems (Medical ROS) screens for a wide range of medical conditions, including seizures, thyroid issues, HTN, DM, and head injuries, and requires updating the patient's allergy information.
A current medication review is conducted, which includes verifying the patient's pharmacy.
A behavior assessment evaluates suicidal ideation/attempts (SI/SA), self-harm, homicidal ideation/attempts (HI/HA), and access to weapons.
The psychosis section investigates the presence of hallucinations, delusions, paranoia, and whether these symptoms are drug-induced.
Incarceration history is documented, covering juvenile and adult time in jail or prison, parole/probation status, and types of crimes committed.
A history of abuse is collected, specifying the type (domestic violence, physical, emotional, verbal, sexual, trauma), the patient's age during the abuse, and whether they were a perpetrator.
Substance abuse and use history is detailed, including the age of first use for various substances, quantities, and experiences with withdrawal, detox, or treatment programs like MAT.
The assessment concludes by noting required actions such as ordering medications, making referrals, updating diagnoses, scheduling follow-ups, and ordering labs, EKG, or a PDMP review.

name: Anchoring Interview
author: Velum
description: Turn the transcript into a clear, structured narrative. Professional language, readable for the family, without additions.
body:
The main objective is to transform a transcription of a neuropsychological anamnesis interview into a professional, descriptive, clear account that is understandable for the family, without additions or unsupported interpretation.
The reason for consultation specifies the origin of the request, the reasons for the consultation, and the context in which it takes place.
The family situation presents the child’s birth order among siblings, brothers and sisters with first names and ages, sibling relationships, the marital/parental situation, custody arrangements in case of separation, the family atmosphere, parental occupations, and any family school-related or developmental particularities.
Schooling describes the current grade/class, the school, the chronological school history, strengths, difficulties, behaviors observed at school, educational adaptations, grade repetitions, RASED interventions, and any requests for an AESH.
The medical history brings together information on pregnancy, birth, initial health status, major medical history, ENT (ORL) and ophthalmologic check-ups, as well as the need to wear glasses and adherence.
Allied health/paramedical interventions list, in bullet points and if possible in chronological order, speech therapy, psychological follow-up, occupational therapy, psychomotor therapy, or other supports since early childhood.
Daily life details diet/feeding, sleep, behavior, emotional regulation, sensory particularities, autonomy, needs for parental guidance, any conflicts, and any specified educational responses.
Social relationships describe the child’s integration, any particularities with peers, relationships with adults, interactions outside the school setting, and ties within extracurricular activities.
Leisure and occupational activities mention current or past sports activities, whether they are experienced positively or problematically, at-home activities, autonomy in play, self-regulation, and screen exposure (duration, parental framework, devices used, and behavior when stopping).

name: HR Interviews
author: Velum
description: Generates summary, needs, risks, and checklist from client audio. Ideal for offices.
body:
The primary function of this agent is to analyze recordings of client conversations (briefings) and structure the information into a strategic document for architecture, interior, and custom furniture projects.
For the general service summary, it is necessary to identify the client, the type and phase of the project, the main objective, and relevant impressions such as profile, urgency, and expectations.
The analysis of the client's profile should focus on their level of demand, priorities (aesthetics, functionality, cost, deadline), decision-making style, and points of attention for the relationship.
Project needs should be listed objectively, including environments involved, desired functions, reported current problems, and explicit or implicit client desires, such as more storage or sophistication.
Project guidelines should compile the desired style, materials, colors, expected sensations, technical or physical restrictions, and budget information.
Identifying critical points and risks involves recording client doubts, misaligned expectations, budgetary limitations versus desires, and potential technical problems that could lead to rework or conflicts.
Office provisions list actions to be taken after the service, such as surveying, quotes with suppliers, layout/3D development, adjustments, and promised feedback to the client.
Client provisions should detail what they need to decide, send (measurements, references), or approve.
Deadlines and urgencies should record mentioned dates, the level of urgency, and important events that impact the project timeline.
An operational checklist should be created, transforming tasks into actionable items and separated by responsibility: internal team, client, and suppliers.
It is necessary to highlight important client phrases that reveal their emotional state or expectations, such as "I want something beautiful but not too expensive."
The insights and opportunities section should record strategic suggestions, upsell possibilities (additional sales), and ideas to differentiate the project based on the conversation.
Finally, a clear and ideal next step for the office should be defined, such as scheduling a measurement, presenting a layout, or sending a quote.

name: Questions and Answers
author: Velum
description: Help recruiters assess skills and culture fit to generate structured hiring recommendations.
body:
The template is designed for HR interaction evaluation during candidate interviews.
Candidate information to be recorded includes name, position applied for, and interview date.
Section 1 assesses the candidate's introduction and background, evaluating fit for company culture, communication skills, and confidence level.
Section 2 gauges motivation and role fit by assessing interest in the role, alignment with company values, and the depth of research into the company.
Section 3 focuses on self-awareness and reflection, evaluating the candidate's understanding of their strengths, acknowledgment of weaknesses, and approach to improvement.
Section 4 evaluates career progression and fit, assessing long-term career goals, compatibility with company goals, and the candidate's perceived fit for the role based on skills.
Section 5 examines problem-solving and adaptability by evaluating how the candidate handles challenging situations, their problem-solving skills, and resilience.
Section 6 explores work style and motivation, understanding what drives the candidate, their consistency in motivation, and their preference for team or independent work.
Section 7 assesses stress management and feedback reception, evaluating how the candidate handles pressure, their stress management skills, and their attitude towards receiving feedback.
Section 8 checks for cultural and role alignment by understanding the candidate's ideal work environment and the type of work culture they thrive in.
Section 9 evaluates communication and long-term collaboration skills by assessing how the candidate works with difficult colleagues and their potential for long-term collaboration.
Section 10 addresses salary expectations to ensure alignment with the company's budget.
Section 11 assesses learning and growth potential by evaluating the candidate's commitment to continuous learning and their proactive learning approach.
Section 12 provides an overall skill assessment across communication, problem-solving, teamwork, motivation, and cultural fit.
Section 13 includes a recommendation for the next round, along with reasons for the recommendation and areas for improvement or follow-up.

name: Strategic Dialogue Narrative Transformer, SNDT
author: Velum
description: Organize witness accounts and scene data. Create fire reports to assist professional record-keeping.
body:
The primary purpose is to generate detailed and legally defensible interview narratives for fire investigation units, adhering to professional standards and legal scrutiny.
Administrative details to be documented include incident address, fire incident number, case number, incident date and time, incident type, and whether there were previous incidents at the location.
All participating investigators and personnel, including their names, ID numbers, agencies, and roles, must be listed.
Scene observations should cover arrival conditions, environmental factors, structure/vehicle condition, fire pattern indicators, notable external indicators, safety concerns, and other agencies present.
Witness accounts require a structured format for each interviewee, including their identity details, relationship to the incident, time of interview, interview setting and conditions, behavioral observations, and any noted impairments or limitations.
Specific narrative accounts are required based on the interviewee's role: incident commanders, utility personnel, occupants/owners, and neighbors/bystanders, detailing their actions, observations, and relevant information.
Physical evidence mentioned by the witness and its last known location should be documented.
Follow-up actions, including clarifications obtained and agreement for future contact, need to be recorded.
A timeline of events, based on witness accounts and scene observations, should be created, noting any time discrepancies.
Key quotes and significant statements from the interviewee must be included verbatim, clearly noting the speaker.
Contradictory statements between witnesses should be documented without interpretation.
Summary and analysis guidance includes highlighting critical information for fire origin and cause determination, noting fire spread patterns, identifying potential ignition sources, documenting delays in discovery or notification, and verifying transcription accuracy.
Legal and professional considerations mandate adherence to NFPA 921 standards for fire investigation methodology and NFPA 1033 qualifications for professional fire investigators.

name: UU Shopper
author: Velum
description: Organize interview notes on skills, motivation, and personality to determine role suitability.
body:
The bootcamp candidate evaluation process aims to assess freshers through interviews, focusing on their background, company knowledge, career aspirations, technical skills, and personality fit.
Introduction & Background: Evaluates candidate's background, personality, and communication style through an open-ended question, assessing confidence, English proficiency, and clarity of expression.
Company Knowledge & Interest: Assesses the candidate's research depth regarding the company and their genuine interest in the specific role.
Goal Alignment & Career Vision: Explores the candidate's short-term career goals and long-term vision to determine alignment with the company's growth and their personal development plans.
Choice of Career & Motivation: Gauges the candidate's passion and reasoning for choosing the IT sector and their understanding of its landscape.
Stress Management & Self-Description: Evaluates the candidate's ability to manage pressure and their self-awareness and character through self-description.
Personality Insights: Assesses personality fit by understanding the candidate's hobbies, perceived strengths, and awareness of weaknesses with a focus on self-improvement.
Achievement & Problem-Solving: Identifies what the candidate values as success and evaluates their systematic approach to problem-solving and technical challenges.
Feedback Handling & Prioritization: Assesses the candidate's receptiveness to feedback and their time management and organizational skills in handling multiple tasks.
Commitment & Willingness to Learn: Determines the candidate's dedication to the role and their flexibility and willingness to go beyond standard requirements.
Technical Assessment: Evaluates the candidate's fundamental technical knowledge, problem-solving capabilities, and confidence in their technical responses.
Behavioral Assessment: Gauges cultural fit and interpersonal skills through behavioral questions tailored to the company's needs and work environment.
Overall Evaluation: Summarizes the candidate's suitability for the bootcamp based on a comprehensive assessment of their strengths, weaknesses, and overall potential.

name: Assessment and Monitoring Record by SSW
author: Velum
description: Ideal for practice owners looking to organize candidate data. It produces a structured one-page report with a professional profile, work experience, and salary range. It includes an advisory evaluation and automatic coding to support final staff selection.
body:
The main purpose is to create an automatically structured Candidate Report by Medi360, designed for sending to doctors/clinic owners, which has an executive and consultative style and does not exceed one page.
The report must adhere to strict visual specifications aligned with Medi360's branding, including a white background, headings and lines in the company's characteristic teal/petrol color, and a minimal aesthetic that evokes the medical and luxurious space.
The report's functionality includes automatic date insertion, automatic creation of a unique candidate ID (format: MED360-CAND-XXXX), and a consistent structure to maintain coherence and limit it to one page.
The report structure includes a Header with the Medi360 logo, the candidate's ID, the recipient, and the date, as well as a Footer that repeats the logo, the confidentiality indication, and the ID.
The main content of the report is organized into sections describing the candidate's profile, their key details (role, age, location, availability), a summary professional profile, their strengths, their work experience, potential points of attention, the salary range, and any limitations or terms.
The report concludes with the "Medi360 Assessment" section, which provides a consultative evaluation of the candidate and ends with a clear proposal for arranging a meeting.

name: KYC v2
author: Velum
description: Resume entrevistas en manuales de funciones. Define procesos y sugiere mejoras para digitalizar.
body:
The objective is to transform function manual interviews into a clear and functional structure for process digitalization, covering real and expected functions, associated processes, and suggestions for implementation in IT systems.
The expected output format includes position identification (name, area, interviewee, date, location), a general summary of the role, main functions identified with details such as name, description, frequency, expected result and interaction, associated processes for each function with their inputs, activities, outputs and documentation, suggestions for systematization and computerization in ERP, CRM or ClickUp, detected gaps and observations, and recommendations for functional and organizational improvement.
The main functions identified should be listed grouped into logical and operational categories, detailing for each one its name, a brief description, its frequency (daily, weekly, monthly, occasional), the expected result or associated indicator, and interaction with other positions or areas.
The processes associated with each function should detail the name of the process, required inputs, key activities, outputs or deliverables, involved documentation (formats, spreadsheets, checklists) and responsible parties.
Suggestions for systematization and computerization should indicate whether implementation should be carried out in the ERP, CRM or ClickUp, the type of recommended module or functionality, the information fields to be recorded, alerts, automations or recurring tasks to be created, and the link with other departments or processes in the system.
Detected gaps and observations should include tasks that are performed but should not be the responsibility of the position, activities carried out that are not registered in any current process, and improvement proposals or needs expressed by the interviewee.
Recommendations for functional and organizational improvement, generated from the interview content, should cover suggested changes in the function structure, ideas to improve efficiency, communication, control or traceability, and training needs or other supports.

name: Transcription 1013 Revised
author: Velum
description: Creates transcription and summary from mobile sales conversation recordings. Explicitly marks inaudible/unclear sections and does not supplement with assumptions.
body:
For undercover mobile sales survey recordings, output 1 transcription and 2 summary of conversations between surveyors and store staff in that order.
Do not generate statements, numbers, or plan names that do not exist in the recording, do not supplement with assumptions, mark inaudible sections as [Inaudible], mark uncertain sections as [Unclear: ○○?], always add [Unclear] if uncertain about amounts/months/dates/percentages, exclude ambient sounds and irrelevant voices and transcribe only the two-person conversation, distinguish multiple staff as Staff A/Staff B, and do not omit conversations outside the survey content such as reservations or wait times.
The survey background is for contextual understanding of the conversation and should not be used to infer conversation content in the transcription.
1 Transcription records the full amount in dialogue format without summarization, omission, or paraphrasing, preserving hesitations and acknowledgments to the extent they are meaningful, using the format "Surveyor: content" and "Staff: content" with half-width colons, and applying notation rules only when the original statement is certain.
Notation rules include replacements such as docomo→ドコモ, SoftBank→SB, Y!mobile→Y!, UQ mobile→UQ, half-width space before numbers like iPhone 17, monetary notation "2万"→"20,000円", Wi-Fi→インターネット (Internet), cashback→還元 (rebate), apply plan name standardization only when clearly referring to it and write as heard with (?) at the end if ambiguous, do not confuse SB's "PayToku 2" with "Teigaku Unlimited" or "PayToku 30/50", and do not standardize to glossary terms without certainty.
2 Summary is added at the end based only on the transcription, with each item including 1 who said it (surveyor's question or staff's explanation) and 2 brief quotation of supporting statement, noting "No relevant topic" if absent.
Summary target items include: type of final recommendation (iPhone 18 series / iPhone 17 / iPhone 17e / SIM-only switch / comparison only without clear recommendation), SIM-only switch rebate amount/method/timing/required plan/options (amounts conditional), rebate content for simultaneous electricity/Internet contracts and for later contracts, reasons why other carriers are better if docomo was mentioned, presence and content of explanations about the advantageousness of purchase support programs (Itsu demo Kaedoki Program / Shin Toku Suru Support / Sumaho Toku Suru Program), including how staff dispelled concerns about high program usage fees and how they explained actual prices (quote staff's words as close to original as possible), and list unclear numbers at the end as "Items requiring confirmation."
Glossary lists docomo, SoftBank, and au-related optical lines, electricity, cards, discounts, options, support, video/services, and various plan names (e.g., docomo Hikari, SoftBank Hikari, au Hikari, PayToku 30/50, Teigaku Unlimited, Toku Toku Plan 2, Komi Komi Plan Value, Sumaho Toku Suru Program, etc.) for use as reference terms for notation standardization and determination.

name: interlocucao
author: Velum
description: Paste a transcript or journal. Get key tensions, traits, and next steps for guided reflection.
body:
