An assessment of how others responded to Paul is conducted to determine if they were receptive or defensive, identifying who was most and least receptive and the possible reasons why.
The analysis of influence and persuasion identifies instances where Paul successfully changed minds, gained agreement, or managed conflict, detailing the situation, technique used, its effectiveness, and potential improvements.
Emotionally charged interactions are analysed to assess the appropriateness of emotional responses, the justification for frustration or anger, and whether a different approach could have yielded a better result.
A specific analysis based on the principles from "How to Win Friends & Influence People" scores Paul's performance on behaviours like showing genuine interest, listening, and avoiding criticism, identifying strengths and areas for improvement.
The audit identifies missed opportunities where Paul could have improved outcomes by thanking someone, showing empathy, or asking better questions, providing specific examples of what could have been said.
The process includes identifying the top 10 communication wins of the day, explaining what happened, why it worked, the benefits for all parties involved, and the specific skill demonstrated.
A coaching report projects the long-term career impact of the day's behaviours, identifying strengths that could accelerate success, weaknesses that could limit it, and three key habits to strengthen and three to eliminate.
A personal development action plan is created, focusing on specific replacement behaviours for the following day to substitute undesirable actions with more effective ones.
The final assessment provides a balanced, evidence-based summary of Paul's performance, identifying his best and worst moments, the behaviours that most enhanced or damaged his influence, and the most valuable lesson from the day's interactions.

name: EXECUTIVE ASSISTANT - MEETING SUMMARY
author: Velum
description: Ideal for consulting: centralize needs and data to create accurate industrial quotes.
body:
The purpose of this template is to capture key client meeting information in industrial consulting, specifically for the agri-food sector, to generate a client file, a targeted quote, and to document standards, constraints, and challenges.
The first section, "General Information," aims to record logistical details of the meeting, including date, time, location, as well as the identification of client and Ycarus participants.
The "Company Presentation & Industrial Context" section collects information on the sector, products, production sites, current process organization, and the client's motivations for the project.
The "Identified Problems / Pain Points" section is used to list in detail the technical, organizational, or regulatory irritants encountered by the client in areas such as process, hygiene (CIP/NEP), maintenance, safety, quality, ergonomics, 3D/CAD documentation, and control systems.
The "Client Objectives & Expectations" section aims to clearly define what the client wishes to obtain, detailing the main objective, secondary objectives, major constraints (budget, deadline), and expected deliverables.
The "Shared Technical Data" section is intended to note essential information for creating a quote or a study, such as production capacities, existing equipment, availability of diagrams (P&ID) or 3D scans, and specific regulatory requirements.
The "Identified Ycarus Service Opportunities" section structures the potential services Ycarus can offer into four categories: Process Consulting & Engineering, Project Management, 3D & CAD, and Special Machines design.
The "Additional Information" section allows for noting future client projects, operational constraints, identifying decision-makers, knowing the client's ideal timeline, and anticipating potential risks.
The "Actions to be Taken (Ycarus To-Do)" section contains a list of internal tasks to be performed and specifies important technical documents to request from the client, such as P&ID diagrams, 3D/2D plans, and incident history.
The "Assisted Summary & Analysis (Ycarus AI)" section is intended for an automatic summary generated by AI, identifying the major problem, relevant technical solutions, and a recommended prioritization of actions.
The final "Appendices" section is an optional space to attach visual aids or additional notes such as site photos, quick sketches, or diagrams.

name: Analytical Meeting Notes Template
author: Velum
description: Paste a transcript. Get structured notes of key points, decisions, risks, actions.
body:
Analytical meeting notes should present a concise, substantive synthesis that captures the discussion’s structure, significance, arguments, decisions, risks, opportunities, stakeholder considerations and follow-up actions rather than functioning as a transcript.
Structure should be adapted to the purpose, substance and dynamics of each meeting, with sections included only when supported by meaningful content and without forcing irrelevant headings or speculative material.
Executive Overview must always open the notes and explain the meeting’s purpose, context, most important issues, direction or outcome, and any significant strategic implication.
Thematic Analysis should use approximately 3–6 specific, substance-led sections where appropriate, consolidating related points, preserving nuance and disagreements, distinguishing facts from views or proposals, and retaining material examples, organisations, policies, countries, figures and comparisons.
Decisions & Emerging Consensus should appear only when confirmed decisions, agreed directions or meaningful consensus emerged, with clear separation between confirmed decisions, emerging consensus, preferred directions and proposals.
Action Items & Next Steps should appear only when follow-up actions were explicitly discussed or clearly assigned, capturing the action, owner, timing and dependencies where available, and avoiding invented ownership or deadlines.
Outstanding Questions / Open Issues should appear only for substantive unresolved matters, including strategic tensions, remaining decisions, evidence gaps, dependencies, alignment needs and uncertainties that could materially affect next steps.
Meeting Dynamics & Sentiment should appear only when tone, organisational dynamics or stakeholder sentiment materially explains the discussion, while avoiding over-interpretation and separating participant sentiment from external stakeholder or public sentiment.
Analytical approach should prioritise strategic significance, synthesis, specificity, nuance, decisions, implications, actions and genuine differences in viewpoint over chronology, generic commentary or artificial consensus.
Attribution should be selective and used when views are distinctive, disagreement exists, responsibility matters, proposals come from specific people or the identity of the speaker is strategically relevant.
Accuracy rules require avoiding invented facts, decisions, motivations, consensus, actions or speaker positions; preserving uncertainty, contradictions, key distinctions, names, organisations, countries, policies, dates, figures and technical terms; and excluding minor conversational detail unless relevant.
Style should use British English, polished analytical language, clear headings and concise bullets, producing professional notes that explain why the meeting took place, what mattered, what participants thought, where the discussion landed, what remains unresolved and what happens next.

name: Needs Analysis for Automation and AI Research
author: Velum
description: Analyzes interviews and maps processes. Proposes specific AI solutions and evaluates their benefits and risks.
body:
The goal is to create an interview analysis template that serves to identify and evaluate opportunities for the deployment of automation and artificial intelligence within the client's work processes.
The template defines the analyst's role as a "Product Discovery Analyst" and "AI Opportunity Mapper," whose task is to recognize workflows, processes, tools, repetitive steps, and pain points, and based on this, propose AI solutions.
The first step of the analysis is to create a brief summary that includes the user's role, main interview topics, their key problems, and identified opportunities.
For a detailed understanding, a workflow mapping is required, which involves specifying the user's role, the tools and systems used, and a detailed breakdown of work activities into a structure including steps, inputs, outputs, tools, dependencies, manual parts, risks, frequency, and duration.
The analysis focuses on identifying problems, both explicitly mentioned by the user and implicit ones derived from the context, as well as risk areas in the workflow, such as manual data transcription or switching between systems.
For each identified AI opportunity, an "Opportunity Card" is created, which details the situation, problem, ideal state, proposed AI category, justification for its use, benefits, risks, and a proposal for further verification.
Each opportunity (use-case) is then scored on a scale of 1–5 according to criteria such as impact, frequency, time consumption, suitability for AI, adoption risk, data availability, and business value, from which the resulting priority is calculated.
The template also includes a section for recording concerns and barriers to AI adoption, both directly expressed and derived, such as distrust in technology accuracy or fear of loss of control.
To ensure completeness of information, recommended supplementary questions for further interviews, questions specific to particular roles or departments, and questions for the analyst to find information off-record are defined.
The final analysis output is to be delivered in two formats: as a structured text document containing all analytical sections and as a clear table summarizing key information about individual opportunities (use-cases).

name: Individual Consultation
author: Velum
description: Processes recordings of 1:1 consultations for leaders. Records tasks and goals for team member development.
body:
The main purpose is to create a structured and clear summary from the recording of an individual 1:1 consultation between a manager and a financial team member, recording only the information actually stated.
The introduction should identify the participants (manager and team member), the context of the meeting, and the main goal of the consultation, such as performance evaluation, development, or problem-solving.
It is necessary to record the advisor's current status, including their business results, activities (meetings, calls), motivation, successes, failures, and any significant changes in personal life.
All discussed topics, such as performance, discipline, time management, working with clients, pipeline, technical aspects, mindset, problems, and opportunities, should be summarized in bullet points.
Specific problems and obstacles, their causes, impacts, who is addressing them, proposed solutions, and any concerns of the advisor need to be specified.
Only the advisor's strengths that were mentioned or are clearly evident from their expression, such as discipline, communication, results, or proactivity, are recorded.
Only mentioned weaknesses or risks, such as lack of activity, poor planning, low consistency, or fear of rejection, are recorded.
All manager's recommendations need to be recorded, including recommended procedures, changes in strategy, workflow, and references to educational materials.
Specific tasks and commitments of the advisor are recorded in the format "Task: [description] | Deadline: [if mentioned]", including measurable indicators and tasks related to personal development.
Manager's commitments, such as promised support, provision of materials, individual guidance, results control, or arranging the next meeting, are summarized.
All important insights for further collaboration with the advisor are recorded, including key insights, risk signals, and areas requiring increased support.
The agreed next steps are precisely recorded, including the date of the next consultation, topics for review, and goals for the next meeting.
Only information not mentioned during the consultation is listed, in the format "– Not found: X", considering areas such as performance, activity, motivation, goals, and others.

name: Chen Yu-Chieh Orthopedics Consultation Coach
author: Velum
description: Suitable for clinic consultants, analyzing recordings to optimize communication and diagnose deal-closing keys. Automatically generates patient characteristic tags and follow-up memos to improve management efficiency.
body:
The main purpose of this document is to define the role of a "Chen Yu-Chieh Orthopedics Consultation Coach and Deal Analyst", aimed at analyzing consultation recordings between consultants and patients to improve the conversion rate of self-paid treatments and optimize patient services.
The primary task is to diagnose key deal factors, including determining the consultation outcome, listing the best performing scoring points, and identifying losing points that cause patient hesitation.
The core part involves refining communication scripts, requiring the identification of three conversation segments needing improvement, analyzing problems with the original statements, and finally providing a "Suggested Golden Phrase" that aligns with the clinic's image and can be directly used by consultants.
It is necessary to analyze the patient's main concerns, evaluate the consultant's responses to objections, and propose better response strategies to handle patient resistance.
The content requires extracting marketing and health education materials from the conversation, including the patient's original words describing pain and their top three most concerned questions (FAQ).
Suggestions for optimizing service processes need to be proposed, checking the execution of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and providing insights for management regarding process bottlenecks or information discrepancies during physician-to-consultant handovers.
Finally, a patient tracking memo needs to be generated for consultants, including patient profile tags, pain point expectations, personality style, emotional memory points, and next specific follow-up actions, for quick archiving in the CRM system.

name: Veterinary Behavioral Assessment Report Generator
author: Velum
description: Summarize key points from photography client calls. Input call information and requirements, then outline scope, deliverables, shoot details, timeline, and budget terms. Facilitates expectation alignment and follow-up on action items.
body:
This template outlines the key points to capture during a photography client call, covering everything from project scope to final deliverables and payment terms.
The "Meeting Overview" section is for recording basic details such as client name, date, participants, and project name.
"Project Scope & Vision" focuses on defining the desired photography style, key subjects, intended image use, and any brand guidelines.
"Deliverables" details the specifics of the final output, including the number of edited images, required formats, inclusion of raw files, and the delivery timeline.
"Shoot Details" covers logistical aspects like the number of shoot days, proposed dates, daily hours, locations, and any access restrictions.
"Production Requirements" lists all necessary elements for the shoot, including styling, lighting, models, special equipment, and post-production needs.
The "Team & Logistics" section addresses the composition of the photography and client teams, as well as needs for equipment rentals, permits, or insurance.
The "Timeline" segment establishes key dates for project kickoff, pre-production, the shoot itself, and the delivery of proofs and final images, including revision rounds.
"Budget & Commercial Terms" outlines the fee structure, usage rights, additional costs, payment schedule, and cancellation policies.
"Next Steps & Action Items" assigns responsibilities, sets deadlines, and schedules future check-ins to ensure project momentum.
The "Questions or Concerns Raised" section serves to document any unresolved issues, client hesitations, or items that need further research.

name: MFOME
author: Velum
description: Summarize meeting recordings. Extract transcripts, action items, and strategic insights.
body:
This document outlines a comprehensive, 12-part structure for analyzing and summarizing client meeting recordings, focusing on transcript creation, extracting key information, and generating actionable insights.
The initial step requires creating a complete, verbatim transcript of the meeting, including speaker identification, timestamps, and an English translation if the original language is different.
Key meeting highlights are to be extracted, focusing on important decisions, critical information, breakthroughs, agreements, and identified risks or concerns.
All action items must be clearly listed, specifying the responsible person (Who), the specific task (What), the deadline (When), and the reason for the action (Context).
A separate, prioritized to-do list should be created for follow-up tasks, information gathering, contact points, document preparation, and necessary research.
A detailed meeting summary of 300-500 words is required, covering the meeting's purpose, chronological discussion points, decisions made with rationale, challenges, and next steps.
All quantitative data and metrics mentioned, such as financial figures, timelines, percentages, and performance indicators, must be extracted and organized, preferably in a table.
A client needs analysis must be performed to categorize both explicitly stated and implicitly inferred needs, ranking them by priority (High/Medium/Low).
The analysis should include insights into each participant's personality and communication style, covering their decision-making approach, engagement level, key traits, and professional priorities.
A mood and sentiment analysis for each participant is required, assessing their overall tone, emotional indicators, satisfaction level, and specific topics they liked or disliked.
Any unique information and special insights shared during the meeting, such as personal details, company-specific context, or hidden opportunities, should be captured.
A relationship management guide needs to be created with key facts to remember about the client, best practices for communication (Do's), and approaches to avoid (Don'ts), along with considerations for future conversations.
Finally, a list of 8-12 strategic questions for the next meeting should be generated, including follow-up, deepening, forward-looking, and proactive questions.

name: Consulting 3.0 [EN]
author: Velum
description: For managers and consultants. Analyzes meeting transcripts to find waste and critical issues.
body:
The goal is to generate a detailed and useful summary of business meeting transcripts to understand the functioning of a third-party cosmetics company, aimed at a structured report and proposals for operational and organizational improvement.
The context is a company with a complex structure and cross-functional departments, where critical issues related to vertical dynamics, complex flows, and cross-functional communication may arise.
The guidelines for the summary include completeness of information, thematic reorganization, attribution of statements to those who expressed them, a double level of analysis (technical/operational and relational/organizational), critical interpretation to deduce inefficiencies and opportunities, highlighting roles and decision-making levels, detecting declared or implicit objectives, mapping dependencies and blocks between departments, identifying cause-effect relationships, and linking content to business objectives.
The structure of the summary must be organized by functional areas such as planning, production, purchasing, quality, sales, human resources, information systems, communication, decisions, timing, and procedures, detailing for each area who spoke, what was said, problems, practices, opportunities, objectives, and interdependencies.
The Lean perspective involves analyzing wastes (muda) such as waiting, overproduction, unnecessary movements, inventory, defects, rework, transport, and wasted talent, evaluating the presence or absence of standards, continuous flow, Kaizen, visual management and problem solving, and identifying cultural obstacles such as resistance, habits, and lack of vision.
The analysis of KPIs and performance requires reporting any reference to data or indicators, verifying the presence or absence of KPIs, the use of data, the sharing of KPIs, and evaluating whether the measures are based on concrete data or on perceptions, reporting numbers if available and assessing maturity in KPI management and data orientation.
The purpose of the summary is to understand the current functioning, highlight inefficiencies and risks, detect operational, managerial, and cultural opportunities, and build a roadmap for Lean transformation, continuous improvement, measurement culture, and organizational evolution.

name: Updated ISP - Discovery Session
author: Velum
description: For reviewing a discovery recording. Outputs responses, evidence, priority and summary.
body:
This document outlines a structured process for a consultant to analyse a discovery session with an Australian business, assessing its capabilities across seven key areas: Business Overview, Financial Management, Commercial Management, Strategy, Quality Management, Environmental Management, and Safety Management.
The process requires the consultant to analyse a recording and, for each predefined question, provide a factual response, assess the evidence type and confidence level, write consultant notes on maturity and gaps, and assign a priority level, all adhering to specific Australian standards and legislation.
The consultant must follow a strict output format for each question, including fields for the question, sub-section, response, evidence type, assessment notes, status, and priority, with clear definitions provided for confidence ratings and priority levels.
The assessment covers a Business Overview section to understand the company's history, services, structure, roles, and workforce capabilities.
A Financial Management section is included to evaluate how the business tracks performance, manages cash flow, handles budgeting, estimates costs, and utilises accounting systems.
The Commercial Management section assesses how the business secures work, manages contracts and tenders, tracks project commercial performance, and maintains client relationships.
The Strategy section aims to understand the business's long-term goals, planning, market position, and approach to growth and capability development.
A Quality Management section, aligned with ISO 9001:2015, evaluates the documentation and application of work processes, quality assurance, continuous improvement, and system certification.
The Environmental Management assessment, aligned with ISO 14001:2015 and Australian law, focuses on environmental awareness, risk management, incident and waste handling, and system documentation.
A Safety Management section, aligned with the WHS Act 2011 and ISO 45001:2018, examines safety leadership, risk management processes, worker training, incident reporting, and formal safety systems.
The final step requires the consultant to produce an overall session summary, including a confidence rating, the top five strengths and gaps, and a list of recommended priority actions for the next 30 days.

name: Present State and Planning Capture
author: Velum
description: Organize client needs, stakeholder views, and project goals from discovery session notes.
body:
The primary purpose is to create a comprehensive note-taking template for consultant-client discovery meetings to capture explicit discussion points and underlying dynamics for operational performance transformation work.
Meeting Context: Record date, time, location, attendees with their roles, and meeting objectives.
Company Landscape (Current State): Map the operational structure, identify pain points as "pressure points," tag tools, processes, and workflows as "existing infrastructure," and capture metrics, KPIs, and performance indicators as "current vital signs."
Problem Space (Undesirable Aspects): Tag problems with symptoms and root causes, associate problems with speakers, note emotional intensity in problem descriptions, and identify contradictions in problem characterizations.
Vision Landscape (Desired Future State): Capture explicit goals as "destination markers," note desired capabilities as "future state functions," highlight success metrics as "target vital signs," and track differences in future state descriptions among speakers.
Prioritization Signals: Note repeated issues, capture explicit priority statements, tag topics with high discussion/energy, and identify subjects leaders return to after tangents.
Constraints Radar: Identify limitations related to resources (budget, personnel, expertise), timelines and deadlines, technical aspects, organizational factors (policy, culture, structure), and external influences (market, regulatory, competitive).
Stakeholder Dynamics: Create profiles for each speaker, noting their priorities, concerns, enthusiasm versus resistance, alliances or tensions, and decision-making authority signals.
Engagement Planning: Outline potential work phases, mentioned action items, areas of responsibility, and decision points/approval processes.
Thematic Undercurrents: Identify recurring themes, note emotional tone shifts, capture unresolved tensions or questions, and flag potential stakeholder misalignments.
Output formatting should include a timestamped and speaker-attributed transcript, a visual "heat map" of topics, an executive summary by category, recommended focus areas, and potential roadblocks.
Each section should include both direct quotes and analytical insights, clearly distinguishing between stated and implied information.

name: Consulting - meeting session
author: Velum
description: Overview of topics, tasks and decisions. It captures team motivation and missing points for financial assistants.
body:
The goal is to provide an assistant to the Czech financial team with a complete template for automated and structured processing of team meeting minutes.
The introductory part of the minutes should contain basic information such as the date, type, and purpose of the meeting, along with a list of participants.
For the main topics discussed, it is necessary to briefly and in bullet points record what was discussed, in what context, who opened the topic, and what were the key arguments.
Decisions made should be recorded in a separate section, stating who proposed them, who approved them, and from when they are valid, in the format: – Decision: [text] (responsible: name).
Specific tasks and responsibilities need to be recorded with a description of the task, the responsible person, and the deadline in the format: – Task: [description] | Responsible: [name] | Deadline: [date/description].
Important information and announcements for the team, such as news, changes, training dates, results, or risks, should be summarized.
The minutes should include a section for problems and proposed solutions, specifying the problem, who is solving it, proposed solutions, impact, and next steps.
Positive impulses, such as new business opportunities, ideas for improvement, and other suggestions from team members, should also be recorded.
The minutes should also reflect motivation and team dynamics, including mood, members' approach, how the manager communicates important points, and any praise or criticism.
Unresolved or postponed points should be recorded with information on who should open them next time and when the team will return to them.
At the end of the meeting, a brief summary of the main results, most important tasks, and next steps should be created, within 4–6 sentences.
The minutes must also include a section with missing information that was not mentioned at the meeting, such as deadlines, responsibilities, or specific goals, in the format: – Not mentioned: X.
The overall style of the minutes should be concise, clear, comprehensible, in bullet points, written in standard Czech, and strictly adhere to the information actually mentioned at the meeting.

name: Performance Mental Coaching
author: Velum
description: Analysis of the conversation and specific techniques for managing pressure and focus.
body:
This document defines a prompt for creating a comprehensive mental coaching template for athletes, which generates a structured report with analysis, interventions, and plans based on a conversation transcript.
The role of the mental coach is defined as an elite expert who draws inspiration from top world experts and combines principles from elite sports, psychology, neuroscience, mindfulness, and cognitive-behavioral approaches to create practical and immediately usable outputs.
The primary task is to create a report based on the athlete's conversation transcript, which first summarizes their mental, emotional, and performance state, context, and goals.
The report must identify warning signs such as loss of self-confidence, fear, fatigue, or frustration, and quote specific statements from the athlete.
It is necessary to explain the hidden mental mechanism and translate it into practical aspects of performance, such as attention focus, self-talk, emotions, physical manifestations, and trust.
For immediate use during a match, intervention protocols are suggested for various time segments: micro-moments (Power Pose, 4-2-6 breath), short breaks (Neutral Thinking, PETTLEP visualization), and longer breaks (CBT reframing, WOOP).
The short-term plan for 1–2 weeks includes daily micro-rituals, creating a self-talk library, visualizations, and preparing if-then plans for specific triggers.
The medium-term plan for 3–6 weeks focuses on psychological flexibility training (ACT), pressure simulation in training, and stabilizing pre-performance routines.
The template includes a description of practical exercises such as Power Pose, breathing techniques, touch anchors, eye-lock drill, and PETTLEP mini-visualization.
To support the athlete, a selection of 3–5 self-reflection questions focused on control, triggers, and objectively influenceable factors is provided.
The report concludes with a concise summary (Executive Summary) that includes the main cause of decline, immediate intervention, key mindset, direction for the next phase, and the athlete's personal mantra.
The output's stylistics must be concise, actionable, and in the coach's language, with specific recommendations and a safety protocol for detecting serious psychological problems, in which case clinical care must be recommended.

name: ISMP Stakeholder Interview
author: Velum
description: Analyzes the current status and issues from the transcripts. Completes professional meeting minutes structured into four areas.
body:
This guide presents a method to produce professional meeting minutes by analyzing ISMP stakeholder interview transcripts to derive current status, issues, and improvement requirements, distinguishing between 'Inquiry' and 'Issue Sharing', and systematizing them into the four domains of 'Process', 'System', 'Operations/Collaboration', and 'Policy/Regulation'.
The goal of the minutes is to understand the current state through transcript analysis, identify key issues, and create a structured deliverable that includes specific improvement requirements.
The first step in writing the minutes is to set basic information such as interview name, date/time, location, and participants, and place an Executive Summary at the beginning summarizing the core content of the interview.
Detailed interview content is structured by agenda and clearly recorded as two types: 'Inquiry', a consultant-led information-gathering process, and 'Issue Sharing', where the interviewee voluntarily raises issues.
'Inquiry' agendas include question background, key questions, and answer summary, while 'Issue Sharing' agendas include problem situations, actual cases, and improvement ideas; consultant opinions are recorded only in a limited way when the interviewee clearly agrees.
Every agenda must be classified into at least one of 'Process' (work procedure issues), 'System' (IT tool issues), 'Operations/Collaboration' (organizational and communication issues), and 'Policy/Regulation' (rules and authority issues).
Compile all derived content by the four domains and summarize current state, key issues, improvement requirements, and priority in tables, and also summarize statistics by agenda type.
Specify follow-up actions and additional checks, and adhere to writing principles such as objectivity, specificity, structure, and practicality, recording with an interviewee-centered approach.
Give special consideration to differences in stakeholder perspectives, conflict points, separation of quantitative/qualitative data, and the balance between inquiry and issue sharing to deepen the analysis.

name: Systemic Counseling
author: Velum
description: Assist healers in transforming case records into structured content. Extract summaries and golden quotes, generate social media and program materials, and turn deep experiences into high-quality records.
body:
Serving as a senior program production consultant with over 20 years of experience, specializing in assisting spiritual workers to transform deep soul experiences into structured content products such as podcasts, IG posts, and publications.
Receiving verbatim transcripts from soul exploration guides, including guiding words, soul world scenes, two-way dialogues, soul messages, and client feedback.
Output formats include "Soul Journey" experience records, condensed content summaries, highlight quotes, segmented records of the soul journey, and extended application suggestions.
The condensed content summary should outline the theme of the soul journey, core messages, scene highlights, touching moments or special symbols, and be presented in a narrative language.
Highlight quotes should collect 3-5 important messages delivered by the soul, presented in the tone of "Soul Quotes", suitable for IG posts or Reels subtitles.
The segmented record of the soul journey should include pre-guidance and preparation process, soul channel and scene description, soul appearance and message delivery, dialogue segment narration, and journey summary with transformation tips.
Dialogue segment narration should clearly indicate roles and can use dialogue format.
The extended application suggestion section can include mid-podcast guiding words, Reels editing segments, and directions for designing interactive questions for "Ask the Soul".
The ultimate goal is to help quickly transform transcripts into high-quality content modules including podcast copy, graphic scripts, soul quotes, and social interaction materials, while retaining the tone and rhythm of healing power, confidentiality, and artistry.

name: Employee consultation with HR
author: Velum
description: Convert HR talks into neutral notes: facts, concerns, decisions, actions. Flags review needs.
body:
The primary goal is to create structured, neutral, and factual meeting notes for employee-HR consultations, ensuring clarity and proper documentation for follow-up.
The process requires separating facts, observations, concerns, decisions, and actions, while avoiding speculation, judgment, or diagnosing conduct without explicit evidence or a prior HR determination.
A confidential HR consultation summary should be structured into specific sections: intake overview, employee-reported facts, requested support, HR assessment needs, information provided by HR, next steps, confidentiality/retaliation reminders, and a determination on the need for review or escalation.
The intake overview section must capture the date, employee details, reason for contact, and the type of issue presented.
The employee-reported facts section details what the employee stated, including timelines, individuals involved, any referenced evidence, and whether the issue was previously raised with management.
The summary must document the employee's desired outcome, such as advice, a specific resolution, or immediate protections.
The HR assessment section identifies missing facts and categorizes the issue (e.g., conflict, policy question, safety concern) to determine if escalation is required.
It is necessary to record the information HR provided, including explanations of processes, reporting options, requested documentation, and any interim support offered.
The next steps section clearly outlines commitments made by both the employee and HR, including timelines and any other parties to be involved.
A dedicated section confirms that confidentiality limitations and anti-retaliation policies were communicated to the employee.
A "Review / escalation needed" section must state "Yes" or "No" with a brief justification, especially for issues involving potential harassment, discrimination, safety, or serious misconduct.
The note-taking style must be neutral and respectful, distinguishing between employee statements and HR guidance while minimizing sensitive personal details.
Essential metadata to be captured includes meeting date, participants, scenario type, confidentiality level, related case files, follow-up deadlines, and escalation status.

name: Client Consultation
author: Velum
description: Analyzes processes, tools, and digital culture in SMEs based on interviews.
body:
The objective of this interview template is to answer a questionnaire to implement AI improvements in SMEs, based on the transcription of interviews.
If the source information is insufficient to answer a question, it will be indicated as "It is not possible to determine the answer based on the source information".

Block 1: Current Processes

A description of the main processes in charge is requested, detailing the most important process step by step, its inputs, results, responsible parties, key decisions, interactions with other areas, pain points, improvement opportunities, existing documentation and its updating, evaluation and monitoring methods, indispensable tools, frequent risks and their management, standardization, dependence on tacit knowledge, and frequency of redoing tasks or correcting errors.

Block 2: Digital Tools

Inquires about the tools or software used in the area, the level of adoption of these tools, their integration with each other or the need for manual information transfer, and the existence of missing digital tools or limitations in the current ones.

Block 3: Automation and Efficiency

Asks about manual and automated processes or tasks, identification of repetitive or time-consuming manual tasks, automation attempts and their results, and processes with clear opportunities for future automation.

Block 4: Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

Seeks to describe the level of knowledge about AI technologies applicable to the work, current use of AI tools or solutions and for which tasks, and processes or tasks where AI could be applied in the future.

Block 5: Digital Culture and Change Management

Requests to define digital transformation in the work context, assess the willingness to adopt new digital approaches, describe the team's attitude towards technological changes, and observe obstacles or barriers that hinder the adoption of new technologies.

Block 6: Sentiment towards AI

Inquires about perceived opportunities or benefits in adopting AI solutions, risks or concerns generated by incorporating AI into processes, and comfort in using an AI-generated recommendation to make a decision.

Interview Closure

Asks for a quick win that could be implemented immediately and if there is any other relevant topic that has not been addressed and that should be mentioned.

name: MIS Board
author: Velum
description: Critiques the MIS issue. Provides a decision and index table.
body:
This document defines a Management Information System (MIS) Advisory Board for a spinning factory to transform the MIS unit from a report producer into a credible data reference and decision-making supporter within the organization.
The Management Information System (MIS) Advisory Board is tasked with acting as an expert body in the fields of reporting, dashboards, business intelligence (BI), metric design, and data quality. Its audience consists of the MIS supervisor and specialists at a spinning factory with approximately 600 personnel.
The advisory board members include specialists in data architecture and BI, data quality and governance, statistical thinking, performance management, data visualization, and critique of measurement-fixation, representing viewpoints from various schools of thought such as Inmon, Kimball, Redman, Deming, Kaplan, and Tufte.
Key disagreements the board must address include data centralization in MIS versus departmental data ownership, correction of data at the point of entry versus cleaning at the reporting layer, acting on deviations from target versus distinguishing normal variation, and the imperative of numerical targets versus the risk of dysfunctional behavior caused by them.
The board's working method involves selecting 4 to 7 relevant members for each analysis, with the mandatory presence of at least one dissenting member against the prevailing view for comprehensive issue examination.
The output structure of the board's analysis must include 16 specific sections, including an executive summary, decision and data chain, data quality, report architecture, metric analysis, visual design, member analysis, judgment on disagreements, risk analysis, post-mortem, The Tenth Man concept, MIS monitoring metrics, action plan, required information, and three most impactful actions.
The board's judgment principles emphasize that decision must precede report, metrics must have precise operational definitions, data correction should occur at the point of entry, there should be one source for one number, direct data from ERP is preferred, signal must be distinguished from normal variation, and the behavioral impact of metrics should be reviewed.
The writing style of the report should be professional and frank, use common English technical terms as they are, and each report should conclude by presenting three key actions with the greatest impact.

name: Follow-up HZT
author: Velum
description: For consultants. Transforms transcripts into process diagnostics and automation suggestions.
body:
The main objective is to analyze technical assessment meeting transcripts to identify pains, challenges, and opportunities in companies, proposing innovative technological solutions aligned with best market practices, as well as suggesting process improvements.
The experienced business consultant specializes in process optimization, digital transformation, artificial intelligence, and organizational strategy, with deep knowledge of the technological ecosystem and experience in industrial and backoffice processes.
The experience covers various ERPs, applications, portals, sector modules, complementary solutions, partner tools, and technological integrations, with a practical, clear, concise, and provocative approach.
The consultant's behavior and style include being analytical, solution-focused, strategic, practical, innovative, and commercially consultative, seeking patterns, proposing concrete improvements, relating challenges to business vision, considering real limitations, and turning pains into sales opportunities.
The steps to be performed upon receiving the transcript include initial contextualization (identifying topic, areas, participants, and objective), in-depth diagnosis (categorizing problems, describing impact, finding root causes), mapping opportunities (process optimization, automation and AI, suggesting solutions and integrations), and generating commercial insights (turning problems into sales and highlighting differentiation with ERP).
The preferred output format for analyses includes a refined diagnosis with identified challenge, business impact, probable root cause, and additional perception; action paths with process optimization, automation and AI, practical examples, and action proposals with expected benefits; a table of consultative opportunities detailing area/responsible, challenge, root cause, partner, and expected benefit; and a meeting summary with main points and identified opportunities.
The final message should invite prioritization and definition of an implementation roadmap and commercial opportunities, aiming to act as an intelligent co-pilot for the ERP specialist team, turning conversations into commercial opportunities and real improvements for the client.

name: Family Assistance
author: Velum
description: From raw text: 10-point check with questions, measures, and legal references. For SME leadership.
body:
Professional occupational safety and compliance output format to transform raw texts (e.g., consulting report, audit interview, meeting transcript, inventory) into an action-oriented “10-Point Quick Check” or a “Compass Checklist” in the style of a compliance checklist.
Focus on extracting typical error patterns and risk areas in occupational safety, including examples such as missing/outdated risk assessments, unclear role allocation, inadequate documentation of inspections/training, escape and rescue routes, first aid organization, and fire protection.
For each focus area, provide a precise self-check question with the answer options “Yes / No / Unsure.”
For each focus area, provide concrete, actionable recommendations under the formula “How to avoid the error,” with a direct focus on measures.
For each focus area, assign legal references or normative orientation based on the specified regulations such as ArbSchG, DGUV Regulation 1, BetrSichV, GefStoffV, ASR A2.2, ASR A2.3, and ASiG.
Structural specification for the header with a main title (e.g., “[ORGANIZATION NAME] BG-Ready in 30 Minutes” or “[ORGANIZATION NAME] BG-Ready Compass”), a subtitle/purpose line with error and time reference, and the instruction line “Please mark Yes, No, or Unsure.”
Structural specification for the main section as consecutively numbered items (e.g., 1 to 10) with a fixed block format consisting of a headline (error description/core problem), check question, checkbox line, and the sections “How to avoid the error” and “Orientation” with paragraphs/regulations.
Optional alternative as a tabular checklist by topic areas (e.g., occupational safety, occupational medicine, equipment & plant safety, fire protection) with numbered checklist rows and checkboxes.
Structural specification for the footer as a call-to-action with the heading “Found gaps? Let’s talk.” and complete contact details (contact person, role, address, phone number, email, web URL).
Tone and style guidelines with professional, factual, instructive, legally robust, and action-oriented wording, direct active language for executives and managers in SMEs, and a conciseness goal of a maximum of 2–4 sentences per solution section.

name: executive level chapter summary
author: Velum
description: For therapists. Summarizes sessions and maps defenses. Organizes themes and paths to support the clinic.
body:
The main objective is to generate an in-depth psychoanalytic clinical summary from a session transcript, acting as a clinical psychoanalyst who follows classical and contemporary principles.
The thematic summary of the session should identify the main manifest themes, changes in mood, silences, and avoided or superficially addressed contents.
Technical observations should focus on the predominance of primary or secondary process, observable defense mechanisms, resistances, and the dynamics of transference and countertransference.
The floating diagnosis consists of formulating provisional hypotheses about traits of neuroses, indications of trauma, repetitions, narcissism, and instinctual fixations, without establishing conclusions.
Important trackings seek to identify symbolic repetitions, contradictions in discourse, absent affects, movements of displacement or condensation, and present psychic investments.
The section on possible intervention paths suggests future avenues of work, such as constructions, interpretations, the use of silence, and transference, without rushing interpretations.
Observed changes record progress, regressions, and notes on the evolution of the transference bond throughout the therapeutic process.
The analysis of the transferential field focuses on the predominant configuration (maternal, paternal, etc.) and the projective or introjective identifications manifested in the session.
It is necessary to list potentially sensitive contents, such as suicide or violence, explaining the clinical context in which they emerged to alert about possible triggering of safety policies.
The priority points of the session should be highlighted in bullet points to focus on the most relevant elements.
The template generates a continuity prompt for ChatGPT, which integrates the current session's summary with previous ones for a longitudinal analysis, focusing on repetitions, the evolution of defense mechanisms, and themes for the next session.
General instructions reinforce the need to maintain neutrality, technical rigor, avoid direct advice or closed diagnoses, and focus on psychic hypotheses with clear and objective writing.

name: Workshop Process Analysis Table
author: Velum
description: Extracts current status, issues, and reactions from sales meeting audio and organizes contract feasibility judgments and next actions based on facts.
body:
The purpose of this prompt is to define a template for generating operational logs from consulting interview audio that can be used for contract decisions and next actions.
As basic case information, it records items such as hospital name, corporate name, location, interview type, interview date, interview location, and result.
For the hospital's current status, only objective facts are stated, such as years in operation, number of chairs, number of doctors, number of dental hygienists, outpatient situation, status of home dental care implementation, and main numerical information.
For the director's/corporation's intent/background, it organizes reasons for considering home dental care, mid- to long-term goals, and past external support experience.
For issue organization, issues identifiable from the audio content are analyzed from the perspectives of organization/personnel, medical administration/billing, operations, announcement/patient acquisition, and dependency on individuals/systematization.
For proposal content, the proposed service, the reason for the proposal, and the reasons for not adopting other options are clearly stated.
For the counterparty's reaction/enthusiasm, the counterparty's level of understanding of the proposal, main questions and concerns, and remarks that influenced the decision are recorded, including subjective evaluations.
For result and reason for decision, the final result of the interview and the decisive factors for contract or non-contract are analyzed.
For next actions/remarks, concrete next steps are described, such as the next interview schedule, homework, internal response matters, and notes on contracts and billing.
The output rules stipulate that bullet points should be primarily used, vague expressions should be avoided, speculation of information not included in the audio is prohibited, and expressions understandable to a third party as a business document should be used.

name: POP
author: Velum
description: Send audio or text of the case. Receive analysis, strategy, documents, drafts, and tasks for the process.
body:
The objective is to transform immigration case descriptions in Portugal, received by audio or text, into a complete system that covers legal production, procedural management, and strategy for the law firm.
PHASE 1 — CASE ANALYSIS consists of identifying the client's profile, migratory situation, objective, urgency, and risk, followed by creating an executive summary, a chronological timeline, and identifying legally relevant facts.
PHASE 2 — LEGAL DIAGNOSIS involves framing the case based on relevant Portuguese legislation, such as the Foreigners Law and the Nationality Law, and assessing the legal basis, strengths, weaknesses, risks, and probability of success.
In PHASE 3 — PROCEDURAL STRATEGY, the most appropriate legal path is recommended, such as a residence permit application or an administrative action, justifying the choice and presenting alternative strategies if the first option is not viable.
PHASE 4 — AUTOMATIC LEGAL PRODUCTION focuses on generating a complete checklist of necessary documents, drafting the main legal document, and suggesting the structure of other petitions that may be needed in the future.
PHASE 5 — PROCESS MANAGEMENT aims to create an internal report for filing and establish procedural control with tasks, pending documents, probable deadlines, and upcoming procedural acts.
PHASE 6 — CLIENT RELATIONSHIP establishes communication through drafting an email with the initial analysis and next steps, and creating a fee proposal template detailing services, stages, and values.
PHASE 7 — RISK MANAGEMENT includes identifying possible legal or administrative obstacles and suggesting strategies to mitigate or reduce these risks.
PHASE 8 — OFFICE STRATEGIC INTELLIGENCE focuses on providing practical observations based on experience, suggesting ideas for social media content from the case, and identifying possible additional legal services to be offered to the client.
The required writing style should be legal, clear, and rigorous, with logical reasoning, accessible explanations of complex concepts, and empathy, while the response format should be organized into numbered sections with clear subtitles.

name: Career Development & Coaching Plan
author: Velum
description: It extracts conclusions, figures, and technical decisions from meeting recordings. It provides a clear record in Czech.
body:
The main goal is to create a structured record of the future energy concept for the energy integrator AGROWOOD support s.r.o. (AGWS) based on a meeting recording, focusing on technical decisions and conclusions.
The required structure of the record includes a header with meeting details, the material's objective, an analysis of the initial state including consumption, existing infrastructure, and financial data, with an emphasis on highlighting any data inconsistencies.
The document should define short-term, medium-term, and long-term strategic goals, such as optimization, preparation for regulatory changes, and achieving self-sufficiency, and identify key conditions for project success.
It is necessary to describe in detail the discussed technological pillars, such as cogeneration (CHP), photovoltaics (PV), battery energy storage systems (BESS), and heat accumulation, including their technical parameters, benefits, and interdependencies.
The presentation and comparison of solution variants in a table format are required, including the technology mix, capital and operational expenditures (CAPEX/OPEX), payback period, degree of self-sufficiency, suitability (star rating), with a clear recommendation for the most suitable variant.
The economic section must detail CAPEX by item, annual OPEX, overall payback, and annual savings compared to the current state.
The concept includes an analysis of regulatory conditions (Energy Regulatory Office, Electricity Market Operator), distributor requirements, license thresholds, safety standards, and relevant subsidy programs.
It is necessary to identify critical project risks, such as fuel price or heat utilization, and create a list of open points and tasks with assigned responsible persons and deadlines for further action.
The conclusion should confirm AGWS's readiness to assume the role of technological integrator and guarantor for the coordination of the entire project from concept to operation, with the document's style being factual, professional, and emphasizing the interconnectedness of the overall solution.

name: Interview Questionnaire for Organizational Diagnosis and Digital Maturity in SMEs
author: Velum
description: Form for site info, style, and budget. Helps consultants organize landscape design next steps.
body:
This document is a structured form for an initial client consultation for a landscape design/build project, designed to capture all necessary information from property details to project scope and next steps.
The first section gathers fundamental client and property information, including contact details, lot size, specific areas for design, and any existing hardscape elements to be retained.
Project goals are quantified by having the client rate the importance of aspects like curb appeal, privacy, entertaining space, shade, and creating a poolside oasis on a scale of one to five.
Client style and plant preferences are detailed by selecting from predefined styles (e.g., Tropical, Modern, Mediterranean), and specifying plants, colors, or animals they particularly love or dislike.
Site conditions are assessed by documenting sun exposure, the current irrigation system status, and the levels of salt and wind exposure on the property.
The client's lifestyle is evaluated by asking about entertaining frequency, parking needs, expected duration of residence, and the presence of pets, children, or specific allergies.
Maintenance preferences are determined by establishing the client's comfort level with upkeep (low, moderate, high) and their preference for standard or organic fertilizer.
Potential extras and add-ons are identified, including options for accent lighting, water features, and artificial turf, along with any other specific requests.
The project budget is defined by capturing an approximate investment range, a wishful budget tier, and notes on spending priorities.
An open-ended section is included to record any additional information the client wishes to share that was not covered in previous sections.
A dedicated section for the consultant's internal notes captures the top three client outcomes, key constraints, observed opportunities, and potential risks.
The process concludes by outlining next steps and action items, such as scheduling site measurements, requesting materials from the client, defining internal tasks, and setting a follow-up date.
A final section is reserved for noting any missing answers or information that requires a follow-up with the client.

name: ABA ABCs
author: Velum
description: Record shop floor observations to identify waste, safety risks, and quality issues for improvement.
body:
This document outlines the structure and fields for a Gemba Walk analysis, designed to capture observations and drive continuous improvement by identifying and addressing waste, safety, and quality issues.
General instructions for data entry require filling in information if available from the audio source, leaving fields blank otherwise, and repeating general Gemba details like date and observer across all relevant rows.
The "GEMBA SECTION" captures global information for the walk, including date, time, observed area, observer, and high-level summaries of the process, identified wastes (Muda), and any safety or quality observations.
The "PROBLEM SECTION" details each identified issue in a separate row, including the machine or process involved, a concise problem description, and its classification within Lean frameworks.
Problems are classified using the TIMWOODS framework to specify the type of waste (e.g., Transportation, Inventory, Motion) and the 3M framework to categorize it as Muda (waste), Mura (variation), or Muri (overload), with explanations for each.
A root cause analysis is conducted using a "2–4 why?" chain (RCA_Elite), and the problem is formally defined for DMAIC, specifying what, where, when, and its impact.
For each problem, a concrete corrective action is proposed, categorized by initiative type (e.g., Kaizen, DMAIC), and prioritized based on impact level and urgency, also noting if it's a quick win.
Responsibility for analysis and execution is assigned to primary and supporting roles or areas, with space for notes and pending activities to ensure clear ownership.
A "Gemba Summary" section, repeated for all rows, consolidates the key findings and initial recommendations from the entire Gemba walk, and records the source of the information.
The document provides clear, short definitions for the eight wastes of TIMWOODS: Transportation, Inventory, Motion, Waiting, Overproduction, Overprocessing, Defects, and underutilized Skills.
It also defines the 3M concepts: Muda (non-value-adding waste), Mura (inconsistency/variation), and Muri (overburden on people or machines), including ultra-short versions for quick reference.

name: master template Esd
author: Velum
description: For ESD and cleanroom conversations. Generates agreements, risks, and emails from your notes.
body:
This document is a universal conversation template for a technical-commercial conversation assistant from Eurostat Group, specializing in ESD protection, which automatically generates relevant sections based on the conversation content.
Section A is a mandatory section that includes the customer profile, key decisions, and a draft for the follow-up email. Customer data, conversation details, and a summary of customer needs are recorded, along with a numbered list of concrete agreements and a complete, ready-to-send email on behalf of the Director Benelux & UK.
Section B is used in discussions about audits or standards such as IEC/ANSI and structures the analysis of EPA compliance in seven steps: detection of the standard system (IEC/ANSI), status of the ESD program, a version check of standards with warnings for outdated versions, cross-references between IEC and ANSI equivalents, an overview of limit values, a list of discussed standards, and a checklist of relevant services.
Section C covers technical product specifications when resistance, material, or tests are discussed, recording the type, application, resistance values, and standards per product, including specific technical warnings and a list of open technical points.
Section D is applied when discussing workbenches and workplace equipment and specifies the frame type, worktop, grounding solution, accessories, and the required quantities and sizes, with a specific warning about the lack of grounding for an ESD worktop.
Section E describes the specifications for clothing, shoes, and chairs, including type, version, size, and quantity, with automatic recommendations for specific situations such as ATEX or cleanrooms and warnings for incorrect use or maintenance that affects ESD properties.
Section F records commercial and planning details, such as project scope, volumes, delivery dates, budget, payment terms, and the decision-making process, if a quote or price is discussed.
Section G is a mandatory concluding section that provides a prioritized risk summary of all identified issues, a list of open items that still require confirmation, and a concrete description of the next logical action from Eurostat.

name: Mission to Market- Staging Walkthrough
author: Velum
description: Input a staging walkthrough recording. Get room-by-room actions and next steps, with review notes.
body:
Mission to Market report converts a staging walkthrough recording into a warm, professional, client-facing home preparation and staging recommendation document for Mission Design Co.
Report must address the homeowner directly, organize recommendations by room, keep actions specific and easy to follow, and rely only on the recording and supplied notes.
Content must preserve stated identifying details only, avoid invented recommendations or commitments, distinguish agreed decisions from suggestions and unresolved questions, and place unclear details in Amanda Review Notes.
Required report opening includes “Mission to Market,” “Home Preparation & Staging Recommendations,” property address, client name, walkthrough date, and “Prepared by: Mission Design Co.”
Your Home’s Presentation Plan briefly states the overall direction discussed and the buyer impression or features intended to be noticed.
Top Priorities Before Listing lists the most important discussed actions with essential preparation first, using “essential” only when supported by the discussion.
Room-by-Room Recommendations include only discussed rooms and exterior areas, with room or area name, goal, recommended actions, keep or highlight items, explicit responsibility and timing, and a photo placeholder.
Room recommendations use concise bullets and preserve actionable details involving removal, relocation, cleaning, repair, painting, purchasing, or styling.
Staging Plan summarizes discussed furniture, accessories, layout changes, and services while separating Mission Design Co. supplied items from client tasks or purchases.
Before-Staging Checklist consolidates explicitly discussed preparation tasks without unnecessary repetition.
Confirmed Next Steps list agreed actions, responsible parties, and dates when stated.
Amanda Review Notes must remain included, capture unclear details, conflicts, missing information, decisions needing confirmation, and internal operational comments, or state “None identified.”
Final report must omit empty sections except Amanda Review Notes and exclude transcript timestamps, speaker labels, filler conversation, and unrelated personal discussion.

name: Problem Solving PDCA
author: Velum
description: Process Steps Extraction & Assessment from Meeting
body:
The primary role is to act as a professional summarizer specializing in the Insurance Business, covering Motor, Property, Carriers, Engineering, Asset, Accident, and Health sectors.
The core directive is to create a detailed account of provided text with absolute completeness and fidelity to the original content, rephrasing for clarity without summarizing or condensing information.
Every piece of information must be included unless explicitly marked as 'chit-chat', with a focus on capturing all nuances and details of each distinct topic discussed.
Information should be presented comprehensively, using paragraphs and sub-points as needed, and grouping related information logically within each topic.
Substantive information must not be omitted, condensed, or summarized, with the sole exception being casual chit-chat, filler words, or irrelevant conversational tangents.
The goal is to rephrase text into simple, clear, and concise language, ensuring all details are fully present and easy to understand.
The context involves transforming transcriptions of meetings, training, or procedures into professional Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for teams and stakeholders.
The objective is to convert transcriptions into comprehensive SOPs, extracting the AS-IS (current) process with absolute fidelity to all details, including task performers.
The objective also includes proposing a TO-BE (improved) process or filling gaps using best practices and Insurance Business Transformation expertise, clearly defining responsible parties for each proposed step.
Processes, steps, resources, responsible parties, warnings, and notes are to be organized into a clear, actionable guide.
The required style is professional technical documentation, similar to corporate training or employee handbooks, using clear, direct language, numbered steps, bullet points, structured sections, and consistent terminology/formatting.
Process Handling Guidelines require extracting all process steps, decision points, roles, and details exactly as described, explicitly identifying the responsible individual/role for each step/task without inferring or adding unmentioned AS-IS steps.
Gaps and ambiguities in the AS-IS process, including unclear task ownership, must be noted.
Every action, instruction, or piece of information in the transcription's process flow, along with its performer, must be captured as a detailed step/sub-step, breaking down complex actions into granular components.
The response format is a complete SOP document, structured into two main sections: AS-IS and TO-BE processes.
The AS-IS section includes: Process Name, Objective and Scope, Procedure Overview (numbered main sections), Definitions and Acronyms, Detailed Step-by-Step Instructions (elaborating on 'how' and including responsible parties), Decision Points and Flowcharts (described in text), Roles and Responsibilities (explicitly listing involved parties and their core responsibilities), Quality Checks/Verification Steps, and Related Documents/Reference.
The TO-BE section includes: Process Name, Recommended Process Overview, Detailed Recommended Steps (same format as AS-IS, elaborating on 'how' and including responsible parties, with specific suggestions for improvements/additions and rationale/benefits), Recommended Roles and Responsibilities, and Expected Benefits (e.g., cost reduction, efficiency, improved data insights, enhanced collaboration).
An "Action Point" section is required, structured with columns for Sequence, Topic, Action Details, Impact, Responsible Person, and Due Date, with additional rows as needed for all identified action points.
An "Initiative / Improvement Idea / Quick-Win Solution" section is required, structured with columns for View, Type, Project Name, Description, Benefits, Risks, and Related Parties, capturing opportunities for cost reduction, innovation, simplification, competitive advantage, and other improvements from various strategic perspectives.
A "Related Documents" section is required, presented in a table format with columns for Document Name and Purpose.

name: Legal Master - Dr. Fabrício
author: Velum
description: Transforms transcripts into structured reports with market analysis and risk management.
body:
The goal is to generate a structured and informative summary from transcribed text, following specific style, content, and formatting guidelines.
The summary should extract and organize information about the overall market context, recent events, geopolitical/macroeconomic impacts, technical analysis, trading strategies and risk management, institutional flows, altcoin analysis, liquidity and volatility strategies, long-term outlook, investor mindset, and trading opportunities.
The summary should begin with the institution's logo/name and the report date, followed by a relevant link if available.
Content should be structured into sections with bold titles, such as "Market Correction Context," "Geopolitical Impact on the Market," "Bitcoin Technical Analysis," "Trading and Risk Management," "Institutional Flow and ETFs," "Altcoin Analysis: Ethereum and Others," "Managing Volatility in Altcoins," "Liquidity Chart and Trading Strategies," "Long-Term Outlook and Accumulation," "Importance of Mindset and Discipline," "Opportunities to Trade Calmly and Elegantly," "Strategies for Investors and Traders," and "Final Considerations."
Bullet lists (•) should be used for hypotheses, strategies, or key points within each section.
Paragraphs should be short, direct, and objective, averaging 2 to 4 lines.
Each section should be separated by highlighted titles and spacing, with bold for section titles and technical terms, assets, important values, dates, or key concepts.
Price zones, percentages, dates, and asset names should be highlighted whenever possible.
Numbering should be avoided, preferring bullets and titles for organization.
A "Final Considerations" section should synthesize the scenario and present recommendations or warnings.
The tone should be formal, objective, informative, and professional, using accessible technical language and avoiding personal opinions.
The summary should be detailed, covering all relevant topics without excessive length, with 1 to 3 short paragraphs per section and lists when necessary.
The final result should faithfully mimic the style, structure, organization, and visual emphasis of an analyzed example, conveying clarity and professionalism.

name: Detection of instincts in the Enneagram
author: Velum
description: Summarize and organize problem awareness and decision-making dilemmas based solely on statements from audio, memos, etc. Also present points for the next hearing.
body:
The purpose is to create a document for consultants that clarifies management's awareness of issues, progression of thought, and hesitation in judgment, by organizing the contents of executive interviews using only statements from audio data, input memos, and attached images.
This document is positioned not as a meeting record but as an organizational document to accurately understand management's thinking. It must not include external knowledge, speculation, or evaluations, and if there are no statements, it should be noted as such.
The output will be structured into five components: "Overall picture of the interview," "Organization of management's awareness of issues," "Organization of thoughts by topic," "Points where decisions have progressed and reasons for stalled decisions," and "Topics for the next interview."
In "Organization of thoughts by topic," the background, summary of main statements and flow of discussion, and insights/values discernible from statements will be summarized for each major theme, with keywords related to judgment enclosed in quotation marks.
In "Points where decisions have progressed and reasons for stalled decisions," content where a direction has been shared and reasons for stalled decisions (e.g., insufficient conditions, conflicting criteria) will be organized as a set.
As for expression rules, abstract statements will include supplementary explanations, preconditions and stances influencing judgment will be bolded, and colloquialisms will be adjusted to standard language without changing meaning. Verbatim transcription and presentation of conclusions are prohibited.
The final document aims to enable consultants to comprehensively understand management's thought progression and stagnation points, making it clear which issues to address in the next interview.

name: OT Consulting
author: Velum
description: Summarizes mining meetings into risk tables, tasks, and indicators for operational management.
body:
The primary role is to process transcripts of Operational Technologies (OT) meetings in mining to generate a structured professional summary, compatible with the Velum.ia platform templates, aimed at areas such as Operations, Maintenance, and OT Cybersecurity.
The objective is to produce outputs that clearly differentiate notes, decisions, next steps, tasks, risks, and impact, in addition to a complete record of Questions and Answers (Q&A) with their reference in the transcript, without inventing data.
Key meeting metadata must be detected and extracted, such as title, date, duration, location, meeting type, moderator, and a detailed list of attendees with their role, company, and attendance status.
Discussion topics should be classified according to specific OT domains if they appear, such as Production/KPIs, Maintenance, Automation, Industrial networks, ICS Cybersecurity, among others.
The generation of 15 specific deliverables is required using Velum.ia templates, including an executive summary, metadata and attendee tables, and a breakdown of the discussion by OT topic (facts, analysis, agreements).
Decisions, risks, and tasks must be documented in structured tables with defined fields such as ID, owner, reason, criticality, owner, priority, and commitment dates.
It is mandatory to record all explicit questions and their answers in a Q&A table, specifying who asks, who answers, the time reference in the transcript, and the status (e.g., "Pending" if there is no answer).
Other deliverables include operational impact on KPIs, relevant technical details (systems, versions, networks), a timeline of next steps, a list of open questions, a conclusion for management, a team sentiment assessment, and a glossary of terms.
The output style should be concise, using bullets and tables, maintain standard units and dates, distinguish between proposals and decisions, unify person aliases, and highlight critical alerts for HSE or OT Cybersecurity.
Additionally, a JSON output must be generated that contains structured information on metadata, attendees, topics, decisions, risks, and KPIs to facilitate integrations with other systems.

name: Leadership Challenge
author: Velum
description: Transcript in, chaptered summary out; keeps tone, quotes, names, numbers. Flags dropped topics.
body:
The primary purpose is to generate a high-fidelity summary of a lecture, keynote, or working conversation that accurately reflects the speaker's tone, concepts, and reasoning.
The summary is structured into a few substantial chapters that follow the chronological flow of the conversation, with each chapter representing a distinct phase or territory explored by the speaker.
Chapter boundaries are placed only where the conversation genuinely shifts to new territory; ideas that develop or illustrate the current topic remain within the same chapter as elements.
A chapter must not be a single idea but a substantial segment of the conversation; it must account for every move the speaker makes within its span, with each move becoming a distinct element.
The summary opens with a "spine" of no more than five lines: title, speaker, setting, a single sentence stating the talk's core argument, and a numbered index of chapters.
Each chapter begins with a "Core Idea" sentence stating the speaker's main assertion for that section, followed by named elements derived from the speaker's actual actions, such as "Methodology," "Framework," or "Key Analogy."
Specific details like numbers, names, and timeframes must be preserved exactly as stated, and any conflicting mentions of the same figure should be noted.
The speaker's original language, including analogies, metaphors, coined phrases, and tone, must be mirrored throughout the summary to retain its authenticity.
The summary should not contain action points, owners, or deadlines, but may include an element outlining an unstated consequence of the speaker's point if it is clearly supported by the material.
A final "Raised and dropped" section captures topics, questions, or names that were mentioned once and not revisited, and an optional "What you missed if you weren't there" block can list up to five key moments of presence or audience reaction.
Before finalizing, a thorough check against the transcript is required to ensure complete coverage, accuracy of all details, and proper structure, with the summary written in the dominant language of the source transcript.

name: GPT PA
author: Velum
description: Turn interview transcripts into structured reports. Identify blockers and clear process improvements.
body:
The primary purpose is to define a structured template for a solution architect to analyze workflow discovery interview transcripts, transforming them into actionable documentation that identifies optimization and automation opportunities.
The analysis begins by capturing administrative details like the meeting date and a list of attendees' first names.
An executive summary must be created, stating the core focus of the meeting, the top opportunity, the primary blocker, and the recommended first action with an assigned owner.
