The "CURRENT STATE WORKFLOW (AS-IS)" section requires extracting all mentioned workflows, mapping their steps sequentially, and providing context on stakeholders, timing, and constraints.
Pain points and friction are to be categorized by severity (Critical, Moderate, Minor) and detailed with a description, a verbatim quote, affected stakeholders, and any current workarounds.
The "DESIRED STATE & OPPORTUNITIES" section summarizes requested improvements, ideal outcomes, success metrics, and efficiency goals in bullet points.
Strategic alignment between teams or projects should be identified, noting shared goals and opportunities for collaboration to accelerate progress.
The "INTEGRATION LANDSCAPE" section lists all tools and platforms, maps data flows, and outlines potential for automation and any security or compliance considerations.
Potential solutions are categorized by implementation complexity (Quick Wins, Medium Lift, Strategic), detailing the related pain point, solution type, and a brief description.
A section for "KEY QUOTES" requires capturing 3-5 impactful direct quotes with speaker attribution and context.
"FOLLOW-UP ITEMS" are documented to list unanswered questions, additional stakeholders to interview, documents to request, and areas needing deeper exploration.
A list of 3-5 prioritized "RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS" must be created, each with a title, owner, timeframe, and any dependencies.
The "OUTSIDE THE BOX" section challenges an assumption from the interview by offering a fresh perspective and a first step to test its feasibility.

name: 🚌 - POP VIA BRASIL MOBILITY | Standard Operating Procedure for B2G Urban Mobility
author: Velum
description: For Via Brasil teams. Send the transcription and receive a step-by-step SOP for compliance.
body:
The main objective is to convert a verbal explanation into a structured Standard Operating Procedure (POP) for Via Brasil Mobility, an urban mobility company focused on the public sector (B2G).
The operational context of Via Brasil Mobility involves over 26 years in the market for mobility solutions for the public sector through tenders, managing complex fleets that include school, health, adapted, and security transport, with predominantly B2G contracts requiring compliance and accountability.
The POP must be written in formal and instructive Portuguese, with numbered steps using infinitive verbs, and must be specific about systems and governmental portals, considering compliance clauses, deadlines, and audits of B2G contracts.
The procedure must identify handoff points between areas, such as operations and administrative/financial, and include alerts about risks of contractual non-compliance, such as penalties and fines.
The mandatory structure for the POP document includes sections such as Header, Objective, Scope, Materials, Step-by-Step Instructions, Precautions, Frequency, Performance Indicators, Records, Specific Attention Points, and References.
The step-by-step instructions should detail each action, indicate the system to be used, the estimated time, mark handoffs to other areas, and signal linkage to contractual clauses or legal requirements.
Precautions regarding compliance, common errors to avoid, best practices, special conditions (such as adapted vehicles), risks of non-compliance (penalties, rescission), and operational safety, especially in passenger transport, must be listed.
The document must specify the frequency and trigger for task execution, as well as Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to measure the procedure's effectiveness, and where and how execution records should be maintained for traceability and audit purposes.
Specific attention points for Via Brasil's B2G operation include the need for auditable records for accountability, vehicle compliance for adapted vehicles, management of drivers with specific qualifications, and strict adherence to contractual deadlines.

name: 컨설턴트 전용 회의록_고객인터뷰
author: Velum
description: Organize decisions and assignments from transcripts. Separate "our company" and "other party" as spoken, clearly state if unmentioned. Output organized by agenda.
body:
This document defines comprehensive rules and formats for creating structured meeting minutes from recorded meeting content, titled "Ultimate Meeting Minutes".
The output must be based solely on facts actually spoken in the recording, with amounts and proper nouns transcribed as is, and unclear parts marked as [???], requiring objective description.
Required sections include "Basic Information", "Today's Conclusion", "Content by Agenda Item", "Hearing Check", "Concerns/Negative Statements", "Homework/Deliverables", "Action Items", "Next Schedule", and "Unconfirmed Matters", which must always be output.
Optional sections include "Current Business Flow and Challenges", "Requests/Desired Outcomes", "Data, Forms, Existing Systems", "Usage Scale/Environment", "Cost, Estimate, Contract Terms", and "Q&A", which are output only if relevant statements are found in the recording.
Basic information includes date, location, attendees, purpose, and an overall summary of up to 5 lines.
The conclusion section clearly separates decided matters from undecided matters, with undecided matters supplemented by points of contention and missing information.
Content by agenda item organizes topics in the order discussed, summarizing key remarks from both parties, decisions, and pending matters in bullet points.
Business flow describes the sequence of operations with numbered points, and challenges are listed with their scope of impact.
Requests are categorized by priority as "mandatory" or "desirable", and data-related information records form names, quantities, etc.
Statements regarding usage scale and environment, costs and contract terms, and Q&A are also output in the specified format if applicable.
The hearing check covers 8 items: current challenges, budget sense, decision-maker/process, desired implementation/delivery date, existing tools, competitor consideration, number of users, and internal promotion lead, stating either the mentioned content or "not mentioned".
Negative statements that could hinder order reception or promotion are listed with direct quotes.
Homework and deliverables specify what, by when, and by whom they are to be prepared, and action items are summarized in a table.
The next schedule includes date, time, location, and agenda, indicating if it's confirmed or tentative, and unconfirmed matters list points to be verified next.

name: Dental Consult
author: Velum
description: Collect dental history in chat. Returns labeled transcript and structured history summary.
body:
Category is Consulting; content type is Tutorial/Knowledge focused on conducting an initial dental consultation, dialogue-based data collection, and structured reporting.
Primary purpose is to guide a dental therapist through staged patient interviewing to obtain a complete medical history and produce a transcript plus a structured summary report without speculation.
Stage 1 defines contact and basic data collection: warm greeting, purpose explanation, patient provides full name, age, and main reason, leading to identification of the primary problem.
Stage 2 clarifies complaint details: localization, sensation type, onset, dynamics, aggravating/alleviating factors, night pain/swelling, inclusion of patient fears; address aesthetics/function/pain/mucosa/TMJ as relevant.
Stage 3 reconstructs disease progression: initial notice timing, symptom changes, periods of relief, self-treatment attempts, patient tells a concrete chronological story.
Stage 4 gathers dental history: recent visits, treated teeth and timing, complications, extractions, crowns/bridges/implants; patient mentions at least one concerning incident.
Stage 5 records medical history and safety: chronic diseases, allergies to anesthetics/antibiotics, current medications, pregnancy/lactation, recent surgeries, previous/concomitant diseases, with at least one significant response.
Stage 6 assesses habits and everyday factors: hygiene practices, use of floss/irrigator, diet specifics, harmful habits (smoking, bruxism, hard foods), patient shares at least one honest detail.
Stage 7 elicits psychological comfort and expectations: concerns about dental visits, important pre-exam notes, desired outcomes; result identifies expectations, concerns, feelings; doctor summarizes complaints, priorities, significant history, and next step.
Output format requires a labeled dialogue transcript ([DOCTOR]/[PATIENT]) followed by [HISTORY: STRUCTURED DATA] covering basic data, main complaint, complaint details, disease development, dental history, medical safety, habits, patient priority, expected outcome/deadlines, preferences/limitations, and next stage.

name: Meeting to CRM-ready Notes
author: Velum
description: Extracts problems from transcripts. It identifies frustrations and maps how issues are linked.
body:
The primary objective is to identify all explicit and implicit Undesirable Effects (UDEs) from interview transcripts following the UDE identification script.
The core interview script context involves understanding a person's title, what it entails, what they actually do, the problems they face, and the consequences of those problems, iterating to reach root UDEs.
Explicit UDEs are identified through direct complaints, stated problems, obvious frustrations, and clear cause-and-effect chains described by the interviewee.
Implicit UDEs are detected by analyzing emotional undertones, time contradictions, defensive language, casual asides, hypothetical statements, frequent qualifiers, and energy shifts.
Conversational archaeology involves examining tangential stories, throwaway comments, what is not said, contradictions, and repeated phrases or themes to uncover systemic issues.
For each identified UDE, the output format requires a concise statement of the UDE, its type (Explicit/Implicit), supporting evidence, resulting manifestations, potential interconnections with other UDEs, and a confidence level.
Analysis guidelines emphasize trusting instincts about emotional subtext, looking for patterns, paying attention to energy shifts, considering what is missing, connecting unrelated comments, and noting defensive language.
Analysis should avoid assuming causation without evidence, over-interpreting single comments, confusing symptoms with root causes, missing the broader context, or ignoring obvious problems.
Special attention points include the role-reality gap, workaround culture, communication breakdowns, resource constraints, decision-making delays, quality vs. speed tensions, tribal knowledge, and measurement misalignment.
The example analysis structure demonstrates how to present identified UDEs with their type, evidence, manifestations, interconnections, and confidence level.
The final reminder emphasizes uncovering systemic issues that perpetuate problems, with each UDE needing to pass the test of whether its elimination would significantly improve multiple other problems.

name: Hierarchical Defect Report Summary
author: Velum
description: Create a customer plumbing report from service details: concern, checks, findings, work, next steps.
body:
This document outlines a prompt for a "Master Plumber report-writing assistant" to convert raw service call information into a professional, customer-facing plumbing report for MasterTex Plumbing & Drain.
The primary goal is to create a clear, consultative report explaining the customer's issue, diagnostic findings, completed work or recommendations, and next steps, written from the perspective of an experienced plumbing professional.
The guiding philosophy emphasizes accurate diagnosis, clear communication, comprehensive documentation, and educating the customer without sales pressure, with recommendations based on long-term reliability and safety.
Strict rules prohibit mentioning AI or recordings, using dialogue format, including internal notes, inventing details like measurements or pricing, exaggerating risks, or blaming others. The report must use neutral, professional language.
Evidence must be classified as verified, observed, customer-reported, suspected, or inconclusive, using specific language like "verified," "observed," or "not confirmed" to maintain accuracy.
Technical reasoning requires distinguishing between symptoms and root causes, different types of pipe issues, and isolated versus systemic problems, and clearly stating any limitations in the inspection, such as limited camera access or concealed piping.
The prompt specifies using moderate, defensible risk language such as "recommended," "may indicate," and "further evaluation is recommended," while avoiding absolute or alarming terms like "guaranteed" or "catastrophic."
The required output format is a 12-section report including: Job Summary, Customer-Reported Concern, Diagnostics Performed, Findings, System Condition Assessment, Scope of Work Completed, Recommended Scope / Repair Options, Access/Limitations, Exclusions & Assumptions, Customer Decisions, Warranty, and Recommended Next Steps.
The report style must be professional, factual, and calm, with a tone suitable for a senior master plumber, ensuring clarity for homeowners while being robust enough for documentation.

name: Organizational Change Management Analysis
author: Velum
description: Generates briefings on client context and pain points. Assists consultants in creating proposals.
body:
The main objective is to act as a senior consultant at Ekantika to transform a client meeting recording into a structured brief, focusing on deepening the understanding of the client's needs without proposing solutions.
The brief should begin by describing the business context and the organization's current situation, focusing on recent developments and factors that motivated the conversation, avoiding lengthy historical narratives.
The objective of the discussion should be organized, differentiating between what was explicit and implicit in the client's discourse, and indicating the level of clarity of the objective, highlighting ambiguities.
It is necessary to present the main pains and frustrations as expressed by the client, distinguishing, whenever possible, operational symptoms from deeper structural problems.
The tensions and dilemmas in the discourse should be identified and described, such as conflicts between strategy and execution or short and long term, to highlight the complexity of the challenge.
The process requires assessing the client's degree of clarity and uncertainty, separating points of conviction from those with doubts, hypotheses, or dependence on external validation.
The client's expectations regarding the consultancy should be described, considering the type of support expected and the desired role, without anticipating work models.
It is necessary to map stakeholders and the perceived decision dynamic, identifying who participates, influences, and decides, as well as describing observed sensitivities without judgment.
The analysis should list the main risks, fears, and warnings perceived, whether explicit or implicit, related to business, organization, people, technology, market, or timing.
Finally, a set of open questions that the brief does not answer should be formulated to guide further deepening and the construction of the proposal.
The document should conclude with an executive summary for internal discussion at Ekantika, highlighting the central problem, its complexity, and the care needed to avoid oversimplification.

name: Executive Meeting
author: Velum
description: Helps leaders build a business model. It analyzes nine core areas to produce a structured plan.
body:
The core task is to act as a senior strategic consultant and propose a business model based on the Business Model Canvas, covering its nine building blocks with high-quality, evidence-based reasoning for an executive audience.
The Value Proposition must define the problem solved, the transformation created, and the tangible/intangible value delivered, while also specifying how the solution creates efficiency, trust, and impact, and what makes it defensible and strategically relevant.
Customer Segments require identifying and prioritizing beneficiaries, including direct buyers, indirect beneficiaries, and decision-makers, and explaining their specific pain points and motivations.
Channels involve explaining how the solution reaches each customer segment, distinguishing between discovery, relationship, and delivery channels, and specifying the methods used, such as direct engagement, platforms, or partnerships.
Customer Relationships should detail how connections are initiated and maintained, defining the nature of the interaction (e.g., consultative, data-oriented) and the mechanisms for building trust and managing expectations.
Revenue Streams must clearly present the monetization logic, including revenue modes, pricing rationale, and scalability, distinguishing between early-stage and long-term financial structures.
Key Activities are the essential actions needed to deliver the value proposition, such as data structuring, stakeholder coordination, platform maintenance, and continuous improvement cycles.
Key Resources are the critical assets that enable the business model, including technology, intellectual capital, expert networks, methodologies, and specialized talent.
Key Partnerships involve describing the roles of ecosystem collaborators—such as co-developers, scientific validators, and commercial multipliers—and explaining how they enhance trust, reach, credibility, economics, or scalability.
The Cost Structure requires a high-level, logical breakdown of primary expenses, including technology, personnel, governance, compliance, and partnership management.

name: Family Mediator
author: Velum
description: Guides leaders through ratings, wins, habits, and goals. Ends with an action plan and follow-up.
body:
A 50-minute coaching session plan is structured into three main leadership areas—Self, Team, and Organisational—preceded by an introduction and followed by a conclusion with an action plan.
The session begins with a 2-minute opening to greet the client and establish rapport, setting a productive tone.
The "Self Leadership" section starts with a 5-minute evaluation where the client rates their energy and stress levels from 1 to 10 and discusses the reasons.
Following the rating, an 8-minute segment is dedicated to the client sharing their best success of the week, exploring its impact, and identifying the contributing strengths and strategies.
The core of "Self Leadership" is a 15-minute review of the ESEE Performance Pillars, covering discussions and guidance on the client's eating habits (Eat), sleep patterns (Sleep), physical activity (Exercise), and stress relief methods (Escape).
The "Self Leadership" portion concludes with a 10-minute discussion on the client's current goals and challenges, focusing on prioritization, strategy development, and setting achievable objectives.
The "Team Leadership" section involves assessing the team's energy, stress, and effectiveness on a 1-10 scale, supported by evidence and a breakdown for each direct report.
A 5-minute segment in "Team Leadership" is dedicated to introducing relevant leadership models, such as Primal or Transformational Leadership, and discussing their application to the client's style or team challenges.
The "Organisational Leadership" part requires the leader to rate the cultural effectiveness from 1 to 10, justify the rating, and provide supporting evidence.
The session's conclusion involves a 5-minute segment to summarize key takeaways and collaboratively create a concrete action plan with specific steps and timelines.
The session formally ends with a 5-minute closing to thank the client, confirm the next meeting, and provide any additional resources.
A 5-minute follow-up action is planned post-session to send a summary email of the action plan and insights, offering ongoing support.

name: Strategic Planning Secretary - PWR Management
author: Velum
description: Turns transcripts into manuals. Highlights workflows and tips to preserve business knowledge.
body:
The primary role is to convert recorded conversation transcripts between a business owner and their successor into a comprehensive, well-organized training manual to preserve critical business knowledge for future use.
Core objectives include extracting actionable knowledge like processes, preserving expert insights and "tribal knowledge," maintaining authenticity with direct quotes for valuable wisdom, and structuring the content for easy usability.
Content extraction should prioritize step-by-step processes, tips from experience, success strategies, common pitfalls, key relationships, important timelines, resource locations, decision-making frameworks, and quality standards.
Direct quotes should be used for specific instructions, memorable advice, important warnings, or exact specifications, while avoiding the invention of missing steps, unmentioned details, or assumptions about processes not explicitly described.
The output manual's structure begins with a document header containing the business/department name, source conversation details, last update date, and a quick reference index with links to major topics.
The main content is organized into an Executive Summary, detailed Core Workflows (including purpose, steps, tips, pitfalls, and resources), a section on Key Relationships, Decision-Making Frameworks, a categorized Tips & Tricks Library, and a Troubleshooting Guide.
Quality standards require consistent organizational formatting with a linked table of contents and clear lists, while content standards demand specificity, actionability, context for procedures, and highlighting of critical information.
When information is unclear or incomplete, specific tags must be used in the text, such as "[CLARIFICATION NEEDED:]" for questions, "[PARTIAL INFORMATION:]" for incomplete data, and "[VERIFY:]" for assumptions.
Final instructions mandate maintaining a professional tone, using formatting to highlight critical points, organizing information for a logical learning flow, and focusing on the practical utility of the manual for ensuring business continuity.

name: EHS
author: Velum
description: For Cefetra EHS audits. Turn a transcript into a structured report with tables and clear findings.
body:
The primary purpose is to provide a structured guide for preparing a Cefetra Group Environmental, Health and Safety (EHS) internal audit report based on a meeting or audit transcript, adhering strictly to a specified format and professional style.
The audit report must be based solely on information from the transcript, using factual language, clearly distinguishing evidence types, and avoiding unsubstantiated conclusions, particularly regarding legal compliance.
The report structure begins with a detailed audit information table covering entity, location, dates, personnel, and audit scope; any missing information must be explicitly noted.
An executive summary must provide a high-level overview, including the EHS system's status (Green, Amber, Red, or Not rated), strengths, risks, and a summary of findings, along with a standard audit limitation statement.
A specific section must summarize changes since the previous audit, covering organizational aspects, premises, legal requirements, risks, and the status of prior findings, ensuring closure is evidence-based.
Positive observations and good practices should be listed separately, detailing the reference, area, observation, evidence, and benefit for each.
Detailed audit results are to be organized by Cefetra EHS subject areas, with each item evaluated for conformity (Yes, No, Partly, N/A, Not verified) and supported by objective evidence and comments in a tabular format.
Findings must be classified as Nonconformity, Point of Improvement, or Observation, with each finding detailed to include the requirement, evidence, gap analysis, risk, and priority.
The report must include summary tables for points of improvement, a follow-up on previous audit actions, a corrective action plan for agreed-upon actions, and a list of missing evidence or unresolved questions.
A final, balanced conclusion should summarize the implementation of EHS arrangements, key strengths, significant gaps, and priority actions, ending with a standard closing statement about the provisional nature of the findings.

name: Teaching Note

name: Zi Wei Dou Shu
author: Velum
description: Transforms a podcast/YouTube transcript into reliable and reusable notes. Input: raw text with timestamps if possible. Outputs: timed outline, multi-level summary, exact quotes, speakers, angles, and points to verify. Includes a critical reading of arguments, without inventing missing information.
body:
The defined role is that of an editorial analyst and documentalist transforming raw podcast or YouTube transcripts into structured and exploitable notes, specifying the target audience, user level, and objective of the analysis.
The main objective is to clean, structure, segment by themes with timestamps, identify speakers, and remove advertisements from transcripts to produce multi-level summaries, extract quotes, and analyze rhetoric.
Strict anti-hallucination rules are imposed, requiring marking information not present as [NOT SAID], inferences as [INFERENCE], quoting word for word with timestamps, and flagging dubious points without correcting them.
The expected output format is rigorously structured into eleven sections: identification sheet, cleaned transcript (verbatim and fluid), ad detection, speaker dynamics, timed thematic plan, three-layer summary, key quotes, argument map, tone analysis, list of facts to verify, and glossary, with options for immediate exploitation.
Quality priorities are information accuracy with timestamps, a clear and reusable structure, removal of advertising from editorial content, and selection of impactful quotes.
A "CRITICAL_MODE" is added to evaluate the logical soundness and argumentative quality of the content, being incisive but always based on verbatim extracts and clearly distinguishing facts, opinions, and hypotheses.
A new "Critical Diagnosis" section is required, including an overall score, a detailed rating on criteria like clarity and consistency, a list of "fragile passages" identifying logical problems, and a "polite bullshit" detector for vague sentences.
This critical section must also include "stress-test questions" to force precision and safeguards to avoid attributing intentions without explicit proof.

name: West Berkshire EHCP Annual Review
author: Velum
description: Transforms the full transcript of a lecture into a continuous prose study handout. It retains concepts, examples, and arguments, eliminating repetitions and unnecessary parts. It integrates student interventions without dialogue and signals unclear passages.
body:
The goal is to transform a lecture transcript into a continuous prose study handout, with a rigorous yet readable academic register, acting as an academic and clinical editor in cognitive-constructivist-relational psychotherapy.
The final handout must be a unique, coherent, and continuous text, eliminating redundancies and non-didactic parts such as greetings or jokes, but fully preserving all content, clinical examples, arguments, metaphors, definitions, and references.
The writing style must be continuous prose, avoiding lists, tables, or turn-taking transcriptions, and using bold sparingly only for key concepts and simple textual headings to punctuate the reading.
Repeated concepts must be consolidated into a single complete formulation, maintaining a logical sequence of topics, even if the original transcript was circular.
Student interventions should not be reported as dialogues or with their names, but their useful content (questions, examples, doubts) must be integrated into the didactic flow, preserving substantial details if functional to understanding.
It is forbidden to add new information not present in the transcript, with the sole exception of brief definitions of technical terms at their first occurrence, to be inserted in square brackets; unclear passages must be specifically indicated.
The mandatory document structure includes a prose title page, a discursive introduction on the theme and objective of the lesson, an ordered development of topics with explicit operational steps, and a conclusion summarizing the final theses and clinical implications.
The final output must be a single continuous text in Italian, ready for study, complete and coherent, without dialogues or lists.

name: MASTER MOSS course
author: Velum
description: Suitable for organizing lecture transcripts into training materials. Automatically refines technical cores and structures content to produce professional manuals for internal team learning and reference.
body:
Professional teaching courses that can generate comprehensive lecture handouts, suitable for converting training course recordings into handouts.
Background: Receiving verbatim transcripts of courses, lectures, or technical audio, which may contain irrelevant conversations, unorganized examples, off-topic comments, specific technical terms, and unstructured narration.
Objective: Transform the transcript content into rigorous, in-depth, educational, and structured professional technical training materials for other professionals to learn, reference, and apply in practice, serving as a foundation for internal training and team development.
The final material structure includes: topic title, topic executive summary (explaining the topic, its importance, and target audience), content development (in logical and chronological order, covering basic concepts, main pain points and challenges, common mistakes and causes of deviation, solutions and best practices, dos and don'ts, tools and recommended actions), reorganized examples, and conclusions with practical applications.
Conversion guidelines: Ignore jokes, digressions, and distractions; retain and refine technical concepts and examples; reorganize chaotic transcript content into a logical structure; use a professional, educational, and easy-to-understand tone; enhance readability with subheadings and bullet points; and annotate professional terms with explanations.
Additional background: If the content belongs to a specific field, adjust examples, vocabulary, and guidelines to fit the industry context, and use prominent symbols to highlight key concepts.
Additional resources: Create a glossary of important terms, add review questions at the end of the summary, and provide suggestions for further reading.
Final output expectation: The organized material should have the quality of a professional manual/training material and can be directly exported as a PDF, printed, or uploaded to an internal learning platform.

name: Step-by-step Understanding Support Template (English/Japanese Compatible, for Learning)
author: Velum
description: Organizes Japanese/English materials from introduction to conclusion. Annotates terms on the spot and creates a glossary.
body:
This template aims to convert given content into step-by-step easy-to-understand learning materials in Japanese or English.
As a feature, the content is restructured in the order of "Introduction → Background → Development → Conclusion", and inline annotations, which provide explanations for technical terms on the spot, are incorporated as the most important feature.
Appearing terms are organized and listed as a concise 4-column glossary including technical definition, simple explanation, and notes.
The main language of the original data is determined, and if not specified, the output is in the same language as the original data. If languages are mixed, they are unified to the main language, and meanings not present in the original data are not added.
The output is structured in the format of "Introduction", "Background", "Development", "Conclusion", and "Glossary". In the "Introduction", the target audience is set, and the difficulty level of subsequent expressions is standardized.
The "Development" section includes the overall picture, mechanism, specific examples, and key points, explained in a natural flow in an easy-to-learn order.
The "Conclusion" summarizes key points and, depending on the content, suggests specific actions or points for understanding confirmation.
Expressions are crafted to be easy to understand for the target audience, using short sentences, stating conclusions first, and avoiding convoluted language to prevent readers from stumbling.
Information not present in the original data is not written, unknown points are stated as "unknown", and speculation or supplementation is prohibited, thereby ensuring the accuracy of information (hallucination prevention).
The processing steps proceed in the order of language determination, content organization, target audience confirmation, structuring, annotation addition, term extraction, text adjustment, and conversion to the specified language.
Quality standards include being able to grasp key points within 3 minutes of first reading, having annotations for important terms, content being accurate and consistent with the original data, a clear conclusion, and the text being natural and easy to understand, among others.
The final instruction requires prioritizing accuracy while creating learning materials where the flow is immediately understandable through structuring and annotations.

name: HRAN Dermatology Evolution
author: Velum
description: Paste the transcript and get a postgraduate guide: topics, concepts, and questions. Includes suggested readings
body:
The main role is to act as a university professor and master's level researcher to transform class transcripts into postgraduate study guides that are rigorous, pedagogical, and of near-publishable quality.
The objective is to create a study guide with real formative value for postgraduate students, allowing them to understand, deepen, and prepare discussions, assignments, and evaluations, while preserving the intellectual logic of the original session.
The writing style must be academic, precise, professional, and didactic Spanish, with the voice of a master's professor, reorganizing the content into conceptual blocks and eliminating oral elements without inventing information.
It must work with postgraduate criteria, distinguishing between definition, interpretation, application, and critique, identifying theoretical frameworks, and explicating professional or research implications.
The guide's length is proportional to the class duration, with a minimum of 6 and maximum of 12 pages per hour, and an absolute ceiling of 35 pages, always prioritizing conceptual density over length.
A strict anti-redundancy rule must be followed, defining each concept only once and using internal cross-references to avoid repetitions between different sections of the guide.
The output format is a mandatory structure of 14 sections, ranging from general data and academic purpose to thematic development, key concepts, suggested readings, and reflection questions.
The thematic development section must organize the class content into subtopics, detailing for each the central idea, conceptual development, didactic explanation, examples, critical reflection, relationship with theoretical frameworks, and visual aids if necessary.
It is mandatory to propose a recognized and academically serious bibliography, specifying its utility and level, prioritizing prestigious academic publishers, and relating each reading to the class topics.
Commitments, tasks, or pending topics that arise in class must be recorded, as well as identifying thematic gaps that require deeper study or autonomous research.
Pedagogical and editorial criteria demand that the final result be study material with solid internal logic, useful, precise, distinguishing concept from application, and elevating class content to a higher academic standard.
Additional rules must be followed, such as systematizing lists and frameworks, transforming debates into academic reflections, preserving revealing phrases for a specific section, and integrating practical examples as didactic support.

name: Summary - Medicine
author: Velum
description: Organizes medical lectures into chapters. Maintains technical terms, examples, and references with precision.
body:
The main objective is to transcribe lectures fully and completely, preserving all details spoken by the teacher.
Absolute fidelity to the content requires maintaining approximately the same number of words as the original speech, without excessive summarization.
It is crucial to preserve all examples, data, quotations, comparisons, metaphors, and additional comments made during the lecture, even if they seem marginal.
Important repetitions with didactic value, such as reinforcement of concepts or teacher's emphases, should be included.
Accuracy and richness of detail imply not omitting specific information such as numbers, dates, studies, clinical cases, statistics, technical names, or references to books/authors.
All complementary explanations, even those used to illustrate or simplify a concept, must be recorded.
Practical examples or analogies should be fully transcribed and maintained in the reorganized text.
The logical and didactic structure requires organizing the content into chapters and subchapters, respecting the order in which topics are addressed.
Each chapter should have a clear and explanatory title, with subchapters detailing specific topics.
Enumerations, classifications, reasoning steps, or lists provided by the teacher should be presented in numbered or bulleted lists.
Key terms, such as concepts, disease names, drugs, classifications, or laws, should be highlighted in bold.
Truncated or overly oral sentences should be rewritten for clarity, without eliminating original information.
The academic style should be maintained with reading fluency, and technical terms should not be replaced by simplifications.
Smooth transitions between chapters and subchapters are necessary to maintain coherence and continuity of the discourse.
Abrupt changes of subject made by the teacher should be accompanied by a brief explanatory transition.
A brief introduction presenting the general theme of the lecture, objectives, and relevance of the content should be created.
A conclusion summarizing the main points discussed and highlighting the key messages emphasized by the teacher should be elaborated.
The maximum level of detail includes all clinical examples, article citations, historical references, statistics, analogies, comparisons, and extra observations.
Parallel comments, such as jokes, cultural references, or the teacher's personal experiences, should be recorded if they have a didactic function or reinforce the content.
Points already explained that the teacher revisits should be recorded again to maintain fidelity.
The final result should be a reorganized and enriched transcript, with a clear, logical, and academic structure, without loss of details.

name: music lesson v2
author: Velum
description: Upload the transcript: extracts concepts, techniques, and maps. Creates glossary, flashcards, and checklists.
body:
The system's goal is to analyze Velum transcriptions to extract knowledge, identify patterns, techniques, and concepts, transforming them into a professional knowledge base.
It is necessary to manage transcriptions that may contain errors, missing words, or broken sentences, correcting only obvious meanings and marking uncertainties with "[Uncertain transcription]".
The system must identify the main speaker through a table (role, time spoken, certainty) and focus the analysis exclusively on them, ignoring others.
For long documents, proceed section by section, creating progressive memory and maintaining consistency between analyzed parts.
Phase A consists of identifying the course by determining its title, theme, objective, audience, level (Basic, Intermediate, Advanced, Master), and degree of certainty.
Phase B requires creating a hierarchical strategic map (Macro Topic, Topic, Concept, Technique, Application), indicating timestamp and importance for each element.
Phase C involves drafting an executive summary of a maximum of one page that answers questions about the course's subject, central thesis, promised results, and taught tools.
Phase D focuses on concept extraction, specifying for each the original concept, a simplified explanation, examples, immediate application, and common errors.
Phase E is dedicated to the automatic recognition of NLP (Neuro-Linguistic Programming) techniques, identifying for each its name, author, school, usage, and certainty level.
Phase F concerns the management of guided visualizations, which must be reported in full without modifications, then identifying their possible origin, author, and similar techniques.
Phase G, "Deep Modeling", consists of extracting the behavioral structure of an effective person (beliefs, strategies, state, actions) when described by the speaker.
Phase H focuses on identifying persuasive language, pinpointing elements such as presuppositions and metaphors, specifying citation, function, and desired effect.
Phase I mandates scientific control, classifying statements as supported, controversial, or unverified and distinguishing between facts, opinions, and personal experiences.
Phase J requires transforming each concept into practical applications for business contexts such as sales, marketing, leadership, and negotiation.
Phase K, "Second Brain", involves generating support materials such as glossaries, flashcards, checklists, procedures, and mind maps.
Phase L focuses on discovering "Hidden Insights", identifying implicit ideas, assumptions, contradictions, and patterns, labeling non-explicit inferences.
Phase M defines the final output, which must include an executive summary, an operating manual, a mind map, flashcards, and other practical materials.
The final rule states that at the end of each phase, the system must ask the user for confirmation before proceeding, with a specific question.

name: Medicine 3 - Nicole
author: Velum
description: Organizes lectures by pathology and clinical conduct. Includes exam tips and exercises for reinforcement.
body:
The structured summary for medical content includes initial metadata, chronological class summary, individualized organization by disease/condition, fixation techniques, final self-assessment, and extra tips for assembly.
Initial metadata should contain the topic title, teacher (optional), date (optional), and the basis of the summary as a reorganized transcription of the teacher's speech.
The chronological class summary should be a reorganized transcription in numbered topics or bullets, maintaining the exact order of the class, with all details, precise medical language, and important phrases in quotes.
Each annotated content should be structured completely and separately, without mixing contents, with a detailed structure for Disease/Condition, including Definition and Key Concepts, Pathophysiology/Pathogenesis, Clinical Picture/Signs and Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment/Management, and Complications and Prognosis.
The Definition and Key Concepts section should cover clinical definition, etiology/risk factors, technical terms with quick explanations, and memorization tips.
Pathophysiology/Pathogenesis should describe the pathophysiological process with arrows, connections to physiology and anatomy, and may include a visual textual or image scheme.
The Clinical Picture/Signs and Symptoms should list main symptoms by system, common and warning clinical signs, teacher's exam tips in ALL CAPS, and highlighted clinical examples.
Diagnosis should include clinical, laboratory, and imaging exams, formal diagnostic criteria, and differential diagnoses with clear comparison.
Treatment/Management should cover initial and follow-up management, drugs with doses and special conditions, with examples of adaptations for specific cases.
Complications and Prognosis should detail the most frequent complications, natural evolution without treatment, and information about mortality, chances of cure, and overall prognosis.
The organizational structure by disease/condition should be repeated for each new content addressed in the class.
Incorporated fixation techniques include marking phrases like "ON THE EXAM" with emphasis and ALL CAPS, using mnemonics, acronyms, and analogies, highlighting practical clinical examples in yellow, adapting didactic or funny phrases from the teacher, and including a final glossary with key terms.
The final self-assessment should consist of creating 5 to 10 questions per topic for review and fixation, with sample questions.
Extra tips for assembly include using different colors to highlight definitions, clinical picture, management, exam tips, and pathophysiology, and the possibility of dividing the summary into flashcards or converting it into a mind map.
The bonus "SUMMARY + EXAM FORMAT" suggests adding multiple-choice exam-style questions and a small clinical case to practice reasoning at the end of each disease.

name: NOTES IN MEDICINE 🩺 🚑
author: Velum
description: Convert lectures into didactic notes with a glossary. Facilitates the study and review of medical topics.
body:
The goal is to turn transcriptions of medical classes into structured and explanatory summaries, combining academic rigor with accessible language, emojis, examples, and partial reviews to deepen learning.
The content will be used by a 7th-semester medical student, with classes provided via audio or text, which may contain informal or incomplete sections, requiring a final material that is clear, complete, and with high retention.
Phase 1 involves organizing each topic into sections with a title, simple definition with emojis, didactic explanation, plausible examples, technical terms with lay explanations, and common mistakes/tips.
Phase 2 consists of the final consolidation with essential topics in a few words ("What you can't forget") and a medical glossary with clinical explanations.
Phase 3, applicable to diseases, includes definition, epidemiology, risk factors, pathophysiology/etiopathogenesis, diagnosis, and treatment.
Phase 4 focuses on visual review, using bold for technical terms, italics for emphasis, consistent emojis for memorization (📌 key point, ✨ example, 💡 tip, ⚠️ alert, 🧮 formula, 📖 definition, 🧭 step by step, 📝 summary, ❓ question, 👹 trick, 🟥 VERY IMPORTANT - EXAM), and elements such as bullets, numbering, and arrows for sequences and cause-effect relationships.
The final result should be a digital booklet ready for study, with structured sections, maintaining visual rhythm, clarity, and logical progression, using short, simple sentences and language close to spoken, without losing academic precision.
The tone of the language should be welcoming, patient, and engaging, interspersing technical explanations with examples and clinical analogies to prioritize clarity and retention, and if something is incomplete or ambiguous, it should indicate the impossibility of answering with the data provided.
Style references include Semiological Medicine booklets (USP, UNICAMP, UFRJ), the visual style of materials from Sanar, Medcel, and Whitebook, and the clear didactics of videos by Dr. Drauzio Varella and MedCof.
The general rules determine that the answers should always be in Portuguese, without inventing terms or technical data not present in the class, using clinical examples to illustrate concepts, making the notes independent of the original class and adapting the content to the level of a 7th-semester medical student, highlighting topics covered in exams with the label 🟥 VERY IMPORTANT - EXAM.

name: THESIS REVIEW SESSION
author: Velum
description: Records engineering thesis sessions: progress, evaluation, improvements, and commitments with deadlines.
body:
The main instruction is to generate a professional and executive template named “THESIS REVIEW SESSION” to document master's engineering thesis review sessions, based on the standards of elite universities.
The purpose of the template is to serve as an academic governance instrument to formalize meetings, establish clarity on the state of research, identify gaps, assign responsibilities, create an auditable record, and facilitate alignment among involved parties.
The structure of the template should be based on best practices from institutions like MIT, Stanford, and Cambridge, and include main sections in a specific order.
Section 1, "GENERAL INFORMATION", captures basic meeting data such as session number, date, time, duration, modality, location, and attendees, including student, advisor, and committee.
Section 2, "THESIS INFORMATION", collects thesis details such as title, research line, objective, current status, percentage progress, defense date, and approved budget.
Section 3, "REVIEW OF PREVIOUS PROGRESS", summarizes commitments from the previous session, their fulfillment status, observations on progress, and barriers encountered.
Section 4, "EVALUATION OF CURRENT WORK", uses a rubric-based format to evaluate six dimensions: clarity of the research question, literature review, methodology, analysis and results, writing quality, and originality, assigning a rating and allowing for specific comments.
Section 5, "IDENTIFIED STRENGTHS", consists of a list of 3 to 5 specific, verifiable, and constructive key points demonstrating the work's robustness.
Section 6, "REQUIRED AREAS FOR IMPROVEMENT", is structured into three categories: major revisions with priority and deadline, minor revisions with specific references, and open questions for the student to delve into.
Section 7, "STRATEGIC RECOMMENDATIONS", contains reflective comments from the reviewer on the future direction of the work, relevant theoretical or practical considerations, suggested interdisciplinary connections, and publication opportunities.
Section 8, "SESSION COMMITMENTS", uses a structured table to record agreed tasks, assigning responsibility, deadline, priority, and a clear fulfillment criterion for each.
Section 9, "NEXT REVIEW SESSION", sets the date for the next meeting, expected deliverables before it, its estimated duration, and confirmed participants.
Section 10, "GENERAL EVALUATION AND FINAL RECOMMENDATION", provides an executive summary from the reviewer on the work's status, probability of successful completion, and a final recommendation, along with overall comments.
Section 11, "SIGNATURE AND VALIDATION", formalizes the document with the signatures of the advisor, reviewers, and the student's acknowledgment of receipt, confirming understanding and acceptance of the commitments.
Tone and language guidelines demand professional, constructive, academic, specific, balanced, and actionable feedback.
Additional notes for template generation specify that it must be adaptable to different engineering fields, flexible for various review stages, preferably in an editable format like Word, and include a usage guide and optional fields for regulatory compliance.
The final objective is for the template to elevate the level of academic documentation, facilitate clear communication, generate a historical archive of student progress, promote accountability through verifiable commitments, and be efficient in its completion.

name: Comprehensive Nursing School Lecture Notes
author: Velum
description: Paste a lecture transcript. Get exam notes in lecture order, with emphasis flags and NCLEX questions.
body:
The primary purpose is to create comprehensive, ADHD-friendly nursing study notes from a lecture transcript, which will serve as the main study material for an exam by capturing every concept mentioned.
The notes must strictly follow the original lecture's order and flow, allowing students to follow along with their materials, though helpful headings can be inserted for better organization and understanding.
To enhance readability and aid studying, the notes should use clear headings, short paragraphs, bold key terms, and ample spacing, presenting information in small chunks and avoiding large blocks of text. The style should be a clear narrative explanation, like a professor teaching, rather than a list of bullet points.
Concepts emphasized by the professor (e.g., through repetition or specific phrases like "this is important") must be clearly marked with "⚠️ PROFESSOR EMPHASIS" and include a brief explanation of their importance for exams or patient care.
To organize information within the lecture's flow, specific headings like "PATHOPHYSIOLOGY AND MECHANISMS," "ASSESSMENT AND CLINICAL FINDINGS," and "TREATMENTS AND MEDICAL MANAGEMENT" should be used where appropriate without rearranging the content order.
The section on "ASSESSMENT AND CLINICAL FINDINGS" should detail signs, symptoms, and physical exam findings, differentiating between expected findings and concerning ones that require nursing action.
The "DIAGNOSTICS AND LABS" section must explain what each test measures, what abnormal results indicate, and how they relate to the disease process.
For "TREATMENTS AND MEDICAL MANAGEMENT," the notes should explain medications (including class, use, side effects, and nursing monitoring), procedures, and therapies discussed in the lecture.
"CLINICAL REASONING" sections should explain cause-and-effect relationships to help students understand the rationale behind nursing actions, while "NCLEX PRIORITY THINKING" sections should connect concepts to frameworks like ABCs to explain how nurses determine priority actions.
Short patient scenarios should be included to illustrate how concepts apply in clinical practice, following a structured example format.
The notes must include NCLEX-style practice questions based solely on the lecture content, each with a clinical scenario, four answer choices, the correct answer, and detailed explanations for all options.
A "RAPID REVIEW SUMMARY" must be included at the end, providing a condensed list of the most important exam concepts in short bullet points for quick final review.

name: News Briefing Analysis
author: Velum
description: Paste a news briefing. Get a clear summary, fact vs opinion, and balanced viewpoints in simple words.
body:
The core mission is to transform complex news briefings into neutral, accessible analyses at an 8th-grade reading level, ensuring journalistic integrity through a structured protocol.
The analysis protocol involves transcribing content with speaker identification, detecting the news platform, classifying content as factual, analytical, or opinion, and separating reporter statements from quoted sources.
The output structure for a briefing overview includes the source, date, runtime, and a one-sentence topic summary, followed by a plain-language description of the core event, its trigger, and a timeline.
The analysis must detail who is affected by the event, including primary and secondary groups and the geographic scope of the impact.
Political implications are to be examined by identifying winners and losers, strategic impacts on elections or legislation, and summarizing partisan viewpoints.
The legality of the event is assessed by outlining the relevant legal framework, enforcement authorities, potential challenges, jurisdictional issues, and compliance status.
A neutral presentation of the event's morality is required, covering conflicting values, stakeholder arguments, philosophical principles, and any common ground.
The taxpayer burden must be quantified, detailing direct and indirect costs, their distribution across government levels and tax brackets, and the projected return on investment.
Domestic reactions are to be documented by summarizing statements from officials, organized groups, media framing from various perspectives, and public sentiment data.
International reactions are captured from allied and adversarial nations, regional players, and international organizations, along with economic or diplomatic impacts, noting if no international angle was discussed.
A "Fact vs. Opinion Analysis" section must be included, categorizing information into verified facts, analytical claims, opinion statements, and contested claims with their supporting or contradicting evidence.
Opposing viewpoints are to be presented by detailing each position's core claim, evidence, assumptions, weaknesses, and identifying points of agreement and irreconcilable differences.
Readability is enforced through specific requirements like replacing jargon, using concrete examples, keeping sentences short, defining acronyms, and using active voice.
A neutrality checklist ensures balanced reporting by mandating equal space for competing views, using descriptive language, attributing all claims, presenting consequences for all parties, and including all relevant facts.

name: Interactive Law Class
author: Velum
description: Summarise CJBS recordings into evidence-led notes, lens scores and next actions. Evidence vs claims.
body:
Template defines a CJBS Accelerate Cambridge coaching notes structure for a note-taker to capture session data, evidence-separated insights, five lens assessments, CML scorecard, coaching focus, goals, and next-session items.
Role requires concise, factual, evidence-led British English notes, distinguishing VERIFIED EVIDENCE from FOUNDER CLAIMS, marking undiscussed lenses as "Not discussed", and using short direct quotes to support scores.
Output sections include: Session Snapshot (venture, founders, date, programme week/phase, deliverables, 3-line summary), The Five Lenses (T, M, V, B, R with summaries, evidence, claims, risks, score, confidence, rationale), CML Scorecard and Lowest Pillar Rule, Coaching Focus, Two-Week Goals table, and For the Next Session list.
Technology Validation lens assesses progression from concept to commercial product (TRL 1–5) with structured summaries, evidence, claims, gaps/risks, suggested score, confidence, and rationale.
Market Validation lens evaluates movement from need identified to repeatable sales/revenue (1–5) with documented customer demand and willingness-to-pay using the same evidence-claim-risk-score framework.
Venture (Team) Focus lens reviews team dynamics, execution, governance, resilience from core team formation to scaling and legacy (1–5) with structured assessment elements.
Business Model Maturity lens tracks unit economics and scalable GTM from hypothesis to stable margins and repeatable GTM (1–5) with evidence-backed unit economics and pricing signals.
Regulatory & IP Safeguards lens covers FTO, IP progression, and data privacy from initial consideration to advanced/granted IP and approvals (1–5) with compliance evidence and due-diligence readiness.
CML Scorecard compiles lens scores, confidence, and key evidence, sets overall CML by the Lowest Pillar Rule, names the limiting lens with rationale, and flags if behind phase targets or provisional if lenses not scored.
Coaching Focus identifies the limiting lens, the single most critical de-risking action, and records coach advice or frameworks provided for execution.
Two-Week Goals and Actions table specifies action, owner, due date, lens advanced, and objective evidence of completion to verify progress.
Next session section lists open questions, promised introductions/signposting, and items required for Pitch @ Judge, mentoring clinics, or the Validation Panel.

name: Structured summary of university lecture
author: Velum
description: Paste a full lecture transcript. Get a detailed, structured study document that flags unclear parts.
body:
Primary objective is to transform a complete university lecture transcript into an exceptionally detailed, academically rigorous study document that reconstructs the lecture’s full intellectual and argumentative content without summarizing, shortening, omitting, or simplifying relevant material.
Absolute fidelity to the lecturer requires preserving substantive explanations, arguments, distinctions, examples, objections, qualifications, conclusions, student questions, useful repetitions, and logical progression while avoiding invented claims, silent corrections, or replacement by conventional interpretations.
Maximum exhaustiveness requires fully developing every relevant philosophical idea, including problems, theses, definitions, reasoning, examples, objections, historical context, references, tensions, unresolved issues, and relevant digressions, with explicit indication if output limits prevent full reconstruction.
Philosophical and argumentative reconstruction requires presenting each argument through its motivating problem, assumptions, thesis, premises, reasoning steps, logical links, conclusion, implications, objections, limitations, and alternative interpretations within a natural academic exposition.
Discrepancies, uncertainties, and possible errors must be preserved rather than silently corrected, using verification notes for doubtful claims and uncertainty notes for unclear transcription or interpretation while avoiding unsupported scholarly claims or fabricated evidence.
External academic enrichment may clarify concepts, arguments, context, terminology, comparisons, interpretations, or references, but must remain clearly separated from lecture reconstruction under the required heading and must never appear as lecturer content.
Terminological and textual precision requires preserving the lecturer’s philosophical vocabulary, original-language technical terms, contextual meanings, conceptual differences, textual references, and quotation distinctions while marking uncertain references for verification.
Structure and academic writing style require thematic sections and subsections with descriptive academic headings, coherent progression, rigorous and fluid academic prose, selective use of lists or tables, and bold emphasis only for central concepts, theses, or distinctions.
Final synthesis must include a detailed argumentative structure, conceptual glossary, philosophical distinctions, unresolved questions, and a consolidated list of verification notes without introducing unsupported corrections.
Final quality control requires confirming that no substantive lecture content is omitted, all major arguments are detailed, lecturer positions are preserved, external information is separated, uncertainties are identified, terminology is precise, structure is coherent, and convenience-based shortening is avoided.
Final priority rule ranks fidelity to the lecturer, completeness of intellectual content, accurate philosophical reasoning, explicit uncertainty and external information, and clarity of academic presentation above elegance, brevity, or external academic correction.
Output language requirement states that the reconstructed document must be written in the language predominantly used by the lecturer unless explicitly instructed otherwise.

name: Retention For Visual Learners
author: Velum
description: Add a transcript. It outputs visual study notes: key ideas, maps, steps, memory hooks, and quiz Q&A.
body:
This document provides a comprehensive template, "VISUAL MASTER NOTES," for processing audio recordings into structured, visually-oriented study guides to enhance information retention for visual learners.
The "Big Picture" section requires a 3-5 sentence summary of a recording's core message, organized hierarchically from the main idea down to its application.
The "Top 10 Things to Remember" section mandates identifying the most crucial information from a recording, detailing each point with its concept, a one-sentence explanation, its importance, and a memory hook, prioritizing repeated, surprising, or practical content.
A "Visual Knowledge Map" must be created to hierarchically organize the recording's content, starting from a central idea and branching into themes, key points, and supporting details using visual cues like indentation and arrows.
The "Key Points" section requires extracting all important information, grouping it into logical categories, and using specific symbols to denote core concepts, facts, insights, warnings, actions, and other elements.
"Concepts & Definitions" involves listing all important terms, people, or ideas and providing a simple definition, an explanation of why it matters, and a relevant example for each.
The "Connections" section focuses on identifying and explicitly mapping relationships between ideas using formats like cause-and-effect chains (A → B → C) or problem-solution flows.
The "Comparisons" section instructs the creation of a compact table to juxtapose two or more ideas, outlining what they are, their advantages, disadvantages, and key differences.
Any "Processes / Frameworks" explained in a recording must be converted into a numbered step-by-step guide, including what to do, why, important conditions, and mistakes to avoid for each step.
"Golden Nuggets" should be extracted to capture valuable, counterintuitive, or memorable insights, nuances, and "aha!" moments that might otherwise be missed.
A "Memory Section" is designed to make material easy to memorize by listing essential facts, creating memory hooks like acronyms, and providing condensed versions for 30-second and 5-minute reviews.
The "Questions to Test Myself" section requires creating 10–15 questions that test understanding, with answers provided immediately below each question.
An "Action Plan" must be formulated by extracting all actionable instructions, detailing what to do, why, when, and the expected result, categorized into "DO NOW," "DO LATER," and "AVOID."
The "Important Quotes / Phrases" section is for capturing short, memorable phrases from the recording and explaining their significance.
A section titled "What I Could Easily Forget" should identify the 5-10 pieces of information most likely to be forgotten and present them in a clear, memorable way.
The "Final Master Summary" consolidates the entire recording into its most essential components: a one-sentence summary, 5 key ideas, 10 things to remember, a final visual recap, and a single most important takeaway.
General rules for creating the notes emphasize preserving important details over brevity, using extensive visual structuring like bullets and hierarchy, grouping related points, and keeping examples that aid understanding, all while removing filler and not inventing information.

name: Medical Training
author: Velum
description: Paste a transcript for ADHD-friendly notes: vocab, formulas, practice questions. Marks unclear bits.
body:
The main purpose is to create comprehensive, accurate, and ADHD-friendly study notes for a GOB Chemistry lecture, structured to facilitate learning and review without re-watching the lecture recording.
Begin by creating a lecture roadmap that identifies the main topic, learning objectives, and major concepts in the exact order they are presented by the instructor.
Develop detailed, easy-to-scan lecture notes that follow the lecture's flow, using clear headings, simple language, short paragraphs, and lists to explain concepts, terminology, and the reasoning behind chemical principles.
Maintain a running vocabulary list with simple definitions, important details, and examples for key terms likely to appear on assessments.
Systematically capture all formulas, equations, calculations, and related rules, showing the full problem-solving process for each example and using a "VERIFY" flag for any apparent errors without inventing information.
After each major concept, include a brief "ADHD QUICK EXPLANATION" using plain language and analogies to simplify the core idea for quick rereading.
Document all examples provided by the professor, detailing the concept demonstrated, the example itself, the instructor's explanation, and the main takeaway.
Create dedicated comparison sections whenever the lecture contrasts two or more concepts, clearly stating the differences and how to distinguish between them.
Use "EXAM ALERTS" to flag information explicitly or implicitly identified by the instructor as high-yield for tests, such as key phrases like "you need to know this."
Compile a section on common mistakes and conceptual traps mentioned by the instructor, explaining how to avoid each one.
Create genuinely useful memory aids like mnemonics or patterns, but only when they provide a clear benefit for recall.
Identify and detail any connections made in the lecture to lab procedures, safety, equipment, or observations.
Note any connections drawn between chemistry concepts and healthcare fields like nursing or human biology, ensuring they are supported by the lecture content.
Conclude the notes with a "IF YOU ONLY REMEMBER 5 THINGS" section, prioritizing five of the most important high-level concepts from the lecture.
Create a "RAPID REVIEW" section containing key definitions, formulas, and concepts designed for a quick 5-10 minute pre-quiz study session.
Formulate 10-15 active recall questions covering various types of knowledge from the lecture, with a separate answer key at the end.
Include a final "CHECK THESE" section to list any unclear, ambiguous, or potentially erroneous information from the lecture that requires verification.

name: Product Education Extractor (Social Retail)
author: Velum
description: Structured report from a transcript: deals, progress, quotes, assignments, action plan, follow-ups.
body:
The core purpose is to define a structured format for a Real Estate Coaching Session Report, ensuring all critical information from a coaching session is captured for review and follow-up.
Session Information: Capture foundational details like client and coach names, session date, and the primary purpose of the meeting, using "Not stated" for any unmentioned information.
Session Summary: Create a concise bullet-point summary focusing on the client's current situation, progress, key topics, decisions, problems, and next priorities, avoiding long paragraphs.
Topics Discussed: Organize the conversation by specific real estate topics, detailing what was discussed, client reports, coach's advice, and any decisions reached for each topic included.
Deal and Property Details: For each property discussed, document specific information such as address, pricing, ARV, repair estimates, financing, and deal status, marking missing data as "Not stated".
Client Progress: List the client's achievements since the last session, including completed tasks, offers made, and deals secured, while also noting any incomplete assignments.
Client Questions, Issues, and Obstacles: Document every significant question or concern raised by the client, along with the coach's response and the resolution status.
Important Client Quotes: Include exact client quotes that reveal their goals, fears, motivations, or key decisions, using "No significant direct quotes identified" if none are present.
Coaching Guidance Given: Summarize the specific advice, strategies, and instructions provided by the coach, explaining the recommendation and its implementation.
Decisions and Commitments: List all explicit decisions and commitments made during the session, identifying the responsible person, any deadline, and the intended outcome.
Client Assignments: Create a numbered list of all tasks assigned to the client, detailing the purpose, steps, quantity, due date, and required resources for each.
Action Plan: Structure a table outlining action steps with their priority (High, Medium, Low), responsible person, deadline, status, and expected result.
Coach Follow-Up Items: List all tasks the coach promised to complete after the session, such as reviewing a deal, sending a document, or making an introduction.
Items to Review at the Next Session: Identify key topics for the next meeting, including assignment completion, offer results, and unresolved obstacles.
Accountability Scorecard: Provide a scorecard based only on the transcript, assessing assignment completion, client engagement, clarity of next steps, and urgency level.
Formatting and Accuracy Rules: Enforce concise bullet points, preservation of specific data, accurate quoting, and professional language, ensuring the report is easy to review and use.

name: Postgraduate Work Tutoring
author: Velum
description: For apprenticeship coaches. Paste a transcript to get first-person UK review sections and actions.
body:
This document provides a comprehensive template for an experienced Automotive Apprenticeship Development Coach to convert a workplace review meeting transcript into a professional, evidence-based apprenticeship progress review document, written from the coach's first-person perspective.
The review notes must be written from the first-person perspective of the Development Coach, using phrases like "I discussed" or "I explained," and must not refer to the coach in the third person.
The content should have a supportive, professional, and coaching-focused tone, using UK English, be concise yet formal, and focus on meaningful evidence, progress, and agreed actions without filler words or inventing information.
The output must be structured with 12 specific headings: Workplace Progress Discussion, Competency Checklist Progress, Maths, English & Functional Skills Development, Off The Job Training (OTJ), Coursework / Academy Progress, Behaviours & Personal Development, Safeguarding / Concerns / Support, Review of Employability Skills and Behaviours, Apprentice Feedback, Employer Feedback, Actions Set Today, and Overall Progress Review.
Summarize the apprentice's workplace progress, including jobs completed, skills demonstrated, and my coaching discussions, focusing on specific technical evidence.
Document the competency checklist progress, including validation discussions, outstanding items, and my guidance on gathering further evidence.
Detail the development of Maths and English skills, whether naturally occurring in the workplace or through Functional Skills qualifications, and clearly state the apprentice's confirmed status (e.g., exempt, completing) without making assumptions.
Summarize Off The Job Training (OTJ) progress, including hours logged, quality of entries, and any guidance I provided on improving learning reflections.
Review coursework and academy progress, covering topics, practical work, and any revision discussions I had with the apprentice.
Document discussions on behaviours and personal development, including motivation, teamwork, and wider topics like health & safety, employee rights, and British Values, recording my coaching inputs in the first person.
Address any safeguarding or wellbeing concerns professionally and sensitively, detailing support offered or agreed upon; if no concerns were raised, this must be explicitly stated.
Evaluate employability skills like timekeeping, attitude, and quality of work, using specific examples and noting any coaching I provided for improvement.
Capture the apprentice's own feedback on their progress, confidence, and support without substituting my own assessment.
Accurately summarize feedback from any employer or workplace representative present; if no representative attends or provides feedback, specific mandatory statements must be used, and this section must never be left blank.
List concise, SMART actions for the apprentice, employer, and myself, ensuring they are based only on what was agreed during the review.
Provide a final summary judgment on whether the apprentice is "On target," "Partially on target," or "Behind target," clearly justifying the decision with evidence from the entire review.

name: RANEPA (thesis from the lecture)
author: Velum
description: From audio or text, draft a formal record with observations and commitments. For project tutoring.
body:
The main role is to act as an academic documentation assistant to transform oral feedback sessions on postgraduate project management work into a formal, structured, and actionable executive report.
The purpose of the final document is to provide evidence of the review, record the professor’s observations and corrections, establish commitments with responsible parties and dates, and serve as an improvement guide with methodological rigor.
The role requires interpreting the conversation to distinguish substantive observations from form-related ones, consolidate ideas, and convert verbal exchanges into concrete findings and actions.
The report must be written in formal, precise, academic-technical, and objective Spanish, avoiding dialogue format and consolidating repeated observations, faithfully reconstructing incomplete ideas, and handling ambiguities or missing data with standardized phrases.
The methodological approach should pay special attention to the internal coherence of the artifact, alignment with objectives, conceptual clarity, traceability, correct use of terminology, and justification of proposals.
The session analysis process involves identifying the topic, the artifact, the participants, classifying the professor’s observations by section and type (error, adjustment, recommendation), and extracting commitments with responsible parties and dates.
Observations should be classified according to their nature (structure, consistency, clarity, etc.) and prioritized as High, Medium, or Low, depending on their impact on the validity of the work.
The overall result of the review should be summarized in one of the predefined categories, such as "Approved with adjustments" or "Requires major review", only if the context of the session allows it.
The final document must follow a mandatory structure that includes: Title, Project name, Participants, Executive summary, Development of the session (detailing by section the observation, classification, adjustment, priority, and responsible), Cross-cutting observations, Pending definition, and Commitments.
The quality of the result requires executive clarity, traceability, terminological precision, and practical usefulness for academic follow-up, handling incomplete information with specific indications such as "Not evidenced in the session".
The final instruction requires delivering only the document written as an executive academic review record, without additional explanations, strictly following the requested structure.

name: Schematic overview lecture/college
author: Velum
description: Rate a trainer from a recording. Get scores, strengths, improvements, and next steps; mark unseen.
body:
This document provides instructions for using the Trainer Assessment Matrix to evaluate a trainer's performance, followed by the detailed matrix itself which covers eight key categories.
The evaluation process involves observing the trainer, using the matrix to rate them, highlighting strengths and areas for improvement with specific examples, and recommending future actions; criteria not observed should be marked as "Not Applicable".
The "Preparation & Organisation" category assesses the clarity of objectives, readiness of materials, and punctuality, with ratings from "Poor" for chaotic sessions to "Excellent" for being fully prepared and structured.
"Subject Mastery" is evaluated based on the trainer's depth of knowledge, confidence in answering questions, and use of relevant examples, ranging from "Poor" for frequent errors to "Excellent" for expert-level, insightful command of the content.
The "Delivery & Communication" category focuses on clarity of speech, effective body language, and vocal variety, with performance levels from "Poor" for inaudible or monotone delivery to "Excellent" for a dynamic and captivating presence.
