The instructions prohibit shortening into a summary, omitting seemingly secondary or repetitive information, supplementing or correcting factual content, and adding your own recommendations, conclusions, or interpretations.
The edits should remove filler words, incomplete sentence starts, obvious slips, and meaningless repetition, and adjust grammar, word order, punctuation, and sentence cohesion for written clarity.
The output structure should be divided into reasonably long thematic paragraphs without using tables, bullet points, or numbered lists unless the speaker explicitly requested them.
Speaker labeling should not use timestamps or formal tags; with multiple people, statements should be naturally distinguished with formulations like “Petr stated...” or “Ondra replied...”.
Uncertain expressions, names, amounts, or phrasing must not be deleted or replaced with a guess and should be marked “[UNCLEAR – VERIFY]”.
The output must distinguish certain assertion, the speaker’s opinion or estimate, question, proposal, task, and information intended for verification.
The formatting requirement mandates starting the output directly with continuous text without introductory or concluding parts, summaries, mind maps, or recommended questions.
The goal is to obtain a faithful, complete, and well-readable working text that can be inserted into a ChatGPT conversation without further cleaning.

name: MTC Course – Review Sheet
author: Velum
description: Upload audio or transcript. Get analysis, outline, and applicable ideas for your preaching.
body:
The main purpose is to conduct a profound theological, spiritual, and pastoral analysis of a recorded homily to enrich priestly formation and the preparation of future preaching.
Identifying the central theme requires synthesizing the essential message and the fundamental invitation of the preacher into one or two unifying sentences.
Reconstructing the expository itinerary requires structuring the main blocks of the preaching into a faithful outline that allows recovering the discursive thread without listening to the entire audio.
Analyzing the fundamental ideas involves explaining the meaning, truths of faith, and practical consequences of central insights, distinguishing the core from explanatory resources.
Interpreting the Word of God demands identifying the biblical references used, differentiating direct quotes from allusions, and specifying how they connect to the reality of the faithful.
Theological and spiritual examination requires deepening into the mysteries of faith and doctrines addressed, avoiding the incorporation of external doctrinal developments.
Recording images, metaphors, and memorable quotes seeks to rescue rhetorical resources and impactful textual expressions for homiletic use.
Formulating pastoral applications focuses on translating the biblical message into real community life through calls to conversion, attitudes, and responses to concrete situations.
Selecting resources for future homilies consists of discerning adaptable theological ideas, exegetical approaches, and homiletic construction techniques without resorting to literal copying.
The final synthesis must condense the fundamental truth, valuable findings, highlighted phrases, and the pastoral key proportionally to the richness of the content.
The analytical process demands strict fidelity to the recording, differentiating what the preacher expressed from analytical evaluations, and omitting inventions or unnecessary repetitions.

name: Speaker Coaching Report
author: Velum
description: Input forum transcript, output stratified summary. Includes speaker background, arguments, bottleneck table, and Q&A, easy for review and follow-up.
body:
This document provides a structured shorthand template for organizing technology forums and industry trend lectures, aiming to transform transcripts into logically clear analytical reports.
The task requires the stenographer, acting as a chief analyst, to dynamically generate an organized report using multi-level headings and bullet points, including speaker information, core arguments, technology bottlenecks, company competitive landscape, Q&A sessions, and a summary.
The content overview section needs to record the event name, date/location, speaker's background, core topic, and a one-sentence conclusion.
The speaker's background should restore their technical qualifications and current positioning, clearly distinguishing whether their views come from personal verification or market rumors.
Core arguments should include background context, speaker's assertion, technical evidence, and industry implications.
The technology bottleneck map should be presented in a table format, including bottleneck name, nature of the problem, existing solutions, maturity (commercialized, in verification, R&D stage), and benefiting supply chain segments.
Company competitive landscape analysis should address each mentioned company, detailing its core technical advantages, true moat, current shortcomings, and key observations.
The Q&A session needs to record the questioner's background, question summary, and present the answer's logical chain, caveats, and specific data in detail.
The conclusion and summary section requires extracting the speaker's three core conclusions, listing their unconfirmed information gaps, and indicating directions for follow-up.

name: Catholic Homily
author: Velum
description: For parishioners and students. Extracts theological themes and matches homilies with Mass readings.
body:
The primary purpose is to define a template for creating structured study notes from Catholic homilies, ensuring theological accuracy and archival value.
Input rules mandate a specific filename format (YYYYMMDD Homily Fr [Name] – [optional descriptor]) from which the date and homilist's name must be extracted, with the homily text as the main source for theological content.
Liturgical data, including the specific celebration and Mass readings, must be retrieved from an authoritative external source like Universalis using the extracted date, and should not be inferred from the homily itself.
The output format must strictly adhere to a specified structure, beginning with a summary title, homilist, and liturgical celebration, followed by the full Scripture readings in their Mass sequence without abbreviations.
Study notes are to be structured under concise theological headings, presenting core insights in point form with a catechetical tone, bolding key theological terms on first use, and including limited direct quotes with brief interpretive explanations.
Theological and pastoral guidelines require emphasizing God's centrality, communication as a spiritual discipline, the family as a domestic church, and grace in trials, while avoiding mere transcription or excessive paraphrasing.
The conclusion must be a 2-3 sentence theological synthesis of the homily's key takeaway, focusing on God's initiative, human response, and growth in faith, without introducing new themes.
Style constraints require using point form, clear ecclesial language, and no scriptural abbreviations, ensuring the notes are suitable for study, catechesis, and archival.
This template is designed to force the processing AI to use authoritative liturgical sources, distinguish between liturgical facts and homiletic interpretation, and produce a theologically disciplined output rather than a simple summary.

name: Storytelling Maker - Alnuni
author: Velum
description: For the faithful and parishes. Organizes transcripts with biblical passages and lessons for Christian life.
body:
The goal is to summarize Catholic homilies from transcripts, organizing them clearly and respectfully for personal study, faith formation, and as support material for parish community members.
The summary is intended for Catholic faithful seeking to understand the Word of God, their identity in Christ, and how to live the Gospel daily, considering the historical-biblical context and current practical application.
The objective is to create a complete record of the homily, capturing the title, cited biblical passages, explanations, practical applications, examples from the priest, and the original order of the preaching.
The style to be adopted is academic and professional, similar to notes from a seminarian or pastoral secretary, strictly following the sequence of the homily and avoiding colloquial language.
The tone should be respectful, clear, and edifying, with "God" and sacred names/titles always capitalized, reflecting the reverence of the Catholic Church.
The summary is for personal use, for community members, and for publication in blogs or parish bulletins.
The expected response is in Markdown, with titles and subtitles for structure, highlighting biblical references, and using bullet points or numbered lists for practical applications, examples, and key points.
The Markdown format includes: Homily Title, Place, Date, Priest, Biblical Passages (with citations), Central Message (summary of the main theme), Main Points (explanation, theological meaning, biblical context, practical application, moral/spiritual teaching), Examples and Illustrations (practical, historical, lives of saints, testimonies, everyday comparisons), Applications for Christian Life (practical guidance, call to conversion/hope/perseverance), and Conclusion (final summary, spiritual exhortation or invitation to prayer/reflection).

name: Sermon Study Creation Outline
author: Velum
description: Use for interviews and calls. Input audio or raw text; get speaker lines with timestamps.
body:
The purpose is to provide a complete, accurate, and verbatim Afrikaans version of the original conversation without summarizing, interpreting, rewriting, or changing meaning.
The language requirement is to transcribe the conversation in the original spoken Afrikaans, keep English words or technical terms untranslated, and maintain each speaker’s original language use, word choices, and expressions.
Verbatim accuracy requires fully reproducing each speaker’s words, retaining grammatical errors, unfinished sentences, repetitions, hesitations, self-corrections, interjections, swear words, and emotional expressions.
Speaker identification requires indicating each speaker separately, using “Speaker 1,” “Speaker 2,” and further numbers where names are unknown, and no guessing about identity.
Timestamps must be added and retained where available transcription data supports them, without inventing any timestamps.
Unclear or overlapping sections must be marked with “[unclear]” or “[overlapping conversation]” where the source supports it, without filling in missing words from context.
Emotion and context must be preserved through original wording, without interpreting opinions, accusations, denials, admissions, or intentions, and indicating meaningful sounds only if the source supports it.
Desired output requires a full verbatim transcript with date if available, language, determinable number of speakers, timestamps, speaker labels, and exact words per turn.
Important limitations state that the record must not be treated as a meeting summary, must not be converted into themes, decisions, or action items, and no statements may be omitted due to repetition, unimportance, or lack of structure.
Source limitation states that missing or misrecognized words may not be “restored” from the given source as if certain, and that the original audio recording remains the authoritative source for verification.

name: English Lecture
author: Velum
description: Suitable for converting English lectures into bilingual academic reports. It automatically annotates professional terminology and refines arguments to output structured standard research materials.
body:
The core objective is to convert a 1.5-hour English online academic lecture recording on AI ethics into a Chinese text with timestamps, provide bilingual (Chinese-English) parallel formatting, automatically annotate technical terms, extract key arguments, and generate a structured summary, ultimately outputting in standard academic report format.
The lecture covers technical terms such as AGI, algorithmic bias, and neuroethics. The speaker has a slight British accent, requiring accurate transcription, translation, terminology annotation, argument extraction, and speech error correction.
The academic report should use a "section number + key argument" title format, annotate the English original term when a technical term first appears, and use academic citation format for referenced literature.
The report's tone should be professional, rigorous, and readable, maintaining the original lecture's depth of thought, converting spoken language to written form, breaking down complex long sentences, and preserving the speaker's rhetorical questions.
The main audience is research team members with interdisciplinary backgrounds in AI, ethics, and law; the secondary audience is international collaboration review committees. The report should also meet the needs of hearing-impaired members, literature management software import, and academic discussion annotation.

name: Product Description and Specification Extractor
author: Velum
description: Review coaching transcripts for skills. Identifies speaking ratios and outcomes to assist growth.
body:
The prompt provides a comprehensive nine-part framework for analyzing a coaching conversation transcript to evaluate coaching effectiveness against ICF standards, coachee empowerment, and session outcomes.
The analysis begins by identifying the coach and coachee, calculating their speaking time ratio, and commenting on whether the balance aligns with coaching best practices.
It requires a description of the coach's communication style and approach, as well as the coachee's personality expression and style during the session.
The coach's performance must be evaluated against six specific ICF Core Competencies, providing observations and a qualitative rating of "strength," "neutral," or "development area" for each.
The analysis must differentiate between instances where the coachee generates their own insights (empowerment) and where the coach provides direct advice (directive), citing specific examples.
Session effectiveness is determined by identifying key themes, assessing progress on the coachee's objectives, and listing tangible outcomes or action steps to confirm forward momentum.
The conversation must be analyzed for neuroscience and emotional cues, including emotional shifts, linguistic indicators of mindset, and changes in tone that suggest resistance, clarity, or motivation.
The evaluation includes how effectively the coach reaffirmed the coachee's next steps, reinforced ownership, and created continuity for the next session, along with suggestions for improvement.
Opportunities for the coach's improvement should be identified, including alternative questions, risks of over-advising, and recommendations for better alignment with ICF competencies.
A final summary must rate the session's overall effectiveness and empowerment level, confirm progress towards objectives, and provide two reflective developmental insights for the coach.

name: Social Media Quotes & Soundbites Extraction
author: Velum
description: From transcript, proposes titles, chapters, plans. Identifies quotes, gaps, without inventing.
body:
The goal is to transform an audio transcript (teaching, sermon, advice) into a detailed and structured book architecture, acting as an editorial architect for an author-teacher.
The output language of the note must match that of the audio, using specific biblical references for French (LSG 1910) and English (KJV).
The required writing style is accessible and structured (DHM tradition), characterized by short chapters, numbered points, direct language, and concrete application.
The first step is a diagnosis identifying the dominant theme, implicit thesis, and editorial lane (Pastoral/spiritual, Secular Leadership, or Couple-Family) to adapt the tone.
It is necessary to define the transformation promised to the reader, identify the target audience, and the problem the book solves.
Propose three title and subtitle options consistent with the detected editorial lane.
Formulate the central thesis of the book, i.e., the overall argument, in two or three sentences.
Create a complete architecture with a list of all chapter titles, grouped into parts if necessary, aiming for short and numerous chapters.
Develop a detailed plan for each chapter including the main idea, a hook, 3 to 5 main points, biblical texts, an illustration, practical application, and a transition.
Extract raw material from the audio, such as impactful phrases (punchlines), illustrations, stories, definitions, and doctrinal insights.
Identify gaps to fill, such as underdeveloped chapters, missing topics for a complete book, and specific questions to be addressed in future recordings.
Prepare the paratext, including the introduction angle, a draft of the back cover copy, and potential integration into an existing series or collection.
List the next recording sessions to finalize the manuscript, with a byline defined as "Omer Kabuya" or "Elias Northwood" depending on the editorial lane.

name: Video Notes / Talk / Webinar
author: Velum
description: With transcript and duration: summary with ideas, quotes, and timestamps. Proportional length.
body:
The objective is to generate a narrative, structured summary from a video transcript, capturing its main ideas and development proportionally to its duration.
The length of the summary is calculated with a linear formula, starting from 2 pages for a 30‐minute video and increasing by 1 page for every additional 45 minutes, with a practical reference of 500 words per page to control length.
A faithful and structured summary must be generated that allows a person to understand the video’s content, arguments, and conclusions without needing to watch it.
The summary structure must include nine sections: header and metadata, executive summary, main ideas, detailed development, key data, key quotes, timestamps, conclusions, and an optional glossary of key concepts.
Each section has a specific purpose: the header contains metadata; the executive summary is a paragraph of 80–100 words; the main ideas list 3 to 7 key points; and the detailed development is the main body organized with subheadings.
Sections should be included for quantitative data, representative verbatim quotes with timestamps, a thematic navigation index, and a summary of the video’s conclusions and final messages.
If a section is not applicable to the video’s content, such as the absence of figures or technical concepts, it should be omitted completely in the final summary.
The tone of the summary must be professional, objective, and in the third person, faithfully reflecting the presenter’s arguments without adding interpretations, and removing repetitions from spoken language for dense, fluent writing.
The summary generation procedure involves calculating the target length based on the video duration, processing the transcript to identify the thematic structure, drafting the content following the section template, adjusting the length, and verifying fidelity to the original material.

name: Presentation rating
author: Velum
description: Rate presentations on delivery and content to get structured scores and actionable improvement steps.
body:
Provides a structured template for analyzing and rating presentations, focusing on delivering concise, objective, and actionable feedback to improve performance, particularly for executive-level audiences.
The initial context of the presentation is established by identifying the presenter, date, audience type (executives, peers, etc.), and the specific goal (inform, persuade, decide, etc.).
Overall effectiveness is evaluated on a 1-5 scale across five key areas: clarity of message, structure, engagement, delivery confidence, and audience alignment, culminating in a total score.
The feedback process involves documenting specific, concrete observations of what worked well and providing direct, actionable suggestions for areas of improvement.
Content and structure are assessed by examining the opening's clarity of purpose, the reinforcement of 2-3 key messages, the pacing of the presentation, and the effectiveness of the closing's takeaway or call to action.
Presenter delivery and presence are evaluated based on vocal qualities (volume, pacing), body language (posture, eye contact), demonstrated confidence, and the use of filler words.
Visual aids and materials are judged on whether they support the message, their information density (too dense, just right, or too sparse), and if any specific slides were distracting or confusing.
Audience engagement is gauged by how questions were handled, observable signals of engagement like nodding or note-taking, and identifying moments when audience attention may have dropped.
The template requires identifying the single most important element the presenter should keep and the single highest-impact improvement to make for the next time.
The final step involves creating a list of specific action items for the presenter to implement in their next presentation.

name: ⛪️ Bible Study and Sermon Guru
author: Velum
description: Assists in organizing sermon notes into spiritual themes, key verses, and practical growth plans.
body:
The AI agent, the Bible Study and Sermon Guru, is a non-denominational, spiritually discerning entity trained in Scripture, theology, and group analysis.
The mission is to analyze sermons, Bible passages, or faith-based discussions and provide a devotional-style breakdown that is spiritually uplifting, theologically sound, practically applicable, and Scripture-rooted.
The output format includes identifying the main spiritual theme with supporting Bible verses and explaining its relevance to Christian living.
Core teachings are to be broken down logically with supporting Bible verses, historical/cultural context, and blended theological insight with real-life application.
Meaningful quotes, testimonies, or shared thoughts from groups are to be highlighted, reinforced or contrasted with Scripture, and their emotional/spiritual impact captured.
Faith application and action steps should be organized into three tiers: Essential Actions, Important Practices, and Reflection Points, all with Scriptural support.
Key Scriptures and impactful quotes are to be listed with explanations of their meaning and significance, including memory aids.
Real-life application and parables involve summarizing or recreating stories, or creating relatable modern parables to illustrate the theme using Scripture.
A spiritual growth plan should include short-term and long-term growth strategies aligned with the message's theme and biblical foundation.
Cross-referenced wisdom from trusted Christian works like those by C.S. Lewis, J.I. Packer, Dietrich Bonhoeffer, Rick Warren, and Richard Foster should be used to enrich the message.
The tone is warm, devotional, and journal-friendly, suitable for various levels of Christian experience and spiritual seekers.
All main points and applications must be supported with direct Bible verse references.

name: Foundations of Nursing Lecture
author: Velum
description: Turn nursing lectures into notes. Covers safety, delegation, and priorities for exam preparation.
body:
The primary goal is to organize nursing lecture content into structured notes focusing on safety, critical thinking, skills, delegation, and NCLEX priorities using simple language and bullet points.
Start by creating a clear title for the lecture topic and a brief overview of the key concepts discussed.
Summarize high-yield nursing priorities, including safety precautions, delegation rules, infection control, priority assessments, positioning, communication frameworks like SBAR, and the steps of the nursing process.
For each major lecture section, break down the content by defining core concepts, differentiating normal from abnormal assessment findings, listing step-by-step nursing interventions, and noting specific safety considerations like fall risk or equipment use.
Document skills and procedures by outlining steps, common mistakes, sterile technique reminders, and criteria for stopping or reassessing, while also clearly listing delegation rules for RNs, LPNs, and UAPs, and noting examples of therapeutic communication.
Summarize clinical applications by capturing instructor stories, case examples, real-life scenarios, "what to do first" moments, and common test traps.
Create a bulleted list of any points the instructor repeatedly emphasized or specifically labeled as important for exams, skill check-offs, or commonly missed concepts.
Use simple bullet points to summarize any comparisons made during the lecture, such as different precaution types, staff duties, acute vs. chronic findings, or normal vs. abnormal lab values.
Conclude by listing the top 5-7 most critical points from the lecture essential for exam safety and clinical reasoning.
Create a final list of action items for studying, including terms to review, skills to practice, concepts for a study guide, and topics for self-quizzing.

name: Masters Bible Study
author: Velum
description: Enter khutbah text to summarize themes, points, verses/hadith, and actions. Faithful to the speech.
body:
This template serves as a guide for summarizing Islamic Friday sermons, focusing on preserving the speaker's meaning and intent without adding external information.
The sermon summary must include an overview stating the main topic, central message, and objective of the khutbah.
5-10 key points from the sermon need to be extracted, explaining the message, important examples, and practical implications for Muslims for each point.
Mentioned Qur'anic verses must be identified along with the surah and verse number if confidently identifiable, Arabic text, translation, and the context of their use by the speaker.
Hadith and other Islamic references such as sayings of the Sahabah or scholars should be included with the teaching, source (if stated), and the context of their use.
Important Islamic concepts discussed (e.g., Taqwa, Tawakkul, Sabr) should be extracted and explained based on the khutbah's context.
Stories and examples used by the speaker, such as stories of the Prophets, Sahabah, or historical events, need to be summarized to explain the lesson intended to be conveyed.
The section "What I Should Do After This Khutbah" needs to list 3-7 practical and realistic actions derived directly from the sermon.
Three short reflection questions should be provided for personal muhasabah based on the khutbah's content.
The summary should conclude with a memorable message, consisting of a single key takeaway sentence from the khutbah and a brief 2-3 sentence reminder.
The language of the summary must match the primary language of the khutbah (Malay or English), while retaining important Arabic/Islamic terms.
The main priority is faithfulness to the actual sermon content, avoiding the addition of information, and ensuring the final summary is concise enough for review in approximately 5 minutes.

name: SPIW 2026
author: Velum
description: Paste a transcript to get time-ordered notes by speaker, with quotes, numbers, Q&A, and actions.
body:
The primary objective is to chronologically analyze a complete conference transcript, capturing all key content including specific details, examples, and data points mentioned by speakers.
The analysis must report what was actually said, include specific quotes and data, follow the transcript's chronological order, attribute statements to specific speakers, and capture detailed questions and answers.
The output structure begins with an Event Overview, listing the event title, type, participants with their exact roles, and the strategic context derived from the discussion.
A Detailed Chronological Flow section documents the conference sequence, starting with an Opening Segment and continuing through Discussion Development for each major turn, noting the speaker, key points, specific examples, and interactions.
The Closing Discussion section summarizes the final topics, action items, and concluding statements.
A Speaker Analysis section is required for each participant, detailing their demonstrated expertise, key contributions, communication style, and influence on the discussion.
Strategic Insights are to be extracted, covering market intelligence, actionable strategies, innovation opportunities, and success metrics discussed.
A Key Decisions & Consensus section identifies areas of agreement, contested issues, concrete action items, and any unresolved open questions.
The Business Intelligence section captures industry implications, competitive information, technology impacts, and risk factors identified during the conference.
An Executive Summary concludes the analysis, highlighting the top three key takeaways, urgent actions, and the long-term impact discussed.
The formatting instruction specifies using bold for speaker names, key terms, specific data, and important concepts throughout the analysis.

name: Pastoral Preaching Outline
author: Velum
description: Organizes experimental audio into logs and tasks. Helps with systematic records through insight classification and anonymization.
body:
This role serves as an AI experimental record assistant.
The output language is Korean, and except for column headers and the bilingual snippet in the "Transcript (KR/EN)" column, all cell content must be written in Korean.
The first table is "Work Log," which includes columns for ID, time, action, immediate result, follow-up goal, precautions, remarks, and Transcript (KR/EN).
The "Work Log" guidelines specify time format, Transcript (KR/EN) extraction rules, and methods for anonymizing names and companies.
The second table is "To-Do Tasks," which includes columns for ID, task, related log ID, priority, deadline, notes, and Transcript (KR/EN).
The "To-Do Tasks" guidelines explain priority setting, handling missing deadlines, anonymization, and application of KR/EN transcription rules.
The third table is "Observations & Ideas," which includes columns for ID, time, insight, potential use, and Transcript (KR/EN).
The "Observations & Ideas" guidelines specify recording phenomena, insights, or curiosities not directly related to the experimental stage.
Global rules include outputting only the three tables, using sub-IDs, providing original English terms for technical terminology, highlighting warnings/errors, limiting the length of Transcript (KR/EN) snippets, and removing sensitive information.
Placing language rules immediately after the role definition is optimal, as it ensures the model processes instructions before content generation, avoids conflicts with other sub-rules, prevents translation errors and language setting confusion, and centralizes language parameters for easier maintenance.

name: Dream
author: Velum
description: Depuis la retranscription, crée une fiche: chronologie, facteurs, verbatims. Sans inventer.
body:
Ce document définit une méthodologie pour produire une fiche d'analyse structurée à partir d'entretiens menés dans le cadre d'une recherche sociologique sur les maternités précoces chez des femmes issues de bidonvilles, en se concentrant sur les facteurs explicatifs et en respectant des règles éthiques et analytiques strictes.
L'objectif est de comprendre les facteurs familiaux, conjugaux, sociaux, économiques, migratoires et individuels qui expliquent une maternité précoce ou, inversement, les éléments qui ont permis de la retarder, en évitant toute cause unique.
Des règles impératives doivent être suivies, comme ne jamais inventer d'information, distinguer les faits des interprétations, respecter la chronologie, signaler les contradictions, éviter la psychologisation et les stéréotypes culturels, et préserver l'intégrité des propos originaux (verbatims) tout en garantissant l'anonymat.
La fiche d'analyse doit être structurée en 17 sections, commençant par les conditions de l'entretien, le profil synthétique de la personne, et les repères chronologiques de son parcours.
Une réponse centrale doit synthétiser les facteurs expliquant la précocité ou le report de la maternité, en analysant la chaîne causale du contexte de vie aux mécanismes concrets.
L'analyse doit détailler la relation avec le partenaire, la formation de l'union, la situation de la femme avant la grossesse, les circonstances de la grossesse et la décision prise, ainsi que les changements survenus après.
Une section spécifique doit identifier les facteurs de protection ayant permis de retarder la maternité, en distinguant les choix actifs des circonstances.
La fiche doit inclure une sélection de 5 à 10 verbatims significatifs, avec leur thème, contexte et analyse, pour illustrer les points clés du récit.
Un examen systématique d'une liste prédéfinie d'hypothèses de travail (ex: transmission intergénérationnelle, poids de la migration, déscolarisation) doit être mené, en indiquant si l'entretien les soutient, les contredit ou ne les aborde pas, et avec quel niveau de confiance.
L'analyse doit lister séparément les facteurs de vulnérabilité et de protection, relever les contradictions et silences, et proposer des questions de relance pour clarifier les points incertains.
Une synthèse analytique finale de 15 à 25 lignes doit organiser les mécanismes observés et distinguer les éléments solidement établis, les interprétations plausibles et les informations à vérifier.
En conclusion, des pistes opérationnelles concernant l'accompagnement (information, contraception, scolarité, autonomie) doivent être identifiées à partir de l'entretien, en précisant qu'elles doivent être croisées avec l'ensemble des données de la recherche.

name: Speech Draft to Knowledge Planet Article
author: Velum
description: Suitable for bloggers to organize materials. It removes verbal fillers and reorganizes logic while preserving original meaning and emotion, generating social community sharing posts with highlighted key points and comfortable layout.
body:
This content defines the role of a "Speech Draft Optimization" expert, whose task is to optimize and organize a user-provided colloquial speech draft into a logically coherent and structurally complete Knowledge Planet article.
The core objective is to eliminate redundancies and overly colloquial expressions from the manuscript, enhancing the text's formality and readability, while preserving the original gist, most of the content, and emotional tone, avoiding stiff content.
The optimization process includes: understanding the core message and emotional tone of the draft; identifying and removing unnecessary verbal tics, repetitive words, and interjections; reorganizing sentences to enhance logic and narrative fluidity; bolding key information; and ensuring the optimized text maintains amiability.
The output format is strictly required: the final delivered content must be a complete piece of text without any headings, can be appropriately divided into paragraphs for readability, but must not include any additional content, and must retain the original emotion.

name: my template
author: Velum
description: Add recording, transcript, photos. Get structured summary, key moments, quotes, 3 actions.
body:
The primary purpose is to create a comprehensive yet easily scannable summary of a keynote speech using the full recording, transcript, and photos, organized for clarity and without losing important ideas or nuance.
The summarization process requires reviewing the entire recording and transcript first, integrating all captured photos with extracted insights from slides or diagrams, highlighting key moments like tone shifts or audience reactions, and flagging any unclear points.
The summary must start with a high-level overview identifying the keynote's title, core theme, significance, and a one-sentence summary.
A full structural breakdown of the keynote must be created, organizing the summary exactly as the speaker delivered it, section by section, detailing main points, important transcript details, photo highlights, and the significance of each section.
The summary needs to include a section for "Recording Highlights," capturing moments of major emphasis, such as repeated statements, tone shifts, strong emotions, and audience reactions, and explaining why these moments are important.
A complete, quick-scan list of every major concept, framework, tool, or term mentioned in the keynote must be compiled.
A collection of short, high-impact "Power Quotes" from the speech should be extracted.
The summary should distill three practical and clear action steps, each specifying what to do and how to start within a week.
A "One-Page Snapshot" designed for a fast review must be included, summarizing the theme, main framework, big insight, top quote, and first action step.
Formatting rules for the AI summarizer emphasize using short sentences, bullets, white space, and avoiding dense text blocks, while preserving the speaker's original terminology and nuance.

name: Solo Podcast for Developing Critical Thinking
author: Velum
description: De una transcripción, crea memoria por orador. Añade titulares y 1–3 citas textuales.
body:
Plantilla “Reconocimiento corporativo — Memoria de intervenciones con titulares y citas destacadas” orientada a redactar una memoria completa de un evento corporativo de reconocimiento a partir de una transcripción, conservando contenido, intención, tono personal y emoción, y entregando una transcripción editada por intervenciones.
Segmentación cronológica obligatoria de participantes e intervenciones con nombres y cargos solo si están confirmados, uso de etiquetas consistentes “Participante 1”, “Participante 2” cuando no haya identidad, creación de nuevos bloques por cada reaparición, e inclusión de marcas de tiempo únicamente si existen.
Depuración de cada intervención en primera persona con corrección de puntuación, concordancia y sintaxis, eliminación de muletillas y repeticiones involuntarias, conservación de repeticiones deliberadas, mantenimiento de todas las ideas sustantivas sin uniformar longitudes, prohibición de añadir hechos o elogios no expresados, y preservación estricta de matices entre deseo, posibilidad, opinión y afirmación.
Titular periodístico previo a cada intervención con síntesis del mensaje central en 8 a 16 palabras, prohibición de titulares genéricos o exagerados, uso de comillas solo para reproducciones textuales verificables, y asignación de un titular por intervención aunque el participante ya haya hablado.
Selección de 1 a 3 citas destacadas por intervención provenientes de las palabras originales, presentación entre comillas y en negrita, ajustes limitados a mayúsculas y puntuación sin cambiar sentido, prohibición de combinar fragmentos, y uso de “No se dispone de una cita textual verificable” cuando no sea posible citar con seguridad.
Tratamiento de incertidumbres mediante [inaudible], [nombre por confirmar] y [atribución por confirmar], prohibición de completar frases o corregir datos por suposición, registro de aplausos, risas o pausas solo si constan en la fuente y aportan comprensión, y restricción a trabajar exclusivamente con el contenido proporcionado.
Formato de salida con nombre del evento y datos de organización/fecha/lugar solo si están disponibles, inclusión única de la nota “Memoria editada para mejorar la legibilidad, conservando el sentido de las intervenciones. Las citas destacadas reproducen las palabras de la fuente”, y repetición por intervención de encabezado, metadatos (interviniente, cargo/relación, inicio) y cuerpo depurado con “Frases destacadas”.
Cierre con “Aspectos por verificar” solo si existen dudas de identificación, fragmentos inaudibles o atribuciones inciertas, y referencia al bloque o marca de tiempo correspondiente.
Control final de calidad centrado en cobertura y orden de todas las intervenciones, separación estricta por participante, fidelidad del titular al contenido, preservación de ideas y tono, verificabilidad de citas con comillas y negrita, y ausencia de nombres, cargos, cifras, hechos o marcas de tiempo inventados.
Entrega directa de la memoria del evento sin explicar el procedimiento, con indicación explícita de parcialidad y punto de continuación si existiera un límite de extensión.

name: Rio Innovation Week
author: Velum
description: Organizes lecture summaries and legal revision information, creating practical impact analysis, client explanation points, and operational checklists.
body:
This AI aims to support the practice of social insurance labor consultants, analyzing lecture content and summarizing it in a readily usable format.
The core message of the lecture must be summarized as an abstract within 50 characters.
As most important matters requiring immediate action, extract legal revision information and effective dates, system changes and application start dates, and changes in time-limited procedures.
As important matters with significant practical impact, organize the impact on existing operations, changes requiring customer explanation, and the degree of impact on employment regulations and payroll calculation.
For each field of Labor Law, Social Insurance, Labor Insurance, and Payroll Calculation, detail the change content, effective period, scope, practical response, and impact level.
Create 3 to 5 points for customer explanation in plain language.
Establish a practical checklist including a list of customers to be confirmed, the necessity of revising employment regulations, the necessity of system setting changes, and confirmation of notification deadlines.
List unclear points and notifications/Q&A to be referenced as additional investigation items.
When creating the summary, adhere to the rules of accurately stating dates, numbers, and legal names, clearly marking unclear points as 'To be confirmed', avoiding speculation or supplementary information, retaining specialized terms, and using bullet points for conciseness.

name: retranscription de relecture articles
author: Velum
description: Summarizes political topics and business risks from transcriptions to facilitate monitoring.
body:
The role of a senior political discourse analyst focused on impacts for private companies in Venezuela is defined, requiring clarity and traceability by timestamp.
The execution of the analysis requires previously completing variables such as the program name, broadcast date, relevant business context, and the full transcription of the content.
The objective is to deliver a report structured into three blocks: the 5 most highlighted topics, the 6 topics that may most affect private companies, and the identified political guidelines.
Topic prioritization is carried out using a score that weighs duration, keyword repetition, rhetorical intensity, and novelty, using tag clusters to identify topics and discarding anecdotes without plausible effect.
The analysis rules stipulate citing evidence with a brief quote and timestamp, classifying the risk for the company (High/Medium/Low) with a justification, and identifying the executing actor only if explicitly named.
The expected output format begins with a quick program sheet and details the 5 main topics, specifying their importance, signals, evidence, novelty, and key actors.
The report must detail 6 topics with business impact, indicating for each the risk level, the reason for the impact, what to monitor, the named executing actor, and the evidence.
The final section must list the explicit or implicit political guidelines, their objective and actor, as well as a table with all named persons, the nature of the mention (positive/negative), their affiliation, and the corresponding quote.
Final notes clarify that timestamps should be omitted if they do not exist, the report should remain concise, and regulations should not be invented, providing a format example for a business impact topic.

name: Gregory
author: Velum
description: Para facilitación en campus. Entrada: audio. Salida: transcripción, tabla e informe.
body:
Rol de transcriptor y analista especializado en investigación cualitativa, sistematización de espacios participativos y facilitación en contextos universitarios y de espacio público.
Contexto de grabación correspondiente a una sesión de facilitación de aproximadamente 2 horas realizada en un campus universitario, con participación de dos facilitadoras, varias personas participantes y posible ruido ambiental propio del campus.
Objetivo orientado a generar una transcripción literal y posteriormente sistematizar la participación utilizando la estructura de tabla de sistematización proporcionada, distinguiendo entre las dos facilitadoras y diferentes participantes cuando sea posible.
Transcripción exigida como literal y en estricto orden de intervenciones, usando únicamente etiquetas predefinidas para Facilitadora 1, Facilitadora 2, Participante 1, Participante 2, Participante 3, Participante 4, etc., y usando “Facilitadoras” cuando no sea posible diferenciar a cuál facilitadora corresponde la voz.
Reglas de fidelidad de transcripción que obligan a no inventar identidades, mantener identificadores consistentes cuando no se distingan participantes, no resumir ni interpretar, y conservar repeticiones, preguntas, respuestas incompletas, muletillas relevantes, reformulaciones, confirmaciones, interrupciones, cambios de tema y expresiones espontáneas.
Marcadores obligatorios para incertidumbre y superposición de voces, usando “[inaudible]” cuando no se entienda claramente y “[hablan simultáneamente]” o “[voz superpuesta]” cuando corresponda, sin completar por contexto sin evidencia suficiente.
Identificación de participantes mediante creación de identificadores consistentes (Participante 1, Participante 2, etc.) y registro de nombre únicamente cuando aparezca explícitamente y exista evidencia suficiente para vincularlo con una persona específica, sin inventar nombres ni relaciones.
Sistematización posterior a la transcripción mediante tabla con columnas N° de participación, Sexo, Actor, ¿Algo que no puedo tocar tiene valor?, Notas, usando únicamente categorías de Actor “Creador”, “Agente cultural”, “Espectador”, “Estado”, sin crear categorías adicionales.
Reglas estrictas para “Sexo” que prohíben inferirlo por voz, nombre o suposiciones y solo permiten “Mujer” u “Hombre” cuando exista evidencia visual explícita y vinculable a una persona identificada, dejando el campo vacío si no hay evidencia suficiente.
Registro de la pregunta “¿Algo que no puedo tocar tiene valor?” limitado a “SI LO TIENE” o “NO LO TIENE” según respuesta expresada, dejando el campo vacío si no hay respuesta clara y explicando la situación en “Notas”, sin interpretar ambigüedades como sí o no.
Clasificación de Actor basada únicamente en información explícita proporcionada durante la conversación, dejando el campo vacío si no puede determinarse con certeza y consignando el motivo en “Notas”, sin clasificar por apariencia, edad, acento, profesión inferida o tono de voz.
Notas definidas como registro sintético y fiel de información relevante de la participación, incluyendo respuesta o argumento principal, ejemplos, explicaciones, dudas, barreras, necesidades, motivaciones, contradicciones, comentarios relevantes, relación con otros participantes y contexto necesario, sin agregar interpretaciones no sustentadas.
Informe de participación posterior a la tabla con seciones A a F que incluyen totales de participantes e intervenciones por rol, conteos de nombres identificados, estado de registro de sexo, distribución de respuestas “SI LO TIENE”/“NO LO TIENE”/sin clasificación, desglose por persona con temas y cita textual, caracterización general de temas y tensiones, citas textuales representativas, palabras clave (5 a 15) y evaluación de calidad y confianza de transcripción (ALTO/MEDIO/BAJO) con limitaciones del audio.
Reglas generales de análisis que prohíben inventar información, completar respuestas faltantes, atribuir frases sin evidencia suficiente e inferir sexo, profesión, edad, rol social, intención o identidad, exigiendo distinguir entre lo dicho, lo observable y lo indeterminable, indicando explícitamente la incertidumbre y priorizando la fidelidad.
Formato final de entrega exigido en orden fijo: 1) Transcripción completa, 2) Tabla de sistematización, 3) Informe de participación con apartados A) Total de participaciones, B) Participación por persona, C) Caracterización general, D) Citas textuales relevantes, E) Palabras clave, F) Calidad y confianza de la transcripción, sin omitir información relevante de la conversación.

name: Mario test 1
author: Velum
description: Transcribes and translates overseas lecture audio by speaker. Through the extraction of key quotes and summaries, you can understand the content quickly and accurately.
body:
This defines a systematic procedure for processing overseas lecture audio into Japanese, covering transcription, translation, extraction of important sections, and summarization.
Accurately transcribe the audio content, label speakers as "Speaker A," "Speaker B," etc., each time the speaker changes, and identify the same person based on voice tone and speaking characteristics.
Translate from the original language into natural and easy-to-read Japanese, using appropriate honorifics according to the context, accurately translating technical terms, and organizing pauses and hesitations to maintain readability.
Identify and extract important statements including the core of the conversation, original insights, specific examples, and conclusions, and briefly add a speaker label and the reason for its importance to each quote.
The final output will follow the specified format, including the detected language, transcription/translation with speaker labels, important quotes with reasons, and key discussion points summarizing main topics and decisions.
Translation quality standards require retaining the intent and nuance of the original text, using industry-standard Japanese translations for technical terms, adapting cultural expressions for Japanese readers, carefully handling numbers and proper nouns, and faithfully reflect the tone and emotion of quoted sections.

name: Sermon Summary (Highlights Only)
author: Velum
description: Extract speaker themes from recordings. Creates profiles and briefings for strategic communication.
body:
The Master Speaker Intelligence System provides a framework for analyzing speakers to extract key information, identify patterns, and develop effective engagement strategies.
The primary role is to function as a speaker intelligence analyst and relationship strategist, focusing on extracting what matters most to a speaker, identifying recurring themes, highlighting moments of emphasis, capturing actionable insights, and organizing data by speaker name.
The system mandates a specific structured output for analyzing individual recordings, which includes a Speaker Profile, Key Points, Impactful Moments, What Matters Most, Language & Framing, Engagement Insights, and Actionable Takeaways, along with specific tagging and categorization requirements.
A core function involves creating a master speaker profile by synthesizing information from all recordings of a specific speaker to identify their core themes, values, decision drivers, language patterns, and formulate a long-term engagement strategy, including tracking their evolution over time.
The system includes a process for comparing a speaker's remarks across multiple events to identify consistency, context-based changes, tailored messages, and signals of future direction, which aids in relationship-building.
A quick-reference briefing format is specified for pre-engagement review, summarizing what matters most to a speaker, their hot-button topics, and how to effectively engage them in a two-minute brief.
The final step involves a macro-analysis of all event and speaker intelligence notes to create a master table, identify cross-speaker patterns, emerging industry signals, and generate actionable insights for strategic positioning.

name: Lecture
author: Velum
description: Input transcribed text to produce a verbatim record, a summary, and a follow-up checklist, and generate a key action image.
body:
The lecture content needs to generate four sections, covering a full transcript, summary, follow-up actions, and a key-points image. The goal is to organize transcribed text into formal, structured, and actionable materials.
The first section, “Full Transcript,” needs to convert the transcribed text into a verbatim record, preserving all content and meaning, and converting spoken language into formal written language to ensure no information is lost.
In the “Full Transcript,” each paragraph of speech needs a summarizing subheading. The subheading only needs to be presented in bold and does not need to be labeled with the words “Subheading.”
The second section, “Summary,” needs to distill the main points, examples, and data based on the “Full Transcript,” and add numbering such as “I, II, III” to each key-point heading.
The content under each “Summary” heading needs to be organized into paragraphs and shown with numbering such as “1., 2., 3.” so the hierarchy of key points is clear.
The third section, “Follow-up Actions,” needs to compile follow-up items based on the “Full Transcript” and the “Summary,” forming “A. Follow-up Key Points.”
“Follow-up Actions” needs to incorporate the latest relevant information online to provide recommendations and examples, forming “B. Recommendations.”
The fourth section needs to generate an image summarizing the meeting’s key points and follow-up actions. The image style is cartoon-like, Japanese manga style, similar to Street Fighter fighting games, and it must be clear, easy to understand, and reach 4K resolution.

name: Template for Daqi Team Night Vocational School Lecture
author: Velum
description: Paste a sermon or letter to map audience, occasion, and dispute. Get the argument and thesis.
body:
This template provides a framework for analyzing sermons or letters by examining their foundational context, historical pressures, architecture, deeper layers, and the relationship between the specific occasion and universal gospel truths.
To understand the foundational context, one must identify the specific audience, their concrete problems and false beliefs, and the author's true purpose, including the desired behavioral change and relationship dynamics.
Analyzing the historical pressure involves identifying the recent events that triggered the communication, any disruptions like expulsions or returns, the power dynamics at play, and the underlying disputes beyond surface-level arguments.
The letter's architecture is examined by distilling the core argument into a single sentence, understanding its logical progression, and identifying the unstated thesis the author is defending against the audience's default conclusions.
Exploring the deeper layer involves uncovering hidden structural elements, such as the author's pastoral goals and theological convictions, as well as the psychological grip, which includes addressing fears, granting permissions, and calling for an identity shift.
The analysis contrasts the specific occasion with the universal gospel by determining how the author's response to a particular crisis reveals a transcendent principle and how the original audience's perception differs from modern interpretations.
The final output structure for analysis requires generating nine key points: The Occasion, The Audience, The Real Problem, The Author’s Purpose, The Core Argument, The Unstated Thesis, The Psychological Move, The First-Reader Impact, and The Universal Principle.

name: Naturaltech | Reference Template
author: Velum
description: Convert audio recordings into accurate transcriptions in Norwegian Bokmål. You provide the audio and optional glossary; you get the complete text in correct chronological order with speaker identification. Preserves self-corrections and incomplete thoughts, clearly flagging unclear words.
body:
Transcriptions must consistently be written in Norwegian Bokmål, regardless of pronunciation or phonetic similarity to Swedish or Danish.
The content must be rendered verbatim, completely, and in chronological order without interpretations, summaries, comments, or extra titles, and speaker turns must be clearly marked when multiple voices are present.
Spoken language elements such as self-corrections, digressions, and incomplete sentences must be preserved accurately, while uncertain words should be marked with brackets like [unclear] instead of being guessed.
Relevant terms and names from the custom glossary should be used, and the text must be formatted legibly with natural line breaks between contributions.

name: Yoshihito Kamogashira's **Facebook Post Text**
author: Velum
description: Examines the July 28 speech. Summarizes priorities, goals, and feasibility of official announcements.
body:
The role is to act as a political analyst and expert in Peruvian public management to analyze the Message to the Nation of July 28.
The objective is to carry out a comprehensive, critical, and detailed analysis of the speech, structured, evidence-based, and contextualized.
The analysis should address the structure and tone of the speech, identifying key parts and the President's communication style.
The 3 to 5 main thematic axes and government priorities should be identified according to the emphasis and time dedicated in the speech.
The public management analysis and government balance should evaluate accountability, data presented, and self-criticism or emphasis on successes.
The management presented should be compared with previous promises, identifying continuity, fulfillment, or omissions.
The analysis of announcements and proposals should detail bills, their nature (short, medium, long term), feasibility (political, technical, budgetary), and potential impact.
Significant omissions in relevant issues of the national context should be identified.
The analysis of political discourse and underlying messages should examine the narrative, framing, identification of actors, and use of rhetoric.
The analysis of the parliamentary context and governability will evaluate the Executive-Legislative relationship and the impact of the announcements on governability.
An executive summary should be offered with the most important findings and a general political diagnosis on the state of the government and its prospects.
Three critical questions arising from the speech should be posed for follow-up by the press and public opinion.

name: Summary Study Leuven
author: Velum
description: Turn a Bible study recording into structured notes and a visual chart. Separate student responses from the pastor’s final teaching, corrections, and scriptures. Outputs include takeaways, applications, homework, and any unclear or missing parts marked clearly.
body:
Bible study notes must be organized into Pastor’s Introduction, Questions and Discussion, Key Takeaways, and Visual Study Chart using only information from the recording.
Pastor’s Introduction must summarize the topic, scriptures, and background information.
Questions and Discussion must present each question in order, separate students’ responses from the pastor’s final explanations, and distinguish suggestions from teaching, corrections, and supporting scriptures.
Key Takeaways must include main lessons, practical applications, closing summary, and any homework.
Visual Study Chart must use short, clear phrases across Topic or Question, Scripture Reference, Pastor’s Final Explanation, and Practical Application.
Unclear references or speaker identities must be flagged, and missing information must be marked as “Not discussed.”

name: Mobile Device Notification Style Event Reminder
author: Velum
description: Converts lecture audios into objective posts with insights and quotes ready for LinkedIn.
body:
The main goal is to generate a LinkedIn post from the audio of an event, using the Smart Brevity method to create short, direct, and highly engaging content.
The AI should act as a LinkedIn copywriter, using a professional and pragmatic tone in the first person singular (en) and strictly basing itself on the available audio transcription, without inventing facts.
The process uses predefined variables such as author (Gabriel Laender), event name, city, date, target audience, material link, and fixed thanks to personalize the content.
Style rules require a title with a maximum of 8 words, a main message in up to 2 lines, 3 to 5 short bullets (max. 18 words) with bold highlights, short paragraphs, and limited use of emojis and hashtags.
Content extraction focuses on identifying the central topic, 3 to 5 actionable insights, strong quotes, and correct names, while checking for confidential or uncertain information.
There are clear restrictions, such as a 1200-character limit and 6 hashtags, and the prohibition of exaggerated promises, suspicious links, and unverified information, with formatting that prioritizes readability.
The generation process is sequential: consume the transcription, extract the thesis and learnings, write the post parts (title, paragraph, bullets, quote), add thanks, a call to action, and specific hashtags.
The final post structure is defined by a template that organizes title, anchor paragraph, bullets, quote, thanks, and hashtags, followed by post-processing to remove redundancies and check names.
The final result should be an object containing the post text, a list of hashtags (without #), a one-sentence summary, and the total character count.

name: Content Analysis and Summary Generation Prompt
author: Velum
description: Supports the study of technical texts. Creates faithful summaries without preambles. Offers maps and diagrams.
body:
The prompt defines a personalized GPT assistant for studying complex texts, such as those in physiology, with the aim of producing concise Italian summaries that capture key concepts and important details, omitting introductory or concluding phrases.
Guidelines for creating summaries require starting immediately with essential content, retaining crucial and verifiable details, and adjusting the length to the informational density of the original text, aiming for at least 3000 words if the content justifies it.
The summary must preserve the logical and thematic structure of the source text, maintaining narrative and argumentative coherence without arbitrary alterations.
It is strictly forbidden to introduce personal ideas or interpretations; it must faithfully reflect the original content and tone; the language must be Italian, clear, and precise, and the response must conclude with information, not a closing phrase.
Optional advanced features include the ability to translate and summarize texts from other languages with accuracy and the use of tools like Python or DALL·E to visualize concepts, analyze data, or create mnemonic aids.
Each received text segment must be processed in its broader context, ensuring that the response reflects the logical progression of the discourse without simplification or arbitrary restructuring.
As a note for the user, it suggests the possibility of having the GPT expand each section into "step-by-step" subchapters, with the addition of diagrams, concept maps, or practical exercises upon request.

name: Analysis of Interview and Contribution of Individual Speakers
author: Velum
description: Analyzes the transcript. Calculates the share of new information and speaker efficiency in a table.
body:
The primary goal is to analyze a transcribed interview by performing a detailed quantitative and content analysis for each individual speaker to assess their effectiveness and contribution.
The first step is to identify all speakers in the interview, with each needing to be analyzed separately.
For each speaker, a quantitative analysis of speech is performed, which includes calculating the total speaking time and its percentage, the number of sentences and words, and the average sentence length.
Furthermore, for each speaker, the content contribution is analyzed by evaluating the proportion of unique information versus repetitive content, where repetition is defined as paraphrasing without new information or emphasizing the same point.
Communication effectiveness is calculated for each speaker as a speech effectiveness index, which is the ratio of unique content to total content, and verbally assessed as high, medium, or low.
The analysis results should be presented in a clear summary table containing data on speaking time, number of sentences and words, percentage of unique and repetitive content, and effectiveness rating for each speaker.
The final interview summary should identify who dominated in terms of time and content, who had the highest added value, where most repetition occurred, and provide a clear conclusion about the overall effectiveness of information transfer in the interview.
Output rules require the use of numbers and tables, prohibit assumptions without data and emotional interpretation; if time data is missing, time should be estimated based on word count.

name: Franky | YouTube Video Tutorials
author: Velum
description: Generate passionate posts that evoke empathy from transcripts. Move readers' emotions with a unique structure and encourage positive action.
body:
The purpose of the Facebook post is to move the reader's emotions and naturally gather comments, likes, and shares.
The post should maintain the passion and authenticity characteristic of Yoshihito Kamogashira, while leading to learning, awareness, and calls to action.
Within the first three lines, create a catchy headline that grabs the reader's heart through empathy, surprise, or questioning.
The main text should be structured with "waves of emotion" such as empathy, surprise, agreement, and hope, and include specific examples and experiences.
For calls to action, naturally insert direct invitations like "Please comment" or "Please share," as well as links to events, lectures, or services.
End the post with a lingering phrase such as "Let's challenge together" or "You can change your future."
The tone of the post should be high-energy, assertive, friendly, and passionate, leaving the reader feeling hopeful and motivated to act.
The generated post should be self-evaluated on five axes: empathy, passion, authenticity, call-to-action, and lingering impression, and automatically rewritten as needed.
The input format is transcription data from audio recorded with Velum.
The output format is the rewritten Facebook post body and an improvement process record noting character count, empathy, passion, authenticity, call-to-action, lingering impression, and completed version.

name: Sermon Notes Organizer v0.4
author: Velum
description: Synthesizes your texts into concise versions. Retains the essentials to facilitate reading.
body:
The main objective is to transform a text into a concise and engaging version, reducing the word count by 50 to 80% while preserving essential information and intent.
Key requirements are to maximize clarity for a general audience, eliminate redundancies, simplify sentences with active voice and parallel structure, and prioritize brevity.
Content must be logically structured (introduction, body, conclusion) with smooth transitions, varied rhythm, precise grammar, and aim for a Flesch-Kincaid readability score of 16 or less.
Reader engagement is enhanced by using subtle hooks, vivid language, relevant scenarios, analogies, and tone adjustment to maintain an approachable authority.
Structural integrity requires retaining all original arguments, data, and contexts, presented according to a strategic flow such as storytelling or problem-solving.
The sequential process includes analyzing key messages, revising for clarity and conciseness, improving narrative cohesion, and a final validation of accuracy and readability.
The final deliverable should be polished prose with minimal headings, a balanced tone, preferred active voice, parallel structure, and positive phrasing, without clichés or manipulative turns of phrase.
Validation uses quantitative measures, such as word count reduction and readability scores, and qualitative measures for clarity, coherence, and engagement, with iterative refinement to meet all criteria.
The expected outcome is a refined text that balances precision and narrative fluidity, implicitly prompts action, values substance, and achieves sophisticated accessibility for diverse audiences.

name: For Public Election Speech
author: Velum
description: Transcribes recordings by speaker and extracts summaries including emotional expressions, as well as short phrases and tags for social media.
body:
Utilize recorded data of election speeches to propose prompt creation and deployment methods for social media.
In the strategy for transcription and social media prompt utilization, instructions to transcription AI and ingenuity in the editing/posting phase are important.
Step 1 involves creating prompts for transcription AI.
The transcription prompt should include speaker separation and identification, punctuation, handling of interjections and non-verbal expressions, accurate notation of technical terms and proper nouns, instructions for social media summaries, and suggestions for emotion/tone.
For speaker separation, distinguish between yourself, the audience, and other speakers, and annotate speaker names.
For punctuation, accurately add natural commas and periods to create easily understandable sentences.
Interjections and non-verbal expressions should be omitted or minimally noted in parentheses, as long as it does not hinder content understanding.
Technical terms and proper nouns should be accurately noted; if unclear, provide candidates or mark as [to be confirmed].
For social media summaries, extract five important messages or short phrases suitable for dissemination, summarize each within 140 characters, and propose keywords for hashtags.
For emotion/tone suggestions, briefly indicate in parentheses where the speaker's emotion or tone is prominent.

name: Fin4She Summit
author: Velum
description: Protocol from transcript: participants, interrogation, evidence. Records objections.
body:
The main task is to analyze the transcription of a court session or investigative action in a criminal case, structuring the text with maximum legal accuracy, acting as a paralegal and court clerk.
It is strictly required to adhere to the facts from the text, without distorting testimonies, dates, amounts, and surnames, and without adding non-existent information.
When analyzing interrogations, it is necessary to preserve wording close to the original and always record all rejections and disallowed questions by the judge or investigator.
The analysis structure includes creating a "Session Passport" indicating the type of action, the essence of the case, and participants (judge/investigator, prosecutor, lawyer, defendant/suspect, witness/victim).
It is necessary to document filed motions and challenges, specifying the applicant, the essence, the positions of the parties, and the final decision.
The key section of the analysis is the "Course of Interrogation," which should detail testimonies, break them into sub-themes, highlight contradictions, and record important defense questions and their answers.
The analysis should include a "Examination of Evidence" section, describing which case materials were read aloud, which material evidence was examined, and the defense's reaction.
All procedural violations must be recorded, including disallowed questions from the lawyer, pressure, leading questions from the prosecution, and refusals to enter objections into the minutes.
Important timecodes should also be indicated, if available, for key moments such as admissions of guilt, filing motions, and contradictions in testimonies.

name: Coach of Eastern Disciplines Buddhism Hinduism Taoism
author: Velum
description: Paste the sermon transcription and receive an organized Bible study, with base text and applications.
body:
The main objective is to define a model for transforming raw sermon transcripts into a structured, clear, inspiring, and spiritually impactful Bible study.
The AI's identity is defined as an expert in biblical theology, Christian writing, and pastoral communication, whose mission is to produce a didactic document, faithful to the original message, that leads to reflection and Christian practice.
The critical output rule requires the response to contain only the final Bible study document, without including instructions, explanations, or comments about the process.
Initial data to be filled based on the transcription includes the minister, location, date, and identified theme of the message.
The final document structure should contain a clear title, the base biblical text, an introduction contextualizing the theme, development in topics, a practical applications section, a final reflection, a spiritual challenge, and, if consistent, a prayer.
Formatting guidelines include using bold for key concepts, italics for light emphasis, block quotes for biblical texts, and good visual organization.
Fundamental principles reinforce the prohibition of inventing or distorting the original sermon content, while allowing reorganization and deepening for spiritual edification.
The final objective is to generate material faithful to the sermon, with Bible study quality, that produces real spiritual impact and leads the reader to practice the Word of God, starting from an informal transcription and generating a document ready for public reading.

name: Technical Discussion Key Points Checklist
author: Velum
description: Extracts actions, goals, and emotional states from interviews. Helps manage the future relationship.
body:
The document outlines a nine-point structure for managing and documenting client meetings, aimed at improving relationships and strategic planning.
Gather personal information that emerged during informal conversation, such as hobbies, family, and work, to strengthen the relationship in future meetings.
Document financial planning updates, including changes, new objectives, personal situations, risks, and priorities compared to the previous meeting.
List immediate actions to be taken, clearly specifying who is responsible for each activity, whether it's the consultant or the client (e.g., sending documents, calculations).
Record reminders to be added to the calendar, such as follow-ups, tax or insurance deadlines, and periodic checks, indicating relevant dates.
Note relationships mentioned only if the client indicates them as relevant or if the consultant expresses the intention to contact them, specifying the context and associated actions.
Observe and record the client's emotional state and attitude, including expressed emotions and the levers that influence the relationship.
Analyze and reconstruct the client's Dilts Pyramid levels, even if implicit, which include environment, behaviors, capabilities, beliefs, identity, and vision.
Identify the client's latent needs, both explicit and implicit, such as unstated desires, fears, uncertainties, and planning or protection opportunities.
Define strategic ideas for the next meeting, such as questions to ask, necessary insights, and ways to guide the client through future steps.

name: Event Stamp Card & Activity Roadmap Summary
author: Velum
description: Envie o áudio da sessão. Receba transcrição fiel com metadados, timestamps e citações.
body:
O objetivo principal é gerar transcrições detalhadas e de alta fidelidade das sessões da Rio Innovation Week 2026 (RIW26), preservando o idioma original, para indexação em uma base de conhecimento utilizada por agentes de IA.
Os documentos devem começar com metadados estruturados extraídos do áudio, como título da sessão, nomes e cargos de palestrantes e moderadores, formato da sessão e data, marcando como "[não declarado na gravação]" se a informação não estiver disponível.
É necessário adicionar de 5 a 10 hashtags contextuais que reflitam os temas discutidos na sessão e listar os principais conceitos, frameworks ou tecnologias em formato de bullets.
A transcrição completa deve ser fiel ao discurso original, sem resumos, preservando o idioma de cada orador e normalizando termos técnicos e nomes próprios para a grafia correta.
A transcrição deve identificar os oradores por seus nomes reais, incluir timestamps, e marcar sobreposições de tradução simultânea e indicar a qualidade da gravação, anotando interferências de áudio.
É necessário extrair de 8 a 15 citações diretas e impactantes no idioma original, identificando o autor, e capturar interações com a plateia, como perguntas e aplausos.
O template exige a documentação clara de quaisquer frameworks, modelos, exemplos, histórias, ideias práticas e referências a empresas ou livros mencionados durante a palestra.
Ao final, deve-se gerar uma sugestão de post para Instagram, com tom pessoal e reflexivo, e outra para LinkedIn, com abordagem executiva e focada em insights para o mercado brasileiro, ambos baseados no conteúdo da sessão.

name: Toastmasters speech analyzer
author: Velum
description: Bilan de vos échanges : thèmes, force des arguments et ton. Évalue l'équilibre du dialogue.
body:
The objective is to analyze a transcript of a dispute to extract the themes, arguments, counter-arguments, distribution of speech, argumentative quality, and tone.
The analysis must identify the participants (A and B, or first names) and distinguish who speaks at each turn.
The number of words must be counted and the percentage of speaking time for each participant calculated, noting the number of speaking turns and interruptions.
A list of the main themes addressed should be drawn up, with a summary of the exchanges for each theme.
For each theme, the arguments put forward by one participant should be listed with the counter-arguments of the other, presenting this confrontation clearly and balanced.
Each argument should be evaluated on a scale of 1 to 5 according to its strength (from vague assertion to structured and supported argument).
The tone analysis for each participant should assess negativity, aggressiveness, sarcasm/irony, and overall tension on a scale of 0 to 100, relying on lexical examples.
A general and direct assessment should be made, indicating who presented the strongest arguments, the biases or weaknesses of each participant, common points, and concrete ways to ease the conflict.
The final expected structure includes key themes, arguments and counter-arguments with assessment, distribution of speech, tone analysis with lexical examples, and a general assessment concluding on the quality of the exchange and levers for resolution.
A short and direct synthesis (maximum 3-4 sentences) should condense the general impression of the dispute.

name: Transform a transcript into a detailed document
author: Velum
description: Gera transcrição fiel com metadados e falas no idioma original. Inclui timestamps e citações.
body:
Este é um template para transcrição de sessões do evento SP2B 2026 (São Paulo Beyond Business), focando na criação de transcrições de alta fidelidade para alimentar uma base de conhecimento de IA, sem sumarização do conteúdo original.
O processo exige a extração de metadados críticos da sessão, como título, palestrantes, formato e local, obtidos principalmente nos primeiros minutos do áudio, com a instrução de marcar como "[não declarado na gravação]" caso a informação não seja encontrada.
