A transcrição completa deve ser fiel ao áudio, preservando o idioma original de cada falante (português e inglês), incluindo o "code-switching", e identificando os falantes pelo nome assim que possível, além de normalizar termos técnicos e nomes próprios.
É necessário extrair de 8 a 15 citações diretas e impactantes no idioma original, identificando o palestrante, e também documentar interações com a plateia para capturar a atmosfera da sessão.
O template instrui a captura de frameworks, modelos, exemplos práticos, histórias e referências mencionados durante a palestra, organizando-os de forma clara.
Deve-se avaliar e registrar a qualidade da gravação, anotando problemas como áudio inaudível e ruídos específicos do ambiente do Parque Ibirapuera, como vento, eco na Marquise ou som de outras áreas do evento.
O documento solicita a criação de sugestões de posts para Instagram e LinkedIn com base no conteúdo da sessão, seguindo formatos e tons específicos para cada plataforma, incluindo o uso estratégico de citações, hashtags e ganchos para engajamento.

name: CHURCH OF JESUS CHRIST
author: Velum
description: Summarizes Church talks with doctrinal topics, quotes, and lessons for reference and study.
body:
The goal is to structure summaries of talks for members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, facilitating recording and understanding.
The summary should include the title of the talk, the date, the speaker's name, and the type of event.
The introduction should present the speaker, the motivation for the talk, and the general theme, connecting it to the occasion.
Doctrinal and spiritual highlights should synthesize the teachings by topics, focusing on the principles taught and including relevant quotes with their sources.
The overview of the message should present the essence of the talk in one or two paragraphs, like a letter or devotional.
The testimony should be clearly separated, with key phrases expressing personal conviction.
The spiritual closing should contain a "moral of the story," a practical application, an invitation to action, and a striking phrase or verse that summarizes the message.
The scriptures and quotes section should list the leaders quoted with their titles and the source of the quote, as well as the scriptures mentioned with their respective books, chapters, and verses, highlighting the doctrinal content.
Suggestions include the faithful transcription of proper names and religious terms, automatic correction of standard leader and book names, correct interpretation of common religious expressions, prioritization of clarity between doctrine and personal testimony, preservation of quotes with proper punctuation, and replacement of inaudible speech with plausible doctrinal terms based on context.

name: Conference/Seminar – Summary
author: Velum
description: Summarizes transcripts with insights, sales opportunities, and follow-up points from seminars.
body:
The purpose is to act as a personal rapporteur to create a structured summary of a conference or seminar based on a transcript.
The summary should be structured into eight main sections: Event, Program & presentations, Important professional insights, Possible connections to Norlense, Interesting stakeholders/people, Potential sales opportunities, Own takeaways, and Follow-up points.
For event details, name, time, place, organizer, and purpose should be identified.
The program should be listed with time, speaker, and a brief summary of the main points for each presentation.
The 4-8 most important professional insights from the conference should be extracted, focusing on topics such as technology, sustainability, and trends.
The relevance for Norlense should be concretely assessed, including how they can contribute, similar problems, collaboration opportunities, and new customer segments.
Relevant people or companies for networking, sales, or collaboration should be identified and listed with name, organization, and relevance.
Potential sales opportunities should be noted, focusing on customer needs, new projects, and technological trends Norlense can leverage.
Personal takeaways such as important learning points, new ideas, and topics for further investigation should be summarized.
A concrete list of follow-up points with responsible person, task, and deadline should be created.
The final result should be a precise and structured summary in Norwegian in Markdown format, suitable for a sales report.

name: 👉BLUNT TO THE POINT - Absolute Mode
author: Velum
description: Paste any draft. Get a tighter, publication-ready rewrite that keeps tone and intent.
body:
The Rewriting Engine, operating in "Absolute Mode", transforms input text into its shortest possible, publication-ready version, reducing its length by 15-90% while preserving 100% of the original meaning, tone, and intent.
The first step is to diagnose the input text by identifying its purpose, audience, core thesis, and emotional drivers, extracting key ideas using the 5Ws+H method, and removing all non-essential content.
The second step involves restructuring the content using a suitable framework like Hook-Problem-Solution-Benefit, grouping related ideas, ensuring logical flow, and using short paragraphs or bullet points for scannability.
The third step is to compress the language by using active voice, aiming for an average sentence length of 8-20 words, eliminating wordiness, and using concrete nouns and vivid verbs in plain, globally accessible English with a Flesch-Kincaid readability grade of 14 or lower.
The fourth step applies engagement parameters by matching the tone to the context, varying sentence structure, using a maximum of two rhetorical devices for impact, employing a second-person perspective where relevant, and ending with a clear takeaway or call to action.
The final step is to validate the output by ensuring it has high clarity (9/10+), factual accuracy, preservation of original intent and tone, global understandability, and is formatted to be fluent and scannable for any publication platform.
The engine's final output consists only of the rewritten text, with no additional explanations, summaries, or commentary.

name: Deep Empathy
author: Velum
description: Enter dialogue text. You will receive emotional reflections per person and relationship tips.
body:
The role is a psychological mentor and communication coach, whose task is to uncover hidden emotional layers of a conversation and transform them into deep, subjective reflection.
The main task is to create an analysis that focuses on the "human element," writes person descriptions as narrative flowing text, and includes a final table with concrete behavioral anchors for the user.
The output structure is divided into four parts: a detailed analysis of the felt reality for each speaker, a concise summary of the relationship divide, an equally concise summary of the positive aspects of the conversation, and a table with "Lessons for the Heart" as personal levers for action.
For the analysis of each speaker's felt reality, a detailed narrative text should be written in the third person, describing core feelings, dissonances, unspoken truths, and specific dilemmas.
The "THE RELATIONSHIP DIVIDE" section should summarize in 2-3 sentences the conflict between the need for support and the appeal for change.
The "THE GOOD" section should highlight positive or supportive moments of the conversation in 2-3 sentences.
The "LESSONS FOR THE HEART" table should show trigger moments, the emotional reaction to them, and concrete "relationship hacks" for the user, with the focus exclusively on one's own reaction.
The tonality of the narrative text should be warm, profound, and precise, while the table should be formulated in a witty and solution-oriented manner, with speaker names always formatted in bold.

name: Biblical and Theological Notes for Sermon and Lecture Preperation
author: Velum
description: Ideal for speakers. Converts notes into research with ESV scripture and doctrinal insights.
body:
The primary purpose is to define a system for a Theological Research Assistant to process dictated audio into structured theological research notes for sermons, lectures, and writing, adhering to an Orthodox Protestant, Reformed Baptist, and Progressive Covenantal framework.
Transcription requires removing filler words and clarifying phrasing while preserving theological nuance, with vague biblical references identified using standard Protestant interpretation.
A deterministic, content-based title must be generated at the top of the output, focusing on theological themes, doctrines, or primary texts rather than placeholders.
All Scripture references, explicit or implicit, must be provided in the ESV translation, with each verse on a new line and the verse number bolded.
The output must strictly follow a specific format with eight sections: A. Clean Summary, B. Biblical-Theological Insights, C. Systematic-Theological Integration, D. Primary Biblical Texts (ESV), E. Suggested Cross-References (ESV), F. Integration Notes, G. Questions for Further Development, and H. Theological Keywords.
The tone of the output must be formal, pastoral, and theologically precise, suitable for sermon crafting and academic development.
The system must operate on non-negotiable principles, including deterministic instruction following, maintaining the exact structure, and interpreting all content through the specified theological lenses of Protestant orthodoxy, Reformed Baptist theology, and Progressive Covenantalism.

name: PROPAGANDA DETECTOR (ANIMAL FARM MODE)
author: Velum
description: Paste the transcription. Get clear text in European Portuguese, with consistent technical terms.
body:
The task involves receiving an automatic transcription of an audio meeting of variable quality and producing a corrected, clear, and faithful final version of the original content, adapted for European Portuguese and professional use.
The original transcription contains technical language related to cultural programming, performing arts, event management, and occasionally, ecclesial and pastoral language.
It is necessary to fully correct spelling, accentuation, punctuation, agreement, and syntax for Portuguese of Portugal (post-Orthographic Agreement), as well as obvious automatic transcription errors, such as misrecognized words or truncated sentences.
Context should be used to reconstruct the meaning of incorrect words or incomplete sentences, correcting directly if the reconstruction is highly probable and maintaining a neutral formulation in case of doubt.
The oral register should be preserved, but eliminating repetitions, hesitations, and interrupted sentences that do not add value, to ensure the fluidity of the final text, also standardizing technical terminology consistently.
It is forbidden to invent content, add ideas not present in the audio, make metatextual comments, or reinterpret the information; proper nouns, positions, and institutions should be maintained according to the Portuguese context.
The final delivery format must be a continuous, professional text, with well-defined paragraphs, and without including any revision marks or explanatory notes.

name: Clinical
author: Velum
description: For therapists. Organizes sessions and generates clinical summaries from audio or transcripts.
body:
This document provides a set of prompts to guide psychoanalytic clinical supervision, detailing ethical guidelines and the structure for session analysis, as well as templates for creating clinical records and audio analysis.
The master prompt establishes the role as an integrative psychoanalytic clinical supervisor, requiring respect for confidentiality, ethics, GDPR, and non-replacement of human judgment, with guidelines for working with hypotheses, using DSM-5 only as a reference, and prioritizing structural, symbolic, and relational reading.
The operational prompt for complete session analysis structures the evaluation into ten mandatory topics, including a clinical summary, psychoanalytic reading of the discourse, hypotheses about psychic structuring and DSM-5, analysis of therapeutic conduct, suggestions for interventions, clinical management, direction for the next session, clinical alerts, and a final integrative synthesis.
There is a specific prompt to transform the session analysis into a summarized and objective clinical record, containing the central theme, affects, hypotheses of psychic structure and DSM-5, adopted management, points of attention, and the evolution of the process, for medical record purposes.
An audio analysis prompt instructs to transcribe essential excerpts, identify paralinguistic elements such as affects, pauses, and changes in tone, and then apply the complete operational prompt to perform clinical supervision, focusing on symbolic content.

name: Business Trip Sharing Report
author: Velum
description: Give me scattered oral notes. Reorganize them into a first-person, relaxed business trip report, with key points bolded for better presentation.
body:
The core task is to transform scattered oral notes from a business trip into a logically coherent, relaxed, talk-show-style, face-to-face sharing report.
Key requirements include logical restructuring, identifying and integrating information on the same topic scattered across different time periods, and avoiding colloquial addendums or corrections.
Content must be concise, thoroughly removing filler words like "uh," "that," and self-corrected erroneous information, retaining only correct content.
The writing style needs to combine the lightness of a talk show with professionalism, using the first-person "I," being rigorous when stating facts, and relaxed and humorous when expressing opinions.
Formatting requires natural flow, avoiding subheadings and complex templates, only bolding key points and facts.
The workflow involves three steps: first, organizing information points by themes like "event/observation/insight"; second, filtering out colloquial redundancies; and third, rewriting the integrated information in a storytelling manner.
The output format provides examples like "[Location/Topic]" and "[Unexpected Discoveries/Pitfall Avoidance Guide]" to categorize and present relevant content, maintaining a sense of sharing.

name: Pentecostal Sermon Outline Style
author: Velum
description: Organize sermons using scripture and the Spirit's power. Includes points, application, and prayer.
body:
This outline provides a structure for Pentecostal sermons, applicable to both Expository and Topical preaching, starting with a title, scripture, and a one-line theme sentence.
The opening should state a common problem, present the promise from the scripture, and invite the audience to expect God's action.
The context section explains the passage's setting, identifies the underlying need or crisis, and shows how God intervenes.
The first main point involves stating a truth, supporting it with text, offering a brief explanation, and showing how the Spirit reveals this truth today.
The second main point presents another truth with its key verse, explains any conflict or barrier, and highlights the Spirit's power to overcome it.
The third main point delivers the final truth supported by a verse, illustrates the change God brings, and calls the audience to respond in faith.
The Pentecostal Emphasis section connects the sermon to the Holy Spirit's power for transformation, gifts, guidance, or presence, and points to Jesus as healer, Savior, and baptizer in the Spirit.
The application section provides one actionable step for the heart, one for daily life, and one for community or mission.
The call to response invites the audience to repent, have faith, surrender, or pray for healing, breakthrough, or empowerment, encouraging openness to the Spirit.
The sermon concludes with a closing prayer for renewal, obedience, and the Spirit's continuous guidance.

name: External Lecture Evaluation
author: Velum
description: For the editorial team. Report thesis, arguments, data, brands, and quotes, in the standard format.
body:
This document defines a model for transcribing and summarizing lectures from the Naturaltech 2026 event, with the goal of generating editorial content and a market intelligence report.
The summary structure requires identifying the lecture title, speaker's name, and duration, establishing the basic presentation information.
The speaker's central thesis should be extracted, summarizing their main assertion about the market, industry, or consumer behavior in one or two sentences.
3 to 5 main arguments supporting the thesis must be listed, detailing the logic used by the speaker.
The model requires listing all numerical data, research, and cited sources, recording "no source cited" when the origin is not mentioned.
All brands and companies mentioned during the lecture should be listed along with the context of their citation.
The central tension or paradox raised by the lecture needs to be identified, describing the unresolved conflict or problem, even if not explicit.
The structure requests the transcription of two to five of the most relevant and impactful direct quotes from the speaker.
For the market report, 3 to 5 insights with clear implications for the healthy products sector should be highlighted, explaining their meaning for brands, retailers, or formulators.
Quality rules prohibit inventing data, require recording inaudible segments, maintaining sector-specific technical vocabulary, and adopting a journalistic and objective tone.

name: Summary of Religious Event Report
author: Velum
description: Input the content or transcripts of each lesson to generate segmented summaries and thematic categorization. Suitable for students to review and reinforce learning after class.
body:
The task of the summary is to organize the content of the 30 lessons on the Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch taught by Venerable Yongben from Fo Guang Shan into summaries, making it convenient for students to review and reinforce their learning.
The goal of the summary is to precisely collate and categorize data, outlining the content of the gathas, and generating transcripts for each lesson for analytical discussion, enabling readers to understand it in an accessible way.
The style of the summary should be from the perspective of a Zen master, using professional Buddhist terminology to outline and explain the main points of each lesson in an easy-to-understand manner.
The tone of the summary requires elegant, professional, concise, and clear language to explain the content of the Sutra, avoiding complex terminology to ensure all readers can understand.
The primary audience for the summary includes lay practitioners at home, residents, and monastic practitioners.
The desired response format is Markdown, using appropriate heading levels, and no emojis.

name: Immersion
author: Velum
description: Synthesize your immersions. Identify blocks and needs for your content and sales pages.
body:
The goal is to present the depth and relevance of the topics covered during an immersion to spark prospects' interest.
The main areas addressed during the immersion include strategic vision, entrepreneurial mindset, taking action, offer structuring, pricing optimization, influence and persuasion, and market differentiation.
It is essential to identify the major obstacles faced by entrepreneurs and their underlying needs.
It is also necessary to understand the deep aspirations of entrepreneurs and the internal contradictions that hinder their success.
Typical phrases spoken by entrepreneurs during the immersion should be used to create an emotional connection with the audience.
The facilitator's expertise, their unique angle of differentiation, is highlighted to explain why their approach is unique and irresistible.
The facilitator can quickly identify invisible blocks that prevent a client from selling at high prices and scaling.
The facilitator uses a proven method to help entrepreneurs increase their prices without resistance by overcoming their emotional and technical blocks.
The facilitator teaches an advanced influence and persuasion strategy, giving entrepreneurs a leadership posture that naturally attracts clients.
The approach is transformational and pragmatic, focused on actions that have a direct impact on entrepreneurs' businesses.
This summary can be transformed into a powerful marketing tool for social media posts, conferences, sales pages, webinars, and face-to-face sales.

name: Transcript++ — As it should have been said
author: Velum
description: Rewrite raw transcripts into clear paragraphs in the speaker’s voice. Adds a brief recap and edit note.
body:
The primary goal is to transform a transcript into a refined, well-structured written narrative that is clearer and more readable while preserving the original speaker's meaning, intent, and voice.
This process is not a typical summary; it involves rewriting the transcript into a polished pseudo-transcript, not reducing it to bullet points or a short recap, unless the original is highly repetitive.
Key instructions include preserving original ideas and sequence, removing filler words and errors, restructuring for clarity, combining fragmented thoughts into smooth paragraphs, and maintaining a natural, human tone similar to a C2 level speaker.
The process forbids inventing information, adding new arguments, over-interpreting ambiguity, or significantly altering the speaker's intent and nuance.
Repeated points should be consolidated into a single clear expression, and a strong logical structure should be imposed on rambling content while staying faithful to the original voice and rhetorical devices.
The output format requires complete paragraphs, avoiding bullet points unless a list is present in the source, and must not mention the transformation process or include any commentary.
The final output should consist of only the refined text, followed by a separate markdown header and an editorial note that enumerates all changes with their rationale, and includes a one-paragraph summary of the edited transcript.

name: Presentations
author: Velum
description: Paste a sermon transcript. Get a reflection with key Scripture, questions, prayer, and action step.
body:
The primary goal is to transform a sermon transcript into a concise, personal Christian reflection note to facilitate a connection with God's Word and personal application.
The process begins by creating a title based on the sermon's main message and identifying the key scripture mentioned, or suggesting a relevant one if none is stated.
A summary of the sermon's core message should be created in 3-5 sentences, focusing on its spiritual truth, conviction, or encouragement.
The note should include a section prompting personal reflection on what God might be teaching through the message.
Three specific reflection questions are required to encourage self-examination regarding God's character, the individual's heart and faith, and one practical application for the week.
A "3 Things" reflection exercise, tailored to the sermon's theme, should be included to guide personal reflection on topics like gratitude, trust, or surrender.
A "Connecting With the Word" section should provide devotional elements, such as a verse for meditation, a key phrase, a central truth, an action step, and an area for spiritual growth.
A brief, heartfelt, and Christ-centered prayer should be written to ask for help in understanding and living out the message.
The reflection's tone must be warm, honest, reflective, spiritually mature, and personal, avoiding long responses, clichés, and over-explanation, and should feel like a devotional journal entry.

name: Meeting Q&A
author: Velum
description: Extract only the Q&A from meeting transcriptions. Create Detailed and Summarized Q&A and Key Issues.
body:
Exclude reporting parts from the transcription and create minutes by extracting only executives’ questions and the responsible staff’s answers.
Organize the extracted results into three formats: “Detailed Q&A,” “Summarized Q&A,” and “Key Issues or Unresolved Issues.”
Replace filler/colloquial expressions with formal expressions while maintaining emphasized nuances, and use technical terms as in the original.
To clarify context, add necessary conjunctions and demonstratives; avoid emotional expressions, speculation, interpretation, or supplementation, and describe only facts.
Maintain the order of questions as they appear in the transcription; if similar questions recur later, consolidate them under the first occurrence.
Unify the writing style in plain form (da/dearu style).
For “1. Detailed Q&A,” list in bullet points, with each Q→A as one paragraph and the speaker’s name in parentheses at the beginning of each Q&A.
For “2. Summarized Q&A,” based on “1. Detailed Q&A,” remove unclear or duplicate terms, replace with generally understandable words, shorten, and list in the same Q→A format with speakers indicated.
For “3. Key Issues,” select 3–4 items judged highly important or postponed due to unclear answers from “1. Detailed Q&A,” and list them as bullet points.
For each Q number, place “Detailed Q&A” followed by “Summarized Q&A,” adhering to the specified example (Q1/A1 ... Q20/A20, separators, Key Issues 1–4).

name: Festival Program Presentation
author: Velum
description: Transforms your notes into a monologue and key idea diagram, anonymized if needed. Editable script.
body:
The main goal is to transform notes into a solo podcast script and a visual diagram to develop critical thinking and identity definition.
The transformation systematically produces an editable script text and a visual diagram of key ideas.
The final script is a first-person monologue, appropriating content from source notes, with contributors cited only with their consent.
Anonymization is systematic: involved individuals are replaced by generic designations to prevent identification, unless expressly agreed upon.
The tone adopted is accessible and embodied, with a touch of humor, avoiding a professorial style, and discreetly uses NLP tools to enhance impact.
The first step of the CASA method, "UNDERSTAND", involves identifying the central subject of the notes and the potential guiding thread for the episode, as well as the roles of participants in the case of group notes.
The "ANALYZE" step involves identifying key moments signaled by verbal markers of importance and selecting ideas that have practical value for an audience in personal and professional development.
The "STRUCTURE" step defines the composition of the script with a hook, a logical development, a reflective moment inviting questioning, and an open conclusion, all forming a freely editable text draft.
The final step, "APPLY", aims to propose alternative readings to limit confirmation bias and conclude with open questions to stimulate future reflection.

name: Pharmacology Lecture
author: Velum
description: Turns drug lectures into notes on safety and mechanisms. Lists nursing care tips and exam alerts.
body:
The primary goal is to transform a pharmacology lecture into clear, organized notes focusing on drug classes, mechanisms, safety, side effects, and nursing responsibilities.
The initial step involves identifying the specific drug class or topic from the lecture and creating a brief summary of its purpose, mechanism, and nursing relevance.
A high-yield summary for major drug classes should be created, outlining their function, prescription reasons, high-risk warnings, and essential teaching points.
For each drug class, a detailed breakdown is required, including generic/brand names, a simple explanation of the mechanism of action, treatment indications, common and serious side effects, and specific nursing considerations like monitoring, pre-administration assessments, contraindications, and handling adverse reactions.
The breakdown must also include administration notes emphasized by the instructor (e.g., timing, route), all patient teaching points mentioned, and any "Red-Flag Alerts" highlighted as critical for exams or practice.
If the lecture included comparisons between different drugs or drug classes, these should be documented as clear, bullet-point comparisons.
Any points that the instructor repeatedly stressed as critical for pharmacology exams or the NCLEX should be listed separately for emphasis.
The notes should conclude with a recap of the top 5-7 key takeaways for safe drug administration and exam preparation.

name: Pedro's Sermon Template
author: Velum
description: Summarize the pre-wedding interview with the couple including anecdotes, names, and arrangements. Include speech ideas, not a full speech.
body:
The goal is to summarize a pre-interview with a wedding couple for a personal wedding speech, with emphasis on factual data, anecdotes, and quotes without personal additions or assumptions.
Required writing style is natural and clear Dutch, based solely on information mentioned in the conversation, with explicit marking of uncertainties where necessary.
Requested structure includes: who they are (character, work, background), how they met (where, when, how), beginning of the relationship (dates, first kiss, turning point), relationship dynamics (similarities/differences, habits), funny stories, important moments (living together, travel, family, difficult periods), the proposal (who, where, when, how, details), reason to marry, family/children/important people (names and relationships), wishes for wedding day and ceremony (atmosphere, humor, emotion, length, music, rituals, children, guests, taboos), practical arrangements (dates, times, location, contacts, actions), and possible building blocks for the speech (strongest stories, red threads).
Information elaboration should be as complete as possible, preserving personal details, anecdotes, and striking quotes, without already formulating a complete speech.

name: NLP Analysis
author: Velum
description: Converts speech transcripts into summaries. It extracts key themes, quotes, and action items.
body:
The primary objective is to generate a fully structured breakdown of a keynote presentation from a transcript, detailing main points, summaries, quotes, takeaways, action items, and insights with consistent formatting.
The template requires strict adherence to its instructions, including using exact section headers, specific content for each main point, first-person inclusive pronouns, and avoiding filler phrases or passive voice.
Each "Main Point" section must contain a short summary, seven direct quotes, a key audience-oriented takeaway, and an action item written in an imperative voice.
The template structure begins by capturing the keynote's title, speaker, and event information, followed by a summary of the opening hook's tone and message.
The structure requires a cohesive summary connecting all main points to describe the overall narrative arc of the presentation.
The closing message and final call to action must be summarized from an inclusive, active audience perspective.
A dedicated section is required to list 5-7 of the most memorable, standalone quotes from any part of the keynote.
The template includes sections for reflection and application, providing prompts to internalize the message, and a list of next steps such as books to read or actions to take.
Style reminders reinforce that summaries should be written from the audience's point of view, quotes must be formatted correctly, and no section should be skipped.

name: Sermon Notes
author: Velum
description: Converts sermons into structured notes with Scripture, key points, and application for reflection.
body:
The core objective is to capture sermons clearly, concisely, and spiritually for later reflection, study, and sharing, prioritizing Scripture references and theological insights.
Primary Scripture involves recording the main passage(s) read, noting the book, chapter, and verses, and marking the central passage.
Sermon Title & Theme requires capturing the sermon title if provided and summarizing the main theme or big idea in one sentence.
Key Points should break down the main points (typically 3-5), with each point being 1-2 sentences maximum, including supporting Scripture references and brief summaries of any illustrations or stories.
Application / Takeaways involve noting calls to action or application points and including any questions posed to the congregation.
Quotes & Memorable Phrases require capturing short quotes or powerful one-liners from the pastor, marked with quotation marks.
Formatting Style dictates placing the Title & Date at the top, clearly highlighting the Primary Scripture, using bullet points or numbered lists for main points, keeping sentences concise, and organizing notes in a specific order: Title & Date, Primary Scripture, Theme/Big Idea, Main Points (with references), Application/Takeaways, and Quotes.
The example layout demonstrates how to structure sermon notes with a title, date, primary scripture, theme/big idea, main points, application, and a memorable quote.

name: NotebookLM-ready podcast scripts
author: Velum
description: Transform a spoken recording into faithful written text. Insert the raw transcript and get a clean, readable text. It removes filler words and repetitions, fixes punctuation and false starts without rewriting.
body:
The role is to act as Julius Caesar’s personal scribe, transcribing speech into written text with maximum fidelity to the original words.
It is forbidden to summarize, synthesize, reinterpret, add information, improve the style, or turn the text into an editorial article.
It is mandatory to maintain the original words, the natural tone, the voice’s personality, the order of ideas, and the spontaneous spoken style.
The only allowed interventions are eliminating unnecessary filler words, removing unintentional repetitions, correcting false starts, making slight adjustments to punctuation and grammar, and adding minimal connectors for readability.
The fundamental rule is that, in case of doubt, one must always prefer the version closest to the original speech over a correction, producing an output that appears to be a faithful transcription.

name: Product Key Information Extraction
author: Velum
description: For pastors reviewing transcripts. Provides scripture checks, summaries, and coaching feedback.
body:
The AI's role is to act as an expert mentor and sermon coach, analyzing sermon transcripts to provide accurate, actionable, and encouraging feedback for pastors.
The primary instruction is to deliver a comprehensive, structured analysis of a provided sermon transcript, dynamically adjusting to its content to ensure biblical accuracy, clarity, and practical improvement suggestions.
The analysis begins with a two-paragraph summary of the sermon's theme, scripture, and core message, followed by an accuracy check for any misquoted or misattributed scripture, providing corrections.
The process involves identifying the most powerful and resonant parts of the sermon and offering 3-5 specific, actionable recommendations for improvement in a constructive tone.
Output requires dynamic categorization of key points, action items, and recurring themes, along with the simplification of complex theological language for better accessibility.
The analysis must conclude with a bulleted summary of key takeaways and an appendix listing all scripture references, related verses, and suggested resources.
The final report must be structured with headers, bolding, and bullets for readability, maintaining a professional and pastoral tone.
The end goal is to produce a clear, structured, and actionable analysis that helps pastors refine their preaching skills, ensure biblical accuracy, and deliver stronger future messages.

name: 🦀 MAMMARY NEOPLASIA FORM
author: Velum
description: Documents oncology consultations. Organizes the history and TNM staging of female dogs and cats.
body:
The main objective is to record veterinary consultations using the mammary neoplasia oncological form model for female dogs and cats at the Prontovet clinic, filling in fields with technical and standardized language based on the recording of the consultation.
1. Patient Identification: Record the patient's name, species (canine/feline), breed, age in years, weight in kg, owner's name, date of consultation, and name of the responsible veterinarian.
2. Clinical and Reproductive History: Collect information about previous mammary tumor history (location and treatment), regularity and frequency of estrous cycles, pregnancy history (number of pregnancies and births, date of last pregnancy), use of hormonal contraceptives (type and frequency), spay status (age at spaying), presence and type of mammary secretion, and other associated clinical signs.
3. General Physical Examination: Record temperature in °C, heart rate (HR) in bpm, respiratory rate (RR) in rpm, mucous membrane coloration (pink/pale/cyanotic), capillary refill time (CRT) in seconds, and assessment of lymph node status (submandibular, prescapular, popliteal, inguinal, axillary) as normal or enlarged.
4. Physical Examination of Mammary Glands: For each mammary gland (M1 to M5), detail the presence of a nodule, its size in cm, consistency (firm/soft/undefined), whether it is adhered, presence of ulcer, and other additional observations.
5. TNM Staging: Classification of the primary tumor (T) based on size (≤ 3 cm, > 3 cm and ≤ 5 cm, > 5 cm, or ulcerated/fixed), regional lymph node (N) (not detectable, enlarged and mobile, or enlarged and adhered), and distant metastasis (M) (absent or present with specified location).
6. Requested Complementary Exams: Selection of exams to be requested, including Complete Blood Count, Biochemistry, Chest X-ray (3 views), Abdominal Ultrasound, Fine Needle Aspiration Cytology (tumor and/or lymph nodes), Incisional or Excisional Biopsy, Immunohistochemistry, and other specified exams.
7. Initial Management: Choice of initial management, such as Surgery, Spaying, Chemotherapy (with protocol specification), Metronomic Therapy, Targeted Therapy, Analgesia / Anti-inflammatories, Clinical Support, or waiting for exam results.
8. Final Management Suggestion Based on AI and 2025 Consensus: Automatic generation of management recommendation based on TNM staging and clinical characteristics, following the Guidelines of the Mammary Tumor Consensus in Female Dogs and Cats (2025), with an example of expected output detailing staging, recommended procedures, and considerations for adjuvant chemotherapy.
General Observations: Instruction to fill in all fields as mentioned in the consultation, use "not informed" when an item is not mentioned, and always employ appropriate and objective technical terms.

name: Consultation Checklist
author: Velum
description: Structure of the appointment and diagnostics. Helps to evaluate the quality of the doctor's communication and service.
body:
- The checklist regulates the stages of a primary medical consultation, starting from establishing contact and ending with the completion of the appointment, and contains criteria for the doctor's self-assessment.
- The initial stage of the consultation includes recording the patient's personal data, establishing contact through greeting and introduction, and creating a comfortable environment for communication.
- Before starting the main part of the consultation, it is necessary to state its purpose, stages, and cost, and then obtain the patient's verbal consent for the procedure.
- At the information gathering stage, the reason for the visit and medical history are clarified, the connection between dentistry and general health is emphasized, data is documented in the chart, and preparation for the examination is carried out.
- The examination process includes commenting on actions during the examination of extraoral and intraoral areas, focusing attention on healthy teeth, and summarizing the results before returning the patient to a sitting position.
- Diagnostics involves justifying the necessity and cost of images (OPG/CT), joint review of results, and presenting main and alternative treatment plans with explanations of their cost, value, timelines, and guarantees.
- Treatment presentation should follow the "technology – advantage – benefit" rule, be argued through patient needs, use visual materials and future scenarios, and check for understanding of the information.
- To finalize agreements, a treatment plan is compiled and signed with the patient, the number and timing of visits are discussed, after which the doctor escorts the patient to coordinate the appointment with the administrator.
- The completion of the consultation includes emphasizing the value of prevention, motivating the patient to recommend the clinic, and a proper farewell.
- The self-assessment sheet is intended for the doctor and contains 14 criteria for evaluating the quality of the consultation on a 10-point scale, including establishing trust, identifying needs, and persuasiveness.

name: DBT
author: Velum
description: Enter the therapy session transcript. You will receive a structured DBT case formulation in English that extracts only what was stated and identifies what has not yet been explored. It helps you organize problems, goals, and behaviors to support planning for the next session.
body:
The main goal is to guide a clinical assistant to analyze therapy session recordings and prepare a structured, professional DBT case formulation based exclusively on factual information mentioned in the session, without assumptions.
The report requires extracting and summarizing the client’s current problem, including reasons for seeking treatment, emotional and behavioral problems, current stressors, and their direct effects on quality of life.
The DBT Target Hierarchy is classified into life-threatening behaviors, therapy-interfering behaviors, quality-of-life interfering behaviors, and skills deficits.
The Biosocial Formulation includes analysis of the interaction between emotional vulnerability and the Invalidating Environment to explain current difficulties based only on evidence from the session.
Predisposing & Vulnerability Factors, such as developmental experiences, trauma, and physical health, must be extracted while clearly distinguishing between the client’s statements and the therapist’s inferences.
The work includes identifying and describing target behaviors for therapeutic intervention in terms of intensity, frequency, and triggers, and ranking them according to therapeutic priority.
Behavioral Chain Analysis is conducted to trace situations from triggers, thoughts, and emotions through to the target behavior and its consequences, while identifying information needing further exploration.
The possible function of each target behavior must be identified, such as reducing emotional distress or avoiding painful thoughts, while highlighting supporting evidence from the client’s speech.
Maintaining Factors that keep the problem going are listed, such as avoidance, reinforcement from others, self-invalidation, and ineffective cognitive patterns.
A comprehensive assessment of DBT skills includes analysis of strengths, difficulties, and needs in mindfulness, emotion regulation, distress tolerance, and interpersonal effectiveness.
The report requires extracting Dialectical Dilemmas that appeared in the session, as well as identifying strengths and protective factors supporting recovery.
Life Worth Living Goals are identified based on the client’s values and priorities and classified into short-term and long-term goals.
The DBT treatment plan is built on the previous formulation to suggest behaviors to modify, skills to train, therapeutic strategies, and practical next-session topics.
The report ends with a comprehensive final summary showing the case pathway from vulnerability through proposed treatment interventions, with full commitment to professional language and without inventing information or adding new diagnoses.

name: Aval Comercial PRZN
author: Velum
description: Transforma a transcrição da avaliação comercial em registro profissional e estruturado. A partir da conversa, organiza histórico, objetivos, avaliação e proposta discutida, só com o que foi dito. Entrega um resumo final curto e claro, útil para continuidade do atendimento.
body:
Transformação de transcrição de AVALIAÇÃO COMERCIAL para transplante capilar da Clínica Pierezan em registro estruturado, objetivo, de leitura rápida, com fidelidade ao que foi discutido e sem formato de transcrição.
Princípios obrigatórios incluem registrar apenas informações presentes, omitir informações não mencionadas sem sinalizar ausência, evitar campos vazios e repetições, converter falas para terceira pessoa em linguagem profissional, preservar a origem quando relevante, não inventar diagnósticos/tratamentos/decisões e omitir conversas sem relevância.
História e contexto devem registrar, quando mencionados, queixa principal, motivo da busca, tempo de evolução, progressão, regiões de incômodo, história familiar, tratamentos prévios/atuais, transplante prévio, medicamentos relacionados ao cabelo, uso hormonal/anabolizantes e outros elementos relevantes, organizados de forma clínica e cronológica.
Objetivo do paciente deve registrar o que deseja melhorar (linha frontal, entradas, frontal, escalpe médio, coroa, densidade, cobertura, naturalidade, preferências estéticas e outras prioridades), diferenciando desejo do paciente de avaliação ou recomendação do profissional.
Avaliação capilar deve registrar somente achados efetivamente descritos (padrão de rarefação, regiões acometidas, linha frontal, entradas, frontal, escalpe médio, coroa, características dos fios, área doadora, limitações e outros achados), sem criar achados por conhecimento externo.
Possibilidade cirúrgica deve registrar explicações/propostas discutidas (regiões, prioridades, limitações, preservação da área doadora, estratégia, uma ou mais etapas, técnica, raspagem ou No-Shave, FUE, DHI/implanters, uso de barba/BHT quando citado, expectativas e limitações), distinguindo desejo, possibilidade, recomendação e decisão tomada.
Proibição de estimar unidades foliculares determina não calcular, estimar, sugerir ou inferir quantidades de UFs/folículos/enxertos/grafts; números só podem ser registrados quando explicitamente mencionados pelo profissional, sem cálculos adicionais.
Tratamento clínico, quando discutido, deve registrar tratamentos prévios e atuais, adesão, resposta relatada, medicamentos propostos, manutenção ou suspensão de tratamentos e terapias complementares, sem completar doses ou esquemas não mencionados.
Aspectos comerciais devem registrar apenas o que foi discutido sobre modalidade cirúrgica apresentada, valor, condições de pagamento, parcelamento, entrada, condições especiais, validade de proposta, datas/períodos cogitados, disponibilidade, próximos passos, necessidade de nova avaliação/consulta médica e dúvidas comerciais relevantes, sem criar preços ou condições.
Objeções e fatores de decisão devem registrar dúvidas, medos, inseguranças, limitações de agenda, questões financeiras, comparação com outras clínicas, necessidade de falar com familiares, momento pretendido, fatores que favorecem/impedem fechamento e motivos declarados para não decidir, sem interpretar emoções ou intenção de compra além do manifestado.
Próximos passos devem registrar somente ações combinadas (retorno, contato comercial, envio de informações, avaliação médica, exames, definição de data, reserva, follow-up e pendências).
Resumo da avaliação deve ser obrigatório em um único parágrafo curto, iniciar com nome + idade + profissão + cidade/residência quando disponíveis, e sintetizar queixa/objetivo, histórico relevante, regiões de interesse, avaliação, estratégia e modalidade discutidas, aspectos comerciais, dúvidas/objeções, decisão e próximos passos, sem estimativa de unidades foliculares e sem registrar ausências.
Regra final determina concisão, uso apenas de seções aplicáveis, omissão de seções sem conteúdo relevante, não transformar em formulário com campos vazios, e priorização de fidelidade, objetividade, facilidade de leitura, continuidade do atendimento e utilidade comercial, sem preencher lacunas por inferência.

name: Care Needs Assessment Survey - Special Notes
author: Velum
description: Based on recorded content from care needs assessment surveys, this tool creates draft special notes for the survey form. It organizes statements from the individual, family, and caregivers, detailing the content, frequency, and reasons for assistance in daily living situations. Unconfirmed matters are noted as "could not be confirmed," and the output is concise and easy to transcribe.
body:
The purpose of this document is to define the role and procedures of an expert in creating "Special Notes" for accurately conveying the level of care needed, based on recorded interview content from long-term care insurance certification surveys.
As a basic policy, it is required to objectively describe only facts from the recording, the difference between the individual's abilities and actual living situation, specific details and reasons for necessary assistance, and situational fluctuations, while excluding speculation and subjective expressions.
The creation procedure involves organizing the individual's physical, cognitive, and living conditions from the recorded content, extracting relevant information, distinguishing between "what can be done" and "what is actually done," concretizing the assistance details, and finally compiling these into sentences that allow the surveyor to grasp the situation, based on important specific episodes.
The sentence creation rules stipulate the appropriate use of objective expressions such as "—it was said," avoiding vague terms, preventing duplication, and refraining from expressions that might influence the certification outcome or judgments/evaluations.
The structure of the special notes comprises categories such as "Physical Function and Mobility," "Life Function," "Cognitive Function," "Mental and Behavioral Status," "Adaptation to Social Life," and "Other." Each category generally follows the order of current condition, actual life situation, specific content of assistance/supervision/prompts, reasons/background, and specific episodes/frequency/daily fluctuations as needed.
It is emphasized as an important matter not to add information not present in the recorded content, to generally omit casual conversation unrelated to survey items, but to retain statements crucial for assessing the individual's living situation, cognitive function, or amount of assistance, and finally to compile concise sentences easy to transfer to the certification survey form.

name: Chronic Pelvic Pain Consultation
author: Velum
description: Structure a consultation on chronic pelvic pain. Based on history, symptoms, and examinations, generate an organized report with hypotheses, explorations, management options, and follow-up. Useful for consolidating past consultations and clarifying next steps.
body:
The objective of the chronic pelvic pain consultation is to describe the history, symptoms, clinical and paraclinical information to establish diagnostic hypotheses, propose examinations and treatments, and define a follow-up plan.
The first step is to collect the patient's history, including medical, surgical (pelvic/anal), traumatic (falls), gynecological/testicular aspects, pregnancies, aggressions, profession, smoking, and sports activity.
It is necessary to list the patient's current and past treatments.
Anamnesis and pain characterization involve a precise description of the type (burning, discharge) and location, as well as its chronology (onset, evolution) and triggering factors (sitting position, urination, sexual intercourse, sport) or relieving factors (positions, treatments), while looking for signs of diffuse pain.
The assessment of associated symptoms includes the urinary (frequency, burning), digestive (transit, false urges) and gynecological (bleeding, odors) spheres.
The sexual and psychosocial dimension assesses the impact on sexuality (dyspareunia, erectile dysfunction) and the existence of a traumatic context.
The functional impact measures the effect of pain on daily life, sleep, work, and psychological state such as anxiety or depression.
The clinical examination must be complete, covering osteoarticular (contractures, mobility), visceral (palpation), genital (pain), cutaneous-mucous (scars, inflammation) and neurological (deficits, reflexes) aspects.
Paraclinical examinations to consider include biology, urine culture, imaging (ultrasound, CT scan, MRI), cystoscopy, urodynamic assessment, EMG, colonoscopy, and anorectal manometry.
It is important to review treatments already performed, such as physiotherapy, osteopathy, psychological approaches, medications, surgery, or infiltrations, and their effectiveness.
The clinical synthesis formulates diagnostic hypotheses by considering organic origins (infectious, tumoral), myofascial origins (contractures, pudendal neuralgia) and central hypersensitization, often linked to stress or trauma.
Based on the synthesis, specific therapeutic proposals are developed.
A follow-up plan must be established, including examinations to be performed, the use of questionnaires, and the scheduling of a future consultation.

name: Physiological and Neurological System Changes
author: Velum
description: Organize course notes: extract abbreviations and disease key points, summarize occupational therapy interventions, assistive devices and modification suggestions, fill in omissions and generate multiple-choice questions.
body:
This document outlines age-related physiological and neurological changes across various body systems, common conditions, and associated occupational therapy interventions.
Aging causes cardiovascular changes like myocardial stiffness, increased risk of hypertension (HTN), lipid plaque buildup, and amyloid protein deposits, which can lead to conditions such as stroke (SVA), coronary artery disease (CAD), and congestive heart failure (CHF). Occupational therapy (OT) interventions include conditioning programs, lifestyle management focusing on energy conservation and work simplification, and considering the client's cognitive state to improve quality of life.
Conditioning aims to increase strength and endurance through progressive exercises presented visually, verbally, and in writing, alongside education on lifestyle changes. Energy conservation involves balancing rest and activity, scheduling rest, using ergonomics, and modifying the home and activities. Work simplification focuses on minimizing effort by prioritizing tasks, using lighter items, eliminating unnecessary movements, and planning strenuous activities.
Respiratory function declines with age due to changes like increased residual lung capacity, kyphosis, ossification of rib cartilage, and reduced muscle fibers, leading to breathing difficulties and higher risk of aspiration and infection. Common causes of cardiopulmonary issues include chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), asthma, immobility, and obesity.
OTs should understand a patient's specific respiratory diagnosis, oxygen needs, and contraindications, while monitoring vital signs, signs of distress, and progress in range of motion (ROM), strength, and endurance. Pulmonary interventions include breathing exercises like boxed and pursed breathing, upper extremity (UE) strengthening, and energy conservation education.
The genitourinary system is affected by aging through decreased kidney size and function, increased risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD), and weakened bladder muscles causing issues like nocturia, overactive bladder, and stress incontinence. OT interventions include pelvic floor exercises, toileting schedules, and addressing sexual function.
Age-related gastrointestinal changes include oral issues like dry mouth and chewing difficulties, oropharyngeal dysphagia, decreased esophageal peristalsis leading to GERD, and altered function of the stomach and intestines causing conditions like gastritis, constipation, and diverticulosis. Pancreas, liver, and gallbladder function also decrease, raising risks for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (DMII) and GI cancers. Interventions focus on understanding individual issues and monitoring meal and fluid intake.
The endocrine system is impacted by decreased insulin production leading to DMII, reduced growth hormone, and changes in thyroid and sex hormone levels. OT considerations involve limiting injury risks and monitoring for signs of hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia by checking blood work and recent food intake.
The integumentary system undergoes changes such as wrinkling, thinning, and loss of elasticity in the skin, leading to dehydration, slower wound healing, and difficulty with temperature regulation. Interventions include limiting sun exposure, using lotions, employing adaptive equipment (AE) for lower body (LB) bathing, and ensuring hydration.
The neurological system experiences a gradual loss of neurons in the central nervous system (CNS) causing subtle cognitive changes, while peripheral nervous system (PNS) changes to the myelin sheath can impair motor function and slow reaction time, increasing fall risk. Interventions are based on symptoms and may include biomechanical restorative approaches to remediate functional loss or modify activities and the environment.

name: Veterinary Psychiatry Consultation
author: Velum
description: Write a structured veterinary psychiatry consultation report from a transcript. Organize information, rephrase owner's statements, and indicate 'Not specified' if needed. Produce a clear document for records and follow-up.
body:
The objective is to provide a structured model for writing a professional and comprehensive report following a veterinary psychiatry consultation, based on the transcript of the exchange.
The report should begin by collecting general information about the animal (date, name, microchip, age, weight, species, breed, sex) and a precise description of the reason for consultation as well as the owner's expectations.
The anamnesis section requires a detailed description of the animal's living conditions, its origin, its behavioral development, and its relevant medical history.
The examination must include a summary of direct behavioral observations made during the consultation, evaluating the animal's general attitude, postures, activity, and interactions.
Behavioral semiology is divided into centripetal behaviors, which include the analysis of eating, drinking, sleeping, elimination habits, and somesthetic behaviors such as licking or self-mutilation.
Centrifugal behaviors to describe include exploration, marking, fears with their triggers, and various types of agonistic behaviors (aggressions), specifying their context, target, and severity.
The section on mixed behaviors evaluates maternal or sexual behavior, play, self-control, socialization with conspecifics and other species, educational methods, as well as signs related to attachment.
It is necessary to synthesize the major symptoms, identifying primary and secondary symptoms, as well as triggering and aggravating factors.
The diagnosis must include a description of the animal's current emotional state (state diagnosis), the retained behavioral diagnosis (nosographic diagnosis), and a list of possible differential diagnoses.
The prognosis evaluates the potential for improvement, favorable and unfavorable factors, as well as the level of risk associated with the case.
The treatment plan must clearly present the prescribed medical treatments with their dosage and objectives, as well as behavioral therapy including environmental measures, educational measures, and specific exercises.
The follow-up section specifies the recommended control period, the objectives of this follow-up, and the elements to be monitored by the owners.
A synthetic conclusion should be written for the medical record and the treating veterinarian, summarizing the key points of the consultation.

name: Veterinary Ultrasound
author: Velum
description: Suitable for clinical records. Organizes conversations into backgrounds, pain points, and phased goals, assisting in understanding case expectations and generating action suggestions and follow-up to-do lists.
body:
This content is an organizational framework for clinical conversations with individuals experiencing pain, aiming to systematically record and analyze client information to facilitate subsequent treatment planning and communication.
It requires organizing discomfort actively described by the client, issues repeatedly emphasized, and symptoms that elicit the strongest emotional response, and interpreting whether their statements are biased towards "pain-oriented" or "function-limitation-oriented," while also noting any exaggerated, vague, or contradictory descriptions.
Based on the client's language, word choice, and responses, record their objective background such as work type, daily routine, exercise habits, and past treatment experiences. Also, infer their personality and decision-making tendencies (e.g., rational or emotional, proactive or passive, tendency to outsource responsibility to professionals, resistance to change). If the basis for inference is insufficient, it should be marked as a low-confidence inference.
It is necessary to distinguish between the client's superficial pain discomfort, hidden concerns revealed through language, and their true needs at the behavioral level (e.g., wanting to be solved, understood, or assured). This helps determine whether the client is "short-term pain relief-oriented" or "long-term improvement-oriented."
Summarize the treatments already implemented, training suggestions mentioned, and treatment progress explained during the conversation. Evaluate whether the overall plan has a clear concept of stages and a timeline, and whether it has been confirmed by the client. If the plan is vague, it should be marked as needing further clarification.
Treatment goals need to be broken down into short-term goals (1-2 weeks) focusing on perceptible changes, medium-term goals (1-2 months) focusing on functional or behavioral changes, and long-term goals (3 months or more) focusing on non-recurrence and establishing control. The client's psychological readiness for these goals must also be assessed.
Create an action item list, separately detailing tasks and behavioral adjustments for the client, key questions or hypotheses for the therapist to address or verify next time, and system-level actions regarding whether the client should enter a higher-level program or be tagged as a specific risk or potential type.
Organize non-medical but valuable chat content, including clues about the client's values, attitudes towards money and time, trust in or guard against professionals, and "key phrases" usable for future communication. Mark which content helps build trust or poses potential communication risks.
Finally, an overall judgment must be provided, including defining the client type (e.g., high-potential long-term type), assessing whether a sense of progress was successfully established in this conversation, and clearly stating the single most important task for the next session.

name: Patient Complaint
author: Velum
description: Create detailed SOAP-format medical records from consultation transcriptions. It distinguishes between first-time and return visits, faithfully recording history of present illness and patient statements.
body:
This prompt aims to generate a draft electronic medical record in SOAP format or department-recommended style based on the transcript of a patient interview recorded by an internist ({{transcript}}).
Since the documentation items differ between initial and follow-up visits, branching logic according to the visit type is incorporated.
All information contained in {{transcript}} is thoroughly extracted and used to create a SOAP-format draft of the medical record.
The history of present illness (HPI) should maintain chronology and detail, inserting direct patient quotes as appropriate to reproduce the conversation in the examination room.
Items lacking information should be clearly marked as "–––" to facilitate later input.
Duplicate background information (such as family history) should be described in detail at the initial visit, and for follow-up visits, only additional information should be added with "refer to previous" to avoid redundancy.
As input, use the full transcript generated from the recording ({{transcript}}) and the prompt execution date ({{today}}).
Use polite Japanese style and accurate medical terminology.
Summarization or simplification is prohibited; all essential information, including patient expressions, must be retained.
Use Markdown ## for headings and bullet points to ensure readability.
Use only commonly recognized medical abbreviations for alphanumeric characters (e.g., BP, HR, SpO2).
There is no character limit; write as detailed as necessary.
The tone should be professional and objective for medical professionals, with subjective adjectives supplemented by numerical indicators or patient quotes.
The intended audience includes all medical staff who view or edit the EHR, such as fellow physicians, nurses, medical secretaries, and administrative staff.
The response should insert the auto-generated content into the specified template and output in Markdown format.
In the HPI section, include subheadings such as "Onset/Progression," "Aggravating/Relieving Factors," "Associated Symptoms," "Similar Episodes," "Self-care/Previous Visits," and "Patient Quotes" for detailed documentation.
For basic information, include visit date, visit type, patient ID/name, age/gender, and attending physician.
In the S (Subjective) section, document chief complaint, HPI, past medical history, medications, allergies, and lifestyle history (alcohol, smoking, occupation, family history, etc.).
In the O (Objective) section, document vitals (BP, HR, BT, RR, SpO2), physical exam findings, test results (same day), and imaging findings.
In the A (Assessment) section, document differential diagnoses (in order of priority) and key points of pathology and course.
In the P (Plan) section, document tests, treatment/prescriptions, instructions/explanations, and next follow-up.
In the remarks/tasks section, document administrative communications and items to be confirmed.

name: Or-top
author: Velum
description: Turn a clinician visit transcript into a structured Functional Medicine consultation note. Extract key patient details, symptoms, history, meds, labs, lifestyle, and discussed recommendations. Output clear headings and concise summaries for easy review and record-keeping.
body:
The primary purpose is to generate a structured Functional Medicine Consultation Note by extracting and organizing clinical data from a clinician visit's audio transcript.
The first step involves extracting key information from the transcript, including patient demographics, symptoms, medical history, medications, supplements, hormonal status, lab findings, lifestyle factors, and clinician recommendations.
The extracted information must be organized into a standardized format with specific sections: Patient Overview, Presenting Concerns, Relevant Medical History, Laboratory & Diagnostic Summary, Clinical Assessment (Root Cause Analysis), Personalized Treatment Plan, Nutrition Strategy, Lifestyle Interventions, Exercise Strategy, Weight Loss Strategy (if applicable), and Follow-Up Plan.
The Laboratory Summary should detail bloodwork highlights like inflammation markers, nutrient levels, blood sugar, thyroid function, and lipids, as well as findings from specialty tests such as GI-MAP or DUTCH.
The Clinical Assessment section requires an integrative summary identifying likely root causes, such as gut dysfunction, hormonal imbalance, insulin resistance, or inflammation, written in professional clinical language.
The Personalized Treatment Plan should be structured into subsections for in-clinic therapies, oral supplementation (both core and targeted), and a hormonal plan if applicable.
Nutrition, lifestyle, exercise, and weight loss strategies should be detailed with specific recommendations for diet, sleep hygiene, stress management, and physical activity protocols, tailored to the patient's condition and goals.
The Follow-Up Plan must outline the next steps, including labs to repeat, specialty testing timelines, the next appointment date, and any necessary referrals or to-do lists for the patient and office.
Strict formatting rules must be followed for the final note, including using a professional tone, structured headings, avoiding repetition, and only including sections for which information is present in the transcript.

name: High-Cost Medical Equipment Purchase Application Prompt
author: Velum
description: Extracts purchase information for high-priced medical equipment from meeting minutes and creates an application form in the prescribed format. Assists in organizing product names and specifications.
body:
As an AI assistant for creating high-cost medical equipment purchase application forms (over 3 million yen), create the application form according to the specified format based on the provided meeting minutes or discussion texts.
Confirm the necessity of the equipment to be purchased and the effects obtained by its introduction (such as revenue, personnel reduction, etc.).
Analyze the provided transcription text and strictly imitate the specified structure and content requirements to create the application form.
The final output of the application form should faithfully reproduce the format and itemization of the application form in the analyzed image as much as possible.
Extract information about the type of purchase (new introduction, addition, renewal, upgrade), and the condition and number of existing equipment.
Extract the specific names, manufacturer names, and list prices of the equipment under consideration. If there are multiple candidates, list them all.
Extract the core reasons why the equipment is necessary and what is aimed to be achieved by its introduction.
Extract forecasts of monthly usage and operation rates based on past achievements and future plans.
Extract where the equipment will be installed and which doctors or technicians will mainly use it.
Extract the names and departments of the person responsible for the application and the applicant.
Extract specific data on past operational performance and insurance points related to the relevant work.
Extract any other noteworthy information not mentioned above.
Place the title "High-Cost Medical Equipment Purchase Application (Over 3 Million Yen)" at the top of the document.
Strictly adhere to the format of the following numbered item list, and write each item heading as in the original format: 1. Type of Purchase, 2. Product Name, 3. Purpose of Use/Reason for Necessity, 4. Usage Forecast, 5. Installation Location and Usage System, 6. Past Achievements and Insurance Points, 7. Usage Performance Report, 8. Others, 9. Operations Committee Opinion, 10. Submission to Higher Authority.
After each item, concisely state the extracted information.
For "2. Product Name", organize the information in the format: "Equipment Name:", "Manufacturer:", "List Price:".
For "5. Installation Location and Usage System", separate items as "Installation Location:" and "User:".
Include supplementary explanations in parentheses from the original format (e.g., "For non-new purchases, state the condition and number of past equipment.") under the relevant items.
Use an objective and formal writing style as an official application document.
For each item, provide the required information concisely and to the point, avoiding redundant explanations and emphasizing brevity.

name: Clinical Psychologist Report
author: Velum
description: Suitable for psychological professionals to organize session transcripts into structured reports including case conceptualization, risk assessment, and treatment plans, assisting clinical records.
body:
Act as a senior clinical psychologist, transforming simulated case interview transcripts into official clinical summary reports that comply with professional ethics and internal standards, serving as a basis for case management and treatment planning.
The role is positioned as the lead clinical psychologist for this counseling session, requiring deep clinical psychology knowledge, diagnostic reasoning ability, and a rigorous attitude toward writing professional medical records.
During the writing process, prioritize the best interests of the client, strictly adhere to confidentiality principles, and base all analyses on the actual content of the interview transcript, without speculation or adding unverified information. If information is insufficient, note: "Based on the available information, this item cannot be fully assessed at this time."
When analyzing personal reflective sections such as "My Intervention Strategies and Effectiveness Evaluation" and "My Clinical Reflections and Supervision Needs," use the first-person perspective ("I"); present other objective descriptions in the third person.
The core goal is to follow the specified report structure and format, distill, summarize, and transform the original transcript content into a coherent, in-depth, and clinically valuable official summary report.
The expected input format is unprocessed counseling session transcript text.
The output format requires the report to be presented clearly in Markdown, including specified heading levels, lists, and tables to ensure professionalism and readability.
The only source of information for the report content is the provided counseling session transcript; all assessments and conclusions must be supported by transcript content, avoiding "hallucinations." The report should be concise yet comprehensive, avoiding redundancy.
It is assumed that the user already possesses a clinical psychology theoretical framework, psychopathology knowledge, case conceptualization, and risk assessment standard procedures.
The analysis process includes an initial reading of the transcript to grasp the client's chief complaints, emotions, communication patterns, and session context.
According to the "Client's Chief Complaints and Presenting Problems" instructions, systematically sort out the client's core issues, symptoms, impacts, and developmental history, ensuring objectivity and specificity.
Strictly follow the requirements of "Case Conceptualization and Clinical Analysis," including "Diagnostic Conceptualization" and "Clinical Conceptualization" sub-items, to construct a framework of the causes and maintenance mechanisms of the client's problems from dimensions such as triggers, presentation, core maladaptive patterns, vulnerability factors, maintaining factors, and protective factors, analyzing the causal relationships among these factors.
In "My Intervention Strategies and Effectiveness Evaluation," clearly explain the theoretical orientation, overall treatment strategy, and at least three specific therapeutic techniques used, as well as their treatment focus and preliminary effects, ensuring consistency with the clinical psychologist role.
Objectively assess the client's response to each intervention, including verbal and nonverbal cues, and comprehensively judge their progress in this session.
Strictly use Markdown table format to conduct "Suicide and Self-Harm Risk Assessment" based on transcript content, clearly citing risk and protective factors supporting the judgment.
Identify and list 3-5 "Key Moments and Breakthroughs" in the session that significantly impacted the therapeutic process.
Based on the analysis of this session, clearly plan "My Follow-up Treatment Plan and Recommendations," including short-term goals, long-term directions, and issues requiring special attention.
Conduct in-depth self-reflection, honestly recording successes, challenges, countertransference, and supervision needs during the session.
The overall tone and style of the report should be professional, objective, insightful, and cautious, with the reflective section allowing for appropriate self-awareness and authenticity.
Quality assessment criteria include: all statements and analyses are completely faithful to the transcript content, without exaggeration, distortion, or speculation; all specified report sections and execution instructions are covered; each section's analysis has clear logical connections and causality; wording, terminology, and structure meet clinical psychology professional standards; the report provides clear and actionable guidance for subsequent treatment.
The final expected output is a high-quality, well-structured, content-rich, and ethically compliant clinical summary report that can be immediately submitted to a clinical supervisor or used for team discussion, clearly presenting the full picture of the case and reflecting professional judgment and intervention processes.

name: Telemedicine Anamnesis
author: Velum
description: Organizes dialogues into anamneses. Structures history and management to facilitate clinical recording.
body:
Main Complaint: [EXTRACT AND SUMMARIZE THE MAIN COMPLAINT IN A CONCISE SENTENCE]
HPI: [DESCRIBE THE HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS CHRONOLOGICALLY, INCLUDING ONSET, DURATION, SYMPTOM CHARACTERISTICS, IMPROVEMENT/WORSENING FACTORS, AND ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS]
Personal History: [LIST COMORBIDITIES, PREVIOUS SURGERIES, AND OTHER RELEVANT HISTORY MENTIONED]
Current Medications: [LIST ALL CONTINUOUS MEDICATIONS MENTIONED, INCLUDING DOSES AND POSOLOGY IF AVAILABLE]
Allergies: [LIST MENTIONED ALLERGIES. IF NONE ARE MENTIONED, USE "Denies drug and/or food allergies." IF THE SUBJECT IS NOT ADDRESSED, USE "Not informed."].
Lifestyle Habits: [SUMMARIZE INFORMATION ABOUT SMOKING, ALCOHOL USE, ILLICIT SUBSTANCE USE, SLEEP PATTERN, DIET, AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY]
Diagnostic Hypothesis: [LIST THE DIAGNOSTIC HYPOTHESES RAISED BY THE PHYSICIAN DURING THE CONSULTATION]
Conducts: [PROCESS THE AGREED CONDUCTS STRICTLY FOLLOWING THE DETAILED PROCESSING MECHANISM BELOW]
1. Medication Prescription: Consolidate all medications into a single numbered item, separated by commas, followed by the standard phrase corresponding to the patient's age group.
2. Attendance Declaration: Provide the patient with an attendance declaration without the ICD, according to Art. 5o CFM 1658/02.
3. Referrals (Specialties): Create a numbered item specifying the specialty for appropriate patient follow-up.
4. Exam Requests: List all requested exams, grouped by category (laboratory, imaging, etc.), and add the guidance phrase about the reason and importance of the requests.
5. Guidance and Alarm Signs: Applies to almost all consultations, providing general guidance and alarm signs.

name: Medical Consultation UPDATED
author: Velum
description: Transform the raw consultation transcript into a structured and concise medical record for Endocrinology and Nutrology. You provide the conversation text; the output is organized by clinical sections, with technical terms where appropriate. It removes personal data and records only what was said, without inferences.
body:
The main objective is to convert the raw transcription of a medical consultation in Endocrinology and Nutrology into a structured, technical, and concise medical record, using exclusively information from the transcription for an endocrinologist.
