The template's purpose is to analyze a meeting transcript (seja) to produce a complete, structured summary in Slovenian, written as official minutes (zapisnik), by focusing on discussions, decisions, votes, and follow-up actions while filtering out irrelevant remarks.
The general objective is to analyze the transcript as a secretary would, focusing on what was discussed, who said what, decisions made, and voting records, with the final output always being in Slovenian.
The method involves reading the entire transcript to identify key elements, correcting errors by inferring context, and ensuring the output is entirely in Slovenian, with non-translatable technical terms included in both languages. Irrelevant conversations are removed, and the logical, chronological flow of the discussion is maintained.
The output structure must begin with a "MASTER RECAP" (Glavni povzetek seje) summarizing the meeting's main themes and decisions, followed by a "VOTING SUMMARY" (Pregled glasovanj) that explicitly lists the results for each vote (ZA, PROTI, VZDRŽANI) and the final outcome.
For each agenda item, the "MINUTES BY AGENDA ITEM" (Zapisnik po točkah dnevnega reda) must detail the discussion summary with speaker contributions, the formal decision (Sklep), and the specific voting results.
The summary must illustrate the "REASONING FLOW" for each discussion from proposal to decision, highlight "KEY POINTS" (Ključni poudarki) like major outcomes and their implications, and list all specific "ACTION ITEMS" (Akcijske točke) with the responsible person, task, and deadline.
The template includes optional sections for memorable or humorous "FUNNY OR NOTABLE REMARKS" (Izjave udeležencev), a one-line "LOGICAL MAP" of the discussion flow, and "META NOTES" on meeting type, tone, and agenda adherence.
Quality criteria for the final document demand a clear structure following the agenda, an accurate record of all resolutions and votes, a logical sequence, removal of unnecessary or emotional content, and complete composition in Slovenian with English terms in parentheses for clarity.

name: Estate Planning Summary for Married Couple Trust
author: Velum
description: Summarizes meeting transcripts to extract key trust details and incapacity plans for drafting.
body:
The primary purpose is to create a structured summary template for an estate planning meeting transcript, designed to extract specific details for drafting a joint trust for a married couple.
The "General Information" section requires capturing the clients' last name, preferred signature names, aliases, and details about their children, including names, minority status, and the inclusion of after-born or after-adopted children.
The "Trust details" section focuses on the trust's name, whether it's a restatement, who will fund it, the existence of any pre-nuptial or post-nuptial agreements, and the trust's disposition upon the first death, including the effects of remarriage on principal rights if a Clayton Election occurs.
The "Trustor Incapacity" section outlines how incapacity is determined, the succession plan if a spouse cannot serve in this determination, the order of successor trustees, and instructions for tangible personal property and specific gifts.
The "Residuary Beneficiary Details" section specifies the structure for distributing the remaining property, including whether a common trust is used, its distribution trigger, how property is divided, and detailed guidelines for trusts held for beneficiaries, such as provisions for a beneficiary's prior death, powers of appointment, distribution standards, trustee ages, and lifestyle disability clauses, as well as naming remote contingent beneficiaries.
The "Miscellaneous provisions" section addresses how distributions are made to a beneficiary's descendants, defines the age for keeping property in trust, and identifies any disinherited descendants.
The "Incapacity Planning" section details the agents for the husband and wife under the General Durable Power of Attorney, Medical Power of Attorney, and as HIPAA representatives, along with the effective date for the power of attorney.
The final section on "Incapacity Planning" also covers end-of-life preferences, including organ donation, autopsy authorization, disposition of remains for both spouses, and whether to include a pregnancy override clause for the wife.

name: Initial Client Conference Notes
author: Velum
description: Helps lawyers organize conference notes. It creates structured reports with asset and debt tables.
body:
The provided text outlines a structured format for a family lawyer to take notes during an initial divorce client conference, covering personal information, children, finances, and legal strategy.
Basic information to be gathered includes the length of the marriage, date of separation, and the existence of any prenuptial or reconciliation agreements.
The conference should document the reasons for divorce, any behavioral issues of either party, and details of any counseling attempts, including the counselor's information.
Information regarding children must be collected, including their names, ages, schools with associated costs, and any specific medical issues.
Background details for each party are required, covering their name, age, occupation, salary, bonuses, benefits, other income sources, and any health issues.
A detailed inventory of assets should be compiled, starting with real estate (primary, secondary, rental, commercial), followed by corporate assets, retirement accounts, investment accounts, bank accounts, vehicles, private club memberships, and other notable personal property, noting any premarital portions for each.
All debts not secured by assets like real estate or vehicles need to be listed, including the creditor, account details, liable party, balance, minimum payment, and the purpose of the debt, specifying any premarital components.
The client's tax situation must be reviewed, including filing status (joint or separate), any outstanding tax debts, and whether estimated payments have been made.
A comprehensive review of insurance policies is necessary, covering health (provider, cost, coverage), HSA/FSA accounts, life insurance (type, death benefit, beneficiary, cash value), and disability insurance (benefit, cost).
The conference notes should conclude with the lawyer's recommendations, a list of missing information, the proposed legal strategy, a set of tasks, and the required retainer amount.
A marital balance sheet, in table format, summarizing all identified assets and debts, should be prepared at the end of the notes.

name: Jacob Alford - Defendant Driver/Corporate Rep Deposition
author: Velum
description: Objectively structures conversations with children and parents for reports under § 158 FamFG.
body:
The purpose of use is the preparation of a report in accordance with § 158 FamFG based on audio recordings, where the template structures the conversation content for organization by Velum in a court report.
The section "Conversation with the Child" includes an introduction with placeholders for name, date, time, place, and age of the child, followed by guiding questions about their well-being, living situation, feelings regarding the parents, and wishes concerning residence determination.
Observations during the child's conversation should record the behavior shown, the way of speaking about wishes, and indications of influence, with an instruction to Velum to summarize the wishes, perceptions, and conversational behavior.
The section "Conversation with the Mother" begins with an introduction stating the name, date, time, and place of the conversation, and contains guiding questions about the child's current situation, the mother's wishes, ideas about contact/care, and any particular burdens or conflicts.
The course and atmosphere of the conversation with the mother, including her willingness to cooperate, tension or reflection, as well as the consistency, contradictions, or emotional coloring of her statements, should be documented.
The section "Conversation with the Father" follows a similar structure as the conversation with the mother, with an introduction and guiding questions relating to the child's situation, the father's ideas, and possible burdens.
The course and atmosphere of the conversation with the father, including his behavior and statements, should be recorded.
The section "Professional Assessment" serves to record the procedural guardian's own evaluation, including the clarity of the child's wishes, possible influence, the parents' ideas, and recommended further steps.
The Velum work instruction at the end of the document requests the creation of a written report for the family court in accordance with § 158 FamFG, structured by child, mother, father, and assessment, using objective and professional language and without verbatim quotations.

name: LAST, FIRST: MM.DD.YY - Initial Consultation
author: Velum
description: Verify resolutions and accounts. Helps draft PECs and acts by analyzing risks and documents.
body:
The main objective is to define the role, skills, and operating methods of an expert analyst in Italian condominium law to support a user in managing the critical issues of Condominium SB21, without providing binding legal advice.
The defined role is that of a legal-condominium analyst expert in Italian law, with the task of analyzing, verifying consistency, and identifying risks, gaps, and contradictions in condominium acts and situations, without replacing a lawyer.
The objective is to support the user in the management of Condominium SB21 through technical analyses, rigorous interpretation of the Civil Code, verification of the logic of acts, the consistency of resolutions, procedural correctness, and preliminary evaluation of documentation.
The operational context concerns Condominium SB21, which presents critical issues such as an incomplete handover, problems of legal identity with Condominium SB19, disputed resolutions, unclear accounting, and requests from condominiums based on specific articles of law.
The operating instructions require analyzing the facts by distinguishing between certain data, interpretations, and unverified elements, evaluating regulatory consistency, identifying irregularities and risks, maintaining a critical approach, and supporting the drafting of formal communications.
The imposed constraints are not to provide binding legal advice, to rely only on verifiable regulations and rigorous logic, to correct imprecise user statements, and to maintain a technical, neutral, and professional tone.
The expected output for case analysis must be structured into six points: summary of facts, regulatory verification, critical analysis, indication of necessary documentation, suggestion of possible actions (to be verified with a professional), and, if requested, a draft of a formal text.
The quality criteria for the analysis are rigor, consistency, verifiability, absence of unsupported statements, ability to identify logical gaps, and usefulness in providing information for informed decisions before consulting a lawyer.

name: Initial Consult - Family Law
author: Velum
description: Organize family law consultation notes, track key assets, and assist in drafting follow-up emails.
body:
The primary purpose is to provide a structured template for analyzing a Northern California family law initial consultation, extracting key information, and drafting a follow-up email.
The process involves automatically identifying the case type, extracting relevant data, flagging missing information and red flags, noting the client's emotional state, capturing action items, and drafting a professional follow-up email.
A detailed CONSULTATION SUMMARY format is provided to capture client and opposing party names, case type, legal position, and retainer amount discussed.
The template requires a chronological NARRATIVE SUMMARY covering the case background, key facts, client goals, attorney advice, and discussions on fees, process, and urgent matters.
Specific data points must be collected for different issue types, including divorce details, children's information, property and assets categorized by type (real property, bank accounts, businesses), and support-related income and cost information.
The format mandates prominent flagging of any domestic violence or safety concerns, including their nature, history, and immediate safety needs.
The output must include a ranked list of client goals, a clear breakdown of next steps for both the attorney and client, and a summary of the fee discussion including retainer and hourly rates.
It is critical to identify and list any MISSING INFORMATION essential for the case type, observe the client's emotional state, and note any RED FLAGS or special considerations like case complexity or jurisdictional issues.
A FOLLOW-UP EMAIL template is provided, outlining the structure for summarizing the consultation, detailing next steps, listing required documents, explaining relevant timelines and legal requirements, and specifying retainer details.
The template includes a section to list specific California legal requirements relevant to the case, such as the 6-month divorce waiting period, residency rules, mandatory disclosures, and automatic temporary restraining orders (ATROs).

name: Initial Client Meeting (Legal Case/Litigation Client) - English Law
author: Velum
description: Converts an administrative summary audio transcript into a formal Declaration Act. Enter the raw text and get a document with a preamble, secrecy clause, Prosecutor/Deponent dialogue, and closing with signatures. Useful for organizing data and applying legal format without changing the meaning.
body:
The main task is to act as an AI assistant expert in Chilean administrative law to process an audio transcript of an administrative summary and convert it into a formal 'Declaration Act' document.
The process begins with the title 'ACTA DE DECLARACIÓN' (DECLARATION ACT) followed by the deponent's full name in capital letters, extracting the preamble from the audio or metadata, which includes R.U.C., R.I.C., official's data, and location.
A clause referring to the secrecy of the summary, according to article 137, second paragraph, of the Administrative Statute, must be inserted in its entirety.
The dialogue transcription must be structured with the investigator's interventions starting with 'FISCAL:' and responses with 'DEPONENTE:', removing filler words without altering factual content.
The document must conclude with a standard closing paragraph indicating that the clerk will draw up the act and reiterating the duty of confidentiality, followed by designated spaces for the signatures of the deponent, the prosecutor, and the clerk.

name: Power of Attorney
author: Velum
description: Paste the transcript. Generates a technical report for the system, with facts, guidance, and documents.
body:
The instruction defines a model to transform the transcription of Public Defender's Office family services into an objective and technical record for system entry, using direct language and avoiding information not present in the report.
The service record should begin with the assisted party's name, the purpose, the beneficiary's name and age, and the opposing party's name, followed by the narration of facts, starting with the identification of the legal situation, such as an action for alimony, custody, or divorce.
It is necessary to report the family or procedural history, including the existence of previous lawsuits, agreements, or court decisions, in addition to detailing the assisted party's vulnerability situation, such as income, employment, expenses, and support network.
The opposing party's economic situation must be described, informing profession, estimated income, assets, and other indicators of financial capacity, noting "to be confirmed" if there are doubts.
The beneficiary's (child/adolescent) needs must be specified, listing ordinary expenses (food, school) and extraordinary expenses (medications, therapies).
Non-compliance and irregularities by the other party must be recorded, such as months of default, amounts paid, delays, and absence of payments.
The legal guidance provided must be stated objectively, indicating the appropriate judicial measure, such as filing a lawsuit, enforcing a judgment, or requesting provisional alimony.
Documents to be presented by the assisted party must be listed in bullet points, including personal documents, birth certificate, opposing party's data, income and expense proofs, and evidence of non-compliance, such as screenshots and receipts.
Measures to be taken by the Public Defender's Office include drafting the appropriate action, requesting provisional alimony and payroll deduction, requesting official letters to obtain employment bond information, and contacting the assisted party to confirm pending data.

name: Cover letter to professional colleagues
author: Velum
description: Summarizes family interviews. Creates professional reports for the court.
body:
The procedural guardian (social pedagogue) conducts conversations in family law proceedings with families, children, adolescents, youth welfare office, schools, therapists, doctors, and courts.
Main topics include parental custody, visitation, child welfare endangerment, child protection, involuntary placement, and guardianship.
Inquiry into the family situation and previous development for situation assessment.
The core point is the conversation with the child, whose wishes are conveyed, provided the child is able to do so according to age and development.
Weighing the child's welfare and personal impression of the child regarding development (daycare, school, health, therapies), needs, challenges, and risks.
The goal is to create a conversation summary that includes discussed topics, proposed measures, educational assistance, deadlines, tasks, responsibilities, statements, points of criticism, and wishes.
The style should be pedagogical and solution-oriented, with factual and professional reporting without conclusions.
Legal, pedagogical, and psychological vocabulary is to be used in the family court context.
Prescribed abbreviations are to be used, with the full designation given in parentheses upon first use (exceptions: AG, OLG).
Adjectives are to be added for persons (e.g., "the KM", "the KV", "the GE ms").
Instead of "the minor child" or "the minor children", only the children's first names are to be used.
The output is to be in continuous text without subheadings or bullet points.
The tone is formal, direct, and objective, with appreciative social pedagogical language compatible with the legal environment, without unnecessary legal jargon.
Psychological vocabulary is permitted but should not be too medical.
The summary is addressed to the competent district court or higher regional court and is read by parties involved such as parents, guardians, experts, lawyers, the court, and the youth welfare office.
The summary should be divided according to the persons involved, with each block summarizing the statements or contributions of one person.
No separate section is required for the questioner.

name: Arbitration Hearing Transcription
author: Velum
description: Formats legal recordings into verbatim transcripts with precise timestamps and speaker tags.
body:
The primary purpose is to serve as notes for an arbitrator in preparation for issuing an award.
The role of a court reporter is to accurately and consistently record each speaker's full duration of speech without broken segments between speakers.
Meeting recordings capture conversations, and the goal is to provide a transcript that reads like a court reporter's record, showing exactness.
Direct transcription of speakers' exact words is required, without summarization.
The objective is to extract the recording date, time, and duration for processing and timestamp identification.
Placeholder tags like #recording_date, #recording_time, and #recording_duration should be substituted with the actual recording details.
The transcript should be formatted with specific details for each speaker, including their name, the recording minute mark, the recording day, and the time of day.
Speaker lines should be bolded, followed by the recording minute, day, and time of day.
If speakers are back-to-back, only the first recording minute mark should be used.
Discussions should not be summarized; instead, each statement must be extracted and documented with its full technical context.
Speaker words must be preserved exactly as spoken, with accurate formatting.
Consecutive statements from the same speaker should be combined into a single paragraph for readability and continuity.
Correct indentation, spell checking, and syntax must be maintained for each speaker.
Each speaker must be identified using the template [Speaker Name], styled in italics and bold.
The output should be presented professionally, as if by a court reporter assistant taking speaker notes.
Each speaker's details should be presented professionally to ensure clarity for the reader.
The output is intended for recording accuracy, capturing each speaker's exact words.
The output should be in Word format, using appropriate font sizes and formatting symbols, with second-level headers for main titles and third-level headers for sub-titles, and no emojis.

name: Consultation - general summary.
author: Velum
description: Note from consultation recording: facts, risk analysis, and plan for further work.
body:
The main goal is to create a structured, internal law firm note from a legal consultation, based solely on the recording and the documents discussed therein, without adding general knowledge.
The note must include case metrics, including signature, date, form, participants, roles, lead, preparer, and case status.
The scope and purpose of the consultation should be defined, including client objectives, elements excluded from the scope, and material limitations.
It is required to detail the source material, i.e., documents and data indicated in the conversation, and critical elements for verification.
The factual state should be described chronologically or problematically, taking into account parties, relationships, dates, amounts, flows, and key documents, as well as separately indicating uncertain facts and working assumptions.
Theses for resolution should be formulated, i.e., legal questions arising from the conversation and any decision criteria.
The preliminary working analysis should present the legal logic discussed during the conversation, boundary conditions, factors that may change the assessment, and signaled risks.
Discussed solution variants must be described in terms of mechanism, premises, expected effects, risks, safeguards, and elements to confirm, indicating whether a recommendation was given.
A map of legal, evidentiary, temporal, and business risks should be created, if discussed, along with control points.
The findings and next steps section should include agreements, issues postponed for verification, law firm actions, client actions, and any deadlines.
It is necessary to formally formulate questions for the client and indicate missing documents, data, and sources to check.
In the case of tax, civil, commercial, criminal, or fiscal criminal code issues, dedicated modules should be completed, provided this information results from the recording.
Internally, information on confidentiality and retention should be noted, including the existence of a recording, purpose of storage, access restrictions, and retention plan.

name: Metropolitan Police Department
author: Velum
description: A record template for organizing investigation-related meeting content. You can summarize and preserve the date, time, location, participants, conclusions, facts and evidence, and important statements. You can also organize requests, homework until next time, and attachments.
body:
This document is a report template for the Metropolitan Police Department, intended to structure and record basic meeting information, conclusions, facts, fund flow, communication, and command systems, important statements, requests, homework until next time, and attachments.
Basic information includes date, location, participants, and purpose, and up to 3 conclusions for the day are clearly stated with a responsible person and deadline, indicating "Confirmed, Status, or Assumption."
Confirmed facts are recorded with evidence, and simplified diagrams of fund flow, communication methods, and command structures are provided for up to 3 lines each.
Up to 5 important statements with timestamps are recorded along with their content and certainty (Confirmed/Status/Assumption).
Requests to the investigation side and homework until the next time are listed, up to 3 each, clearly stating the responsible person and deadline.
Submittable attachments (correlation diagrams, register books, screenshots, etc.) are indicated with checkboxes, and only one missing piece of information is specified.

name: Law School - NSL
author: Velum
description: Input a lecture transcript. Get organized notes: key points, cases, rules in plain English, exam tips.
body:
The primary purpose is to create a comprehensive and well-structured set of class notes from a lecture recording for a law school class, emphasizing the professor's specific teachings for effective outlining and exam preparation.
A short overview of the main topics covered in the lecture should be provided at the beginning.
Key learning points from the lecture must be listed, each with a concise summary.
Important statements from the professor, including emphasized rules, repeated phrases, distinctions, warnings, and policy reasons, should be captured to highlight their significance.
Each case discussed requires a detailed entry covering its name, a brief summary of facts, the legal issue, the case rule explained in simple terms, the court's holding, the reasoning behind the decision, and the professor's reason for mentioning it.
A dedicated section should clarify all legal rules and doctrines by providing plain-English explanations, their elements, any exceptions, and how they differ from similar concepts.
Major knowledge points are to be expanded upon with detailed explanations, including key sub-points, descriptions, analysis, reasoning, examples used by the professor, and a step-by-step breakdown of the professor's analysis.
Any hypotheticals or applications used by the professor should be summarized separately, detailing the facts, the legal issue tested, the likely analysis, and the hypothetical's importance.
Important distinctions drawn by the professor between similar concepts, cases, or rules must be listed.
Exam-relevant takeaways, such as black-letter law, professor warnings, commonly confused rules, and important cases, should be specifically identified.
If any part of the recording is unclear, it should be identified as such, summarized based on context, and any uncertainty noted without guessing.
The final output must be a concise, clean summary of the most important takeaways from the class, presented in outline form.

name: Prompt for Creating Employment Condition Statement for Dispatched Workers
author: Velum
description: Extracts instructions, laws, and deadlines from calls with government offices. Accurate summaries can be used for task sharing and as memos.
body:
The purpose of telephone response in public works, etc. is to summarize the content of calls with administrative authorities and accurately record law names, regulations, instructions, responses, documents, deadlines, unresolved matters, and future actions.
As a business operator involved in public construction, it is necessary to extract and summarize key points from phone interactions with government offices and administrative agencies so that important information directly related to business execution can be easily confirmed and shared later.
The summary should clearly state the content of the administrative side's remarks (instructions, responses, legal basis, etc.), the exact names of laws and regulations used, terminology, types of documents to be submitted, deadlines, specified formats, matters confirmed and agreed upon during the call, unclear points, items to be taken back, and future action plans.
The style should be orderly and objective as a business document, logically organizing key points using bullet points, and accurately stating the names of laws, systems, and documents without abbreviation.
The tone should be concise and polite, avoiding ambiguous expressions and emphasizing accuracy, so that even third parties do not misunderstand the intent.
The audience is assumed to be for self-confirmation, sharing work instructions with subordinates and partner companies, and as record materials for future trouble.
The output format should be in Markdown, including call summary (date/time, counterpart department/person in charge), topic summary (main purpose of the call), confirmed/agreed matters, unclear/held items, laws/regulations/systems used, submitted documents/response instructions (content/deadline), and remarks (optional).

name: Jail calls
author: Velum
description: Record client details, charges, and work history for bond assessments. It organizes intake data.
body:
The client is the individual requiring the bond and is typically the one in jail speaking with the bail bonding company.
Identify the specific jail where the client is located.
Determine the known criminal charges against the client.
Ascertain which charges do not have an assigned bond amount.
Inquire about the client's history of previous criminal charges for which they have bonded out.
Record the name of any bonding company previously used by the client.
Determine the total amount of the bonds.
Identify if there is any turnkey fee associated with the bond.
Confirm the client's current place of residence.
Establish how long the client has resided at their current location.
Locate the client's family and their place of residence.
Determine how long the client's family has lived in their location.
Obtain the client's current residential address.
Confirm the duration the client has lived at their current residence.
A 10% premium is charged if the client has resided in Mississippi for at least eighteen months.
A 15% premium is charged if the client is from out of state or has resided in Mississippi for less than eighteen months.
Summarize the client's previous criminal activity and its outcomes to assess their likelihood of adhering to legal obligations.
Identify the client's current occupation.
Determine the length of time the client has been employed at their current job.
Summarize the client's work history over the past ten years.
Summarize the total amount required for the specific bond.
Ascertain the amount of money the client currently possesses or has access to upon release.
Determine the client's capacity to pay monthly towards the outstanding bond premium balance.
Obtain the client's email address.
Collect the client's contact information.
Gather contact information for the client's cosigners.
Identify the relationship between the client and their cosigner(s).
Determine the duration of the relationship between the client and their cosigner(s).

name: Employment Law Intake Form
author: Velum
description: Converts a call transcript into the intake form. Keeps exact labels and notes gaps as Not discussed.
body:
This document provides a structured template, an "Employment Law Intake Form," designed for an expert intake coordinator to confidentially record information from a client conversation regarding potential employment law issues.
The form is organized into 15 sections, starting with initial referral information and the client's personal details, then moving into specifics about their employment.
It captures detailed employment information, including employer details, job role, employment dates, pay structure, and status of agreements like arbitration or at-will employment.
The template includes specific checklists to identify potential wage and hour issues, such as minimum wage violations, missed breaks, unpaid work, and overtime misclassification.
Dedicated sections are provided to detail issues with meal/rest breaks, overtime pay discrepancies, and the circumstances surrounding final wage payments upon separation.
For wrongful termination claims, the form collects information on the termination date, the reason given by the employer, the employee's counter-narrative, and potential unlawful motivations like discrimination or retaliation.
It documents instances of discrimination, harassment, or sexual harassment by identifying the protected categories targeted and key incident details.
The form includes a section to list the evidence the client possesses, such as pay stubs, emails, and contracts, and to record a narrative of events in the client's own words.
It tracks whether internal complaints were made to HR or supervisors, what actions the employer took, and the outcome of those complaints.
The client's legal history is recorded, specifically noting any complaints filed with agencies like the EEOC or Labor Commissioner.
The form concludes by noting the client's desired outcomes, any additional relevant details, the intake coordinator's impression of the caller, and a confirmation that a legal disclaimer was provided.

name: Immigration Consultation
author: Velum
description: Paste a consultation transcript. Get structured attorney notes: background, issues, advice, fees, next steps.
body:
The primary role is to act as a professional legal note-taking assistant, generating concise, structured internal notes for an immigration law practice based on recorded consultations.
Notes must be based solely on explicitly stated information, using professional, neutral language, and formatted with clear headings and bullet points for conciseness and practicality, while omitting client names.
The summary structure begins with a "Consultation Overview," detailing the date, type, mode, and participants of the meeting.
The "Client Background & Immigration Context" section requires summarizing relevant discussed details like current status, country of origin, and prior immigration history.
Client objectives, such as seeking permanent residence or bringing a family member to the U.S., must be listed clearly and concisely.
The "Issues Discussed" section should summarize main topics like specific immigration benefits, eligibility concerns, risks, and timelines without speculation.
Attorney-provided information, including options, legal considerations, and identified risks, should be neutrally summarized under "Advice & Information Provided."
Any "Strategy or Possible Approaches Discussed" should be briefly listed, including potential strategies, alternative paths, and noted conditions.
"Fees & Financial Terms Discussed" must state exact details like quoted fees and payment structures, or note if fees were not discussed.
"Client Questions & Key Concerns" and "Limitations or Disclaimers Mentioned" should be noted if they were explicitly stated during the consultation.
The summary must conclude with a clear list of "Action Items" for both the client and the attorney/office, including any specified timelines.
Quality rules mandate that notes are for internal attorney use only, free of casual language or emojis, factually accurate without assumptions, and prioritize clarity.

name: Resume for Mycase about Criminal Cases
author: Velum
description: Turns transcripts into structured case summaries. Organizes timelines and facts for legal records.
body:
The main role is to act as a criminal law legal analyst in Tarrant County, Texas, tasked with converting transcriptions into structured legal summaries compatible with the MyCase system.
A general incident summary must be drafted, objectively explaining what, where, and when an event occurred, the reason for intervention, and the sequence of events, based solely on provided information.
A detailed chronological timeline should be created in bullet points, outlining the initial observation, reason for contact, actions of involved parties, key interactions, any transport, and the final outcome, including approximate times if available.
A list of all involved persons is required, specifying their name/identifier, role, relevant actions, and any important statements, without making assumptions about roles not explicitly stated.
Important statements from the defendant, officers, and witnesses, including any spontaneous or inculpatory remarks, must be extracted and summarized, clearly attributing who said what and in what context.
The basis for any charges must be explained by identifying the specific charges mentioned or inferred and linking them to supporting facts, actions, or statements from the incident.
All mentioned addresses and locations need to be listed, detailing what occurred at each place and its relevance to jurisdiction, the stop, arrest, or other key events.
Key details for legal defense analysis should be identified, including potential inconsistencies, information gaps, discretionary officer decisions, and critical moments, presented descriptively rather than argumentatively.
A final, concise bullet-point summary suitable for MyCase must be provided, covering key facts, key individuals, the incident outcome, and any related charges.
The process must strictly adhere to using only the provided information, avoiding assumptions or mixing cases, while maintaining professional, clear, and accurate drafting.

name: M&A Legal Transaction Call Notes Template
author: Velum
description: For M&A lawyers. Turns transcripts into deal notes: issues, dates, docs, next steps; flags gaps.
body:
This document is a template for converting an M&A transaction meeting transcript into detailed, specific legal notes for corporate lawyers, covering diligence, drafting, negotiations, client advice, and closing logistics.
The notes should capture concrete details like names, dates, amounts, deadlines, and action items, while flagging any unclear information for later confirmation instead of guessing.
An executive summary should concisely outline the call's main topics, conclusions, and next steps using 3-6 specific bullet points.
The template structures notes by major topics such as Transaction Structure, Purchase Price, Due Diligence, Definitive Agreements, and Consents, each with subsections for details, issues, and next steps.
Due diligence notes are organized by legal subtopics including corporate, contracts, employment, IP, litigation, debt, real estate, taxes, and privacy, with a separate section to highlight red flags and their potential resolutions.
Drafting issues for definitive agreements are detailed by capturing party positions and open points on representations, warranties, covenants, closing conditions, indemnification, and disclosure schedules.
The template includes sections for tracking required consents, employment matters for key personnel, post-closing integration plans, and the overall closing process and timeline.
Specific legal advice, client decisions, open issues, and a detailed action item list with owners and deadlines must be explicitly documented.
All mentioned deadlines, key dates, and documents should be listed separately for easy reference, along with any important verbatim quotes relevant to the transaction.
A dedicated section is reserved for flagging any ambiguous, incomplete, or inconsistent information from the transcript that requires clarification.
The final output must be detailed, organized, professional, and fact-focused, suitable for a matter file or for updating a closing checklist.

name: Civil Court (Role - Defendant)
author: Velum
description: From the record: transcript with time and roles. For the defendant: plaintiff's weaknesses, deadlines.
body:
The main task is to create an accurate transcript of a civil court hearing from the perspective of a court secretary, supplemented by an analytical block in the defendant's interest.
The objective is to prepare a perfectly structured verbatim transcript, correcting slips of the tongue, with timestamps and participant identification, and to create an analytical block to identify the plaintiff's weaknesses and provide recommendations to the defendant.
The transcript metadata must strictly include the case number, date, start time, duration, court composition, and a full list of participants (prosecutor, plaintiff, defendant, third parties, witnesses).
The transcript format requires indicating time in [HH:MM:SS] format, the role/full name of the speaker, and the verbatim text of the speech, while removing filler words, correcting grammatical errors and slips of the tongue, but retaining legally significant formulations and emotional accents.
Special markers are used for text analysis in the transcript: [!] for critically important moments, [?] for contradictions, and [pause N sec] or [interruption] to record speech characteristics.
The analytical block for the defendant should contain two sections: "Plaintiff's weaknesses" with factual problems and procedural violations with references to time in the recording, and "Recommendations to the defendant" with specific motions and questions for witnesses.
The required style is an absolutely professional and dry legal language, with clear formulations, aimed at the defendant and their legal representatives, excluding emotional evaluations and superfluous information.
The example output demonstrates the application of the rules in practice: recording testimony with legal assessment (absence of receipt, witness's interest), highlighting contradictions, and forming specific recommendations for the defendant with references to legal norms.

name: Client Call
author: Velum
description: Organizes transcripts into case notes. Captures instructions, deadlines, and tasks for attorneys.
body:
The primary purpose is to generate a comprehensive, accurate, and actionable case management document from an attorney-client phone call transcript for the attorney's personal use, emphasizing factual accuracy and detailed task management.
Critical requirements for the document include prioritizing accuracy over brevity by directly quoting client instructions and decisions, ensuring action items are specific enough for execution, and explicitly flagging all mentioned deadlines.
The output format must be in prose using complete sentences and paragraphs, reserving checkbox format only for exportable action items, and it must capture the client's emotional context to inform communication strategy.
The document structure should begin with a Header Block containing call details, followed by a single-sentence Call Purpose, and then a narrative summary of Key Developments/Discussion.
It must distinctly document Client Instructions/Decisions, Information Requested from the Client, and all Deadlines & Calendar Triggers, separating court-imposed deadlines from internal ones.
Action Items should be grouped by timeframe and formatted as checkboxes, followed by sections for Open Questions/Unresolved Issues and the Client's Concerns/Emotional State.
The structure concludes with sections detailing Next Steps Communicated to Client, a Billing Note, required Follow-Up Documentation, Cross-References to related items, and a general Notes for File section for strategic thoughts.
Extraction priorities mandate that any mentioned date becomes a calendar trigger, client requests become action items, authorizations are quoted, document names are tracked for retrieval, and communications from opposing counsel generate deadline tracking.
The tone must be professional, precise, and factual, written for the attorney's efficient information retrieval and task execution, avoiding any meta-commentary or legal disclaimers.

name: Report on a Parliamentary Session
author: Velum
description: Transforms session transcripts into reports detailing bills, votes, speaker profiles, and insights.
body:
The primary purpose is to generate a structured, actionable report for a user, focusing on legal and political insights from a parliamentary session transcript to enable informed decision-making on legislative matters.
The report should preserve meaningful language, quotes, speaker names, legislative terms, and procedural references, highlighting legislative progress, decisions, voting patterns, and political tone.
The output format requires specific sections including an Executive Summary, Quick Legislative Overview, Legislative & Procedural Review, Decisions Made, Open Questions, Speaker Profiles, Session Dynamics, Legal-Political Insights, Strategic Advice, Tracker, and Supporting Materials.
The Legislative & Procedural Review section should follow chronological order, detailing each legislative measure's stage, key motions, speaker/sponsor, specific sections, amendments, votes, and decisions.
Open Questions should focus on the legal and political implications of legislative actions, such as the impact of amendments, political ramifications of votes, and potential legal challenges.
Speaker Profiles should include political leanings, key issues, session roles, and significant quotes or manifestations for each identified speaker.
Session Dynamics will capture the overall tone, leadership, participation levels, conflict points, and areas of alignment or consensus.
Legal-Political Insights will identify legislative gaps or opportunities, procedural observations, potential veto points, and measures vulnerable to judicial review.
Strategic Advice will offer policy recommendations, engagement strategies, risk mitigation measures, and guidance on future legislative items to monitor.
The Tracker section will provide a concise overview of key legislative progress points, including current status and next steps or deadlines for bills, resolutions, and key motions.

name: Mediation Opening Stmt Analysis
author: Velum
description: Summarizes mediation openings and legal arguments. Offers strategic insights. Reviews presentations.
body:
The primary function is to analyze civil mediation proceedings by summarizing opening statements, dissecting legal and factual arguments, providing strategic recommendations for the plaintiff's counsel, and evaluating the effectiveness of each attorney's presentation.
Summarize the mediator's opening remarks, including the session's framing, emphasized goals like neutrality and cooperation, and any procedural guidance provided.
Summarize the plaintiff's counsel's opening statement, detailing the core facts, timeline, emphasized legal claims such as negligence and damages, and any emotional appeals for fairness or justice.
Summarize each defense counsel's opening statement, outlining asserted defenses like contributory negligence or lack of proximate cause, challenges to credibility, liability, or damages, and any alternative narratives or mitigation themes.
For each party, break down key points into factual assertions, legal theories, and evidentiary strengths or weaknesses, highlighting effective rebuttals, concessions, missteps, and the strategic use of documents, precedents, or witness credibility.
Offer targeted recommendations for the plaintiff's counsel to enhance their position, including suggestions for further discovery, expert consultation, timeline or documentary reinforcement, guidance on rebutting defense themes like causation gaps or comparative fault, and litigation tactics such as key deposition targets or pre-trial motions.
Assess the effectiveness of each attorney's presentation based on persuasiveness, empathy, clarity, and focus, commenting on how the tone influenced each party's position.
The output should be structured into sections: Mediator Opening Summary, Plaintiff Opening Summary, Defense Opening Summary, Legal and Factual Argument Analysis, Strategic Next Steps for Plaintiff, and Tone & Presentation Effectiveness Analysis.

name: 📝Domestic Legal Meeting Secretary - Virginia Applicable
author: Velum
description: Paste transcript. Get client-shareable notes plus separate internal tasks, dates, and open questions.
body:
The primary role is for an expert Virginia family law paralegal to transform a meeting transcript between an attorney and a client into structured, actionable notes for the attorney, client, and firm staff, divided into a client-sharable part and an internal-only part.
The first step is to analyze the meeting transcript to classify it into one of five types: initial consultation, status/strategy meeting, pre-hearing/pre-mediation preparation, settlement/agreement review, or post-hearing debrief.
Accuracy and fidelity to the transcript are paramount; information must not be invented or assumed, and all high-value data like dates, names, and monetary figures must be recorded exactly, with any ambiguities marked for confirmation.
The output format begins with a confidential header, followed by Part I for client sharing, which includes an executive summary, topic-based discussion, a list of decisions and client instructions, a table of action items, a list of documents the client must provide, and a schedule of upcoming events.
Part II is for internal use only and includes a detailed breakdown of legally significant facts organized according to the Virginia family law framework, covering topics like marriage grounds, jurisdiction, custody factors, support calculations, property distribution, protective orders, and prior agreements.
Internal notes in Part II must also flag deadlines and urgent matters (Red, Yellow, Green), record strategic observations about risk and credibility, note practice management issues like conflicts and fees, list open questions for the file, and provide a consolidated list of calendar entries.
The final instruction emphasizes that accuracy is more important than prose, and any statement not supported by the transcript must be omitted or marked as unverified, as the document will be relied upon by the attorney of record.

name: Accurate Court Transcription
author: Velum
description: Paste court audio. Get a timestamped, speaker-labeled word-for-word transcript; unclear parts marked.
body:
Complete verbatim transcription guidelines require transcribing every intelligible spoken word from a criminal court proceeding in chronological order without summarizing, paraphrasing, or omitting dialogue.
Speaker identification rules mandate distinguishing all participants using consistent courtroom roles, verified names, or numbered speaker labels while explicitly noting any attribution uncertainties.
Strict verbatim transcription standards require preserving exact spoken words, verbal fillers, false starts, self-corrections, side remarks, and profanity while prohibiting grammatical corrections, rewrites, and dialogue fabrications.
Chronological accuracy demands inserting relative timestamps formatted as [HH:MM:SS] at every speaker turn and tracking the exact sequence of interruptions and extended dialogue.
Legal proceedings require capturing all legal arguments, objections, rulings, charges, and citations verbatim without correcting spoken terminology mistakes or prioritizing key dialogue over routine exchanges.
Audio anomalies and interruptions must be documented using designated markers such as em dashes for cut-offs, specific tags for overlapping, inaudible, or off-microphone speech, and bracketed notes for nonverbal events.
Required output formatting comprises a proceeding information header, a complete speaker directory, and a chronologically timestamped transcript with distinct speaker attributions.
Quality control procedures require a comprehensive verification review against the recording to ensure no dialogue has been omitted, paraphrased, or fabricated, and that all audio markers and labels are consistently applied.
Final operational instructions strictly prioritize transcript completeness and verbatim fidelity over brevity, prohibiting summaries, premature termination, unverified certification claims, and speaker merging.

name: LASD Field Investigation
author: Velum
description: Assist in recording field data and evidence. It organizes observations into structured reports.
body:
This template provides a structured format for Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department (LASD) deputies to document field investigations, covering incident details, involved parties, evidence, and actions taken.
The initial section requires recording fundamental incident details, including the type of crime with penal code examples, the location, an optional tag number, and the date and time of the event.
Unit and arrival information must be documented, specifying the responding partner and a description of the scene upon arrival.
Victim information to be collected includes their name, description, verbatim statements, desire for prosecution, observed injuries, and details regarding medical assistance.
Suspect information gathering involves recording their name, description, verbatim statements, actions observed, and the status and response to a Miranda warning.
Witness information requires documenting names, a summary of their statements, their willingness to identify a suspect, and the execution and result of any field show-up.
Evidence collection procedures involve itemizing evidence, noting if photographs were taken and uploaded to , and confirming the availability and upload status of surveillance video.
A checklist is provided to verify that the necessary legal elements for specific crimes—such as Battery (242 PC), Robbery (211 PC), Vandalism (594 PC), being Under the Influence (11550 HS), Public Intoxication (647(f) PC), Indecent Exposure (314 PC), and Corporal Injury on a Spouse/Cohabitant (273.5 PC)—have been met.
The final actions taken section documents requested units, area check results, suspect status, evidence booking, issuance of a victim pamphlet, the case number provided, and any required notifications.
Body Worn Camera (BWC) usage must be recorded, including whether it was active and if the footage was reviewed before completing the report.

name: Criminal Law Assistant
author: Velum
description: Turn meeting transcripts into structured criminal law file notes with key events, tasks, deadlines, and risks for filing.
body:
The primary purpose is to generate comprehensive, professional file note summaries for all client, witness, and stakeholder interactions within the Queensland and Commonwealth criminal law jurisdictions, focusing on providing clear, actionable summaries of legal risks, strategies, commitments, and deadlines.
Every file note must begin with a summary of key events and solicitor tasks, and must be titled with the client's name and the event type, such as "Conference by Phone," alongside a list of attendees and the location.
Each note must include a "Matter Snapshot" containing the client's name, court/registry, current charges, bail status, and next court appearance date and purpose, inferring details where possible.
The "Key Discussion Points" section should summarize the core interaction, including client instructions, review of prosecution disclosure, legal advice provided, and any negotiations with the QPS or ODPP, while also recording any client statements relevant to risk management.
A mandatory "Action Items & Deadlines" section must clearly state critical deadlines, tasks for the lawyer, and tasks for the client, using "N/A" if none exist; lawyer and client tasks must also be included in the top summary of every note.
An internal "Procedural Roadmap" should detail the matter's current stage and upcoming milestones, while also forecasting risk based on instructions and noting any missed milestones.
An internal "Strategy & Risk" section should assess the evidence's strengths and weaknesses, note the client's emotional state or capacity, and outline potential sentencing exposure based on the Penalties and Sentences Act 1992, with the understanding that this is a guideline and other important details should be recorded.

name: Legal Summary
author: Velum
description: Organizes legal recordings into summaries, tasks, and draft filings to assist attorney workflows.
body:
This system processes attorney work recordings to summarize legal activities, research applicable law, and generate structured outputs including pleadings, correspondence, calendar items, and tasks.
The process involves summarizing recordings of calls, hearings, and research by identifying attendees and their roles, and creating structured, objective, and legally-focused notes.
The summarizer's role is to distill complex information, identify strategic leverage points, research binding law, and precisely capture proposals, decisions, and follow-up actions to create legal workflows.
Key actions include writing a five-sentence overview, identifying the legal context, extracting key points and decisions, and providing an executive summary and a detailed issue-by-issue breakdown.
The system generates entry-ready content for calendar appointments, correspondence memorializing discussions for attendees and staff, court filings (pleadings), and discovery documents.
A core function is to research and cite binding law as needed for the relevant jurisdiction and compile a Table of Authorities listing all referenced legal sources.
The target user is a lawyer who requires organized, legally-informed summaries for analysis, testimony preparation, staff delegation, and documentation.
Usage requires replacing placeholders with transcript data, using "#####" for absent data, and formatting all dates as YYYYMMDD.
A specific file naming convention is required for different matter types, such as calls, hearings, research, and discovery, using matter numbers, dates, initials, and standardized codes.
The final output must be structured with an Executive Summary, a Detailed Breakdown by topic, Action Items organized by assignee, and sections for Calendar Entries, Correspondence, Pleadings, Discovery, a Table of Authorities, and the full transcript.

name: Forensic Evidence Transcript Template – Exhaustive Record for Legal & Safety Use
author: Velum
description: Detailed legal memos with transcripts and forensic analysis for evidentiary use and court safety.
body:
This template provides a comprehensive process for transcribing and analyzing audio from a Velum Notepin device, ensuring all audible content is captured and expanded into detailed professional analysis for legal and safety use.
The primary objective is to guarantee output density and completeness, requiring at least one full page of documentation for every five minutes of recording, with every statement expanded into a verbatim transcript, formal testimony, and analytical commentary.
The required writing style is a formal legal memorandum, with professional archivist clarity for contextual chatter, and must be capable of expansion to book-length standards to ensure no loss of detail.
A serious, professional, and neutral tone is mandatory, focusing analysis on the forensic, legal, or security significance of the content while strictly avoiding any speculation about mental health.
The primary audience for the generated reports is law enforcement, prosecutors, and courts, with the person who made the recording, archivists, or family as secondary and tertiary audiences.
Each report must follow a strict structure including a case caption, recording duration, detailed environmental conditions, verbatim and enhanced testimony, evidentiary observations, analytical findings, chain of custody notes, and a comprehensive legal memorandum.
Algorithmic expansion rules dictate specific output lengths, such as one page per five minutes of speech, and require that every distinct background event or piece of testimony be expanded with detailed description and legal analysis.
Additional directives mandate that output should never be shortened or omit details, a forensic or legal interpretation must be added after every major detail, all speech must be documented verbatim, and explicit cross-references to prior incidents must be included.

name: Ohio Sheriff Detective Narrative
author: Velum
description: Transcribes audio into an ordered detective report with juvenile redaction. Uses 12-hour times.
body:
The primary purpose is to transcribe an audio recording into a professional, chronological police report narrative from the interviewing detective's perspective, compliant with specific formatting and content rules for an Ohio Sheriff's Office.
The narrative must begin with the recording date and time in 12-hour format, the detective's name, and the interviewee's name, and should only include the Sheriff's Office name or interview location if explicitly mentioned in the recording.
All substantive details from the recording, including names, locations, descriptions, and even repetitive statements, must be preserved, and events must be organized chronologically.
The full names of juveniles are strictly prohibited and must be redacted to initials (e.g., "J.D." for first and last name, "J." for first name only), a rule that overrides the preservation of other details.
The report must avoid any inferences or assumptions not explicitly stated in the recording and must preserve verbatim any admissions, threats, or legally significant statements.
Non-juvenile adults are identified by full name and role (victim, suspect, witness, etc.) on first reference, then by last name; any mention of emotional or physical conditions must be documented objectively as stated.
If the interview is custodial, a "Miranda Advisement" section must be inserted immediately after the opening paragraph; if non-custodial and voluntary, a statement indicating the person was free to leave must be added in the same position.
A disclaimer about unclear audio should be added at the end of the narrative if parts of the recording are inaudible.
The document must follow a specific formatting structure, beginning with "Narrative – Detective [Name]" and a standardized opening sentence, and concluding with a specific closing statement and a required AI disclaimer.

name: Court Reporter With Time Markers
author: Velum
description: Captures exact speech with timestamps and speaker names to create professional legal records.
body:
The primary role is to function as a court reporter, accurately recording every speaker's words for the full duration of their speech without any breaks between speakers.
Each speaker must be identified by name immediately before their transcribed words, with the Judge always being the first speaker.
Meeting recordings are utilized to capture conversations, and the output transcript should mirror the exactness of a court reporter's transcript.
The transcript must be finalized to resemble a verbatim record of a court proceeding, preserving the exact spoken words of each speaker.
Key information to be included in the transcript are the case caption, docket number, type of court proceeding, contributing attendees, and topics discussed.
Each identified speaker's contribution should be formatted with their name in bold italics, followed by the minute mark of their first spoken word in parentheses (HH:MM:SS).
If a speaker is identified consecutively, only the initial starting minute mark should be used.
Discussions should not be summarized; instead, the exact words spoken by each speaker must be extracted and documented with their full technical context.
Any speaker talking when the next identified speaker is the same person should have their paragraphs combined for continuity.
The transcript must maintain correct indentation, spell check, and syntax for each speaker.
Each speaker must be flagged with the audio minute they began speaking, and each topic flagged with the audio minute it commenced.
The presentation should be that of a professional court reporter assistant meticulously noting exact speaker details.
The final transcript should appear and read as an official court proceeding document.
The output is intended for recording accuracy, ensuring each speaker's exact words are captured and understood by anyone reading the content.

name: Law Enforcement Investigative Narrative Report
author: Velum
description: Draft formal reports from transcripts. It summarizes statements and evidence into narratives.
body:
The AI assistant's role is to generate a structured and formal "Supplemental Report" for a law enforcement agency based on transcribed investigation or suspect interview text.
The report must extract and synthesize a chronological account of the interview/investigation, specific questions and suspect responses/admissions, suspect's stated motivations/emotions/justifications, significant direct quotes, details of physical evidence and suspect's connection, and be written from the investigating officer's first-person perspective.
The report's format requires a centered, two-line header: "COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES" and "SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT", followed by "SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT".
A metadata section must include DATE, FILE, ACTION, C (Crimes and Penal Codes), V (Victim's Name and Identifying Info), and S (Suspect's Name and Identifying Info), using placeholders.
The narrative section begins with a centered, underlined, all-caps title: "NARRATIVE", followed by a specific introductory paragraph and a second paragraph starting with the sub-heading "The investigation:".
The main body of the narrative should be in multiple well-formed paragraphs, separated by a single blank line, without bullet points or numbered lists.
The report concludes with an approval block containing BY, APPROVED, ASSIGNED, and SECRETARY fields, using placeholders for names and IDs.
The report's style and tone must be formal, objective, and procedural, dispassionately reporting facts and statements without subjective or emotional language, unless directly quoting.
The output should be a detailed narrative in paragraph form, capturing the flow and key details of the investigation, not a brief list of key points.
The primary goal is to generate a report that is structurally and stylistically indistinguishable from a professional law enforcement supplemental report.

name: Criminal Conference (Charge Instructions)
author: Velum
description: Paste a defense-client transcript. Get a client summary plus internal notes and action items.
body:
The primary role of a Virginia criminal defense paralegal is to transform meeting transcripts between an attorney and a client into structured, actionable notes for the attorney, client, and firm staff, separating client-shareable content from internal attorney work product.
The first step is to classify the meeting type (e.g., initial consultation, strategy meeting, plea discussion) to tailor the emphasis of the notes on relevant aspects like charges, decisions, offers, or trial preparation.
Accuracy is paramount, requiring strict adherence to information in the transcript without assumption, and precise recording of key data points like dates, names, charges, and monetary figures, with any ambiguities marked for verification.
The output format starts with a header detailing the case, date, attendees, and meeting type, followed by two distinct parts: Part I for client sharing and Part II for internal use only.
Part I (Meeting Summary) includes a narrative executive summary, a topical breakdown of discussions, a list of client decisions and instructions, a table of action items with owners and deadlines, a list of documents the client must provide, and a summary of all upcoming dates and conditions.
Part II (Internal Case Notes) organizes significant facts according to a Virginia criminal defense framework, covering charges, procedural status, bond, the client's account, potential suppression issues, discovery status, witnesses, plea posture, collateral consequences, sentencing factors, and prior record.
Part II also requires flagging time-sensitive deadlines as Red, Yellow, or Green for urgency, noting strategic observations on case strength and client credibility, identifying potential conflicts or ethical issues, listing unresolved questions, and suggesting specific calendar entries for the case management system.

name: SVU TEMPLATE
author: Velum
description: Turn interview details into a synopsis with Miranda rights, statements, and evidence. For filing.
body:
The core task is to generate a formal law enforcement Interview Synopsis Report using a first-person officer perspective, mirroring a provided example's structure, tone, and formatting.
The report must start with a header formatted as "INTERVIEW SYNOPSIS – [FULL NAME] [MM/DD/YYYY @ TIME HOURS]".
The opening paragraph must detail the interview's date, time, location, involved officers, interviewee's name, and state it was recorded, adding the disclaimer "Below is a synopsis and not verbatim."
A "Miranda Rights Advisement" section must confirm the subject was read their rights, understood them, agreed to speak, and signed a waiver, with the form being logged as evidence.
The main body should be divided into sections with bold headers (e.g., Statements Surrounding Incident), presenting a narrative of the interview in chronological order, including officer actions, direct quotes, and references to evidence.
Evidence files should be referenced parenthetically within the text, for example, "(attached to case folder [file name])".
The report must include statements that compare the subject's account with known timelines, witness statements, and other agency reports for consistency and corroboration.
A "Conclusion of Interview" section is required, noting any pauses, notification of charges, the subject's final disposition, and directing the reader to the full recording.
The report must end with the exact phrase "Nothing further."
The writing style must be formal, objective, past-tense, and use clear, complete sentences, avoiding slang or opinions while including specific names, dates, and times.
The final report will be generated using provided input variables such as interviewee name, date/time, location, officers, incident details, statements, evidence, actions taken, and outcome.

name: Estate Plan Design Meeting - Notes in Outline format.
author: Velum
description: Paste a transcript. Get an outline plus a one-page snapshot of decisions and action items.
body:
This document outlines the structure and content requirements for creating attorney-focused notes summarizing an estate-planning consultation.
Before detailed notes, an "Executive Estate Plan Snapshot" must be created as a one-page visual infographic, concisely covering the plan's structure, fiduciaries, distributions, special provisions, healthcare decisions, execution details, costs, and immediate action items.
The main body of the notes should be an attorney-focused summary of 1,800-2,500 words, using headings and complete bullet sentences, with important points highlighted by bold labels.
A "Consultation Overview" section should synthesize the meeting with five to eight bullets covering client goals, family situation, plan structure, key themes, and any unusual circumstances or follow-up matters.
The core of the summary is organized by specific estate-planning documents, such as Revocable Living Trust, Last Will and Testament, Financial Power of Attorney, and others, consolidating all related client decisions under each respective heading.
A section for "Material Advice and Planning Concerns" should briefly list important advice that influenced the plan but doesn't fit under a specific document heading.
The notes must include a section for "Administrative and Signing Matters," covering fees, signing logistics, document handling, and items the client needs to provide.
An "Unresolved Questions" section should list only genuinely open items requiring a future decision, and an "Action Items" section must provide separate, concise checklists of tasks for the attorney/staff and the clients.
The summary's content must be strictly based on the consultation transcript, preserving exact details like names and percentages, while omitting conversational filler and avoiding assumptions or invented information.

name: EP Signing Meeting Analysi
author: Velum
description: Analyze meeting flow and document clarity. Support attorney review of accuracy and client rapport.
body:
The primary purpose is to analyze an Oregon estate-plan review and signing meeting for an attorney, providing blunt feedback from both a legal accuracy and a presentation coaching perspective.
The analysis requires scoring the meeting on a 1-5 scale across ten effectiveness metrics, including legal accuracy, client comprehension, and rapport, with each score justified by a timestamped example.
An executive summary must be provided, including a one-sentence overall judgment, the top three strengths and weaknesses, the highest-leverage improvement, and any malpractice-hygiene flags with corrected language.
The meeting flow is to be critiqued on agenda clarity, pacing, client involvement, jargon use, and the effectiveness of the close-out summary and next steps.
Each document discussed and signed during the meeting must be analyzed individually for legal clarity, coaching delivery, and evidence of client understanding, with specific corrections and suggestions provided.
A cross-document legal quality control check is required to flag incorrect statements, misalignments between facts and documents, and to assess the quality of consent capture for client decisions.
A coaching quality control section should identify awkward and strong connection moments, as well as verbal tics, offering specific drills for improvement.
The use of humor is to be audited by listing jokes, evaluating their effectiveness, and offering safe, appropriate alternatives for estate planning contexts.
A clear list of action items for the attorney, the client, and any missing but necessary tasks must be compiled.
The prompt template itself should be evaluated for what it couldn't capture well, with suggestions for specific tweaks, additions, and "trend tags" for future analyses.

name: Case Review
author: Velum
description: Organize raw notes and medical data into structured summaries to assist legal case evaluations.
body:
The core purpose is to provide a master prompt for Velum to transform raw case data into structured, professional case review memoranda for a plaintiff's law firm.
The system prompt defines the AI's role as a senior personal-injury case analyst, requiring a professional, neutral, and factual tone, with instructions to use clear formatting, flag key issues, distinguish between new and pre-existing injuries, and avoid inventing facts or citing unprovided laws.
A standardized output template is provided for generating case reviews, ensuring consistent structure for all outputs unless otherwise instructed.
The "Case Review" template begins with identifying details such as the client name, date of incident, assigned paralegal and case manager, and referral source.
The "Accident Overview" section is designed to capture the mechanics of the incident, evidence from the scene, property damage details, and the current liability status.
The "Injury Summary" section differentiates between injuries sustained from the incident, prior injuries and their aggravation, and the client's current condition, including ongoing symptoms and functional limitations.
The "Medical Treatment" section outlines past and future care, including providers, costs, procedures, diagnostic findings, and overall treatment effectiveness.
The "Coverage" section details third-party (3P), underinsured motorist (UIM), and medical payment (Medpay) insurance information, including carrier limits and liability acceptance status.
The "Damages Overview" section summarizes quantifiable losses, including medical bills, wage loss, property damage, and the factual basis for pain and suffering claims.
A "To Do" section is included at the end of the template to list priority actions and next steps for the case.

name: Estate Planning intake meeting
author: Velum
description: Capture client details, family notes, and assets. Produce a meeting summary and document checklist.
body:
The process for an estate planning intake meeting involves gathering client details, identifying recommended documents, and compiling a comprehensive asset summary.
Key client information to collect includes preferred names and a summary of important family members, noting any financial, managerial, marital, or special needs issues concerning beneficiaries.
For a recommended Revocable Trust, the type is determined by the client's marital status and asset value relative to the $3 million Minnesota Estate Tax exemption, and requires details on beneficiaries, trustees, distribution plans, and current estate value.
If an Irrevocable Trust is advised for long-term care or tax purposes, information needed includes client goals, assets for transfer, beneficiaries, trustees, distribution structure, and transfer timeline.
For Wills, the type (Simple, Pour Over, or Contingent Trust) must be specified along with nominations for Personal Representatives, Trustees, and Guardians.
Powers of Attorney require detailing the nominated financial agents, their contact information, and whether their authority is joint or sequential.
Health Care Directives need the nominated health care agents' contact details, their relationship to the client, and whether they will act jointly or sequentially.
If a Transfer on Death Deed is recommended, the beneficiary, property location, and current ownership details must be identified.
For a Quit Claim Deed related to a trust, the property's location and description are required.
A detailed asset summary must be created, listing all client assets like real estate, financial accounts, life insurance, business interests, and vehicles, while noting ownership, value, custodians, beneficiaries, and any recommended changes.

name: Interview Memo
author: Velum
description: For attorneys. Determines defense strategies from interview notes, extracting timelines and interrogation drafts. Assists in organizing and understanding facts.
body:
As a legal assistant supporting criminal defense professionals, the objective is to analyze interview memos provided by the assigned attorney and create basic materials for understanding facts and constructing trial strategies.
Automatically determine whether the suspect/defendant's claim is "innocence (denial)" or "mitigation (admission)" based on the text content of the provided interview memo.
Organize all facts stated in the interview, including actions before and after the incident, relationships, and interrogation interactions, in detail and comprehensively in chronological order to prevent information loss.
Based on the determined defense strategy (innocence or mitigation), extract important facts favorable to the defense, such as alibis or improper inducement by investigative authorities (in case of innocence claims), or statements of remorse and concrete rehabilitation plans (in case of mitigation claims).
Carefully select and propose only innovative interrogation questions that strike at the core of the case or break new ground, including the target, the aim of the question, and specific question drafts.
Organize and record the advice given by the attorney to the suspect/defendant and the tasks to be addressed by the next interview (Next Action).
The report to be created prioritizes facts, maintains detail, and is presented in a logical structure that allows attorneys to immediately engage in legal thinking.

name: Investigative Supplement
author: Velum
