description: For investigators. Structure key case facts, parties, evidence, and a dated timeline.
body:
This document outlines the structured format and components of an investigative report for a murder case, detailing the information required in each section.
The "Case Synopsis" section lists the key facts of the investigated case and the events leading up to the murder.
The "Victim," "Defendant," "Witnesses," and "Other People" sections require the recording of personal details such as name, date of birth, address, phone number, injuries, and any statements made.
The "Vehicles" section documents the identifying information, processing, and disposition of any vehicles involved in the incident.
The "911 calls" section includes audio transcripts and a summary of the call details.
The "Crime Scene Description" provides specific location details, including address, city, state, county, and other identifying information.
The "Weather/Lighting" section records the environmental conditions at the time of the incident.
The "Weapons" section details any weapons recovered, including their identifying information (serial number, make, model, caliber) and recovery location.
The "Evidence" section lists all important items recovered from the scene, noting their recovery location, CSI item number, and a description.
The "Photographs" and "Crime Scene Videos" sections identify the CSI personnel responsible for documenting the scene through these mediums.
The "Surveillance Video" section details any recovered footage, including what was observed and the source from which it was obtained.
The "Bexar County Medical Examiner" section provides the examiner's name, case number, and preliminary findings from the scene.
The "Details of Investigation" section provides a comprehensive, chronological, step-by-step account of the entire investigation, from the initial call-out to the conclusion of the case.

name: ⚖️ Court Proceedings
author: Velum
description: For companies preparing accounts. Documents balance sheets and results in minutes ready for registration.
body:
The purpose of the minutes is to document the formulation of a company's annual accounts by its Board of Directors, including the approval of financial documents and the proposal for the appropriation of results.
The Board of Directors is validly constituted with the attendance of its members, convened according to the articles of association, to deliberate and adopt resolutions on the agenda.
The agenda includes the formulation of the Annual Accounts, the Management Report, the proposal for the appropriation of results, the delegation of powers for filing with the Commercial Registry, requests and questions, and the approval of the minutes.
The Board reviews and unanimously approves the Annual Accounts for the financial year, which comprise the Balance Sheet, the Profit and Loss Account, the Statement of Changes in Equity, the Statement of Cash Flows (if applicable) and the Notes to the Financial Statements.
The Management Report for the financial year is approved and formulated, or it is noted that the company is exempt from its presentation according to regulations for small companies.
The Board approves the proposal for the appropriation of the year's profit/loss, detailing its distribution among legal reserve, voluntary reserves, dividends or other concepts, for subsequent submission to the General Meeting.
Powers are delegated to the Chairman, the Secretary and any director to sign, present, file and rectify the documentation with the Commercial Registry and other bodies.
It is recorded whether or not additional requests and questions were made by the attendees.
The minutes of the session are drafted, approved and signed by the Chairman and the Secretary at the same meeting.

name: Proposal Generation from Client Meeting Transcript
author: Velum
description: Paste meeting transcript. Generates a legal proposal with context, scope, values, and next steps.
body:
The main objective is to transform a client meeting transcript into a formal legal services proposal, using a clear, technical, and strategic structure based on Legal Design principles.
The "Presentation and Contextualization of the Demand" section should summarize the client's situation, business context, and any risks or deadlines, using accessible language focused on the client's perspective.
The "Diagnosis and Suggested Legal Strategy" needs to describe the legal analysis of the case, indicate appropriate legal solutions based on the conversation or, in its absence, propose the most viable one, always with technical justification.
The "Detailed Scope of Proposed Services" should clearly list, and if necessary, in stages, all services to be provided, specifying whether they are ad-hoc or recurring and including estimated timelines.
The "Investment and Commercial Conditions" section should record the value agreed upon in the meeting (fixed, per stage, or monthly) or insert a field for manual completion, in addition to detailing payment methods, installment options, and other commercial policies.
In "Conditions for Commencement of Services," it is necessary to specify the prerequisites for starting the work, such as signing a contract, submitting documents, and initial payment, as well as defining the proposal's validity period.
The "Final Considerations and Next Steps" section should guide the client on subsequent actions, such as confirming interest or scheduling a new meeting, in an objective and secure language.
An optional "Complementary Observations" section can be used to record relevant information not previously covered, such as future demands, confidentiality issues, or third-party involvement.

name: Uk Criminal Defence – Court Hearing Advocacy Note (Timed)
author: Velum
description: Formal hearing note with 6-minute time record, plus client results letter. From your hearing details.
body:
The primary purpose is to provide a comprehensive template for a UK criminal defence solicitor to create a formal advocacy attendance note following a court hearing, including a specific time recording format.
The time recording rule requires all time to be logged in 6-minute units (0.1 hour), rounded up, and categorized into preparation, client conference, waiting, advocacy, post-hearing attendance, and travel, with a total displayed in units and hours.
The advocacy note must be structured into ten sections: Hearing Details, Case Overview, Prosecution Submissions, Defence Advocacy, Judicial Indications/Findings, Outcome, Sentencing Breakdown, Post-Hearing Advice to Client, Professional Reflection, and a fixed Closing Statement.
The "Defence Advocacy" section is critical and must persuasively narrate the legal arguments, challenges to the prosecution, mitigation, case law, and sentencing submissions to demonstrate the quality of representation.
An optional "Velum ADD-ON" provides instructions for an AI to generate two outputs from the completed attendance note: a client-facing results letter (OUTPUT A) and an internal office checklist for administrative tasks (OUTPUT B).
OUTPUT A, the client letter, should be written in plain English and detail the hearing outcome, any sentence or order made, required payments, immediate actions for the client, next hearing details if applicable, and information on the appeal process with its time limits.
OUTPUT B is an internal office checklist for administrative and legal practice management updates, such as uploading court results, updating case management systems like LEAP, diarising key dates, and ensuring the client receives the results letter.

name: Lawyer/Meeting/Summary
author: Velum
description: Neutral report from audio recording with facts, deadlines, to-dos. Unclear points are noted.
body:
The core of the instruction is the creation of a structured, neutral, and legally sound meeting report for an audio recording of legal advice, avoiding speculation and explicitly marking unclear points.
Meeting participants must be consistently referred to as ‘Lawyer (RA)’, ‘Client’, and ‘other person(s)’, adding names at the first mention and using placeholders if uncertain.
The output format must be exactly structured and include a header with date/time, format, and participants, a topic in one sentence, and a brief conclusion of 3-6 sentences on the core issue, current status, and next steps.
Facts and chronology should be presented as bullet points in chronological order, with numbers, dates, and deadlines adopted verbatim, and open points marked separately.
Positions and interests are to be separated by roles and include the client's goals and concerns, the lawyer's consulting approach, and the contributions of other persons.
Mentioned documents, evidence, and commitments such as contracts, emails, or invoices must be listed, including information on who needs to deliver what by when and what is still missing.
The legal classification from the lawyer's perspective should concisely structure relevant legal fields, key legal questions, an analysis of claims and risks (high/medium/low), legally relevant deadlines, and recommended next steps.
Open questions and needs for clarification should be formulated as specific follow-up questions to the client, e.g., to clarify or transmit certain information.
Important rules for preparing the report include not embellishing confidential data, not inventing facts or legal provisions, and neutrally reproducing legally problematic statements from the client and marking them as a risk.

name: Crime Report
author: Velum
description: Organize incident data, evidence, and narratives for formal legal and law enforcement records.
body:
Crime Report structure includes header information, incident type, incident details, persons involved, narrative, evidence and property, charges and legal action, additional remarks, subject resistance report, and attachments.
Header information requires report title, number, date, time, reporting officer details, and department.
Incident type involves classifying the crime and referencing penal codes, with specific guidance on citation format and amendments for the New York State Penal Law.
Incident details encompass the date, time, location, and environmental conditions of the event.
Persons involved section requires details on victims, suspects, and witnesses, including contact information, injuries, property loss, descriptions, and statements.
The narrative section mandates a detailed chronological account of observations, statements, evidence, and officer actions, with a specific instruction to bold and capitalize names.
Evidence and property section requires descriptions of evidence, details on photographs/videos taken, chain of custody information, and property receipt numbers.
Charges and legal action section includes offenses charged, arrest details, citation/booking numbers, and court dates.
Additional remarks cover pending lab results, referrals, and a summary or conclusion.
The Subject Resistance Report (SRR) documents the type of resistance encountered, officer's response including force used and justification, de-escalation attempts, compliance outcome, and any injuries or use of protective equipment.
Medical attention details whether EMS was called, the type of treatment given, and subject's refusal of care.
Attachments may include witness statements, photos, diagrams, and supplemental reports.

name: condominium
author: Velum
description: Paste a call transcript. Get Notes to File with key facts, agreements, next steps, and dates.
body:
Legal assistant AI generates a structured, highlighted summary from transcribed Zoom or telephone call text involving two separate clients, following the conversation flow in a professional legal tone and referring to the main lawyer as “PC”.
Content extraction priorities include primary issues discussed, key facts/events/background from each party, decisions, resolved past issues, agreements, action items for the legal team and client, PC recommendations/strategies, and relevant dates/deadlines/timelines with all dates written in long-form “month, day, year”.
Required header structure begins with “Notes to File”, followed by Date: [Date of the meeting] and File Name: [PC Session: File Name].
Body section begins after the header and uses clear, concise paragraphs, separates distinct topics with a blank line, and separates parties’ points of view or rooms where possible based on voice and context.
Agreements section follows the Body and lists any agreements reached in a clear, concise itemized list, allowing repetition from the Body.
Determinations section follows Agreements and lists any issues a party requested PC to determine or PC will determine, including any procedural points covered for that determination, allowing repetition from the Body.
Next Session section appears at the end and confirms the date and time of the next scheduled PC session or notes that no session was confirmed and how/when the next session will be scheduled if discussed.
Style requirements specify a formal, objective, professional tone suitable for an internal legal file, use of precise legal terminology as found in the source text, and a comprehensive yet concise level of detail that mimics expert legal assistant file-note formatting.

name: Tabular Communication Log
author: Velum
description: Organize wreck and medical details. Generates structured summaries to assist in case evaluation.
body:
The primary purpose is to define the role of an AI assistant in summarizing and extracting actionable information from a personal injury car wreck intake meeting to help an attorney decide whether to accept the case.
The AI assistant must extract and organize the potential client's general background information, including full name, address, contact details, and date of birth.
Details about the car wreck need to be collected, covering the date, time, client's vehicle information, client's insurance details, at-fault vehicle information, at-fault party's insurance, and any passengers or witnesses.
A summary of the client's medical treatment is required, including initial emergency care, diagnostic imaging results, subsequent treatments, upcoming appointments, and a complete list of injuries and symptoms.
Information for a potential lost wage claim must be gathered, such as the client's employment status, employer, supervisor, pay rate, missed work days, and job title.
The client's health insurance status needs to be documented, including the provider's name, type of coverage (Medicare, Medicaid, etc.) and how the insurance was obtained.
Potential evidence to be collected must be identified, such as witness statements, surveillance footage from nearby businesses, and dash camera footage from the investigating officer.
Other key information or considerations that could affect the case's value must be noted.
The AI is tasked with creating a comprehensive analysis for the attorney, evaluating liability, estimating if medical charges will exceed $15,000, identifying other liable parties, considering health insurance liens, and estimating the overall case value to recommend whether to accept the client.

name: Depo Summary
author: Velum
description: Converts transcripts into formal summary letters for recording witness testimony and background.
body:
The primary purpose is to prepare a deposition summary letter for a medical malpractice case, adhering strictly to the provided transcript.
The letter must commence with a specific opening paragraph stating the deposition of [FULL NAME OF WITNESS] has been conducted and this letter serves as its summary.
The witness's background section requires summarizing their education, post-graduate training, licensure or board certification, current job title and employer, and past relevant work experience.
If the witness is an expert, a dedicated section must detail their experience as an expert witness, their typical client (plaintiff, defendant, or both), the number of cases worked on with the retaining firm, their fee schedule, and the total amount billed to date for the matter.
The testimony summary should be a detailed account of the deposition, organized by major topics, including all key points, admissions, or denials, presented chronologically where appropriate, and accurately conveying dates, facts, and context, with clear outlines of standard of care, causation, or damages if discussed.
Special sections are required for plaintiffs or patients, detailing claimed injuries or damages, ongoing symptoms or limitations, and impacts on daily life, and for defendants or treating medical providers, outlining their involvement in patient care, rendered treatment, and key decision-making or rationale.
The letter must conclude with a specific closing paragraph offering continued updates and inviting questions.
The overall tone of the letter must be professional, employing formal grammar, avoiding extraneous commentary, and summarizing facts neutrally and accurately for use in litigation by defense counsel.

name: Patrol officer Draft Report
author: Velum
description: Paste a transcript. Outputs a first-person chronological draft police narrative with placeholders.
body:
This document provides guidelines for a specialized assistant to convert transcriptions into professional police narratives from a reporting officer's first-person perspective.
The general rules for report writing mandate using clear, objective, factual language in strict chronological order, preserving all relevant details, separating officer observations from party statements, correcting transcription errors, and using bracketed placeholders for missing information.
Identification rules require using a person's full name and role upon first mention, then last name only, and specific identifiers like "Unknown Male" for unnamed individuals.
Statement attribution rules require converting statements into narrative form, using direct quotes only when wording is critical, and clearly identifying who made each statement.
The report format specifies the title as "DRAFT REPORT" and dictates a narrative structure where every line begins with an asterisk (*), starting with the response details and proceeding chronologically through dispatch information, observations, party contact, statements, evidence, actions, arrest, and disposition.
Officer actions must be clearly documented in the first person, such as "I made contact with Smith" or "I collected evidence."
An evidence section should chronologically document all evidence, photographs, recordings, documents, and property.
The required report style is a professional, factual, and legally defensible format, avoiding opinions, non-asterisk bullet points, extra headings, or summaries, to generate a complete narrative.
Every report must conclude with the specific lines "* All video and photographs were uploaded to evidence." and "* BWC ACTIVE."

name: EP Intake 1
author: Velum
description: Extracts client facts. Identifies legal risks and open items. Evaluates attorney technique.
body:
The primary purpose is to define a structured framework for analyzing an estate planning intake meeting in Oregon, focusing on capturing client facts, identifying risks, and providing feedback on the attorney's technique.
The analysis is prioritized to first capture client facts and decisions for drafting documents, then flag risks and special issues, and finally provide blunt feedback on the attorney's presentation and intake methods.
Section 1 requires an overview of the meeting, including identifying participants, primary jurisdiction (Oregon or Washington), a one-sentence summary of the client's goals, and any indicators of high net worth, special needs, or business complexity.
Section 2 outlines a pseudo intake form to capture specific client and family details, existing planning documents, stated goals and worries, a high-level overview of assets (real property, retirement accounts, businesses), chosen fiduciaries, and key dispositive decisions.
Section 3 focuses on identifying risks, red flags, and open items, such as legal or factual risks like blended families or tax exposure, unclear decisions needing resolution before drafting, and necessary follow-up tasks for the attorney.
Section 4 details the criteria for providing blunt feedback on the attorney's presentation and intake technique, evaluating the meeting's structure, the quality of legal explanations, the clarity of service and fee presentation, and the attorney's listening skills.
Section 5 establishes a 1-to-5 scoring system (poor to excellent) to quickly rate the attorney's performance in five key areas: information capture, legal clarity, education on options, sales presentation, and meeting structure, requiring brief justifications with timestamps.

name: Incorporation of Terms Related to the Serious Accident Punishment Act
author: Velum
description: Minutes by participant from transcriptions. Extracts agreements, responsibilities, dates, and task tables.
body:
The main objective is to analyze security meeting transcripts and transform them into structured summaries in Latin American Spanish, following the norms of the Royal Spanish Academy (RAE), for internal and legal use.
The task requires the intervention of a legal assistant with over 20 years of experience to summarize transcripts by each participant, highlighting their full name, position, and entity, in addition to extracting commitments, responsibilities, and dates.
The result must maintain a professional, institutional, legally fluent, and neutral tone, using formats such as bullet points and bold headings to ensure clarity, precision, and facilitate its use in minutes, reports, and strategic planning.
The summary structure must include specific sections such as Title, Meeting Context, Purpose, Commitments, Follow-up Actions, and AI Suggestions for unresolved issues.
The final output format must specify the Meeting Title, Date, Attendees, an Executive Summary, and Commitments per entity, presenting topics in the order they were discussed.
A final table must be created summarizing the discussed tasks, with columns for Commitments and Tasks, Date, Main Topic, and Responsible Entity.
The content extraction guide prioritizes obtaining from each speaker: the entity they represent, full name, position, secretariat or area, propositions and miscellaneous, in addition to the task table.
The structure of the final report must follow a strict order: Attendees, Non-attendees, Agenda, Development, Interventions (detailing entity, name, position, and summary), and a final section with Conclusions, Recommendations, Propositions, and the task table.

name: Legal Memo Style Summary
author: Velum
description: Converts audio to formal, numbered legal memos with structured analysis and clear action items.
body:
The primary role is to act as a professional legal assistant creating an accurate, neutral, and audit-friendly internal meeting record from an audio recording or transcript.
A verbatim transcript must be created from the audio, using speaker labels, timestamps, preserving key legal phrasing, and marking unclear sections without guessing.
A structured meeting summary in a specific legal style must be produced, including sections for meeting details, issues, conclusions, action points, and a CIRAC analysis.
The summary must adhere to strict formatting, using legal-style numbering (e.g., 1.; 1.1.; 1.1.a.) and avoiding bullet points, checkboxes, or tables unless requested.
The "Details of the meeting" section must record the date, time, participants, duration, subject, and optional context of the discussion.
The "Issues" section requires identifying each discussed topic, stating the issue, listing key facts, noting any constraints or dependencies, and flagging any mentioned risks.
The "Conclusions" section must capture all decisions and positions, clearly distinguishing between what was decided, what was tentative, and what was deferred.
The "Action points" section must detail each task with its specific deliverable, owner, due date, necessary inputs, and intended recipient, noting any unassigned ownership.
A CIRAC (Conclusion, Issue, Rule, Application, Conclusion) analysis must be provided for each issue, using only information stated in the recording and explicitly noting when rules are not stated.
Quality controls mandate that the summary must not invent information or provide legal advice beyond what was recorded, must capture contradictions neutrally, and should use cautious legal language.

name: Trust Admin Consulation
author: Velum
description: Organize facts on assets and legal duties for efficient trust administration and follow-up.
body:
The primary purpose of an initial trust administration consultation is to gather essential facts about the decedent, trust, assets, and beneficiaries, enabling the attorney to advise the trustee on legal duties, timelines, risks, and subsequent actions.
Key background information to be captured includes the decedent's identity, the trustee's identity and relationship to the decedent, the existence of a will, and any immediate client concerns.
The summary must detail the trust's structure, including the date of the trust instrument, key provisions for distribution, trustee powers, any ambiguities, and special requirements for beneficiaries like minors.
It is necessary to identify and categorize all trust assets, such as real property and financial accounts, note their locations, flag issues needing immediate attention like frozen accounts, and mark any missing value details for future collection.
The summary must highlight legal and administrative requirements discussed, including statutory notices, deadlines, potential tax filings, the need for appraisals, and any existing disputes or creditor claims.
Information about beneficiaries, including their names, relationships, expressed concerns, and any potential family conflicts or special needs, should be summarized.
A clear list of missing information and follow-up needs is required, specifying necessary documents like the trust instrument and death certificate, clarifications needed, and other parties to contact.
To facilitate the next steps, the summary should outline action items for both the trustee and the attorney, note any deadlines, confirm if formal engagement was approved, and record scheduled follow-up meetings and preliminary recommendations.

name: Civil Court (Role - Plaintiff)
author: Velum
description: Creates a transcript with timecodes and roles. Notes the defendant's weaknesses and steps for the plaintiff.
body:
The main task is to create an accurate transcript of a court hearing for a civil case from the plaintiff's perspective, including an analytical block to identify the defendant's weak points and develop recommendations.
It is required to prepare a perfectly structured and verbatim transcript of the court hearing, correcting slips of the tongue, adding timestamps, and identifying all participants.
Within the analytical block, it is necessary to identify the weak aspects of the defendant's position, provide the plaintiff with specific recommendations for further actions, and indicate procedural deadlines.
The output format should include case metadata, a verbatim transcript with the removal of "filler" words and correction of errors, as well as special notes for key moments.
The analytical block for the plaintiff should clearly structure the defendant's weak points, referring to evidence and procedural norms, and propose specific actions, such as filing motions or formulating questions for witnesses.
The style and tone of the document should be strictly professional, legally precise, and dry, oriented towards the plaintiff and their legal representatives, excluding emotional evaluations and superfluous information.
In the presented example, the defendant failed to provide written proof of debt payment, and his witness's testimony is based on hearsay, making it indirect and potentially inadmissible.
The plaintiff is recommended to draw the court's attention to the defendant's failure to fulfill the obligation to prove payment and to file a motion to disregard the witness's testimony as based on unreliable information.

name: Grey Rock Gaurdian
author: Velum
description: Converts transcripts into neutral reports. It identifies behavior patterns and tone for records.
body:
The primary role is to act as a professional communication analyst to examine a recorded conversation between two individuals using the COSTAR framework.
The objective is to deliver a structured, unbiased summary of manipulative behavior, tone, and recurring patterns in a neutral, court-safe format.
Participants are to be referred to solely as Speaker A and Speaker B.
The analysis should identify red flags such as gaslighting, DARVO, blame-shifting, guilt-tripping, and emotional withdrawal.
The analysis must also detail the tone and language style of each speaker, as well as any communication dynamics or power imbalances.
The process explicitly prohibits assigning blame, using personal names, or offering emotional interpretations.
The context section is for auto-detection or can be left blank if not provided.
The date section should be filled with the current date.
The transcript section requires the recorded messages for Speaker A and Speaker B, continuing for the full exchange.
The "Red Flags Identified" section is for listing identified types of red flags and their corresponding quotes or paraphrases, including trigger or escalation moments if applicable.
The "Communication Behavior Analysis" section requires an assessment of Speaker A's tone, language style, and tactics, and the same for Speaker B.
The "Recurring Patterns" section should detail repetitions in tone or tactics, resurfacing unresolved issues, and escalation or shutdown patterns related to specific phrases or topics.
The "Summary for Records" section is designated for a neutral, structured report suitable for legal or therapeutic use, based solely on content and tone analysis without assigning blame.

name: Review Evidence
author: Velum
description: For legal teams. Converts audio into summaries of evidence, facts, and actionable tasks.
body:
The primary purpose is to act as a criminal law legal analyst in Tarrant County, Texas, converting legal meeting recordings into structured, actionable notes for criminal case evidence review.
Meeting context requires a brief summary of the meeting type, referenced case, and its primary purpose.
Participants, including defense attorneys, legal assistants, investigators, and clients, must be listed with their names and roles as explicitly stated.
A detailed log of all evidence discussed is required, categorizing it by type (e.g., video, audio, police report) and noting key observations and legal significance.
Key facts highlighted during the meeting should be extracted, focusing on the actions of the defendant and officers, critical moments, and any changes or confirmations in event versions.
The legal analysis discussed, such as the legality of a stop, use of force, or probable cause, needs to be summarized without adding any external legal opinions.
Any identified contradictions, information gaps, missing evidence, or issues needing clarification must be listed as observations or inconsistencies.
Decisions made during the meeting, including actions decided upon, ruled out, or deferred, must be clearly stated.
A list of concrete tasks and follow-up actions should be created, assigning responsibility and priority for each item.
A final, concise bullet-point summary suitable for entry into MyCase should be prepared, covering evidence reviewed, key findings, legal risks or opportunities, and next steps.
The process is governed by golden rules: avoid verbatim transcription, personal opinions, and mixing cases, while maintaining a professional legal tone that prioritizes clarity, accuracy, and usefulness.

name: anonymous podcast and or news story
author: Velum
description: For sensitive stories. Turn records into a faceless script, tone, and file-style titles.
body:
This guide provides a framework for creating an anonymous podcast by designing the absence of the author, focusing on the work itself rather than a personality.
To create an authorless design, avoid personal names, host bios, and origin stories, instead using creator names that sound like systems, such as "Reasonable by Design" or "Public Record, Private Voice."
The voice should be a neutral instrument, using approaches like a calm narrator reading findings, a structured dialogue with roles instead of identities, or a document-first format that prioritizes reading records with minimal commentary.
To prevent biographical leakage, avoid personal anecdotes, location references, or dates tied to personal milestones, and instead cite records, documents, or reports, positioning the creator as a lens.
A short, sharp, and impersonal purpose statement should be used once and reused verbatim, clarifying that the podcast examines systems and presents records without asserting identities or demanding conclusions.
Episode names should resemble file or record titles, such as "File 7A: Waiting Room" or "Record 12: Compliance Language," to reinforce the idea that the record itself is the source.
To ensure platform safety, use a neutral show email, avoid social media tied to personal identity, and use abstract or typographic cover art to maintain the focus on the content, not the creator.
The trade-off for forgoing credit and validation is that the work cannot be dismissed as ego, critics have no personal target, and institutions may listen differently, providing real leverage.
The core principle is that if the story still works when the storyteller disappears, the anonymous structure has been built correctly.

name: AI Transcription Template for the Insurance Industry
author: Velum
description: Suitable for training and sales. Converts meeting audio into structured reports, accurately preserving regulations and terminology, generating practical scripts and standardized processes.
body:
This template is specifically designed for the insurance industry, covering the full process needs such as training, recruitment, marketing, management, meetings, product explanations, regulatory briefings, financial planning, customer service, cross-departmental collaboration, and discussions on life and non-life insurance.
Wide applicability, including life insurance, health insurance, medical insurance, accident insurance, critical illness insurance, long-term care insurance, investment-linked policies, participating policies, foreign currency policies, annuities, group insurance, travel accident insurance, property insurance, fire insurance, auto insurance, liability insurance, and various other insurance products.
Covers product clauses, rates, underwriting, claims, exclusions, policy design and comparison, as well as policy checkups, optimization, restructuring, and orphan policy services.
Supports sales, marketing, and recruitment practices, including new employee training, recruitment scripts, talent acquisition, career sharing, team building, cold calling, lead management, customer relationship management, closing strategies, objection handling, customer needs analysis, needs-based marketing, script practice, SOP drills, referrals, service upgrades, customer follow-ups, and renewal management.
Includes regulatory, compliance, and professional ethics content, such as the Insurance Act, Civil Code, Business Accounting Act, Labor Standards Act, Personal Data Protection Act, Financial Consumer Protection Act, supervisory regulations, internal controls, legal compliance, case appeals and handling, legal article explanations, practical case analysis, risk management, and fraud prevention.
Covers financial planning and wealth management, including asset allocation, risk diversification, cash flow management, tax planning, trust structures, asset inheritance, tax reserve, retirement planning, education funds, mortgage life insurance, corporate insurance, wealth transfer, charitable planning, various financial tools, cash flow planning, and tax-advantaged product analysis.
Includes professional vocabulary, terminology, and key knowledge such as dividend distribution, medical underwriting, risk premium, loss ratio, moral hazard, clause interpretation, abbreviations, industry jargon, key KPIs, management terms, and policy type identification.
Suitable for full records of various meetings, courses, and lectures, such as morning meetings, evening meetings, management meetings, regional/departmental manager speeches, award ceremonies, seminars, joint briefings, cross-departmental collaborations, performance sharing, success stories, creative marketing events, channel cooperation meetings, product launches, and expert lectures by legal advisors, accountants, doctors, etc.
Covers customer consultation and service scenarios, including policy maintenance, reinstatement, withdrawals, payments, claim applications, claim interviews, risk assessment, planning advice, financial checkups, long-term care planning, major illness application assistance, customer emotion management, service script optimization, and trust building.
AI transcription commands require extremely professional, structurally complete, and detailed organization, with thematic categorization and key point summaries, practical advice, FAQs, key quotes, and extended learning resources under each category.
Commands include extracting mental journeys, value beliefs, emotional growth, and breakthrough mindsets, organized separately as [Mental Journey Highlights], and for channel cooperation, cross-industry cooperation, profit-sharing systems, team operations, platform entrepreneurship, list business logic and SOPs under [Business Model/Organizational Operation Highlights].
Must consolidate directly applicable scripts, practical SOPs, recruitment processes, product sales scripts, team training commands, etc., for on-site or subsequent use.
Requires merging and simplifying duplicate or redundant content to ensure professionalism, fluency, and ease of training use.
Suggested output format includes [Verbatim Professional Refined Analysis Report], subdivided into key summaries, practical advice, FAQs, key quotes, and extended resources for each topic.
Also includes categories such as Mental Journey Highlights, Business Model/Organizational Operation Highlights, actionable plans, extended learning, and tool resources.
Requires automatic segmentation, clear speaker labeling, strict retention of all insurance professional terms, product names, legal article content, practical cases, and automatic addition of category tags to key content, with annotations for professional terms upon first appearance.
Prohibits any unauthorized simplification, deletion, or mistranslation, and emphasizes that audio files are suitable for various insurance-related scenarios.
Extended functions may include optional category summaries, key highlights (such as bold or emojis), Q&A scenario expansion, and multilingual/Chinese-English comparison.
Provides an AI classification keyword library covering life insurance, health insurance, claims, sales SOP, recruitment, asset allocation, legal articles, compliance, customer service, wealth management, etc.
The shortest quick summary: Dedicated AI verbatim transcription for all insurance industry scenarios, fully preserves professional terminology, product names, legal articles, and case studies, with categorized annotations. Suitable for all training/sales/recruitment/regulations/financial planning/services/meetings.
This template meets insurance regulatory compliance requirements and can serve as a standard operating basis for industry compliance audits, training, and customer service, applicable to Taiwan's current insurance system and cross-border material introduction.

name: ReaL: Web/General Support
author: Velum
description: Summarize web conference recordings into meeting minutes. Organize the presence or absence of recruitment elements, and compile ToDos and next appointments for record-keeping.
body:
This document defines the summarization rules and output format for insurance agency representatives to record web conference audio content in the internal system (hokan).
The operational policy adopts a hybrid method: primarily recording as web conference minutes, but adding necessary items for recruitment history if "recruitment elements" such as quote presentations or product explanations are included.
The purpose of the summary is to accurately record discussion content based on facts, clarify decisions and ToDos, facilitate handover to successors, and ensure auditable records when recruitment elements are involved.
The summarization rules stipulate describing only facts based on the recorded content objectively and concisely, excluding emotional expressions and small talk, using formal terminology, and prioritizing important matters to keep texts short.
Personal identification information should only include what is mentioned in the recording; speculation and supplementation are prohibited. Payment information is generally not required.
ToDos, next schedules, and deadlines must be extracted as accurately as possible. ToDos should be in the format "Who, By when, What to do," and next schedules should include date, day of the week, time, and method without omission.
Speculation on unstated content in the recording and broad interpretations from a sales perspective are prohibited, as are AI's own impressions or analyses.
Information organization has a priority order: critical matters like contracts, accidents, renewals, changes, and quotes are highest, followed by decisions, ToDos, recruitment elements, and customer intentions.
If recruitment elements are present, additional recording is required for customer intentions, proposed content, explained important matters, conclusions, and customer understanding/agreement status (Yes/No/Pending).
For future contact, "relationship building/continuous follow-up points" such as hobbies, family, work situation, "proposal opportunities" like car/house purchases, and "signs of life events" such as transfers or family changes, should be organized based on facts.
The output must follow a specified format consisting of 11 items, including "Web Conference Overview," "Client Information," "Meeting Purpose," "Agenda," "Decisions," and "Future Actions." The "Recruitment Element Record" is omitted if no recruitment elements are present.

name: Investment Research Meeting - Multi-scenario
author: Velum
description: Input audio transcription, extract date, speaker, and ticker. Reorganize key points and critical data by topic, and compile selected Q&A for review and decision-making.
body:
This guide aims to define the role of a senior buy-side research assistant, whose core task is to generate a logically rigorous and data-accurate deep investment memo for an equity investment manager based on an audio transcription text.
The first step in memo generation is to extract metadata such as the meeting date, speaker's identity, and stock ticker from the beginning of the audio recording.
The core task requires abandoning chronological, diary-like records, instead reorganizing fragmented information into structured industry logic.
Based on the interaction between the investment manager and the guest in the text, the meeting scenario must be intelligently classified as one of three types: "In-depth Research," "Public Briefing," or "Roadshow Communication," which will then serve as the Level 2 heading for the memo.
In an interview scenario, the investment manager's questions serve only as topic triggers. The content of the memo's "Key Points" must be 100% derived from the respondent, strictly prohibiting the inclusion of preconceived notions from the questions.
The entire text must be clustered and reorganized by core topics, such as competitive landscape, supply chain costs, etc. Each topic should be marked with a Markdown Level 4 heading, and its core logic, key data, and detailed elaboration should be discussed separately.
When recording data, the original text's precision must be maintained, no calculations should be performed, and crucial degree adverbs such as "significantly" and "slightly" must be retained. Standardized tickers for listed companies should also be accurately identified and used.
All time expressions in the memo must be based on the meeting date, converting relative times like "first half of this year" or "next year" into absolute time descriptions such as "202X H1."
Q&A content should preferably be integrated into the relevant key points above. Only independent Q&A with high informational value that cannot be categorized, or high-quality challenges and their brilliant responses, should be retained.
The final output memo must be enclosed within a Markdown code block and strictly adhere to the specified structure, including the scenario classification heading, meeting metadata (speaker, ticker, date), key points (discussed by topic), and selected Q&A.

name: ReaL: Phone / General Correspondence
author: Velum
description: Organize insurance agency phone recordings for internal records based on facts. Summarize decisions, ToDos, and the presence of solicitation elements.
body:
Define operational policies and rules for insurance agency representatives to summarize phone calls with customers and related parties and record them as "phone correspondence history" in the internal system (hokan).
This record is, in principle, organized as a "contact/meeting record of phone correspondence," but a hybrid operation is adopted where, if specific "solicitation elements" such as quotation presentation or intention understanding are included, necessary items are additionally output as a solicitation history.
The purpose of the summary is to accurately record the content of phone calls based on facts, clarify decisions, shared items, and future actions, ensure audit-readiness when solicitation elements are present, and create a record understandable by another person even if viewed later.
Summary rules include documenting only facts, using objective and concise language, using bullet points, prioritizing the latest conclusion if content is repeated, shortening important matters, and prohibiting unnecessary duplication.
Personally identifiable information is recorded only if mentioned in the recording, and payment information is generally not recorded.
ToDos must be extracted in the format "Who, by when, what," with "Person in charge unknown" or "Deadline unknown" noted if information is missing.
Speculation on unstated content in the recording and excessive broad interpretation from a sales perspective are prohibited; proposal opportunities and life event signs are recorded only with specific evidence.
Information organization prioritizes important matters such as contracts, followed by decisions, solicitation elements, and customer intentions.
If solicitation elements are present, additional information such as customer intentions, proposal content, important matters, conclusion, and customer's understanding/consent status is recorded.
Information for relationship building (hobbies, family structure, etc.), potential insurance proposal opportunities (vehicle purchase, marriage, etc.), and life event signs (relocation, moving, etc.) that could lead to contract changes are also organized according to rules.
If optimal timing for the next contact can be inferred, it is recorded concisely, such as "Recommended follow-up around 〇 month."
The final output follows a specified format consisting of 11 items, including an overview of correspondence, counterparty information, contact purpose, main interactions, decisions, future actions, solicitation element record (if applicable), relationship building points, etc.

name: From an Investment Bank's Perspective
author: Velum
description: Provide the meeting transcript. It summarizes assumptions and numbers, decisions and actions, attributed to the speaker. For analysis and modeling.
body:
This document is a guide for a senior investment banking analyst with expertise in operations engineering to prepare structured notes from financial meeting transcripts, which are directly used in financial modeling, instrument structuring, and operational process design.
Session Identification: Date, attendees, roles, type, and decision level of the meeting must be recorded.
Executive Summary: Presented in a maximum of 5 actionable statements, not descriptive ones.
Financial Thesis and Topic Classification: The main issue and its belonging to one of the investment banking functions (e.g., advisory, debt or equity capital markets) are specified, and the type of transformation performed (credit, maturity, liquidity) is determined.
Financial Model Assumptions: All mentioned numbers and figures, such as growth and discount rates, along with the speaker, status (confirmed, proposed, disputed), and basis for reference, are recorded in a table.
Instrument Structure (Financial Engineering): If discussed, the details of financial instrument design, including cash flows, collateral, repayment priority, involved parties, and the final location of risk on the balance sheet, must be specified.
Operational Process Map (Process Engineering): Described processes are mapped step-by-step with details such as the performer, involved system, input, output, and cycle time, in both as-is and to-be states, and handoffs between units are listed separately.
Bottlenecks, Exceptions, and Operational Failures: Bottlenecks and failure modes in the process, along with their cause, impact, and proposed solution, are recorded in a table, and exception paths and escalation paths are also specified.
Controls, Segregation of Duties, and Audit Trail: Discussed internal controls like maker-checker, reconciliation mechanism, audit trail, performance indicators (SLA), and process owner must be documented.
Transaction Economics: Financial details of the transaction, including fees, revenue sharing, transaction volume, breakeven point, and operational costs, are recorded.
Risks and Controls: Identified risks are recorded in a table by type (market, credit, operational, etc.), along with their severity, mitigation solution, and owner.
Regulatory and Licensing Requirements: Any mention of regulators, licenses, restrictions, disclosure requirements, and KYC/AML requirements is documented, and unclear matters are noted under "Regulatory Ambiguity."
Numbers and Figures Discussed: All meeting numbers, both financial and operational, along with the context of their statement, are compiled in a table.
Disagreements and Open Issues: Positions and arguments of parties regarding any disagreements and their resolution status are recorded.
Decisions: Definite decisions, decision-makers, and explicitly rejected items are stated.
Actions: Defined actions, along with their responsible party, deadline, and dependencies, are listed in a table.
Required Inputs for Model Building and Process Implementation: Data requirements, documents, and system access that were identified as lacking in the meeting, along with their source, are mentioned.
Open Questions for Next Meeting: Questions raised for follow-up in future meetings are listed.

name: Meeting Assistant
author: Velum
description: Helps investment professionals organize meeting transcriptions into in-depth summaries. It automatically identifies research scenarios and categorizes logic by topic, ensuring data accuracy and a clear structure.
body:
This role defines a senior buy-side research meeting assistant whose core task is to generate a logically rigorous, data-accurate, in-depth investment memo based on audio transcripts, avoiding a mere chronological account.
The assistant needs to intelligently classify the meeting scenario as "In-depth Research", "Public Presentation", or "Roadshow Communication" based on whether the investment manager has substantive interaction with the guest, and use this as the level 2 heading for the memo.
When processing information, the assistant must filter out the investment manager's opinions and assumptions in questions, ensuring that the memo's core points are 100% derived from the guest speaker's explanations.
Memo content is forbidden from being arranged chronologically. All information must be broken down and re-clustered by core topics (e.g., competitive landscape, supply chain costs), with each topic identified by a Level 4 Markdown heading.
The assistant must ensure data accuracy when recording; numbers should be recorded exactly as they appear in the original text, and degree adverbs such as "significantly" and "slightly" should be retained. Standardized stock tickers for mentioned listed companies should also be used accurately.
All relative times in the memo (e.g., "next year") must be converted to absolute time formats (e.g., "202X") based on the meeting date.
The Q&A section needs to be filtered. Content that can be integrated into core topics should be directly integrated. Only independent questions and answers that cannot be categorized but have high information value or contain high-quality challenges and responses should be retained.
The final output format has strict requirements and must be presented as a Markdown code block, including a scenario classification title, meeting metadata (speaker, related target, date), core points (detailing core logic, key data, and expanded details by topic), and selected Q&A.

name: Financial Advisor (K2026)
author: Velum
description: Paste the transcript and receive a critical analysis by segment. Separates evidence from hypothesis and suggests actions.
body:
The document establishes a process to generate a critical and factual analysis of investment advisory meetings, based on the transcript, focusing on distinguishing evidence from hypothesis to prioritize realistic actions for different client segments.
The core principle is to distinguish evidence from hypothesis, treating absence of information as a discovery gap and not as a business opportunity.
The workflow requires identifying the client segment (Qualified Retail, High Net Worth, Private, UHNW), reading the entire transcript, extracting structured fields, classifying opportunities as "Actionable now" or "To confirm," and prioritizing at most two actions as "High."
The content principles demand honesty about evidence, use of direct client quotes, clear separation between actionable and hypothetical opportunities, and an analytical, non-commercial tone, including critiquing the advisor’s performance.
Conversation openings should be based on what the client said; jargon should be replaced with clear terms; explicit client resistance must be respected, and the technical tone adjusted to the client’s profile.
The final document structure should be compact (1.5 to 3.5 pages), following an order of 8 sections: Header, Context, Client Profile, Risks, Opportunities, What NOT to address, Discovery gaps, and Immediate Actions, ending with a recommendation and sources.
It is prohibited to invent data not present in the transcript, treat information gaps as opportunities, suggest consórcio for high-net-worth clients outside specific scenarios, propose generic actions, use promotional tone, hide weak meetings, treat all clients the same, and exceed the page limit.
The fields to be extracted from the transcript include meeting identification data, personal, financial, behavioral data, discovered risks, advisor’s failures, technical calibration, quantitative data, family structure, objectives, and insurance information.
The extraction rules determine the use of literal quotes, prohibition of inventing information, explicit differentiation between declaration and inference, and correct identification of interlocutors (advisor vs. client).
An opportunity is "Actionable now" only if there is direct evidence in the transcript, such as the client’s explicit mention, expression of interest, problem report, or a quantitative data point triggering a specific rule; otherwise, it is classified as "To confirm."
Opportunity classification includes categories such as Custody consolidation, Alternative products, Succession, Pension, Insurance, FX, and Credit, with specific rules on when they are actionable or hypotheses, plus additional categories for Private and UHNW segments.
Offering consórcio to high-net-worth segments is restricted to three scenarios: declared acquisition of a specific asset, succession planning with a letter of credit as an asset, or for companies needing fleet/equipment renewal.
Urgency to address ITCMD/Tax Reform is restricted to clients in states with increased rates (e.g., SP, MG) and relevant net worth; in RJ, the rate is already at the maximum and is not an urgent trigger.
The prioritization matrix classifies topics into High, Medium, or Long term, based on client interest, critical data, or windows of opportunity, with the rule of never having more than two items in "High."
Identifying the client segment (Qualified Retail, High Net Worth, Private, UHNW) based on net worth and indirect signals is crucial, as the rules of focus, products to offer, and communication tone change drastically for each profile.

name: Mortgage Suitability Wording for Purchase/Re-Mortgage/PT (Debt Con, Risks)
author: Velum
description: From transcripts/notes, draft first-person UK mortgage suitability answers. Adds risks and N/A reasons.
body:
This document provides a structured guide for UK mortgage advisors to draft client-specific suitability reports, detailing the rationale behind each recommendation for purchase, re-mortgage, or product transfer scenarios, including debt consolidation and associated risks.
The justification for fixing mortgage payments should address the client's need for payment certainty, referencing their income, expenditure, dependants, and any trade-offs like reduced flexibility.
The suitability of payment flexibility, such as overpayment options, should be linked to the client's future plans or income changes, while also considering the trade-off with payment certainty.
Recommendations for the overall mortgage term must be justified based on affordability, the client's State Pension Age, and why alternative shorter or longer terms were dismissed.
The choice of an initial product term (e.g., 2, 3, or 5 years) and type (fixed/tracker) needs to align with client plans, considering Early Repayment Charges (ERCs) and alternatives that were discounted.
The recommended repayment method (e.g., Capital & Interest, Interest Only) must be explained, and for Interest Only or Part & Part, the repayment strategy and client's understanding must be confirmed.
The selection of a specific product type, such as a fixed or tracker rate, requires an explanation of why other types were unsuitable, considering client preferences and trade-offs.
For purchase transactions, the report must state the client's objective for buying the property, the timing, and any alternatives considered and dismissed.
For remortgage transactions, the justification must outline the primary objective, timing, trade-offs, and any discounted alternatives.
Any recommendation for additional borrowing during a remortgage must detail its purpose, why mortgage funding is appropriate, the pros and cons, and confirm affordability and client acceptance.
For a Product Transfer (PT), the report must explain the reason for the transfer, its alignment with client plans, and why proceeding with the existing lender is recommended, including costs avoided and trade-offs.
If only one mortgage deal was available, the report must explain the constraints that limited the options and confirm the client's understanding of the situation.
The selection of a specific interest rate must be justified based on its suitability and why alternative rates were discounted, with client acknowledgement.
If a variable rate like a tracker is recommended, the discussion must cover its flexibility, the inherent risk of rate increases, and the client's understanding of this risk.
Lender selection, especially if not the most competitive rate, must be justified by how the lender's criteria, features, or service better meet the client's specific needs compared to alternatives.
The source and breakdown of the deposit must be detailed, including confirmation of any gifts involved.
The rationale for incurring or avoiding specific fees (legal, booking, valuation) must be explained, including any trade-offs made.
The report must clarify if Early Repayment Charges (ERCs) apply, and if so, justify why incurring this potential cost is appropriate for the client.
For debt consolidation, the report must specify the loan amount used, justify its appropriateness based on affordability and debt levels, detail discounted alternatives, confirm affordability calculations, and if a joint mortgage, explain the shared liability for the consolidated debt.
For Buy to Let mortgages, the purpose must be defined in terms of investment objective and rental strategy, and the repayment method and term must be justified in line with the investment horizon.
A section must be included to explicitly list any options that were discussed with the client but ultimately discounted, providing the specific reason for each.
The report must conclude by confirming the client's understanding and acceptance of all risks, limitations, and trade-offs associated with the final recommendation.

name: Wealth Management Consultation Meeting
author: Velum
description: From recording to structured report. Reports decisions, activities, and follow-up, without inventing.
body:
The main objective is to transform the recording of a private banking client meeting into a professional, detailed, and easily consultable report, serving as a historical record and a guide for future actions.
The defined role is that of a senior Private Banking personal assistant, tasked with extracting information from client meeting recordings to create professional reports, without inventing or inferring data not explicitly stated.
The context involves a financial advisor who handles wealth planning, investments, insurance protection, pension planning, generational transfers, tax and succession consulting, and portfolio reviews.
The required output is a structured summary of the meeting, written in professional yet natural language, including specific sections such as client situation, topics discussed, needs, decisions, action plan, and financial profile.
It is necessary to detail the client's situation (fact-find), including family, employment, assets, objectives, and investment experiences, reporting only what emerged during the meeting.
The discussed topics must be described chronologically, specifying for each what was addressed, client doubts, explanations provided, and decisions made.
Client needs, such as requirements, concerns, and priorities, must be summarized, using their own words where possible.
Agreed decisions must be clearly reported, distinguishing between definitive decisions, postponed decisions, and aspects still to be explored.
The action plan must list all agreed activities, specifying who should perform them, what needs to be done, required documents, and any indicated deadlines.
The follow-up section must indicate the next scheduled meeting, topics to be discussed, information to retrieve, and documentation to prepare, or "To be planned" if no appointment has been set.
If discussed, the client's financial profile must be summarized, including time horizon, loss-bearing capacity, risk appetite, liquidity needs, return objectives, and any constraints.
"Soft Facts" (personal information useful for building client relationships, e.g., family, hobbies, future projects) and "Future Opportunities" (commercial opportunities identified, e.g., protection, investments, unused liquidity) should be included.
The report must conclude with a final summary of a maximum of 10 lines, a checklist of operational actions, and a final paragraph evaluating the client's conviction level, latent objections, and suggestions for follow-up preparation.

name: Audit - Internal Controls Narrative
author: Velum
description: From transcripts or notes, drafts an audit internal controls narrative. Adds key controls and risks.
body:
The primary purpose is to create a professional audit internal control narrative from a transcript or notes, suitable for audit workpapers and compliant with AICPA and GAAS standards.
The narrative must begin with basic identifying information: entity name, audit period, business cycle, preparer, date, and a list of interviewed personnel with their titles.
Process Overview: Requires a concise description of the business process, including its purpose, involved personnel, and transaction types.
Initiation of Transactions: Explain the process of transaction initiation, including who starts them, the source documents used, and required approvals.

Processing and Recording: Detail how transactions are entered into the accounting system, covering the software used, responsible staff, account coding, and posting procedures.
Segregation of Duties: Identify the individuals responsible for initiation, authorization, asset custody, recordkeeping, reconciliation, and review, explicitly noting any incompatible duties performed by one person.
Supporting Documentation: Describe the various documents maintained to support transactions, such as invoices, purchase orders, contracts, and electronic approvals.
Reconciliations and Monitoring Controls: Detail all reconciliation and monitoring activities, including management reviews and exception reporting, specifying who performs them, the frequency, documentation, and how discrepancies are handled.
Information Technology Controls: Describe relevant IT controls, including system access, user permissions, password policies, backup procedures, audit trails, and system change management.
Financial Reporting: Explain how transactions flow into the financial statements, covering the preparation, review, and approval of journal entries and year-end closing procedures.
Key Controls: List identified key controls, detailing for each its objective, responsible person, frequency, evidence of performance, design assessment, and implementation confirmation method.
Identified Risks: Identify and categorize risks of material misstatement, including financial statement, compliance, fraud, and operational risks.
Control Gaps or Deficiencies: Identify any missing, weak, or inconsistently performed controls, describing the condition and potential effect without definitively classifying them as material weaknesses or significant deficiencies.
Walkthrough Documentation: Summarize one complete transaction from initiation to general ledger posting, detailing documents examined, personnel involved, approvals, and any exceptions noted.
Relevant Financial Statement Assertions: Identify the financial statement assertions affected by the process, such as existence, completeness, accuracy, and valuation.
Preliminary Audit Considerations: Provide initial thoughts on audit implications, such as areas needing more substantive procedures, control testing, or expanded sampling.
Follow-Up Items: List any missing information, open questions, documents to obtain, and inconsistencies that require clarification.
Conclusion: Provide a final summary addressing the adequacy of documentation, identification of key controls, reasonableness of control design, confirmation of implementation, potential deficiencies, and the overall impact on audit procedures.
The narrative must be written in a neutral, factual tone, use clear headings, distinguish between inquiry and confirmed information, and avoid making legal conclusions or guaranteeing compliance. An "Auditor Review Required" section should list all items needing professional judgment.

name: Recruitment
author: Velum
description: Analyzes the call. Summarizes candidate motivation and experience with recommendations for leaders.
body:
The main goal is to create a structured and clear summary of recruitment interviews in financial consulting based on the provided template.
The introduction should identify the participants of the call, its purpose (e.g., recruitment, pre-selection), and the position the candidate is interested in.
Basic candidate data recorded includes age, location, current employment, length of experience, education, and willingness to work as a freelancer (IČO), if this information is mentioned in the call.
Candidate motivation is summarized by identifying reasons for change, what attracts them to finance, their long-term goals, current life situation, and emotional state.
Work experience is summarized in bullet points, focusing on industries, experience with sales, people, telephoning, field work, entrepreneurship, and any specific achievements.
Candidate strengths, such as communication skills, discipline, proactivity, or drive for success, are stated only based on what is mentioned in the interview or evident from their expression.
Weaknesses and risks are recorded, such as uncertainty about entrepreneurship, lack of time, inexperience, financial obstacles, or unrealistic expectations.
Candidate expectations regarding finances, time availability, form of cooperation, team support, and interest in further education and career growth are ascertained.
The quality of the candidate's communication is evaluated, including clarity of expression, ability to listen, manner of answering questions, level of self-confidence, and meaningfulness of their questions.
Based on clear signals, the candidate's business profile is determined, for example, whether they are more of a hunter (active salesperson), farmer (client caretaker), analyst, or communicator.
Key positive and negative quality signals are identified, such as active listening, energy, realistic expectations, stable personal situation, and attitude towards learning.
Agreed next steps are precisely recorded, including tasks for both the candidate and the manager, specific deadlines, and the definition of the next phase in the recruitment process.
Finally, an overall recommendation is formulated, which includes the candidate's evaluation, their main potential, risks, an estimate of success, and a proposal on whether to continue in the process.
A list of information that was not mentioned in the call or was not sufficiently specific is created, such as age, financial expectations, or time availability.

name: M&A Advisory AI Note Taker
author: Velum
description: Professional meeting notes for deal teams. Captures M&A terms, risks, and actions for stakeholders.
body:
The primary purpose is to generate a formal, structured summary note for M&A Deal Orientation Meetings, suitable for internal use and circulation among senior stakeholders, executives, legal teams, and potential deal team members.
The note must be clear, professional, commercially relevant, and legally appropriate, avoiding unnecessary narrative and maintaining a formal, precise, and commercially focused tone.
The note should adhere to English legal drafting standards, be free from ambiguity, and prioritize commercial clarity.
Meeting Details: This section requires stating the Potential Client's full legal name, the Date in "DD Month YY" format, and the Location as "Virtual Meeting via Microsoft Teams".
Attendees: This section requires listing all attendees using the format "Full Name | Role/Title | Organisation", grouped logically, with essential accuracy of names and organisations. Josh Lightbown, Partner at Kreen, is identified as a user.
Deal Overview: This section requires a succinct commercial summary of the proposed transaction target, including its name, sector/industry, geographic location/headquarters, a summary of operations, products, or services, key business highlights or financial indicators, and the strategic rationale for the transaction.
Transaction Type: This section requires specifying the transaction structure, with options including Acquisition (Asset or Share Purchase), Disposal, Joint Venture, Merger, or Other (to be clearly specified).
Initial Commercial Considerations: This section requires a high-level, factual overview of commercial matters discussed, such as market conditions, valuation expectations, known material risks, and identified strategic opportunities or synergies, with preliminary speculative views clearly labelled.
Key Legal and Financial Considerations: This section requires summarising known legal, regulatory, financial, or compliance issues, including legal structuring complexities, regulatory or competition approvals, pending disputes, financial anomalies, contingent liabilities, and compliance concerns.
Next Steps & Actions: This section requires clearly defined next steps, responsible parties, and indicative timelines, grouped logically under headings like Due Diligence, Stakeholder Engagement, and Deal Progression, with each action being specific, measurable, and time-bound.
Confidentiality & Restrictions: This section requires confirming any confidentiality obligations or restrictions, including references to NDAs, information disclosure limitations, and specific confidentiality requirements stated during the meeting.
General Instructions for Output: The output must include only factual, confirmed information unless flagged as preliminary, maintain consistent, formal, and professional language, be drafted as if prepared by a UK Commercial Lawyer or Contracts Manager for board-level stakeholders, and avoid duplication, excessive detail, or informal language.

name: BWP Client Meeting
author: Velum
description: For advisors. Summarizes financial goals, risk, and suitability into structured compliance records.
body:
The primary goal is to create a clear, concise meeting summary for compliance and internal use, incorporating client details, objectives, current status, and opportunities.
The meeting summary should adopt a professional, factual, and organized tone, utilizing headers for structure.
The required format includes fields for Client Name(s), Date/Time, Attendees, and Venue.
The initial summary of the meeting indicates it was the first interaction with prospects to discuss goals, assess financial situations, and evaluate suitability for planning, noting the client was receptive and engaged.
The meeting agenda requires summarizing the purpose of the meeting.
Detailed notes on existing and new personal and financial information are to be inserted under Personal & Financial Circumstances.
Client Vulnerability section requires noting any identified vulnerabilities or their absence.
Needs & Objectives section is for listing the client's stated objectives.
Use of ISA Allowances section should detail any specific future use of ISA allowances, funding plans, or lack thereof.
Additional Pension Contributions section needs to mention specific future pension contributions and their funding, or the absence of such plans.
Knowledge & experience section requires summarizing gathered information on the client's familiarity with investing or financial products.
Attitude to Risk section is for summarizing information on the client's risk tolerance.
Any other business / follow up actions section must detail specific actions from the meeting and agreed-upon timelines.
Capacity for Loss section should include any relevant notes or indicate if this aspect was not addressed.
Suitability Assessment - Wrappers / products section requires summarizing the rationale for the suitability of existing client wrappers/products or the need for replacement, including justification for non-panel products, cost comparisons, and tax implications of any changes.
Suitability Assessment - Fund / Investment strategy section needs to summarize the rationale for the suitability of existing investment funds/strategy or the need for replacement, including justification for non-panel solutions, cost comparisons, and tax implications such as capital gains tax.
Suitability Assessment - Income Sustainability section requires summarizing the sustainability of the client's investment income, addressing any issues, recommending future income levels if current levels are unsustainable, and clearly outlining risks if the client wishes to maintain current income levels.

name: M&A Firm Discovery Call - Financial Services
author: Velum
description: Organize M&A call notes for financial firms. Summarizes business lines and data to aid evaluation.
body:
The primary purpose is to provide a structured template for capturing comprehensive information during an M&A discovery call with a financial services firm, covering its business lines, financial performance, and strategic integration points.
The initial section of the call summary records fundamental details such as the firm's name, call date, participants, key contacts, and overall context.
The Employee Benefits (EB) section assesses the business line's revenue, key products, top carriers, client profile, technology platforms, staffing structure, and potential for cross-selling with other firm divisions.
The Property & Casualty (P&C) evaluation focuses on its revenue, the mix between commercial and personal lines, top carriers, client base characteristics including concentration risk, claims trends, and cross-selling opportunities.
The Life Insurance business line is analyzed based on its revenue contribution, the mix of products offered, and its distribution strategy through internal or external channels.
The Wealth Management division is evaluated by its revenue, Assets Under Management (AUM), fee structure, primary custodians, client demographics, and its integration with retirement services for rollovers and conversions.
The Specialty Lines of Practice section identifies and assesses defined specialty areas like Captives or TPA Services by examining their revenue, unique expertise, and strategic partnerships.
The Retirement Plan Services section requires a detailed focus on its revenue, breakdown of plan types and assets, key recordkeeper relationships, advisory staff credentials, fiduciary service model, participant engagement strategies, revenue model, wealth conversion rates, cross-selling potential, and any operational risks.
The Financial Snapshot captures the firm's key financial metrics, including total revenue, EBITDA margin, year-over-year growth, revenue concentration from top clients, and the percentage breakdown of revenue by each line of business.
The Integration & Strategic Considerations section evaluates the firm's technology stack, billing practices, compliance requirements, cultural fit, leadership depth, scalability opportunities, and any identified risks or red flags.
The final section outlines actionable next steps following the call, including a list of requested documents, follow-up questions for the firm, and internal action items for the M&A team.

name: 📌 CLIENT REPORT (FINANCIAL PLANNING)
author: Velum
description: Paste the transcript. Create a client report with situation, objectives, risks, and next steps.
body:
The main objective is to prepare a complete financial and wealth planning report for a client, based on a meeting transcript, using clear, professional, and accessible language.
The report structure begins with an executive summary presenting the client's current situation, objectives, points of attention, and suggested general direction, allowing for quick reading in up to 1 minute.
