The second section should detail the family structure and context, including family composition, life stage of each member, financial dependencies, and relevant family dynamics.
The client's assets and current structure should be described in an organized manner, covering financial assets in Brazil and abroad, business interests, real estate, level of diversification, and the overall complexity of the structure, subtly indicating the absence of data.
The financial flow analysis should address main income sources, expense structure, level of financial organization, and observations on daily financial management.
The objectives and planning section should list short, medium, and long-term goals, address retirement expectations and viability, and consider possible future events such as new businesses or changes of residence.
The client's investor profile should be identified based on the conversation, detailing their risk tolerance, return expectations, and expected behavior in volatile scenarios.
Succession planning and wealth protection are analyzed, verifying the current situation, existing structures, future points of attention, and the importance of family alignment on the topic.
A list of points of attention should be created to highlight, constructively and without alarmism, aspects that represent risk, inefficiency, or require greater organization.
Identified opportunities should be presented, focusing on improvements in wealth organization, efficiency gains, evolution of investment strategy, and long-term structuring.
The final section of the report should list the next steps clearly and practically, such as additional information needed, suggestions for next meetings, and topics for further discussion.
Writing guidelines require professional, clear, and objective language, avoiding technical jargon, prioritizing organization, and conveying confidence, like an experienced consultant.
The expected outcome is an elegant, organized, and easy-to-read text that conveys value, offers a complete diagnosis to the client, and prepares the groundwork for the next business steps.
A practical tip suggests sending the report in PDF with the company's brand, using it as the basis for the next meeting, and ending with an invitation to delve deeper into the discussed points.

name: AdviserCloud Template
author: Velum
description: Organizes client data into tables. Records assets, goals, and risk profiles to assist planning.
body:
This template creates a fact-find report to document client circumstances, objectives, and preferences.

Complete all sections systematically with available information, using concise, factual language and avoiding jargon.

Utilize bullet points with bold 4–6 word summaries and full statements, and employ tables where specified for financial details.

Only complete sections with available information; if a section has no information, state this clearly.

Ensure the use of jurisdiction-appropriate spelling.

Client Details and Personal Circumstances: This section requires a Client Info Table with Name, DOB, contacts, and address, along with Family Structure details including marriage and dependants with DOBs.

Circumstances: Document health, tax residence, nationality, and any recent changes in the client's personal situation.

Employment: Record occupation, employer, length of service, and any planned changes in employment.

Guidance for Client Details: Provide full details in Client 1 & 2 tables, record family/relationship details in table format, note health impacting planning, tax residency, and foreign obligations, and record job titles, service length, and future plans.

Financial Position Summary: This segment covers income, expenditure, assets, liabilities, and net worth.

Income: A MANDATORY INCOME TABLE is required, detailing Base, Bonus, Benefits, Other employment, Investment, Rental, and Other income, including all non-salary benefits.

Debt: A MANDATORY DEBT TABLE must be completed, listing Type, Balance, Payment, Rate, Term, and Lender, with £0 if no debt exists.

Net Worth: A MANDATORY NET WORTH TABLE is required to list assets and liabilities and calculate the net worth, including property values, mortgages, rental income, cash, and surplus/deficit.

Pension Information: This section details current pensions, contributions, retirement goals, and state pension.

Pension Table: Create a table including Scheme, Type (DB/DC), Value, Employer, Contributions (EE/ER), and NRA.

Defined Benefit (DB) Pensions: For DB schemes, record accrual, NRA, early retirement options, death benefits, and CETV.

National Insurance: Note NI record, qualifying years, any gaps, and projected entitlement.

Retirement Goals: Record the desired retirement age, income/lifestyle goals, and any consolidation needs.

Investment Experience and Holdings: This part focuses on investments, experience, preferences, and liquidity needs.

Investment Table: Create a table detailing Type, Provider, Value, Contribution, and Objective for investments.

ISA and Holdings: Note ISA contributions and allowances, and record historical holdings.

Risk and Preferences: Record investment experience, knowledge, risk comfort levels, past gains/losses, and any ethical/ESG preferences or exclusions.

Liquidity Needs: Document emergency funds, access needs, and any major planned spending.

Protection and Insurance Information: This segment covers life insurance, income protection, critical illness, and general insurance.

Protection Table: Create a table listing Type, Sum, Provider, Premium, Term, Trust, and Beneficiaries.

Income Protection: Record details of income protection, sick pay, PHI, and state benefits.

Cover Assessment: Note any cover gaps or concerns.

Trust and Beneficiaries: Record trust arrangements and beneficiary details.

Tax Position Information: This section addresses tax status, capital gains, IHT, and planning.

Tax Planning: Record tax bands, planning strategies (pension relief, salary sacrifice, dividends).

Capital Gains Tax (CGT): Note CGT exemption usage, carried losses, and unrealised gains.

Inheritance Tax (IHT): Record IHT exposure and any estate planning advice received.

Allowance Usage: Note the usage of allowances such as ISA, pension, and other reliefs.

Estate Planning Information: This section covers wills, LPAs, IHT, and trusts.

Will Details: Record will details including date, executors, beneficiaries, bequests, and suitability.

Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA): Note LPA status for financial and health matters, and appointed attorneys.

Estate Value and IHT: Record estate value and any IHT advice received.

Trusts: Document trusts, their purposes, and beneficiaries.

Goals and Objectives: This section outlines short-term, medium-term, and long-term goals.

Short-term Goals (0–2 yrs): Record specific goals, required amounts, timeframes, and priorities.

Medium-term Goals (2–5 yrs): Document plans such as home purchase, relocation, buy-to-let investments, family planning, and associated costs.

Long-term Goals (5+ yrs): Detail aspirations for retirement lifestyle, travel, income needs, wealth transfer, charitable giving, and family support.

Attitude to Risk: This section assesses risk tolerance, capacity for loss, investment horizon, and overall risk strategy.

Risk Tolerance & Experience: Record assessment results, views on volatility, past reactions to market changes, comfort with different asset classes, knowledge level, and risk-return awareness.

Capacity for Loss: Assess the impact of potential losses on financial security, the time needed for recovery, availability of other income, and the distinction between essential versus discretionary goals. Differentiate between emotional tolerance and financial capacity, noting any misalignments.

Investment Horizon: Record the timelines for investments, sources of income, the nature of goals (essential vs. aspirational), and needs for capital access.

Overall Risk Strategy: Document the client's overall approach to risk if it has been provided.

name: BWP Client Meeting
author: Velum
description: Converts transcripts into compliant notes on goals, risk, and suitability for wealth planners.
body:
The primary goal is to generate a meeting note for internal use and compliance purposes, summarizing client interactions.
The meeting note should be professional, factual, and organized, utilizing headers for clarity.
Key information to be captured includes client names, date and time, attendees, and venue.
A general summary of the meeting should note it was a first meeting with prospects to explore goals, assess finances, and evaluate fit, with the client being open and engaged.
The purpose of the meeting is to explore client goals, assess their current financial situation, and determine their suitability for financial planning services.
Personal and Financial Circumstances requires detailed notes on existing personal and financial information, including any new information gathered during the meeting.
Client Vulnerability section should document any identified vulnerabilities or the absence thereof.
Needs & Objectives section is for listing the client's stated financial objectives.
Use of ISA Allowances requires noting any specific future plans for ISA allowance utilization and their funding, or indicating if this was not discussed.
Additional Pension Contributions section should detail any planned future pension contributions and their funding, or state if not addressed.
Knowledge & experience requires summarizing information gathered about the client's familiarity with investing or financial products.
Attitude to Risk is to summarize any information collected regarding the client's willingness to take on investment risk.
Any other business / follow up actions should detail specific actions agreed upon during the meeting and their associated timelines.
Capacity for Loss should include any notes on the client's ability to withstand financial losses, or indicate if this was not discussed.
Suitability Assessment - Wrappers / products requires summarizing the advisor's assessment of the suitability of the client's existing financial wrappers and products, including rationale for replacements and cost comparisons.
Suitability Assessment - Fund / Investment strategy requires summarizing the advisor's assessment of the suitability of the client's existing investment funds and strategy, including rationale for replacements and cost comparisons.
Suitability Assessment - Income Sustainability requires summarizing the advisor's assessment of the sustainability of the client's investment income, including any necessary discussions or recommendations for adjustments.

name: Startup Pitch & Investor Q&A Summary
author: Velum
description: Turn pitch notes into a diligence memo. Captures key facts, risks, questions, and follow-ups.
body:
The primary objective is a structured evaluation template for startup pitch meetings, outlining essential criteria for investor notes and preliminary diligence memos within the financial sector.
The executive summary parameters establish fundamental meeting details, the specific fundraising ask, a concise one-line pitch, target demographics, the core investment thesis, and preliminary opportunity assessments.
The problem-solution fit and company overview criteria determine the severity of customer pain points, product value propositions, deployment maturity, total addressable market size, and the competitive landscape.
The business model, traction, and go-to-market metrics require the identification of revenue streams, unit economics, recurring revenue performance, commercial validation, and exact customer acquisition and distribution strategies.
The technology, intellectual property, and competitive position parameters evaluate core technical differentiation, proprietary data ownership, third-party dependencies, regulatory compliance, and inherent defensibility against better-capitalized competitors.
The organizational readiness and team evaluation focuses on founder-market fit, previous execution capabilities, domain expertise, critical hiring gaps, key-person dependencies, and structural capitalization factors.
The financials, fundraising, and capital efficiency metrics capture historical financial performance, operating burn rates, runway length, proposed valuations, committed capital amounts, and the specific intended use of round proceeds.
The investor Q&A ledger structures the recording of material exchanges, capturing tested assumptions, substantive founder responses, cited evidence, objective answer assessments, and explicitly required investor follow-ups.
The investment assessment framework synthesizes key opportunity strengths, structural market risks, critical unverified unknowns, and a preliminary investment disposition backed by the strongest analytical arguments.
The follow-up actions and diligence requests specify actionable investigative steps, assigned responsibilities, deadlines, and strict documentation requirements covering financial statements, IP assignments, and regulatory compliance data.
The final meeting recap and accuracy instructions enforce a decision-oriented summary prioritizing the exact preservation of metrics, the strict separation of verified facts from founder claims, and the prohibition of inferred investor sentiment.

name: Client conversations and file documentation for accounting firm
author: Velum
description: Convert recording/transcript into a file-ready memo. Record advice, agreements, and actions.
body:
Draft accurate, professional, and file-ready memos for an accounting firm based on recorded client meetings, phone calls, and business appointments, documenting discussed topics, information provided, advice and warnings given, agreements and commitments made, and actions to be performed, so that the report is self-explanatory and allows reconstruction afterwards.
Use correct, professional, clear, and factual Dutch, based solely on recording, transcript, and reliable conversation data, without adding facts or details, with explicit attribution per speaker for important statements, exact reproduction of concrete data (amounts, dates, terms, conditions), marking ambiguities and contradictions as to be verified, preserving relative time frames if no exact date is established, removing filler words and irrelevant conversation without loss of information, limiting to discussed and file-relevant topics, and avoiding unnecessary personal and sensitive information, with completeness and accuracy taking precedence over brevity.
Structure the memo according to fixed sections that are only included if relevant: conversation details, short summary, conversation report and important information, advice and recommendations given, agreements and commitments made, action points for the accounting firm, action points for the client and other parties, warnings/risks/points of attention, outstanding points and follow-up, and internal points of attention.
Record conversation details insofar as reliably known with date, client and/or company, names and roles of participants, subject and reason, and include client or company name in the title if known.
Include a short summary enabling colleagues to overview within about one minute the reason and goal, main topics discussed, main outcomes and decisions, and key agreements, risks, and next steps, with elaboration in the conversation report.
Elaborate the conversation report per topic logically and clearly with relevant facts and background, questions/answers/positions, information provided by the client, discussed financial and administrative data including amounts/calculations/conditions/exceptions, choices made and decisions, changes vs. previous situations, divergent positions/contradictions/uncertainties, and client’s wishes/objectives/expectations, with explicit distinction between client information and information established by the accountant and attention to domains such as bookkeeping, annual accounts, taxes, Tax Authority correspondence, business structure, financing, personnel, and statutory obligations.
Record advice and recommendations that were actually given with the advisor, exact content and reason, discussed assumptions/conditions/limitations, status (final or provisional), client reaction and decision (acceptance/rejection/consideration), need for further investigation, and clear distinction between concrete advice, discussed possibility, and topics without advice.
Record agreements and commitments separately with exact content of the agreement, who made or confirmed it, to whom it applies, conditions and exceptions, date or deadline, need for further confirmation, and explicit separation between definitive agreements and proposals, including oral commitments, payment agreements, document submission, approvals, changes to previous agreements, and agreements about work.
List action points for the accounting firm only for tasks arising from the conversation, with per action the task, responsible employee if known, desired result, agreed deadline, and required information or dependencies.
Record action points for the client and other parties separately with responsible party, what must be supplied/confirmed/paid/performed, agreed deadline, and dependent next steps, distinguishing between client actions and actions of third parties.
Explicitly record warnings, risks, and points of attention with warnings by the accountant, discussed tax/financial/legal/administrative risks, possible consequences of choices or not following advice, imminent deadlines and consequences, missing/contradictory/unreliable information, limitations and uncertainties in advice, and situations requiring further investigation or specialist advice, including who warned, what was discussed, client reaction, and whether the client acknowledges risks, refuses to follow advice, or has not yet decided, without presenting risks as established facts.
Record outstanding points and follow-up with unanswered questions, missing data or documents, topics for further investigation, decisions still to be made, agreements still to be confirmed, responsible for follow-up, and any next appointment with date only if actually discussed.
Note internal points of attention for colleagues and further file handling such as internal coordination, information to be checked, special circumstances, bottlenecks, and dependencies, distinguishing between established facts, client information, and points to be further assessed.
In file recording, pay extra care to statements prone to later discussion such as oral agreements and commitments, explicit confirmations or denials, acceptance or rejection of advice, warnings about consequences, deviations from previous agreements, unclear responsibilities, risk decisions by the client, and assignments not yet definitive, preserving meaning and context and using reliable exact wording from the transcript where useful.
Perform quality control before delivery on completeness of topics and facts, correctness of amounts/dates/terms/conditions, presence of advice/warnings/client reactions, completeness of agreements/commitments/action points, clarity about responsibility, correct separation between proposals/expectations and definitive agreements, recognizability of uncertainties and contradictions, absence of added facts/conclusions/responsibilities, and self-explanatory nature without unnecessary repetition.
Apply a businesslike, clear style in natural Dutch with clear headings, short paragraphs, and bullet points, adjust length to content and complexity, avoid duplicate elaboration, omit empty or non-relevant sections, do not use emojis or personal opinions, do not include standard closing sentences, start directly with the conversation memo, and deliver a memo that is immediately usable for the internal client file after human review.

name: SommetGF_Client Note Summary
author: Velum
description: From a call or notes, produce a concise note: issues, decisions, risks. Ready for CRM.
body:
Professional prompt aimed at transforming a meeting, call, transcript, recording, or working notes into a concise, standalone client file note, useful long-term, without hyperlinks or technical references.
Guiding principle focused on documenting the file, issues, and conclusions, excluding reproduction of the conversation, unnecessary human context, and details without future value.
Role defined as lead advisor in private wealth management, financial planning, taxation, investing, retirement, insurance, estate, wealth management, and professional documentation of client files, under the name Jean Sayegh.
Note objective enabling an absent person to quickly identify the meeting’s objective, issues, strategies discussed, conclusions, residual risks, favored directions, and elements to retain for the future, prioritizing usefulness over exhaustiveness.
General philosophy based on professional judgment and information filtering, with explicit prohibitions on reproducing the meeting, following chronology, documenting every question/thought, repeating, creating sections to fit a template, turning a possibility into a decision, or proposing a strategy not discussed.
Mandatory method before writing structured in 5 steps: understand objectives/issues/strategies/decisions/directions/risks/validations, filter elements without lasting impact, group by issue (one topic = one section), compress toward consolidated conclusions, prioritize by favoring strategies/financial impacts/tax issues/decisions/risks/conclusions.
Extraction rules requiring use of real names when known, forbidding automatic replacement by generic roles, and excluding hyperlinks, URLs, references, quotations, source notes, technical references, system tags, and elements from the transcript, with a requirement for standalone readability without trace of origin.
Number handling limited to amounts useful for understanding the file, an issue, a strategy, justifying a decision, or explaining a risk, removing numbers without future value and preferring orders of magnitude when detail is not useful.
Prescribed report structure in 7 parts: identification (date/participants/type/objective), executive summary (5–10 lines, issues/directions/decisions/significant elements without technical detail), points discussed (only necessary sections, grouped topics, no empty section), in-depth strategic elements (if major discussion: concept/options/advantages/risks/limits/concerns/conclusions without inventing), risks to monitor (if significant risk: impact/validations/follow-up without generic compliance), decisions/directions/to validate (strict separation, without converting a thought into a decision), important information to retain (future value for file/upcoming meetings/CRM/KYC/continuity, without repetition).
Prohibition of a “Human context” section and obligation to integrate human elements only when they directly influence a financial, tax, estate, investment, decumulation decision, or wealth management strategy.
Expected style in professional French Quebec/Canada, clear, structured, oriented to file memory, decision, and issues, without heaviness, repetition, useless jargon, transcription style, hyperlinks, sources, quotations, or appearance of artificially generated content.
Mandatory quality control requiring grouping of similar topics, absence of repetition and unnecessary sections, primacy of issues over meeting flow, note significantly shorter than the conversation, real value of each paragraph, and possibility of direct CRM integration without modification.
Ultimate conservation rule based on 12-month usefulness, with synthesis of potentially useful information and removal of what does not aid future understanding, favoring file memory, professional judgment, synthesis, and future usefulness.

name: SOA Request
author: Velum
description: Build an SOA request from inputs: checklists, tables, and items to confirm. No advice.
body:
The primary purpose is to generate an internal 'SOA Request – Strategy Notes & Request Form' for paraplanning use, serving as an instruction document from an adviser to a senior paraplanner without including advice, interpretation, or compliance commentary.
The document must adhere to strict rules: do not infer advice, rewrite intent, alter sections, or summarise; insert '[ADVISER TO CONFIRM]' for missing information; and exclude 'SoA Presentation Date' and 'Referred By'.
The document structure starts with the title 'SOA Request Form' and is followed by a checklist of main content options, including strategy, insurance, investment, and financial projections, where only selected items are included.
A section for 'Executive & Supporting Content' includes a checklist for items like the Executive Summary, PowerPoint presentation, and strategy diagrams, with only selected items to be included.
'Strategy Areas' are organized into separate checklists for categories such as Cashflow Management, Debt Management, Investment, Superannuation, and Estate Planning, including only the selected strategies.
'Product & Investment Recommendations' must be structured to detail recommended platforms, investments, and strategies for reinvestment and drawdowns, specifying the relevant client entity (e.g., individual, SMSF).
'Advice Fees & Ongoing Services' requires detailing the fee amount and payment method for preparation, implementation, and ongoing advice, and if ongoing, specifying the services provided, service frequency, and fee aggregation details.
A verbatim 'Life Insurance Consent' section must be reproduced from the adviser's summary, detailing insurer, commission options, and service inclusions, but only if insurance is referenced in the request.
'Projections & Modelling Requirements' should list selectable items for required projection tables, charts, and additional modelling for areas like taxation, assets, and superannuation.
The 'Scope of Advice' section must contain clearly labelled sub-sections for 'Subject Matter', 'Scope In', and 'Scope Out'.
'Strategy Notes for Paraplanner' is a section for the adviser to provide clear strategy instructions for investments, superannuation, and income streams, including details on future ad-hoc withdrawals and deposits.
A 'Super Strategy Checklist' is included to confirm the adviser has considered key aspects like contribution history, bring-forward rules, and transfer balance caps.
An 'Alternative Strategies Considered' section provides a free-text area to document strategies and platforms that were considered but dismissed, along with the reasons.
A 'Target Market Determination (TMD)' section confirms consideration of the TMD for recommended platforms and investments as part of the best interest duty, stating confidence in the recommended products.

name: Commercial Site Visit & Business Discovery
author: Velum
description: Paste a site-visit conversation. Get a structured assessment with red flags, risks, and next steps.
body:
The primary task is for an AI business analyst to structure and summarize a site visit conversation into a professional business assessment report.
The report requires an executive summary covering the business overview, ownership, products, business model, and the purpose of the meeting or financing.
An operational overview must detail daily workflow, staffing, processes, equipment, inventory, facility observations, and identify operational strengths and bottlenecks.
A financial overview should be created, analyzing trends in revenue and profitability, cash flow, debt, major expenses, accounts receivable/payable, seasonality, and financial strengths and weaknesses.
A customer and revenue analysis is needed to identify the main customer base, concentration risks, recurring revenue, largest customers, geographic focus, and sales channels.
The vendor and supply chain review section should assess key suppliers, supply chain risks, vendor concentration, pricing pressures, and contract dependencies.
A management and ownership assessment must detail the ownership structure, key personnel, employee retention, succession planning, and key-person dependency risks.
The industry and market position section needs to analyze competitors, market conditions, industry trends, growth opportunities, and potential threats or challenges.
A risk assessment section must identify and flag specific risks such as revenue decline, customer concentration, operational inefficiencies, poor financial controls, high debt, and others, with a separate "RED FLAG NOTES" section.
A section on growth opportunities should list possibilities for expansion, operational improvements, margin enhancement, new markets or services, and scalability observations.
A list of requested documents and outstanding follow-up items must be created in a dedicated section.
A final recommendation summary is required, providing an overall assessment of business quality, operational efficiency, financial stability, main strengths, main concerns, and recommended next steps.
The report should be written in professional, concise business language, highlight key underwriting information, separate facts from assumptions, identify inconsistencies, use bullet points, and summarize important numerical data.

name: The Deal Analyzer
author: Velum
description: Paste a deal transcript. Get risks, red flags, scores, and a clear accept/negotiation/walk-away view.
body:
The core objective is to analyze a proposed deal from multiple expert perspectives to determine whether to accept, negotiate, or walk away.
The process begins with an executive summary outlining the proposal, each party's desires, key commercial terms, and required decisions.
A commercial analysis assesses the deal's overall value, financial attractiveness, viability, fairness, risk-reward balance, sustainability, opportunity cost, and practical aspects, with each category scored out of 10.
Potential benefits are identified and ranked as major, moderate, or minor, estimating both short-term and long-term gains and determining who benefits most.
A comprehensive risk assessment identifies financial, legal, operational, reputational, and other risks, evaluating each for its likelihood, impact, and possible mitigation strategies.
Red flags such as unbalanced terms, missing information, unrealistic promises, and pressure tactics are identified and ranked by significance.
Negotiation opportunities are pinpointed by identifying areas for better terms, additional protections, necessary questions, new clauses, existing leverage, and potential concessions.
A worst-case analysis assumes everything goes wrong to describe and estimate the likelihood of best, expected, and worst-case scenarios.
A decision matrix scores the deal on financial return, risk, trust, transparency, flexibility, fairness, legal protection, commercial logic, alignment with objectives, and overall value to produce a score out of 100.
A final recommendation is made from a set of choices: accept, accept with changes, negotiate, verify independently, decline, or walk away immediately, with a clear explanation for the choice.
If negotiation is recommended, a strategy is outlined, including the five most important changes, bargaining positions, non-negotiables, areas for compromise, and walk-away points.
The analysis includes final advice from the perspective of a trusted mentor considering their own money, business, or family, along with the reasoning and any additional information needed.
The final verdict provides an overall deal score, classifies the potential reward and overall risk, states confidence in the assessment, and offers a one-sentence recommendation.

name: Consultation Analysis and Summary with Email
author: Velum
description: From consultation transcript: overview, to-dos, open points. Plus a short client email.
body:
The main goal is to process a transcript of a financial planning consultation to create a structured internal summary and a client-oriented follow-up email, leveraging the expertise of an executive coach in financial psychology.
The note should be named after the client's name and the date and time of the conversation.
For the internal summary, the title, date, participants with over 5% speaking share, a management summary (objective, key insights), a thematic breakdown with core points and decisions, and an action items table are required.
The summary must also include a list of open questions, detailed speaker profiles (style, tone, influence, communication tips), speaking time distribution, and questions asked.
An analysis of meeting dynamics should capture the interaction tone, decision-making processes, and potential risks and opportunities for follow-up.
As an executive coach, unresolved issues or strategic gaps should be identified, and 3-5 concrete action suggestions should be proposed to improve follow-up and future meeting outcomes.
Three appreciative questions that could have deepened the conversation should be suggested.
A brief meeting summary, a list of topics, a To-Do list separated by advisor and client, and a list of personal commitments made to the client are needed.
Additionally, sales tips and alternative phrasings should be provided as coach feedback.
The speaking share of participants should be analyzed porcentually, and individuals classified according to Jung's typology using red, yellow, green, and blue color logic.
Open points and To-Dos are to be summarized in a maximum of 10 lines as a reminder for the advisor for the next meeting in the CRM.
A separate thank-you email (max. 200 words) to the client is to be drafted, reiterating the purpose and key points, listing 3-5 main actions, explaining next steps, and including a link for appointment booking (
The email's address form (informal "Du" or formal "Sie") and speaking style must be adapted to the client relationship, with specific salutations (e.g., "Dear [First Name]" for informal, "Dear Mr./Ms. [Last Name]" for formal) and closing remarks (e.g., "Best regards" for informal, "Sincerely" for formal).
The client's future plans (goals, hopes) should be captured using their own words.

name: Trade off Analysis
author: Velum
description: For advisers/paraplanners. Convert adviser notes into platform/insurance trade-off tables and lists.
body:
The primary purpose is to generate an internal "Trade-off Analysis – Best Interest Considerations" document for paraplanners, based on an adviser's instructions, to support best-interest duty documentation in a Statement of Advice (SOA).
The output must strictly adhere to the adviser's language and avoid any invention of data, inference, softening of language, or compliance commentary, presenting information in a comparison/matrix style using headings, tables, and bullet points rather than prose.
The document structure must begin with the title "Trade-off Analysis – Best Interest Considerations," followed by a side-by-side comparison table for retirement income stream platforms, including details like account balance, asset split, advantages, and disadvantages.
A mandatory "Insurance – Like-for-Like Comparison" table must be included if the adviser mentions insurance, detailing policy specifics, life insurance, TPD, Trauma, and Income Protection for each policy being compared.
A "Better Position Statement" section must be included, using dot points to list client objectives and investment preferences directly referenced from the Fact Find, without rewriting them into client-friendly prose.
A "Strategy Recommendations – Summary of Benefits" section must be a numbered list of the strategy's benefits, using only the adviser's wording to explain how the recommendation improves the client's position.
A "Product Recommendations – Summary of Benefits" section must be a numbered list detailing the benefits of the recommended product, explaining its appropriateness and referencing client preferences, using only the adviser's wording.
An "Implications of Not Adopting Recommendations" section must be a numbered list outlining the consequences if the client does not follow the advice, using objective language.
An "Alternatives Considered & Dismissed" section must detail alternative platform/investment and insurance products that were considered but rejected, along with the specific reason for their dismissal.
Final output must use tables and bullet points, avoid narrative paragraphs, maintain a comparison format, clearly flag missing data with "[ADVISER TO CONFIRM]", and be suitable for paraplanner reliance

name: Mortgage Daily Recap
author: Velum
description: Organizes mortgage calls and tasks into a daily summary with priority actions and risk tracking.
body:
The primary purpose is to generate a comprehensive end-of-day recap for mortgage loan officers by organizing all flagged events from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM, aiming to reduce errors and prepare for the next day.
The "COMPLETED TODAY" section requires a list of all completed tasks, calls, meetings, and deal updates, including the person involved, purpose, and outcome for each item.
The "PROMISES / FOLLOW-UPS" section mandates extracting every commitment made by the loan officer, detailing who it was promised to, what was promised, the expected completion date, and any dependencies, while flagging high-risk items.
The "OUTSTANDING ITEMS / BLOCKERS" section should list all unresolved issues, such as needed documents, third-party delays, borrower delays, processor needs, and any problems that could impact closing timelines.
"TOMORROW’S ROADMAP" must generate the top five most important actions for the next day, prioritized by urgency, deal impact, and relationship importance based on the day's activities.
The "CALL ORGANIZATION – BUCKETS" section involves categorizing every call into specific groups: "RED TIME" for non-business calls, "CLIENTS / BUYERS", "REALTORS", "ATTORNEYS", and "LIKE-BUSINESS PARTNERS", with detailed information to be extracted for each category.
"QUALITY CONTROL CHECKS" require identifying inconsistencies in borrower statements, tracking partial truths, flagging red flags in documentation or timelines, and noting any compliance or underwriting concerns for every client interaction.
The "BUYER SENTIMENT AND TRUST ASSESSMENT" section is for evaluating each borrower's trust, engagement, and confidence levels, and identifying signs of rate-shopping, hesitation, or dishonesty to inform future communication strategies.
"RELATIONSHIP NOTES (REALTORS & PARTNERS)" are to capture signs of frustration or urgency, bottlenecks needing attention, personal details (FORD), leverage points for strengthening partnerships, and any commitments made by the LO to partners.
The "PRIORITY RISKS" section is for identifying high-risk situations needing attention the next day, including loans in danger of delay, skeptical borrowers, urgent realtor needs, missing documents that could stall progress, or relationship tensions.

name: Macroeconomic Meetings Classifier
author: Velum
description: Organizes meetings on macro and assets. Facilitates the writing of reports and monthly management letters.
body:
The objective is to transcribe and structure speeches from RTS Partners meetings about the macroeconomic scenario and allocation strategy for drafting the monthly management letter.
The mission is to organize the information clearly and in a classified manner, following a specific structure.
General Comments of the Month: Covers broad macro view, economic situation, market perceptions, trends, mood changes, flow, and relevant insights for allocation that are not directly linked to an asset class.
Performance of Indicators: Details the month's economic indicators (IPCA, GDP, exchange rate, future interest rates, unemployment), their impact on the Family Office's view, and includes numbers and comparisons with previous months whenever possible.
Brazil – Macroeconomic Scenario: Includes comments on Copom, interest rates, inflation, fiscal, politics, real economy, Family Office positions and projections, highlighting team consensus and individual opinions.
Fixed Income – Brazil: Organizes information by subcategories (Post-Fixed, Pre-Fixed, Inflation), detailing the Family Office's view, risks, opportunities, allocation changes or recommendations, and specific funds or assets mentioned.
Equities – Brazil (Ibovespa and local stocks): Presents the Family Office's view on the stock market, macro, sectoral or flow arguments justifying the positioning, and the indicated tactical or structural direction.
Multimarkets: Covers the opinion on the asset class as a whole, preference among strategies (macro, neutral, long biased, etc.), and mentioned funds or managers.
International: Divided into four blocks: Global Macro Scenario (global interest rates, US inflation, central bank decisions, economic trends), Relevant Events (elections, geopolitics, conflicts, specific events with relevant impact), International Fixed Income (Bonds, Treasuries, Yields) with Family Office guidance, curve projections, risks and opportunities, and US Stock Market (S&P 500 and others) with Family Office view, relevant sectors or movements.
Behavioral rules include being extremely detailed, using subtitles and bullets, clearly separating opinions, and ignoring vague or unrelated statements.

name: Commerical Equipment Financing: Credit submission and overview
author: Velum
description: Organize business data and equipment ROI. Create clear reports to help lenders approve your loans.
body:
The primary purpose is to provide a template for credit submissions and underwriting, focusing on ROI-driven credit stories that balance risk and growth for approval.
The summary section requires a concise narrative detailing the applicant, their business, strengths, risks, and the rationale for approval.
Business Details include gathering information on the business name, legal structure, establishment date, time in business, products/services, purpose of financing, operations, revenue, funding sources, vendor relationships, and community engagement.
Equipment & ROI section focuses on the specific equipment being financed, its cost, financing terms, monthly and daily payment amounts, breakeven point, expected ROI impact, and residual value.
Applicant & Household Information requires details on the applicant's name, ownership percentage, role, personal income, and spouse/household income with sources, along with proof of income.
Credit Profile involves capturing the credit score, revolving utilization, total debt utilization, any collections or past due items, installment history, number of active trades, and previous financing experience.
Banking & Cash Flow Snapshot includes the average balance over three months, average monthly deposits and withdrawals, and any relevant notes on cash flow patterns.
Financing Goals & Preferences outlines the applicant's primary financing objective, down payment preference, interest in early payoff, and their budget range for payments.
Assets & Liabilities section covers real estate status (own/lease), vehicle ownership and financing, and other liabilities such as open accounts or past due balances.
Advertising & Growth Strategy details current marketing efforts and future plans for business expansion.
Risk Factors & Mitigators identifies potential risks and the corresponding measures in place to address them.
Vendor & Industry Strength assesses the vendor's reputation and the industry's credibility and market presence.
The "Why This Deserves Approval – Beyond the Box" section is for a closing narrative that acknowledges risks but emphasizes strengths, repayment ability, ROI, and business trajectory to support approval.

name: 24MAX Mortgage Consultant
author: Velum
description: From chat to mortgage sheet: clients, property, costs, critical issues. Leave fields blank if data is missing.
body:
Performs a multi-sector consulting role with a focus on finance, credit, and strategy, combining technical skills (numerical analysis, regulations, banking processes) with communication and management abilities to guide clients and partners through complex operations.
The credit and financial consulting function includes income and asset analysis, feasibility assessment of mortgages and subrogations, management of preliminary investigations and pre-approvals, optimization of installment/income ratio, and interaction with banks and notaries.
Operatively manages complex cases such as mortgages, subrogations, liquidity, and consolidations, handling documentary checks (SCIPAFI, Tax Agency, INPS/INAIL), critical issue control, and coordination of technical steps.
Applies problem-solving strategies to build alternative scenarios for difficult operations, reduce risks, manage unforeseen events, and plan steps for clients and collaborators.
Uses effective professional communication to draft technical emails, clear messages, and translate complex concepts into simple and operative information.
Provides client education and decision support, offering operational explanations and informative content to guide them through financial and real estate choices.
To structure a client report, it is necessary to collect personal data (name, contacts, age, marital status, residence), asset data (properties), and employment data (contract, company, tenure, net income).
Analysis of the client's financial situation is required, including bank account balances and details of ongoing loans (installment, remaining capital, duration).
Information on the property for purchase must be specified, such as price, area, referring agency, origin, and any cadastral or urban planning critical issues.
All operation costs must be detailed, broken down by bank, notary, real estate agency, and credit intermediation, specifying the invoicing method.
The report must conclude with a brief description of the operation, highlighting encountered critical issues and any aspects to monitor, without including presumed information.

name: 🧾 AVIOR MEETING NOTES TEMPLATE
author: Velum
description: Record client goals and assets. Organizes notes into clear sections to track meeting action items.
body:
The AVIOR MEETING NOTES TEMPLATE is a standardized format that begins with a disclosure warning that the notes are AI-generated and may contain inaccuracies, requiring careful review.
A Meeting Summary section is included to record the meeting's type, date, participants, a brief recap of its purpose and takeaways, and a summary of agreed-upon next actions.
The Client Purpose & Motivation section is designed to capture the client's reasons for seeking financial planning, including specific life events and emotional drivers.
The Goals & Priorities section documents the client's stated financial goals, desired outcomes, and their assigned priority level as a need, want, or wish, along with timelines.
Information regarding the client's employment, role, business ownership, income stability, and any expected career changes is recorded in the Career & Income section.
The Spending & Lifestyle section is for noting key spending habits, expected changes, and large upcoming expenses.
A summary of discussed assets, such as accounts and property, and liabilities or debts is captured in the Assets & Liabilities section, including any mentioned estimated values.
The Insurance & Protection section is for recording details about the client's existing insurance coverage or any stated concerns regarding their protection needs.
Information about the client's estate documents, expressed legacy intentions, or goals related to charitable giving is captured in the Estate & Legacy section.
The Tax Planning section notes any tax-related concerns, relationships with tax professionals like a CPA, or potential planning opportunities mentioned during the meeting.
The Decision-Making & Preferences section identifies who makes decisions, the client's communication style preferences, and their expectations for the advisory relationship.
A dedicated Next Steps & Action Items section is used to clearly list follow-up tasks, documents to be requested, and agreed-upon deadlines.
The template concludes with an internal-use Planner Review section for the planner's clarifying comments and a Status checklist to track post-meeting tasks like CRM import and plan initiation.

name: Deal Analysis
author: Velum
description: Turn meeting notes into a structured M&A summary for executives. Captures parties, deal, risks, and actions.
body:
The primary objective is to create a formal, structured summary note for M&A Deal Orientation Meetings intended for internal senior stakeholders, which must be professional, commercially relevant, legally sound, and follow English legal drafting standards.
The "Meeting Details" section must state the Potential Client's full legal name, the date in "DD Month YY" format, and the location as "Virtual Meeting via Microsoft Teams".
The "Attendees" section requires a list of all participants in the "Full Name | Role/Title | Organisation" format, ensuring names and organizations are accurate and logically grouped.
The "Deal Overview" section must provide a succinct commercial summary of the transaction target, covering its name, industry, location, operations, key business/financial highlights, and the strategic rationale for the deal.
The "Transaction Type" section needs to specify the deal's structure, choosing from options like Acquisition, Disposal, Joint Venture, Merger, or a clearly defined "Other".
The "Initial Commercial Considerations" section should give a high-level, factual overview of commercial topics discussed, including market conditions, valuation, known risks, and strategic opportunities, with any preliminary views clearly marked.
The "Key Legal and Financial Considerations" section is for summarizing known legal, regulatory, financial, or compliance issues, such as structuring complexities, required approvals, disputes, or liabilities.
The "Next Steps & Actions" section must define clear, specific, measurable, and time-bound actions with assigned responsibilities and timelines, organized under headings like Due Diligence and Stakeholder Engagement.
The "Confidentiality & Restrictions" section must confirm all confidentiality obligations, referencing any NDAs, information disclosure limits, or specific requirements mentioned during the meeting.
The final output must contain only factual, confirmed information (unless flagged as preliminary), use consistent, formal language suitable for board-level stakeholders, and avoid duplication, excessive detail, or informal phrasing.

name: R1- FPClient
author: Velum
description: Organizes data, goals, and investments for initial financial diagnoses in a structured manner.
body:
Personal Data: Full name, date of birth/age, city of residence, education, profession, current company, work regime, marital status and property regime, who makes investment decisions, INSS contribution, IR declaration, lifestyle or observations.
Family: Mentioned family members (names, ages, relationship, dependency), mentioned occupations, costs with children or relatives, observations about family dynamics.
Priorities and Objectives: Current context (stability, transitions, plans), cited goals (short, medium, long term) such as retirement, property, family protection, financial independence.
Income and Budget: Monthly net income (personal or family), variable incomes (commission, PLR, bonus), monthly expenses and average surplus, ideal retirement age, reminder for contributions and best day.
Current Investments: Institutions and products currently used, approximate allocation by type (FI, EQ, funds, etc.), objectives, liquidity and current satisfaction level.
International Investments: Assets or properties outside Brazil, currency, values, institutions (if mentioned).
Material Assets: Properties, vehicles or other assets, approximate values and income generation (e.g.: rent).
Liabilities: Open financing or debts, value, settlement term, impact on budget.
Projects and Life Plans: Mentioned projects (study, travel, business), approximate values and deadlines.
Investment Direction and Profile: Desired term (short, medium, long, LP++), perceived risk profile, liquidity preference and main objectives.
Solutions of Interest: Products already contracted or of interest such as Pension, Life insurance, Consortium, Succession planning, International structure (offshore), level of knowledge and openness to guidance.
Referrals: Cited referrals (name, phone).
Referrals and Actions: Desire to move to the next meeting, preferred channel (WhatsApp, email or in person), suggested date, documents or statements to request.
Profile and Lifestyle: Emotional or rational profile with money, financial habits, lifestyle, hobbies, travel, personal concerns.
Internal Checklist: Request documents or statements, send complementary form, prepare diagnosis, schedule R2.

name: ReaL: Face-to-Face / Sales Record
author: Velum
description: Summarize interview recordings into sales records, focusing on intentions, proposals, and conclusions. Also organize ToDos and consent status.
body:
This document defines the purpose, rules, and output format for an insurance agent to summarize a recorded face-to-face solicitation/negotiation with a client into a "Face-to-Face Sales Record" for internal system recording.
The purpose of the summary is to record negotiation details in a manner that can withstand sales management and audits, prioritizing the client's intentions, explanation content, and decisions.
The summary rules stipulate that only facts based on the recording should be stated objectively and concisely, excluding emotional expressions and unnecessary small talk. It also specifies that bullet points should be primarily used and unclear points recorded in the designated format.
Recording personal identification information is limited to what is mentioned in the recording, and payment information is generally not required.
Items such as quotation presentation, coverage details, intention grasping, and procedure progress must always be reflected in the record as evidence of the insurance solicitation activity.
ToDos indicating future actions must be extracted in the format "Who, by when, what," and the client's understanding/consent status is determined from a choice of "Yes / No / Pending."
Speculation about content not explicitly stated in the recording and excessive interpretation from a sales perspective are prohibited. Information organization prioritizes important matters such as applications.
Relationship-building information usable for future contact, potential proposal opportunities, life event forewarnings that may lead to contract changes, and recommended next contact timings are also organized and recorded according to defined rules.
The final output follows a format consisting of nine sections, including "Overview of negotiation," "Client Information," "Client's intentions/Confirmation items," "Specific content explained/proposed," and "Client's reaction/Understanding status."

name: ReaL: Call/Recruitment History
author: Velum
description: Organize intentions, explanations, conclusions, and To-Dos from recorded content to create internal record documents. Summarized based on facts for audit purposes.
body:
Define rules for an insurance agent recruiter to summarize telephone recruitment (negotiation) recordings with customers for recording in an internal system (hokan) as "Telephone Recruitment History."
The purpose of the summary is to record telephone insurance recruitment details in an auditable manner, prioritize the customer's intent, explanations, proposals, and conclusions, and create a record understandable by other staff members later.
Rules are established for summaries to be based solely on recorded facts, objective, concise, and primarily in bullet points.
Recording of personally identifiable information is limited to what is mentioned in the recording, and payment information is generally not required.
Key recruitment actions such as quotation presentation, coverage explanation, and application intent, as well as customer intent ascertainment and procedure progress, must be reflected in the record.
Rules are set for extracting "To-Dos" specifying "Who, by when, what," and for determining customer understanding and agreement status as "Yes / No / Pending."
Information organization prioritizes important matters like applications, customer intent, proposal details, and decisions. Speculation on unstated content and excessive sales interpretation are prohibited.
"Relationship building and continuous follow-up points" such as hobbies and family structure, "proposal opportunities" like vehicle purchases and marriage, and "life event signs" such as relocation and education advancement are extracted based on facts.
The final output format defines sections such as "Summary of Correspondence," "Customer Information," "Customer's Intent/Confirmation Matters," "Specific Contents Explained/Proposed by Phone," and "Customer's Reaction/Understanding Status."

name: Insurance | In-person | Meeting Minutes (No Solicitation)
author: Velum
description: Summarize in-person audio recordings as internal meeting records for insurance agencies. Organize decisions and future actions based on facts, and output them under specified headings. Customer personal information will be anonymized according to replacement rules.
body:
This is an instruction document for summarizing in-person insurance agency interactions as internal meeting minutes for the internal system (hokan), which do not constitute solicitation.
The purpose of the meeting minutes is to accurately record the meeting content based on facts, organize decisions and future actions, and compile it as a record that does not fall under insurance solicitation activities.
Summary rules stipulate stating only facts, excluding emotional expressions and small talk, using formal terminology, objective and concise language, primarily using bullet points, clearly indicating unknown points, and prohibiting expressions that could be interpreted as solicitation.
Customer personal information must be anonymized; full names, addresses, contact details, dates of birth, workplaces, and various numbers should not be recorded. Specified replacement rules (e.g., "Customer (Individual)", "Spouse") must be used. However, the names of our company's responsible staff must be kept real.
The output format must follow a five-heading structure: "1. Meeting Overview," "2. Meeting Purpose/Background," "3. Main Topics/Explanation Content," "4. Decisions/Shared Items," and "5. Future Actions/Issues," and must be output in this exact order.

name: PevocoCapital client meeting
author: Velum
description: Paste the transcript and receive a factual client report. Marks agreements, gaps, and points to be verified.
body:
The document contains working rules and a 19-part structure for converting a client meeting transcript into a factual and compliance-aware internal report for PevocoCapital.
Processing must use only verified information from the conversation, with an explicit distinction between existing situations, client wishes, concrete agreements, and merely discussed possibilities.
Identification and context include meeting details, persons present, reason, and the key context of the meeting.
The personal, family, and professional situation structures family composition, marital status, professional activity, income, and any corporate structures.
The wealth and real estate situation categorizes liquid assets, investments, debts, and specific immovable property, with amounts and values recorded only if explicitly stated.
Existing investments and the pension situation inventory current financial contracts, cost structures, accrued reserves, and concrete income objectives after retirement.
Succession, wealth transfer, and client objectives record existing arrangements such as wills and gifts, as well as formulated short-, medium-, and long-term goals.
Risk preferences and discussed solutions document the investment horizon, risk profile, and explored avenues, while discussed options are not automatically qualified as definitive advice given.
Important client statements are paraphrased to capture the essence of return expectations, liquidity needs, objections, and reasons for decisions.
Missing information, documents to request, and action items specify the required data and concrete next steps for both the client and PevocoCapital, including planning a next appointment.
File warnings flag essential missing data, contradictions, unrealistic expectations, and compliance risks without drawing premature legal conclusions.
The management summary closes the file with a maximum of 10 key points that give the adviser immediate insight into the client situation, primary goals, current attention points, and next actions.

name: CFO Financial Advisory Board
author: Velum
description: Provide meeting minutes or a financial report to receive an executive summary, decision proposals, and executive actions. It includes analysis of liquidity, costs, investments, risks, and scenarios. It also summarizes key KPIs and three impactful priorities.
body:
The main goal of the prompt is to create a "virtual financial advisory board" composed of prominent financial experts to assist the CFO of Tararis company in making precise and value-creating decisions.
The members of this virtual advisory board include notable figures such as Ruth Porat, Amy Hood, Luca Maestri, Brian Olsavsky, Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger, and Howard Marks.
The board's mission is to analyze financial information after each meeting, provide the independent opinion of each member, and reach a common conclusion along with actionable recommendations.
The expected output from the board includes 13 key sections such as an executive summary, proposed decisions, member analysis, liquidity management, cost control, investment, risk management, scenario analysis, and key financial indicators (KPIs).
The key financial indicators (KPIs) used for evaluation include metrics such as EBITDA, net profit, profit margin, operating cash flow, return on invested capital (ROIC), and liquidity and debt ratios.
The governing principles of the board are based on truthfulness, data-driven decision-making, capital protection, liquidity priority, identification of hidden risks, a long-term perspective, and challenging assumptions.

name: Insurance | Face-to-Face | Solicitation History
author: Velum
description: Organize recordings of face-to-face business meetings based on facts. Output customer intent, explanation content, and conclusions for internal records. Personal information is redacted.
body:
Define procedures to summarize the recorded content of face-to-face solicitation (meeting) according to internal rules for recording in our system (hokan).
The purpose of the summary is to record solicitation/discussion content in a form that withstands audits, prioritizing organization of customer intent, explanations, and decisions.
As summary rules, record only facts from the recording; exclude emotional expressions and small talk; use industry terminology; write objectively and concisely. For unclear points, write “Unknown” or “Unintelligible,” and prioritize the latest statement.
To protect personal information, anonymize customer-identifying information such as names, addresses, contact details, dates of birth, workplaces, and various numbers, and follow specified replacement rules (e.g., Customer → “Customer (individual)”). However, record our company’s staff names as is.
From the perspective of audit/solicitation management, prioritize extracting words related to “Solicitation Activities,” “Explanation of Important Matters,” “Understanding Customer Intent,” “Decision/Consent,” and “Procedure Progress,” and describe so it is clear “who explained what and how, and how it was judged.”
The output format follows five headings: “1. Overview of the Meeting,” “2. Customer Information,” “3. Customer Intent/Confirmation Items,” “4. Specific Content Explained/Proposed Face-to-Face,” and “5. Customer Reaction/Understanding Status.”
Customer understanding and consent must be explicitly indicated as one of “Yes,” “No,” or “Pending,” and blanks are not allowed.

name: Mortgage Factfinding Call
author: Velum
description: For brokers. It organizes call notes into fact-find reports, client emails, and reminders.
body:
The primary purpose is for a UK mortgage broker to conduct an initial consultation call, capturing key fact-finding information in a structured format for internal alignment and client communication.
A comprehensive client call summary must be produced, detailing client identity, contact information, referral source, and client type, such as First-Time Buyer (FTB) or Buy-to-Let landlord.
The summary needs to capture specifics about the mortgage, including its type, the property, deposit amount, requested mortgage amount, and available equity, along with term preferences and their respective pros and cons.
Client background information required includes their insurance experience, any vulnerabilities, occupation, income, credit history, assets, lifestyle, debts, and number of children.
The summary must document the main discussion topics, future plans in the client's own words, their goals and preferences regarding mortgage structure and rates, and an assessment of communication and rapport.
A mortgage readiness score from 1 to 5 with reasoning, a list of pending documents and adviser actions with deadlines, agreed-upon actions, and the next meeting date must be included.
Internal notes should cover urgency, strategic considerations, and client mood, complemented by an action plan listing tasks, responsible parties, and due dates.
An insurance review is necessary, covering current policies, coverage gaps, focus areas, client interest, and readiness on a 1-5 scale.
A detailed, friendly, and professional email must be generated for the client, recapping their personal situation, mortgage needs, insurance status, required documents, and next steps in a natural, narrative style.
A separate, friendly reminder message should be drafted to prompt clients who are delayed in submitting their application or required documents.
The style for summaries should be clear and structured, while client-facing communication should be warm, supportive, and reassuring, with different tones for internal teams and the client.

name: Financial Review Meeting Summary
author: Velum
description: Turn notes into a clear summary. Extract stated facts, concerns, tasks, plus a follow-up email.
body:
The primary role of a Registered Investment Advisory meeting assistant is to support a CFP® professional by accurately summarizing client meetings, extracting key data points, and organizing outputs for client follow-up, internal execution, and compliance.
A concise executive summary should be created to capture the meeting's purpose, key topics, decisions, next steps, and the client's overall tone, while excluding recommendations or tasks.
The assistant must identify and summarize personal context shared by the client, such as family updates, career changes, health, and expressed values, using neutral, short bullet points.
All explicit financial facts mentioned by the client, including account details, income, investments, and tax considerations, must be extracted and listed without making estimations or assumptions.
Client-expressed friction points, such as confusion, risk aversion, time constraints, or resistance to action, should be identified and phrased neutrally.
The assistant should observe and identify potential planning opportunities like planning gaps, coordination needs, or inefficiencies, framing them as observations rather than recommendations.
A recommendations section for internal compliance files must be drafted, stating each recommendation, its alignment with client goals, and any mentioned trade-offs, using professional, objective language.
Clear, specific, and actionable tasks for the client must be listed, along with 3 to 5 questions to fill information gaps or clarify strategy.
Internal tasks should be delegated by listing those requiring Lead Advisor review, tasks suitable for a Junior Planner, and operational follow-ups like scheduling and paperwork.
A professional, warm, and clear follow-up email summarizing the meeting, key next steps, and what to expect next should be drafted for the client.
Agenda items and focus areas for the next meeting should be suggested based on open questions, incomplete data, and identified planning opportunities

name: Advanced Analyst Visit Report
author: Velum
description: From the file, compile an impersonal visit report. What is missing remains blank.
body:
The objective is to generate an impersonal visit report for an Advanced Analyst, detailing company information, with instructions to leave blank fields where information is not available and to present data clearly and objectively.
The report should explain in detail the company's main activity, its origin, including the founder, founding date, and the business opportunity that initiated operations.
It is necessary to detail the professional experience, education, and type of relationship between the partners, in addition to specifying whether the company's management is professional or family-run.
The company's structure must be described, including whether the headquarters are owned or leased, their size, location, and whether the vehicle fleet is owned or outsourced.
The document must record the total number of employees, identify the main clients and suppliers, and check if there is a concentration of sales in any specific client or segment.
It is necessary to list the main competitors and the average payment terms, in days, for suppliers and receipts from clients.
The operating cycle needs to be explained, detailing the time between purchasing goods and receiving payment for the sale.
The forms and percentages of receipt must be specified (card, bank collection, credit to account, Pix, cash), and the bank where transactions and cash are concentrated must be identified.
The report should indicate whether there is seasonality in revenue, explaining the periods and reasons, and whether informal revenue exists.
The revenue outlook for 2026 and planned investments for the year (machinery, branches, vehicles, etc.) with their dates must be reported.
It is necessary to include company specificities such as operating margin, inventory, and tax regime.
Business opportunities in credit lines discussed at the meeting must be detailed, specifying modality, amount, collateral, and purpose.
The company's tax liability needs to be explained in detail, including how management is handling the resolution, with estimated timelines and values.

name: annual review
author: Velum
description: Organize client housing goals and financial changes to streamline annual mortgage review summaries.
body:
The annual mortgage review client summary checklist is to be completed during or after each annual review conversation to gauge the full health of a client's financial picture, not just their mortgage.
Client Information section requires capturing names, email, and phone number.
Topics of Interest section prompts for client discussion points such as rates, refinance, or future planning.
Real Estate & Housing Goals section assesses the client's 5-year housing goal (stay put, move/upgrade, downsize, buy 2nd home/rental, or other) and their anticipated length of stay in their current home.
Financial & Life Changes (1–2 Year Outlook) section inquires about any major financial changes like tuition, home improvements, large purchases, or expected changes in employment/income.
Current Mortgage Overview section checks for a second mortgage or HELOC, desired mortgage changes (lower rate, shorter term, cash-out, or other), and overall mortgage satisfaction.
Financial Planning Snapshot section verifies if the client has a Will & Trust, a Transfer on Death Deed, and if they are debt-free excluding their mortgage.
Financial Priorities section asks clients to rate their priorities from 1-5, including paying off debt, building net worth via real estate, paying off the mortgage by retirement, stock market investing, and saving for college.
Partner Ratings section allows for rating of professionals such as Insurance Agent, Financial Planner, CPA, and Realtor on a scale of 1-5 or N/A.
Communication & Marketing section confirms if the client receives the Homebot Digest and E-newsletter.
Referrals & Networking section asks if any referrals were provided and to list the names if applicable.
Follow-Up Items section outlines what the client is owed, including refinance analysis, referrals to various professionals (CPA, Financial Planner, Insurance Agent, Estate Planning Attorney, Realtor, Contractor or Vendor), additional resources, and other next steps.

name: summary meetingp
author: Velum
description: Paste notes or docs; get key business facts and names organized for credit analysis.
body:
Core objective is to capture business facts, names, and information required for credit analysis in a Financial context.
Key identification elements include company legal name, trade name, registration number, incorporation date, domicile, and ownership structure.
Management details include directors, key executives, ultimate beneficial owners, and contact information.
Operational profile includes industry classification, products/services, geographic footprint, subsidiaries, and major counterparties.
Financial data requirements include historical financial statements, cash flow details, liquidity metrics, leverage metrics, profitability ratios, and auditor information.
Banking relationships include primary banks, account details, credit lines, covenants, and collateral arrangements.
Credit history elements include existing debt, repayment performance, defaults, restructurings, and external credit ratings.
Legal and compliance checks include litigation, liens, bankruptcies, regulatory licenses, sanctions screening, and KYC/AML documentation.
Market and risk factors include competitive position, customer concentration, supplier concentration, macro exposure, and contingency plans.
Projections and assumptions include management forecasts, capex plans, working capital needs, and sensitivity analyses.
Purpose of credit and terms include facility type, amount, tenor, pricing, collateral, guarantees, and covenants.
Security package details include assets pledged, valuation reports, perfection status, and priority ranking.
Insurance coverage includes policies, insured assets, limits, deductibles, and insurer credit quality.
Environmental, social, and governance considerations include ESG risks, policies, certifications, and incident history.
Documentation checklist includes corporate documents, financial statements, tax filings, bank references, legal opinions, and board approvals.
Data validation steps include source verification, reconciliations, cross-checks with public records, and audit trail maintenance.

name: 101 VC PE Investor Model (Startup / M&A)
author: Velum
description: Convert meetings into clear minutes. Capture decisions, risks, and actions with owners and dates.
body:
This document provides a template for creating concise, decision-useful meeting minutes for Venture Capital and Private Equity firms, covering startup pitches, M&A discussions, and internal meetings.
The outline requires a professional, objective tone, focusing on facts and decisions, and using a specific title format (# YYYY-MM-DD | Company / Counterparty | Meeting Type — Concise Subject) and a short list of meeting details.
Critical layout rules emphasize readability, concise bullet points, and restrict the use of tables to a single, optional, three-column table for key metrics (| Metric | Value | Note |), prohibiting empty sections or placeholder text.
The required output structure starts with a five-bullet Executive Summary covering the decision, core investment case, key risk, a financial headline, and the next step.
A section for "Decisions and Key Agreements" should only be included if decisions were made, using specific labels like Decision:, Agreed:, or Condition:.
An "Action Items" section is included only for concrete actions, formatted as - [Owner] Action / deliverable — Deadline: YYYY-MM-DD, sorted by deadline.
The optional "Key Metrics & Deal Snapshot" section should only be used if specific figures were discussed, presenting them in the single allowed table format with relevant metrics for startups or M&A.
The "Detailed Discussion" section should be organized using concise headings chosen from a predefined list (e.g., Vision & Problem, Product & Technology, Deal Terms) and should use short bullet points with optional labels like Fact:, Risk:, or Pro:/Con:.
A "Key Risks and Open Questions" section is included only if material risks or unresolved items were raised, organized by subheadings like Commercial, Financial, or Legal.
A final quality check ensures the document is concise, correctly formatted, free of empty sections, uses no more than one table, properly labels calculated values, and omits any mention of AI generation.

name: SPORTS BETTING RECORD AND ANALYSIS TEMPLATE
author: Velum
description: Record a bet and its analysis. Indicate data, odds, stake, risks, and bankroll. Get metrics and a summary with lessons and improvements.
body:
This template aims to systematically record, analyze, and evaluate sports bets to improve decision-making and long-term profitability.
The first section, Bet Summary, gathers basic information to identify the event, including date, sport, competition, event, bookmaker, and start time.
In Bet Details, the specifics of the operation are detailed, such as bet type, selection, odds, stake, amount, own estimated probability, Expected Value (EV), and the main reason for the decision.
The Pre-analysis is divided into Favorable data, which considers factors like recent form, statistics, head-to-head record, and external factors, and Identified risks, which lists potential setbacks.
Bankroll management focuses on controlling capital, recording the current bankroll, the percentage risked in the bet, and the associated confidence level.
The Result section documents the outcome of the bet, specifying if it was won, lost, or void, the profit or loss obtained, and the new bankroll balance.
Decision evaluation analyzes the quality of the betting process regardless of the outcome, detailing confirmed and unfulfilled arguments, missing information, and detected errors (statistical, emotional, management, or information).
The Learnings section extracts lessons from the experience to refine future strategies, indicating what actions to repeat, what to avoid, and what adjustments to make.
Performance tracking is done through key Metrics such as ROI, Yield, Win Rate, accumulated profit, and the identification of best and worst markets.
The Executive summary concludes the template with a brief summary of bet quality, risk management, the main lesson, and a recommendation for future similar operations, also suggesting an instruction for AI-assisted analysis.

name: Teachers Fact Finder
author: Velum
description: Fill a teacher fact finder from a chat: personal info, accounts, insurance, goals. Summary table.
body:
The primary purpose is to provide a structured financial fact-finding framework tailored for educators to systematically record personal, employment, and comprehensive portfolio data.
