It is required to provide a concrete and chronological action plan of 4 to 6 priority steps, including pros and cons, as well as a list of 3 to 5 potential risks with alternatives.
The final output format must be a structured Markdown document, containing sections dedicated to transcription, summary of exchanges, analysis by theme, action plan, risks and alternatives, and legal references.

name: SOP - Purpose Planning
author: Velum
description: For financial planning teams. Add a meeting transcript to get a structured SOP for notes or Excel.
body:
This document provides a highly structured master template for creating a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), optimized for AI transcript extraction and integration with systems like Velum, GoHighLevel, and Excel.
The SOP Information section captures essential metadata, including the SOP name, department, system used, creator, creation/update dates, version, and the purpose of the process.
The Pipeline Overview section outlines the entire process flow by listing the names of up to five sequential stages.
Pipeline Stage Details provides a granular breakdown for each stage, requiring specification of the objective, responsible person, and trigger. This section further details individual tasks with responsible parties and timeframes, a step-by-step process guide, systems used, required documents, automation actions, a completion checklist, and the next pipeline stage.
The template structure is designed to be repeated for each stage in the pipeline to ensure consistent and thorough documentation.
The Internal Process Notes section is for capturing common issues, staff tips, compliance considerations, and suggestions for future improvements to the procedure.
An Approvals section is included to record who approved the SOP, the date of approval, and the next scheduled review date.
A specific ChatGPT prompt is provided to guide the automatic creation of a structured SOP from a meeting transcript, formatted for transfer into Velum Notes and Excel using simple Australian English.

name: Family Law – Financial Expert Initial Meeting Valuation Engagement
author: Velum
description: Transcript in, report out: roles, method, costs, dates. With to-dos.
body:
The core purpose is to create a structured report for an initial meeting of a financial expert in the field of business valuation in family law, based on a conversation transcript.
The report should identify the participants and their roles, including the parties, lawyers, the expert, and who mandated whom.
The initial situation must be documented, including the reason for the valuation (e.g., divorce), the company concerned, its legal form, ownership structure, and relevant contracts.
The discussed or contractually stipulated valuation method, such as the ABV formula or the earnings value method, should be recorded.
It is required to capture and evaluate the substantive contributions, facts, and documents provided by each participant, and assess who actively shaped the conversation.
The emotional state and expressed concerns or fears of the clients, as well as the relationship dynamics between the parties, should be captured.
The procedure explained by the expert, required documents, planned meetings, and digital collaboration are to be documented.
Each party's expectations for the valuation report, such as understandability and defensibility in court, must be recorded.
Costs and conditions, including hourly rate, cost estimate, allocation, and invoicing, are to be documented.
The timeline with milestones and presentation date must be recorded.
Concrete next steps with responsibilities and deadlines must be listed as action items.
Surprising insights and strategic advice for the financial expert, including risks and opportunities for the engagement, should be identified and marked as assessments.

name: candidate call/meeting
author: Velum
description: Organizes meeting recordings into detailed notes on roles, pay, performance, and motivations.
body:
The primary purpose of this template is to convert a recording of a candidate meeting into detailed notes for internal use within a Commodities Trading Headhunting business.
The template specifies that notes should be in bullet point form, using a non-exhaustive list of categories as headers to structure the information.
The "Role" section requires highly detailed and technical notes on the candidate's responsibilities, including what they do and how they do it.
The "Team" section should list colleagues the candidate mentioned, their specific roles (product, region, style), and the candidate's assessment of them.
The "Comp" section must capture all relevant details about the candidate's compensation package, including base salary, bonus structure, and any deferrals.
The "PnL" section is for recording trading performance, including returns, risk metrics like VaR, the ratio of paper to physical trading, and whether trading is proprietary or flow-based.
The "Motivations" section should detail the candidate's job search status, what interests them in new opportunities, important future career factors, location preferences, and any complaints about current or past roles.
The "Referalls & People moves" section is for noting information about other professionals moving between firms and, crucially, identifying other individuals the candidate rates highly in the industry.
An "Other" category is included for any additional relevant information not covered by the specified sections.

name: Client chronical
author: Velum
description: For finance pros. Turns voice or text into records. Extracts key info and syncs follow-up tasks.
body:
ClientChronicle is a voice and text-based note-taking assistant for financial services, designed for structured data capture in lending, property investment, post-settlement care, and referral tracking.
The agent's purpose is to convert client interactions into structured, searchable notes, categorize content into specific workflows, extract and label important data, auto-tag notes, and trigger follow-ups.
ClientChronicle accepts voice or text input, transcribes voice using OpenAI Whisper, identifies and parses financial terminology, and classifies notes into categories like #FactFind, #Refinance, #InvestmentReady, #PostSettlementCare, #EquityOpportunity, #PMReferral, and state tags.
The agent can respond to queries about client discussions, list opportunities, and show clients for follow-up, while also suggesting actions like annual reviews or referrals.
Output formats include Google Sheets with separate tabs for each category, Notion databases with filterable views, and synchronization of follow-up dates with Google Calendar or Task API.
Data structure includes sections for Client Profile, Lending, Investment, Property Assets, Aftercare, and Cross-Sell/Referrals, detailing specific data points for each.
A sample input prompt demonstrates capturing client details, financial information, investment preferences, and service requests, with an expected structured JSON output including client profile, lending, investment, cross-sell data, and relevant tags.

name: Mortgage Broker Client Discovery and Needs Analysis
author: Velum
description: Paste a mortgage call transcript. Get a structured discovery summary, risks and next steps.
body:
The primary objective of this document is to provide a template for a mortgage broker to automatically generate a client discovery and needs analysis from a recorded conversation transcript.
The template requires extracting the client's main goal, such as buying a first home or refinancing, their target timeline, and the key drivers for the deal, like securing the lowest rate or maximizing borrowing capacity.
It outlines capturing a detailed client profile, including full names, employment status, gross and additional income, existing liabilities, and number of dependants for up to two applicants.
A summary of the client's financial position is needed, covering estimated monthly living expenses and available funds or equity from savings and existing properties.
The client's specific requirements must be detailed, including the target purchase price or refinance amount, desired loan structure (e.g., variable, fixed, offset), and preferred loan features.
For compliance with Best Interests Duty (BID), the template requires documenting the client's ranked priorities, the reasoning for loan selection, and any potential risks or trade-offs involved.
A credit and risk assessment section is included to note the client's credit history, identify potential policy hurdles, and list any mitigating factors that strengthen the application.
The final section specifies creating checklists for both client and broker action items to outline the next steps in the mortgage application process.

name: Role-play
author: Velum
description: Evaluates from an expert perspective whether proposals are being made that support the customer. Organizes and communicates strengths and improvement tips.
body:
You are a professional coach with extensive experience in guiding [Sales/Proposal Role-playing], and your role is to objectively and developmentally evaluate the provided role-playing content from a third-person perspective.
The evaluation assumes a client who "dislikes hard selling / has little interest in insurance or money matters" and prioritizes whether the dialogue is empathetic from a life planning perspective, rather than short-term product proposals.
The evaluation criteria consist of eight points: 1 First Impression / Approach, 2 Listening Skills, 3 Affirmation / Empathy Stance, 4 Utilization of PREP method, 5 Presence/Absence of Pushiness, 6 Naturalness of Proposal Content, 7 Creating a flow where the client wants to consult, and 8 Overall comfort of conversation.
The specific evaluation method stipulates that "Good points," "Points for improvement (how to make it better without blame)," "3 key points to keep in mind for the next role-play," and an "Overall evaluation (5-level)" should be presented.
Finally, the full text of the provided role-playing scenario should be pasted into the [Role-play content] section to execute the evaluation process.

name: Financial Meeting
author: Velum
description: Organizes billing by professional. Transforms speech into reports with goals and expenses.
body:
The goal is to transcribe, organize, and generate a complete report of financial meetings at the Integrative Clinic, conducted by Dr. Samara and Dr. Débora, with the team.
The meeting may include Dr. Samara (integrative endocrinologist), Dr. Débora (integrative neurologist), administrative staff, and financial consultants.
Identify who is speaking, associating name or position whenever possible.
Record and organize data such as plans sold (with values and who sold them), procedures performed, payment methods, expected receipts, and pending issues.
Record the breakdown by professional (Samara, Débora, others) and expenses or investments made.
Highlight goals, indicators, or critical observations about performance.
The final report structure should include a meeting summary (date, participants, type), total billing (gross, received, forecast), distribution by professional, and sales by employee.
Include mentioned expenses, pending issues, and observations (clients with pending entry, installments to be received, plans to be renewed, suggestions or criticisms).
Record goals and proposed actions, such as the start of a campaign or billing target for the next month.
Generate an executive summary with the overall total for the period, doctor with the highest sales volume, employee with the best performance, and points of attention.
Ignore casual or off-topic remarks unless they bring a relevant suggestion or insight.
Record values accurately and highlight them whenever mentioned.

name: Bprrower PreApproval
author: Velum
description: Helps loan officers create structured summaries of credit, income, and next steps for loan files.
body:
The primary purpose is to generate a professional Pre-Approval Overview for a mortgage loan file, acting as a senior mortgage underwriter presenting the summary to a Loan Officer or Processor for documentation.
The Borrower Profile section requires the borrower's full name, credit scores, application type, employment type, and the monthly income used for qualification.
The Loan Details section must specify the loan's purpose, type, occupancy, purchase price or value, loan amount, LTV/CLTV, and the estimated rate, term, and P&I payment.
The Property Details section should include the subject property's full address and type, along with any known notes regarding appraisal, title, or HOA.
The Credit Analysis section involves reviewing the middle credit score, total debts, DTI ratio, any payment issues, and commenting on the overall credit health, including tradeline depth and mix.
The Income & Assets Review section requires detailing the income sources and stability based on reviewed documents, the assets for down payment and reserves, and any use of business funds.
The Underwriting Notes section should contain AUS findings, compensating factors for approval, and any potential red flags or conditions that need to be cleared.
The Action Items / Next Steps section must list specific outstanding items, state the file's readiness for the next stage, and provide a clear recommendation to proceed, hold, or declare ineligibility.

name: Report for Mortgage Application PB1
author: Velum
description: Supports the collection of financial and real estate data for mortgages, defining objectives and documents.
body:
The purpose of the document is to structure a report for a mortgage application, gathering all necessary information about the client, the property, and financial details.
The first section collects the client's contact details, including name, phone, and email.
The second section defines the characteristics of the requested mortgage, specifying the type (purchase, construction, refinancing, liquidity), interest rate type, and duration.
The third section, if applicable, collects information about the property subject to the mortgage, such as address, purchase price, type, energy class, and estimated timeline.
The fourth section lists the applicant's key personal and financial details, such as occupation, income, family dependents, credit profile, assets, and available funds for the down payment.
The fifth section is dedicated to inserting personal notes related to the practice.
The sixth section documents the client's specific preferences and objectives regarding the loan structure and other unique considerations.
The seventh section lists promised or pending items, particularly documents the client still needs to provide.
The eighth section is a space for notes in case the client has not yet formally submitted the application.
The ninth section defines a list of activities to be completed, divided between those to be handled by the client and those by the team.

name: Tech Transfer Commercialization Eval
author: Velum
description: Assess tech readiness and funding fit. Analyzes market potential and risks to guide research to market.
body:
This document outlines a framework for evaluating early-stage university technologies for commercialization readiness, assessing their fit for specific funding programs like TCF and MII, and providing guidance on de-risking and next steps.
The evaluation process assesses technologies for their fit with three specific funding programs—TCF for proof-of-concept, MII Phase 1 for validation, and MII Phase 2 for company formation—from the dual perspective of a critical reviewer and a practical mentor.
A five-step evaluation framework is used to analyze the technology's overview and TRL, define its use cases and markets, assess its tech-to-market translation, identify key risks, and determine its fit for funding, with the process halting if the initial TCF threshold is not met.
For eligible technologies, a de-risking plan must be proposed with feasible objectives, activities, and deliverables within budget and time constraints, addressing technical, market, IP, and business risks.
The evaluation output must be structured into four parts: a concise, evidence-driven reviewer summary; constructive, action-oriented advisor guidance; a fund fit summary table; and a timeline of next steps.
The evaluation must adhere to core principles that prioritize honesty, evidence, clarity, and realism, with a market-first approach to defining value as a function of the problem, customer pain, and proof.

name: Real Estate Sales Plan Generator
author: Velum
description: Analyze customer desires and concerns based on viewing recordings. Visualize sales quality and support the improvement of future proposals and actions.
body:
The purpose of the viewing is to support customers in making property decisions with confidence.
Sales representatives are evaluated not just as property guides, but as consultants who propose lifestyles to customers.
The analysis focuses not on confirming customer information, but on whether support was provided to demonstrate lifestyle possibilities.
1. Viewing Summary and Consulting Evaluation
Summarize the overall atmosphere of the viewing, customer satisfaction, the moments when the customer's emotions were most stirred, and the final likelihood of closing.
Evaluate, based on specific actions, how well the representative stimulated the customer's latent desires and functioned as a trusted companion.
Analyze, based on data, the customer-centric listening attitude, the quality of questions exploring values and latent needs, and the use of keywords that evoke emotions.
2. Phase-by-Phase Dialogue Analysis (Based on the 5-Phase Model)
Divide the flow of the viewing into five phases and analyze/summarize the consultant's practical actions.
■ Phase 1: Preparation and Relationship Building
Evaluate the establishment of trust through ice-breaking and the agreement on the purpose and process of the viewing.
■ Phase 2: Needs Discovery (Listening to Setting Issues)
Identify, with concrete examples, the customer's verbalized requests and the underlying stories, as well as deep-dive questions that draw out essential desires and values that even the customer may not be aware of.
Clarify the true issues that the customer needs to solve through moving, as identified through dialogue.
■ Phase 3: Proposal and Value Appeal (Future Storytelling)
Describe specifically how a "rich future lifestyle" was depicted at the property location and imagined by the customer.
Evaluate the methods used to explain the property's features by linking them to the customer's desires (experiential value).
Identify the proposals that elicited the strongest positive reactions and emotional responses from the customer.
■ Phase 4: Consensus Building (Turning Objections into Trust)
Identify the main concerns expressed by the customer and the fundamental anxieties underlying them.
Describe the methods of empathy, information provision, and reassurance, as well as specific dialogue examples that turned objections into trust.
■ Phase 5: Follow-up and Expectation Building
Summarize the wrap-up of the viewing and the alignment of expectations for the next steps in the process.
3. Next Actions and Points for Improvement
Organize agreed items and tasks for the representative, customer, and next contact schedule.
Present coaching points focusing on the strengths (Good) and areas for improvement (More) from this dialogue, especially regarding the depth of exploration and specificity of future depiction.

name: Bali Gaya - Land Discovery Facts Sheet
author: Velum
description: For real estate sales. Examples of questions to delve deeper into the background and ideals behind customer requests. Supports optimal proposals that capture latent needs.
body:
Real estate salespeople learn phrasing to draw out not only the customer's apparent wants but also their latent and deeper needs (ideal lifestyle), which even the customer may not be aware of.
To elicit the customer's "true feelings," avoid directly asking "Why?" and instead use polite questions that help the customer organize their thoughts and speak comfortably.
For example, rephrase "What is the main reason you thought that way?" to "What is the main reason you are looking in this area this time?" or "If you don't mind sharing, could you tell me why you are particular about a detached house among the many options?"
Also, change "Could you tell me a bit more about the background that led to that decision?" to "If you don't mind, could you tell me more about what prompted you to start considering moving this time?" and "What results do you expect to achieve by making this happen?" to "By realizing this home, how do you expect your family's life to change?" or "What kind of lifestyle do you want to lead in your new home?"
To explore the "ideal lifestyle" with future-oriented questions, have the customer freely imagine their ideal future by temporarily forgetting about budget and constraints, thus drawing out the values they truly cherish.
Examples of future-oriented questions include rephrasing "If you had a magic wand and could change anything, what would you change?" to "If there were no budget or location constraints, what kind of home would you like to live in?" or "If you could get your ideal home, how would you like to spend your days off?", "When do you think you would feel, 'I've got the best house'?", or "A year after moving into this home, what kind of smiles do you envision your family having?"
Using the SPIN® method, clarify the current problems (Problem), have the customer consider the implications (Implication), and imagine the value when solved (Need-Payoff), thereby strengthening the motivation for house hunting.
For problem questions (P), ask about issues or dissatisfactions with the current home, such as "Are there any aspects of your current home where you feel, 'I wish it were more like this'?", "Do you feel cramped as your children grow?", or "Do you find daily commuting time or many slopes burdensome?"
For implication questions (I), ask about the impact of problems on the future, such as "How do you feel the lack of sunlight affects your family's mood or health?", "Are you concerned about securing private space for your children as they grow?", or "How do you think continuing to pay the current rent will affect your asset formation in 10 or 20 years?"
For need-payoff questions (N), ask about the value a new home would bring, such as "If you had this property five minutes from the station, how would your daily life change?", "How would a spacious living room enrich your family's time together?", or "How important is it for your family to have a room for each child?"
As a practical phrase collection, provide questions to understand the customer's past house-hunting experiences and lessons (e.g., "What was the one non-negotiable point in the properties you've seen so far?"), clarify current issues (e.g., "Which part of your current home's layout do you find most inconvenient?"), explore ideal lifestyles and desired outcomes (e.g., "If all your current concerns were resolved in this home, how would your family's time become richer?"), and understand the values that guide decision-making (e.g., "What is the most important value in your current house search?").
As a "cheat sheet" for deepening dialogue, introduce techniques such as exploring root causes (e.g., "What experiences have led you to think that way?"), understanding motivations (e.g., "How does realizing that preference connect to your ideal lifestyle?"), exploring impacts (e.g., "If that point is not met, what other inconveniences might arise?"), and concretizing abstract expressions (e.g., "For you, what does a 'convenient location' mean? For example, what kind of shops would you like to have nearby?").
To use these questions effectively, it is essential to first listen empathetically and build trust so that the customer feels safe to share their true feelings.

name: Appraisal: Sales meeting with the seller
author: Velum
description: Organizes interview records including small talk and repair history. Assists in creating professional documents that reflect property overviews and the seller's thoughts.
body:
This template aims to organize the contents of an interview with the seller and comprehensively record the sales story, property information, repair history, seller's emotions, expenses, brokerage agreement, and sales strategy to create a practical document.
As basic information about the seller, we record their name, age, family composition, occupation, and the atmosphere, personality, and way of speaking perceived from casual conversation.
We record the contents of casual conversation during the interview and understand the seller's "emotional background" from the reason for consultation, their life so far, likes and dislikes, recent events, family and neighborhood stories, anxieties and hopes for the future, and changes in their tone of voice.
We clarify the reason for selling, urgency, whether other companies have been consulted, and the seller's biggest concerns and wishes.
As basic information about the property for sale, we organize the location, lot number, land category, land area, road access, zoning district, building coverage ratio/floor area ratio, infrastructure status, and presence of boundaries.
If there is a building, we summarize information about the year built, structure, total floor area, layout, presence of extensions, and concerns about illegality.
To understand the property's maintenance status, we check the repair history such as exterior wall painting, roof repair, water area replacement, termite inspection/termite control work, and water heater replacement.
We confirm the amount of remaining items, the desire for demolition, the need for a demolition estimate, and whether bare land delivery is desired.
To assist with appraisal and advertising copy creation, we interview about stories related to the property, family memories, past troubles, rights relations, and relationships with neighbors.
We record the seller's emotions such as anxiety, sadness, relief, anger, and expectation, and the reasons for their changes, to understand their feelings.
For various expenses such as brokerage fees, registration fees, surveying fees, demolition costs, and capital gains tax, we record the explained content and the seller's understanding and reaction.
We describe the type of brokerage agreement (exclusive, non-exclusive, general), the reason for selection, the seller's satisfaction, the contract period, and the explained advertising methods.
We interview about the seller's desired sales price and its basis, the anticipated final line, and whether time or price is prioritized.
As additional information required for appraisal, we confirm the availability of property documents such as drawings and contracts, items to dispose of, items not to dispose of, key status, and the current condition of the room.
We clarify future tasks and agreements, such as the next visit date, documents to be prepared by our company, and documents to be prepared by the seller.
As the final deliverable, we request that the "Seller Interview Record," "Property Overview," "Sales Story," "Seller's Emotional Organization," and "Draft Sales Strategy" be compiled into a single document.

name: ACS - Funding Department Intake Form
author: Velum
description: Generates a complete extended resolution protocol for homeowners' association meetings from a meeting transcript. Suitable for administrators and minute-takers; the input is the transcript, the output is a clearly structured protocol with agenda items (TOPs), motions, votes, and findings. Missing information is marked as "[please complete]" and discussions are factually condensed.
body:
The core task is to create a legally sound, extended resolution protocol of a homeowners' association meeting based on a transcript, strictly adhering to the legal requirements of § 24 para. 6 WEG and relevant case law.
The protocol must be written in an objective, precise, and legally impeccable language to withstand annulment actions, and must not contain invented content, opinions, or detailed discussion flows.
The extended resolution protocol must follow a specific structure, including a header, findings at the beginning of the meeting, detailed documentation of each agenda item including reports, resolution motions, voting results and announcement, legally relevant statements, the end of the meeting, signatures, and an annex list.
For each agenda item, the subject, any reports, the exact wording of the resolution motion, an optional explanation, the precise voting result (Yes, No, Abstentions), and the verbatim announcement of the adoption or rejection of the resolution by the meeting chairman must be documented.
Strict quality and legal rules apply, such as the complete recording of rejected motions (negative resolutions), the precise and understandable formulation of resolutions including a cost ceiling and financing source, and the neutral, fact-based summary of reports and discussions.
The minutes must be prepared without delay and signed by the meeting chairman, a homeowner, and – if applicable – the chairman of the advisory board, with missing or unclear information in the transcript to be marked with "[please complete]".

name: DONNA
author: Velum
description: Paste a rehab walkthrough recording. Get a room-by-room task list, buys, trades, budget, and next steps.
body:
Convert a recording into an organized real-estate rehab walkthrough and punch list with concise, easy-to-scan, action-oriented output.
Capture Property & Walkthrough Info including property address if mentioned, date, and people involved.
Identify Priority Items covering anything urgent, unfinished, holding up work, or needing immediate attention.
Produce a Room-by-Room Punch List organized only by areas actually mentioned, using categories such as Exterior, Garage, Entry/Living Room, Kitchen, Bedrooms, Bathrooms, Basement, Laundry/Utility, Deck/Yard/Landscaping, and Other.
List Items to Buy or Order including every material, fixture, light, hardware item, appliance, paint, or product mentioned, and include quantities, measurements, colors, finishes, brands, or styles when stated.
Organize Contractor & Trade Items by trade when possible, including electrician, plumber, HVAC, painter, flooring, carpenter/trim, handyman, landscaping/exterior, or other trade.
Capture Prices & Budget including every price, quote, estimate, budget amount, allowance, or cost mentioned.
List People to Contact including anyone who needs to be called, texted, scheduled, paid, or followed up with and the reason.
Track Orders & Deliveries including items ordered or needing to be ordered, and any delivery dates, pickups, backorders, or deadlines when mentioned.
Document Aaron's Decisions on keeping/replacing items, colors, finishes, materials, fixtures, design choices, budget, or changes to plans, using the latest decision when changed.
Compile Donna's To-Do List including every task assigned to Donna or anything Donna says she will handle.
Maintain a Waiting / Needs Decision list for items waiting on Aaron, a contractor, pricing, measurements, materials, delivery, inspection, or more information, using NEEDS CLARIFICATION only when meaning or final decision is genuinely unclear.
Separate Completed items explicitly stated as finished from work that still needs to be done.
End with Next Steps as a short prioritized action list covering what must happen first, what must be purchased, who must be contacted, what must be scheduled, and what Donna must follow up on.
Enforce constraints to not invent information, not leave out small details, include only rooms/categories/purchases/trades/topics actually mentioned, and avoid adding missing specifications or unnecessary NEEDS CLARIFICATION flags.

name: 🏠Mortgage- Purchase Lead intake call
author: Velum
description: Turn defect notes or photo notes into concise inspection comments. Flags unclear items for follow-up.
body:
The primary role is to act as a licensed Texas home inspector and generate concise, TREC-compliant inspection comments ("rapid remarks") for the official REI 7-6 report form, based on various inputs like defect lists or photo descriptions.
All remarks must be grouped under the correct TREC REI 7-6 section, written as bullet points for deficiencies, and kept concise at a 6th-grade reading level. Informational comments should be bolded, and no TREC section labels should be included in the remark itself.
Comments must be objective, active, and declarative, using TREC-appropriate terminology such as "deficient" instead of "bad." They should avoid speculation, repair pricing, and include recommended actions or causes where applicable, with a specific note for water temperatures outside the 120oF-135oF range.
Specific categorization rules apply: dryer vents go under V.H, fireplaces under I.J, window caulking under I.H, and gutters under I.C.
The AI should be familiar with TREC SOP 535.227–535.233, the REI 7-6 report structure, and relevant home inspection literature, stopping only when all remarks are generated or when input is unclear.
As a persona, the AI must write like an experienced field inspector, focusing on observing and reporting existing conditions without diagnosing root causes, designing repairs, estimating costs, or predicting future performance, maintaining a practical and defensible mindset.
Professional conduct requires writing that is neutral, factual, and avoids alarmist language, sounding like a disciplined Texas inspector documenting field conditions, not a textbook, contractor, or chatbot.
The operational role is to assist during a live inspection by converting short, fragmented, and sometimes incomplete dictation into clean, paste-ready rapid remarks for the TREC REI 7-6 report without extra explanation.
The core objective is to write concise inspection comments reflecting only observable conditions, matching the natural tone of a professional Texas home inspector without narrative or fluff.
When interpreting dictation, the AI must assume it describes a real condition, fill in only obvious context, avoid inventing details, and state if location is unclear or inspection was limited.
The output for each comment must be 1-3 sentences, with no special formatting, conversational tone, code references, or speculation, following a structure of "Observed condition → Brief impact."
If a single dictation contains multiple distinct deficiencies, each must be separated into its own paragraph, addressing only one condition, without combining unrelated defects.
To avoid repetitive impact language, a variety of restrained alternatives should be used to describe potential consequences like moisture intrusion, safety concerns, or reduced function, while keeping the language brief and neutral.
Recommendations for repair by a qualified contractor should only be added when specifically cued, using a rotating list of concise, approved phrases and avoiding stacking multiple recommendations or impact statements.
The AI should use professional judgment to identify conditions needing repair, such as safety hazards or active moisture intrusion, using restrained, approved phrasing without assigning urgency unless there is an immediate, clear hazard.
The tone must remain plain and factual, avoiding words like "severe" or "major," and comments should generally be under 50 words unless specified otherwise.

name: Buyer Client Call
author: Velum
description: Analisa visitas de imóveis para listar objeções e preços. Cria planos de ação e métricas para CRM.
body:
The goal is to act as a third-person service analyst, processing audio or transcripts of real estate interactions in Brazilian Portuguese to generate an executive and actionable record for the agent.
Tasks include transcribing with diarization (who said what), synthesizing the events in the third person, highlighting key points discussed (features, price, location, objections), defining agreed next steps and an action plan, as well as calculating metrics such as speaking time and number of objections handled.
The communication style should be executive clarity, concise, factual, and decision-oriented, using bullet points and timestamps in key sections, and indicating "not mentioned" when information is missing.
The tone should be neutral, welcoming, and observant, avoiding unnecessary jargon, commercial exaggerations, and promises of appreciation.
The target audience is the agent/broker and the sales team, with the document prepared for use in CRM and for client follow-up.
The response must follow a mandatory format, starting with a header containing property/address, date/duration, participants, and channel, followed by an executive summary in 3-5 sentences.
The main points discussed should be detailed in topics such as product/features, price/conditions/financing, location/mobility/services, and questions/objections addressed.
The client's updated preferences, restrictions, and criteria should be listed, as well as pending questions or data that need to be confirmed or obtained.
The next steps agreed with the client should be specified with details about what, responsible party, date/schedule, channel, and success criteria for each step.
An agent action plan, in operational checklist format, should be included with priority, task, responsible party, deadline, and evidence of completion.
Perceived risks and their mitigations, as well as opportunities for properties/solutions aligned with the client's criteria, should be presented.
Key excerpts with evidence, including the quote and timestamp, should be provided, explaining the relevance of each excerpt.
Service metrics, such as speaking time per participant and number of objections handled, should be calculated, along with a note on the property's adherence to the client's criteria, justified in one sentence.
A JSON block containing the extracted information should be provided at the end of the response for CRM integration.
Quality rules require short sentences, action verbs, consistency between summary, points, and next steps, marking divergences, and indicating limitations if the audio is incomplete.

name: Visit Properties Asunción
author: Velum
description: Record site access, utilities, and setbacks to identify project risks and define clear next steps.
body:
This document provides a comprehensive template for an on-site property parcel check, designed to assess feasibility, identify obstacles, and outline next steps for a potential construction or installation project.
A preliminary "Bottom Line Up Front" (BLUF) summary captures the overall feasibility, major obstacles, and key positive (green flags) and negative (red flags) indicators, along with the auto-filled county name.
The access and delivery path evaluation involves checking road, driveway, and gate widths, driveway slope, and potential obstructions like tight turns, low powerlines, or trees, with next steps including potential gate widening, tree trimming, power line clearance, or driveway reinforcement.
Existing structures on the property are assessed for type, dimensions, and proximity to property lines and the proposed pad, identifying potential setback conflicts or unpermitted structures that may require verification with the County Planning Department or demolition.
The proposed buildable area or pad is evaluated for its footprint, setbacks, and physical conditions like slope, soil stability, and drainage, with potential red flags including instability, poor drainage, or insufficient size, which may necessitate a grading contractor or layout adjustments.
For properties with a well and septic system, their locations and distances to the proposed pad and each other are checked to ensure they meet separation requirements, with potential issues requiring a septic inspector or consultation with County Environmental Health.
The location and distance of utilities like power and gas to the proposed pad are assessed to identify potential hazards or extensive trenching needs, with next steps involving contacting utility providers or calling 811 before digging.
A log of photos for the driveway, pad area, structures, utilities, and any obstacles is maintained to ensure a clear visual record for evaluation, with follow-up actions if visuals are obstructed.
A final on-site summary consolidates the overall feasibility and obstacles, highlighting major issues like setback conflicts or difficult access, and outlines the next steps for county research and customer follow-up.
Customer updates regarding timing, utilities, home options, and financing are tracked to monitor alignment and identify potential delays or scope changes, with corresponding actions for the customer and KMH.
A master summary consolidates all identified green and red flags from the entire assessment into a single, rolled-up overview.
A global action plan outlines the final, sequential next steps required to move the project forward based on the complete on-site check.

name: Universal Real Estate Prompt (Catch-all_V.1.0)
author: Velum
description: For mortgage brokers to organize call notes. Captures goals, finances, and helps plan next steps.
body:
This document provides an AI prompt template for mortgage brokers to generate a structured summary of a client discovery call, covering their real estate and financing needs.
The prompt instructs an AI assistant to use a detailed template to summarize a call transcript, extracting key information, tone, next steps, financial and emotional insights, while flagging red flags and opportunities.
The summary begins by capturing basic client data, including name, call date, referral source, realtor, and the type of inquiry such as purchase, refinance, renewal, or investment.
The template includes a section to document the client's relationship with the referral partner, the tone of the conversation, and personal details shared to establish a connection.
A section is dedicated to identifying the client's primary objective, their motivation for taking action, and their main pain point.
For purchase inquiries, the template gathers information on the client's buyer status, plans for any current property, new property type, ownership structure, down payment source, budget, and timeline.
For refinance inquiries, the template collects the purpose of the refinance, property value, ownership details, existing mortgage balance, and the client's monthly budget.
The client's financial overview is captured by recording their self-rated credit, detailed employment information, other income sources, and tax filing status.
The template provides fields to list other properties or assets owned by the client, including their values, rental income, outstanding balances, and future plans.
A section is included for recording any previous pre-approvals or offers from other lenders, the broker's competitive positioning, and the client's reaction.
The template confirms whether the monthly budget and down payment options have been discussed and assesses the client's comfort level with the total cost.
A dedicated section is used to flag potential issues, note the client's emotional tone and financial literacy, and identify opportunities for additional support.
The summary outlines actionable next steps, including sending application links, securing a submission commitment, booking a strategy call, and noting any promised follow-ups.
A checklist is provided for a follow-up email to the client, ensuring it recaps the discussion, lists next steps, and includes necessary links and invites.
A final section is reserved for the broker's internal notes regarding the call, including additional comments on tone, relationship dynamics, and potential opportunities.

name: RENAH Template
author: Velum
description: Assess property walkthroughs to score sales tactics, rapport building, and negotiation outcomes.
body:
The primary objective is to evaluate how well an Acquisitions Manager (AM) executed a scripted "walkthrough" (WT) with a seller, assessing adherence to the sequence, coverage of all points, and the use of sales tactics.
The introduction phase is evaluated on whether the AM built rapport with the seller on topics beyond the house itself.
The "Establishing the Rules" step requires the AM to outline the appointment structure, clarify the goal is to provide the seller with options, state that they may not buy the house, and get the seller's commitment to providing a "yes" or "no" decision.
During the property walkthrough, the AM is expected to have the seller point out any items of concern regarding the house's condition.
The evaluation checks if the AM discussed the seller's pain and motivation after the walkthrough, using tactics like impact questions, mirroring, labeling, or painting "hell/heaven island" scenarios.
The AM must uncover the timeline and all internal (mortgage, liens, other owners) and external (realtors, other investors) decision-makers, while also strategically addressing the competition.
In the "Priorities & Price" section, the AM should determine what is most important to the seller, manage who gives the first price, and ask for a commitment to sign that day if a price agreement is reached.
The "Underwriting Call," a separate conversation between the AM and an underwriter, is to be reviewed to identify what information the AM failed to gather from the seller.
Before making an offer, the AM must perform an "SVU" (Summarize Validate Understand) to confirm key information, highlight the seller's pain and priorities, and address any missing details.
When presenting the offer, the AM should express vulnerability, ask how the seller feels about the price, justify the offer if necessary by citing condition or timeline, and tie it back to the seller's motivation.
Negotiation is assessed based on the AM's use of specific tactics and whether they successfully withheld leverage points, such as closing flexibility or junk removal, until after the initial offer was presented.
Each of the 10 sections must be rated from 1-5, noting successes and misses, and a final category, "Follow the sequence / control the conversation," requires an overall synopsis of the entire walkthrough.
The evaluation must also determine if the AM did a good job reviewing the contract to ensure the seller understood it.
A final overall score, averaged from the category ratings, must be provided along with identified areas for improvement, such as motivational probing or leverage management.
The reviewer is required to create their own conversational examples of how the AM could have used "hell and heaven island" scenarios to trigger emotions.
A final summary of the call must be produced, including high-level details on the seller's pain/motivation, timeline, decision-makers, property condition, offer information, and the time elapsed between the offer and signing.

name: Real Estate Development Team Quarterly Meeting Recap
author: Velum
description: Add a call transcript. Get a structured borrower summary with goals, gaps, docs, and follow-ups.
body:
The primary role is to assist a Mortgage Loan Officer by extracting, organizing, and summarizing all pertinent borrower and application information from customer consultation calls to create a comprehensive profile for mortgage qualification.
A concise borrower overview should be created, summarizing names, transaction purpose, occupancy, estimated purchase price or loan amount, timeline, financial strength, and any major concerns or opportunities.
Detailed borrower information must be collected for each applicant, including personal and contact details, relocation plans, marital status, personal notes for relationship building, referral source, and whether the application is individual or joint.
Information about the subject property is required, including its location, type, occupancy, price, down payment, closing date, and any associated costs like HOA dues, taxes, and insurance, alongside the borrower's financing goals such as desired payment, rate preferences, and long-term plans.
The borrower's current housing situation must be detailed, including whether they rent or own, their current housing payment, and their intentions for the existing property if they own it, such as selling or converting it to a rental.
A record of all other real estate owned by the borrower is necessary, detailing the property's address, type, value, mortgage details, associated costs, and rental income information for each additional property.
Employment and income details must be gathered for each borrower, including employer information, job history, and a breakdown of all compensation types like salary, bonus, commission, and self-employment or retirement income.
A summary of the borrower's assets and funds for closing is needed, covering bank, investment, and retirement accounts, as well as identifying the source of funds and any potential sourcing or seasoning concerns.
The borrower's credit profile must be assessed, noting their approximate credit score, any known derogatory events like bankruptcies or late payments, current debts, and any other credit-related concerns.
Based on the conversation, potential loan structuring opportunities that could benefit the customer, such as Conventional, FHA, VA, or other specialized loan types, should be identified.
Any red flags or qualification concerns must be identified, such as job changes, declining income, high debt-to-income ratios, low credit scores, or insufficient documentation.
A specific list of documents likely needed from the borrower should be generated based on their unique situation, including items like pay stubs, tax returns, bank statements, and purchase contracts.
A chronological checklist of follow-up tasks for the Loan Officer should be created, including actions like running pricing scenarios, issuing pre-approvals, and communicating with realtors.
A clear list of action items for the borrower needs to be compiled, specifying tasks like uploading documents by a certain date or providing required agreements.
A final section should be created to list all important missing information, unanswered qualifying questions, and areas that require clarification before proceeding with pre-approval or underwriting.

name: Property Discovery Sheet
author: Velum
description: Organize call transcripts into summaries of client needs, property details, and follow-up plans.
body:
This document outlines a structured approach for analyzing real estate voice call recordings to extract key insights for agents.
The objective is to analyze conversations between agents and clients (buyers or sellers) to understand participants, their priorities, and actionable next steps.
The analysis style should be clean, direct, and focused on actionable insights, mimicking an assistant tagging key moments.
The tone should be warm, neutral, and observant, presenting facts and nuances without forcing conclusions.
The intended audience is the agent, who will use the summary to recall the call, plan follow-ups, and personalize service.
The response format requires clear section headers and bullet points, including specific details about the call type, participants, and summary points.
Call Type: To be identified as either a Buyer or Seller call.
Call Details: Includes date, duration, channel (phone/WhatsApp), participants and their roles, and lead source.
5-Line Summary: A concise overview of the conversation's main points.
Motivation and Urgency: Captures the reasons for buying or selling, desired timelines, and any mentioned trigger events.
For BUYER Call: Extracts preferences for location, property type, size, budget, payment methods, must-haves, deal breakers, decision-makers, and perceived obstacles.
For SELLER Call: Gathers property description, occupancy, access details, paperwork status, price expectations, openness to exclusivity, and listing timelines.
Questions, Comments, and Objections by Participant: Lists comments from each person with relevant quotes.
Emotions and Signals: Identifies emotional tone, confidence levels, hesitations, pauses, and other non-verbal cues.
Search Criteria or Strategy Updates: Notes any explicit or implied changes in the client's search criteria or strategy.
Rapport-Building Insights: Captures personal details shared by the client that can be used for future connection.
Next Steps and Commitments: Details agreed-upon actions and deadlines for both parties.
Risks and Flags: Highlights potential issues that could hinder progress and suggests mitigation strategies.
Next Meeting: 3 Touchpoints: Provides three specific, actionable follow-up hooks for future interactions.
Talk Time Ratio: Breaks down the percentage of speaking time for each participant, including the agent, with a note on conversational dominance.

name: Debt-Side Asset Management – Client & Prospect Meetings
author: Velum
description: Create concise OAC minutes for Owners. Capture decisions, actions, key risks, and next steps.
body:
The primary purpose is to create concise, professional Owner-Architect-Contractor (OAC) meeting minutes from the Owner's perspective, serving as a reliable project record and highlighting key information for the Owner.
Meeting minutes should be a non-transcript style summary, avoiding casual conversation, repetitive discussions, and routine updates without project impact, ensuring each item is recorded only once in its most useful section.
Basic meeting information must be recorded, including project name, date, time, location, attendees by name and organization, absent parties, and the next meeting date, without guessing any unknown details.
The Owner Summary should consist of up to six brief bullet points covering only the most important matters, such as major decisions, necessary Owner actions, cost or schedule risks, and significant design or construction issues.
Confirmed decisions and directions must be listed separately, stating what was decided, who approved it, its impact on cost or schedule, and any required follow-up, while clearly labeling the item's status (e.g., Final Decision, Pending Approval).
A structured table should be created for all action items, detailing the task, responsible party, due date, status, and specific impact on the Owner, using predefined labels and capturing all clear commitments.
The budget and change management section should only include material items like change orders, potential costs, and scope gaps, clearly identifying the description, reason, cost status (e.g., Approved Cost, Potential Exposure), and next steps for each.
A concise schedule and construction progress update is required, covering work status, critical milestones, delays, recovery plans, and necessary inputs to maintain momentum, with the overall schedule classified only when supported by discussion.
Design, construction, and coordination issues should be documented only if they require a decision, could impact cost or schedule, or otherwise need Owner attention, stating the issue, status, responsible party, and next action.
A section on project requirements and approvals should be included only when relevant, flagging any issues that could affect contractual, regulatory, or funding commitments, and marking any proposed change that might conflict with them.
A chronological list of confirmed upcoming milestones should be created, including key dates for decisions, deadlines, inspections, and completion, specifying the date, milestone, and responsible party without adding unstated details.
Any remaining material notes should be organized under Detailed Agenda Notes by topic, providing only useful context not already captured elsewhere, such as material updates or reasons for decisions.
Drafting rules mandate clear, direct, neutral language; preserving exact figures; marking uncertainty or unclear information; identifying conflicts rather than choosing a side; and focusing on information critical for the Owner's decision-making and risk management.

name: OSA LISTING APPOINTMENT GRADING
author: Velum
description: Evaluate agent sales. It scores rapport, pricing, and closing to generate CRM training notes.
body:
The primary purpose is to grade an agent's listing appointment performance against OSA appointment standards using a proprietary scorecard model, with the output formatted for Salesforce notes and resembling a trainual training.
Pre-Appointment Preparation (10 pts) involves reviewing lead details, motivation, DISC profile, pre-framing the appointment with a package, and sending an introductory video.
On-Time Arrival & Professionalism (5 pts) requires arriving early, appropriate dress, professional demeanor, respectful tone, confident body language, and displaying branded materials.
Rapport & DISC Matching (10 pts) focuses on identifying the seller's DISC style, adapting communication accordingly, and engaging in light rapport before proceeding.
Setting the Agenda / Controlling the Appointment (5 pts) includes clarifying the meeting's purpose, gaining agreement to proceed with the presentation, and avoiding premature pricing discussions.
USP Mastery (10 pts) requires clearly presenting the Your Home Sold Guaranteed USP, explaining the Guaranteed Sale Program or VIP Seller Benefits, and framing the brokerage as the best option.
Problem Identification (5 pts) involves asking questions to uncover the seller's motivation, challenges, timeline, financial needs, and pain points, using active listening and restating goals.
Marketing Plan Delivery (10 pts) entails presenting the Proprietary Marketing Plan, differentiating from traditional agents, and explaining how the plan attracts buyers and achieves top dollar.
Pricing Strategy (10 pts) requires using a script to frame price around market behavior, educating the seller with market data and CMA, and guiding the seller to choose the price.
Objection Handling (10 pts) involves anticipating and addressing objections using a guide, remaining non-defensive, and overcoming common objections like commission, timing, and other agents.
Closing for the Signature (10 pts) requires using approved closing scripts confidently, directly asking for the signature, and handling hesitations without backing down.
Paperwork Mastery (5 pts) includes properly presenting disclosures and listing paperwork, confidently explaining each section, and smoothly answering questions.
Post-Appointment Follow-up (5 pts) involves setting clear next steps and adding follow-up actions to the CRM or notifying administrative staff.
The total score is out of 100, with a grading scale provided: Mastery (90–100), Proficient (75–89), Needs Development (60–74), and Re-training required (<60).

name: SCB Standard
author: Velum
description: Review buyer meetings. Get scored notes on rapport and closing to improve agent performance.
body:
This document provides a proprietary 100-point scorecard to grade an OSA (Outside Sales Agent) real estate buyer consultation, with the output formatted for use as a Salesforce note and training material.
The Pre-Appointment Setup, worth 5 points, requires the agent to review lead information, send a pre-appointment video, and confirm the meeting details in advance.
The First Impression & Rapport Building category, worth 5 points, assesses the agent's punctuality, professional dress, confidence, and use of DISC awareness to match the buyer's communication style.
Setting the Agenda & Framing the Meeting, worth 10 points, involves explaining the meeting's purpose as a mutual evaluation, gaining permission to lead, and confidently managing the consultation's structure.
The Discovery / Motivation & Needs Assessment, worth 10 points, evaluates the agent's ability to uncover the buyer's motivation, goals, timeline, budget, and emotional drivers.
Introducing the USP / Company Differentiator, worth 10 points, grades the agent on confidently presenting the Buyer Satisfaction Guarantee and positioning YHSGR as the best choice.
Addressing Buyer Fears & Concerns, worth 5 points, requires the agent to ask about and resolve buyer skepticism using guarantees, experience, and a proven process.
Explaining the Homebuying Process, worth 10 points, assesses the agent's ability to educate the buyer on all steps from offer to closing, including the roles of key personnel.
Demonstrating Value, worth 10 points, involves emphasizing the benefits of representation, explaining how to find off-market deals or save money, and sharing success stories.
Presenting & Signing the Buyer Agency Agreement, worth 10 points, grades the agent's confidence in presenting the agreement as a standard step and using official scripts to secure a signature.
Outlining Next Steps Clearly, worth 5 points, involves scheduling follow-up actions, documenting notes in the CRM, and communicating the follow-up cadence.
Objection Handling, worth 10 points, evaluates the agent's use of calm, confident responses from approved scripts to address objections directly and persuasively.
Closing the Appointment, worth 10 points, requires reconfirming motivation, setting the next meeting or task, and ensuring the buyer leaves with clear expectations.
The total performance is scored out of 100, with an optional scale classifying agents from "Excellent" (90–100) to "Not Ready" (Below 60), determining their need for further training.
