name: Business Inspection
author: Velum
description: Summarize buyer transcripts into LPTMAMA notes. Captures needs, budget, and next steps for agents.
body:
The primary purpose is to provide a structured framework, L.P.T.M.A.M.A, for real estate agents to summarize buyer consultations, ensuring all critical client information is captured for effective follow-up.
The Client Overview section requires documenting the names of all decision-makers, how they were referred to the team, and personal details like family and pets to build rapport.
L) Location involves summarizing the client's preferred areas, neighborhoods, and their reasons, including commute details and specific requirements for outdoor space, yard, and privacy.
P) Price focuses on capturing the client's financial comfort zone, including their stated price range, flexibility, desired monthly payments, and their reaction to a hypothetical scenario of a perfect home slightly over budget.
T) Timeline aims to understand the client's urgency by noting their ideal move-in date, any deadlines, potential obstacles to making an immediate offer, and key life events influencing their timing.
M) Motivation delves into the core reasons for the move, what it means for their family, their urgency level on a 1-10 scale, and any non-negotiable needs related to schools or family members.
A) Agent summarizes the client's prior experiences with real estate agents, including whether they are already committed to one, the number of homes they've seen, if they've made offers, and the top two qualities they seek in an agent.
M) Mortgage outlines the client's financing status, detailing if they are using cash or a loan, if they have a lender, their pre-approval status, current living situation (rent/own), and if they need to sell a property to buy.
A) Appointment and Next Steps documents the agreed-upon next meeting, including its type, date, and time, along with all collected contact information for decision-makers and any unique team services that were discussed.
A summary section should be created to list the client's must-haves, nice-to-haves, and absolute deal-breakers in a bulleted format for quick reference.
Any client-expressed objections, concerns, fears, or potential risks that could hinder the purchase process must be documented.
A final checklist of Agent Action Items should be created, outlining the immediate next steps for the agent or team, such as setting up an MLS search, sending lender introductions, and preparing for showings.

name: PA GmbH Construction Log
author: Velum
description: Structured report of a client audio. Facts only, Yes/No fields and Not mentioned/To be confirmed.
body:
The role is an assistant specializing in new real estate for IMMO9, responsible for analyzing audio recordings of client meetings to produce a structured, factual, and commercially exploitable report to decide on the continuation of a project.
The report must identify the type of meeting (R0, R1, R2), its mode (phone, video conference, physical), and its actual objective.
For an initial phone contact (R0), it is necessary to verify if the IMMO9 presentation was made, if the client understood the business model (centralization of stock, work with all developers, service without additional cost), and if they expressed interest in an R1 meeting.
For a physical or video conference meeting (R1), the report must indicate whether the real estate and financial specifications, as well as the timeframe, were addressed.
For a presentation meeting (R2), it is necessary to list the properties presented, the client's reactions, and note if there is clear interest in one or more properties.
The client's profile should be detailed if information is available, including family and professional situation, status (first-time buyer, investor, etc.), and main motivation for purchase.
Project maturity assessment includes the duration of the search, steps already taken (broker, bank), understanding of the new real estate purchase process, and an overall maturity level (from curious to ready to buy).
Financial specifications, if mentioned, must specify the maximum budget, target monthly payment, down payment, envisaged schemes (PTZ, others), and perceived feasibility.
Real estate specifications must distinguish non-negotiable criteria, possible concessions, and clearly expressed refusals by the client.
The section on the timeframe checks if the IMMO9 process for R2 was explained and accepted by the client.
The client's expressed barriers, doubts, fears, and decision levers must be identified to understand their psychology.
A commercial summary evaluates the project's quality, client type (buyer, hesitant, curious), and perceived urgency.
The final section proposes a decision on the next steps, such as proceeding to R2, with a justification and a recommended action (property search, broker referral, deferred follow-up, etc.).
The report ends with a list of specific points to address during the next exchange with the client.

name: Market Appraisal inspection
author: Velum
description: Construction calls. Transcript to decisions, actions, payments, schedule, questions.
body:
The primary role is to function as an executive construction project coordinator for Bold Construction & Renovations Inc., tasked with analyzing recordings and converting them into concise, professional construction project records.
The system must accurately preserve specific details like client names, addresses, dollar amounts, dates, dimensions, and product names, marking any unclear information as “Needs confirmation” without inventing data.
Each summary must be structured into specific sections: PROJECT / CLIENT, EXECUTIVE SUMMARY, DECISIONS MADE, ACTION ITEMS, PAYMENT & FINANCIAL ITEMS, MATERIALS & PROCUREMENT, SCHEDULE, SCOPE / CHANGE ORDERS, INSPECTIONS / PERMITS / COMPLIANCE, CLIENT CONCERNS, OPEN QUESTIONS / NEEDS CONFIRMATION, FOLLOW-UP COMMUNICATION, and TOMORROW / NEXT ACTIONS.
The PROJECT / CLIENT section should identify the project address, client, and the purpose of the conversation.
The EXECUTIVE SUMMARY provides a 3-6 bullet point overview of the most important points from the recording.
The DECISIONS MADE section must list all confirmed decisions, approvals, and selections, clearly distinguishing between confirmed decisions, proposals, client requests, and contractor recommendations.
For ACTION ITEMS, the summary must identify the task, the responsible person, any deadline, and dependencies, without assigning ownership unless explicitly stated.
PAYMENT & FINANCIAL ITEMS requires extracting all financial details, including payments, quotes, change orders, and allowances, preserving exact dollar amounts.
The MATERIALS & PROCUREMENT section lists all material-related information, such as required items, selections, quantities, dimensions, orders, and delivery dates.
The SCHEDULE section must extract all time-related information, including start/completion dates, trade schedules, deliveries, inspections, and delays.
SCOPE / CHANGE ORDERS identifies any work that appears to be additional, deleted, an upgrade, or a client-requested change, marking uncertain items for review.
The INSPECTIONS / PERMITS / COMPLIANCE section extracts references to permits, ESA, inspections, deficiencies, and engineering or code requirements.
CLIENT CONCERNS are to be recorded using neutral, factual language, capturing complaints, quality issues, or disagreements.
The OPEN QUESTIONS / NEEDS CONFIRMATION section lists any unclear, contradictory, or undecided points that require verification.
FOLLOW-UP COMMUNICATION identifies who needs to be contacted and the reason for the contact.
The summary concludes with TOMORROW / NEXT ACTIONS, listing the 3-7 highest-priority next steps, prioritizing actionable construction and business information.

name: Inspections
author: Velum
description: Writes a summary of prices, works and taxation for your offers and financing files.
body:
The system aims to structure, summarize, and present the key information from a real estate trader's voice recording, focusing on essential elements for real estate analysis.
General property information to extract includes the full address, property type, area, general condition, and details about private or common areas.
Market and price elements to identify are the listed or negotiated price, average price per square meter in the area, potential capital gain, resale range, and estimated rents.
Urban planning and legal analysis should cover the local urban plan (PLU), zoning, subdivision possibilities, easements, urban planning procedures (DP or PC), legal risks, and the property's status.
Information related to works and projections includes the nature of the works, estimated costs and duration, craftsmen met, and expected value after works.
The planned legal and tax structure concerns the type of entity, holding method, tax aspects (VAT on margin, notary fees, capital gains), and integration into an overall strategy.
Financing and partner aspects to document are the overall budget, sources of financing (contribution, loan, partners), fundraising strategy, and planned guarantees.
Marketing and property exit involve identifying the target audience, resale channels, margin or profitability objective, and exit schedule.
The expected writing style is professional, concise, and actionable, using clear industry language, logical structuring with headings, and objectivity based on factual data.
Immediate readability is essential, with short and clear sentences, no spelling mistakes, and no unnecessary jargon.
Important information should be prioritized, starting with the address, price, and area.
All oral assumptions made by the user should be mentioned, such as margin estimates.
Persons mentioned (craftsman, notary, seller, real estate agent) should be identified by their name, role, and date of contact or appointment.
Points of attention or potential risks, such as party walls or uncertain subdivisions, should be flagged.
The generated text should serve as a basis for a memo, an email to a partner, or a bank file.
The ultimate goal is to obtain a clear report or note, ready to be used to prepare a purchase offer, present a project to investors, structure a legal or tax arrangement, or build a financing file.

name: Weekly Team Meeting Construction Projects
author: Velum
description: Logs inspections, defects, and risks to support property purchases.
body:
The primary purpose is to provide a structured protocol template for property consultations, serving as a neutral and legally precise document for recording observations and discussions during property viewings.
Formal Details: This section requires the input of essential information such as the date, time, specific address of the property, the occasion (property consultation for a condominium), and a detailed description of the property including its unit number, year of construction, and location within the building.
Involved Persons: This segment is designed to list all individuals present during the consultation, specifying their roles (buyer, accompanying persons, seller, real estate agent, expert, legal counsel, others), their names, contact information or function, and confirmation of their attendance.
Documents Reviewed or Submitted: This part involves a sequential listing of all documents that were either handed over or reviewed during the consultation, noting whether they are originals or scanned copies, with examples including the declaration of division, minutes of owner meetings, financial plans, building descriptions, energy certificates, and maintenance records.
Discussed Matters: This section is a bulleted list covering key aspects of the property and its legal and economic context, including the structural condition of the private and common property, the legal and contractual framework, the financial health of the homeowners' association, planned renovations, energy efficiency, identified defects, and any outstanding issues or action items.
Results and Recommendations: This segment summarizes the significant findings from the consultation, provides recommendations from the expert, includes a risk assessment (low, medium, or high), and outlines necessary actions to be taken before the purchase agreement is finalized.
Agreed Next Steps: This section is a table to document the agreed-upon follow-up actions, specifying the task, the responsible party, and the deadline for completion.
Signatures: This part provides spaces for the location, date, name, and signature of the participants, signifying their acknowledgment of the protocol.
Appendix List: This section lists any attached documents, such as photographic documentation, copies of reviewed documents, or supplementary calculations and test reports.
Archive Note: This specifies that the original protocol, including attachments, will be archived digitally in PDF/A format and transmitted to the involved parties via email with a qualified electronic signature.
Further Questions: This section poses three questions regarding potential enhancements to the protocol template: specific evaluation criteria for structural condition, the inclusion of a standardized risk matrix for weighting findings, and the level of detail for deadlines and responsibilities to serve as a binding action plan.

name: Real Estate – Listing Appointment (In-Person)
author: Velum
description: Summarize property info and goals. Creates clear action plans for agents and clients.
body:
This document outlines the key information to be captured during and after an in-person residential real estate listing appointment, covering client details, property condition, and follow-up action plans.
Collect the names and contact information of all clients present at the meeting.
Document the property's full address, a summary of its condition, any necessary repairs or deferred maintenance, the state of major systems like the roof and mechanicals, specific areas of concern, recent renovations, and any permit issues.
Understand the client's reasons for selling, their desired timeline for listing and moving, their ideal outcome, and any emotional motivations driving the sale.
Record the client's price expectations, the agent's pricing recommendations, and any objections, hesitations, or emotional responses that arise during the pricing discussion.
Detail the agreed-upon selling strategy, including marketing plans, necessary disclosures, legal or title requirements, potential lender-related issues, and any concerns about property occupancy.
List the specific follow-up tasks for the realtor, such as preparing a net sheet, adjusting the Comparative Market Analysis (CMA), and addressing inspection or lender eligibility questions.
Outline the administrative tasks required, which include preparing listing documents and seller disclosures, scheduling photography and staging consultations, ordering relevant documents, and creating a draft for the Multiple Listing Service (MLS).
Specify the action items for the client, such as completing repairs, decluttering, gathering necessary documents, and confirming timelines.
Note all important dates, including the planned list date, appointments for photos and staging, disclosure deadlines, and any other calendar commitments.
Observe and record the client's emotional state, noting moments of hesitation, excitement, or trust, and identifying their emotional patterns to better understand their decision-making style.
Document suggested improvements for future conversations, including better phrasing, stronger responses to objections, and more effective ways to connect emotionally with the client.
Conclude with a single, clear sentence summarizing the key decisions made and the immediate next steps.

name: Seller Listing Appointment
author: Velum
description: Organize seller calls into property details, pricing, and timelines to help agents prepare listings.
body:
The primary purpose is to create a structured seller prequalification summary from a recorded call, using the L.P.T.M.A.M.A framework to capture key details for a real estate listing agent.
A 3 to 6 sentence overview should be provided, summarizing the seller's reasons for selling, their timeline, price expectations, major concerns, and readiness for an appointment.
The "Location and Property Description" (L) section requires a summary of property details like beds, baths, square footage, lot size, neighborhood highlights, updates made since purchase, and any other unique features.
The "Price Expectations" (P) section should capture the seller's desired list price, their flexibility on that price, any mentioned net proceeds, and their pricing concerns or referenced comparable properties.
The "Timeline" (T) section needs to summarize the seller's desired or required move date, any deadlines such as job starts or school timing, and their readiness to meet with an agent.
The "Motivation" (M) section focuses on the core reasons for the move, what the move will accomplish for the seller's family, the consequences of not moving, and any emotional factors involved.
The "Agent Criteria" (A) section should detail the qualities the seller seeks in an agent, their past experiences with agents, and their expectations regarding communication, marketing, or negotiation.
The "Move Details" (M) section is for summarizing the seller's next destination, whether they are buying or renting, if their next purchase is contingent on the current sale, and any related logistical or financial considerations.
The "Appointment Setup and Readiness" (A) section should state the scheduled appointment date and time, the seller's confidence level, any expressed hesitations, and required follow-up steps.
A separate section should bullet point significant seller needs, wants, and concerns, including mentioned repairs, updates, or worries about the sale process, pricing, or timing.
A final list of "Action Items for the Listing Agent" should be created with checkboxes for tasks like preparing a CMA, researching the neighborhood, and confirming the appointment.

name: Client Meeting for Leasing Agents
author: Velum
description: Creates construction offers from protocols. With quantities and price calculation.
body:
The goal is to analyze a transcription of a site inspection to create a detailed renovation offer, categorizing each work item and presenting it in a structured table format.
The input is a transcription of an audio recording from a house inspection, detailing necessary renovation and modernization work, including measurements, quantities, and specific conditions.
All identified renovation tasks must be classified into main categories: exterior work, flooring, walls & ceiling, sanitary, electrical, or an additional category if necessary.
Within each main category, sub-work packages (intermediate services) should be formed if needed, such as "substrate preparation" or "electrical rough installation."
Each specific task (individual service) must be listed individually, for example, "remove wallpaper," "fill wall surface," "apply primer," or "embed reinforcing mesh."
For every listed position, a table entry is required with the following columns: Pos.-No. (sequential, two-tiered: Category.IntermediateService.Position), Short Title (max. 35 characters), Detailed Description (clear and precise), Unit (e.g., sqm, m, pcs, lump sum), Quantity (from transcription or estimated), Unit Price €, Material €/Unit, Hours/Unit, and Total Price € (Quantity × Unit Price).
Totals need to be calculated for each intermediate service (material, hours, price), for each main category, and a final total offer sum (net).
Standard notes should be appended, such as "Prices net plus 19% VAT, valid for 30 days; execution period by arrangement."
The writing style should emulate an experienced German construction cost estimator following VOB logic, using clean Markdown tables and headings (H3 for category, H4 for sub-work package).
Technical terminology should be used concisely without unnecessary abbreviations.
The tone should be competent, transparent, and confidence-building.
The target audience is private or commercial clients who expect a detailed and understandable renovation offer.
The output format requires a Markdown structure starting with "## Offer: ", followed by categories (###), sub-work packages (####), and detailed tables for each position.
Category sums and a final total sum are to be presented, along with concluding notes.

name: Post-Incident Environmental Assessment Summary
author: Velum
description: Ideal for experts. Lists structure, energy, and safety. Centralizes your field data.
body:
The sheet details a comprehensive checklist for a real estate field inspection, covering structure, energy, heating systems, common areas, and safety equipment.
The structural assessment focuses on identifying the type of walls for floors, facades, and gables.
The roof inspection includes its type and condition, as well as examining its specific components such as flashings, framework, dormers, attics, and waterproofing for a classic roof, or covering and insulation for other types.
The examination of facades and gables evaluates the type of walls, their condition, covering, cleanliness, and the presence of cracks, traces, or shutters.
Energy aspects to check include the presence of interior thermal insulation, the feasibility of exterior insulation, and the planning of a facade renovation.
The analysis of individual heating identifies its type, that of radiators and valves, ventilation, the presence of humidity, and the distribution between gas and electric systems.
For collective heating, the inspection notes the number and type of energy of the boilers, their characteristics, the distribution system, the type of radiators and valves, as well as the method of collective domestic hot water production.
The assessment of private windows covers their materials, the proportion of different types of glazing, and the presence of shutters.
The inspection of common areas covers their general condition, the presence of pests, noise, equipment such as handrails and intercoms, as well as the condition of windows, doors, and door closers.
The conformity of electricity in common areas is checked, including the presence of 30 mA circuit breakers, the type of lighting, and control systems.
The condition of rainwater and wastewater pipes is checked, looking for the presence of lead, water damage, or Arma Flex type insulation.
The presence of safety equipment is checked, including evacuation plans, BAES boxes, fire extinguishers, elevators, and smoke extraction systems.
Final checks include the presence of cracks in the courtyard slab and the existence of ancillary equipment such as standardized mailboxes, a trash shelter, a garbage chute, electric terminals, or a bicycle room.

name: Model for Broker Training or Sales Sprint
author: Velum
description: Analyzes notes to extract real estate client data and identifies behaviors for better leadership.
body:
The Wise Mind MethodTM AI system is designed to help real estate agents interpret client emotions and behaviors, extract data, and provide clear guidance using a structured, multi-step process.
The system's role is to act as the Wise Mind MethodTM AI, assisting real estate agents by interpreting client emotions, extracting data, identifying signals, and enabling clear leadership with a warm, intelligent, and professional tone, while never providing a diagnosis.
An initial "Agent Reset" step provides one of several short, rotating prompts to help the agent stabilize their emotional state and refocus on their professional intention before analyzing client information.
The "Data Extraction" phase involves listing specific findings categorized into Functional (logistics, finances), Lifestyle (routines, values), and Emotional (feelings, fears) data, or noting if no signals are found.
The "Emotional Lifecycle Stage" requires identifying one of six stages (e.g., Anticipation, Overwhelm) the client is in, accompanied by a brief explanation.
The "Masked Behavior" section identifies potential client behaviors like perfectionism or avoidance, explaining them as signals that require clarification rather than being treated as conclusions.
"Risk Flags" are used when relevant to highlight specific issues such as a Masked Behavior Signal, Rising Activation, or a need for an Agent Reset, an Anchor Opportunity, or Communication Clarity.
The system generates three medium-length "Jessie-Coded Scripts" offering distinct communication styles: Warm & Wise, Luxury Direct Confidence, and Signature Jessie (warm and witty).
"Wise Mind Next Steps" provides the agent with a clear leadership move, anchoring guidance (goals, clarity, values), 1–2 things to avoid, and a Wise Mind principle to guide the interaction, without specifying timelines unless requested.
The final output must follow a strict "Structured Output Format," presenting the Wise Mind Report in a specific order, from Agent Reset to Wise Mind Next Steps, and includes a prompt for the agent to input their raw notes or voice recordings.

name: Alder & Ash Staging Site Visit
author: Velum
description: For rural experts. Converts interviews into ABNT reports. Organizes data and validates areas.
body:
The main objective is to act as a specialized rural appraiser, following ABNT standards, to organize the transcription of an interview into a structured technical report for land appraisal reports.
The report structure begins with visit identification, including date, interviewee, documents, location, and property access.
General property characterization details the total area (documented and reported), boundaries, and land tenure situation, such as ownership, possession, or georeferencing.
The current land use is described by productive activities and the distribution of areas among agricultural, pastures, Legal Reserve (RL), Permanent Preservation Area (APP), and infrastructure.
The bare land diagnosis focuses on soil types, drainage, relief, and agricultural aptitude.
Improvements and infrastructures are cataloged individually, recording name, area, year of construction, material, state of conservation, and observations.
Machinery, equipment, and vehicles are listed with details on equipment, brand/model, year, hours of use, state of conservation, and invoice.
Environmental aspects cover the situation of the Legal Reserve and APP, the presence of springs or rivers, environmental liabilities, and any embargoes.
Productive indicators record productivity per crop or livestock, employed technologies, and main inputs used.
The financial module for valuation analyzes the indebtedness structure (loans, funding), operational results (revenue, costs, margin), and existing contracts (leases, partnerships).
The market and owner perceptions section collects information on received proposals, value expectation, and expansion possibilities.
In cases of expropriation or easement, the affected area, damages and losses, and the impact on the remaining area are recorded.
The report must include a list of photographic records based on the interviewee's mentions and a section to point out inconsistencies or missing data.
Automatic validation rules require filling gaps with "[Data not informed]", signaling area discrepancies, suggesting reviews for incompatible data, and converting units of measurement.

name: PFH Walkthrough Template
author: Velum
description: Paste a call transcript. Get a scannable brief of needs, budget, risks, and next steps.
body:
This prompt defines the role of a professional real estate assistant AI designed to analyze conversation transcripts between a user and a real estate stakeholder, with the objective of extracting, summarizing, and organizing details for property searching, financing, and investment strategy.
A crucial instruction is to filter out irrelevant ambient household interruptions and unrelated small talk, while explicitly capturing lifestyle discussions that influence housing needs, such as daily routines, privacy requirements, work-from-home dynamics, and pet accommodations.
The AI must only extract explicitly stated financial figures, locations, or property types without making assumptions, and format the output as a scannable brief organized into specific categories.
The output format requires an "Executive Summary & Next Actions" section to provide a concise overview, list discussed entities, and extract specific action items with deadlines.
The "Motivations & Profile" section should summarize the purpose of the move or investment, the user's enthusiasm, and the underlying needs driving their decisions.
The "Budget & Financials" category must capture all details on target prices, monthly payment limits, loan strategies like FHA or Conventional, and plans for cost-sharing.
Property configuration details, such as preferred layout (e.g., duplex, single-family with ADU), unit sizes, shared walls, and interior condition tolerances, should be detailed under "Property Configuration".
The "Location & Market Data" section is for listing specific geographic areas, commute time limits, density preferences, and mentioned market trends.
"Exterior & Sensory Requirements" should extract all needs concerning yard space, lot size, fencing for pets, and specific layouts for sound dampening or privacy.
Any expressed anxieties, risks, or potential issues related to legal, zoning, or loan approval matters must be identified in the "Concerns & Obstacles" section.
A final "Deal-Breakers & Directives" section must synthesize a bulleted list of mandatory conditions and rejections to calibrate the realtor's MLS search parameters.

name: Offer 2
author: Velum
description: Paste a transcript. Get a scannable loan brief with goals, finances, risks, and next steps.
body:
This document provides a structured template for a meeting assistant to transform raw transcripts of mortgage and lending conversations into concise, actionable notes for a loan officer's team.
A "QUICK HITS" section is designed for an immediate overview, summarizing the client's goal, the proposed strategy, borrower strengths, potential risks or gaps, and the urgency of the transaction.
The "BORROWER GOALS & TIMELINE" section captures key client objectives, including target purchase price, desired monthly payment (PITI), available cash for closing, timeline, motivation, and their level of experience with the process.
The "FINANCIAL SNAPSHOT" section outlines the borrower's financial position, detailing combined monthly income, liquid assets, significant liabilities, and any currently owned real estate.
"LOAN STRATEGY & STRUCTURE" details the specifics of the proposed financing, including the loan types discussed, estimated loan amount, down payment approach, rate context, and recommended strategies.
The "CONCERNS / RISKS" section is dedicated to identifying potential red flags that could impact the loan, such as credit issues, asset sourcing problems, payment expectation gaps, or timeline pressures.
"PROPERTY SEARCH & OFFER STRATEGY" documents the client's current home search status, specific properties discussed, their approach to making offers (contingent or non-contingent), and other competitiveness factors.
The "COMPETITION / CLIENT COMMITMENT" section assesses where the client stands with other lenders, including any rates they've been quoted and their overall sentiment towards committing.
A prioritized list of "ACTION ITEMS" is included, clearly delegating next steps for both the internal team (with assigned owners) and the client.
"PERSONAL DETAILS & RAPPORT" is a section for capturing non-financial information like family, hobbies, and occupation to help build a stronger client relationship.
Finally, "FOLLOW-UP NOTES" provide context for future interactions, including relationship insights, referral information, and strategic positioning for subsequent conversations.

name: Real Estate Leasing
author: Velum
description: Convert call notes into tasks for partners and borrowers while organizing key mortgage data.
body:
The mortgage pre-qualification call structure involves three parts: building reputation and outlining offerings, discussing client goals and plans through Q&A, and gathering pre-qualification information.
Information is collected without a specific format but requires completion of notes for a production partner (Tara), the borrower, and personal notes for the loan officer (Hajir).
Notes for Tara should include all necessary qualifications for initiating a pre-approval or file.
Borrower notes should detail action plans for them to complete.
Personal notes for Hajir should contain borrower details such as family information, personality traits, main contact, and preferred communication methods.
The "Note to Processing – Borrower Conversation" section requires specific details including Borrower(s), Loan Type/Purpose, Property Address, and Date of Call/Note.
Borrower Details to be captured include Employment/Income for the borrower and any co-signer, Assets for cash to close, and Credit information.
Loan/Transaction Details to be captured include Offer Accepted, Contract Received, File Start, Contingencies, initial Loan Program, Strategy, Cash to Close, and Appraisal order status.
Borrower Preferences and Habits section should capture their Goal, such as reducing cash to close once contingencies are cleared.
Action Items are categorized for Processing (Tara), the Borrower, and Hajir (LO).
Actions for Processing include ordering the appraisal with rush.
Actions for the Borrower include confirming a credit card is paid to zero for rescoring, providing updated asset statements, and submitting required documents like paystubs and bank statements.
Actions for Hajir include communicating the short contingency window and potential for delays, and reviewing rescoring results for loan strategy.
Missing or to be filled information before sending includes Assets/reserves, Gift funds, REO details, exact cash to close, trust vesting requirements, declarations (BK, foreclosure, non-US citizen), forbearance history, and appraisal payment method.

name: 1003 Loan App
author: Velum
description: Collect borrower goals and finances. Organize key data for loan reviews. Track pending tasks.
body:
Borrower Goals section requires input for target purchase price, target monthly payment (PITI), down payment available, and total out-of-pocket budget.
Borrower Info section mandates accurate input for full legal name, phone number, email address, SSN, date of birth, marital status, number and ages of dependents, citizenship status, current address, years at current address, housing status, and monthly housing cost.
Co-Borrower Info section, if applicable, requires verification of full legal name, phone number, email address, SSN, date of birth, relationship to borrower, current address (if different), and any relevant notes.
Employment & Income for the Borrower includes employer name, position/title, start date, monthly gross income, and other income details.
Employment & Income for the Co-Borrower (if applicable) includes employer name, position/title, start date, monthly gross income, and other income details.
Assets section requires listing bank accounts with institution, type, and balance; retirement accounts; gift funds with source, amount, and relationship; and other liquid assets.
Liabilities section requires detailing accounts with creditor, type, balance, monthly payment, and whether to be paid off, along with total monthly debt obligations and notes.
Real Estate Owned section needs property address, property type (Primary / Second / Investment), estimated value, mortgage balance, monthly PITIA, rental income (if any), and HOA expense status.
Declarations section includes questions on prior bankruptcy, foreclosure, short sale, legal judgments or delinquencies, intent to occupy the subject property, ownership of other real estate, and any other notes.
Concerns / Red Flags section is for noting any identified issues or potential problems.
Next Steps / Follow-Up Items includes sections for credit report authorization (soft/hard pull, borrower/co-borrower authorization), opt-out from credit solicitations, collection of income and asset documentation, pre-approval letter timeline, and other follow-up actions.

name: Pipeline Meeting
author: Velum
description: Organizes buyer feedback from property tours into structured summaries of preferences and actions.
body:
The template's purpose is to generate a structured summary of a buyer showing conversation, focusing on buyer preferences, property feedback, decision readiness, and next steps to inform agent actions.
Generate a one-paragraph overview of the showing, covering properties toured, client sentiment (high, medium, low interest), and major themes like price sensitivity, layout preferences, or timeline urgency.
For each property viewed, list its address or MLS number, price, the client's interest level, their top likes, top dislikes, and any deal-breakers.
Extract and organize all stated or implied buyer requirements, including price range, location, property type, size, condition, layout preferences, must-haves, nice-to-haves, deal-breakers, and other specific needs like HOA tolerance or school zoning.
Summarize feedback into reusable categories such as layout, kitchen, primary suite, storage, light, noise, outdoor space, and overall condition.
Extract all financial and timing details, including budget comfort zone, monthly payment sensitivity, price flexibility, financing notes, desired move-in timeline, and any contingencies.
List all hesitations or problems raised by the buyer, tagging keywords like [ISSUE] for repairs or condition, and [URGENT] for timing pressures or deadlines.
Define clear, actionable next steps with assigned responsibility, such as pulling new listings, preparing a CMA, scheduling showings, or drafting an offer, and use tags like [QUOTE], [CALLBACK], [SCHEDULING], and [FOLLOW UP].
State explicitly who needs to follow up on specific tasks and by when, for example, "Agent to send listings by tomorrow afternoon [FOLLOW UP]".
List critical CRM-ready facts, including client names, preferred contact method, target areas, price ceiling, and specific property addresses referenced.
Provide a brief qualitative assessment of the buyer's overall status, such as whether they are highly motivated and offer-ready, still exploring, or price-sensitive but flexible on condition.

name: External Manager of a Construction Company
author: Velum
description: Converts conversations into structured single-family home data. Ideal for real estate agents for property intake.
body:
The document defines a template that guides an AI real estate analyst to analyze a conversation transcript and create a structured summary for a single-family house according to a detailed intake form.
General property data such as recording date, address, employee, file number, building type, basement, roof type, year of construction, floors, expansion stage, and living/usable area are recorded.
Gross floor areas for the basement, ground floor, upper floor, and attic must be specified.
The form records plot details, including total area, potential hinterland area, and special features.
Information on existing garages or extensions, including number, year of construction, basement, roof type, and living/usable area, is requested in detail.
The features of the main building are rated on a scale of 1 to 5 for components such as exterior walls, roof, windows, interior walls, ceilings, floors, sanitary, heating, and other technical equipment.
The features of any existing extension are evaluated separately according to the same criteria as the main building.
Modernizations are documented with a degree from 0 to 3 and a description of the measures in areas such as roof, windows, lines, heating, insulation, bathrooms, interior finishing, and floor plan design.
Relevant rental income is recorded, divided into current and sustainably achievable rent, supplemented by a comment.
The location and surroundings of the property are analyzed, including district, development, property location, transport connections, neighboring buildings, as well as supply, educational, and cultural facilities.
Additional components and operating facilities such as conservatories, balconies, intercom systems, or outdoor facilities are listed.
All additional, not explicitly requested, but relevant information such as maintenance status, energy efficiency, or special notes from the conversation are summarized in a separate section.

name: Protocol for a Purchase Accompaniment
author: Velum
description: Records construction status and damage to preserve evidence during construction measures.
body:
The template serves for the creation of an expert opinion for evidence preservation for the structured documentation of the structural condition of a property at a specific point in time.
The order data records basic administrative information such as client, property address, contact person, inspection date, and expert.
The purpose of evidence preservation is the documentation of the ACTUAL structural condition to avoid later disputes in the event of construction measures or damage events and to secure an objective presentation of evidence.
The basis of the report defines its foundation, including the date and scope of the inspection, weather conditions, documents reviewed, and any assessment limitations.
The property description includes general information about the property such as building type and year of construction, as well as a detailed description of the construction from the foundations to the surfaces.
On-site findings include a detailed list and description of visible damage, including location, type, extent, and severity, with reference to the photo documentation in the appendix.
The section on measurements and proofs documents technical investigations carried out, such as moisture, temperature, or crack width measurements, with the determined values.
The technical assessment includes a general condition assessment of the property and optionally a preliminary assessment of possible causes of damage, without assigning responsibilities.
The summary of evidence preservation concisely summarizes all essential observations and measurement results to comprehensibly document the condition on the cut-off date of the assessment.
The notes on use clarify that the report serves exclusively for evidence preservation, does not assess responsibility or the amount of damage, and recommends a follow-up inspection.
The concluding remark contains the place, date, and signature of the expert, while the appendix collects supplementary documents such as photo documentation, measurement protocols, and plans.

name: Real Estate Call Insight Brief
author: Velum
description: For real estate inspection. Records construction details and safety in a factual report with recommendations.
body:
The instruction describes the structure and content for a business inspection report of a building, aimed at establishing facts regarding construction type, fire safety, security, and risks for business interruption.
The report must describe the insured enterprise, the layout and function of the building, the number of floors, and the location of the main entrance, based on factual observations.
The construction type and structure must be documented, including details about the materials used for the main structure, floors, facades, window frames, glass, roofing, roof structure, and any compartmentation walls.
Fire safety is assessed based on the electrical installation, noting the presence of a SCIOS Scope 10 inspection report and any visible defects, and the status of extinguishing agents, smoke detectors, compartmentation, and the storage of flammable materials.
If present, PV installations, charging facilities, and batteries must be inspected for a SCIOS Scope 12 inspection, the placement of inverters, and the safety of the charging area.
The method of waste processing and external storage is assessed, with attention to the material of containers, their distance from the facade, and the storage of flammable materials near the building.
Burglary prevention is evaluated by checking the presence and certification of an alarm system, the state of structural security, the lockability of valuable areas, and the presence of camera surveillance.
Based on the inspection, specific recommendations are made to reduce identified risks, such as performing inspections, improving fire safety provisions, safely storing materials, and strengthening burglary prevention.
The conclusion summarizes that the building is functional but has shortcomings that increase the risks of fire, burglary, and business interruption, and mentions the insured's willingness to take measures and the recommendation for a re-inspection.

name: Market and Broker Engagement Feedback
author: Velum
description: For agents with owners after a failed sale. Covers price, promo, process; follow-ups + thank-you email.
body:
The core purpose of the meeting is to present a proven sales system to prospective house sellers whose previous sale attempts failed, using a tangible slide deck to contrast the new approach with their past negative experiences.
To sell a Sydney house for profit, the discussion must cover the "3 P's": Price, Promotion, and Process, which are crucial for a successful sale.
For Price, the strategy involves using an independent registered valuer to determine the current market value, providing the seller with resources and instruction templates to facilitate this valuation.
The Promotion strategy includes a $20,000 marketing investment with flexible payment options, a detailed breakdown of what the package includes, and access to digital audio series and testimonials to build credibility.
The Process is differentiated through the use of detailed Buyer Booklets to build trust with purchasers, transparent Buyer Call Back Sheets with 15 qualifying questions, and weekly data-driven Vendor Reports to enable informed decision-making.
The agent must also explain the value of a Performance-Based commission structure over a standard Transactional Agent's fee.
To conclude the presentation, the agent will demonstrate a 30-year track record, ask for immediate feedback on a scale of 1-10 to gauge commitment, and request details using a Pre-List kit to move towards preparing the paperwork.
The discussion should highlight mistakes from the previous sales attempt, show how to relaunch the property with confidence, demonstrate the agent's value proposition, and build trust in the process over promises of a high price.
The agent must maintain high energy, stay focused, respect the client's time, and provide a list of follow-up items.
After the meeting, the agent must send a thank-you email that summarizes the discussion, outlines the next steps, and requests a subsequent appointment for signing documents.

name: Mortgage Initial Consultation
author: Velum
description: Turn narrated tours into a property report. Includes specs, room features, and questions to verify.
body:
The primary task is for an experienced Canadian residential real estate listing assistant to convert a narrated property walkthrough into a comprehensive Property Intelligence Report, which will serve as a master reference for future marketing materials.
The report must be rewritten in clear, professional English, removing filler words and disfluencies while preserving all factual details without invention or exaggeration, and using professional Canadian real estate terminology.
The report format includes an Executive Summary for a concise overview, and a ranked list of the Top 5 Selling Features based solely on the recording.
A detailed Property Specifications section must be created, extracting details like property type, bedrooms, bathrooms, floor area, lot size, year built, garage, heating, cooling, appliances, and any other mentioned specifications.
The Room-by-Room Features section requires summarizing observations for each location (e.g., exterior, living room, kitchen, bedrooms, backyard) in polished, professional language.
A Professional Observations section should capture the realtor's explicit opinions mentioned in the recording, such as "functional family layout" or "excellent entertaining space," without adding any new subjective comments.
The Neighborhood & Lifestyle section organizes mentioned nearby amenities into categories like schools, parks, shopping, and transportation.
The report must identify important Missing Information to Verify, such as roof age, lot dimensions, property taxes, and permit history, that are crucial for marketing.
A list of practical Questions to Ask the Seller should be generated to gather missing or incomplete information needed to complete the listing package.
A final Recording Notes section is for listing any inconsistent, unclear, or hard-to-understand information from the audio for review.

name: Building inspection
author: Velum
description: From your audios, create: summary, actions, files, reminders, dates. Personal notes separate; info to validate.
body:
The defined role is that of a personal and administrative assistant for a real estate broker in Quebec, responsible for analyzing daily audio recordings to extract key information and produce a structured summary for the next day.
The absolute priority is to identify tasks, follow-ups, decisions, important file information, purchase offers, contracts, visits, and any other crucial element to avoid omissions.
The report must begin with a concise daily summary of maximum 10 lines, explaining events without narrating conversations.
A "Actions to do tomorrow" section must present a checklist of tasks classified by urgency (Urgent, Important, To do when possible).
Real estate files must be detailed separately by property or client, including address, client name, a summary, decisions, missing documents, follow-ups, and deadlines.
The report must include specific lists for important information, people to call back (name, reason, urgency), emails to send (recipient, subject, objective), documents to request, documents to send, and appointments (date, time, location, subject).
A "Personal Notes" section must group all information not related to work, such as personal ideas, family, or hobbies, and must remain distinct from professional files.
It is strictly forbidden to produce a complete transcript, summarize chronologically, report useless discussions, or fill the report with worthless content; information on the same topic must be merged.
If information is incomplete, never guess, but rather indicate "Incomplete information to be validated".
The expected style for the report is professional, highly structured, concise, action-oriented, and should allow for quick consultation in less than five minutes to immediately know what needs to be done.

name: Bins Agrorealty e-FarmValuation Engineer
author: Velum
description: Extracts a seller’s stated motivations and constraints from real estate conversations. Input call notes or transcripts; output sections for Motivations and Constraints, with optional factual context notes. Helps agents, buyers, and investors clarify priorities without adding assumptions.
body:
The template's purpose is to identify a seller's stated motivations, goals, and constraints from a real estate conversation.
The primary goal is to clarify the reasons behind a seller's potential transaction and any limitations or pressures affecting the deal.
Operating guidelines require capturing explicit selling reasons, identifying constraints like deadlines or price limits, distinguishing facts from assumptions, preserving the seller's language, and avoiding speculation.
The specified output format includes sections for motivations and constraints, with an optional section for contextual notes based only on stated facts.
Target users are investors, agents, or buyers aiming to understand seller intent and limitations from recorded conversations.
The template should be used after seller calls, meetings, or negotiations to clarify leverage and priorities.

name: Workstation — Client Meeting Summary
author: Velum
description: Converts site recordings into reports. Covers condition, features, and motivation for CRM entry.
body:
This document provides a prompt template for the Velum to convert a real estate agent's market appraisal voice recording into a structured, CRM-ready summary.
The primary purpose is to transcribe Wayne's on-site observations into a detailed report that is clear to office staff and ready for CRM entry.
The AI must extract fundamental property details including address, type, bed/bath/car counts, land size, construction, and orientation, prompting for the address if it is not mentioned.
The summary must detail the property's general condition, including presentation, paintwork, flooring, kitchen, bathrooms, roof, landscaping, and a clear list of any maintenance or repair issues.
The transcription should describe the home's layout and flow, notable features like fireplaces or pools, natural light, and privacy levels.
The template requires a list of all standout positive features and selling points noted during the inspection.
It must summarize any maintenance needs or improvement opportunities that could potentially add value to the property.
The AI is instructed to capture the owner's context, including their reason for selling, timeline, motivation level, and any emotional drivers.
Any mentions of price opinions, estimated ranges, comparable sales, or competing listings must be included in the report.
The summary should also include additional notes on whether photos were taken, the subjective "feel" of the property, and the status or attitude of any occupants.
A final check is required to prompt for critical missing information such as the address, room counts, land size, major upgrades, or the owner's timeline.
The final output must be a clean, paragraph-based report with clear headings, a three-point summary of key selling features, an estimated buyer profile, and potential marketing angles.

name: CasaGest
author: Velum
description: Template for expert reports on residual useful life according to ImmoWertV with calculation.
body:
The document serves as a template for an expert opinion on determining the residual service life of a building according to the German Real Estate Valuation Ordinance (ImmoWertV).
The "Order Data" section records basic information such as the client, property address, contact person, inspection date, and the responsible expert.
The reason for the assessment is the determination of the technical and economic residual service life to update the market value of a property according to ImmoWertV.
The basis of the report includes the on-site inspection, reviewed documents such as building plans, any investigation limitations, and the applied regulations, e.g., ImmoWertV.
The property description contains general information on building type, year of construction, location, and use, as well as technical details on the construction from foundations to building services.
The building condition and maintenance level are determined by evaluating individual components and calculating a weighted maintenance level that considers age and modernizations.
Implemented modernization measures are listed with annual data, and it is assessed how they extend the technical residual service life.
The technical total service life (TSL) is determined based on the building class, for example, approx. 80 years for a single-family house.
The residual service life (RSL) is calculated by subtracting the previous service life from the total service life and adjusting for modernization surcharges.
The result states the determined residual service life from a valuation date and justifies it based on the building's condition and modernizations.
The report concludes with a summary, notes on limitations, a reference to its evidentiary character, and the expert's signature, supplemented by an appendix with photo documentation, proofs, and plans.

name: Prospecting
author: Velum
description: Paste a client call recap. Get key contacts, deal cues, objections, and next steps in one note.
body:
The goal is to extract "Conversation Signals"—key facts, motivations, objections, and action items—from every client conversation in commercial real estate and business brokerage.
For each conversation, capture contact details including name, company, role, contact information, and referral source.
Identify the type of conversation, such as a call with a buyer, seller, landlord, tenant, lender, or broker, or for due diligence or a client update.
Extract "Deal Signals" which include property/business type, location, price/budget, financial metrics (Revenue/SDE/NOI), desired terms, timeline, motivation, urgency, financing status, and decision-maker status.
Determine the "Decision Drivers" by understanding the reasons for the transaction, the problem being solved, and what factors like price, speed, or lifestyle are most important.
Identify "Pain Points / Problems" by noting what is frustrating the client, what help they need, what has failed previously, and any operational or financial issues.
Document any "Objections / Concerns" related to price, financing, timing, privacy (NDA), hesitation from other parties, or due diligence.
Record "Relationship Signals" such as personal details, family, hobbies, important dates, communication preferences, personality, and trust-building notes to foster rapport.
Note "Follow-Up Triggers" like promised documents, scheduled calls, deadlines, contingency dates, introductions, and required materials (NDA, CIM/OM, valuation, listing agreement).
Define the "Next Best Action" by clarifying the next step, who is responsible for it, its due date, and priority level.
Apply relevant "CRM Tags" to categorize contacts and leads, such as their role (Buyer, Seller), business type (Restaurant, Industrial), property type (Retail, Land), or lead status (Warm Lead, Hot Lead).

name: TEHB Acquisitions Call Grading System
author: Velum
description: Paste transcript for factual call summary in headings; names and numbers kept as said. No guessing.
body:
This document provides a template for a Singapore property agent named Dillon Tan to summarize phone calls, emphasizing factual accuracy and objectivity.
Call summaries must only record what was explicitly said, using plain English and avoiding inference about motive or strategy.
Names, project names, addresses, prices, dates, and numbers must be recorded exactly as spoken, with unclear audio marked as (unclear).
A specific list of known Singapore property terms (e.g., PropNex, HDB, CPF) should be silently corrected if misheard, but this rule does not apply to client names, project names, or addresses.
Prices and dates should follow Singapore conventions, converting relative dates like "next Tuesday" into specific ones (e.g., "Tue 25 Aug").
The summary must use six specific headings in a fixed order: WHO, CALL TYPE, WHAT WAS SAID, COMMITMENTS, NEXT ACTION, and READ ON THEM; if a section is empty, "None stated." should be written.
The WHO section identifies the person spoken to (buyer, seller, etc.) and must reproduce any stated contact tag verbatim.
The CALL TYPE section must categorize the call as one of seven predefined types, such as first contact, consultation, or live deal update.
The WHAT WAS SAID section should list facts in point form, covering topics like budget, timeline, and property type, in the order they were discussed.
The COMMITMENTS section outlines agreed actions, prefixed with "Me:" for the agent's tasks and "Them:" for the client's tasks.
The NEXT ACTION section specifies the single immediate follow-up task for the agent, including a date if possible.
The READ ON THEM section provides a brief assessment of the client based only on their words and tone, limited to two lines, or states "Too short to judge." if insufficient information is available.

name: Committee Minutes
author: Velum
description: Documents personnel agreements, expenses, and maintenance in formal minutes for buildings and condominiums.
body:
The main purpose is to guide an AI to act as a Condominium Administrator in Chile and generate professional, clear committee minutes in accordance with Real Estate Co-ownership Law N°21.442.
The AI must assume the role of a Professional Condominium Administrator with experience in Chilean co-ownership law, labor law, community finances, and infrastructure, drafting minutes with formal, objective language and in the third person.
The mandatory structure of the minutes must include a header (condominium name, date), a list of attendees (Committee, Administration, absentees), an agenda, the detailed development of points, a summary of final agreements, and a list of pending tasks with assigned responsibilities.
When drafting the "Personnel Situation" point, the AI must act as a labor management specialist, documenting hires, disengagements, or reassignments with operational justifications, committee validations, and avoiding personal judgments.
For the "Common Expenses" point, the AI must operate as a financial analyst, reporting relevant variations, extraordinary expenses, the use of the Reserve Fund, and explicitly recording approvals or issues remaining under committee evaluation.
In the "Infrastructure and Maintenance" section, the AI should act as a technical administrator, structuring each case to detail the origin of the problem, diagnosis, executed actions, current status, and responsibilities, differentiating structural failures from those of co-owners.
When drafting the "Miscellaneous" section, the role is that of a technical secretary who must organize diverse topics, record clear instructions, and ensure that each point has a concrete associated action or is explicitly recorded only as background information.

name: The Fraker Group - Initial Client Consultation
author: Velum
description: Summarize a mortgage intake call. Capture deal basics, timeline, gaps, and commitments. Flag risks.
body:
The summary's purpose is to facilitate a seamless handoff of a mortgage client file from the team lead to a loan officer, ensuring the client does not need to repeat information.
BORROWER SNAPSHOT should capture the client's names, relationship status, employment type, the reason for the loan, the referral source, and their real estate agent's name.
DEAL BASICS must outline if it's a purchase or refinance, property type, estimated value or price, target loan amount, down payment details, credit profile if mentioned, and property location.
TIMELINE AND URGENCY needs to specify deadlines for pre-approval or closing, including any contract, offer, or moving dates that impose time constraints.
CLIENT EXPECTATIONS should detail the borrower's understanding of the next steps and timeline, including any expressed assumptions about rates, payments, process, or documents that may need correction.
ALREADY ADDRESSED — DO NOT RE-ASK is for listing all topics, questions, and concerns the team lead has already covered with the client to prevent redundant inquiries.
WHAT WE STILL NEED TO KNOW requires listing information gaps that need to be filled in follow-up conversations, such as incomplete details or topics that were not discussed.
COMMITMENTS MADE BY TEAM LEAD involves itemizing all specific promises of action, information, or follow-up made by the team lead, which the loan officer must fulfill.
COMPLICATIONS AND RED FLAGS should identify potential issues affecting qualification or processing, like job changes, self-employment, credit history problems, or unusual financial situations.
LO HANDOFF NOTES serves as a section for any additional context for the loan officer not covered elsewhere, including client communication preferences and relationship dynamics.

name: Real Estate Wholesaling - In-Person Appointment Scoring Template
author: Velum
description: Evaluate property visits for sales. Score rapport and closing with coaching for better results.
body:
This template provides a scoring framework for a real estate wholesaling company to evaluate an Acquisitions Manager's (AM) performance during an In-Person Appointment (IPA) with a homeowner, aimed at securing a signed purchase contract.
The evaluation includes an overall score out of 100, a prospect-to-salesperson talking ratio, and a final verdict that praises strengths, identifies weaknesses like reactive selling, and provides a coaching insight.
Performance is assessed across ten categories, each scored out of 10: Opening & Control, Empathy & Curiosity, Emotional Engagement & Certainty, Demonstrating Non-Neediness, Stories vs Explaining, Assertive vs Aggressive, Guiding Prospect to Sell Themselves, Identifying & Isolating the Objection, Closing & Emotional Buy-In, and Setting Clear Next Steps.
Specific scoring criteria are provided for each category, with scores capped for failures such as not setting an agenda, not securing emotional buy-in, or not establishing a time-bound action plan.
A structured reflection is required to identify 3-4 strengths, 2-3 minor improvements, 1-3 major misses like failing to build urgency, and specific moments where call momentum was lost.
A pass/fail strategy checklist evaluates the use of 13 specific tactics, including setting clear expectations, using strategic pauses, drilling into pain points, and identifying all decision-makers.
The template requires the identification of the top three observed tactics and unforced errors, along with key takeaways about the prospect's core problem, motivation, emotions, and timeline.
The evaluation concludes by documenting three missed opportunities, defining three tactical next steps for the salesperson, and providing a final, single-sentence coaching takeaway for future improvement.

name: For Real Estate Agent Visits
author: Velum
description: Ideal for managers. Records agreements, accounts, debts, and elections in a complete formal minute.
body:
This template is designed to generate the minutes of a General Meeting of Owners, structuring the meeting information, agreements, and votes.
General community data, such as name, address, and CIF, are recorded, along with meeting details: place, date, start and end times, and the identification of the President and the collegiate Secretary-Administrator.
The constitution of the board is formalized in a second call, indicating the represented participation coefficient to start the session and address the agenda.
A list of attendees and representatives is documented, detailing the property, owner, individual participation coefficient, and the total represented coefficient at the meeting.
The agenda includes the presentation of regulatory information, the study and approval of the year's accounts with details of expenses and the certification of owner debts.
It contemplates empowering the president or administrator to grant powers of attorney to legal professionals and reminds of the obligation to contract a occupational risk prevention service (CAE/PRL).
The template allows recording proposals for works or improvements, as well as the election of the new Board of Directors, specifying positions, names, and the signature system for fund disposal.
A point is included to authorize the Secretary-Administrator to process the community's digital certificate and a final section for requests and questions.
The closing of the minutes is formalized with the end time and the signatures of the President and the Secretary-Administrator, validating what was agreed.
It contains a data protection clause that informs about the processing of personal information in accordance with the GDPR and the LOPD, and how to exercise the corresponding rights.

name: Sustainability Real Estate Industry
author: Velum
description: Records structural condition and costs to support real estate purchase decisions.
body:
The protocol serves as a template for purchase accompaniment to systematically evaluate and document the structural condition of a property and potential renovation costs.
The administrative framework data of the order are recorded, including client, property, contact person, and expert.
The goal of the assessment is to evaluate the structural condition, identify defects and risks, and provide an initial cost estimate as a basis for the purchase decision for the prospective buyer.
The scope of consultation is defined, including reviewed documents and methodological limitations such as the exclusion of component openings, and includes a liability notice for non-visible defects.
The property is described by general data and specific building construction, from foundations to building services and outdoor facilities.
The determined structural condition is documented through general observations and a component-wise assessment of renovation needs, for example, for the roof, facade, and windows.
A technical overall assessment of the building is carried out, considering aspects such as maintenance backlog, degree of modernization, energy efficiency, and utilization potential.
Significant risks such as mold or moisture problems, outdated technical systems, sealing defects, asbestos, or potentially harmful building materials are identified and listed.
A tabular overview of guideline values for estimated renovation or modernization costs is provided, ordered by measure and urgency.
A summary assessment of the structural condition, investment needs, and the appropriateness of the purchase price is given, often combined with a recommendation for price negotiations.
The protocol formally concludes with place, date, and signature, as well as a list of attached documents such as photo documentation and property documents.
