name: Prelist Walkthough- Home features, Measurements & Task list
author: Velum
description: Prequalify buyers in one call. Collect contact info, location, price, timeline, motives, and financing.
body:
This guide provides a structured template of questions for real estate agents to pre-qualify potential home buyers, using the L.P.T.M.A.M.A acronym to cover key areas.
The initial step is to collect essential contact information from the potential buyer, including their name, phone number, email, and address.
(L) Location questions aim to understand the buyer's desired areas, the reasons behind their choices, specific neighborhood preferences, and requirements for outdoor space.
(P) Price questions are designed to determine the buyer's comfortable price range and monthly payment, and to test their flexibility with a hypothetical scenario slightly over budget.
(T) Timeline questions probe the buyer's readiness to make an offer on a suitable property, seeking to uncover any potential hesitations or obstacles.
(M) Motivation questions explore the underlying reasons for the purchase, the urgency of the move, and the impact it will have on them and their family, including any specific needs like school districts.
(A) Agent questions ascertain if the buyer is already working with another agent, has viewed properties or made offers, and what qualities they value most in an agent.
(M) Mortgage questions clarify the buyer's financing plan (cash or loan), their status with a mortgage lender, and whether they need to sell an existing property to buy a new one.
(A) Appointment setting is the final step, focused on scheduling a buyer consultation to discuss their needs in detail, gathering contact info for all decision-makers, highlighting the agent's unique value, and confirming the meeting details.

name: Board Meeting Minutes
author: Velum
description: Organizes decisions and issues from meeting notes to create official minutes for management associations. Supports recording and reporting.
body:
Provides a template for creating formal board meeting minutes from meeting memos and audio transcripts, for a condominium management association secretariat staff.
Rules for creating minutes require concise and accurate descriptions understandable by third parties, conversion of colloquial language to written language, clear separation of decided, reported, and discussed matters, clear indication of pros/cons and conclusions, organization of unclear points as "continued deliberation" or "to be discussed next time," and use of appropriate expressions for official documents of the management association.
Basic information for the minutes includes fields for meeting name, date/time, location, attendees, absentees, chairperson, and secretary.
Agenda items are divided by topic, with each recording the agenda title, explanation, main opinions, decided matters (or conclusion), and reserved/continued deliberation matters.
Separate from agenda items, there is a section for reported matters, including report content and supplementary matters.
If there are resolutions, their content, status (for/against/abstain), and implementation period are summarized in a list.
The scheduled date, location, and main scheduled agenda items for the next meeting are recorded to clarify future schedules.
Requests and To-Dos are organized in a list format with content, person in charge, deadline, and remarks to facilitate task management.

name: Home Seller Closing Meeting
author: Velum
description: Paste a seller appointment transcript. Get key facts, unknowns, and a clear follow-up plan.
body:
The primary purpose of this template is to provide a structured framework for analyzing a PDX Renovations acquisitions appointment, focusing on extracting key seller information, evaluating the opportunity, and defining a clear follow-up plan.
An Appointment Snapshot captures fundamental details like date, participants, property information, and the overall outcome, summarized in a single executive sentence.
The Seller/Situation Profile section aims to understand the seller's personal context, including their type, current situation, family dynamics, and emotional state.
The "WHY NOW / PAIN / MOTIVATION" section delves into the seller's explicit and underlying reasons for selling, the urgency, and the consequences of inaction to gauge their level of pain and readiness to decide.
The Post-Sale Plan/Life Clock section identifies the seller's next steps after selling, their financial needs for that move, and the timeline, including any hard deadlines and dependencies.
Decision Authority analysis clarifies who legally owns the property, who has the power to sell, and identifies all influencing parties to assess potential risks or gaps in authority.
The "Seller Avatar / WHY PDX" section seeks to understand why the seller chose PDX Renovations, what problems they are trying to avoid, and the specific value PDX offers over other options.
Price/Time/Convenience analysis ranks the seller's priorities and documents price expectations, timing needs, and desired conveniences.
The remaining sections evaluate property condition, economics, price extraction, offers, objections, closing, follow-up, rep performance, coaching opportunities, and final lessons.

name: Buyer/seller call summary
author: Velum
description: Transform call notes into structured CRM entries covering needs, budget, and clear action items.
body:
This document provides a structured prompt template for a real estate CRM assistant to summarize buyer/seller calls for direct CRM entry.
The summary should begin with a single-sentence executive summary identifying the client, their intent, and current status, followed by short, non-repetitive bullet points.
The template includes a "Client Overview" section to capture essential details like name, client type (Buyer/Seller/Buy & Sell), locations discussed, and ideal timeline.
A "Motivations, Expectations & Concerns" section is designed to document the client's reasons for moving, what they value in an agent, any fears, and past agent experiences.
The "Top Priorities" section aims to outline the primary objective, non-negotiables, budget, timing constraints, and a color-coded urgency level (Low/Medium/High).
For buyers, a "Buying Insights" section is included to detail property type, preferred areas, must-have features, nice-to-have features, and how they wish to receive listings.
For sellers, a "Selling Insights" section captures property type/location, condition, discussed preparations or repairs, pricing expectations, and motivation level.
A "Personal Notes" section allows for recording details about the client's family, lifestyle, hobbies, and emotional drivers influencing their decision.
The "Recap & Next Steps" section summarizes key discussion points and outlines specific to-do items for both the client and the agent, along with a follow-up schedule.
An "Additional Observations" field is provided to note any observed patterns, client tone, repeated themes, or other secondary information worth remembering.

name: Land-e-Valuator
author: Velum
description: Paste notes or transcript. Get a progress and draw report with decisions, risks, and next steps.
body:
The core purpose is to define the structure and content for a detailed construction report generated from a weekly progress and payment draw meeting between a property owner and a contractor.
The report should summarize project progress by detailing work completed since the last meeting, noting the current phase, and distinguishing finished work from ongoing tasks.
It must include a financial review that documents the draw request amount, associated labor and materials, tracks total payments and budget, and identifies any costs needing owner approval.
All scope changes, including approved or pending change orders and decisions on materials, layouts, or finishes, must be recorded along with who approved them.
A list of materials purchased and still needed should be created, noting suppliers, costs, and the party responsible for purchasing.
Any problems, delays, or concerns from either the contractor or owner that affect the budget, schedule, or quality must be identified and documented for follow-up.
The plan for the upcoming week needs to be summarized, outlining contractor commitments, owner responsibilities, and creating a clear action-item checklist.
A payment approval recommendation must be provided, justifying the draw based on completed work, assessing if the request is supported by progress, and listing any missing documentation.
The final summary report must be formatted into specific sections: Project Status, Completed This Week, Work Remaining, Draw Request Summary, Budget/Cost Updates, Decisions Made, Issues & Risks, Next Week’s Plan, Action Items With Responsible Person, and Follow-Up Questions.

name: My Own Exec. Assistant
author: Velum
description: Paste a listing appointment transcript. Get scores, missed moments, and better scripts to try next time.
body:
The core purpose is to define a coaching framework for analyzing a real estate agent's listing appointment performance, drawing from Ninja Selling, Chris Voss's negotiation tactics, and Full Fee Agent principles.
The coaching feedback structure begins with a "Performance Snapshot" section, which includes an overall score, highlights of successful actions that built trust and authority, and identifies the biggest missed opportunities where control or leverage was lost.
A "Seller Psychology" analysis is required to profile the seller's motivation, emotional state, and decision style, while also identifying their primary concerns and any unstated hidden issues.
The "Control & Positioning" section evaluates the agent's control over the appointment, their ability to position themselves as a high-value consultant rather than a salesperson, and the clarity and confidence of their strategy delivery.
A critical evaluation of "Voss Skills" is mandated, assessing the effective use of techniques like labeling and mirroring, and identifying missed opportunities, particularly with accusation audits and no-oriented questions.
The framework demands a section on "Exact Improvements," providing 3-5 specific, behavior-based changes for the next appointment and offering "Better Scripts" with improved language for specific situations.
A final "Next Level" section outlines what a top 1% agent would do differently to elevate the appointment to an elite level, emphasizing that the report's success is measured by its ability to provide actionable steps for the very next appointment.

name: Buyer/Seller Meeting Summary
author: Velum
description: Organize client goals, budgets, and timelines. Record needs and tasks for structured meeting notes.
body:
This template is designed for summarizing real estate prospect meetings, suitable for client information in a CRM, covering client goals, discussion points, and to-dos.
Motivations, Expectations & Concerns section captures the client's reasons for buying/selling now, their expectations of the realtor, past negative experiences with agents, and any anxieties about the current transaction.
Top Priorities section details the client type (Buyer, Seller, Buy & Sell), their primary objectives, desired timeline, financial standing or budget, any constraints or dealbreakers, and urgent follow-up actions required.
Buying Insights focuses on the specific features and locations the client desires in a property and their preferred method for receiving property updates.
Selling Insights outlines the details of the client's current property, any necessary preparations or repairs needed before listing, and their expectations regarding the selling price.
Personal Notes section records relevant family details, important personal dates, client hobbies and interests, and their underlying values or emotional drivers influencing their property decisions.
Recap of Topics & Next Steps summarizes the key discussion points from the meeting and outlines the immediate actions required from both the client and the realtor.
Additional Observations is a section for less critical or repeated information that may be useful for reference but does not require immediate action.
Emojis and checkboxes can be utilized within a CRM to highlight urgency or emotional aspects of client interactions for quick recognition.

name: PROPERTY VISIT WITH CLIENTS
author: Velum
description: Record visit data and impressions. Generates feedback for the seller and next steps for decision-making.
body:
The main objective is to provide a structured form to record feedback from a property visit in Asunción, supporting negotiation with the seller or real estate agent.
The document should begin by identifying the property (address, neighborhood, registration/cadastral number), the date of the visit, and the names of the participants.
It is necessary to record the property specifications, including measurements (land and built area), ceiling height, number of suites, parking spaces, and other rooms.
The form should detail the price and payment conditions, including values in USD, Guaranis, and Reais, price per m2, negotiation margin, financing options, and additional costs such as deed and taxes.
It is necessary to collect observations from the visit, separating the positive points from the disadvantages or reservations of the property.
The form allows recording the buyer's level of interest, ranging from "Strong" to "None".
A general appreciation section evaluates cleanliness, maintenance, attractiveness, conformity with advertisement photos, as well as the perception of the neighborhood and the price.
It is essential to assess the location and surroundings, considering street noise, flood risk, neighborhood safety, and available infrastructure.
It is necessary to list pending documentation to be verified, such as property title, certificate of tax debt clearance, and regularity in Public Registries.
The report concludes with a "Next steps" section to define the subsequent actions, their responsible parties, and respective deadlines.

name: Condominium Owners' Association Assembly
author: Velum
description: Summarize the client call in European Portuguese. Profile, objectives, and next steps; if missing: Not mentioned.
body:
Defines the role of a real estate consultant assistant for Felipe Neves Real Estate, a boutique agency in Portugal serving international buyers, specifically Brazilians, Americans, and Canadians looking to purchase in Lisbon, Comporta, and Margem Sul.
Provides a structured template in European Portuguese to summarize client calls, ensuring all key information is captured concisely and completely, with instructions to write "Não mencionado" if a section lacks information.
The summary structure is divided into ten main sections: CALL SUMMARY for basic call details, CLIENT PROFILE for personal information, PURCHASE OBJECTIVE for buying motivations, PROPERTY PREFERENCES for property specifics, and CONTEXT AND HISTORY for the client's background with the Portuguese market.
It also includes sections for OBJECTIONS AND CONCERNS to track client doubts, PROPERTIES DISCUSSED to log properties reviewed, COMMITMENTS AND NEXT STEPS for action items, and LEAD CLASSIFICATION to categorize client readiness (Hot, Warm, Cold).
The template concludes with sections for PERSONAL NOTES FOR FELIPE to capture soft details about the client's personality and communication style, and IMPORTANT QUOTES to record key client phrases for personalized follow-ups.
Final instructions specify using concise bullet points, professional tone, specific data formats (DD/MM/YYYY, € currency, m2 for area), and to strictly use the Portuguese language for the summary, while avoiding fabrication of information.

name: Professional premises search
author: Velum
description: Paste a survey transcript. Get a structured risk assessment on hazards, fire, security, losses.
body:
The primary purpose is to generate a structured facility risk assessment report by extracting specific information from a transcribed inspection or site survey.
The report requires general information (company name, visit date, author, contact details) and an operational overview (website, years in business, annual receipts, hours, employee count).
The assessment must document common hazards like Electrical, Housekeeping, and Building Maintenance, noting any deficiencies, and detail special hazards including Refrigeration, Flammables, Open Flame Processes, Storage, and Fumigation.
Information on specific equipment such as Generators, Boilers, and Compressors, as well as details on rail access including spur capacity, agreements, and inspection status, must be included.
Fire protection details must be captured, covering the nearest fire department, hydrant counts, and the status of fire systems like detection, sprinklers (contractor, test dates, pump data), and alarm monitoring.
Contingency planning status needs to be recorded, encompassing emergency plans, fire walls, Probable Maximum Loss (PML), and Normal Loss Expectancy (NLE).
Security measures must be described, including alarm systems, monitoring services, personnel, and surveillance.
A loss analysis for Property, Liability, and Auto risks is required, detailing loss type, total incurred, trends, and actions taken.
The status of physical areas under premises liability (driveways, floors, lighting, stairs) must be assessed, and discussions on the fleet and mobile equipment must be captured.

name: ARY LAND CO. | LISTING APPOINTMENT & PROPERTY INTAKE
author: Velum
description: For stagers and agents. Capture visit details, access, rooms, timeline. Outputs a ready report.
body:
This content provides a structured template for a Site Visit Report for Alder & Ash Staging, intended to be filled out using AI recording tools after a site visit.
The report begins by capturing essential contact and property details, including the client, agent, brokerage, and property address.
It outlines logistics for the moving team, covering parking strategies, necessary permits, entry points, and any access constraints like truck size limitations or narrow passages.
Details of the house are to be recorded, such as property type, current condition, key features like flooring and paint, and any specific measurements or constraints.
The template requires identifying all rooms to be staged, categorized into primary focus areas, secondary spaces, flexible spaces, and extra-large spaces.
Design intent is defined by specifying the target demographic, the desired aesthetic or vibe, and the overall strategic goal of the staging.
Key priorities are established by highlighting high-impact areas for maximum effect, addressing problem areas, and considering the competitive market context.
Project timelines are documented, including the completion date for construction or prep work, the target listing date, and the final deadline for staging installation.
Expectations are managed by recording both the client's stated expectations and the commitments made by the staging company.
A final summary section is included for a brief narrative of the visit, key takeaways, and next steps, along with a section to link project assets like photos and floor plans.

name: Director MTG
author: Velum
description: Analyzes negotiation content, extracts customer conditions, and provides specific proposals and improvement measures. It streamlines sales reviews and reporting.
body:
A real estate sales broker records customer interactions with the aim of securing appointments and concluding sales contracts. The sales process proceeds in the order of customer situation hearing, proposal, agreement formation, and appointment setting.
The objectives of sales activity analysis are: 1 factual extraction of customer situations and conditions, 2 concise recording of appointments and future tasks, 3 proposal of sales methods to differentiate from competitors and retain customers, 4 provision of reflections and advice from the customer's perspective when sales activities are deemed to have failed (e.g., inability to secure an appointment).
The output will be presented as a professional sales assistant or personal consultant, in a specialized consulting format.
Hearing content should be described concisely based on facts, and reflections and proposals should be concise, avoiding long sentences, even if based on some inference.
The created summary will be used for both the sales representative's personal activity review and for reporting business activities to their supervisor.
The final deliverable will be in Markdown format, using appropriate hierarchical symbols for headings, and without emojis.

name: Automatic Report Generation for Real Estate Trader Activities
author: Velum
description: Paste a call transcript. Get a concise summary, priorities, concerns, and next steps for your CRM.
body:
The core purpose is to provide a structured template for a real estate CRM assistant to summarize client calls, ensuring all critical information is captured for easy reference and follow-up.
The summary begins with a concise 3-5 sentence Executive Summary capturing the client's identity, motivation, timeline, budget, priorities, and next steps.
A detailed Client Overview section is used to itemize essential client data such as name, client type, property preferences, location, budget, timeline, and key motivators.
The Top Priorities section outlines the client's main objective, non-negotiables, budget range, timing constraints, and urgency level.
The Motivations, Expectations & Concerns section delves into the reasons for the transaction, client expectations of the agent, any anxieties, and relevant past experiences.
Separate Buying Insights and Selling Insights sections are included to detail specific preferences for property type, location, features, condition, and pricing expectations, to be used only if applicable.
A Personal Notes section captures details about the client's family, lifestyle, hobbies, and emotional drivers to help build rapport.
The Recap & Next Steps section summarizes key takeaways and lists actionable to-dos for both the client and the agent, along with a follow-up schedule.
An Additional Observations section is for noting secondary details like client tone or recurring themes, and a Suggested Personal Anecdote provides a conversational touchpoint for the next call.

name: Listing Consultation Summary
author: Velum
description: Make a structured listing consult recap with pricing math and timeline. Includes a client email.
body:
The core purpose is to summarize a listing appointment by gathering specific information across seven key areas and then drafting a follow-up email for the client.
Collect contact information including names, property title holders, property address, moving destination and reasons, and necessary legal documents like death certificates or trust documents.
Document home details such as the number of bedrooms and bathrooms, square footage, architectural style, garage size and type (attached/detached), basement status (finished/unfinished), and the school district.
Compile a list of all home upgrades and identify the key features that would be most appealing to potential buyers for marketing purposes.
Determine a suggested list price, calculate the estimated cost to sell (approximately 8% of the list price), subtract the mortgage balance and selling costs from the list price to estimate the seller's Net Proceeds.
Establish a detailed timeline covering the hiring date, staging, photography/videography, a "coming soon" period, the active listing date, the potential closing date, and the final key turnover to the new buyer.
Provide suggestions for property improvements, mentioning specific key vendors discussed during the meeting and including a link to the preferred vendors page on the company website.
Define the immediate next steps, capture any special notes from the consultation, and draft a summary email for the client focusing on the timeline, next steps, and recommended vendors for pre-listing tasks.

name: Prework condition report - Attachment
author: Velum
description: Summarizes calls with buyers, extracting criteria, finances, and urgency for brokers.
body:
The document defines a structure for analyzing and transcribing a call with a real estate buyer client, with the aim of extracting essential information for property curation.
The analysis should be objective, focused on facts and figures, distinguishing essential ("must-have") from desirable ("nice-to-have") criteria, and presented directly to assist the responsible broker.
The analysis report structure should contain call data, a summary of the client's profile, their current situation, family composition, and daily routine.
It is necessary to detail the client's motivation and urgency for moving, including trigger events and the ideal deadline for completing the purchase.
Property preferences must be specified, covering typology, area, features such as balcony and home office, parking spaces, floor, common areas, and non-negotiable items.
The analysis should record location preferences, including neighborhoods of interest and those discarded, and proximity needs to points such as work, schools, gym, beach, and access roads.
The client's financial conditions need to be mapped, including total budget, payment method, use of FGTS, credit status, and sensitivity to monthly costs such as condominium and IPTU.
The client's preferred buying process, involved decision-makers and influencers, and risks or objections raised during the conversation should be documented.
The structure concludes with the definition of next steps, commitments, suggestions for future contacts, and an analysis of participants' behavior during the call, such as the talk time ratio.

name: market appraisal notes
author: Velum
description: For listing appointments. Input a recording; get property facts, follow-ups, VERIFY items.
body:
The primary purpose is to define a standardized process for analyzing a real estate listing appointment recording, focusing on extracting and organizing specific property information, client intelligence, and strategic details rather than creating a generic meeting summary.
Core extraction rules mandate prioritizing factual property data over conversational filler, never inventing information, preserving exact numbers, and distinguishing between existing facts and discussed possibilities.
The process requires creating separate, detailed records for multiple properties or structures on a single listing and using confidence labels (e.g., CONFIRMED, SELLER STATED, VERIFY) to classify the source and certainty of all information.
The required output format is a structured 25-section report covering an executive summary, client details, a comprehensive property overview, and specific breakdowns for residences, improvements, land, water features, and agricultural or recreational aspects.
The format also details sections for utilities, access, due diligence, inclusions/exclusions, property condition, and location information.
Internal/CRM-only sections are designated for sensitive information, including seller motivation, concerns, pricing discussions, and marketing strategy.
The procedure concludes with sections for mapping intelligence, a consolidated list of items needing verification, a record of commitments made, action items, a CRM data snapshot, and source confidence notes, followed by a final quality control check.

name: Field Sheet v2
author: Velum
description: Turns leasing notes into reports. It extracts budget, NLA, and location to track next steps.
body:
The system instruction outlines a five-part template for a Commercial Real Estate (CRE) Transaction Analyst to process meeting transcripts and generate a structured, actionable summary report for Singapore office leasing transactions.
The "Client's Current Situation" section requires extracting and categorizing the client's current lease details, primary motivation for relocating, specific pain points with their existing premises, and their internal work arrangement and density policies.
The "Requirements & Ideal Scenario" section mandates the extraction of all quantitative and qualitative leasing needs, including office grade, budget range in SGD PSF/month, required Net Lettable Area (NLA), lease term, target handover date, preferred location, and non-negotiable technical specifications.
The "Meeting Minutes" section requires a concise, chronological summary of the meeting's key discussion points, decisions, and clarifications, presented as a factual brief rather than a full transcript.
The "Actionable Items Checklist" section involves creating a structured checklist of next steps for both the agent and the client, detailing the responsible party, the specific action item, and its deadline or current status.
The "AI Suggestions and Analysis" section requires identifying unaddressed commercial topics and ambiguities for clarification, and generating proactive, value-added tasks for the agent based on the client's profile and market context, such as verifying eligibility or preparing financial projections.

name: The Wise Mind Method - Agent Path V1
author: Velum
description: Standardize lead intake by recording buyer motivation, financial status, and property requirements.
body:
This lead intake template is designed to capture comprehensive information about new real estate leads for entry into a CRM, covering contact details, motivation, property search criteria, financial status, and next steps.
The initial section gathers basic lead information, including name, contact details, source, first-time homebuyer status, and current living situation, including whether they need to sell an existing property.
To understand the client's motivation, the template includes fields for their reasons for moving and specific details about their home search, such as desired locations, price range, required features, and any urgency related to their timeline.
The financial readiness section assesses the lead's pre-approval status by collecting information on credit score, income type, down payment savings, potential need for Down Payment Assistance (DPA), and any existing debt.
Timeline and decision-making processes are evaluated by asking for the ideal move date, buying timeframe, flexibility, and identifying all individuals involved in the purchase decision.
A section is dedicated to scheduling a consultation, noting whether an appointment is set, its details (date, time, format), and what is required to confirm it.
The template concludes with a plan for "Next Steps," outlining assigned tasks, follow-up schedules, and assigning a lead status (Hot, Warm, Nurture), along with a space for personal notes to build rapport.

name: Workstation — Tender Pitch Debrief
author: Velum
description: Creates WEG minutes with resolutions and tasks from your transcripts.
body:
The main purpose is to create a legally sound minutes for an owners' meeting according to WEG law, based on the analysis of a transcript.
The metadata of the meeting must be recorded, including date, location, time, inviting management, total number of units, and the determination of attendance and quorum.
The agenda items (TOP) must be fully listed, with legal comments on any deviations or additions to the original invitation.
For each agenda item, a discussion analysis must be carried out, summarizing key points, owners' arguments, mentioned documents, economic and technical implications, and identifiable legal risks.
All passed resolutions must be presented in a legally sound manner, including the exact resolution text, voting results, majority type, responsibilities, budget, cost distribution, legal effects, and timetable.
Topics that were not resolved but postponed or rejected must be documented with justifications and indications of missing information.
A list of tasks and measures must be created, specifying the responsible party, deadline, and priority for each item, and distinguishing between "mandatory tasks for management" and "orders from resolutions."
Financial topics such as the business plan, annual statement, liquidity requirements, reserves, and specific cost items that were discussed must be recorded.
A risk assessment should identify legal, technical, and economic risks, such as contestable resolutions.
The minutes conclusion must include the minute-taker, the place and time of the end of the meeting, and a note on the challenge period according to § 44 WEG.

name: PDX Reno Outside Closer Template
author: Velum
description: Converts notes into formal reports. It organizes damage data and remediation protocols.
body:
The primary task is to generate a formal, structured Fire Damage Remediation Report by extracting specific information from a transcribed property damage inspection text.
The report must identify the cause and origin of the damage, provide a narrative description of the observed damage, detail the impact on building systems like HVAC, and describe the overall property condition including secondary damage like soot spread.
Key information to extract includes findings from sample collection and testing, such as the types and locations of contaminants like Soot and Ash (Carbonaceous Materials).
The generated document should also include any recommendations for further professional evaluations and reference external lab analyses.
The output must follow a strict format: a main title "House Fire", a subtitle "Remediation Protocols and Scope of Work:", and specific bolded property details (Home of, Address, Testing Date, Report Date).
The report structure requires a "Scope of loss:" section detailing the damage and next steps, followed by a numbered and underlined "1. Identification of Biohazards:" section with a "Testing and Sample Collection" subsection.
Biohazard findings must be presented in a numbered list with bolded titles, followed by descriptive paragraphs and a concluding reference to the external lab analysis.
The tone of the report must be formal, objective, and technical, using appropriate industry terminology, and consist of detailed paragraphs rather than simple bullet points.

name: The Fraker Group - Client Call, Mid-Transaction,
author: Velum
description: For call reviews. Enter call facts for a short summary, 7 scores, total /100, and A–F grade.
body:
This document outlines a condensed call grading system for "The Easy Homebuyer" acquisitions team, detailing the scoring, grading scale, and seven key performance categories for evaluating appointments.
A call summary requires a 2-4 sentence overview of the appointment's situation, key facts, and outcome, along with the final score.
The "Property & Motivation Profile" section is for factual capture only, recording what was explicitly stated about the property's condition and the seller's motivation without inference.
The scoring system calculates a total score out of 100 by multiplying a 0-4 score in each of seven categories by a specific weight. Grades range from A (90-100) to F (below 60), with an F grade also resulting from any critical failure.
The seven scored categories are: Rapport & Tactical Empathy (Weight 17), Discovery of property and situation (Weight 17), Competition & Red-Flag Positioning (Weight 17), Negotiation & Numbers (Weight 22), Qualifying & Motivation Scale (Weight 11), Closing & Next Steps (Weight 11), and Tone, Pace & Professionalism (Weight 5).
A scorecard template is provided to record the representative's name, appointment details, reviewer information, and the scores for each of the seven categories.
Bonus points are awarded for directing sellers to the company's website and reviews, while points are deducted for specific failures like not capturing financial details or pressuring the seller, which results in an automatic F grade.

name: To do list
author: Velum
description: Structures your audio notes into diagnostic reports detailing walls, systems, and rooms of the home.
body:
The role is to act as a professional real estate diagnostician to write a structured and visual report from an audio transcription, intended for use in EPC reports or energy audits.
The report must begin with the collection of general property information, including the address, type, floor, year of construction, and surface area.
The analysis of the building envelope requires a detailed description of the composition, insulation, and characteristics of walls, floors, ceilings, roofs, joinery, stairs, floors, and skirting boards.
Technical systems must be evaluated, detailing the type, condition, and specificities of heating, domestic hot water (DHW) production, ventilation, and electricity and gas installations.
A detailed description for each room must be provided following a recurring structure that includes the level, coverings, walls, openings, ceiling, equipment, and observed anomalies.
A technical summary must summarize the general condition of the envelope, joinery, heating and DHW systems, ventilation, and annexes.
The report must include recommendations for priority actions, evaluated according to their energy impact, complexity, and priority.
A section is dedicated to the list of points to check or complete, such as missing documents, unseen rooms, or elements to confirm.
The writing must follow strict rules of non-invention, clarity, and structure, with the aim of producing a directly usable final report.

name: Buyer/Seller Real Estate Consultations
author: Velum
description: Turn property consultations into structured summaries and professional follow-up emails for clients.
body:
High-producing realtor assists buyers, sellers, and investors through weekly or daily consultations.
Consultations focus on discussing client real estate goals and current buying or selling strategies.
Meetings are crucial for coordinating efforts, tracking progress, and ensuring alignment with real estate strategies.
Objective is to generate a clear and concise meeting summary outlining the meeting status, to-do items, and follow-up actions for both the realtor and clients.
The summary should be presented in a professional meeting summary assistant style, similar to a personal secretary's work.
The tone should be professional, concise, and clear, facilitating easy creation of follow-up or recap emails to clients.
The meeting summary is intended for the realtor, their assistant, and clients, including those present and absent, as a reference for their real estate goals.
A client-facing summary should be adaptable for both listing (seller) and buyer consultations.
A professional, friendly recap email should thank clients for their time and trust, summarize goals and discussions, outline clear next steps and action items for both parties, detail listing preparation and marketing timelines with dates, provide a showing setup summary, and offer reassurance about progress towards closing.
The system should include an embedded signature with a photograph and contact information when the "compose email" function is opened.

name: MCST Council Meeting Minutes
author: Velum
description: Review a new-home sales transcript in 5 steps. Get buyer notes, CRM snapshot, and coaching tips.
body:
A standardized evaluation framework uses the five Critical Path steps—Welcome, Discovery, Demonstration, Homesite, and Commitment—to analyze new home sales conversations, record objective buyer data, and deliver constructive sales coaching.
The Welcome phase evaluates initial greeting, rapport building, expectation setting, and buyer personal details to support personalized future follow-ups.
The Discovery phase captures core buying motivations, current home deficiencies, feature priorities, lifestyle goals, budget parameters, financing details, timelines, and decision-maker roles, preserving verbatim buyer phrases where impactful.
The Demonstration phase analyzes presented homes and features, verifying how well product benefits were tied to buyer requirements and tracking specific buyer reactions, objections, and buying signals.
The Homesite phase documents discussions regarding specific lot locations, views, orientation, privacy, maintenance tradeoffs, and unresolved buyer concerns.
The Commitment phase examines closing attempts, buyer responses, handled objections, and outstanding barriers, clearly delineating between full purchase agreements and next-step commitments with assigned action items.
The concluding section synthesizes a CRM-ready buyer snapshot, three evidence-based sales strengths, up to three actionable coaching improvements with sample phrasing, and prioritized next steps aligned with buyer needs.

name: Íris 3P
author: Velum
description: Assists agents by extracting visit preferences. Identifies reactions and generates next steps.
body:
The main objective is to analyze an audio recording of a property visit with a client to extract information that helps the agent improve follow-up and strengthen the relationship.
The context of the analysis is a live audio recording of a property visit with a buyer client, capturing real-time conversations and reactions to identify client points of interest and feelings.
The analysis should extract the property address, what clients liked and disliked, important features, questions, emotional tone, updates to search criteria, personal details for relationship building, three follow-up points, and the speaking time ratio of each participant.
The report style should be clean and insight-focused, acting as an assistant who silently notes important moments and profiles during the visit.
The analysis tone should be welcoming, neutral, and observant, focusing on understanding both the facts and subtleties of the conversation without excessive interpretation.
The summary is intended for the real estate agent themselves, serving as an aid to recall the visit, better understand client preferences, and personalize future interactions.
The response should be structured with specific headings, including address, client likes and dislikes, notable features, questions, criteria updates, relationship insights, points for the next meeting, observations, speaking time ratio, and detailed profiles of each participant with observed evidence.

name: Property valuation
author: Velum
description: Generate video call reports with analyses and action plans for monitoring your franchise.
body:
The goal is to generate a structured and professional meeting report (CR) from the audio recording of videoconferences held by a Mikit franchise network facilitator with their teams.
These videoconferences aim to monitor activity, note progress, identify vigilance points, and transmit methods on topics such as sales performance, management, or sales methodology.
The ultimate objective is to provide the franchisee with an operational document summarizing exchanges, observations, decisions, and recommendations, serving as a reference for monitoring actions and strengthening local management, without requiring reformulation.
The meeting report must be dense, with a minimum of 8,000 characters, while remaining concise, and adopt a fluid, professional, and rigorous style.
The document's structure must use numbered titles in uppercase and bold, complete paragraphs, and bulleted lists with bolded titles for key points.
The tone must be neutral and professional, without familiarity or humor, and the content must be presented factually without inventing missing information.
The target audience is field personnel (franchisees, managers) as well as headquarters, which requires clear, understandable, and usable content in a single reading.
The response must be a structured text without polite formulas, following a strict formatting architecture including specific sections like "Analysis" and "Action Plan," and using the abbreviation "PF" for "Franchise Owner."

name: VHG Agent Template
author: Velum
description: Convert a walkthrough recording to a room-by-room move-in/out report. Ready for review and signature.
body:
The primary goal is to transform an audio recording into a structured rental property inspection report for tenant review, signature, landlord records, and future comparison.
The report must be suitable for on-site tenant walkthroughs, PDF export, Adobe Acrobat Pro signature workflows, landlord record retention, and move-out security deposit comparisons.
The required format includes sections for property details, purpose of inspection, overall condition summary, detailed findings by area, an overall condition rating, and statements for supporting documentation.
Detailed findings should be documented for specific areas: Exterior, Entry, Living Areas, Kitchen, Bathrooms, Bedrooms, Laundry, Garage, Systems, Back Yard/Patio, and any other observed areas, noting condition, issues, and recommended actions for each.
The report must include specific, pre-written text for Tenant Acknowledgment, Audio Recording Acknowledgment, and a 48-hour Follow-Up Window for reporting additional discrepancies.
A signature section for both Landlord and Tenant(s) is required, with provisions for multiple tenants.
Style rules mandate using only factual, professional, and neutral observations from the recording, avoiding speculation, and using specific phrases like "Not specifically discussed" or "No visible issues noted" when applicable.
The final report should conclude with a "READY FOR SIGNATURE REVIEW" paragraph.

name: Walkthrough Inspection Report
author: Velum
description: For property managers. Enter date, address, notes, photos. Get a clear renewal walk-through report.
body:
This document provides a standardized template for creating a Walkthrough Inspection Report for a rental property.
The report title must follow the format: "[Inspection Date] – [Property Address] – Renewal Walk-Through", and basic details like the property address, inspection date, and whether the tenant was present must be recorded.
A brief 2-3 sentence overview describing the general condition of the property is required.
The "Owner Attention Items" section is for highlighting issues that the property owner needs to be aware of for potential repair, replacement, or future budgeting.
The "Observations and Maintenance Items" section is for documenting specific issues, each with a clear description of the location/item and a corresponding photo.
The "Exterior and Grounds" section details observations for the front and rear of the property, covering landscaping, porches, walkways, decks, fences, and including photos where applicable.
The "Tenant Comments / Notes" section is for summarizing any relevant information shared by the tenant, such as maintenance concerns, property condition notes, or safety observations.
"Future Maintenance Recommendations" lists preventative or future maintenance tasks that could be done after the tenant vacates or during the next maintenance cycle.
The "Action Items / Next Steps" section uses a checklist format to list required tasks and assign responsible parties.

name: Site Inspection for Real Estate Valuation Expert
author: Velum
description: Converts inspection notes into structured professional reports for real estate.
body:
The instruction serves to structure the summary of a site inspection for real estate valuation, using factual, appraisal-like language and consistently employing the term “valuation object”.
The location description should be written as continuous text and include the access situation, street character, surrounding development, residential environment, and a general location assessment, with plausible additions for missing typical information.
The property description is in bullet form and covers size, cut, topography, soil conditions, development, fences, and outdoor facilities; if information is missing, “no information” should be noted.
The building description includes bullet points on the year of construction, major renovations, floor plan quality, lighting, defects, building type, number of floors, basement, and details on components such as walls, roof, windows, ceilings, stairs, sanitary and heating systems.
The energy status of the building should be assessed based on the inspection, allowing for interpretive classification.
Outbuildings, parking spaces, and garages are to be recorded in bullet form by type, condition, and number, including any special peculiarities.
The outdoor facilities are described in bullet points, including garden areas, terraces, paths, fences, and any special features or damages.
Valuation-specific notes such as economic obsolescence, maintenance backlog, unusual floor plans, or other value-influencing peculiarities are to be recorded in bullet points.

name: TEA - HSD - Presenting to a Failed House Seller
author: Velum
description: From team voice memos, produce address-based notes and explicit tasks only. Flags unclear outcomes.
body:
The primary purpose is to define a system for processing a real estate team lead's voice memos, categorizing them, and extracting structured notes and explicit tasks.
A core rule is to default to creating notes for observations, prices, or commentary, and only create a task when an explicit action is stated using specific trigger phrases like "I need to" or "send".
When creating tasks, do not assign a person or due date unless explicitly named in the memo, and categorize ambiguous items as notes to avoid inventing details.
For handling property addresses, anchor all information to the address stated at the beginning of a showing, and mark any ambiguous addresses for confirmation to prevent misattributing details.
For "Quick Notes / Property Walk-through" memos, extract the address or subject, list observations or prices under "NOTES", and list explicit action items under "TASKS" with assigned person, category, and due date if mentioned.
For "Client Viewing Feedback" memos, always generate a "Follow-up Boss note" summarizing the client, property, viewing date, outcome, reasons, and any requested documents or changes in criteria, noting if the outcome was not stated.
For "Full Buyer/Seller Meeting" memos, create a "Follow-up Boss note" for the summary and next steps, generate "Todoist Tasks" only for explicit actions, and log any changes to client criteria under "Criteria Updates" for Dawn.

name: Real Estate Buyer Discovery
author: Velum
description: Structures buyer calls. Extracts budget, sector, and criteria to organize client follow-up.
body:
The main objective is to synthesize information from a first phone contact with a real estate buyer, focusing on their profile and search, after obtaining their consent for the call recording.
It is necessary to identify the client's profile, particularly whether they are an investor or looking for a primary residence, their place of residence, their age, and the composition of their family, including the age and first name of children.
It is necessary to understand the reasons motivating the client's real estate project.
The budget must be defined by specifying the maximum amount (with or without notary fees) and the ideal budget.
The client's progress in their financing study must be clarified, including budget validation by a financial institution and the amount of their personal contribution.
The search must be targeted to specific geographic areas, such as cities or neighborhoods, taking into account the need for proximity to essential services.
The characteristics of the desired property must be synthesized and prioritized, including the type of property, surface area, number of rooms, presence of an outdoor space, as well as important and deal-breaking criteria for the client.
It is important to summarize the urgency of the acquisition project.
If the conversation concerns a specific advertisement, a summary of this exchange must be included.
The next steps agreed with the client must be synthesized to ensure follow-up.

name: Customer Service Template
author: Velum
description: Help agents turn inspection notes into reports. Organizes room data, issues, and property details.
body:
The primary purpose is to generate a comprehensive summary report from a recorded agent visual inspection (AVID).
The report header must include the Date, Time, Weather Conditions, Property Address, and People Present.
Observations should be organized by room type, distinguishing multiple rooms of the same type (e.g., Bedroom 1, Bedroom 2).
"Primary Bedroom" and "Master Bedroom" are to be used interchangeably, as are "Primary Bathroom" and "Master Bathroom".
Each room summary must include Condition/Features, Issues/Concerns, Measurements/Size, Notable Features, and Recommendations.
Common room categories to watch for include Primary/Master Bedroom, Bedrooms, Bathrooms, hallway/stairs, loft/den, Kitchen, Living Room, Family Room, Dining Room, Office/Study, Laundry Room, Garage, Basement, Attic, Exterior/Outdoor Areas, Utility Room, Pantry, and Closets.
Reports must begin with the header information, list rooms in a logical order, and consolidate all comments for a room into a single section.
The report should use clear, professional language, maintain specific terminology from the inspection, and include exact figures for measurements when provided.
Additional instructions include capturing overall property impressions, noting comparisons between rooms, including relevant client interactions, flagging urgent issues or safety concerns, and preserving pricing discussions or market observations.

name: Daily Standup
author: Velum
description: Review listing recordings to assess agent style, persuasion, and closing for training purposes.
body:
The primary request is to analyze a real estate agent's listing presentation recording, breaking down its structure, delivery, persuasive elements, closing, and overall effectiveness into a structured outline for training purposes.
Analyze the presentation's structure, including how the agenda was set, the flow of topics from introduction to paperwork, the use of visual materials like marketing calendars, and how transitions between subjects were managed.
Evaluate the agent's delivery and communication style, focusing on tone, pacing, confidence, the balance of listening versus talking, the use of stories or case studies, and the clarity of explanations for complex details like fees or sale methods.
Assess persuasive and relationship-building elements by examining how the agent established credibility, aligned the marketing plan with client goals, handled objections about commission or sale method, and used techniques to create urgency or exclusivity.
Examine the closing process, including how the agent signaled the conclusion, the strength of the call to action for signing agreements or booking photography, the handling of final questions, and whether they confidently asked for the business.
Provide an overall impression of effectiveness by identifying key strengths, areas for improvement in building trust or urgency, and the overall persuasiveness of the pitch and the likelihood of the vendor signing.

name: Condominium meeting minutes
author: Velum
description: Organizes discussions and votes into orderly drafts. Structures the points covered for the minutes.
body:
The objective is to generate a draft text from a recording that clearly, orderly, and faithfully describes the conduct of a condominium meeting and the contents discussed at each point on the Agenda, in order to prepare the official minutes.
The Agenda includes the approval of the 2024/2025 financial statements, the appointment of the administrator and counselors, the approval of amounts for the 2025/2026 budget and the replacement of a tree, communications on the liquidation of F.lli Cutrone Estintori and the takeover by Altair S.p.A., and miscellaneous.
The drafting guidelines require professional and clear language in the present tense, the absence of personal interpretations, the consistent use of the denomination "the Administration", and the indication of missing data with [DATA NOT AVAILABLE].
Participants' interventions must be assigned to the Agenda point indicated in the recording, maintaining the original sequence without arbitrary reorganizations.
For each Agenda point, the structure to be produced must include a summary of the discussion, the decisions or determinations emerged (or the wording [NO FORMALIZED DECISION]), and the voting results (or [DATA NOT AVAILABLE]).
A final "Activity Summary" section is required, which synthetically lists the deliberated activities or open issues, specifying the reference Agenda point and any responsible parties or deadlines.

name: Critical Path - NHC
author: Velum
description: Convert tour/call transcripts into a showing card. Capture intent, reactions, objections, next steps.
body:
The primary task is to act as an AI assistant that generates a structured summary, called a "NAV SHOWING CARD", from transcribed real estate client interactions.
The summary must start with the main title "NAV SHOWING CARD" and include a "General Information" section detailing the meeting type, date, property address, MLS, price, clients present, and client type.
An "INTENT" section must be created to capture what the client wants, their timing, must-haves, deal-breakers, stated budget/financing, and current home status.
A "PROPERTY REACTIONS" section is required to log client feedback for each property, using a specific format that includes whether they love, like, or dislike it and the reason.
The summary needs an "OBJECTIONS" section to list any client objections and a "COMMITMENTS" section to document promises made by both the agent ("Nick") and the client, along with the next steps and preferred follow-up method.
A "RISK" section must be included to flag potential issues such as a missing partner, lack of pre-approval, or unrealistic price expectations.
The summary concludes with a "QUOTES WORTH KEEPING" section for memorable direct quotes from the interaction.
All section titles must be in all capital letters and separated by a blank line, with the final output being a concise, fill-in-the-blanks style report strictly adhering to the specified structure.

name: real estate pro
author: Velum
description: For agents. Converts transcripts into reports with budgets, requirements, and clear action items.
body:
The primary task is for a Commercial Real Estate (CRE) broker AI to process a client meeting transcript and generate a structured, five-section summary report for the Singapore office leasing market.
The initial step involves extracting the client's current situation, including their premises status (lease expiry, NLA, rent), primary motivations for moving (expansion, cost-saving, branding), and specific pain points with their existing office.
The leasing brief must detail all client requirements, such as the desired office grade, budget range in Price Per Square Foot (PSF), required Net Lettable Area (NLA) and headcount, preferred lease term, target handover date, location preferences, and any non-negotiable technical specifications.
A concise, chronological summary of the meeting's key discussion points, decisions made, and clarifications sought should be provided, focusing on factual information rather than a full transcription.
An actionable items checklist is required, assigning specific next steps to both the agent and the client, complete with target completion dates or current status for each task.
The AI should provide analysis and suggestions, identifying gaps in the discussion (like fit-out costs or security deposit), ambiguities that need clarification (budget inclusivity, approval timelines), and proactive actions for the agent based on the client’s profile.

name: CRE Broker / Investor Meetings
author: Velum
description: Paste a call transcript; get a clean summary, next-step script, sales plan, and 10-day follow-ups.
body:
The primary role is to act as a systems analyst and personal assistant for a real estate agent, processing call or meeting transcripts to produce structured, actionable outputs.
Outputs must be generated in the same language as the input transcript, with a natural, business-conversational tone, avoiding AI clichés, and using short hyphens.
The system must always produce four specific blocks: a "Traffic-Light Summary" detailing client info and needs, a "Next-Contact Script" for the subsequent interaction, a "Sales Algorithm for the Next Step" defining the deal stage and required actions, and a "10-Day Follow-Up Chain".
The "Traffic-Light Summary" captures the client's name and role, their main concerns and requests, budget and terms, their current situation, and agreed-upon next steps.
The "Next-Contact Script" provides a structured guide for the next call or meeting, including an opening, key questions, supporting arguments, objection handling, and a closing action proposal.
The "Sales Algorithm for the Next Step" clarifies the deal's position in the sales funnel, the primary communication focus, and a specific list of materials to be sent to the client.
A "10-Day Follow-Up Chain" consists of ten distinct daily messages for messengers, designed to be copied easily, blending emotional and rational appeals to prompt a decision, with a predefined theme for each day.

name: Seller Prequal Call - LPTMAMA Listing
author: Velum
description: For rural experts. Organizes interviews into technical reports. Helps check data and finances.
body: The main role is to act as a technical appraiser specialized in rural properties, following ABNT standards, to process field interview transcripts, extract information, structure it into a predefined report model, and validate data to ensure appraisal accuracy. * The first step of the appraisal process consists of identifying the property and the visit, recording the date, time, interviewee's name, presented documents, location coordinates, and information about access and strategic distances. * The general characterization of the property involves recording the total area (documented and informed), boundaries, land situation (registration, georeferencing, possession), and rural zoning or permitted use, if mentioned. * It is necessary to detail the current use of the property, specifying productive activities and the approximate percentages of land use, such as agricultural areas, pastures, legal reserve, APP, degraded areas, and internal infrastructure. * The analysis of bare land requires a physical and agronomic diagnosis, including the identification of soil types, drainage, relief, agricultural aptitude, and the presence of environmental risks. * Improvements and infrastructures, such as the main house, sheds, and fences, must be detailed individually with their purpose, approximate year, area, construction type, state of conservation, and relevant observations. * For machinery, equipment, and vehicles, it is necessary to record the make/model, year, hours of use, state of conservation, and the availability of the invoice for each item. * Environmental aspects to be surveyed include the situation of Permanent Preservation Area (APP), Legal Reserve, the presence of springs and water bodies, as well as environmental liabilities, embargoes, or existing fines. * Productive and operational indicators must be collected, such as average productivities, relevant costs, employed technologies, and operational bottlenecks reported by the interviewee. * The farm's financial information is crucial for valuation and must be organized into debt structure, reported operational flow (revenues, costs, risks), and existing contracts such as leases or partnerships. * It is necessary to record market information, such as previous purchase proposals, the owner's value expectations, and their expansion forecasts for agricultural or livestock activity. * In specific cases of expropriation or easement, the affected area, affected improvements, operational losses, and the impact on the remaining area of the property must be documented. * The system must automatically generate a list of all mentioned elements that require photographic records to compose the appraisal report. * A section for "Inconsistencies / Information to Confirm" must be automatically created to record imprecise values, inconsistent areas, incomplete dates, or any missing data. * The process includes automatic validations, such as highlighting missing data, standardizing units of measure for hectares and m2, converting dates to DD/MM/YYYY format, listing documentary discrepancies, and recommending review in case of logical inconsistencies.

name: Detailed Room Condition Report
author: Velum
description: Transforms transcripts into structured minutes with agreements, votes, and tasks for communities.
body:
The objective is to draft a formal, detailed, and professional minutes of an Owners' Meeting, accurately extracting the content from a transcript, maintaining an objective tone, and eliminating irrelevant information.
The minutes must begin with the meeting data: location, full date, start and end times, and the list of attendees or a mention of the list of those convened.
The development of the meeting is structured according to the agenda, detailing the budget approval with figures and votes, the incident report with its improvement proposals, and any modifications to the internal regulations.
The election or renewal of positions must be recorded, indicating the method and result, as well as any other matter discussed within the agenda along with the associated decisions and actions.
Any topic, complaint, or proposal raised outside the agenda must be included in the "Requests and questions" section, along with the corresponding answers and decisions, even if this point is not explicitly mentioned in the meeting.
For each agenda item, the agreed actions, concrete tasks to be carried out, whether follow-up is needed, and the exact result of the votes held must be specified.
The final document must use formal and precise language, be divided into clear sections, include all relevant details without omission, and record the exact results of the votes.

name: Punch List
author: Velum
description: For inspectors and site leads. Input notes to get tasks with owners and due dates. Highlights gaps.
body:
Punch List
