name: Project Hand Off
author: Velum
description: Create bulleted hand-off lists. Tracks project specs, timelines, and customer expectations.
body:
The primary purpose is to create a concise, bulleted hand-off document to transfer key project information from sales to the production team, ensuring alignment on customer expectations and project specifics.
Document all promises made regarding the work to be performed.
Identify and note what is most important to the customer for the project.
List any customer concerns and the corresponding solutions that were proposed.
Specify paint details, including the color, sheen, and brand where applicable.
Detail which tasks and promises are to be completed in specific rooms or areas.
Record any verbal agreements or discussions that were not included in the final contract.
Note potential upsell or add-on items that interested the customer but were not contracted.
Provide the customer's name, contact information, and their preferred communication method.
Include details about any pets, their names, and the agreed-upon handling procedures during the project.
State the agreed-upon project timeline.
Describe any parking arrangements that have been made.
Document any observed customer agitation or remaining concerns.

name: Template for Meeting Minutes of Custom-Built Home Discussions with Clients
author: Velum
description: Extracts specifications and decision items from conversations to create detailed meeting minutes that organize agreed contents and pending tasks, preventing misunderstandings.
body:
Subject: [Property Name] Residence New Construction Meeting Minutes
Date and Time: [Insert meeting date and time]
Location: [Insert meeting location]
Attendees: List all attendees identified from the transcript, including names and roles
Summary of Decisions Made Today: Concisely list any items that were finally "decided" in this meeting.
Design Foundation:
Lifestyle Analysis: Record details about daily routines, future projections, hobbies and possessions, relationships and visitors.
Design Concept: Record the overall design taste and image sharing using mood boards, etc.
Zoning and Flow Planning: Record the arrangement of public, private, and service zones, separation and efficiency of household, return, and guest flows, and consideration of circulation flows.
LDK (Living, Dining, Kitchen):
LDK Layout: Record principles such as furniture-first, securing passage widths, overall shape of LDK, TV placement, and focal points.
Kitchen: Record kitchen layout, counter height, counter material, shape of facing counter, and task-based simulation.
Room Details:
Entrance: Record storage planning, flow (consideration of walk-through shoe closet), and flooring (tiles).
Bedrooms & Private Spaces: Record bed placement, storage (comparison of walk-in closet and wall closet), flexibility of children's rooms, and consideration for acoustics.
Bathroom & Washroom: Record bathroom type (comparison of unit bath and custom bath), washroom storage (floating storage and storage behind three-sided mirror).
Toilet: Record selection of hand wash basin (necessity of separate basin when using tankless toilet), placement, and storage.
Electrical, Lighting, Finishes:
Lighting Plan: Record basic policy (multi-light per room), light layers, room-specific notes, adoption of dimmers and motion sensors.
Outlet & Switch Plan: Record number and location of outlets based on furniture placement and activities, switch locations considering living flows, adoption of 3-way/4-way switches.
Finishes: Record flooring (comparison of solid wood and engineered flooring), wall/ceiling materials (comparison of vinyl wallpaper, plaster, paint), accent wallpaper, interior doors, window types and functionality, window treatment selection, and confirmation of area effect.
Process Management:
Specifications and Cost: Record understanding of "standard specifications" and "optional specifications", and outlook on optional costs.
Decision Timeline: Record confirmation of decision timing.
Meeting Progress: Record use of master checklist.
Tasks/Homework for Next Time:
Client Side: Record things to decide or confirm by next meeting.
Builder Side: Record materials, estimates, drawings to prepare by next meeting.

name: Comprehensive technical Meeting Minutes & Action Tracker
author: Velum
description: Paste transcript. Output minutes with topics, decisions, risks, and action items with owners and dates.
body:
The primary objective is to create comprehensive, technically accurate meeting minutes from a full transcript, ensuring all key information like participants, discussions, decisions, and action items are captured for anyone who did not attend.
Essential meeting information to be captured includes title, date, time, duration, location, project, meeting type, participants, their roles, and the purpose of the meeting.
An executive summary must provide a concise overview of the meeting's purpose, key topics, major technical findings, significant issues, decisions, commitments, critical actions, and the overall outcome for management.
A detailed record of participants and their contributions is required, including their name, role, primary inputs, questions, recommendations, commitments, and assigned tasks, using generic identifiers like "Speaker 1" if a name is unknown.
The meeting minutes must feature a chronological index of all substantial discussion topics and subtopics discussed.
Each discussion topic requires a detailed chronological summary, including participants, timing, a full discussion summary, specific technical details with exact values, questions and answers, identified problems, decisions made, action items, and any required follow-up.
A consolidated reference section for all important technical data mentioned during the meeting must be created, often in a tabular format, preserving exact values and flagging any inconsistencies.
A Decision Log must be maintained in a table format to track all decisions, approvals, rejections, and changes in direction, clearly distinguishing them from mere suggestions.
An Action Item Master Tracker is required to compile all assigned tasks and commitments from the meeting into a comprehensive table, detailing the action, owner, deadline, and status.
A "To-Do List by Responsible Person" organizes all outstanding tasks by individual, making it easy for participants to see their personal action items.
A log of all problems, risks, and concerns raised during the meeting must be created, detailing the issue, who raised it, its impact, status, and proposed resolution.
A list of all open questions and unresolved items must be documented, specifying the issue, its context, the responsible party, information needed, and next steps.
All deadlines and important dates mentioned, such as for tasks, tests, or meetings, must be listed chronologically in a dedicated section.
The document should summarize the immediate, short-term, and long-term next steps that are explicitly supported by the meeting transcript.
Details for the next meeting, including date, time, purpose, and expected attendees, should be recorded, or marked as "Not Scheduled" if not established.
A list of all referenced documents, drawings, specifications, or other materials mentioned during the meeting must be compiled.
Particularly important direct quotes that convey commitments, approvals, or critical technical conclusions should be captured verbatim with the speaker identified.
The general team sentiment and meeting dynamics, such as tone and areas of agreement or disagreement, should be briefly noted only if clearly supported by the transcript.
The process concludes with a summary of the final meeting outcome, highlighting major decisions, the most critical outstanding issue, the highest-priority action, and the next major milestone.
A strict set of accuracy rules mandates analyzing the complete transcript, never inventing information, using markers like [UNCLEAR] or [NOT PROVIDED] for missing data, preserving exact technical values, and distinguishing facts from suggestions.

name: Electrical Estimate Walk-Through
author: Velum
description: Paste an electrical walkthrough transcript. Get scope items, site logistics, decisions, and follow-ups.
body:
This document provides a structured framework for analyzing an onsite electrical estimate walkthrough, aimed at organizing information for efficient estimate preparation, scheduling, and technician briefing.
A Project Summary should be a 2-4 paragraph narrative covering the client's request, project goals, existing conditions, key decisions, major concerns, and overall project impression to provide quick context later.
Estimate Scope Items are the primary output, where each task (installation, repair, etc.) is a distinct bullet point similar to an estimate line item, including details like quantity, location, equipment type, and client preferences.
Existing Conditions that might affect estimating or installation, such as finished vs unfinished spaces, attic access, or foundation type, should be listed to inform labor and pricing.
Site Logistics relevant to the project, like the home being occupied, parking, pets, or scheduling restrictions, need to be summarized.
A dedicated list should be created for only those materials or equipment the homeowner has confirmed they will provide, such as fixtures or appliances.
Material Decisions Pending requires a list of selections or specifications still needed before estimation or installation can proceed, like fixture models, finishes, or color temperatures.
Field Notes should be created as copy-ready instructions for the performing electrician, including details on wire paths, access points, and specific client requests to ensure efficient work.
Office Notes are for administrative tasks, including estimate follow-up, permit considerations, material ordering reminders, and any communication promised to the client.
A Decisions Made section should be split into two lists: "Confirmed" for finalized decisions and "Pending" for unresolved items that need further clarification.
Additional Scope Opportunities discussed during the walkthrough, such as surge protection or panel upgrades, should be identified to be offered as separate estimate options.
A Follow-Up Items list should be categorized into Office, Field, and Client actions, detailing administrative tasks, technical verifications, and information required from the client.
Unresolved Questions that could impact pricing, scheduling, installation, materials, or scope should be listed as direct questions.
The formatting rules require omitting empty sections, using concise bullet points, preserving technical details, and separating narrative from actionable information to create documentation that requires minimal editing.

name: Managed Repair TPA: Initial Inspection – Scope Comment & Narrative Build
author: Velum
description: Turns an inspection recording into an estimate-ready scope and damage breakdown. Flags items to verify.
body:
The primary objective is to create a professional, clean repair estimate scope summary based on an inspection recording, formatted for use in insurance repair software like Xactimate.
A "REPAIR ESTIMATE SCOPE SUMMARY" must be generated, beginning with a summary of the cause and date of loss, followed by a list of all affected exterior and interior areas.
The summary must document any potential coverage issues or unusual circumstances, such as pre-existing damage or access limitations, using neutral language without making coverage decisions.
It is required to state if flooring was affected, specifying the type, location, damage, and whether an ITEL sample was collected or is pending for any flooring being replaced.
The report must identify any potential for subrogation related to failures or third-party damage, and if none is noted, this should be explicitly stated.
A detailed justification for Overhead and Profit (O&P) should be provided if it's included, detailing the number of trades and complexity; otherwise, its absence should be noted.
Similarly, the need for labor minimums must be explained if applied, citing reasons like small, isolated repairs; if not mentioned, this should be stated.
The summary needs to include any stated information on the age, condition, and potential depreciation of materials like roofing or flooring, without assigning specific percentages unless provided.
Potential permit requirements for structural, electrical, plumbing, or other major work must be noted, with a default statement to verify with the local jurisdiction if not discussed.
The need for Additional Living Expense (ALE) due to unsafe conditions or loss of essential facilities should be stated; if not discussed, its status as unconfirmed must be recorded.
Following the summary, a "DAMAGE BREAKDOWN" section must organize observed damages, first for the exterior (Roof, Elevations, Other Structures) and then for the interior, listed by room.
Within each interior room, damages must be categorized under "CEILING," "WALLS," "FLOORS," and "MISCELLANEOUS" for items like trim, fixtures, and cleaning.
A separate "SPECIALTY ITEMS" section is required to list specific repairs such as plumbing, HVAC, roofing, and cabinets.
A final "ITEMS TO VERIFY" list must be created to document all missing, unclear, or unresolved information needed for the final estimate, such as measurements, material types, and permit requirements.

name: Ironworker Interview
author: Velum
description: Convert walkthrough transcripts into an HVAC estimate report, without contact info. Keeps key specs.
body:
The primary purpose is to define a standardized template for an HVAC technician to structure a report from an audio transcript of a site walkthrough for an AC replacement estimate.
The report begins by identifying the job through a reference ID and general location, without including personal client details.
Client concerns are documented, covering the reason for replacement, specific issues like hot spots or high bills, brand preferences, and performance of the current system in maintaining temperature and comfort, as well as interest in air quality or humidity control.
The existing thermostat's brand, type (compatibility with heat pump, Wi-Fi, multi-stage), blower motor condition, and wire count are recorded.
A section is dedicated to noting the need for new supplies like boots or grilles and listing the sizes of all existing returns.
Details for the air handler are captured, including its brand, tonnage, age, orientation, location, leak status, heat strip rating, access details, and various dimensions, along with a checklist for parts to be replaced.
The attic's conditioned area square footage, existing insulation type and depth, baffle status, and whether removal is required are assessed.
The outdoor condenser or heat pump unit is detailed, covering its brand, tonnage, age, type, leak status, refrigerant type, line set sizes, thermostat wire condition, and required hardware like a hurricane pad or rack.
The electrical breaker panel's brand and the amperage ratings for the condenser, air handler, and other related components are to be specified.
A summary of the client's reactions to discussions about optional add-ons like surge protection, corrosion coatings, extended labor agreements, and insulation is required.
A specific list of all optional upgrades the client has agreed to, such as surge protection, coastal coating, or a whole-house filter, must be documented.
A checklist of all required installation materials mentioned during the walkthrough is to be compiled, including items like pans, hang kits, sensors, and drain lines.
A final section for general field notes captures operational details such as access issues, scheduling constraints, pricing discussions, competitor information, or site hazards.
The template concludes with a mandatory photo checklist for the technician, specifying required pictures of the thermostat, air handler, attic insulation, condenser, and breaker panel.

name: Performance Review
author: Velum
description: Paste a remodel walkthrough. Get a scope report with requests, conditions, sizes, and verify items.
body:
This document provides a comprehensive template for converting a narrated customer walkthrough into a structured Residential Remodel Scope Report for WestIron Construction's estimators.
The core reporting rules require acting as an experienced residential construction estimator, emphasizing accuracy by capturing all relevant details, using professional terminology, and never inventing or assuming information.
A specific set of scope statuses must be assigned to each item, including CONFIRMED REQUEST, EXISTING CONDITION, DISCUSSION / CONSIDERATION, POTENTIAL SCOPE, VERIFY, and EXCLUDED, to clarify the nature of each work item.
The report structure begins with a Project Overview section to capture basic project information, a summary, primary goals, and a major scope glance.
A section on Customer Goals, Priorities & Expectations details must-haves, nice-to-haves, concerns, design preferences, functional goals, and any discussed budget or timeline information.
The template requires documenting Existing Property Conditions, covering the property type, construction details, systems, and any observed problems like water damage or structural issues.
The main body of the report organizes the project scope into construction divisions (General Requirements, Site Work, Concrete, etc.), detailing confirmed scope, existing conditions, materials, dimensions, potential scope, items to verify, and exclusions for each applicable division.
A Room-by-Room Scope section breaks down the project by physical location, specifying the existing conditions, customer requests, scope of work, materials, dimensions, trade impacts, and verification needs for each area.
Consolidated lists for Dimensions & Quantities, Materials & Selections, and Permit/Engineering/Code Items are required to provide quick reference points for the estimator.
The report must clarify responsibilities by creating separate lists for Customer-Supplied vs. WestIron-Supplied items and explicitly documenting any Scope Exclusions.
A prioritized list of Estimator Open Items, a set of Customer Questions to clarify scope, and a summary of Estimating Risks/Unknown Conditions must be generated to guide the proposal process.
Project Logistics, such as schedule, site access, and working hours, must be documented, along with any technical issues found in the original walkthrough recording.
A final Estimator Snapshot provides a high-level summary of the project's key aspects and a concluding statement on whether the project is ready for estimating or requires further information.

name: test Mobula6
author: Velum
description: Paste a field recording. Get a report with tasks, dates, money, and risks. Keeps projects separate.
body:
Defines an AI Construction Management Assistant role for A&R Exteriors LLC in Wichita, Kansas to convert work-related recordings into accurate, detailed, organized, actionable reports across roofing and exterior construction operations.
Requires English-only outputs with accurate Spanish-to-English translation while preserving original Spanish transcript when available, speaker identification, extraction of dates/times/locations/prices/measurements/commitments/quotes, strict non-fabrication, clear labeling of facts vs estimates vs suggestions vs pending approvals vs AI recommendations, and flagging unclear information while separating unrelated customers and projects.
Specifies “Recording Overview” outputs including a descriptive title, recording date/time, location, participants, customers/projects discussed, recording type, priority, and identification of included activities such as inspections, customer meetings, insurance claims, jobsite visits, crew management, supplier visits, sales leads, and financial discussions.
Specifies an “Executive Summary” capturing what happened, who was involved, discussions, decisions, accomplishments, concerns, commitments, and next steps, with chronological organization by customer/project for full-day recordings.
Specifies “Customer & Lead Information” extraction including customer identities and contact details, addresses, referral sources, requested services, property details, preferences, concerns, contact commitments, identification of casually mentioned new leads, and documentation of missing info with recommended follow-up, kept as separate customer records.
Specifies “Inspections & Technical Details” capture for roofing and other trades, including measurements and components (SQ/ft2, pitch, waste, ridge/hips/valleys/eaves/rakes/drip edge), materials and shingle type, decking/flashing/penetrations/ventilation, observed damage and issues, suspected causes, repair recommendations, and code/manufacturer concerns requiring verification.
Specifies “Jobsite Progress & Crews” documentation including completed and in-progress work, remaining tasks, quality/deficiencies, cleanliness and safety hazards, crew assignments and subcontractor instructions, pace and delays, materials required, estimated completion dates, corrective actions with responsible personnel and urgency, and English preservation of Spanish-speaking crew technical instructions.
Specifies “Insurance Claims” extraction including carrier, claim number, adjuster, date of loss, inspection results, approved/denied/disputed items, supplements, documentation needs, code concerns, RCV, ACV, depreciation, deductible, payments, and next steps, distinguishing confirmed coverage from contractor recommendations and identifying scope review opportunities.
Specifies “Estimates, Materials & Finances” capture including scope, quantities, unit costs, quoted totals, Good/Better/Best options, exclusions, warranties, approvals, deposits/balances/invoices/payment methods, additional costs and change orders, and supplier details (vendor/rep/product/manufacturer/color/quantity/pricing/availability/substitutions/order status/delivery dates/shortages) while distinguishing quotes vs purchases and proposed vs approved changes.
Specifies “Conversations, Decisions & Commitments” summarization including key Q&A, disagreements, concerns, expectations, decisions and decision-makers, reasoning, verbal promises, significant attributed quotes, pending approvals, unanswered questions, and potential misunderstandings.
Specifies “Action Items & Follow-Ups” requiring extraction of every work-related task with customer/project, responsible person, priority, deadline, and status (Completed/Pending/Proposed/Needs Approval), organized by urgency, consolidated for duplicates, and prohibiting invented deadlines or unconfirmed completion.
Specifies “Calendar & Scheduling” extraction of events with date/time/location/participants/purpose/prep and confirmed vs tentative status, America/Chicago timezone guidance for Kansas events, flags for missing details, Google Calendar-friendly formatting, and prohibition on claiming automatic event creation.
Specifies “Risks, Missed Details & Opportunities” identification including unclear instructions, missing measurements, contradictions, cost overruns, safety issues, delays, dissatisfaction, payment concerns, warranty exposure, leads and upsell opportunities, missing approvals, and follow-up commitments, separating recorded facts from AI observations with suggested verification steps.
Specifies “A&R Job Tracker Updates” per project including customer/address/job type/lead source/status/amounts/payments/balance/materials/crews/start-completion dates/next appointment/pending tasks and supported recommended status changes using defined pipeline labels.
Specifies “Documents & Customer Communication” identification of needed paperwork (estimates, contracts, photo reports, material lists, change orders, invoices, receipts, supplements, warranties, completion documents) and drafting of a concise professional customer follow-up email when appropriate while excluding internal/confidential details.
Specifies “Daily Productivity & Management Insights” capturing completed inspections/estimates/contacts/meetings/orders/payments/coordination/problems resolved/new leads, separating accomplished vs planned work, and suggesting operational improvements only when supported by the recording.
Requires a “Final A&R Field Brief” quick-reference including what happened, what got done, top priorities, customers to contact, crews/materials coordination, money/insurance follow-ups, upcoming appointments/deadlines, red flags, and the next most important action.
Enforces final constraints for mixed/full-day recordings including separation by customer/project, chronological order, consolidation of duplicate tasks, preservation of decision changes, one master action list, Spanish translation to English, strict non-fabrication, accuracy/completeness over brevity, and no claims of external system updates without confirmation.

name: Final Measure 8.27.25
author: Velum
description: For HVAC techs: paste a job recording to get a sectioned estimate walkthrough plus photo checklist.
body:
The primary purpose is to provide a structured template for summarizing an HVAC estimate walkthrough recording, ensuring all critical information is captured in a specific order that mirrors the technician's physical inspection process.
CLIENT INFO: Document the client's full name, address details (including apartment/suite, city, state, zip), primary and alternate phone numbers, and email address.
CONCERNS (intake interview): Record the main reason for system replacement, specific issues to be resolved, any special requirements for the new system, whether the current system maintains temperature year-round, comfort levels at night, and interest in improved humidity control or indoor air quality.
THERMOSTAT: Note the thermostat's brand, whether it's for a heat pump, has Wi-Fi, is multi-stage, the condition of the blower motor, and the number of wires.
RETURNS & SUPPLIES: Detail the supplies needed and list the size of each return mentioned.
AIR HANDLER: Document the brand, tonnage, age, presence of leaks, heat strip details, orientation, location, attic access method (ladder, light kit), flooring, dimensions of the air handler and its closet, and whether to replace the disconnect, whip, drain, pan, hang kit, along with coffin box dimensions.
INSULATION: State the conditioned square footage, the type and depth of existing insulation, the presence of baffles, and whether existing insulation needs removal.
CONDENSER: Record the brand, tonnage, age, heat pump status, leak presence, refrigerant type, need for manual recovery, sizes of copper lines (suction/liquid), T-stat wire condition, and requirements for a hurricane pad, rack, disconnect, and whip.
BREAKER PANEL: List the panel brand and the breaker sizes for the condenser, air handler, dehumidifier, and furnace.
DISCUSSION POINTS: Note the client's reaction if surge protection, coastal/anti-corrosion coating, extended labor agreements, whole-house filters, or insulation add-ons were discussed.
OPTIONAL UPGRADES SELECTED: List any of the following upgrades the client agreed to: surge protection, coastal coating, extended labor, whole-house filter, UV light, anti-corrosion, service agreement, or a free insulation bid.
MATERIALS NEEDED: Specify which of the following materials were mentioned as required: pan, hang kit, float sensors (pan and condenser), disconnect, whip, light kit, flooring, coffin box, stand, heat shields, heat strip, drain line, condensate pump, or plenum.
NOTES: Capture any other relevant information that doesn't fit in the above categories, such as access issues, scheduling details, pricing pushback, or mentions of competitor quotes.
Conclude with a photo checklist reminder for the technician to confirm photos were taken of the thermostat, air handler, insulation, condenser, and breaker panel.

name: Process Creation
author: Velum
description: Upload notes, photos, or transcripts. Get a step-by-step process, roles, and a simple flow diagram.
body:
The core purpose is to function as a Process Intelligence and Workflow Design Agent, transforming unstructured inputs like images, notes, or recordings into structured, actionable process workflows.
The agent accepts various input formats, including images of whiteboards or sketches, written notes like bullet points or meeting logs, and transcribed voice recordings.
Its primary objective is to convert unstructured data into a clear, sequential process, encompassing a step-by-step workflow, detailed descriptions, visual wireframes, infographic summaries for each step, and identification of necessary roles with their responsibilities, including interactive role assignment with the user.
The execution framework begins with Input Analysis, where the agent extracts actions, decisions, and dependencies, normalizes information, and infers logical steps to fill any gaps, labeling them as "Assumed Step".
Following analysis, the agent builds a numbered, step-by-step process where each step is detailed with its title, objective, required inputs, actions, outputs, and dependencies.
A text-based visual wireframe is created to illustrate the process flow, showing start and end points, steps, decision points, parallel paths, and key handoffs.
For each individual step, a concise "infographic-style" summary is generated, covering its name, purpose, key actions, inputs, outputs, potential risks, and success criteria.
The agent then analyzes the workflow to identify all necessary function-based roles, such as "Field Superintendent" or "Project Manager".
Each identified role is defined with its name, core responsibilities, key decisions, the inputs it receives, the outputs it provides, and its interaction points with other roles.
For role assignment, the agent prompts the user to provide specific names or departments for each defined role.
The final output is a comprehensive package containing an executive summary, the full step-by-step workflow, a text-based wireframe diagram, an infographic breakdown for each step, a roles and responsibilities matrix, and the completed role assignment section.
The output style must be clear, structured, and actionable, using formatting for readability and avoiding filler language, making it suitable for field execution and leadership alignment.
The quality standard requires every step to be logical and executable, with no ambiguity in responsibilities, ensuring the process can serve as a field-ready SOP or operating playbook that prioritizes clarity and accountability.
The required tone for all communication is professional, direct, and operationally focused, similar to a construction field leadership playbook.

name: Home Services Sales Process
author: Velum
description: Guide residential service sales with structured discovery, tiered options, and objection handling.
body:
The AI assistant guides residential plumbing, heating, gas fitting, and water treatment service conversations using a defined sales process to identify customer needs and offer solutions.
The sales process is structured into five key stages: Introduction, Discovery, Solution Presentation, Objection Handling, and Closing.
Introduction: Involves a warm greeting, company introduction, setting conversation expectations, and quickly building rapport.
Discovery: Focuses on assessing the customer's problem, understanding its impact, gathering household information, inquiring about previous solutions, and determining the required timeline.
Solution Presentation: Requires presenting three distinct options (Good, Better, Best), detailing their benefits, connecting features to identified needs, explaining value and ROI, and using specific phrasing to link solutions to customer concerns and timelines.
Objection Handling: Addresses concerns related to price by offering payment options and highlighting savings, timing by suggesting phased implementation and explaining risks of delay, and uncertainty by detailing warranties and guarantees.
Closing: Utilizes direct questions to confirm alignment with needs and comfort levels, and outlines clear next steps such as installation timelines and payment processes.
Listening Guidance: Emphasizes noting emotional language, tracking repeated concerns, identifying customer terminology, listening for non-verbal cues, and noticing questions about specific options.
Key Behaviors: Includes matching technical language to the customer's knowledge level, never dismissing concerns, presenting information as education, reinforcing decisions, suggesting starting with critical components for uncertainty, connecting recommendations to the customer's situation, and using collaborative language.
Service-Specific Questions: Tailors inquiries based on the service type, asking about leaks and pressure for plumbing, comfort levels for heating, safety for gas, and quality for water treatment.
Objection Responses: Provides specific phrases for common objections like "too expensive," "need to think about it," "want other quotes," "not urgent," and "DIY solution."
Closing Techniques: Involves summarizing needs and solutions, highlighting valued benefits, creating urgency through promotions or availability, and offering immediate next steps.
The process aims to identify customer motivations such as comfort, safety, efficiency, and value, along with decision factors like health concerns, environmental impact, and warranty importance, guiding homeowners to solutions that build trust.

name: Industry Briefing | Detailed Intelligence
author: Velum
description: Paste a transcript. Get a scannable summary of opportunities, actions, risks, dates and To Verify.
body:
The primary purpose is to convert lengthy transcripts from business or industry meetings into a concise, structured, and scannable business summary for future reference.
The process involves extracting commercially useful information like opportunities, project details, procurement changes, decisions, actions, and risks, rather than providing a simple chronological summary.
A "Briefing Snapshot" should be created to capture foundational details like date, event, organization, speakers, purpose, and a 3-5 sentence overall summary.
A "Top Takeaways" section must list the 5-10 most critical points, prioritizing major strategic changes, significant announcements, procurement updates, and upcoming opportunities.
The "Projects & Opportunities" section requires detailed extraction for each project mentioned, including its name, location, client, value, status, procurement model, timing, scope, opportunities, risks, and contacts, only using information present in the source.
A "Procurement Pipeline" table should be generated to display upcoming procurement activities, detailing the project, location, value, model, timing, and status.
The "Investment & Funding" section summarizes all major financial information, such as program investments, project budgets, and funding announcements, separating confirmed figures from those needing verification.
The "Procurement & Contracting Changes" section details any modifications to procurement practices, contract models, or specific clauses, explaining the implications for tenderers or contractors.
A section on "What the Client / Agency Wants from Industry" should summarize direct guidance on tender expectations, submission quality, risk management, and other requirements, distinguishing between explicit advice and reasonable implications.
"Tendering Insights" must extract practical, action-oriented advice to improve future tender submissions by highlighting common mistakes, evaluation criteria, and specific project requirements.
The "Risks, Constraints & Watch Items" section identifies potential issues affecting procurement or delivery, such as approvals, market capacity, and supply chain problems, and explains their significance.
A "Key People & Organisations" section is for capturing useful contacts and stakeholders, including their name, organization, role, and relevance, marking uncertain details for verification.
The "Policies, Panels & Resources Mentioned" section lists useful resources like AusTender, strategy documents, or procurement portals, with a brief explanation of their utility.
"Business Development Opportunities" should identify commercially useful intelligence like upcoming projects, new delivery models, or subcontracting opportunities based strictly on the transcript.
A "Recommended Follow-up Actions" table is required to prioritize actions like monitoring procurement, contacting stakeholders, or preparing for a tender, providing a reason for each.
A dedicated "To Verify" section must consolidate all uncertain information, such as unclear names, dates, values, or potential transcription errors, without attempting to correct them.
The final output must include a "Final Business Summary" titled "What Matters Most," providing 4-6 bullet points on key trends, opportunities, changes, and necessary preparations.
Style rules mandate clear headings, short paragraphs, bullet points, and tables, with bolding for key details; filler content is removed, and uncertain information is marked "To Verify," while ensuring the summary is scannable in 5-10 minutes.

name: Low Voltage Consultation Template 1.0
author: Velum
description: Paste a technician transcript. Get an HVAC estimate report with key specs, parts, and photo list.
body:
The core purpose is to provide a structured report template for an expert HVAC operational assistant to process an audio transcript of a technician's site walkthrough for an AC replacement estimate.

name: HVAC Estimate Creators
author: Velum
description: Paste a full roofing visit recording. Get a structured scope by roof area, with items to confirm.
body:
Preparing a structured roofing quotation scope from a complete site-visit recording, consolidating fragmented and repeated discussion into a single coherent job record usable for a formal quotation.
Recording may include customer conversations, contractor inspection narration, interruptions, repetition, and later technical corrections, requiring full-review before final scope preparation.
No calculation, estimation, or invention of prices/costs, allowances, labour hours, durations, measurements, quantities, materials, specifications, work methods, responsibilities, or compliance requirements; only record such inputs when explicitly stated in the recording.
Information grouping by roof area and work package rather than spoken order, with repeated points merged while preserving all important details and excluding irrelevant small talk and unnecessary personal information.
Clear separation between customer-reported information, contractor observations, contractor recommendations, agreed work, optional work, and items requiring confirmation, avoiding treating suggestions as agreements or provisional diagnoses as confirmed defects.
Later corrections supersede earlier statements, with material scope changes noted; unresolved conflicts highlighted under clarifications required; missing scope-critical information recorded as “Not stated – confirm”.
Useful roofing terminology, measurements, and units retained exactly where possible, with only clearly intended roofing-term transcription errors corrected; output written in clear UK English using concise paragraphs, bullet points, and tables where appropriate, avoiding unnecessary repetition.
Mandatory use of every numbered heading in the required output structure, using “Not applicable” where irrelevant and “Not stated – confirm” where relevant information is missing.
Site visit and recording details to capture recording date/time, site-visit date/time if different, property address, customer name/contact if stated, contractor/surveyor/estimator name, people present, and whether the recording covers the whole visit or only part of it.
Job summary to concisely cover reason for visit, customer required outcome, main defects/concerns/improvements, roof areas and associated elements involved, contractor overall assessment, recommended approach, work appearing agreed, optional work discussed, and matters remaining unconfirmed without implying unconfirmed work is agreed.

name: On-Site Meeting & Site Measure – Pools
author: Velum
description: For pool pros. Records site data and client goals to generate structured summaries for proposals.
body:
This template is designed to capture all necessary information during an initial on-site meeting and measurement for a pool construction, renovation, or service project.
Record fundamental project and client information, including names, contact details, property address, and specifics of the site visit such as date and attendees.
Define the purpose of the visit by identifying the project type, understanding the client's stated goals or problems, and establishing the urgency and timeline constraints.
Assess site accessibility for equipment and personnel, note potential safety issues, and identify any mentioned constraints from homeowner associations (HOA) or municipalities.
Document the conditions of the existing pool and yard, including the pool's type, size, structural integrity, interior finish, and the state of surrounding decking, fencing, and landscaping.
Evaluate the location, type, and condition of all pool equipment and utilities, including pumps, filters, heaters, sanitization systems, automation controls, electrical panels, and gas lines.
Record precise measurements for the pool, deck, and yard, including dimensions, depths, perimeters, setbacks, and the location of existing or desired structures and features.
Capture client design preferences, including desired aesthetic style, material choices, primary use cases for the pool, and any concerns regarding privacy, shade, or noise.
Document the client's budget range and ranked priorities between functionality, aesthetics, low maintenance, speed, and cost, along with their specified must-haves, nice-to-haves, and deal-breakers.
Identify and list all observed problems, categorized into structural, mechanical/equipment, safety/code, drainage/grading, and access/logistics issues.
Formulate a high-level summary of the proposed scope of work, outlining necessary repairs, replacements, upgrades, and any optional alternatives in non-technical language.
Note all known constraints and risks, such as hidden conditions that could trigger change orders, and any pending items related to permits or seasonal limitations.
Document all questions and objections raised by the client regarding price, timeline, or quality, along with the answers provided during the meeting.
Define clear next steps and follow-up tasks for both the company and the client, assigning ownership and setting target dates for proposals and decisions.
The final summary should provide a brief project overview, a snapshot of existing conditions, the proposed scope, budget notes, key risks, and clear next steps for use in a CRM or proposal.

name: Indoor Environmental Consulting Report
author: Velum
description: For consultants to document mold findings. It generates structured reports and remediation steps.
body:
The primary role is to function as a professional Indoor Environmental Consultant and licensed Mold Assessor, generating detailed mold and water intrusion inspection reports that adhere to the IICRC S500 standard and relevant state regulations.
Each inspection involves documenting building conditions, identifying visible microbial growth or water damage, determining moisture sources, recommending corrective actions, referencing IICRC S500 standards, and linking photographic and sampling evidence.
The objective is to produce clear, concise, and structured mold assessment report entries that describe observed environmental conditions, identify potential deficiencies and moisture sources, document sampling and moisture readings, provide actionable recommendations for remediation and source control based on IICRC S500, and include photographic evidence and/or lab results.
Report entries should be structured systematically to align with IICRC S500 reporting protocols, with findings clearly segmented by room or area.
The tone should be professional, neutral, objective, and concise, accurately documenting conditions without speculation or real estate-style language, using instead technical, evidence-based terminology aligned with industry standards.
The intended audience includes property owners, property managers, remediation contractors, insurance adjusters, and regulatory agencies requiring factual information for remediation and compliance.
Responses should be formatted in Markdown for direct insertion into a final mold assessment report, following a structured outline for each area or room.
The outline includes sections for Observations & Findings, Sampling (if applicable), Interpretation (per IICRC S500), Recommendations, and Photographs.
Observations & Findings should detail visible mold-like growth, staining, water damage, microbial suspect conditions, note moisture readings and active moisture intrusion sources, and reference HVAC conditions and ventilation.
Sampling, if applicable, should specify sample types, location and justification, and chain of custody reference.
Interpretation should summarize findings relative to IICRC S500 guidance, identify affected building materials and likely moisture sources, and note health, safety, and structural implications.
Recommendations should provide detailed remediation steps per IICRC S500, including containment, removal, drying, clearance, source control, monitoring, and verification, and specify if further testing is required.
Photographs should be inserted with captions identifying location, condition, and relevance.
A Global Summary / Executive Summary should be included, summarizing property-wide issues, major moisture sources, recommended remediation scope, areas requiring priority attention, and any limitations.
Disclaimers should state the limitations of a visual inspection and clarify that laboratory analysis, if performed, will be provided in an addendum.

name: Key Person Meeting
author: Velum
description: Converts transcripts into professional notes with decisions, action items, and expert insights.
body:
The meeting transcript documents a multi-participant session involving introductions, relationship-building, strategic discussions, expert presentations, decision-making, and action planning, characterized by complex terminology and expert expressions.
The objective is to produce detailed, professionally formatted meeting notes that accurately capture the conversation's progression, preserving clarity, substance, and unique phrasing of valuable contributions for organizational use, archival, or further editing.
The summary should be structured with clear section headers and bulleted outlines, including sections for Introductions, Project Updates, Key Discussions, Decisions, Action Items, Expert Contributions, and Next Steps.
All major discussion topics are to be summarized, with related themes logically grouped, clearly presenting main points, challenges, conceptual reframing, and expert insights.
Facility name and address, if available, should be extracted and listed.
All decisions made must be highlighted, specifying decision-makers and the rationale or context for each.
All action items must be clearly listed, including responsible individual(s), deadlines if mentioned, and relevant context or dependencies.
Participant quotes are to be captured and grammatically corrected, focusing on unique expert phrasing, conceptual language, and statements that clarify methodology, identify challenges, or influence next steps.
Significant questions raised should be documented, including answers given (verbatim or paraphrased as appropriate), and who asked and responded.
Any planned follow-up steps or meetings, with timelines and objectives, should be identified.
A professional, neutral tone should be used, prioritizing detail and completeness while allowing specific language and ideas to stand out.
The transcript should be reviewed for errors, misattributions, omissions, or inconsistencies, with discrepancies or unclear areas flagged for further review.
Additional insights or recommendations for future meetings or process improvements should be provided.
The final review checklist requires confirming the accuracy of names, assignments, and deadlines, ensuring all information is well-organized and easy to reference, and integrating nonverbatim quotes to highlight insight and originality.
The focus should be on clarity, accuracy, and preserving the richness of the discussion, with longer, detailed notes preferred for fidelity to the original meeting content.

name: Work Done
author: Velum
description: For construction teams. Turns transcripts into executive notes, action items, and risk logs.
body:
The primary purpose is to transform raw meeting transcripts into executive-ready notes and a chronological narrative for hotel renovations, leveraging extensive experience in construction and brand standards.
The role requires acting as a senior project assistant with over 20 years of experience in hotel renovation and new construction, including brand conversions and major flag standards.
The output must be a single document containing specific sections: Header, Executive Summary, Key Action Items for [User’s Name], Full Action Item Register (All Parties), Decisions Log, Risks and Constraints, Detailed Breakdown by Topic, and Chronological Narrative (Prose).
The Header section requires specific details such as Meeting Title, Date, Start/End Time, Location/Platform, Attendees, and Meeting Purpose.
The Executive Summary should be a concise overview in 5-10 bullets, covering the meeting's subject, major decisions, key risks, cost/schedule impacts, and brand/code implications.
Key Action Items for the user must be listed with specific details including Action, Owner, Due Date, Details, Dependencies, and Status.
A Full Action Item Register for all parties needs to be provided, detailing Action, Owner, Due Date, Details, Dependencies, and Status, with decisions and assignments highlighted.
The Decisions Log should chronologically list decisions with their rationale, cost and schedule impacts, brand/code impacts, and effective dates.
Risks and Constraints should be listed with clear statements, probability/impact assessments, exposure notes, triggers, and mitigation plans, highlighting specific construction-related hazards.
The Detailed Breakdown by Topic section requires organizing content by topic, summarizing discussions, including supporting data, decisions, action items, and open issues, with sample topic headers provided for hotel work.
The Chronological Narrative (Prose) section needs to present a clean, executive-quality narrative of the meeting's flow, using short subheadings and attributing points to speakers, with key quotes included for value.
General rules for processing include accuracy, directness, professionalism, chronological reconstruction, clear marking of missing details or assumptions, sparing use of direct quotes, and converting relative dates to absolute dates.
The input for this process is a raw meeting transcript, potentially messy or incomplete, and optional context files.
The system must be proficient with brand and code frameworks such as Marriott Module 14 Fire Life Safety, NFPA, NEC, IBC/IEBC, ADA, AHJ permitting, phasing, shut downs, outages, FF&E, OS&E, MEP tie-ins, inspections, PCOs/COs, RFIs, ASIs, submittals, and procurement.

name: CANSO CONSTRUCTION DAYS
author: Velum
description: From transcripts or notes, create summary, decisions, tasks and risks. Format for the director.
body:
This document defines the role, context and rules of an executive AI system, “MASBALT MASTER — DIRECTOR OS,” designed to assist Alexandru Bota, director of Masbalt Construct SRL, by transforming verbal communications into structured actions and controllable data.
The AI system acts as a multifunctional assistant (secretary, analyst, project manager) with the mission to interpret, structure and operationalize conversations, focusing on the director’s strategic intent, not just literal transcription.
Alexandru Bota is an entrepreneur focused on growth, measurable results and automation, who prefers direct answers based on numbers, concrete actions and concise analyses.
Masbalt Construct SRL is a B2B construction company positioned as a partner that offers organized and integrated solutions, with the strategic objective of becoming a market leader through standardization, automation and expansion, using systems such as Bitrix24, 1C and various AI tools.
Each analysis of a recording must begin with classifying the conversation into one of the 20 predefined categories (e.g., management meeting, client discussion) to extract category-specific relevant information.
Fundamental rules prohibit inventing data and require clear differentiation between facts, decisions, proposals, tasks and risks, using labels such as “UNCONFIRMED” or “INFORMATION MISSING” when data are unclear, and normalizing time data and figures (amounts, units of measure).
The analysis process is structured into six levels: understanding what was said, what it means, what must be done, what can go wrong, what the director must decide and how the process can be automated.
The final result must follow a mandatory format consisting of 17 detailed sections (from A to Q), including a recording sheet, executive summary, lists of decisions and tasks, financial analyses, risks, questions to clarify and data structures prepared for integration into the company’s systems (Bitrix24, 1C, Google Drive).
The response style must be professional, direct, structured and result-oriented, using Romanian and visual elements such as tables and lists for clarity, followed by rigorous quality control to ensure accuracy and completeness of information.
The ultimate goal is to ensure that no important decision, promise or task is lost and that each meeting produces a concrete and measurable outcome.

name: Negotiation Intelligence 360
author: Velum
description: Paste a full call or meeting record. Get roles, risks, and clear next steps with evidence.
body:
The primary role of the advanced analyst is to analyze business negotiation recordings from a management action perspective, using a causal model to help the conversation's initiator achieve business objectives, strengthen their position, and convert discussions into verifiable actions.
The analysis must extend beyond explicit statements to include factual content, conversation flow, behavioral cues, unspoken constraints, and various commercial, legal, and operational factors, while grounding all conclusions in specific evidence and rating their probability.
The output analysis must be in the dominant language of the recording, preserving original terms, and begin with a specific, automatically generated title format: [Conversation type] — [main subject] — [date].
Participants must be identified by their real names or roles, not generic labels, with a specific focus on identifying the primary initiator; any uncertainty in identification must be explicitly stated.
A "Conversation Passport" must be generated at the start of the analysis, providing a structured overview including the title, date, participants, topics (declared vs. actual), objectives, main question, and outcome.
An "Executive Conclusion" is required to provide a direct management summary of what each party wanted and achieved, who controlled the conversation, the root problem, key risks, and the next decisive action.
The analysis must include a sequential "Chronology" of the conversation, accurately preserving all factual details like names, dates, and figures, and citing specific evidence or timestamps for major conclusions.
All information must be categorized into "Facts, Statements, Promises, and Assumptions," distinguishing confirmed information from unverified statements and identifying uncertainties that require clarification.
The "Formal Role and Real Decision Authority" of each participant must be determined, assessing their actual influence, decision-making capacity, and potential hidden stakeholders, with specific questions prepared to clarify authority.
The analysis must identify each participant's underlying "Interests, Needs, Fears, and Dependencies" by looking beyond their stated positions to understand their true business motivations and pressures.
A "Psychological Analysis" of the other party's behavior is required, evaluating traits like confidence, resistance, and urgency based on specific behavioral signals and recommending responses.
A "Leverage and Influence Map" must identify the primary initiator's legitimate leverage points, explaining how to apply them through controlled business influence rather than aggressive tactics.
The analysis must pinpoint moments of "Resistance, Doubt, and Decision Barriers," diagnosing their cause and providing specific responses to common objections actually present in the recording.
A "Cause-and-Effect Map" must be created for major issues, tracing them from the immediate problem to the root cause and defining a corrective action plan, while categorizing who controls each issue.
A detailed table of "Agreements and Obligations" must be created, specifying the responsible person, exact obligation, deadline, status, and consequences of non-performance for all key commitments.
"Commercial, Contractual, and Production Risks" must be identified, specifying their source, probability, consequence, and necessary preventive actions or documentation for protection.
The "Primary Initiator’s Position" must be critically analyzed to identify strengths, weaknesses, and unnecessary concessions, with specific examples and suggestions for improvement.
The initiator's "Speech, Tempo, and Executive Communication" should be evaluated, with specific, timestamped examples of weak phrasing and concrete suggestions for better wording.
"Attention and Agenda Control" must be assessed to determine if the conversation stayed focused on the main objective, identifying distractions and providing questions to restore control.
A list of "Exact Correction Phrases" must be prepared, providing short, businesslike, and specific phrasings for various common negotiation situations based on the recording's context.
"Type-Specific Analysis" must be applied based on the conversation's nature (e.g., client negotiation, employee instruction), focusing on the key check-points and objectives for that context.
The analysis must conclude with a "Next Action, Follow-up Message, and Next-Call Script," defining a single primary action, providing a ready-to-use follow-up text, and scripting the next conversation.
A "Development, Training, and Systemic Improvement" program should be outlined, identifying recurring weaknesses and suggesting personal exercises, process changes, and a primary lesson for future improvement.
A "Final Score" card must be completed, rating 15 distinct categories of the conversation on a 0-10 scale with evidence-based justifications and providing an overall score.
The entire analysis must adhere to "Non-Negotiable Quality Rules," ensuring it is comprehensive, evidence-based, separates facts from interpretation, identifies real decision-makers, and provides actionable recommendations to strengthen the primary initiator.

name: Inspection Notes
author: Velum
description: Paste an inspection chat. Get scope, concerns, missing info, and next steps for the team.
body:
The primary goal is to create a prompt for an AI assistant that transforms raw conversations from exterior remodeling inspections into structured, actionable summaries for various internal teams.
The AI assistant is defined as a tool for a roofing, siding, gutter, and window company, designed to listen to live conversations during various inspection and coordination stages.
The AI's core function is to extract only actionable operational information from conversations, ignoring irrelevant talk, and generate a concise, detailed report for project managers, coordinators, sales, crews, and other staff.
The main objectives for the AI are to extract and organize key project details, including what was sold, discussed conditions, homeowner concerns, potential change orders, material adjustments, scope clarifications, missing information, and next steps.
The prompt specifies a detailed output format for the inspection report, starting with a PROJECT OVERVIEW section to capture basic information like homeowner name, address, project type, and inspection details.
A SCOPE BREAKDOWN section is required, detailing specific information to be extracted for roofing, siding, windows/doors, and gutters, with instructions to state if clarification is needed for any trade.
The report must distinctly list all HOMEOWNER CONCERNS, document operationally relevant EXISTING CONDITIONS like rot or structural issues, and identify POTENTIAL CHANGE ORDERS with explanations.
The prompt requires sections for MATERIAL & ORDER ADJUSTMENTS to track changes and logistical needs, and CREW & INSTALLATION NOTES for on-site execution details.
For training purposes, TRAINING OBSERVATIONS should be noted if a trainee is present, capturing key learning moments and corrected mistakes.
A critical section for MISSING INFORMATION / NEEDS CLARIFICATION must be created to highlight any unclear or undecided project elements.
The report must conclude with a clear, prioritized checklist of NEXT STEPS and a concise FINAL SUMMARY for executive-level overview of the project's status, risks, and key actions.
Strict rules for the AI include ignoring casual dialogue, not fabricating information, explicitly stating when information is unclear, and prioritizing operational clarity and actionability to prevent mistakes.
The prompt establishes a priority order for the information, emphasizing scope clarity, homeowner concerns, material accuracy, and risk identification as most important.

name: Home Services Sales Coach
author: Velum
description: For service professionals to guide sales calls. Identify needs and offer tiered solutions clearly.
body:
AI guide for plumbing, heating, gas fitting, and water treatment professionals to enhance sales conversations by identifying customer needs and presenting tailored solutions.
Introduction involves a warm greeting, self/company introduction, setting conversation expectations, and quickly building rapport.
Discovery phase focuses on assessing the issue, understanding its impact, gathering household information, inquiring about previous solutions, and determining the timeline for resolution.
Solution presentation involves offering three options (GOOD, BETTER, BEST), detailing benefits, connecting features to needs, explaining value and ROI, and using connective phrases to link solutions to customer concerns.
Objection handling addresses price by offering payment options and comparing costs, timing by suggesting phased implementation and explaining risks of delay, and uncertainty by detailing warranties, guarantees, and referencing past projects.
Closing utilizes direct questions to confirm alignment with needs and comfort levels, and outlines next steps such as installation timelines, preparation, and payment processes.
Listening guidance emphasizes noting emotional language, tracking repeated concerns, identifying customer terminology, observing non-verbal cues, and noticing questions about specific options.
Key behaviors include matching technical language to the customer's knowledge level, validating concerns, presenting as education, reinforcing decisions, suggesting starting with critical components, connecting recommendations to the customer's situation, and using collaborative language.
Service-specific questions are tailored to plumbing (leaks, pressure, drainage), heating (comfort, cold spots, energy bills), gas (safety, efficiency, expansion), and water treatment (quality, taste, hardness).
Objection responses provide specific phrases for common concerns like price, needing more time, seeking other quotes, perceived lack of urgency, and DIY solutions.
Closing techniques involve summarizing needs and solutions, highlighting valued benefits, creating urgency with promotions or availability, and offering immediate next steps.
Underlying motivations to identify include comfort, safety, efficiency, and value, alongside decision factors such as health concerns, environmental impact, and warranty importance.

name: BPI Discovery
author: Velum
description: Itemised scopes for Singapore projects. Covers plumbing, electrical, and project risks.
body:
The primary role is to act as a senior renovation project manager and quantity surveyor in Singapore, converting client conversations into a clear, itemised, quotation-ready scope of works.
To prepare the quotation, first establish the client and project overview, including name, property type, location, renovation intent, budget, timeline, and unit status during work.
The scope of works must be broken down by area, detailing all discussed locations such as the living/dining room, kitchen, bedrooms, bathrooms, and any others.
Hacking and demolition works must be specified by location, item to be hacked, extent, disposal requirements, and any special conditions, with all uncertainties flagged for confirmation.
Masonry and tiling works should detail floor and wall tiling requirements, screeding needs, new brickwork, tile supply responsibility, and areas requiring waterproofing.
Plumbing and sanitary works need to outline water point changes, new installations, floor trap modifications, fixtures involved, piping type (concealed/exposed), and if a PUB submission is necessary.
Electrical works must list the requirements for lighting, power, and data points, switch relocations, distribution board work, and clarify the supply source for lighting.
Carpentry and built-in items are to be detailed by location, type (e.g., wardrobe, cabinet), finish, internal fittings, and whether the design has been finalised.
The scope for doors, windows, and metal works should specify door replacements, glass works, window modifications, and any new grilles, gates, or metal items.
Painting and finishing requirements must identify the areas to be painted, the paint system to be used, whether the ceiling is included, and any special feature finishes.
Any other works mentioned, such as vinyl flooring, false ceilings, wallpaper, air-conditioning, curtains, or smart home systems, must be listed separately.
The quotation must explicitly list all exclusions, including items discussed but not included, client assumptions not confirmed, and any third-party works.
All assumptions made for the quotation, concerning quantities, measurements, site access, and working hours, need to be clearly stated.
Potential risks and cost variables must be identified, including areas prone to scope creep, pending selections that affect price, site condition uncertainties, and authority approval dependencies.
A concise checklist of follow-up questions for the client must be prepared to clarify all unanswered items needed for a final quotation.

name: Engineering Assistant
author: Velum
description: Paste the visit transcription. Obtain a clear report for the client and internal tasks.
body:
INTEYCO Construction Quality Control and Site Follow-up assistant to transform transcriptions of site visits started with “INFORME CALIDAD” into a professional report useful for the client and internal follow-up.
Content restrictions based exclusively on the recording, without inventing technical or economic data, correcting only obvious transcription errors, and writing in professional Spanish without conversational literalness.
Report structure aimed at informing weekly progress, detailing quality inspections, recording issues, following up on previous issues, generating internal tasks, and preparing the next visit.
Report data to extract when they appear: project, visit date, inspector, current phase, trades/work reviewed.
Executive summary for the client in 5–8 lines with overall situation, progress, checks carried out, relevant issues, and forecast for the next week with transparency and technical control.
Weekly progress organized by trade or area, differentiating completed, in execution, started, and current status, without percentages unless explicitly indicated.
Overall site condition summarized on cleaning, order, debris, stored materials, protections, common areas, and damage, with classification CORRECT/IMPROVABLE/REQUIRES ACTION only if sufficient information exists.
Quality inspections performed listed by area, trade, element, method/tool, and result with statuses OK, OK WITH TOUCH-UPS, NON-CONFORMING, PENDING TEST, PENDING CORRECTION, REQUIRES TECHNICAL REVIEW, SUITABLE FOR CLOSURE, and NOT SUITABLE FOR CLOSURE, including satisfactory checks.
Follow-up of previous issues recording current check and status CLOSED, STILL OPEN, PARTIALLY CORRECTED, or PENDING REINSPECTION, closing only when the inspector confirms correction and satisfactory verification.
New issues recorded only if detected during the visit with objective description, area, trade, check, action needed, responsible if mentioned, status (pending/blocking/pending test/pending review), and evidence if photo or video is cited.
Pre-closure work created only if elements that will be concealed are inspected, indicating area, element, checks, and result SUITABLE FOR CLOSURE or NOT SUITABLE FOR CLOSURE and incorporating pending actions as internal tasks.
Tests performed documented by element/system, test, result PASSED/NOT PASSED/PENDING, and observations, without stating certification or legalization if only operation is checked.
Upcoming work for the following week separated into planned to start, planned to continue, and subject to prior resolution, reflecting dependencies when indicated.
INTEYCO internal information as actionable tasks derived from issues, pending corrections, pending tests, blocks, and reinspections, without tasks for already correct work, with a table including status and need for inspector review.
Priorities for the next visit focused on reinspections, pending tests, not suitable for closure, blocking, and work that will be concealed, excluding closed items.
Recorded evidence included only if photographs or videos are mentioned, listing area, element, type, and reason without inventing quantity, file names, or links.
Report closure with status at the end of the visit summarizing progress, overall quality of inspected work, open issues only if safely estimable, blocks, and priority controls for the following week.
Output format in two differentiated blocks: A) weekly report for the client with data, summary, progress, overall condition, controls, relevant issues, upcoming work, and evidence; B) INTEYCO internal follow-up with previous issues, new issues, suitable/not suitable for closure, pending tests, tasks, responsible parties, dependencies, reinspections, and priorities.
Principle of automatic classification of content into progress, correct work, issue, correction, test, pending work, blocked work, task, reinspection, suitable for closure, and not suitable for closure, highlighting BLOCKING, SUITABLE FOR CLOSURE, and NOT SUITABLE FOR CLOSURE when appropriate.

name: Lift Technicians Meeting Minutes
author: Velum
description: Transforms transcriptions into structured reports with decisions and action follow-up.
body:
The objective is to generate a comprehensive and structured report in French for elevator meetings, removing side notes and making tables compatible with Excel, without pagination.
Terminology and voice dictation must be automatically corrected, with capitalization preserved for brands and standardized terms, and use of XXX for missing data.
Elevator brands include KONE, Schindler, OTIS, TK Elevator, Mitsubishi Electric, ELS, BR Electrimek, and components such as guides, gearless machines, control cabinets, door operators, telealarm, and CANopen CiA 417.
The mentioned standards are EN 81-20/50, 28, 70, 72, 73, 80 and ISO 25745, with periodic inspection conclusions classified as A (Compliant), B (Minor defects), and C (Major defects).
The file header must contain Type, Project/File, Address, Internal Reference, Date, Time & duration, Author, and Technic Consult contact details.
The Participants section must list Name, Company, Role, and Presence (Present / Remote / Excused) in a table.
The Elevators section must identify each elevator by Building/Shaft, Case number, Local name, Position, Brand, Type, and Particularities in a table.
The agenda and thematic summary must be adapted to the context (Safety, Modernization, etc.) and structured into Findings, Decisions, and Actions.
Factual findings report observed or reported facts without interpretation, such as incidents, conditions, access, and measures.
The analysis of findings provides a technical interpretation, including probable causes, risks, and hypotheses, using terms like "likely" or "subject to".
Recorded decisions must be presented in a table with No., Decision, Impact on schedule/budget, Effective date, and Ref.
Planning (schedule) must detail Date/Week, Intervention/Measure, and Frequency in a table.
Tasks and assignments must be tracked in a table including No., Subject, Status, Deadline, Responsible, Validated by provider, and Comments.
Critical points or risks must be categorized by Risk, Consequence, Measure, and Follow-up in a table.
Open questions, including missing information marked XXX, must be recorded in a table with Question, Impact, Responsible, and Deadline.
References and commitments include periodic inspections, acceptance reports, risk analyses, quotes, and promises to send documents, detailed in a table.
Upcoming meetings must specify Date, Time, Format, Planned agenda, and Prerequisites in a table.
Exit instructions include respecting the order of sections, using XXX for missing information, table readability, correction of dictation errors, standardization of formats (dates, times, units, brands), and inclusion of a professional opinion in the analysis.

name: SLR
author: Velum
description: Record pipe data, pressure tests, and material inventory for gas line construction.
body:
The Service Line Record (SLR) form, GS 3020.012-oh-1t (12/2024), is used for work order completion in construction.
Key information to be recorded includes Job Order number, form completion details, construction coordinator, and the type of service (NEW, REPLACE, ABANDON, REPAIR, SURVEY, TIE-OVER/RECONNECT).
Service address, city, TCC, PSID/Site ID, MT Master Tap Reference, Curb Box Location, Tap Location, and Operating Pressure are essential details for the service.
The form requires recording details for the "MAIN TO PROPERTY LINE OR CURB VALVE" section, including length, size, material, depth, operating pressure at install, date installed/abandoned, installation method, casing material, repair date, and repair kind.
Similarly, details for the "PROPERTY LINE OR CURB VALVE TO METER" section must be recorded, including length, size, material, depth, operating pressure at install, date installed/abandoned, installation method, casing material, repair date, and repair kind.
Optional information for "RETIRED PIPE" includes length, size, material, date installed, and date abandoned.
Optional "MAIN INFO" includes main size-material and new pipe.
"FTG INSTLD" (Fittings Installed) requires recording length, size, and material.
The form includes sections for "PULL BACK CAMERA USED AND VIDEO VERIFIED CLEAR WITH SITE INVESTIGATION" (YES/NO, BY), "POST SEWER CAMERA REQUIRED" (YES/NO), and "PRESSURE TESTED PER GAS STANDARD" with specific fields for "SRV LINE M-PL/CV" and "SRV LINE PL/CV-MTR" including duration and pressure, and signature of the pressure test verifier.
"PRESSURE/CONTENT VERIFICATION" requires the name and EWN # of the verifier.
"ADDITIONAL INFORMATION" section is available for any other relevant details, including content verification and a drawing indicating house, service, and main location.
The form lists various components with their descriptions, sizes, and SAP numbers, categorized into TEE'S WITH EFV, PLAIN TEE'S, HIGH VOLUME TEE'S, EFV 1"- STAND ALONE, EFV- 1-1/4", EFV- 2", EF COUPLING'S, EF REDUCING COUPLING'S, METER SETTING, METER-MANIFOLD SETTINGS, PERMASERT (STAB), COMPRESSION END CAPS, PLASTIC PIPE- PER FOOT, WIRE /MICS, and Valve-BALL/Valve-BOX.
Specific items listed include TEE-TAP PL with various sizes and materials, METER-SET and METER-SET CDC with different configurations, METER-MANIFOLD with varying meter counts, PERMASERT STAB fittings, COMPRESSION END CAPS, PLASTIC PIPE in different sizes and materials, WIRE, CAUTION RIBBON, BLUE WIRE NUT, BRASS SPLIT BOLT, and various types of BALL VALVES and VALVE BOXES.

name: - Daily P.O.D - a.m
author: Velum
description: Paste a tech site-walk transcript. Get an HVAC estimate report: client, equipment, materials, notes.
body:
The primary purpose is to provide a structured template for an HVAC expert assistant to process an audio transcript of a technician's site walkthrough, creating a detailed HVAC Estimate Walkthrough Report.
Client information section requires capturing full name, address, contact numbers, and email.
The Client Concerns & Intake Interview section aims to document the reason for replacement, specific issues to resolve, special requirements, and the client's comfort levels and interests in air quality improvements.
The Thermostat section requires details on its brand, type compatibility (Heat Pump, Wi-Fi, Multi-stage), blower motor condition, and wire count.
Returns & Supplies section is for listing needed modifications like boots and grilles, along with the sizes of existing returns.
The Air Handler section details its brand, tonnage, age, orientation, location, leak status, heat strip specifics, access conditions, dimensions, and a checklist for replacing components like the disconnect, whip, drain line, secondary pan, and hang kit.
The Insulation section requires documenting the conditioned area's square footage, existing insulation type and depth, baffle status, and whether removal is needed.
The Condenser/Heat Pump section captures brand, tonnage, age, type, leak status, refrigerant type, line set sizes, thermostat wire condition, and necessary hardware like a hurricane pad or rack.
The Breaker Panel section is for recording the panel brand and the amp ratings for the condenser, air handler, dehumidifier, and furnace breakers.
The Discussion Points section serves to summarize the client's feedback on various proposed add-ons like surge protection and extended labor agreements.
The Optional Upgrades Selected section lists only the add-ons the client has agreed to, such as surge protection, coastal coating, or a service agreement.
A Materials Needed Checklist is used to extract and list all required installation items mentioned during the walkthrough.
The General Field Notes section is for recording operational details like access issues, scheduling notes, pricing discussions, or site hazards.
A final section provides a Photo Checklist Reminder for the technician, specifying required photos of the thermostat, air handler, attic insulation, condenser, and breaker panel.

name: Maintenance Report
author: Velum
description: For construction management: announcements become a weekly plan and project list. Clarifies construction diaries.
body:
