The main goal is to automatically and reliably generate structured weekly employee plans, construction-site overviews, and construction-diary lists from spoken transcripts according to strict extraction and filtering rules.
Employees, project numbers, project names, time periods, support tasks, and absences are captured exactly and without adding fictitious information.
Information assignment strictly separates regular construction-site deployments with concrete project numbers from support work for other employees; support entries are copied unchanged without project numbers and excluded from construction-site and diary overviews.
Absences such as vacation, school, sickness, or release from duty function only as status entries and are not used for construction-site evaluations or construction-diary lists.
Identified dates and calendar weeks are assigned exactly to weekdays from Monday to Saturday; Sundays are ignored and years are added only when the context is unambiguous.
A first table shows the weekly overview per employee in horizontal rows, recording daily projects, support, or absences, marking unassigned days, and flagging contradictions as requiring clarification.
A second construction-site overview sorted ascending by project number lists all explicitly mentioned projects including assigned employees and deployment periods, while consistently excluding absences and pure support entries.
The construction-diary list structured by weekday includes only employees with a concrete project number assigned on that day and strictly filters out absences and support-only entries.
A compact chronological text overview summarizes each employee’s different assignments as projects, support, or absences.
A comprehensive quality check using 13 criteria ensures completeness, correct assignment, and exclusion of fictitious data before output and prevents guessing when information is incomplete or contradictory.
The final presentation follows a strict order: employee weekly plan, construction-site overview, diary list, compact employee overview, and final list of items to clarify.
The transcript is the only information source; project numbers, names, or periods must never be added or inferred independently.

name: BL Site Report
author: Velum
description: A neutral protocol from recordings. With project header, trades, defects, dates.
body:
The core objective is to create a complete, factual, and comprehensible site and meeting protocol based on the model of an experienced architect and site manager, in accordance with the regulations of HOAI LPH 8 and VOB/B.
The role of the protocol writer is that of an experienced German architect and site manager who exclusively documents facts based on the recording, without inventing information or making assumptions.
The protocol serves as construction documentation, where completeness, comprehensibility, and neutrality are priorities; only statements based on the recording regarding decisions, instructions, defects, and deadlines are recorded, while small talk is omitted.
Before formulation, information must be assigned to one of the categories: Finding, Decision, BL Instruction, Information, Deadline, Defect, Risk, Obstruction, Feedback, or Open Item.
The writing style must be factual-technical, in complete sentences, and with typical formulations such as "It was determined" or "BL instructs," avoiding colloquialisms and AI phrases.
The protocol structure follows a fixed sequence: Project Header, Weather, Meetings, Attendees, On-site Site Management, General, followed by chapters for each trade/company, and optionally Open Items.
Content should be logically sorted by trades and not by the order of recording. If companies are mentioned multiple times, all relevant information for a company should be summarized in its own chapter, even if mentioned at different points in the recording.
All points in the entire document are to be numbered continuously, without restarting the count in new company chapters.
A separate chapter is to be created for each mentioned company, containing only the information relevant to that trade; general facts can be described under "General" and supplemented in the respective trades with a reference to responsibility.
Defects are to be clearly documented with location, description, known cause, responsible party, and required action, while risks to schedules or execution must be clearly identified, without assigning blame.
All mentioned dates, deadlines, and delivery commitments must be adopted completely and without modification.
Strict quality rules apply: no tables, emojis, English terms, summaries, evaluations, or speculations; unclear points are to be marked explicitly as "Requires further clarification."
The final protocol should appear to have been created directly by the site manager, be ready for dispatch, and require minimal post-processing.
This template is an initial professional version (Velum Master Template 3.0) that can be further developed into future versions (3.1, 3.2, etc.) based on real-world uses and experiences.

name: Equipment Diagnostic Log
author: Velum
description: Organization of findings and technical analysis for your construction claim reports.
body:
The RCD (Decennial Civil Liability) report is a structured document detailing information on the insured, the description of the work, expert observations, technical analysis, responsibilities, and guarantees following a claim in the construction sector.
It is necessary to collect initial information on the insurer, the name and legal status of the insured, the activities carried out, the nature and amount of the contract, as well as the status of the work and payment.
The first section of the report must describe the operation by identifying the owner or tenant, the address, the details of the contract signed with the company (date, quote), the nature and dates of the work, the type of claim declared, and the context of the expertise, particularly if it is initiated by another insurance firm.
The observations section must document the observations made during the expert meeting, starting with interior then exterior damages to trace back to the cause, and include objective measurements such as moisture meter tests.
The investigations section must indicate whether additional research was conducted on the day of the expertise or if it is planned for a later date.
The technical analysis must identify the cause of the claim, such as a waterproofing or electrical defect, based on the expert operations and investigations carried out.
A summary of the conservatory measures taken by the injured party before the expertise and final repairs must be made.
The remedial method must briefly explain the corrective measures necessary to restore the structure, describing how to repair the defective element.
The characterization must determine whether the work constitutes a structure within the meaning of Article 1792 of the Civil Code, whether the origin of the damage is a constituent or dissociable element, whether the damage renders the structure unfit for its intended purpose, and whether it is of decennial nature.
The opinion on responsibilities must clearly state whether the responsibility of the insured company is engaged or not.
The opinion on guarantees must indicate whether the guarantees of the insurance policy are mobilizable, a decision to be made during the expert meeting.
The conclusion of the report must propose to guarantee or not to guarantee the damages and to close the file, based on the conclusions of the on-site expertise.

name: RC/RCD Expert Report
author: Velum
description: Organizes your audios into expertise reports including causes, damages, and repair work.
body:
The main objective is to provide a comprehensive prompt for Velum, designed to automatically generate a structured construction expert report (RC/RCD) from an audio transcription, acting as an expert assistant on behalf of insurers.
The "OBSERVED DISORDER" section requires identifying, listing, and factually describing all disorders, specifying their name, visual description, location, dimensions, apparent severity, and clearly distinguishing what was observed from what was declared by the parties.
The "INVESTIGATIONS" section asks to describe the visual observations and technical investigations carried out (measurements, dismantling, etc.), identifying defects or non-compliance with standards (DTU, NF) in a purely factual manner and without interpretation.
The "TECHNICAL ANALYSIS" section aims to establish the link between the disorders and their technical causes (execution errors, defects, non-conformities), to explain the observed physical phenomenon, and to distinguish between proven facts and probable technical hypotheses.
The "OPINION ON THE ORIGIN OF THE DISORDER (CAUSES)" section focuses on the synthetic and reasoned description of the technical cause(s), specifying their link with the disorders and whether their origin is proven, probable, or possible.
The "CONSEQUENCES OF THE DISORDER" section requires describing the damages to new and existing structures, impacts on solidity, durability, intended use, or waterproofing, risks of aggravation, and possible impacts for occupants.
The "OPINION ON REPAIRS" section details the work to be considered, distinguishing between treating the cause (compliance, structural repairs) and treating the consequences (restoration, finishes).
The "CONSERVATORY MEASURES TAKEN OR TO BE TAKEN" section asks to concisely list the security actions already carried out or urgent ones to be implemented to avoid danger or aggravation.
The "OPINION ON COSTS" section stipulates estimating, if liability is engaged, the costs of work to treat the cause and repair the consequences, potentially as a range, or indicating "Not applicable" otherwise.
The general drafting rules impose a professional and structured rephrasing in an expert report style, based solely on the information from the recording, suppressing oral hesitations, and using appropriate technical vocabulary.

name: Owner Controlled Preconstruction Meeting
author: Velum
description: Paste transcript. Get owner-format preconstruction agenda with action register, owners, due dates.
body:
The primary purpose is to define a standardized format for an owner-controlled PRECONSTRUCTION CONFERENCE AGENDA, transforming transcribed meetings into a formal document that prioritizes actionable project controls and clear communication.
The agenda must begin with a formal title block and a "PRIORITY FOLLOW-UP / ACTION REGISTER" that lists all action items with a checkbox, responsible party, and due date.
The "CALL TO ORDER" section should state the meeting's purpose, date, and the project's current status.
The "INTRODUCTIONS" section requires listing all attendees, including the Owner, Construction Project Manager (CPM), Contractor, and Architect/Engineers, with their contact details if provided.
The "OWNER REQUESTED ITEMS / PROJECT PRIORITIES" section is for documenting specific owner requests, operational priorities, and required contractor responses, cross-referencing action items to the register.
The "PROJECT IDENTIFICATION / CONTRACTUAL REQUIREMENTS" section summarizes the project scope, contract details, duration, liquidated damages, and financial requirements like PO status or change authorization rules.
The "ORDER OF RESPONSIBILITY" section clarifies the roles and duties of the Owner/CPM, Contractor, and Architect/Engineers, noting any ambiguities in authority.
The "CALENDAR DAYS / PROGRESS OF WORK" section must capture the project start date, duration, completion milestones, phasing requirements, and any known delays or risks affecting the schedule.
The "ACCESS CONTROL / BADGING / SECURITY" section details procedures for site entry, badging requirements, background checks, and rules for parking and deliveries, highlighting potential delays.
The "PROJECT PROCEDURES & COORDINATION" section outlines operational rules, including limits of operation, submittal data process, progress schedule updates, payment procedures, and inspection protocols.
The "SUBSTANTIAL COMPLETION / FINAL COMPLETION" section defines expectations for the project's punch-list, owner turnover, closeout documentation, warranties, and final payment.
The final "GENERAL PRINCIPLES / OPEN DISCUSSION / NEXT STEPS" section is for capturing key principles like teamwork, unresolved questions, and immediate next actions, concluding with a note on record accuracy.

name: MC Meeting Minutes (Subcontractor)
author: Velum
description: Paste a meeting transcript. Get minutes with actions, RFIs, schedule, and items to verify.
body:
This document provides a comprehensive set of instructions for a construction project engineer to take minutes during recurring subcontractor coordination meetings.
Before starting, the project engineer must configure the PROJECT SETUP block with project-specific details, including type, delivery method, location conventions, exact names of all involved parties, common company abbreviations, and any custom agenda sections.
The assigned role is an experienced construction project engineer responsible for taking minutes, with expected knowledge of commercial construction processes like sequencing, submittals, RFIs, and change management, writing for an audience of other field professionals.
The system should automatically correct misheard technical terms in the transcript by referencing an extensive, though not exhaustive, DOMAIN VOCABULARY list covering structure, envelope, MEP, interiors, site, and process-related construction terminology, while preserving trade shorthand and not translating it into plain English.
All spoken names of companies, firms, and individuals must be matched to the exact spellings provided in the PROJECT SETUP, and any names not found in the setup list should be transcribed as heard and listed under a NEEDS VERIFICATION section.
Numerical and location data, including RFI/submittal numbers, dates, durations, lead times, and dimensions, must be captured verbatim without rounding or paraphrasing, using standard construction format for dimensions, and marking any unclear numbers with (verify).
Each item in the minutes must be categorized by its statement type: QUESTION RAISED, COMMITMENT, DIRECTION GIVEN, DECISION, or INFORMATION, ensuring that vague statements are not misclassified as firm commitments.
The final output must be a structured bulleted list following a specific 10-section format: ATTENDANCE, SAFETY, ISSUES BY PARTY, RFIs AND SUBMITTALS, SCHEDULE, QUALITY AND OBSERVATIONS, LOGISTICS, COMMERCIAL, ACTION ITEMS, and NEEDS VERIFICATION, with "Not discussed" noted for any section not covered in the meeting.
The minutes must be complete, capturing every item raised without consolidation, and should omit greetings, small talk, and editorial comments while focusing solely on the content discussed in the specific meeting.

name: Electrical Client Call Intake and Job Notes
author: Velum
description: Paste a call transcript. Get client details, job tasks, materials, schedule, and follow-ups.
body:
The primary purpose is to provide a structured template for analyzing and summarizing an electrical client's phone call to efficiently create or update client profiles, estimates, jobs, and schedules.
Classify the call by type (e.g., new client, existing job), and identify required actions such as creating a client profile, preparing an estimate, or scheduling work.
Briefly summarize the call's purpose, the client's request, the outcome, and the next steps in 2-5 bullet points.
Extract specific client and property details like name, contact information, address, and relationship to the property, noting any necessary follow-up for missing information.
Create a clear, itemized list of all requested work, with each task written as a concise scope item suitable for an estimate.
For troubleshooting calls, organize information under specific headings: Reported Symptoms, Problem History, Tests Already Made, Possible Causes Discussed, and Diagnostic Follow-Up Needed.
Compile a separate, copy-ready list of notes for the office, including details for estimating, scheduling, client communication, and purchasing.
Create another separate, copy-ready list of notes for the field technician, covering work locations, site conditions, access details, and problem history.
List all mentioned materials and equipment, categorizing them as Contractor-Supplied, Client-Supplied, or Material Decisions Still Needed.
Summarize all scheduling and access information, including preferences, urgency, deadlines, and coordination details, distinguishing between confirmed arrangements and preferences.
Document any clear decisions made or commitments given by either the client or the office during the call.
Create distinct follow-up lists for the office, field technicians, and the client, detailing required actions for each party.
List any unresolved questions that could impact pricing, scheduling, materials, or the scope of work, phrasing each as a direct question.
Capture any relevant personal or relationship details that could enhance future client communication and service.
Conclude by identifying the specific records that need to be created or updated as a result of the call, such as a new client profile, a revised estimate, or field notes.

name: Job Site Consultation
author: Velum
description: For contractors. It summarizes site conditions, goals, and budget into a structured overview.
body:
The primary purpose is to document an initial on-site consultation for an outdoor living construction company by capturing and organizing all relevant details from the conversation.
Key client and project information to be recorded includes names, address, contact details, referral source, and the date of the consultation.
An assessment of the site's existing conditions is required, covering property type, yard access, drainage, soil, existing structures, and any known constraints like HOA rules or easements.
It is essential to understand the client's goals by distinguishing between must-have and nice-to-have features, identifying problems they want to solve, and clarifying how they intend to use the new space.
The desired layout and design direction should be documented, including the overall vision, size, flow between areas, potential elevation changes, and needs for privacy or shade.
A checklist of specific features discussed, such as patios, pools, outdoor kitchens, firepits, and lighting, must be completed with relevant notes.
The client's preferences for materials and style, including specific materials, colors, overall aesthetic (e.g., modern, rustic), and any mentioned brands or examples, need to be captured.
Details from any budget discussion, including the range, flexibility, potential for a phased approach, and the client's expectations, should be noted.
The project's timeline and urgency must be established by recording the desired start and completion dates, along with any deadlines tied to specific events.
Observations on the decision-making process are important, noting the primary decision-makers, their price sensitivity, and their readiness to proceed with the project.
The agreed-upon next steps, such as the need for a design proposal, estimate, site measurements, or a follow-up meeting, must be clearly outlined.
A section for additional notes is provided to capture unique details, potential red flags or opportunities, and ideas for custom "wow-factor" features.
The process concludes with a final instruction to create a 3-5 bullet point summary for a quick project overview and an optional tip to generate a project nickname and client summary for cleaner record-keeping.

name: Protokoll Ortstermin - ifb
author: Velum
description: From OT transcript: neutral protocol with facts and measures. Gaps marked.
body:
The main objective is to create a structured, professional protocol from the transcription of an on-site appointment regarding building damage from the perspective of an expert.
The protocol must bear the exact heading “Year-Month-Day Protokoll Ortstermin (OT) [number]”, such as “26-03-25 Protokoll OT1”, and the file name should be identical.
Formal header data such as location, date, project number, responsible expert (e.g., Nick Baumann) and the duration of the appointment must be stated in the protocol.
All attendees, including policyholder, remediation contractor, property management and adjuster, must be listed with full name and function.
The damage description, which includes the date and the course of the damage event, must be documented briefly and in detail.
The specific characteristics of the building, such as object type, year of construction, construction type, floors, slabs, roof type, windows, doors, electrical installation, energy source and heating surfaces, must be recorded exactly according to the specified categories. Items not mentioned must be labeled as “not mentioned - please add!”.
Qualities, dimensions, materials and structural assemblies must be structured by building, floor, apartment and room, with objective findings and measures presented room by room. For unmentioned details, use the note “not mentioned - please add!”.
Measures for other areas or units, such as creating an inspection opening to determine the cause, as well as discussed common areas like basement or stairwell, must also be listed.
For discussions about recourse claims, the time of execution, the responsible company and the availability of invoices must be documented separately.
Additional agreements on the further procedure, such as the submission of offers (e.g., by Tronex GmbH by a specified date), must be recorded separately.
The protocol language must be neutral, objective and professional, using technically correct terms and avoiding colloquial language and speculation.
Dimensions must be given in the format “X.XX m x Y.YY m = Z.ZZ m2”, and the specified structures must be strictly adhered to.
Information that is not understood or not mentioned must not be supplemented by the AI, but must be explicitly labeled “not understood” or “not mentioned”.

name: Project Manager - Construction Update
author: Velum
description: Log site updates by building. Track trade progress, inspections, and assignable action items.
body:
Weekly construction update involves the General Contractor (GC), Project Engineer (PE), Superintendents, and various trades like electricians, framers, and plumbers.
The meeting is led by the GC, progressing from building to building and then to general site work such as curb and gutter, and road grading.
During building walkthroughs, all interior and exterior trades are reviewed.
Note-taking follows an outline format, requiring start and end dates or durations for each trade.
Tracking inspections for each trade and identifying prerequisites for inspection completion is necessary.
At the conclusion of each building segment, action items for each trade are determined, along with any identified barriers.
Action item summaries should be logically organized based on the presented information.
Information organization, accurate tracking of durations, and identification of potential task completion barriers are crucial.
Information is organized by building as the primary subject, with interior and exterior as secondary subjects, and trades as tertiary items.
Building F: Interior plumbing trim is scheduled from Monday, 8/4/2025, to Friday, 8/8/2025, requiring flooring and countertops to be completed beforehand.
Building F: Exterior siding trade faces manpower issues with only three workers onsite, causing delays.
Building F: Siding trade needs to be ready for a lath inspection by 8/5/2025, which requires the framer to install awning timber frames at each breezeway after the lather removes foam.
Building F Action Items: Track siding delay due to manpower shortages and request additional personnel.
Building F Action Items: Siding trade must remove foam at each breezeway awning location to allow the framer to install the awning timber frame.
Building F Action Items: Framer to install awning timber frames at each breezeway location.
Clubhouse: Insulation is complete and passed inspection on 7/28/2025.
Clubhouse: Drywall is hung except for four locations pending gas line installation.
Clubhouse: Plumber cannot install the gas line until RFI 115 is answered.
Clubhouse: The tape and mud process will commence after the screw pattern inspection, scheduled for 8/1/2025.

name: sub meeting
author: Velum
description: Paste a transcript for a summary of experience, welding, safety, and pay. Marks gaps Not Discussed.
body:
This document provides a standardized template for summarizing an interview with an applicant for Ironworkers Local 597, ensuring a concise and factual evaluation.
The summary begins by capturing the applicant's basic personal and employment information, including name, location, current job, and pay expectations.
It requires a detailed summary of the applicant's overall work history relevant to construction and ironworking, including specific types of experience like structural steel, rigging, and heavy equipment operation.
The template documents any direct ironworking experience, specifying the types of tasks performed, duration, and any previous union involvement.
A dedicated section assesses the applicant's welding experience, including processes used (SMAW, FCAW, etc.), formal training, certifications, and a self-assessed confidence level.
It lists all safety training and certifications mentioned by the applicant, such as OSHA, fall protection, and TWIC, to gauge their safety knowledge.
The form inventories the applicant's ownership of essential ironworking tools, like spud wrenches and a tool belt, and identifies any tools they would need to acquire.
Work readiness is evaluated by summarizing the applicant's availability, transportation, willingness to travel and work overtime, and comfort with job-specific conditions like heights and heat.
Pay expectations are clearly documented, noting the applicant's desired and lowest acceptable wage, and whether they understand entry-level pay scales.
The applicant's motivation for pursuing an ironworking career is summarized, including their long-term goals and interest in apprenticeship.
The template includes a section for interviewer observations on potential strengths and areas needing follow-up, based solely on the interview content.
An overall applicant snapshot provides a brief 3-5 sentence summary of the candidate's background, experience, training, and expectations.
The format concludes with sections for suggested follow-up questions and a quick-reference checklist summarizing the applicant's qualifications across key areas like experience, training, and pay.

name: ZCP_PLAUDIO_v1.2 – Field Visit Voice Protocol (Bidding Phase)
author: Velum
description: Analysis of the transcription of a BPI discovery
body:
The main objective is to generate a complete, clear, and structured commercial discovery sheet from a transcript of an exchange, intended to be used by sales professionals or AIs.
The discovery sheet has three purposes: to prepare the price announcement and closing of the sale, to control the quality of the commercial discovery, and to allow for later file resumption.
The mandatory structure of the sheet includes: a summary of the project and profile, identification of the interlocutors, a summary of the exchange, consulted competition, actions to be taken, discovery questions with answers, unasked questions, analysis and recommendations, and the full transcript.
The summary of the project and profile must include information such as first name, last name, address, phone, email, date and time of the appointment, client status, client history, nature of the project, number of openings, desired deadline, and date of the next appointment.
The identification of interlocutors requires specifying the number of people present, their first names and roles, and identifying Florian Volle if present, clearly attributing each intervention.
The summary of the exchange must be professional, concise, and structured, detailing intentions, expectations, implicit criteria, objections, emotions, key client phrases, and detectable non-verbal signals.
The consulted competition section must indicate if other companies have been contacted, with details on the name, number of quotes, date, amount, and perceived advantages/disadvantages.
The actions to be taken must precisely list the next steps: quotes to be prepared, visuals to be sent, simulations to be done, questions to be completed, documents to be collected, follow-up strategy, technical points to be validated, and additional needs to be explored.
The discovery questions with answers section must include the 17 essential questions, indicate if they were asked, provide a precise answer with context, include verbatim client phrases, and mention doubts or incomplete answers.
Unasked questions must be listed in their full formulation, with an introduction specifying their listing to assess the quality of the discovery.
The analysis and recommendations must provide a strategic analysis of the client profile, decision-making style, opportunities, obstacles, tipping points, and give precise advice to maximize closing chances.
The full transcript must be inserted, cleaned of hesitations, repetitions, or noise, with each speaker identified by first name or role, and maintaining chronology.
The 17 essential questions to be included cover client aspects (owner, installation, household, moving, work, heating/air conditioning), project (reflection, deadline, facade, knowledge, influence of relatives, expectations), and finances (criteria, purchasing habits, financing, budget, taxable income).
Specific questions must be asked if the project concerns ITE, addressing consumption, surface area, year of construction, type of walls, insulation, temperatures, priorities, aids, source of contact, and decision-maker profile.
The expected format is a professional, structured sheet, with visible titles, clear wording, allowing another salesperson or AI to take over the file and close without re-interviewing the client.

name: Roof Takeoff
author: Velum
description: Turns roofing transcripts into notes. It captures materials, measurements, and action items.
body:
The primary objective is to analyze a roofing takeoff meeting transcription and generate structured meeting notes, focusing on roofing takeoff details and identifying potential errors or insights.
The summary requires clear section headers including Introductions, Project Overview, Roofing Takeoff Details, Key Discussions, Decisions Made, Action Items, Expert Contributions, Major Questions Raised, and Next Steps & Follow-Up.
Within "Roofing Takeoff Details," information to be organized includes measurement methods and tools, area calculations, material quantities, noted discrepancies, and referenced standards or protocols.
Related discussion topics, particularly those concerning takeoff procedures, data accuracy, and technology, should be logically grouped.
All decisions made must be highlighted, specifying the decision, the decision-maker, and any provided rationale or context.
Action items need to be extracted, including the responsible person(s), deadlines if mentioned, and relevant context or dependencies.
Expert phrasing or unique conceptual language should be included as corrected quotes, focusing on statements that clarify takeoff methodology, challenges, or influence next steps, rather than verbatim transcription.
Significant questions and their corresponding answers, including who asked them, must be documented.
Planned follow-up meetings, objectives, or timelines should be outlined as next steps.
The transcript should be reviewed for possible transcription errors such as misattributions, omissions, or inconsistencies, and any areas where the transcript may not align with the original context or intent should be flagged.
Additional insights or observations that could be valuable for future meetings or process improvements should be provided.
The summary must maintain a professional, neutral tone, be skimmable, and retain depth and technical detail, especially in roofing takeoff sections.
A final review should verify the accuracy of names, assignments, and deadlines, ensure all roofing takeoff data is clearly organized and easy to reference, and integrate corrected quotes while highlighting identified errors or additional insights.

name: WESTIRON — Residential Remodel Walkthrough
author: Velum
description: Paste a job recording. Output an HVAC walkthrough in order; gaps noted; and a photo checklist.
body:
This document provides a structured template for creating an HVAC estimate by summarizing a recording of a technician's job walkthrough.
The template requires capturing client information, including name, address, and contact details.
The client's concerns must be documented, covering the reason for system replacement, specific issues, desired new system features, and current comfort levels regarding temperature, humidity, and air quality.
Details about the existing thermostat are required, such as brand, type (heat pump, Wi-Fi, multi-stage), blower motor condition, and wiring.
The estimate must list the supplies needed and the sizes of each air return.
A thorough inspection of the air handler is necessary, noting its brand, tonnage, age, presence of leaks, and other components like heat strips and drain pans, along with its location and dimensions.
The insulation section requires noting the conditioned square footage, insulation type and depth, baffles, remove existing insulation.
Condenser details to be recorded include brand, tonnage, age, refrigerant type, line sizes, and the condition of related components like the disconnect and hurricane pad.
Information from the breaker panel should be gathered, specifically the brand and the size of breakers for the condenser, air handler, dehumidifier, and furnace.
The client's reaction to discussion points like surge protection, coastal coating, extended labor agreements, whole house filters, and insulation add-ons must be noted.
The template includes a section to list optional upgrades the client agreed to, such as surge protection, UV lights, or a service agreement.
A checklist of necessary materials like pans, float sensors, disconnects, and drain lines must be filled out.
A final notes section is for any other relevant information, such as access issues, scheduling, pricing discussions, or mentions of competitor quotes.
The process concludes with a photo checklist to ensure the technician has taken pictures of the thermostat, air handler, insulation, condenser, and breaker panel.

name: Construction/Contractor — Calls, Meetings & Action Items
author: Velum
description: For contractors. Input calls or meetings. Output clear roles, alerts, decisions, and follow-ups.
body:
The primary purpose is to convert audio from calls, meetings, and site visits in residential and commercial construction into structured internal notes, detailing responsibilities, alerts, decisions, and follow-up actions.
Summaries should adapt in length to the source material, using clear headings and bullet points for brevity in short instructions while retaining detail for technical discussions, and omitting empty sections.
Identify the project, subject, date, time, format, and location of the recording, and list all participants with their companies and roles, separating them from individuals who are merely mentioned.
Prioritize time-sensitive issues, business blockers, and safety concerns, labeling them as "Urgent," "Deadline," or "Important," and specifying the next action, responsible person, deadline, and any blocked activities.
List all tasks as open checkboxes grouped by the responsible person, detailing the task, requester, due date, and status, and distinguishing between suggested actions and confirmed assignments.
Summarize the meeting's outcome and organize key details by topic, chronologically documenting decisions, prices, quantities, materials, and schedule changes while attributing them to the correct person.
For technical or municipal discussions, capture each requirement, the requesting authority, necessary documentation, responsible party, and deadlines, and preserve the stated work sequence.
Neutrally document customer concerns, including the issue, requested remedy, and resolution, attributing disputed claims and expressed dissatisfaction without assigning blame.
Identify unresolved issues, conflicting instructions, and pending items, and list agreed-upon follow-up meetings or inspections with their details, distinguishing between agreed tasks and suggested follow-ups.
Base all notes strictly on the recording and provided context, never inventing information, and accurately reflect uncertainties, reported facts versus verified ones, and preserve timestamps for key events.

name: PROJECT Meeting Summary
author: Velum
description: Create a meeting minutes draft from architectural/interior project meeting notes that even absentees can understand and act upon. Unclear points are converted into clarification questions, and decisions, approvals, and changes are organized. Also outputs a re-entry template for generating the final version.
body:
Define rules and formats for creating meeting minutes for architectural/interior projects, enabling absentees and busy superiors to accurately grasp content, make judgments, and give instructions.
It is an absolute rule to assign [Field Tags] to all items, and for decisions, clearly state [Judgment Criteria], [Approver], [Impact]; for changes, clearly state [Before Change → After Change], [Originator], [Impact], [Action].
Prohibit speculation by marking unclear speakers or participants as "To be confirmed" and converting them into Requests for Information (RFI), thereby ensuring the accuracy of information.
The output consists of two parts: "A) Draft Version (with confirmation questions)" and "B) Re-entry Template for Final Version Generation" for the user to input answers.
The draft meeting minutes include sections for meeting overview, agenda, decisions, change management, detailed minutes, risks, next meeting, and a 1-minute summary for superiors.

name: DBM SV
author: Velum
description: Organize site meetings. Tracks progress, claims, and updates for structured project documentation.
body:
Welcome and Introductions are conducted.
Attendance and Apologies are noted.
The Adoption of Agenda and Additional Items are addressed, including discussion and agreement on amendments to the Draft Agenda.
Matters Arising from the Previous Meeting are reviewed, specifically a matter regarding prefinancing of the Works, considering referral for an Opinion versus a Decision.
Administrative matters are discussed, including issues arising from the Employer’s change in name, the appointment of the Engineer and delegation of authority, the appointment of the Contractor’s Representative, DAB Disclosures, and DAB’s invoices.
Documentation for the DAB is prepared, including a Joint Statement, Latest Reports (Monthly Progress Report, Minutes of Site Meetings & Programme Updates), Register of Work Programme Updates, and Claims Register.
The Programme is reviewed, featuring the Contractor’s presentation of his programme, including the date and version of the update, details of changes from the previous version, and an explanation of the critical path of activities.
Progress is assessed, with the Engineer’s presentation of progress of design, including progress versus programme.
Environmental & social safeguards are reviewed, focusing on the Contractor’s compliance.
Updates on other matters are provided, including Variations and Addendums, a List of Variations, and Payment Certificates detailing the amount certified to date and the "S" curve.
Contract administration and matters of concern are addressed, allowing both parties to explain current concerns with the Contract to the DAB, particularly regarding contract administration functions not being followed, and difficulties with Right of Way.
Notices of Claims / Claims / Disputes Status are reviewed.
An update of unresolved issues that Parties may refer to the DAB is provided for both the Contractor and the Employer.
Any other business is discussed.
Confirmation of dates of Meetings in 2025 is made.
The meeting is closed.

name: Tender - Site survey Template / specification document
author: Velum
description: For surveyors. Enter site access, restrictions and package notes. Outputs a tender-ready spec section.
body:
The primary goal is to create a site survey template for gathering site-specific information, which will be integrated into a larger specification document for conducting tenders for CAT B fit-outs.
The template must be structured by specific work packages and include sections for preliminaries, project location details, restrictions, access information, and other relevant points.
The site survey needs to capture information that will influence the installation of various packages, which typically include Partitions, MF ceilings, Ceilings, Decoration, Doors, Joinery, Glazing, Acoustics, and demolition.
For partitions, the survey must record floor-to-ceiling measurements, void dimensions above and below, and details of fixing substrates like the floor slab, soffit type, and perimeter wall composition.
For MF and other ceilings, key information includes heights, soffit substrate types, and any noise restrictions that might affect the installation of hangers.
The decoration survey involves assessing existing finishes that require redecoration to determine the scope of work.
Door surveys must note if matching existing finishes is required, gathering necessary information and photos if so.
The joinery survey needs to determine if new installations, such as tea points or skirtings, must match existing ones.
Glazing surveys should check if new installations need to match any existing glazing.
For acoustics, the survey must measure voids above and below partitions as this is critical for acoustic barrier performance.
The demolition section requires documenting all existing items to be removed, supported by photos and specific mark-ups on drawings.
A miscellaneous section is included to capture any unique, one-off items required for the specific project.
This completed site survey document will constitute the initial part of the tender specification document, with the second part being added after all specifications are finalized and agreed upon.

name: IBTK Construction Report
author: Velum
description: Structures dictations into construction reports with measurements by trade and a completed checklist.
body:
The goal is to structure an unstructured dictation transcript of an on-site appointment into a logically, technically correct, and clearly organized on-site appointment report.
The header section of the report must contain the on-site appointment, project number, object location, date of the on-site appointment, and participants (if mentioned) in this order.
Principles for report creation include only mentioning trades that are named, logically summarizing rooms without duplication, exact adoption of measurements with specific units (m2, lfm, pcs., "flat rate"), summing partial measurements per room/trade, and using a decimal comma with two decimal places.
Sealing work is to be assigned to the tiler trade, and electrical as well as sanitary are to be mentioned as subcontractors only if work is mentioned in the dictation.
If "tabular" or "table" is mentioned, an additional tabular overview by trades must be created.
Missing information must not be guessed; the position is to be recorded and the measurement left blank or "flat rate" used if stated in the dictation.
The trades are to be listed in the following order: drywall, masonry and plastering, screed layer, floor layer, painter, tiler (including sealing), carpenter, sanitary (SUB), electrical (SUB), and drying/demolition, provided they are mentioned in the dictation.
The content structure per trade provides for stating the trade, followed by rooms with measures/material/specification and partial measurements, as well as a sum per room and a total sum per trade.
Special features for drying/demolition include listing demolition work with measurement or "flat rate", mold treatment, partitions, air cleaning and disinfection, as well as equipment use with quantity and period.
The conclusion of the report must contain a checklist with stored images, available measurement, updated offer, consultation with the customer, and documented measures, followed by the date of processing and a signature.

name: BL Construction Site Report 2.0
author: Velum
description: Paste a recording. Get an HVAC estimate walkthrough with Not discussed gaps and photo list.
body:
This document provides a structured template for creating an HVAC estimate by summarizing a technician's walkthrough of a job site.
The first section requires collecting client information, including name, address, and contact details.
The "Concerns" section details the intake interview, focusing on the reasons for system replacement, specific issues to resolve, and interest in humidity control or improved air quality.
The "Thermostat" section involves documenting its brand, type (heat pump, Wi-Fi, multi-stage), blower motor condition, and wire count.
The "Returns & Supplies" section is for listing needed supplies and the sizes of each return mentioned.
The "Air Handler" section specifies capturing details like brand, tonnage, age, location, dimensions, and whether components like the disconnect, drain, or pan need replacement.
The "Insulation" section requires noting the conditioned square footage, existing insulation type and depth, and if removal is needed.
The "Condenser" section is for recording its brand, tonnage, age, refrigerant type, line sizes, and the condition of related components like the hurricane pad and disconnect.
The "Breaker Panel" section lists the panel brand and the sizes of breakers for the condenser, air handler, dehumidifier, and furnace.
The "Discussion Points" section is for noting client reactions to proposed add-ons like surge protection, coastal coating, and extended labor agreements.
"Optional Upgrades Selected" is a list of all upgrades the client agreed to, such as surge protection, a whole house filter, or a service agreement.
"Materials Needed" is a checklist for specific items required for the job, including a pan, hang kit, float sensors, and drain line.
The "Notes" section is for any other relevant information, such as access issues, scheduling, pricing discussions, or competitor quotes.
The process concludes with a photo checklist to ensure the technician has taken pictures of the thermostat, air handler, insulation, condenser, and breaker panel.

name: electrical project management
author: Velum
description: Transforms voice notes into structured reports and clear findings, BNQ compliant. Ready to integrate.
body:
The role is to write residential property inspection reports in Quebec by transforming vocal notes into clear, structured findings, compliant with BNQ 3009-500 standard and Kalité Inspection Inc. style.
The report must follow a mandatory structure starting with general information (property, conditions, persons present, inspection type, limitations), followed by findings by section.
Each finding per section must include a title, a description beginning with "During the inspection, the inspector noted that...", an explanation of the risk, a clear recommendation, and end with a specific danger level.
Mandatory sections to cover in the findings include structural, architectural (exterior, interior, common, garage), plumbing, electrical, heating, air conditioning, ventilation systems, attic, insulation, and security.
Findings must also address frequent issues in Quebec such as pyrite, pyrrhotite, ochre deposit, drainage, radon, UFFI, asbestos, lead, mold, contamination, and infestations.
The report must include supplementary information stating that the inspection is visual and non-destructive, in accordance with BNQ 3009-500 standard.
The danger level for each finding must be chosen exclusively from an authorized list, including terms like "Warning", "Potential danger", "Defect to correct", and "Urgent repair".
Writing must be professional, objective, and neutral, using complete sentences without jargon, without using "I" or "we", and without inventing information; if information is missing, it must be indicated.
The logic for interpreting vocal notes involves transforming brief remarks into complete and professional findings, including risk analysis, appropriate recommendation, and the correct danger level, all within the Quebec context.
The output format is a complete report, structured by section, with each finding visually separated, and an option to group similar issues within the same section into a single coherent finding.

name: Official Procedure and Script Generator
author: Velum
description: Paste rule transcript. Get a one-page sheet: key rule, IF-THEN, bans, disputes, scripts.
body:
This document outlines the creation of a structured operational guide for poll workers, defining the AI's role in generating this guide and detailing the specific content and formatting requirements for a one-page "official procedure" sheet for the June primary.
The AI's primary task is to extract key information from election rules, such as main principles, "IF-THEN" scenarios, prohibited actions, dispute resolution steps, and pre-written scripts for poll workers, and then structure this information into a clear, at-a-glance reference guide.
The guide's format must include a main title, a subtitle, and distinct sections with specific titles like THE POLLPAD RULE and POLL WORKER SCRIPT, using consistent formatting for conditional rules, prohibited actions (bulleted with 'X'), dispute resolution (numbered list), and scripts (quoted text).
For the June Primary, the guide must address confusion when voters from third parties (e.g., Libertarian, Conservative, Socialist, Green) do not appear on the poll pad and when voters try to change party affiliation, by providing clear language and a neutral script for poll workers.
Action items for the June Primary guide include drafting an "Important Notice" about third-party voters, adding a statement that Democrats and Republicans cannot change affiliation at the table, finalizing a poll worker script, and confirming the legal deadline for party changes in New Jersey.
The guide must include explicit step-by-step instructions for poll workers on how to handle voters not listed on the poll pad, with the primary resolution being to issue a provisional ballot and a secondary step to add the voter through the poll pad's "add provisional voter" menu option.
AI suggestions highlight unresolved issues, including the need to confirm the exact legal deadline for party affiliation changes, finalize the list of third parties to be named, assign responsibility for content creation and layout, and verify the on-screen labels and workflow in the poll pad software.

name: Hoel Roofing Inspection Report
author: Velum
description: Notes are transformed into a ready-to-send report, categorized by trades. Open items are marked.
body:
You act as an experienced German architect and construction manager, whose task is to create professional construction site and meeting reports for direct forwarding to clients, specialist planners, and companies, not to summarize conversations.
The writing style requires fluent, technical German in coherent paragraphs and complete sentences, avoiding bullet-point formulations and typical AI phrases.
Before drafting each point, information must be mentally organized according to occasion, technical situation, assessment, decision, instruction, responsibility, and further procedure, without explicitly naming these categories, to ensure a fluid report.
The report must follow a fixed structure, including a project header, weather, meetings, attendees, on-site construction management, a general section, and separate chapters for each trade, with statements sorted by trades and not chronologically.
The content should be factual, technical, neutral, and written without assigning blame, making assumptions, or inventing content, explaining contexts and combining related information in one paragraph.
Site manager logic requires the documentation of decisions, instructions, schedule changes, defects, hindrances, responsibilities, open items, risks, and company feedback; if information is missing, formulations such as "Requires further clarification" should be used.
Preferred formulations include active and directive phrases such as "After consultation", "Site management instructs", or "Execution takes place", to clarify the instructive nature.
The final product should have the quality of a handwritten report created by an experienced construction manager, ensuring readability, comprehensibility, and legally compliant documentation, clearly distinguishing itself from an AI summary, meeting minutes, or a task list.
It is noted that the prompt will be adjusted or divided if necessary to ensure full adoption by the AI and to further personalize the style.

name: Year End Warranty Walk
author: Velum
description: Record goals and room details. Track decisions and actions for clear project planning.
body:
The CasaKeepers project meeting template is designed to capture essential information from initial client meetings for construction projects, ensuring all key details are recorded for planning and execution.
The "Project Snapshot" section gathers fundamental project details, including the type of project, client names, address, meeting date, and attendees from both CasaKeepers and the client side.
The "Big-Picture Goals" section focuses on understanding the client's overall vision, including the remodel's purpose, lifestyle motivations, design preferences, desired timeline, and budget considerations.
The "Room-by-Room Notes" section provides a structured format for detailed discussion of each specific area, covering existing conditions, problems, desired changes, dimensions, technical considerations like structure and HVAC, and material preferences.
The "Global Design & Scope Notes" section captures overarching project changes that affect the entire structure, such as wall reconfigurations, additions, ceiling height adjustments, major system impacts (plumbing, electrical, HVAC), and key future selections.
The "Home Occupancy & Phasing" section addresses the practical logistics of the remodel, determining if the client will live on-site, any required project phasing, and daily access or living arrangements.
The "Decisions Made During Meeting" section serves to formally document any specific agreements or choices finalized during the conversation, along with their relevant context.
The "Action Items" section lists specific tasks to be completed, assigning ownership and setting deadlines to ensure accountability and progress.
The "Next Steps" section clarifies immediate follow-up responsibilities for both the CasaKeepers team and the client, and outlines upcoming meetings or design milestones.
The "Additional Context / Observations" section provides a freeform space to note supplementary information, such as client emotional cues, unstated concerns, or other insights gained during the meeting.

name: Construction Team-v01
author: Velum
description: For construction teams. Input points; output minutes with decisions, actions, owner, deadline, open points.
body:
The main goal is to define a strict template for minuting a formal construction team meeting, emphasizing factual, concise, and verifiable reporting.
The minutes should begin with meeting details, including project details, attendees, and discussed documents, followed by a short management summary of the key points.
The meeting starts with the chairman's opening and the adoption of the agenda, directly noting decisions, actions, or open points.
The minutes of the previous meeting are approved, the status of action points is evaluated (completed, open, or escalation), and the assurance of earlier decisions is checked.
There is an agenda item for announcements from all involved parties, such as the client and contractor, with specific attention to absences and blocking issues.
Contractual topics, such as scope, responsibilities, and deadlines, are discussed if mentioned, with reference to relevant contractual documents.
The Safety (VGM) agenda item addresses incidents, toolboxes, safety rounds, and any deviations from the V&G plan.
Structural topics are discussed per component (e.g., facade, roof) focusing on the status, outstanding choices, bottlenecks, and quality aspects.
Installation topics are split by discipline (Mechanical, Electrical, Control Technology) to discuss progress, bottlenecks, clashes, and testing moments.
Planning is analyzed based on the critical path, risks, necessary decision moments, and coordination of execution.
Additional and less work (VTW) is recorded in an overview table with details on status, financial and planning impact, and the party responsible for action.
The meeting includes an 'any other business' round for questions per party and an item for other relevant matters not fitting into other categories.
The closing contains a summary by the chairman and the schedule for the next meeting, followed by a decision list, action list, and a list of open points.

name: Detailed Factual Multi-Pass v.2
author: Velum
description: From audio or transcripts, captures decisions, dates, scope, action items, and risks in one report.
body:
The primary purpose is to create a detailed, factual record from a recording by performing five systematic extraction passes before writing the final report, prioritizing accuracy and completeness over brevity and avoiding assumptions.
The first pass focuses on extracting confirmed decisions, commitments, agreements, instructions, and responsibilities, while distinguishing them from mere proposals or discussions.
The second pass requires a specific review for all time-related information, including dates, times, deadlines, schedules, and work sequences, preserving exact wording when a calendar date is uncertain.
The third pass is dedicated to extracting technical details such as work scope, measurements, quantities, materials, product specifications, installation methods, and site conditions, retaining exact terminology.
The fourth pass involves identifying all people, companies, speaker roles, and assignments of responsibility to track who said or agreed to what.
The fifth pass aims to capture all problems, risks, contradictions, and any unclear information, reporting conflicts as they are without attempting to resolve them and marking items that require audio verification.
A final verification pass is required after the five extraction passes to compare the collected information against the source again, ensuring no important details are missed, misrepresented, or invented.
The final output format should be a structured report including a recording overview, a detailed chronological record, and separate sections for confirmed decisions, proposed items, schedule details, technical scope, action items, problems, unresolved questions, items needing audio verification, and key direct quotes.
The final accuracy rule mandates that the record must clearly distinguish between confirmed facts, confirmed decisions, proposed items, unresolved issues, and unclear information, with source fidelity taking priority over polished writing.

name: RENOVATION PROJECT ASSESSMENT
author: Velum
description: Paste a site-visit transcript. Get a structured scope write-up with details and follow-ups.
body:
This document provides detailed instructions for a construction estimator to convert an on-site conversation transcript into a structured, estimator-ready project assessment for Work With Miller LLC.
The primary objective is to extract and organize every project detail from a recording, reorganizing the information according to construction workflow, without losing, simplifying, or inventing any information.
Strict accuracy rules mandate clearly distinguishing between confirmed work, options, recommendations, and responsibilities, preserving all specific details like dimensions and materials, and using specific labels to denote the status of information.
The output must follow a specific 18-section format, starting with CLIENT AND PROJECT INFORMATION, followed by a PROJECT OVERVIEW, a method for organizing the scope, and then a DETAILED SCOPE OF WORK broken down by construction phase.
The scope of work must be organized chronologically into categories like preconstruction, demolition, framing, and finishes, detailing all tasks, materials, and responsibilities for each phase.
Subsequent sections must detail existing conditions, client selections, responsibility assignments, options discussed, exclusions, permit information, all measurements, and a list of specific materials mentioned.
The assessment must also include sections covering logistics, scheduling, budget discussions, a list of questions requiring follow-up, and a summary of potential risks that could impact the project's cost or schedule.
The final section, COMPLETE INFORMATION-PRESERVATION NOTES, is mandatory for capturing any relevant details that do not fit elsewhere, ensuring every piece of information from the transcript is preserved.
The document specifies strict writing and formatting standards, requiring clear Markdown headings, numbered sections, bulleted lists with action verbs, professional terminology, and an avoidance of conversational language or contractual promises.

name: Construction Meeting / Design Team BITB
author: Velum
description: For construction teams. Structures meetings per discipline with actions, deadlines, and financial updates.
body:
The goal is to record design team and construction meetings with a template for automatic summary and classification of discussed points by discipline in Velum, including an overview of actions and risks.
The 'General' section covers project coordination, planning, safety, and logistics, where for each topic the summary, actions/decisions, responsible party, and deadline are recorded.
The 'Architectural' section focuses on shell construction, finishing, facades, and painting, where for each topic the summary, actions/decisions, responsible party, and deadline are recorded.
The 'Structural' section includes foundations, concrete and steel structures, and stability calculations, where for each topic the summary, actions/decisions, responsible party, and deadline are recorded.
The 'Installations' section covers mechanical and electrical installations such as ventilation, piping, and lighting, where for each topic the summary, actions/decisions, responsible party, and deadline are recorded.
The 'Utilities' section focuses on the coordination and connection of gas, water, electricity, and data, where for each topic the summary, actions/decisions, responsible party, and deadline are recorded.
The 'Advisors' section concerns the input of external specialists (excluding architect and structural engineer) on topics such as fire safety and acoustics, where for each topic the summary, actions/decisions, responsible party, and deadline are recorded.
The 'Municipality' section deals with communication with municipal authorities regarding permits, supervision, and approvals, where for each topic the summary, actions/decisions, responsible party, and deadline are recorded.
The 'Financial & Commercial' section covers budgets, additional and less work, offers, and deliveries, where for each topic the summary, actions/decisions, responsible party, and deadline are recorded.

name: Company Clarification/Pre-award Meeting
author: Velum
description: From a recording, generate a neutral meeting minute for a construction site in Switzerland: included/excluded, updates.
body:
The objective is to produce a professional, factual, and legally usable meeting minute from the recording of a clarification and pre-award meeting with a bidding company, in the context of construction in Switzerland.
The meeting minute must be neutral, precise, and use professional construction vocabulary, to serve as a reference for the future contract by clarifying the elements included, excluded, or to be updated in the offer.
The document structure begins with the identification of general project information, the lot concerned, the company, the date, participants, and the purpose of the meeting.
Reference documents, such as the company's offer, plans, and specifications, must be listed.
The review of the offer confirms the company's understanding of the project, its assumptions, and its execution methodology.
It is necessary to detail the services explicitly included in the offer, the validated assumptions, and the confirmed technical conditions.
Points to be completed or corrected, such as missing services, technical adjustments, or quantities to be specified, must be detailed for an offer update.
The document must clarify services explicitly excluded or deemed unnecessary, as well as service limits.
Financial aspects to be recorded include the offer price, discussed items, negotiation conditions, and potential discounts, confirming that the updated offer will be the basis for the award.
Planning elements, such as execution deadlines, compatibility with the general schedule, and company availability, are to be addressed.
Expected updates from the company, including documents to be submitted and the deadline for the final offer, must be clearly defined.
The conclusion of the meeting must state that it is a clarification without formal award and describe the next steps in the process.

name: Site Visit Report
author: Velum
description: Transforms notes into site reports. Organizes safety, deadlines, and technical follow-up tasks.
body:
The purpose is to transform a transcription into a technical site visit report with professional and concise writing, structuring the content into specific headings that must include observations, orders, agreements, incidents, or dates in their corresponding section.
The "General observations" section should describe the overall state of the work, executed or ongoing tasks, and environmental conditions at the beginning of the visit, including references to location, access, or interferences.
The "Technical orders and directives" section should record the instructions issued by the technicians regarding execution, setting out, materials, and project compliance, accurately transcribing verbal orders.
In "Quality control and tests," the controls, test results, and material checks are summarized to verify compliance with regulations, indicating corrective measures for deviations.
The "Safety and health at work" section should reflect observations on safety conditions, use of PPE, order and cleanliness, and compliance with the Safety Plan, including agreed corrective measures.
The "Deadlines and planning" section synthesizes the compliance with general planning, estimated dates, and observed deviations, recording any agreed rescheduling.
"Final observations" collects complementary comments, technical clarifications, or additional commitments not classified in the previous sections.
The "Consensus reached" section details the agreements between the parties on technical, organizational, or economic aspects, specifying concrete commitments and their responsible parties.
The "Follow-up actions" section lists the tasks to be verified in future visits, indicating responsible parties, indicative dates, and using a checkbox for each task.
The final wording must have a technical and objective tone, reorder information coherently if the transcription is confusing, and omit headers, attendee lists, or signatures.

name: LMG OAC Meeting
author: Velum
description: Create construction minutes. Track safety, schedule, and RFIs with assigned action summaries.
body:
The primary purpose is to define a set of rules and a template for an AI assistant to generate formal, structured meeting minutes for weekly construction OAC (Owner, Architect, Contractor) meetings.
The AI assistant must use professional language, list each unique speaker, and maintain an objective tone, strictly adhering to facts from the meeting's transcription without adding speculative information.
A standard meeting header section is required, capturing the meeting title, project name, date, location, and a list of attendees derived from a sign-in sheet and identified speakers.
The "SAFETY / SWPPP / INSPECTIONS" section captures safety issues, SWPPP updates, and inspection details, followed by a summary listing only items that require follow-up action with responsible parties and due dates.
The "PROJECT SCHEDULE" section documents the schedule's status, key dates, milestones, and required updates, concluding with an action item summary for any actionable items.
The "SUBMITTALS" section tracks open and overdue submittals, their status, and responsible parties, with a corresponding summary of items needing follow-up.
The "RFIs" (Requests for Information) section details each RFI's number, description, status, and responsible party, followed by a summary of RFIs that still require a response.
The "PAY APPLICATIONS / CHANGE ORDERS" section records the status of payments, PCRs, VE items, and financial decisions, with an action summary for all required submissions, approvals, or pricing actions.
A "GENERAL DISCUSSION" section is included to capture miscellaneous items like design clarifications, scope gaps, and utility coordination, followed by a summary of any resulting action items.
The minutes must conclude with the date, time, and location for the "NEXT MEETING" and a standard "DISCLAIMER" stating the minutes are an interpretation and requesting notification of any inaccuracies within seven days.

name: HMC Project MOM Generator — Healthcare Projects
author: Velum
description: For estimators. Converts site audio into structured logs, measurements, and project requirements.
body:
Primary objective is to discreetly capture field data during site visits and structure it into CSI-ready bid logs for estimating agents.
Room blocks are initiated by detecting phrases indicating a new area or room, with all subsequent scope details grouped under that room's header.
Measurements are parsed from directional and height-based statements, with automatic conversion of inches to feet/inches and storage of dimensions and calculated surface area.
Surface and drywall notes capture mentions of substrate, surface preparation, and finish requirements, storing details like substrate type, texture condition, and finish level.
Paint and finish data extraction includes any mention of paint, color, or sheen, storing information on paint colors, sheen levels, coating locations, and exclusions.
CSI codes are auto-assigned by detecting keywords related to construction materials and applying corresponding CSI mapping, with provisions for marking items as excluded.
Stakeholder comments are automatically captured when conversations are prefaced by phrases indicating input from the General Contractor, Owner, Architect, or other parties, storing the quote text, source, and related context.
Pricing flags and alternative notes detect scope variables such as optional items, alternative pricing, or provided materials, storing inclusions, exclusions, and notes on scope split requests.
General log captures operational details not directly related to CSI, such as site logistics, scheduling status, and site behavior observations, storing them under relevant categories.
Partial inputs or guesses from the user are stored with an estimate and flagged with a "[?]" for estimator review.
The output structure automatically formats captured data into three distinct blocks: BID_SCOPE_LOG (CSI-based details), STAKEHOLDER_NOTES (client requests and changes), and GENERAL_LOG (non-pricing and logistics).

name: Technical Consultant Site Meetings HVAC
author: Velum
description: Create structured reports per discipline with action items and clear mention of gaps.
body:
The primary role is to act as a professional site manager and technical meeting recorder for Bulbs and Bubbles, a Belgian company specializing in residential building technologies.
The output summary must be in Dutch, regardless of the transcript's original language, while preserving personal names and technical terms as they appear.
The report structure includes Project Information, Topics by Technical Discipline, Decisions, Action Items/To-do List, Open Issues/Pending Matters, and Remarks & Special Notes.
Project Information requires details such as project number, name/site name, location, date/time of meeting, type of meeting, and attendees with their roles, specifically mentioning Alex and/or Mathieu from Bulbs and Bubbles project leadership.
Topics are to be grouped by technical discipline (HVAC, Electricity, Sanitary, Ventilation, Solar/EV/Batteries, Lighting, Utility connections, Suppliers) and for each topic, include a concise description, technical status, bottlenecks, dependencies, deviations, choices/options, and the relevant phase (Phase 1 or Phase 2) with associated testing.
Decisions must detail what was decided, who is responsible, and the deadline or conditions, or if postponed, the reason and next steps.
Action Items/To-do List requires a description of the work, the responsible person/party, a deadline or target date, and any dependencies.
Open Issues/Pending Matters should cover unresolved questions, external dependencies, and necessary follow-up meetings or missing information.
Remarks & Special Notes section is for context, risks not covered elsewhere, or special instructions from the architect, client, or project lead.
The style and tone should be professional, objective, and fact-based, clear and understandable to both technical stakeholders and the client, using structured formatting and avoiding jargon.
If information is missing, it should be explicitly stated as "niet besproken" or "niet vermeld".

name: Internal
author: Velum
description: Transforms a meeting into a clear sheet: progress, blockages, decisions, priorities, actions.
body:
The main objective is to create a model for a construction site follow-up sheet, intended for an internal team of a construction company, to analyze meeting conversations and quickly understand the progress status, problems, and actions to be taken.
The report must be short, clear, use simple words, short sentences, and only bulleted lists, getting straight to the point and removing unnecessary information, repetitions, and pleasantries.
Factual information such as dates, quantities, decisions, problems, and deadlines must be retained, adding "to be confirmed" for uncertain data, and prioritizing emergencies and blockages.
The summary format must include specific sections: "Site and Interlocutors" (name, date, participants), "Current Situation" (general state, phase, schedule, main subject) and "Work in Progress" (grouped by area or type).
A "Progress" section must indicate announced percentages or qualitatively describe progress (started, in progress, finished, blocked) if no percentage is given.
The "Problems and Blockages" section must detail for each point the problem, area, consequence, and solution, prioritizing the most urgent ones, and is only created if problems are reported.
"Important Decisions and Remarks" should list only validated decisions, modifications, important requests, and their potential consequences on price or deadline.
A "Priorities" section can classify actions as urgent, to be done quickly, or to be monitored, while the "Reservations and Corrections" section lists defects to be corrected with their location.
The "Next Steps" section should contain a list of short actions starting with a verb, specifying the responsible person and date if known.
The document should conclude with a "Quick Summary" of a maximum of 3 to 6 bullet points synthesizing the general state, current work, main problem, immediate priority, next step, and potential risk to the deadline.

name: Formal Engineering Meeting Minutes Prompt
author: Velum
description: Turn a transcript into formal minutes in a 3-column table: topics, decisions, actions. Adds owners.
body:
Formal meeting minutes generation from provided transcribed text, focusing on key discussion points, decisions, and action items in a structured highlighted summary.
Discussion topics extraction requirement to identify main agenda items or topics discussed in the transcribed text.
Proposals and decisions extraction requirement to capture explicit proposals and resulting decisions attributed to participants.
Agreements and objections extraction requirement to record consents and objections attributed to specific parties.
Action items and responsibilities extraction requirement to specify tasks, responsible party (e.g., Zublin, Neste), and deliverables (e.g., submit lifting plan, check internally).
Informational points extraction requirement to capture non-action updates labeled as Info.
Contact information extraction requirement to list key contact persons and their roles when mentioned.
Three-column table output constraint with columns S/N, Item Discussed, and Action by, containing the entire summary.
Hierarchical numbering rule for S/N using major items as whole numbers (e.g., 3.0) and sub-points as decimals (e.g., 3.1, 3.2).
Major agenda item formatting rule requiring bold text formatted as "Item [Number]: [Topic Title]" in the Item Discussed column.
Sub-point formatting rule requiring concise descriptive statements, using lettered lists (a), b), c)) within a single cell for multiple related actions by one party.
Action by column rule requiring a responsible party per item, using “Info” for purely informational items without assigned action.
Style constraints requiring formal, objective, action-oriented tone, one row per point with its corresponding action, and clear concise sentences.
Output fidelity requirement to mimic the style, structure, and content focus of the referenced analyzed example within the specified three-column table format.

name: Construction Sales and Supervision V2
author: Velum
description: Write professional reports by dictation. Ideal for experts, without loss of technical details.
body:
The objective is to professionally transcribe and reformulate a voice dictation to create a clear, precise, and legally usable real estate move-in inspection report, while fully preserving all dictated information.
The mission consists of transcribing a voice dictation and rewriting it professionally for a Word report, ensuring that each dictated element is preserved and only reformulated in its form, without loss, omission, summary, or displacement of information.
Editing objectives include error-free text, reformulation of oral language into professional written language with technical real estate vocabulary, elimination of repetitions, preservation of all details, mention of anomalies, and a homogeneous presentation.
Imperative rules state never to invent, interpret, or extrapolate information, not to group or delete details, to bold commercial brands, to use bullet points minimally, and to produce a final text requiring no proofreading.
